Nov 10, 2026
Description:
WAKE FOREST UNIVERSITY. The Department of Economics invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position as Assistant Professor of Economics, effective July 1, 2027.
JEL Classifications: G - Financial Economics, E44: Financial Markets and the Macroeconomy, F3: International Finance
Qualifications: Candidates should possess a Ph.D. in Economics, Finance, or a related field; ABD candidates will also be considered. Qualified applicants will demonstrate their ability to teach undergraduate courses, initiate and sustain original research and scholarship in financial economics or related fields, and contribute to an academic environment that fosters learning and growth for all its stakeholders.
Position Summary: This individual will be expected to teach undergraduate courses in financial economics and related areas; the ability to teach courses such as household finance, macro-finance, or personal finance will be especially valued. The successful candidate will also engage in scholarly activities; participate in departmental, College, and University service; and contribute to the University’s community outreach efforts.
Application Instructions: Review of applications will begin immediately. Complete applications should include a cover letter briefly describing the candidate's teaching and research interests, curriculum vitae, job market paper, statement of teaching philosophy, and three letters of recommendation. Applications submitted on or before November 10th will receive full consideration. To apply, visit: hr.wfu.edu/careers. Inquiries should be directed to Prof. Aeimit Lakdawala, Chair of the Search Committee, at lakdawa@wfu.edu or to Wake Forest University Human Resources at askhr@wfu.edu. Wake Forest University conducts background investigations for all final faculty candidates being considered for employment.
About the Department of Economics : The Department of Economics at Wake Forest is one of the most popular majors in the College, and our students are bright and engaged. jobs.title: Tenure Track Assistant Professor of Nineteenth Century Art
jobs.description:
Description
The Department of History of Art and Architecture at Vanderbilt University in Nashville,
Tennessee invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track position Assistant Professor of
Nineteenth-Century Art History to begin in August 2027. We seek a candidate whose research
and teaching consider nineteenth-century art in transnational contexts with a preference for
candidates whose teaching and research complement the department’s existing strengths. In
addition to outstanding scholarly potential, successful candidates will demonstrate their readiness
to contribute to our undergraduate majors, our master’s degree programs, and our new
interdisciplinary minor and graduate certificate in Museum and Market studies. For current
faculty research strengths and course offerings please visit the departmental website:
https://as.vanderbilt.edu/history-art-architecture/.
Qualifications
With a teaching load of 2-2, the candidate will be expected to teach a combination of
introductory surveys (e.g. Nineteenth-Century Art, History of Art Renaissance to the Present)
and area-specific courses. This position will also support the Arts & Science Core curriculum.
Within our new Museum and Markets programs, candidates should be prepared to offer a course
on the nineteenth-century art market, museum culture, or the gallery system. Ideas for travelembedded
courses are welcome and generous funding is available. There are opportunities to
engage with initiatives across campus including the Engine for Art, Democracy and Justice, the
Center for Latin American, Caribbean, and Latinx Studies, the Vanderbilt Museum of Art, the
W.T. Bandy Center for Baudelaire and Modern French Studies, the Robert Penn Warren Center
for the Humanities and as well as Vanderbilt’s campuses in New York city and San Francisco.
Application Instructions
A PhD in Art History, Visual Studies, or a related field must be in hand no later than
August 1, 2027. Applications should include a cover letter; a CV; writing sample of no more
than 25 pages; statement of teaching philosophy (and evidence of effectiveness including recent
teaching evaluations). Letters of recommendation will be solicited from short-listed candidates.
Review of applications will begin November 15th, 2026. Completed applications received by
that date are guaranteed full consideration, and review of applications will continue until the
position is filled.
For questions regarding this position, please email the chair of the search, Rebecca VanDiver
(rebecca.vandiver@vanderbilt.edu).

We welcome applications from scholars of Catholicism trained in Religious Studies or a closely related discipline whose research explores the global circulation of Catholicism. We are especially interested in scholars whose research brings Catholicism into conversation with cross-cultural, interreligious or transnational issues in the academic study of religion. The time period and geographic focus of this scholarship are open, with a preference given for candidates whose research encompasses the Global South.
The successful applicant will be expected to teach courses that contribute to the Religious Studies minor, as well as at least one course in one of the department’s other degrees or programs, including but not limited to Africana Studies, Classics, Jewish Studies, Global Studies, and/or Hispanic Studies. The teaching load is typically two courses per semester.
The Department of Global Languages and Cultures offers degrees/programs in Global Studies, modern languages and Classics, and graduate degrees in Hispanic Studies, in addition to offering undergraduate minors in Religious Studies, Africana Studies, and Jewish Studies. Information about the Religious Studies program is available here, and about the Department of Global Languages and Cultures here.
A Hispanic-Serving Institution (HSI), Texas A&M is one of the largest R1 institutions in the United States. It is located in College Station, Texas, which has a south-meets-southwest culture that is steeped in tradition, and includes vibrant religious life.
Qualifications
Applicants must hold a PhD in Religious Studies or closely related field.
Applicants at the rank of Professor must demonstrate a strong, active research program in the area of global Catholicism commensurate with the expectations of an R1 institution. In addition to strong teaching and research, the successful applicant will show evidence of experience in program development, collaborative work, outreach in and beyond the academy, and/or building research initiatives.
Applicants at the rank of advanced Associate Professor may be considered if the record demonstrates research, teaching, and service commensurable with a full professorship at an R1 institution.

Cover letter
Curriculum vitae (please embed links to your work)
Personal Statement: Your statement of no more than three (3) pages should discuss your philosophy and plans for research, teaching and service.
Names and contact information of five (5) professional references who could be contacted for letters of reference.

Equal Opportunity/Veterans/Disability Employer.

jobs.title: Open Rank Professor, British/Anglophone Literature
jobs.description:
Job Details
POSITION SUMMARY
The Department of English at Occidental College invites applications for a tenure‐track Open Rank, Professor of British/Anglophone Literature with appointment to begin August 2027.
The English Department is searching for a new colleague in British/Anglophone Literature. The specialization is open, though the department is especially interested in the fields of Long Eighteenth Century, the History of the Novel, Romanticism, British Modernism, Contemporary Global Anglophone literature. We welcome a range of methodologies that practice close reading, examine literary form, and attend to literary history. The new hire will offer courses in Modern British Literature, from its 18th-century origins to its 21st-century manifestations. This will include ENGL 288: Modern British Traditions, as well as other courses at the 100, 200, and 300 levels in their area(s) of specialization. In addition, the new hire will teach required seminar courses that rotate among members of the department, including ENGL 290: Literary Methods, the ENGL 390: Junior Seminar and ENGL 490: Senior Seminar. We are particularly interested in courses that would meet College Core requirements or would engage with the city and communities of Los Angeles. As necessary, the new hire will contribute to the First Year Seminar program, which focuses on writing and community-engagement. The new hire will also have the opportunity to mentor undergraduate researchers in Oxy’s renowned Summer Undergraduate Research Program. The new hire will have an active research agenda, producing scholarship that is commensurate with their rank. Finally, the new hire will participate in the life and development of the department, advise students, and serve on broader college-wide committees.
The Department of English studies literature to develop our critical and creative potential in a nation and world going through drastic changes. We embrace the view that historically, geographically, and culturally grounded readings of literature deepen its aesthetic value. Literature continues to be a wellspring for other creative mediums (including television, film, music, visual art, performance art, and beyond). We also introduce our students to archival research in Occidental’s special collections as well as other libraries and archives in Southern California.
Our students embrace literature’s role in nourishing their critical and creative potential. Every English major researches and writes their own critical analysis of a literary work in their Senior Comprehensive Project. In recent years, students have taken up a range of topics for their Senior Comprehensive, including Gothic literature, Margaret Atwood’s fiction, Ecoliterature, Toni Morrison’s fiction, Ekphrastic Poetry, Anticolonial Literature, the relationship between Literature and Gaming, and Reginald Shepherd’s Elegies. Our students who take on the creative writing emphasis have published poetry chapbooks, children’s literature, and short fiction. English majors and minors comprise the majority of the editorial collective that publishes The Oz, Occidental’s literary magazine that features short fiction, poetry, experimental writing, and visual art from students across campus. Our students have also made their mark across Los Angeles, from interning with the Los Angeles Review of Books to volunteering in mutual aid projects. Our graduates go on to work in independent publishing, education, marketing, and law, among other fields. Our faculty are committed teacher-scholars who bring critical inquiry and discovery into the classroom. They establish themselves as exceptional researchers and practitioners in their fields and they provide departmental and college-wide service, as well as service to their professions. As a small institution with a commitment to Shared Governance, faculty across the College collaborate in maintaining the excellence of the College’s academic program.
Located within the vibrant city of Los Angeles, Occidental is committed to a community-engaged curriculum—faculty carry out fieldwork, visit local museums and cultural organizations, and develop long-standing partnerships across the city. For decades, Occidental has been a leader in creating access for a diverse student body. That diversity enriches the education of all students. We seek an innovative teacher, scholar, mentor, and colleague who wishes to work in such an environment and who shares the commitments articulated in the Mission of the College.
Required Qualifications
Ph.D in English, with a focus in British/Anglophone Literature by the position start date, August 2027. Record of or willingness to teach and mentor effectively in a Small Liberal Arts College environment. Record of or willingness to advance equitable opportunities and inclusive pedagogies for learning and mentoring, especially for minoritized students. Record of or willingness to teach courses in Modern British/Anglophone Literature, including ENGL 288: Modern British Traditions, as well as other courses at the 100-, 200-, and 300-levels that fulfill either the Group II, III, or IV Requirements in the major curriculum. Experience teaching or willingness to teach their own versions of required courses in the English major, including ENGL 290, Introduction to Literary methods; ENGL 390, Junior Seminar; and ENGL 490, Senior Seminar (with ENGL 290 being the most important in this series). Ability to teach First-Year Seminar courses. Evidence of an established research agenda, appropriate to the level of appointment. Evidence of active participation in their specialized field(s). Evidence of furthering their research agenda through recent and forthcoming research.
Preferred Qualifications
A Specialty in the Long Eighteenth Century, the History of the Novel, British Romanticism, British Modernism, Contemporary Global Anglophone literature, or related fields. Willingness and ability to teach community-engaged or practice-oriented courses Willingness and ability to mentor students during the school year in Directed Research courses in the English major or during the Summer in the Undergraduate Research Program or MSI. Willingness and ability to organize programming, events, exhibitions Experience in or commitment to departmental leadership and management responsibilities (e.g., curricular development, annual assessment, long-term departmental planning, etc.) Potential to teach some cross-listable courses with other departments/curricula at the College.
EXPECTED SALARY RANGE (for Academic Year, Nine-month Appointment):
If hired at Assistant rank: $87,000 - $94,000 If hired at Associate rank: $103,000 - $116,000 If hired at Full rank: $120,000 - $145,000
If you are offered this position at Occidental College, your final base salary compensation will be determined based on factors such as skills, education, experience, and/or geographic location. In addition to those factors, Occidental complies with applicable pay equity laws and considers internal equity among current employees when developing the final offer. Please keep in mind that the range mentioned above is the base salary range for the role. Hiring at the maximum of the range would not be typical in order to allow for future and continued salary growth.
APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS
To receive full consideration (with the exception of life emergencies), your application materials must be received by midnight Eastern time (9:00 pm Pacific time) on November 15, 2026.
Applicants must submit a complete application package electronically via Interfolio to be considered by the search committee. https://apply.interfolio.com/194069
A complete application includes all of the following:
Cover Letter (2 to 3 pages), detailing your interest in teaching in an urban liberal arts environment; your interest in teaching core courses in the English major and courses in your field specialty or courses elsewhere in the College. Applicants with administrative and leadership experience are welcome to mention this information in their cover letter as well. Curriculum Vitae listing degrees, research fields, scholarly activities, courses taught, and other relevant professional activity (conference participation, contributions to professional associations, journal activity, or editorial work). Research Statement (2 to 3 pages) that includes a discussion of your past and present scholarly work as well as your plans for future research. This can include future articles, single-authored or co-authored book projects, edited collections, or public intellectual work. Statement of Teaching Philosophy (2 to 3 pages) that includes a discussion of your teaching experience, proposed courses, preferred pedagogical practices, as well as your record of and future plans for creating equitable opportunities for learning and mentoring a diverse student body. List of 3 possible references - names and contact information. Please do NOT submit letters with your application
Applicants who advance to future stages will be asked to submit additional materials; please do not submit any of these materials at the initial stage.
Applicants who advance to the Semifinalist phase will be asked to submit the following:
Writing Sample (15 to 25 pages) that represents recently completed or ongoing scholarly research. This could be a published article or book chapter, a forthcoming article or book chapter, or a recently presented scholarly lecture. Whatever form the writing sample takes, it should complement the trajectory explained in the research statement. Two sample syllabi. One sample syllabus must be for ENGL 288, Modern British Literature. The other sample syllabus can cover one of the following courses: ENGL 332, Eighteenth Century Literature; ENGL 351, Modernism and Contemporary British Fiction; or a new 300 level course that would reflect the applicant’s research specialty and fulfill Group II, III, or IV requirements in the English major.
Applicants who advance to the finalist phase will be asked to submit three Confidential Letters of Recommendation.
If you have any questions about the position, the application materials, or the application instructions, please contact: James Ford at jford@oxy.edu or call 323-259-1472. If you have questions about Interfolio or the application process, please contact the Academic Support Administrator, Beatrice Gonzales, at facultysearch@oxy.edu.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
Occidental is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not unlawfully discriminate against employees or applicants on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, pregnancy, breastfeeding or related medical condition, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, age, marital status, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, genetic characteristic or information, military and veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by state or federal law. Occidental is strongly committed to increasing the diversity of the campus community and the curriculum, and to fostering an inclusive, equitable, and just environment within which students, staff, administrators, and faculty thrive. Candidates who can contribute to this goal through their work are encouraged to identify their strengths and experiences in this area. Individuals advancing the College’s strategic equity and justice goals and those from groups that are underrepresented in the field are particularly encouraged to apply.
Salary is commensurate with experience and qualifications. A comprehensive benefits package is available that includes: excellent health, dental, life, and retirement benefits; tuition benefits for the employee, spouse, domestic partner, and dependents; additional extras including use of gym facilities and the College Library. For a detailed description of benefits, please visit https://www.oxy.edu/offices-services/humanresources/benefits-information
All qualified applicants will be considered for employment, including those with criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance.
Occidental College is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with qualifying disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation because of a disability for any part of the application or employment process, please contact Human Resources (hr@oxy.edu).
As a condition of hire for a staff position and for appointment to a faculty position, Occidental College requires that all candidates who have received a conditional offer of employment complete an application form (if they have not already done so) and consent to a background check. Satisfactory completion of a background check, along with pre-employment verifications and references are required as a condition of employment, but only as permitted by federal, state, and local law, including the City of Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Education (Special Education)
jobs.description:
Salary Range - $60,000 - $70,000
Assistant Professor of Education (Special Education)
The Education Department at Randolph College seeks a dynamic tenure-track assistant professor of education to begin July 1, 2027
We seek a faculty member with expertise in special education. Candidates with experience in evidence-based reading instruction are preferred. We welcome applications from candidates who are members of historically underrepresented groups. We expect our new colleague to be committed to inclusive, equitable teaching. This faculty member will likely teach Educational Psychology as well as other undergraduate and graduate courses in special education, including Instructional Approaches for Students with Disabilities and Practicum, Assessment and Evaluation in Special Education, IEP Implementation & Case Management and Transition, Survey of Special Ed and Special Ed Law, as well as graduate methods classes. The faculty member will also organize and facilitate the spring Special Education Conference for area teachers.
Primary responsibilities
● Teach a 3/3 load with a mix of online and face-to-face classes.
● Advise undergraduate students.
● Supervise undergraduate and graduate preservice teachers in local and distance practicum experiences, depending on course assignment.
● Maintain an active scholarly agenda resulting in presentations at local, regional, and national conferences and publications.
● Maintain active membership in relevant state and national organizations.
● Support the Randolph College Educator Preparation Program’s accreditation and program approval processes.
● Collaborate with local schools and school leaders to create and sustain mutually beneficial partnerships.
● Engage in service to the College, community, and profession.
● Demonstrate a strong understanding of and commitment to a liberal arts education.
● Demonstrate a strong understanding of the social constructivist approach to education and commitment to preparing teachers able to combine research skills, social responsibility, effective instructional practice, content expertise, and leadership skills in their future classrooms.
Required qualifications
● A PhD or EdD in special education, curriculum and instruction, or a related field. (ABD candidates with a plan to finish by August 2027 will be considered.)
● At least three years of experience as a licensed teacher in grades PK–12 in a public U.S. school.
● Evidence of or potential for excellence in undergraduate and graduate instruction.
● Evidence of an active or burgeoning research agenda.
The Randolph College Education Department prepares undergraduate and graduate students for licensure in elementary education, special education, and a number of secondary/all-grades areas. At the undergraduate level, we support two undergraduate majors (elementary and special education); a minor in race, culture, and equity in education; and a secondary/all-grades licensure pathway. At the graduate level, we offer a fully online Master of Arts in Teaching leading to licensure and Master of Education for candidates not seeking licensure.
Our department prepares candidates to teach effectively, to act as leaders in school communities, and to serve as agents of equity and change. Our work reflects the College's motto of vita abundantior—a life more abundant—by promoting joy, curiosity, and the love of learning as essential parts of a meaningful life. The philosophical foundation of Randolph’s Educator Preparation Program begins with the fundamental belief that culture and community influence learning, and our social constructivist approach helps candidates grow as culturally relevant and responsive educators. Our primary goal is to foster the development of highly qualified teachers and leaders in PK–12 schools and a range of other educational settings.
How to Apply
To apply, please send the following materials to specialedsearch@randolphcollege.edu:
1. A cover letter addressing position responsibilities and qualifications;
2. A current curriculum vitae;
3. A statement of teaching philosophy that includes evidence of teaching effectiveness and alignment with the department’s social constructivist philosophy and commitment to inclusivity;
4. An unofficial graduate transcript (official transcript required at time of hire); and
5. Names and contact information for three references (letters will be requested for those candidates who are interviewed).
Review of materials will begin on October 16, 2026.
About Randolph College
Randolph College, founded in 1891 as Randolph-Macon Woman’s College, is a traditional small liberal arts college with a longstanding reputation for excellence in teaching and an appreciation for and commitment to inclusivity.
In the College’s unique TAKE2 curricular model, students take two courses in 7-week sessions with two sessions per semester. The result is a curriculum that provides time for students to focus on two courses, while balancing other important aspects of the college experience: internships, extracurricular activities, athletics, and jobs.
More information about Randolph College can be found here: http://www.randolphcollege.edu/
About Lynchburg, VA
Founded in 1757 by abolitionist John Lynch, Lynchburg, VA is located near the geographic center of Virginia, at the edge of the Blue Ridge Mountains. Its expanding population supports a vibrant downtown, and offers a variety of cultural, educational, and recreational opportunities, making it an attractive destination for both residents and visitors. The city boasts ample outdoor activities such as hiking, swimming, boating, skiing, and access to a municipal park system with urban trails, playgrounds, and swimming pools. The city's arts and theater scene is lively, complemented by museums and a minor league baseball team. Lynchburg is a city with a growing number of employers and businesses, but a low cost of living compared to the nearby cities of Charlottesville and Roanoke. Located approximately 180 miles from Washington, D.C., Lynchburg is accessible via an Amtrak station and regional airport.
Lynchburg is also known for its strong educational presence, housing five colleges and universities, including one HBCU. The city was the home of the Virginia Teachers’ Reading Circle. Established in 1887, the Reading Circle provided professional development for teachers of Black students across Virginia. This group evolved into the Virginia Teachers Association, serving Black teachers in the region until it merged with the integrated Virginia Education Association in 1967. This history of diversity continues to be reflected in the city’s schools today.

Job Details
Salary Range or Pay Grade Associate Professor - $139,000 - $162,000; Full Professor: $180,000 - $288,000 Description The Department of English and the Lewis Center for the Arts are seeking an outstanding tenured senior hire working in the field of drama broadly defined, including: the literature, history, practice, and theory of drama; dramatic criticism and the history of dramatic criticism; drama in relation to aesthetics and to other media; the theory and history of theatre and of theatrical performance. jobs.title: Faculty Position in Ethics (Open Rank)
jobs.description: Emory University’s Candler School of Theology invites applications and nominations for a tenured or tenure-track faculty position in Ethics. Rank is open. The successful candidate will hold a PhD or its equivalent in Ethics or a related field by the time of appointment in the fall semester of 2027. Preference will be given to complete applications submitted by October 21, 2026. Candler School of Theology carries a proud legacy in the fields of Christian theological and social ethics, one shaped by scholarly attention to rigorous moral inquiry and debates in public theology and social justice. We seek a faculty member who will build on this legacy and imagine new directions in the field. We welcome applications from scholars pursuing innovative and intersectional approaches to moral challenges and possibilities in church, religion, and public life. Methods and thematic foci might include, but are not limited to, ethnography, aesthetics, ecology, visual and material culture, technology, AI, health, economics, politics, civil and human rights, and law. The person selected for this position will develop and teach courses in several of the degree programs of Candler School of Theology, including the MDiv, MTS, MARL, and DMin programs. The successful candidate will display the capacity to contribute to a broad theological curriculum and situate ethics within larger ecumenical, multi-faith, and global contexts. Candidates should be prepared to teach a wide range of students in both online and in-person modalities. The appointee will have regular faculty rotation in the school’s Contextual Education program. Appointees with a substantial research and publication agenda can apply to participate in the Graduate Division of Religion in the Laney Graduate School of Emory University. In addition to teaching and research, faculty members of Candler School of Theology are committed to service, both within the school and in the larger church and community. Applications for this position should include a letter of interest, a curriculum vitae, a writing sample, and three confidential letters of recommendation. Candidates should apply online at https://apply.interfolio.com/193983. Please direct any questions to Susan Reynolds, chair of the search committee (sbreyn3@emory.edu). People of all backgrounds and all traditions are encouraged to apply. We especially welcome applicants within, or those familiar with, Wesleyan denominations. Emory is an equal opportunity employer, and qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by state or federal law.

jobs.title: Faculty Medical Physicist Opportunity – Radiation Oncology
jobs.description:
Faculty Medical Physicist Opportunity – Radiation Oncology
University of Alabama at Birmingham (UAB) School of Medicine
The Department of Radiation Oncology at the University of Alabama at Birmingham (UAB) is seeking a clinically focused and academically driven Medical Physicist for a full-time, open-rank faculty position. Tenure status, academic rank, and compensation will be commensurate with qualifications and experience.
What We’re Looking For:
Ph.D. in Medical Physics, Physics, or a closely related field
ABR certification in Therapeutic Medical Physics (or board-eligible with completed CAMPEP-accredited residency)
Demonstrated record of scholarly achievement
Strong commitment to clinical excellence, teamwork, and academic collaboration
Clinical Role:
The successful candidate will participate in all aspects of clinical medical physics support, quality assurance, and radiation safety across our main campus and regional satellite clinics. Clinical scope includes:
IMRT, VMAT, IGRT, respiratory gating
Stereotactic Radiosurgery (SRS) and Stereotactic Body Radiation Therapy (SBRT)
Interstitial and intracavitary HDR brachytherapy
I-125 eye plaque therapy, Total Body Irradiation (TBI)
Photons and electrons with advanced linear accelerator platforms
Technology & Infrastructure:
Varian platform: 2 TrueBeam, 1 Edge, 2 iX (with RapidArc and cone beam CT), 1 Ethos
2 Philips Brilliance Big Bore CT simulators
Varian Bravos HDR unit
Treatment planning and R&V systems: Varian Eclipse/ARIA
Academic Environment:
Our physics team includes 15 Ph.D. physicists, working alongside 17 radiation oncologists, dosimetrists, therapists, and administrative leadership to provide high-quality care for more than 170 patients per day across UAB and satellite locations.
We offer an accredited CAMPEP medical physics residency program and train two physics residents and ten radiation oncology residents annually. The department strongly supports academic development and expects faculty to build collaborative, clinically relevant research programs. Faculty are encouraged to collaborate across UAB's Heersink School of Medicine and its nationally recognized academic and research infrastructure.
For additional information about our department, please visit our website at
https://www.uab.edu/medicine/radonc/.
About UAB
The University of Alabama at Birmingham (UAB) is a research university and academic health center that discovers, teaches and applies knowledge for the intellectual, cultural, social, and economic benefit of Birmingham, the state, and beyond. UAB is internationally renowned for its intensely collaborative culture that has — for more than five decades — produced breakthroughs in education, health care, research, and service. UAB Radiation Oncology is a trusted training site for Varian where trainees traverse from across the nation. UAB was ranked #1 in the United States, and in the top 10 worldwide, in the Times Higher Education World University Rankings and 2018 Young University Rankings.
UAB Medicine is the third-largest public academic medical center in the country, with more than 1,900 beds and almost 18,000 employees. UAB Hospital is the centerpiece of the UAB Health System and is the teaching hospital for the UAB School of Medicine. Situated among major research centers and clinics, UAB Hospital provides patients with a complete range of primary and specialty care services, as well as the most up-to-date treatments and innovations in health care. In addition to UAB Hospital, UAB Medicine includes The Kirklin Clinic of UAB Hospital, UAB Callahan Eye Hospital, as well as several primary and specialty care clinics, a dozen member and affiliate hospitals within Alabama, more than 10 cancer associates in the Southeast, and the Viva Health HMO.
Recently, UAB expanded further by acquiring five hospitals from the Ascension St. Vincent’s Health System. This acquisition added 5,000 employees, 409 beds, and outpatient facilities, which include hospitals in Birmingham, Blount, Chilton, East, and St. Clair counties; the One Nineteen campus; the Trussville Freestanding Emergency Department; imaging centers; and other clinics.

The Department of English at Coastal Carolina University invites applications for a tenure track Assistant Professor of English specializing in World Literature and/or Comparative Literature and Media teaching a 3/3 load to begin August 2027. Candidates must hold a PhD in English, World Literature, or Comparative Literature and/or Cultural Studies by August 2027 and have college-level teaching experience. We are particularly interested in scholars who can provide evidence of successful teaching experience with focus on one or more of the following: Digital Humanities; Human-centered storytelling in an age of AI; early literature (particularly world mythologies); folklore and place-based storytelling; medical humanities and narratives.
We seek candidates who show demonstrated potential as a teacher-scholar whose research and teaching engage world literary and cultural studies in diverse historical, cultural, and/or digital, filmic, and media contexts. The successful candidate will teach undergraduate literature and Core Curriculum courses, introductory literature and graduate level courses. We welcome candidates able to contribute related programs and minors such as the B.A. in Digital Culture and Design, English Secondary Education, Film and New Media, the Joyner Institute for Gullah and African Diaspora Studies, and The Athenaeum Press.
The Department of English (https://www.coastal.edu/english/) aspires to create a community of scholars that promote critical reading and writing through an open exchange of ideas, enabling our students to better understand the historical, cultural, and aesthetic dimensions of literature, language, and media. We are committed to innovative teaching and strongly encourage the development of digital or experiential pedagogy and multimodal learning. We embrace Interdisciplinary pedagogy and scholarship.
The department offers three majors: BA in English, BA in Digital Culture and Design, and the newly added BA in English Education. We also offer five minors and house the MA in Writing program, which prepares students for careers in writing, editing, and publishing or for further graduate study in MFA or PhD programs.

The E. Craig Wall Sr. College of Business Administration at Coastal Carolina University invites applications for a full-time tenure-track position at the assistant/associate professor level in the Department of Finance and Economics beginning Fall 2027. To be considered, candidates should possess a Ph.D. in finance from an AACSB-accredited program with a specialization supportive of one or more of the finance degree tracks (wealth management, banking and consumer finance, or corporate finance). The department also offers a major and minor in commercial and investment real estate, as well as a certificate in financial planning. We are also launching a new M.S. Finance program in the fall of 2026. Typically, the successful candidate will demonstrate interest and/or experience in teaching in at least two of the department’s areas of specialization—wealth management, banking and consumer finance, corporate finance, or commercial and investment real estate.
Applicants who are A.B.D. candidates with a clear plan for degree completion by July 2027 may be considered (candidates who are ABD — please ensure you document the timeline of defending your dissertation in your application). A candidate with a completed Ph.D. must have a recent and consistent record of publication in quality refereed journals. The Department of Finance and Economics also values candidates with industry experience and a commitment to community engagement. Candidates holding professional certifications (CFA®, CFP®, etc.) are preferred. The ideal candidate would also have a track record of community engagement and experiential learning that can create value for the department and for student learning experiences.
The teaching load is three courses per academic semester, and may include face-to-face, hybrid, and/or online deliveries. In addition to teaching responsibilities, the successful candidate will be expected to engage in research and scholarship, resulting in high-quality publications. The Wall College of Business has a WRDS platform with access to CRSP, Compustat, Bloomberg, and Datastream to support quality scholarship and teaching. The position also requires service activities, including contributing to the assessment of student learning outcomes, and other service to the department, college, university, community, and profession. It is expected that the individual chosen for this position will possess a commitment to teaching excellence, demonstrated ability or capacity to produce quality scholarly academic research, a commitment to involvement in service to the university and the profession, excellent communication skills, and effective teamwork skills.
Accredited by AACSB International, the Wall College of Business serves more than 3000 graduate and undergraduate students. The college offers undergraduate majors in seven disciplines (Accounting, Commercial and Investment Real Estate, Economics, Finance, Management, Marketing, and Hospitality, Resort and Tourism Management), as well as MBA and M.S. Finance graduate programs. The Department of Finance and Economics houses majors in both disciplines, along with a Commercial and Investment Real Estate major. The finance major offers a choice of three concentrations: wealth management; banking and consumer finance; and corporate finance. Capstone courses in all three concentrations make use of simulations with the Student Managed Investment Fund embedded in the wealth management capstone. Enrollment in the finance degree has increased significantly in recent years, with over 700 students majoring in the discipline. The department also has minors in economics, commercial and investment real estate, and actuarial science and risk management along with a certificate in financial planning (CFP® Board Registered Program). Additional information about the College and the University and its programs can be obtained by accessing the university’s website (http://www.coastal.edu).

ABD candidates with a clear plan for degree completion prior to May 31, 2027, may be considered. Job Details:
The Department of Languages and Intercultural Studies at Coastal Carolina University invites applications for a tenure-track position at the advanced assistant or early associate level in Spanish for the Professions. The teaching load for this position is 3/3 and will begin August 16, 2027. Candidates must hold a Ph.D. in Spanish by the start date and exhibit strong potential for excellence in teaching. Preferred qualifications would be: Evidence of experience teaching Spanish for the Professions, Native or near-native proficiency in Spanish and English, Experience teaching language courses to students from a broad range of majors at a US institution of higher education, Evidence of proficiency in teaching with technology, Experience teaching Spanish for health-related professions, Evidence of scholarly activity related to Spanish for the Professions, Experience with program coordination.
At Coastal Carolina University, we have a thriving program in Spanish for health professions, including both a minor and a new graduate certificate. We also offer a B.A. in Languages and Intercultural Studies with concentrations in Hispanic Studies and Multiple Languages. The successful candidate will take a leadership role in coordinating the Spanish for Health Professions program and contribute to the overall growth of programs in our department, collaborate with community partners, supervise student internships, and contribute to other departmental initiatives. Familiarity with and the ability to put into practice ACTFL Standards are essential. Additionally, the candidate must be able to collaborate and engage productively with faculty in a multi-language department that values a variety of perspectives. Preference will be given to candidates with experience in teaching and developing curricula in Spanish for health professions, but additional areas of expertise in Spanish for the professions will be considered. Advanced assistant professors are encouraged to apply.
Interested candidates should submit electronically to https://jobs.coastal.edu/postings/122666: (1) a letter of application that addresses the qualifications specified in this advertisement, (2) a curriculum vitae, and (3) the names and contact information for three professional references, (4) Copy of Transcripts, (5) Statement of Teaching Philosophy . jobs.title: Assistant Professor, Architecture
jobs.description:
Job Details
The Department of Art, Architecture and Design at Lehigh University invites applications for a tenure-track position as Assistant Professor of Architecture, with expertise in architectural design. The anticipated start date is July 1 2027.
The successful candidate will join a large and multidisciplinary department with undergraduate BA major programs in art, architecture, graphic and product design, and art history. Through a studio culture that encourages peer engagement, collective critique, and open discourse, the department's architecture curriculum fosters engagement with the built environment in its critical, technical, and social dimensions. The standard teaching load for tenure-track faculty is two courses per semester, and the university offers exceptional support to faculty, including generous start up packages for new faculty and numerous internal grant opportunities for ongoing research and creative practice.
As a faculty member in the Department of Art, Architecture and Design, the candidate will be expected to teach introductory- through advanced-level courses in architectural design in regular rotation, as well as courses in the candidate’s areas of expertise. They will also be expected to develop and maintain an active program of scholarship and creative practice that demonstrates excellence and impact, as evidenced by built works, exhibitions, awards, reviews, publications, and other forms of juried or peer-reviewed work, or professional and client-based projects comparably recognized. In both teaching and research, the candidate’s work should be seated in methods that look to make an impact in a range of communities beyond the university setting, serving both disciplinary and public interests. In addition, they will contribute to departmental, college, and university service.
The department promotes forward-thinking scholarship and teaching, with affiliation across the university’s many interdisciplinary programs, centers, and institutes. We are a versatile and experimental program that offers exceptional research opportunities and support for faculty conducting paradigm-shifting work across the boundaries of art, architecture, and design.
About the Department of Art, Architecture and Design
The Department of Art, Architecture and Design is one of Lehigh University’s largest enrolling undergraduate departments. The department offers BA degrees in four majors—art, architecture, graphic and product design, and art history—and minors in each area, as well as in museum studies and apparel design.
We offer an undergraduate education in the arts that combines the depth of an art and design school training with the breadth and flexibility of a liberal arts curriculum. We aim to enable students to become makers and designers, builders and creators—backed by the resources of a R1-level research university that has for generations helped shape innovation, industry, and design in the United States. We also aspire to excellence and distinction in experiential learning by providing students with opportunities to harness the skills they learn in the classroom, both for real-world application and as the basis for service in the community and the world at large. We are part of the College of Arts and Sciences—the heart of Lehigh University—offering a wide variety of academic majors, minors, and interdisciplinary programs at both the undergraduate and graduate level.
The department is housed in a 40,000-square-foot research and teaching facility on Lehigh University’s Mountaintop Campus, with studio and classroom spaces serviced by extensive resources, encompassing a range of computer labs, printing and digital fabrication technologies, shops, and finishing areas. This includes adjacent resources of the university’s Design Labs, a network of fabrication facilities across campus; and the collections and exhibitions of the Lehigh University Art Galleries (LUAG), with a permanent collection of over 20,000 works of art. The department is currently expanding its community-facing design-build research programs and curriculum, with funded research and teaching opportunities for faculty and students.
The department upholds Lehigh University’s Principles of Our Equitable Community, affirming the inherent dignity of every member of our community and working to build a culture of mutual understanding, respect, and academic freedom. We are especially interested in faculty whose research, teaching, design work, and scholarship reflect these principles, whether through studio pedagogy, community engaged practice, or research that examines how the built environment shapes access and opportunity for the communities it serves. These values are central to the department’s mission and purpose.
About Lehigh University
Founded in 1865, Lehigh University has combined outstanding academic and learning opportunities with leadership in fostering innovative research. Recognized among the nation's highly ranked research universities, Lehigh offers a rigorous academic community for over 7,500 students. Lehigh University has some 5,800 undergraduates, 1,800 graduate students, and nearly 600 full-time faculty members. Lehigh University is located in Bethlehem, PA, a vibrant and historic area. Over 840,000 people live in the Lehigh Valley, which is in close proximity to New York City and Philadelphia.
Lehigh University is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital or familial status, national origin (including shared ancestry), pregnancy or related conditions, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, or veteran status. Lehigh University is committed to a culturally and intellectually diverse academic community and is especially interested in candidates who can contribute, through their research, teaching and/or service, to this mission. Lehigh University provides competitive salaries and comprehensive benefits, including domestic partner benefits, and supports faculty members’ work/life balance.
Qualifications
Applicants must hold a MArch, PhD, or other equivalent terminal degree in architecture or a closely related field by date of employment. Applicants must also have at least one year of teaching experience in the university setting, beyond the level of a teaching assistantship.
Application Instructions
For full consideration, applications should be received online by January 8, 2027. Applicants should submit their materials at https://apply.interfolio.com/193666.
● Letter describing the candidate’s interest in the position, also addressing intended contributions to Lehigh University’s Principles of Our Equitable Community (3 pages max.)
● Research statement, outlining current and future scholarship, including the candidate’s disciplinary approach (2 pages max.)
● Teaching statement describing pedagogy, experience, and values (2 pages max.)
● Curriculum vitae
● Portfolio of the candidate’s own creative practice and scholarship (collated as one PDF)
● Examples of work by the candidate’s students, focused on one assignment or project, with an explanation of its scope (collated as one PDF)
● Sample syllabi from courses taught or developed (2 courses max.)
● List of three (3) references with contact information (references will only be contacted if the candidate advances in the search)
Any inquiries regarding this search should be directed to Pamela Mongi, Department Coordinator, Department of Art, Architecture and Design: pgm0@lehigh.edu

jobs.description:

Next Lives at the University of Cincinnati
Founded in 1819, the University of Cincinnati ranks among the nation’s best urban public research universities. Home to more than 53,600 students, 12,000 faculty and staff, and over 360,000 living alumni, UC, a Carnegie 1 institution, combines research prowess with a physical setting The New York Times has called “the most ambitious campus design program in the country." UC's momentum has never been stronger as the anchor of the Cincinnati Innovation District, the oldest cooperative education (co-op) program in the country with students earning $94 million annually through paid experiences, an academic health system, and as a member of the Big 12 Conference. The university contributes $10.6 billion in economic impact to the city and $22.7 billion to the state of Ohio. At UC, next is all of us. Learn more at uc.edu.
UC is a mission-driven organization where we are committed to student success and positively transforming the community through scholarship and service. We thrive on innovation, making an impact, and fostering an environment where staff and faculty are key contributors to UC’s success.
The Department of Clinical and Health Information SciencesThe Department of Clinical and Health Information Sciences (CHIS) is one of the academic units in the College of Allied Health Sciences. The department offers undergraduate degrees in Medical Laboratory Science, Respiratory Therapy, and Advanced Medical Imaging Technology. The department also has four graduate programs in Medical Laboratory Sciences Leadership, Respiratory Therapy, Health Informatics, and the Doctor of Clinical Laboratory Science. The department is physically located in the Health Sciences building located on the UC Academic Health Center.
Job OverviewThe University of Cincinnati's Advanced Medical Imaging Technology Program is searching for a full-time Educator Track faculty member who will serve as the General Sonography Program Director. The faculty member will also contribute to the department's teaching, service, and scholarship goals. This is a 12-month position in a fully on-campus, in person program with the expectation that the faculty member will work the majority of the time on campus. Rank will be commensurate with education and experience. The preferred start date is January 2027.
Advanced Medical Imaging Technology ProgramThe Advanced Medical Imaging Technology program combines the needs of students, health care providers, the public, and the University to cultivate a program for preparing competent, credentialed medical imaging professionals. The UC AMIT Program offers a baccalaureate degree with multi-medical imaging technology credentials and single modality certificate pathways. The curriculum focuses on medical imaging modalities of nuclear medicine, magnetic resonance imaging, general sonography (beginning Fall 2027), and cardiovascular sonography (beginning Fall 2028). Graduates of this program will have obtained the level of didactic and clinical training necessary to meet eligibility requirements for national board examinations in their chosen modality/modalities. Baccalaureate seeking students also focus a portion of their curriculum on a capstone course series providing a bridge for career and academic advancement.
Essential Functions
This position is primarily responsible for teaching and service in the AMIT program Sonography track, the Clinical and Health Information Sciences Department and the College of Allied Health Sciences.
Teaching and service responsibilities include, but are not limited to, course development and curriculum assessment; primary instruction of didactic and laboratory courses, leadership with and mentoring of the clinical coordinator and adjunct faculty, student advising and mentoring, including culminating experiences services on program committees; and tasks as assigned by Department Chair.
The primary teaching responsibilities include courses within the AMIT Program as assigned. While teaching and service are central to this position, scholarship activities are also required with the mission of the program and the University.
As the Program Director, the duties will also include program directorship for the General Sonography accreditation that includes structure and daily program operations; the organization, administration, periodic review and evaluation, continued development, and effectiveness of the program curricula; and ensuring the effectiveness of all clinical affiliates.
The Program Director must also assist with program recruitment, retention, admissions, and academic advisement of current and prospective students.

Possess and maintain appropriate credential(s) specific to one or more of the sonography concentrations offered by the AMIT Program (abdominal and/or obstetrics/gynecologic sonography).
Three or more years of full-time clinical experience as a registered sonographer in the professional sonography field.
Two years of teaching experience as an adjunct instructor or one full year of full-time teaching at the college level in the didactic and/or clinical setting for a sonography program.
Documented experience in supervision, instruction, evaluation, student guidance in educational theories and techniques.
Eligibility for Sonography program director approval by the JRCDMS and CAAHEP accreditation agencies.
Additional Qualifications ConsideredMaster’s degree in education or a health-related field from a regionally accredited or nationally accredited academic institution.
Doctorate degree in education or health-related field from a regionally or nationally accredited academic institution.
Specific sonography credentials with abdominal and obstetrics/gynecology from the ARDMS and/or ARRT.
Prior experience as a Sonography Program Director.
Current knowledge and skill in the use of computer technology and educational learning systems.
Prior scholarly works published or presented.
Strong organizational skills; strong interpersonal skills, including communication, problem solving, counseling, conflict management, and follow-through.

Interest and ability to collaborate with an interdisciplinary team.
Excellent written and oral communication skills with the ability to present complex material to students unfamiliar with a subject.
Additional imaging credentials such as Echocardiography, vascular sonography, nuclear medicine or MRI.

Description:
Assistant or Associate Professor; nine-month tenure-track appointment beginning August 1, 2027. Salary and fringe benefits are competitive and commensurate with rank and experience.
The Knoxville campus of the University of Tennessee seeks candidates who have the ability to promote an atmosphere where all members of the university community feel welcome and can thrive.
The responsibilities of this faculty member include teaching bassoon to undergraduate and graduate students through applied lessons and studio classes, as well as teaching the bassoon component of the Double Reed Methods course within the music education curriculum. In addition, the faculty member will coach chamber ensembles and collaborate closely with the Woodwind Area on student recitals, hearings, proficiencies, juries, and the Woodwind Literature and Pedagogy course.
The successful candidate will be responsible for the effective recruitment of quality bassoon majors and high rates of student retention at the undergraduate and graduate level. The candidate will also collaborate closely with university band and orchestra directors to support placement, development, and performance of bassoon students within large ensembles.
Additionally, this faculty member will also provide leadership for the Natalie L. Haslam College of Music’s chamber music program by developing a sustainable organizational and curricular infrastructure that supports and advances chamber music throughout the College. Responsibilities will include coordinating chamber music activities across areas; working collaboratively with faculty; integrating community outreach and student recruitment initiatives through chamber music; and advancing innovative opportunities for cross-area collaboration, performances, residencies, and related programming.
The successful candidate will be highly organized and collaborative, possess significant experience in chamber music, and demonstrate proficiency and adaptability with administrative processes and technology. They will also bring the vision, initiative, and creativity necessary to develop an innovative, dynamic, and sustainable chamber music program that strengthens artistic collaboration, enriches the student experience, and expands the College’s engagement with its broader community.
The candidate will be expected to maintain a record of national and international creative/scholarly activity and provide service contributions appropriate for a university faculty member.

2) Evidence of successful teaching, recruitment and retention at the college/university level
3) Emerging or established national visibility as a performer as appropriate to rank
4) Ability to organize, communicate, and work effectively with faculty, students, and colleagues
5) Commitment to preparing versatile and innovative musicians for careers in the twenty-first century
6) Additional background or educational experience in chamber music.
Preferred Qualifications
1) Experience building, coordinating, or leading a chamber music program or comparable cross-area curricular initiative
2) Engagement with new music, including commissioning, premieres, or recording.
3) Experience with residencies, community outreach, or public programming built around chamber music.
Candidates for the rank of Assistant Professor must:
Meet the qualifications for being an Assistant Professor within UTK’s faculty handbook and the Natalie L. Haslam College of Music bylaws; these are covered in the above Required Qualifications.

jobs.description:
Job Details
Assistant / Associate Professor of Small Animal Primary Care
Location:
Knoxville, TN, United States
Open Date:
Sep 21, 2026
Description:
The Department of Small Animal Clinical Sciences of the University of Tennessee, College of Veterinary Medicine invites applications for a full-time clinical track faculty position in Small Animal Primary Care. The position is at the Clinical Assistant or Associate Professor level, depending on qualifications and experience.
The missions of the Department are to educate veterinary students and graduate veterinarians to meet the needs of the pet owning public, to provide advanced patient care, and to generate new knowledge in pet health through basic and applied research. Clinical track faculty at the University of Tennessee are expected to participate in teaching, service, and scholarship programs of the College. Responsibilities of the successful candidate will include clinical service and instruction in small animal primary care to DVM students and house officers, didactic program instruction within the preclinical curriculum, and collaboration in clinical discovery or scholarship.
The University of Tennessee Tickle Small Animal Hospital is a comprehensive and fully equipped facility with the expertise needed to provide advanced medical care. Specialty services supported by departmental faculty include: internal medicine, oncology, neurology, soft tissue and orthopedic surgery, dentistry, ophthalmology, dermatology, behavior, radiology, radiation oncology, anesthesiology, nutrition, physical therapy, shelter medicine, zoo, and exotic and avian medicine and surgery. The College also houses a nationally renowned Veterinary Social Work program. Facilities include: nuclear medicine, computerized tomography, MRI, radiation therapy, video endoscopy, laparoscopy, hyperbaric unit, and physical therapy. The hospital provides VECCS Level I emergency and critical care service 24 hours per day, 365 days a year.
The Primary Care clinic serves dogs and cats belonging to students, faculty, and staff of the University of Tennessee and is not open to the general public. Pets are seen primarily for wellness, illness, minor surgery, dentistry, and senior screening. The clinic will soon relocate to a newly constructed, full-service primary care clinic separate from the tertiary referral hospital. The successful candidate will join a collaborative service currently staffed by 3 faculty, 2 technicians, and 1 veterinary assistant. Primary care faculty are also committed to developing and supporting spectrum of care opportunities within our college and community.
The University of Tennessee College of Veterinary Medicine boasts a collegial environment committed to mentoring new faculty to be successful in their academic career. This includes a Master Teaching Program, which provides resources, programs and leadership to support the highest quality of professionalism and instruction within the various educational missions of the college and a Veterinary Social Work program that provides training and support in the areas of communication and conflict management, compassion fatigue, animal-related grief and bereavement, and mindfulness-based stress reduction. New faculty are assigned an experienced faculty mentor, and the Department has an excellent record in helping faculty successfully earn promotion and tenure.
The University of Tennessee is located in Knoxville Tennessee, a vibrant small city located between the Great Smoky Mountains and Cumberland plateau, an area with rich biodiversity and natural beauty. The Knoxville Urban Wilderness provides over 50 miles of trails and greenways within the city offering ample opportunity for outdoor recreation. Knoxville has an energetic cultural downtown area with excellent restaurants, bustling farmer’s markets, live music of all genres, ballet, theater, frequent art and cultural festivals, and men’s and women’s sporting events. The metropolitan areas of Nashville, Atlanta, Asheville, and Chattanooga are only a short drive away.
Qualifications:
Candidates must have a DVM or equivalent degree. All applicants should also have a minimum of 2 years clinical experience in companion animal medicine and/or have completed a small animal internship in medicine and surgery. The successful candidate will be proficient in teaching spay/neuter, minor surgery, and dental procedures. The ideal applicant will have clinical teaching experience as well as board certification or eligibility by an AVMA-recognized veterinary specialty organization.

jobs.description:
Forensic Pediatrics- CLINICAL ASSISTANT/ASSOCIATE PROFESSOR
Job No: 541383
Work Type: Full Time
Location: Jacksonville Campus
Categories: Education/Training/Instructional Design, Medicine/Physicians
Department: 30090000 - JX-PEDIATRICS-JACKSONVILLE
Job Description
Classification Title:
CLIN AST/ASO/FULL PROF
Minimum Requirements:
Applicants must possess a MD/DO degree and possess or be eligible for a Florida Medical License.
Job Description:
The Department of Pediatrics at the University of Florida College of Medicine – Jacksonville has an opening for a full-time position in the Division of Forensic Pediatrics and Child Protection. The position will be at the non-tenure accruing level of Assistant/Associate Professor and will assume the role of Medical Director of the University of Florida's Child Protection Team (CPT) and fellowship program. Major responsibilities will include directing the day-to-day clinical operation of the Child Protection Team, clinical care to victims of child abuse, and teaching of fellows, residents and medical students. Conducting community trainings on child abuse is also required.
The Director supervises the largest CPT in Florida, in what is an advanced statewide Child Protection Team system. This is a large busy clinical and academic team that includes 10 child abuse examiners of different disciplines, 23 case coordinators/interviewers, a supervising Team Coordinator to meaningfully manage contracts, reports, hiring and scheduling, a sexual abuse trauma therapy program, and focused senior CPT assistants working on death reviews and Death Review Teams for multiple counties. Services are provided at CPT Clinics as well as to area hospitals. Including Wolfson Children's Hospital (Level I Pediatric Trauma Center) and the University of Florida Health – Jacksonville (Level II Trauma Center).
This position will report to the Chief of the Division of Forensics and Chairman of the Department of Pediatrics at the University of Florida College of Medicine – Jacksonville. Following is a general description of duties and responsibilities:
Provide overall direction and supervision of the CPT team for program service delivery and administration.
Provide leadership in establishing an effective and coordinated response to Child Abuse Hotline reports with the designated area Department of Children and Families representatives. Participate and represent the team in the designated community service area as appropriate.
Provide advanced medical consultations and supervision, interfacing with 8 different county child protection agencies (Department of Children and Families), the medical examiners, and officers of the State Attorney.
Provide medical evaluations of children, and supervise and review the work of the provider agency's team medical practitioners for the provision of team medical evaluations of children suspected to be abused or neglected.
Arrange for and provide in-service training and other professional development for team staff and medical personnel. Assist the statewide CPT Medical Director in the planning and provision of training for regional and statewide training sessions.
Participate as a committee member (or appoint a medical designee) in the local Child Abuse Death Review (CADR) Committee.
Annually, plan and conduct a minimum of two training sessions in the detection of child abuse and neglect for area physicians and other medical staff, particularly those working in hospital emergency rooms.
Provide guidance and oversee the team's screening of child abuse reports made to the Florida Abuse Hotline, and provide selected direct screening as required by law, or when otherwise determined appropriate.
Be available 24 hours a day, seven days a week for consultation to team members and team physicians including telemedicine consultation, when available and appropriate, for medical assessment needs. Arrange coverage by another CMS approved CPT Medical Director when unavailable.
Assure medical representation for team staffing.
Participate in peer reviews with other team physicians and other medical providers. If designated and approved, participate in monitoring of child protection teams as a member of the statewide-designated monitoring team.
Attend statewide child protection team meetings and other meetings, and training sessions as required.
Provide medical consultation in an area of expertise to other teams when requested.
Provide depositions and expert court testimony when appropriate.
Provide teaching of fellows, residents and students.
About UF Health:
UF Health is the Southeast's premier academic health center and an integral part of the University of Florida. Our mission is to promote health through outstanding and high-quality patient care, innovative and rigorous education in the health professions and biomedical sciences, and research across the spectrum of basic, translational and clinical investigation. UF Health encompasses the Gainesville-based University of Florida colleges of Dentistry, Medicine, Nursing, Pharmacy, Public Health and Health Professions, and Veterinary Medicine; the UF Health Shands family of hospitals in Gainesville; UF Health Jacksonville medical center; UF Health North; an academic campus in Jacksonville that is home to the UF College of Medicine – Jacksonville and includes degree programs offered by the colleges of Nursing and Pharmacy; UF Health St. Johns in St. Augustine; UF Health Neighborhood Hospital in Ocala; and our campus in Central Florida, which includes UF Health Spanish Plaines Hospital and UF Health Leesburg Hospital. It also includes primary care and specialty practices throughout Central, North Central and northern Florida and Southeast Georgia. The UF Health network of hospitals and physician practices manages more than 3 million inpatient and outpatient visits each year, and serves patients from all 67 Florida counties, from across the nation and from dozens of countries around the world.
About College of Medicine – Jacksonville (COM-J):
The UF College of Medicine – Jacksonville is the largest of the three colleges at the Health Science Center Jacksonville. The college's 16 clinical science departments house more than 500 faculty members, 1,560 staff and 450 residents and fellows, as well as medical students from UF and around the country. We offer an incredible breadth of clinical training programs and proud to train many of best primary care providers and specialists throughout the region, the state and the country.
Research, discovery and innovation are critical aspects of our clinical campus and we have some of the country's leading researchers at our locations searching for and finding new treatments and clinical options.
The UF College of Medicine – Jacksonville faculty, administrators, residents, fellows, students and staff work as a team in pursuit of our common mission — to heal, to comfort, to educate and to discover through quality health care, elimination of health disparities, medical education, innovation and research.
To learn more about our college, leadership, mission, faculty resources, and the city of Jacksonville visit https://med.jax.ufl.edu/administrative-affairs/faculty-orientation-guide/.

Negotiable base on experience and academic appointment.
Preferred:
BE/BC Pediatrician

Job Details
Assistant Professor of Teaching in Youth Behavioral Health in the UCLA Department of Psychology
The UCLA Department of Psychology invites applications for a full-time Assistant Professor of Teaching who will contribute to the development and teaching of undergraduate courses in the newly established Youth Behavioral Health undergraduate minor. Additional undergraduate courses may be taught in the area of clinical psychology. We seek applicants who demonstrate excellence in teaching, including experience employing innovative and evidence-based methods in the classroom, engaging in reflective teaching practices, and pursuing ongoing efforts to improve their teaching. Additional responsibilities include: (1) coordinating with other instructional staff who contribute to the Youth Behavioral Health Minor (e.g., Teaching Assistants, Lecturers); (2) working with other faculty and community partners to develop and maintain appropriate internship placements; (3) overseeing matching and placements for undergraduate interns; (4) managing program curricula to align with established competency models and credentials; and (5) contributing to academic standards and admission criteria for the Youth Behavioral Health Minor. In addition, the successful candidate is expected to engage in scholarly/professional activities. These activities could include contributing to research on pedagogy or contributing to research in another area with the support of undergraduate students; developing, evaluating, and disseminating innovative teaching approaches; or maintaining clinical licensure and engaging in activities related to professional clinical practice.
The Assistant Professor of Teaching position is a full-time faculty position with potential security of employment akin to tenure. Those in the Professor of Teaching series are Academic Senate faculty members whose expertise and responsibilities center on undergraduate education and scholarly analysis/improvement of teaching methods. Faculty in the Professor of Teaching series are evaluated on their (1) teaching excellence, (2) professional and/or scholarly achievement and activity, and (3) university and public service. Potential applicants who have questions about the position can contact Prof. Steve S. Lee, search committee chair, at SearchCommittee@psych.ucla.edu.
The UCLA Department of Psychology is located within the Division of Life Sciences, part of the College of Letters and Science that serves undergraduate and graduate students. The search is geared toward candidates who share our belief that, as professors at a leading public university, we strive for inclusive excellence in teaching, service, research, and engagement with our academic community. We are eager to welcome an outstanding scholar and mentor who will create opportunities that will deepen and enrich understanding of psychological principles and perspectives for our students, while also contributing to the collaborative and supportive environment that characterizes our department. We are also interested in applicants who will advance UCLA's mission.
Applicants must hold a Ph.D. in Psychology or a closely related field awarded prior to the position start date. Applicants who hold or are willing to apply for clinical licensure in California are strongly preferred. This is an Assistant Professor of Teaching position; please do not apply if you are an Associate Professor or higher (or if you are undergoing review for tenure at your university, or anticipate a tenure review during our application process) as your application will not be considered. Applicants should demonstrate a record of expertise and teaching excellence in undergraduate courses relevant to clinical psychology. Preferred qualifications include professional experience developing or delivering BA-level youth behavioral health curricula in a university setting, a record of establishing and maintaining collaborative training relationships with youth-focused mental health organizations, experience with working successfully with field placements/practica, and coordinating training with required credentialing and licensing bodies. We also value candidates who have the potential to contribute to the mentoring and service missions of the department and university, particularly in regard to improving the quality of instruction. Applicants with experience mentoring and teaching students from groups affected by disparities in educational access are strongly encouraged to apply.
We seek applications from individuals with a demonstrated commitment to ensuring equal access to the benefits of their teaching and supporting the full participation of all students through consideration and appreciation of differences. The successful candidate will help foster authentic engagement and belonging within our diverse community. UCLA has scaled multiple initiatives such as Rising to the Challenge, Hispanic-Serving Institution initiative, and Native American/Pacific Islander Bruins Rising to promote inclusive excellence. UCLA is home to a diverse student body of approximately 47,000 undergraduate and graduate students and is ranked among the top national universities for social mobility. UCLA has programs to assist in partner employment, child care, schooling, and other family concerns. For additional information, visit the UCLA Academic Affairs and Personnel Office website (https://apo.ucla.edu/faculty-career-development/work-life-balance) or the UC Office of the President's website (https://www.ucop.edu/faculty-affairs-academic-programs/resources/family-friendly-practices-and-policies/family-friendly-policies-and-issues.html).

Applications should include a cover letter, curriculum vitae, contact information for three recommenders, a statement focused on UCLA's mission of no more than three pages, a statement of teaching philosophy of no more than three pages, and a teaching portfolio that includes syllabi, evaluations, and instructional materials used in courses previously taught. Letters of recommendation will be requested at a later date from applicants who progress to a later stage of review. To learn about the required UCLA mission statement, please see the job posting at https://recruit.apo.ucla.edu/JPF11325.
The posted UC salary scales (https://www.ucop.edu/academic-personnel-programs/compensation/index.html) set the minimum pay determined by rank and step at appointment. See Table 1. With this commitment as well as a commitment to addressing all forms of academic misconduct, UCLA conducts targeted employment reference checks for finalists to whom departments or other hiring units would like to extend formal offers of appointment into Academic Senate faculty positions.
