Job Title:Assistant/Associate/Professor in Astronomy
Department:Arts and Sciences | Astronomy
Open Tenure-Track Faculty Search
Department of Astronomy
College of Arts and Sciences
Position Overview
The Department of Astronomy in the College of Arts and Sciences at The Ohio State University invites applications for a tenure-track faculty member. Based in Columbus, Ohio, the position will begin in fall 2027 at the rank of Assistant Professor. In exceptional circumstances, appointments at the rank of Associate Professor or Professor will also be considered. This position is open to candidates with research focusing on any area of astrophysics including observations, theoretical astrophysics, and instrumentation. The successful candidate will work to advance the Department’s mission in research, teaching, and service. In particular, we seek candidates who will contribute to the Department’s highly collaborative and interactive environment, complement and expand existing research strengths, and leverage the Department’s resources to establish an exceptional research program.
Performance Objectives
Develop and maintain a sustained, productive, nationally or internationally recognized (depending on rank), and externally funded research program
Excel at teaching courses and mentoring students at both the undergraduate and graduate level
Contribute to the department’s mission as an active citizen through participation in the department’s interactive and collaborative scientific atmosphere, service on external and internal committees, and/or other administrative roles
Education and Experience Requirements
Required:
A PhD in Astronomy or a closely related field
Desired:
Clear evidence of research excellence as demonstrated by a record of published papers
A record that demonstrates a commitment to teaching and service and the potential for excellent department citizenship
Additional Information
Ohio State provides access to a depth and breadth of opportunities and resources. Starting your first day, Ohio State offers you a comprehensive benefits package.
How to Apply
To be considered, please submit your application electronically via Workday. Application closes 11/16/2026. Application materials must include:
Cover letter
Curriculum Vita (CV) and publication list
Statement of past, current, and planned research
Statement of teaching and mentoring interests, philosophy, and experience
The names and contact information of three references who have agreed to provide a letter of reference on your behalf
We strongly prefer that these be provided as a single PDF document with the elements given in the order listed above.
Additional Information:
The College
With more than 80 majors and 100 minors, the College of Arts and Sciences is the academic heart of the university. The Arts and Sciences provides extraordinary opportunities to collaborate across disciplines, blending creativity and analysis to truly be at the forefront of thought. The breadth and depth of knowledge in the college gives students and researchers the critical thinking and adaptability essential for a lifetime of success.
Department Information
The Department of Astronomy at The Ohio State University is a highly interactive and collaborative scientific environment, with one of the top astronomy graduate programs in the country, and with a vibrant undergraduate major program. Observational facilities include an approximately 1/5th share of the Large Binocular Telescope (LBT), a 25% share of the MDM Observatory, and membership in SDSS V, ASAS-SN, DESI, and other projects. The department has an active instrumentation laboratory and strong ties to the Ohio State Physics Department through the Center for Cosmology and AstroParticle Physics (CCAPP). Computational facilities include access to the Ohio Supercomputing Center, the Unity cluster in the College of Arts & Sciences, and local resources. Current research interests among the faculty include galaxy formation and evolution, active galactic nuclei, cosmology and large-scale structure, exoplanets, Galactic chemical evolution and Galactic structure, gravitational lensing, instrumentation, the interstellar and intergalactic medium, star formation and stellar feedback, atomic physics, stellar structure and evolution, supernovae, time domain astronomy, and theoretical astrophysics, among others.
The University
Ohio State is a top-20 public university, and its Ohio State Wexner Medical Center is one of America’s leading academic health centers. Eligible Ohio State employees receive comprehensive benefits packages, including medical, dental and vision insurance, tuition assistance for employees and their dependents, and state or alternative retirement options with competitive employer contributions.
Grounded in Ohio State University’s Shared Values, our university community welcomes differences, encourages open-minded exploration and courageous thinking, and upholds freedom of expression. Ohio State promotes a culture of work-life balance through institutionalized policies, programs, and resources that help faculty, staff, and their families thrive both professionally and personally.
Ohio State is a dynamic community where opportunity thrives, and individuals transform themselves and their world. Positions are available in countless fields and specialties. Become a Buckeye and contribute to an incredible legacy that serves to guide our future and shape a better tomorrow.
Located in Ohio’s capital city, Ohio State’s Columbus campus is near the center of a rapidly growing and vibrant metropolitan area with a population of over 1.5 million. The area offers a wide range of affordable housing, many cultural and recreational opportunities, excellent schools, and a strong economy based on government as well as service, transportation, and technology industries. Additional information about the Columbus area is available here. Beyond its Columbus campus, Ohio State has four regional campuses including Ohio State Lima, Ohio State Mansfield, Ohio State Marion, and Ohio State Newark, in addition to the College of Food, Agricultural, and Environmental Sciences (CFAES) Wooster Campus, which houses Ohio State ATI.

Job Title:Assistant Director for Community Outreach and Engagement- Faculty (Division of Cancer Prevention and Control)
Department:Medicine | IM Cancer Prevention and Control
Tenure faculty (regardless of rank) - persons with the titles of professor, associate professor, assistant professor and instructor who serve on appointments totaling 50% or more service to the university and who are eligible for tenure or who have obtained tenure. Duties and responsibilities are assigned in accordance with the workload guidelines laid out in the pattern of administration of each faculty member’s tenure initiation unit (TIU) and, as appropriate, regional campus; obligations will include research, service and/or teaching or clinical practice. These faculty will have earned doctorate or other terminal degree in the relevant field of study or possession of equivalent experience.
Additional Information:
The Center for Community Outreach and Engagement
The Ohio State University Comprehensive Cancer Center – Arthur G. James Cancer Hospital and Richard J. Solove Research Institute is committed to reducing the burden of cancer across Ohio through meaningful partnerships with communities, health systems, public health agencies, advocacy organizations, and policymakers. As part of the Cancer Center Support Grant (CCSG) requirements established by the National Cancer Institute, the Center for Community Outreach and Engagement (COE) serves as the bridge between cancer center research and the communities it serves, ensuring that community needs, priorities, and perspectives inform cancer research, clinical trials, education, and cancer control efforts.
The COE Center works to ensure bi-directional engagement between the cancer center and diverse populations across Ohio, with particular emphasis on rural, Appalachian, underserved, and historically marginalized communities. Through partnerships, research translation, dissemination, implementation, and policy engagement, the Center advances equitable access to cancer prevention, screening, treatment, survivorship, and clinical trials.
The Center also plays a critical role in supporting cancer center priorities related to catchment area assessment, health equity, community-engaged research, clinical trial participation, dissemination and implementation science, workforce development, and population health improvement.
Position Overview
The Center for Community Outreach and Engagement seeks an accomplished scholar and leader to serve as Assistant Director for Community Outreach and Engagement.
The Assistant Director will work closely with the COE Founding Director, Cancer Center leadership, research programs, shared resources, faculty investigators, community stakeholders, and health system partners to advance the cancer center's community-engaged mission and CCSG priorities.
This position is designed for a nationally recognized faculty member with expertise in community-engaged research, implementation science, cancer prevention and control, health equity, population health, healthcare delivery, rural health, disparities research, or related fields.
The Assistant Director will provide scientific and strategic leadership for community engagement activities, facilitate integration of community priorities into cancer center research programs, strengthen partnerships throughout Ohio, and develop innovative approaches to reducing cancer disparities across the cancer control continuum.
The successful candidate will maintain an active funded research portfolio while helping lead the cancer center's efforts to demonstrate meaningful impact on cancer outcomes within its catchment area.
Primary Responsibilities
Community Outreach and Engagement
Partner with the Founding Director to develop and execute the strategic vision for Community Outreach and Engagement.
Support implementation of COE goals aligned with Cancer Center Support Grant requirements.
Assist in developing infrastructure that supports meaningful bi-directional engagement between communities and researchers.
Promote integration of community priorities into cancer center planning and research activities.
Serve as a representative of the cancer center in statewide and national community engagement efforts when Founding Director is not available.
Community Partnerships and Stakeholder Engagement
Build and maintain relationships with:
Healthcare systems
Advocacy groups
Schools and universities
Government agencies
Employer organizations
Patient and survivor groups
Support development and management of Community Advisory Boards and COE stakeholder councils.
Promote community trust and long-term partnership development.
Community-Engaged Research
Foster meaningful collaborations between researchers and community stakeholders.
Promote utilization of community-engaged and participatory research approaches.
Facilitate partnerships that address community-identified cancer priorities.
Support incorporation of community perspectives into research design, implementation, and dissemination.
Expand opportunities for community participation in cancer research and clinical trials.
Secondary Responsibilities
Catchment Area and Cancer Burden Assessment
Utilize community input, population data, and stakeholder feedback to develop strategies targeting areas with the greatest cancer burden.
Support translation of catchment area data into actionable research priorities and community interventions.
Cancer Health Equity and Disparities Reduction
Support initiatives aimed at reducing disparities in cancer prevention, screening, diagnosis, treatment, clinical trial participation, and survivorship.
Support strategies that improve outcomes among rural, Appalachian, minority, underserved, and medically vulnerable populations.
Promote culturally responsive and community-informed interventions.
Collaborate with healthcare systems and community partners to address social determinants of health impacting cancer outcomes.
Education and Workforce Development
Develop educational opportunities related to:
Community-engaged research
Health equity
Cancer control
Dissemination and implementation science
Required Qualifications
PhD, DrPH, MD, DO, DNP, PharmD, PsyD, or other terminal degree in public health, behavioral science, implementation science, epidemiology, health services research, social sciences, medicine, nursing, or a related field.
Eligible for appointment at the rank of Associate Professor or Professor.
Nationally recognized record of scholarship in community-engaged research, cancer prevention and control, health equity, implementation science, population health, or related disciplines.
Record of extramural funding as Principal Investigator or Multi-Principal Investigator.
Experience working with community organizations and diverse populations.
Experience leading multi-sector partnerships and collaborative research initiatives.
Strong communication, leadership, and relationship-building skills.
Desired Qualifications
Experience serving within a Cancer Center Support Grant (CCSG) Community Outreach and Engagement program.
Experience contributing to NCI-designated comprehensive cancer center initiatives.
Expertise in:
Community-based participatory research
Dissemination and implementation science
Cancer disparities research
Rural health
Population health
Clinical trial accrual
Health equity
Community intervention research
Stakeholder-engaged research
Experience conducting statewide or multi-state outreach initiatives.
Experience leading Community Advisory Boards and stakeholder engagement programs.
Demonstrated success translating research findings into policy and practice.
Experience mentoring faculty and trainees engaged in community-based research.
Opportunities and Resources
The Assistant Director will join a rapidly growing Community Outreach and Engagement enterprise embedded within one of the nation's leading comprehensive cancer centers. The position offers opportunities to collaborate with experts in cancer prevention, implementation science, epidemiology, survivorship, behavioral science, health services research, biostatistics, rural health, and population health.
The Assistant Director will have access to extensive statewide partnerships, community networks, data resources, and institutional support necessary to advance innovative and impactful community-engaged research programs.
Vision for the Role
The Assistant Director will serve as a key scientific leader advancing the cancer center's commitment to community engagement, health equity, and population impact. Through innovative scholarship, authentic partnerships, and strategic leadership, the Assistant Director will help ensure that the voices, needs, and priorities of Ohio communities drive cancer research and cancer control efforts while accelerating progress toward reducing the burden of cancer for all populations.
How to Apply
All inquiries and nominations should be directed in confidence to: Anna Godwin, Research Faculty Recruiter, Anna.Godwin@osumc.edu
Faculty Defined
Clinical faculty (regardless of rank) - Persons with titles of assistant professor-clinical, associate professor-clinical and professor-clinical. These faculty will have earned a Doctor of Medicine (MD), Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine (DO), doctorate (PhD) or other terminal degree in the relevant field. Clinical faculty members are not eligible for tenure and are appointed for terms of three to five years. They may be reappointed to successive terms. Their principal career focus is the delivery of exemplary clinical care, and may include teaching, and/or research.
Tenure-Track faculty (regardless of rank) - Persons with the titles of assistant professor, associate professor, or professor who are eligible for tenure or who have obtained tenure. These faculty will have earned a doctorate (PhD), Doctor of Medicine (MD), Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine (DO) or other terminal degree in the relevant field of study. Their primary career focus centers on research, service, and teaching. Tenure-track faculty with MD, DO or MD/PhD degrees may also be involved in clinical care.
Research Faculty (regardless of rank) - Persons with the titles of research assistant professor, research associate professor, or research professor. These faculty will have earned a doctorate (PhD) or other terminal degree in the relevant field of study. Research faculty members are not eligible for tenure and are appointed for terms of one to five years. Their principal career focus is research.
The Ohio State University College of Medicine
The Ohio State University College of Medicine, with more than 5,000 learners, is the only academic medical center in central Ohio. Recognized as a Tier 1 school for research in the 2025–2026 U.S. News & World Report “Best Medical Schools” list, it ranks among the top 16 medical schools for research in the nation. It also remains in Tier 2 for primary care, further demonstrating its strength across the academic spectrum. Known for its innovative curriculum, cutting-edge research, and excellence in clinical care through The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center, the college continues to advance its mission of education, discovery and community impact. With more than 2,700 faculty across 20 clinical departments, eight basic science departments, and the School of Health and Rehabilitation Sciences, Ohio State is shaping the future of academic medicine - locally, nationally and globally.
The Wexner Medical Center
The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center consists of The Ohio State University Health System, the College of Medicine, the Health Sciences Library and the Faculty Group Practice. The Ohio State Wexner Medical Center is committed to providing world-class care. At the Ohio State Wexner Medical Center, we're proud to be celebrating our 33rd consecutive year ranked in the U.S. News & World Report Best Hospitals list. This year, the Ohio State Wexner Medical Center has 9 nationally ranked specialties out of 15 and four selected as high performing. U.S. News & World Report consistently ranks the Ohio State Wexner Medical Center as the top hospital in Columbus. The Wexner Medical Center is rated as high performing in 17 out of 22 common procedures and conditions, including abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, aortic valve surgery, arrhythmia, COPD, colon cancer surgery, diabetes, gynecological cancer surgery, heart attack, heart failure, kidney failure, leukemia, lymphoma and myeloma, lung cancer surgery, pacemaker implantation, pneumonia, prostate cancer, spinal fusion, and transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
Our new hospital tower, opened in February, 2026, is the largest single facilities project ever undertaken at Ohio State. It’s designed to enhance a unified Ohio State Wexner Medical Center campus providing world-class patient care, leading-edge research and outstanding clinical training.

The Department of Kinesiology, Nutrition, and Health seeks a teacher- scholar in Exercise Science who will contribute to the department's undergraduate and graduate programs through high-quality teaching, an active program of research, and student mentorship. The successful candidate will bring expertise in exercise physiology and related areas that complements existing departmental strengths and supports the preparation of students for clinical, professional, and graduate careers. Responsibilities include teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in Exercise Physiology, Clinical Exercise Testing and Prescription, Research Methods, Experiential Learning/Capstone, and related kinesiology courses; establishing and maintaining an active research program; pursuing
external funding; advising and mentoring students; and engaging in service at the departmental, college, University, and professional discipline levels. This is a full-time, tenure-track, on-campus position that requires regular campus presence and active engagement with students. The appointment is expected to begin in August 2027.
Minimum Qualifications
Ph.D. in Exercise Physiology, Exercise Science, Kinesiology, or a related discipline by the date of appointment.
Consideration may be given to candidates with:
Experience teaching undergraduate and/or graduate courses in Exercise Physiology, Clinical Exercise Testing and Prescription, research Methods, and Experiential Learning/Capstone.
Postdoctoral research experience.
Professional certification through the American College of Sports Medicine (e.g., ACSM-EP, ACSM-CEP), the National Strength and Conditioning Association (e.g., CSCS), or another nationally recognized exercise science organization.
Evidence of collaborative scholarship or interdisciplinary research.
Experience working with students from diverse backgrounds and fostering an inclusive learning environment.
Department of Kinesiology, Nutrition, and Health
The Department of Kinesiology, Nutrition, and Health is one of the largest in the College of Education, Health, and Society, with sustained enrollment growth and strong student demand. The department is committed to excellence in teaching, research, and student mentorship while preparing graduates for clinical, professional, and graduate careers. We value the breadth of the kinesiology discipline and seek a faculty member whose expertise in Motor Behavior will strengthen our curriculum, expand collaborative scholarship, and contribute to the continued growth of the department.
Faculty in the department maintain active research programs across motor behavior, biomechanics, exercise physiology, nutrition, athletic training, health behavior, and related disciplines. The successful candidate will have access to well-equipped research facilities supporting human movement and performance research, including motion capture and biomechanical analysis systems, force platforms, body composition assessment, ultrasound imaging, exercise physiology laboratories, and other human performance testing resources.
Research Environment
The Department of Kinesiology, Nutrition, and Health (KNH) offers a sophisticated, translational research infrastructure specifically designed to support high-impact Exercise Physiology. Our shared laboratory network facilitates seamless investigation across the physiological spectrum-from molecular pathways to systemic cardiometabolic and performance outcomes-providing an ideal environment for mechanistic, clinical, and applied research.
Core Research Infrastructure:
Human Integrative Physiology & Metabolism: Advanced capabilities for cardiometabolic phenotyping, including gold-standard indirect calorimetry (ParvoMedics TrueOne 2400), comprehensive body composition analysis (DEXA, InBody 770, ultrasound), and resting/exercise metabolic testing.
Vascular Physiology: Specialized infrastructure for hemodynamic assessment, featuring flow-mediated dilation, arterial stiffness analysis, microneurography, and continuous glucose monitoring to characterize vascular health.
Applied Exercise Testing: A large-capacity, adaptable space for clinical and physiological trials equipped with multiple treadmill and cycle ergometers, ECG systems, and on-site clinical chemistry diagnostics.
Molecular & Tissue Bioscience: A collaborative facility that integrates whole-body physiological data with cellular-level analysis, utilizing gene expression profiling (RT-PCR), histology, protein detection, and skeletal muscle tissue processing.
Pre-Clinical Opportunities: Use of the Laboratory Animal Resource (LAR) to conduct experimental physical activity and inactivity studies with rodents utilizing metabolic, behavioral, and functional phenotyping.
This integrated environment fosters a highly collaborative culture, providing faculty the flexibility to execute translational research and offer meaningful, hands-on training to undergraduate and graduate students.
The College of Education, Health and Society:
The vision of the College of Education, Health, and Society is to foster critically engaged leaders prepared to take on complex and interdisciplinary challenges through transdisciplinary problem-solving that seeks equity and justice in our changing global society. The College embraces the rich opportunities available for cross-disciplinary collaboration across its six departments (Educational Leadership; Educational Psychology; Family Science and Social Work; Kinesiology, Nutrition, and Health; Sport Leadership and Management; and Teaching, Curriculum, and Educational Inquiry).
Miami University
Established in 1809, Miami University consistently ranks among the top national public universities for providing students with a superior education and exceptional value. Miami is located in the quintessential college town of Oxford, Ohio, with polytechnic campuses in Hamilton and Middletown, a learning center in West Chester, a European study center in Luxembourg, and a 100% virtual option in Miami Online. A comprehensive research university, Miami empowers students to engage with premiere teacher-scholars and benefit from a well-rounded liberal arts foundation and vibrant campus experience to develop lifelong skills for any career. With more than 240,000 high-achieving alumni, students gain access to an extensive and supportive community that opens doors globally and leads to amazing outcomes. With an ambition to effect meaningful change, Miami delivers the resources and experiences that prepare graduates to learn with purpose and lead with courage.

Consideration may be given to candidates with: 1) evidence of high-quality instruction; and 2) experience teaching sport management courses at the college level including, but not limited to, classes such as Sport Marketing, Sport Administration, Facilities and Event Management, Sport Ethics, or Sport Analytics.
Sport Leadership and Management (SLAM) is a growing department serving 800+ undergraduate students (majors and minors) and 45+ graduate students. The mission of SLAM is to prepare students to succeed in leadership positions in the sport industry by providing them with knowledge and skills to critically analyze and innovatively engage in the business and culture of sport. The SLAM has three undergraduate majors designed to prepare students for specific career opportunities in Sport Management, Sport Coaching, Sport Communication and Media. SLAM students often double major or minor in management, marketing, or entrepreneurship in the Farmer School of Business, a nationally ranked top-25 undergraduate business program.
The mission of the College of Education, Health, and Society at Miami University is to prepare transformative leaders. Through excellence in teaching, scholarship, and community partnerships, the college provides dynamic and innovative programs that encourage international perspectives. Our integrated human experience prepares graduates to generate knowledge, educate, serve, and promote well-being in diverse and global settings through ethical, democratic practices. Faculty members work in an environment that promotes a holistic approach to both teaching and research. They are encouraged to align their teaching, scholarship, and service in an interdisciplinary fashion in order to promote aggressive solutions to the issues faced by our society. The College of Education, Health, and Society seeks out opportunities for cross-departmental collaboration facilitated by the six departments in our division (Educational Leadership, Educational Psychology, Family Science and Social Work, Kinesiology, Nutrition, and Health, Sport Leadership & Management and Teaching, Curriculum, and Educational Inquiry). It is our belief that the synergy from this comprehensive approach creates the kind of integrated human experience that is essential to excellence in research and teaching.
Established in 1809, Miami University consistently ranks among the top national public universities for providing students with a superior education and exceptional value. Miami is located in the quintessential college town of Oxford, Ohio, with polytechnic campuses in Hamilton and Middletown, a learning center in West Chester, a European study center in Luxembourg, and a 100% virtual option in Miami Online. A comprehensive research university, Miami empowers students to engage with premiere teacher-scholars and benefit from a well-rounded liberal arts foundation and vibrant campus experience to develop lifelong skills for any career. With more than 240,000 high-achieving alumni, students gain access to an extensive and supportive community that opens doors globally and leads to amazing outcomes. With an ambition to effect meaningful change, Miami delivers the resources and experiences that prepare graduates to learn with purpose and lead with courage.

The successful candidate will bring expertise in Motor Control, Motor Learning, and related areas that strengthens the breadth of the kinesiology curriculum, complements existing departmental strengths, and supports collaborative scholarship. The faculty member will be expected to contribute to a collaborative academic environment and participate actively in the teaching, research, and service missions of the department.
Responsibilities include teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in Motor Control, Motor Learning, Biomechanics, and related kinesiology courses; establishing and maintaining an active research program; pursuing external funding; advising and mentoring students; and engaging in service at the departmental, college, University, and professional discipline levels. This is a full-time, tenure-track, on-campus position that requires regular campus presence and active engagement with students. The appointment is expected to begin in August 2027.
Job Description
The Department of Kinesiology, Nutrition, and Health seeks a teacher-scholar in Motor Behavior who will contribute to the department's undergraduate and graduate programs through high-quality teaching, an active program of research, and student mentorship. The successful candidate will bring expertise in Motor Control, Motor Learning, and related areas that strengthens the breadth of the kinesiology curriculum, complements existing departmental strengths, and supports collaborative scholarship. The faculty member will be expected to contribute to a collaborative academic environment and participate actively in the teaching, research, and service missions of the department.
Responsibilities include teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in Motor Control, Motor Learning, Biomechanics, and related kinesiology courses; establishing and maintaining an active research program; pursuing external funding; advising and mentoring students; and engaging in service at the departmental, college, University, and professional discipline levels. This is a full-time, tenure-track, on-campus position that requires regular campus presence and active engagement with students. The appointment is expected to begin in August 2027.
Minimum Qualifications
Assistant professor: Ph.D. by the date of appointment in Motor Behavior, Motor Control, Motor Learning, Human Movement Science, Motor Neuroscience, Kinesiology, or a closely related discipline. Associate Professor: Ph.D. in Motor Behavior, Motor Control, Motor Learning, Human Movement Science, Motor Neuroscience, Kinesiology, or a closely related discipline, and evidence of an established, externally funded research program, excellence in teaching, and a record of service commensurate with rank.
Consideration may be given to candidates with:
Experience teaching undergraduate and/or graduate courses in Motor Control and Motor Learning.
Ability to teach biomechanics courses at the undergraduate and graduate level
Postdoctoral research experience.
Demonstrated potential to establish and sustain an externally funded research program.
Evidence of collaborative scholarship or interdisciplinary research.
Experience working with students from diverse backgrounds and fostering an inclusive learning environment.
Department of Kinesiology, Nutrition, and Health
The Department of Kinesiology, Nutrition, and Health is one of the largest in the College of Education, Health, and Society, with sustained enrollment growth and strong student demand. The department is committed to excellence in teaching, research, and student mentorship while preparing graduates for clinical, professional, and graduate careers. We value the breadth of the kinesiology discipline and seek a faculty member whose expertise in Motor Behavior will strengthen our curriculum, expand collaborative scholarship, and contribute to the continued growth of the department.
Faculty in the department maintain active research programs across motor behavior, biomechanics, exercise physiology, nutrition, athletic training, health behavior, and related disciplines. The successful candidate will have access to well-equipped research facilities supporting human movement and performance research, including motion capture and biomechanical analysis systems, force platforms, body composition assessment, ultrasound imaging, exercise physiology laboratories, and other human performance testing resources.
Research Environment
The Department of Kinesiology, Nutrition, and Health (KNH) provides a collaborative research environment that supports innovative scholarship in motor behavior across basic, translational, and applied settings. Faculty maintain active research programs spanning motor behavior, biomechanics, exercise physiology, athletic training, nutrition, and health behavior, creating numerous opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration. The departments shared laboratory infrastructure supports research examining human movement from neural control and skill acquisition to biomechanics, rehabilitation, and performance.
Core Research Infrastructure:
Human Movement Analysis: State-of-the-art motion capture systems, force platforms, wireless electromyography (EMG), and high-speed video analysis support investigations of movement coordination, motor control, gait, balance, and neuromechanics.
Motor Performance & Human Function: Flexible laboratory space equipped for studies of motor learning, functional movement, postural control, balance assessment, exercise interventions, and human performance across the lifespan and in clinical populations.
Integrative Human Physiology: Shared access to advanced exercise physiology laboratories, including metabolic testing (ParvoMedics TrueOne 2400), body composition assessment (DEXA, InBody 770, ultrasound), cardiovascular assessment, and exercise testing, facilitating multidisciplinary research that integrates motor behavior with physiological outcomes.
Collaborative Research Environment: Faculty have opportunities to collaborate across multiple areas of expertise, including biomechanics, exercise physiology, athletic training, nutrition, and neuroscience, while mentoring undergraduate and graduate students in hands-on research. The department supports externally funded scholarship through shared laboratory resources, a collaborative research culture, and access to a diverse participant population.
The College of Education, Health and Society:
The vision of the College of Education, Health, and Society is to foster critically engaged leaders prepared to take on complex and interdisciplinary challenges through transdisciplinary problem-solving that seeks equity and justice in our changing global society. The College embraces the rich opportunities available for cross-disciplinary collaboration across its six departments (Educational Leadership; Educational Psychology; Family Science and Social Work; Kinesiology, Nutrition, and Health; Sport Leadership and Management; and Teaching, Curriculum, and Educational Inquiry).
Miami University
Established in 1809, Miami University consistently ranks among the top national public universities for providing students with a superior education and exceptional value. Miami is located in the quintessential college town of Oxford, Ohio, with polytechnic campuses in Hamilton and Middletown, a learning center in West Chester, a European study center in Luxembourg, and a 100% virtual option in Miami Online. A comprehensive research university, Miami empowers students to engage with premiere teacher-scholars and benefit from a well-rounded liberal arts foundation and vibrant campus experience to develop lifelong skills for any career. With more than 240,000 high-achieving alumni, students gain access to an extensive and supportive community that opens doors globally and leads to amazing outcomes. With an ambition to effect meaningful change, Miami delivers the resources and experiences that prepare graduates to learn with purpose and lead with courage.

Job Details
Faculty Positions in the Division of Addiction Medicine
Location: Philadelphia, PA
Open Date: Sep 24, 2026
Deadline: Sep 24, 2028 at 11:59 PM Eastern Time
The Division of Addiction Medicine within the Department of Family Medicine and Community Health at the Perelman School of Medicine at the University of Pennsylvania seeks candidates for multiple faculty positions in Addiction Medicine in the non-tenure Academic Clinician (AC) track. Successful candidates will hold an M.D. or D.O. degree and must have primary board in a recognized ABMS or AOA Specialty and must be board certified in Addiction Medicine. They should have experience in hospital-based addiction medicine consultation and in underserved and vulnerable patient care and an interest in a career in academic medicine. Preferred candidates will have completion of an Addiction Medicine fellowship; experience in inpatient consultation services; experience caring for patients with opioid use disorder and other substance use disorders; experience working in Bridge/OTP or low-barrier treatment programs.
Teaching responsibilities may include participation in the education and supervision of residents, fellows, and medical students in inpatient, consultative, ambulatory, and Bridge/OTP settings. Opportunities for educational leadership and program development may be available for the right candidate.
Clinical responsibilities may include clinical care based primarily at Pennsylvania Hospital, Penn Presbyterian Medical Center, Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania, HUP Cedar, Bridge/Opioid Treatment Services (OTP) services, and other Penn Medicine-affiliated clinical settings. Faculty may participate in ambulatory addiction medicine, Bridge/OTP services, treatment of opioid and other substance use disorders, hospital-based addiction treatment, community-based addiction services, resident and fellow supervision, and multidisciplinary care coordination. All faculty members will devote a portion of their clinical effort to inpatient Addiction Medicine consult services at one or more Penn Medicine hospitals, including Pennsylvania Hospital, Penn Presbyterian Medical Center, the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania, and HUP Cedar.
The Division of Addiction Medicine is recruiting for three full-time faculty positions that will support Penn Medicine's growing addiction medicine clinical, educational, and community programs. These positions offer flexibility in clinical practice location and scope while supporting access to evidence-based addiction treatment across Penn Medicine.
The Division of Addiction Medicine serves diverse patients across Philadelphia, including many individuals and communities that have historically experienced barriers to health care access and health equity. Assistant Professor of Communication
Job ID: 303684
Location: Kennesaw, Georgia
Full/Part Time: Full Time
Regular/Temporary: Regular
About Us
For more than 60 years, Kennesaw State University has been known for its entrepreneurial spirit and sense of community. A leader in innovative teaching and learning, Kennesaw State is located just north of Atlanta and combines a suburban setting on two metro-Atlanta campuses in Kennesaw and Marietta. As one of Georgia's largest universities, Kennesaw State offers undergraduate and graduate degrees to over 50,000 students. Our high-impact research and Division I athletics also draw students from throughout the region and across the globe. A member of the University System of Georgia, Kennesaw State is a Carnegie-designated doctoral research institution (R2) committed to becoming a world-class academic institution positioned to broaden its academic and research missions and expand its scope on a local, regional, and national level.
Our university's vibrant culture, career opportunities, rich benefits, and values of respect, integrity, collaboration, inclusivity, and accountability make us an employer of choice. As part of the University System of Georgia, Kennesaw State exemplifies the power and promise of a student-centered, research-driven university. In addition, Kennesaw State supports the University of Georgia's core values of accountability, excellence, integrity, and respect. We are searching for talented people to join Kennesaw State University in our vision. For more information, visit the Kennesaw State University website.
Location
Our Kennesaw campus is located at 1000 Chastain Road NW, Kennesaw, GA 30144. Our Marietta campus is located at 1100 South Marietta Parkway, Marietta, GA 30060.
Department Information
The School of Communication & Media prepares ethical, mindful, and effective communicators who combine human skills and technical expertise to pursue fulfilling careers, lead in their communities, tell impactful stories, and grow strong relationships. We blend industry-relevant programs with forward-thinking scholarship to build understanding of the power of communication to innovate, connect, and create.
With more than 400 full-time faculty and 8,100 degree-seeking students, the Norman J. Radow College of Humanities & Social Sciences is dedicated to pioneering workforce readiness in the humanities and social sciences. By staying true to our Liberal Arts values and integrating practical knowledge and experiential learning into our curriculum, we empower our students to become responsible citizens ready for the demands of the modern workplace. The home of three schools and eight departments, the College offers more than 80 graduate and undergraduate programs of study in both traditional and interdisciplinary fields. These programs enable students to develop leadership, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills, as well as a strong sense of civic engagement.
The College is committed to the success of our students, faculty, staff and communities. We seek candidates whose experience has prepared them to fulfill that commitment and engage our students, partners, and stakeholders effectively.
Job Summary
Kennesaw State University is now accepting applications for a full-time, tenure track faculty position as Assistant Professor of Communication in the School of Communication and Media with a preferred start date of August 2027. This is a nine-month contracted position and is for work to be performed in the state of Georgia.
Responsibilities
Teach required and elective courses across the School of Communication and Media, with primary responsibilities supporting the Journalism and Emerging Media program and supplemental teaching in the Media and Entertainment program. Potential courses include Digital Media Production, Uses and Effects of Mass Media, Data Journalism, Investigative Reporting, Narrative Journalism and Fundamentals of Digital Journalism.
Develop and integrate courses in artificial intelligence and data visualization that enhance our offerings to students in the School of Communication and Media.
Teach on the Kennesaw and/or Marietta campuses, as assigned. Courses may be delivered in face-to-face, hybrid and online formats.
Teach courses of various sizes, ranging from lab skills courses in journalism to large lectures in foundations and introductory courses.
Maintain an active program of research or creative scholarship in artificial intelligence and data visualization as it relates to the field of Communication consistent with the expectations of a tenure-track faculty appointment.
Disseminate research and scholarship in appropriate, high-quality outlets.
Proactively seek external funding to support research and creative scholarship consistent with the expectations of a tenure-track faculty appointment.
Contribute expertise in data visualization and artificial intelligence to curriculum development involving the practical, critical, ethical and professional implications of emerging technologies.
Contribute service to the School, College, University and profession and collaborate with colleagues in a multidisciplinary School of Communication and Media.
Contribute, as appropriate, to professional development opportunities for students and communication professionals, community partnerships and interdisciplinary projects within the College.
Opportunities to teach graduate courses may also be available.
Teaching assignments will be based on earned degrees and SACSCOC Faculty Credentials Guidelines.
Required Qualifications
A terminal degree, or the foreign equivalent, in communication, mass communication, journalism, digital media or a closely related discipline is required at the time of hire.
Demonstrated expertise in the application of artificial intelligence to journalism, media production or other communication fields.
Documented teaching, course-development or professional experience demonstrating preparation to teach courses related to application of data visualization and artificial intelligence to communication and media professions.
Documented scholarly or creative activity demonstrating the potential to maintain an active program of research or creative scholarship.
Documented experience or training relevant to face-to-face, hybrid and online instruction, such as prior teaching, course design or formal instructional training.
Preferred Qualifications
Documented teaching, course-development or professional experience demonstrating preparation to teach courses related to digital media, journalism or media production.
Active record of quality dissemination of research in artificial intelligence and data visualization in communication and mass communication fields.
Experience in seeking external funding to support research and creative production in fields of expertise.
At least two years of professional experience in digital or broadcast media production.
Experience with data journalism, data visualization, computational methods, creative artificial intelligence, sports media production or related areas.
Evidence of excellence in teaching and student engagement, as demonstrated by teaching evaluations, peer observations, teaching awards, instructional materials or similar evidence.
Experience contributing to curriculum development involving emerging technologies and their practical, ethical and professional implications.
Required Documents to Attach
CV documenting educational background, teaching experience, research or creative scholarship and relevant professional experience
Cover Letter addressing qualifications for the position, including relevant teaching or professional experience and the applicant's research or creative scholarship agenda.
Unofficial Transcripts (Official Transcripts and Official International Course-by-Course Evaluations Due Upon Hire)
Names, phone numbers, and email addresses of at least 3 references.
Teaching Philosophy
Research Interest (A 2-page statement of research interest that breaks down your anticipated research agenda in a tenure-track role at Kennesaw State.)
Evidence of Teaching Effectiveness (A 2-page white paper that summarizes teaching evaluations, certifications that support more effective teaching, and other efforts to enhance what you bring to the classroom.) Upload as Additional Documents
Incomplete applications will not be considered.
Apply Before Date
Review of applications will begin immediately. For full consideration, please apply by October 26, 2026.
Contact Information
For questions about this faculty opening, please contact Farooq Kperogi, Ph.D., fkperogi@kennesaw.edu.
For technical support or assistance completing a job application, please contact the Shared Services Center at (877) 251-2644 or support@usg.edu.
For questions about a specific job posting at Kennesaw State University, please contact the search chair listed under the contact information section on each posting. For general questions about faculty jobs please email facultyjobs@kennesaw.edu.
USG Core Values
The University System of Georgia is comprised of our 25 institutions of higher education and learning as well as the System Office. Our USG Statement of Core Values are Integrity, Excellence, Accountability, and Respect. These values serve as the foundation for all that we do as an organization, and each USG community member is responsible for demonstrating and upholding these standards. jobs.description:
Description
Position Overview:
The University of Washington Tacoma’s School of Education announces an opening for a nine-month full-time, 100% FTE, tenure-track Assistant Professor in Special Education: Specialization in Critical Disability Studies. We seek applicants who demonstrate commitment to excellence in teaching and service in a diverse and inclusive academic community. This is a full-time (100% FTE) faculty position with an expected start date of September 16, 2027. The initial appointment will be for a three-year term, eligible for reappointment after successful academic review. The successful candidate will be expected to teach and mentor students from varying backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences
Compensation:
The base salary range for this position will be $9,619 to $10,004 per month ($86,571 to $90,036 per 9-month academic year), commensurate with experience and qualifications, or as mandated by a U.S. Department of Labor prevailing wage determination. Additional compensation affiliated with this recruitment may include a one-time relocation allowance and/or start up professional funds, if applicable. A summary of benefits associated with this title/rank can be found at https://hr.uw.edu/benefits/.
Position Description:
All University of Washington faculty are expected to engage in teaching, research, and service. The successful candidate will be expected to perform highly effective and inclusive teaching, using a variety of pedagogical techniques and technologies, in an urban-serving campus environment. Faculty at UWT are expected to teach in multiple modalities, including in-person, online, and hybrid courses.
The expected teaching load for this position is set at a level equivalent to six (6) standard courses per academic year. The successful candidate will be expected to teach in one or more of the following subject areas: special education; critical disability studies; reading and literacy; assessment; inclusion pedagogies; social emotional learning; behavioral development and supports; multi-tiered systems of support; teacher preparation. Additionally, this position is expected to successfully mentor undergraduate and graduate students with diverse experiences and backgrounds, in an academic setting.
The successful candidate will also be expected to perform research and service in the candidate’s area of expertise. This will include the development and maintenance of a rigorous scholarly agenda and actively participating in unit-specific activities such as accreditation, assessment, curriculum development, and program reviews. Additional service expectations include mentoring students, participating in school and campus committees, and maintaining external relationships with communities, school partners, and state-level professional organizations.
About the Tacoma Campus and the School of Education:
The University of Washington Tacoma (UWT) is a growing, urban-servicing university that is deeply invested in its local communities. As one of three campuses of a world-class university, UWT is dedicated to interdisciplinary and innovative teaching and scholarship, and to engaging the community in mutually beneficial partnerships. Consistent with the institution’s urban-serving mission, UWT provides a unique environment for faculty to creatively develop their teaching, scholarship, and service portfolios, and to engage with the Tacoma community. UWT’s commitment to access is central to an environment where students, staff, faculty, and South Sound residents find abundant opportunities for intellectual, personal, and professional growth.
To learn more about UW Tacoma, visit: https://www.tacoma.uw.edu/home/about-university-washington-tacoma.
The School of Education (SOE) at UW Tacoma is one of seven academic units on campus. More information about our conceptual framework, mission, and values is located on our website: https://www.tacoma.uw.edu/soe/conceptual-framework.
Qualifications
Applicants for this position must meet the following minimum qualifications:
An earned doctorate (or foreign equivalent) in Special Education or related field from an accredited college or university by the start of the appointment.
A minimum of 3 years of full-time credentialed experience teaching in diverse PK-12 special education settings in the USA. The earned credential may be outside Washington State.
Demonstrated effectiveness in teaching in the candidate’s areas of expertise.
Demonstrated ability to develop and pursue a scholarly research agenda in the candidate’s area of expertise.
In exceptional circumstances, candidates in the final stages of the degree (pending conferral) may be considered an appointed on an acting basis.
Application Instructions
First consideration of applications will begin on November 2, 2026. Priority will be given to those applications received by that date. The position will remain open until filled.
Applications must include the following materials:
Cover letter, detailing your interest in the position, how you meet the minimum qualifications, and how your work will contribute to the mission and values of the School of Education at UW Tacoma. . (maximum three (3) pages).
Curriculum vitae, including your scholarship, a list of courses taught, their frequency, and your role in each course (e.g., primary instructor vs. teaching assistant), and your academic and professional service roles.
Evidence of teaching effectiveness. Please describe your teaching philosophy and your teaching experience, including brief descriptions of success and/or other accomplishments related to culturally/linguistically responsive and inclusive teaching practices. Please include how your teaching evidence supports the success of learners with disabilities from diverse and historically excluded backgrounds in PK-12 education, higher education, and/or community education. (maximum one (1) page).
Names and contact information for three professional references, with letters available upon request.
One (1) sample peer-reviewed paper or publication such as an article, book chapter, or a full conference paper.
Applicants should articulate how their past experiences and/or future plans in research, teaching, mentoring, and/or service promote a sense of belonging and foster a welcoming and inclusive environment.
All materials must be submitted via Interfolio. Questions about the search should be directed to the Search Co-Chairs, Dr. Julia Aguirre, Director of Teacher Certification Master and Bachelors Programs & Professor (jaguirre@uw.edu) or Dr. Sarah Tov, Assistant Professor (satov@uw.edu).

The Division of Addiction Medicine within the Department of Family Medicine and Community Health at the Perelman School of Medicine at the University of Pennsylvania seeks candidates for multiple faculty positions in Addiction Medicine in the non-tenure Academic Clinician (AC) track. Successful candidates will hold an M.D. or D.O. degree and must have primary board in a recognized ABMS or AOA Specialty and must be board certified in Addiction Medicine. Faculty may participate in ambulatory addiction medicine, Bridge/OTP services, treatment of opioid and other substance use disorders, hospital-based addiction treatment, community-based addiction services, resident and fellow supervision, and multidisciplinary care coordination. All faculty members will devote a portion of their clinical effort to inpatient Addiction Medicine consult services at one or more Penn Medicine hospitals, including Pennsylvania Hospital, Penn Presbyterian Medical Center, the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania, and HUP Cedar.
The Division of Addiction Medicine is recruiting for three full-time faculty positions that will support Penn Medicine's growing addiction medicine clinical, educational, and community programs. These positions offer flexibility in clinical practice location and scope while supporting access to evidence-based addiction treatment across Penn Medicine.
The Division of Addiction Medicine serves diverse patients across Philadelphia, including many individuals and communities that have historically experienced barriers to health care access and health equity. We seek candidates who demonstrate a commitment to caring for medically and socially complex patient populations and who have experience working in underserved communities and resource-limited clinical settings.

The Department of Sociology and Criminology & Law at the University of Florida, College of Liberal Arts and Sciences invites applications for two full-time, nine-month, tenure-accruing positions beginning August 16, 2027 at the rank of Assistant Professor with research and teaching interests related to US criminal justice systems broadly defined. These positions support the Crime and Justice component of our program in Criminology & Law. We seek scholars who study the practice and implementation of criminal and/or juvenile justice systems, for example, local, state, and/or Federal law enforcement, courts, sentencing and/or corrections, capital punishment, juvenile programming and prevention. Applicant research programs can emphasize theory development, methodological applications (quantitative, qualitative and/or mixed), and/or policy analysis (including program evaluation).
We seek applicants whose records show commitment to rigorous scholarship with the promise of external funding, as well as excellence in teaching. The ability to contribute significantly to graduate education and the mentoring of graduate students is highly desirable. Advanced assistant professors are welcome to apply.
The successful candidate will be expected to teach in their topical areas of interest and one or more of our required courses, which include research methods, criminological theory, and/or advanced principles of criminal justice. At the graduate level, successful applicants may also be able to teach required courses in our quantitative methods sequence or a criminal justice process course in addition to their area of interest.
The Department of Sociology and Criminology & Law is a large and dynamic department with nearly 700 undergraduate Criminology majors and roughly 20 Criminology, Law and Society graduate students. The Department has two undergraduate programs, both offered via in-person and online courses, and minors in Sociology of Social Justice & Policy and Environmental Justice & Policy. Faculty conduct research in diverse areas, including criminology and criminal justice; psychology and law; families and gender; health, aging, and the life course; environment and resources; and race and ethnicity. Many faculty are affiliated with other academic programs at UF, including the School of Natural Resources and the Environment, the Center for Latin American Studies, the Center for European Studies, the Department of Gender, Sexuality and Women's Studies, and the Health Science Center. More information about the Department is available at https://soccrim.clas.ufl.edu/, including biographical information about our faculty, students, and staff; and a description of the various projects and research interests in which our members are involved.

About Binghamton University:
Binghamton University is a premier public R1 research institution in the State University of New York (SUNY) system that unites more than 130 broadly interdisciplinary educational programs with some of the most vibrant research in the nation. Our unique character - shaped by our mission, outstanding academics, facilities, and community life - promotes extraordinary student success, research, and service; Binghamton University is where our students, faculty and staff thrive.
Working at Binghamton University is more than about having a great job - it is about having the opportunity to flourish in an exciting, engaging environment. Our faculty and staff appreciate Binghamton's collegial and inclusive culture and its commitment to excellence, education, innovation, and civic engagement. Our diverse campus community contributes to our success.
Binghamton merges rigorous academics, distinguished faculty who value cutting-edge, and community-engaged research, teaching and service, exceptional staff, and ultramodern facilities to engage and challenge its 18,000+ students. Our high-achieving student body represents diverse experiences from first-generation college-goers to international students. Beyond their talent, these classmates share a desire to shape the future through technology, insight, intellectual exploration, and community service.
Job Description:
Department Overview:
The Department of Social Work is entering an exciting period of growth and innovation. In addition to expanding its Bachelor of Social Work (BSW) and Master of Social Work (MSW) programs, the Department is actively developing a PhD program in Social Work, creating new opportunities for faculty leadership in doctoral education, research mentorship, interdisciplinary collaboration, and the advancement of the social work profession. The development of the PhD program reflects both the Department's growth and Binghamton University's broader commitment to expanding high-impact graduate and doctoral education within its R1 research environment.
The Department is part of College of Community and Public Affairs (CCPA), an interdisciplinary college focused on preparing students for careers and leadership in public and community service. CCPA brings together Social Work, Human Development, Public Administration and Policy, Higher Education and Student Affairs, and Teaching, Learning and Educational Leadership, alongside the interdisciplinary Community Research and Action PhD program. The College emphasizes social justice, interdisciplinary collaboration, applied scholarship, and meaningful engagement with local, regional, national, and global communities. Located in downtown Binghamton, CCPA is closely connected to a broad network of community agencies, schools, health and human service organizations, government entities, and nonprofit partners.
The Department offers a growing BSW program, a long-standing in-person MSW program, and an exclusively online MSW program, including full-time, part-time, and advanced standing pathways. The Department's programs are grounded in social justice, multisystem practice, community engagement, and a commitment to preparing social workers to address complex social problems across individuals, families, organizations, and communities.
Job Description:
Binghamton University is seeking faculty members at open rank Professor specializing in advanced quantitative methods or applied statistics to join its Department of Social Work within the CCPA. We seek a collegial and collaborative scholar whose expertise in advanced quantitative methods will strengthen the Department's research capacity and complement faculty whose primary expertise lies in substantive areas of social work, social policy, education, health, and human services.
The candidate's substantive area of research specialization is open. We particularly welcome scholars who develop or apply advanced quantitative methods to complex, real-world data, including administrative, longitudinal, multilevel, multisystem, geospatial, linked, and community-engaged datasets. We are especially interested in scholarship that advances social justice, examines social and structural determinants of health and well-being, informs equitable policy and practice, and addresses systemic inequities affecting marginalized and historically underserved populations.
Key Responsibilities:
Serve as a methodological partner to faculty and graduate students, and interdisciplinary research teams across the full research lifecycle, including:
study design
measurement
data management and linkage
statistical analysis
interpretation
grant development
dissemination
Contribute intellectually to substantive research initiatives and promote rigorous, transparent, and responsible use of quantitative methods.
Maintain an active program of independent and/or collaborative scholarship appropriate for tenure and promotion, with opportunities to pursue external funding as a principal investigator, co-investigator, methodological collaborator, or statistical lead.
Teach and develop advanced level statistics and quantitative methods courses that are rigorous, accessible, and applicable to social work and related social and behavioral sciences. Teaching may include areas such as:
multilevel and longitudinal modeling
latent-variable methods
causal inference
psychometrics and measurement
Bayesian methods
missing-data methods
computational methods
machine learning
reproducible research practices
Binghamton University offers a collegial, collaborative environment within a nationally recognized R1 research institution. Faculty benefit from competitive salaries, research support and start-up resources, and extensive opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration and community-engaged scholarship. Binghamton's research enterprise is supported by substantial institutional investment and a university-wide commitment to translating research into meaningful impact.
Diversity and Inclusion: Binghamton University remains committed to and supports diversity and inclusion as integral to academic excellence. We actively seek applications from underrepresented racial/ethnic groups, sexual minorities, veterans, persons with disabilities, and women.
Requirements:
Requirements:
Doctoral degree conferred by August 1, 2027 in statistics, biostatistics, quantitative psychology, or a closely aligned discipline
Candidates whose doctorates are in social work, psychology, public health, education, economics, sociology, data science, public policy, or another closely related field will also be considered if they demonstrate a strong background in advanced quantitative analysis
Experience working with researchers across multiple substantive areas and adapting quantitative methods
The ability to translate substantive research questions into rigorous and feasible quantitative designs and analytic plans
Demonstrated high-quality teaching, advising, and student mentorship
A record of independent and collaborative scholarship
Preferred:
Expertise analyzing complex datasets
Experience working with large-scale data from human-service systems or other real-world settings
Experience contributing to externally funded, team-based research
Demonstrated ability to communicate quantitative methods to students and colleagues with varied levels of statistical preparation
Experience with reproducible and responsible research practices, (e.g., transparent analytic workflows, data documentation, and appropriate data-sharing practices)
Scholarship addressing social determinants of health and well-being, systemic or structural inequities
Experience incorporating critical, anti-racist, or equity-centered perspectives into quantitative research design, measurement, analysis, and interpretation
Potential to contribute to interdisciplinary research initiatives
Visa sponsorship is not available for this position. If you currently need sponsorship or will need it in the future to maintain employment authorization, you do not meet eligibility requirements. Additionally, please note that Binghamton University is not an E-Verify employer.

This requirement extends to employment and admission. Inquiries about sex discrimination may be directed to the University Title IX Coordinator or directly to the Office of Civil Rights (OCR).
