Professor of Public Health (Open Rank)
North Carolina Wesleyan University invites applications for a 9-month appointment as a tenured/tenure-track professor (rank open) of Public Health beginning in August 2027. Responsibilities may include, but are not limited to, teaching a variety of public health classes at the graduate and undergraduate level; advising and mentoring students; promoting program growth and academic quality; supervising student interns, and serving on internal committees. We are especially interested in candidates with experience and interest in public health approaches to nutrition and food security and/or working with rural communities. Our public health programs provide high-quality courses, collaborative community-engaged faculty, and opportunities to engage in faculty-student research. We offer undergraduate major and minor degrees, an MPH degree with two available concentrations (Physical Activity and Health and Social Epidemiology) and a Graduate Certificate in Public Health.
We seek passionate candidates with online teaching experience, a strong grounding in health equity and community health, and a commitment to growing and nurturing current and future public health professionals. All North Carolina Wesleyan faculty are expected to engage students using pedagogically sound traditional and innovative instructional strategies. A regular teaching load is 12 hours per semester, which may vary based on the distribution of teaching across the graduate and undergraduate programs.
Qualifications: an earned doctoral degree in Public Health, Health Promotion, Nutrition, or closely related field, is required. ABD candidates will be considered but must have obtained a doctorate degree by August 2027. Previous college or university-level teaching experience is strongly preferred, particularly in the areas of public health nutrition, epidemiology, and/or community health. Evidence of advising, supervising, and/or collaborating with students is highly desirable. Evidence of scholarly activities such as peer-reviewed publications and professional presentations is also a plus.
Applications should include: 1) a letter of application; 2) a curriculum vitae, including contact information for at least three professional references; and 3) copies of transcripts showing academic work in higher education and degrees received. Please submit the application as a single pdf file. Review of applications will begin immediately and will continue until a suitable candidate is identified. Application materials should be sent, as a single pdf, to Ms. Tammy Harrell, Manager of Faculty Records and Academic Projects, by email to tharrell@ncwu.edu.
North Carolina Wesleyan University is a liberal arts university, affiliated with the United Methodist Church. The university is located in Rocky Mount, North Carolina, and serves approximately 1,500 students. The Wesleyan community celebrates the rich diversity of its student body, 43% are students of color, and 15% are international students. Rocky Mount is in the eastern coastal plain region of the state, convenient to the Raleigh-Durham area and beaches, including the Outer Banks. Washington, DC, and the mountains of North Carolina are also within easy driving distance.
North Carolina Wesleyan University values a culture of respect, kindness, and understanding and does not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, sex, age (40 years and older), marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, or genetic information. Women, historically underrepresented minorities, and individuals with disabilities are encouraged to apply.
North Carolina Wesleyan University is an equal opportunity employer.

jobs.title: Professor of Teaching in Neuroscience and Undergraduate Neuroscience Interdepartmental Program
jobs.description:
Job Details
Assistant Professor of Teaching in Neuroscience in the UCLA Department of Psychology and Undergraduate Neuroscience Interdepartmental Program
The UCLA Department of Psychology and the UCLA Undergraduate Neuroscience Interdepartmental Program invite applications for a full-time Assistant Professor of Teaching who will develop and teach courses in Behavioral, Cellular, and Molecular Neuroscience. The faculty member hired from this search will have a 50% appointment in the Department of Psychology and a 50% appointment with the Undergraduate Neuroscience Interdepartmental Program, with the Department of Psychology serving as the primary department. We seek applicants with experience employing innovative methods in the classroom and in teaching laboratory and upper-division lecture courses. In addition, the successful candidate is expected to engage in scholarly activities (e.g., contribute to research on pedagogy or contribute to research in another area with the support of undergraduate students; develop, evaluate, and disseminate innovative teaching approaches).
The Assistant Professor of Teaching position is a full-time faculty position with potential security of employment akin to tenure. Those in the Professor of Teaching series are Academic Senate faculty members whose expertise and responsibilities center on undergraduate education and scholarly analysis/improvement of teaching methods. Faculty in the Professor of Teaching series are evaluated on their (1) teaching excellence, (2) professional and/or scholarly achievement and activity, and (3) university and public service. Potential applicants who have questions about the position can contact Profs. Barbara Knowlton or Stephanie White, search committee co-chairs, at SearchCommittee@psych.ucla.edu.
The UCLA Department of Psychology and the UCLA Undergraduate Neuroscience Interdepartmental Program are located within the Division of Life Sciences, which is part of the College of Letters and Science. The search is geared toward candidates who share our belief that, as professors at a leading public university, we strive for inclusive excellence in teaching, service, research, and engagement with our academic community. We are eager to welcome an outstanding scholar and mentor who will create opportunities that will deepen and enrich understanding of psychological principles and perspectives for our students, while also contributing to the collaborative and supportive environment that characterizes our department and program. We are also interested in applicants who will advance UCLA's mission.
Applicants must hold a Ph.D. in Psychology, Neuroscience, or a related field. The degree must be finalized by January 1, 2027. This is an Assistant Professor of Teaching position; please do not apply if you are an Associate Professor or higher (or if you are undergoing review for tenure at your university, or anticipate a tenure review during our application process) as your application will not be considered. Applicants should demonstrate a record of teaching excellence in courses relevant to Behavioral, Cellular, and Molecular Neuroscience and the potential to contribute to the mentoring and service missions of the department, program, and university, particularly in regard to improving the quality of instruction. Applicants with experience mentoring and teaching students from groups affected by disparities in educational access are strongly encouraged to apply.
We seek applications from individuals with a demonstrated commitment to ensuring equal access to the benefits of their teaching and supporting the full participation of all students through consideration and appreciation of differences. The successful candidate will help foster authentic engagement and belonging within our diverse community. UCLA has scaled multiple initiatives such as Rising to the Challenge, Hispanic-Serving Institution initiative, and Native American/Pacific Islander Bruins Rising to promote inclusive excellence. UCLA is home to a diverse student body of approximately 47,000 undergraduate and graduate students and is ranked among the top national universities for social mobility. UCLA has programs to assist in partner employment, child care, schooling, and other family concerns. For additional information, visit the UCLA Academic Affairs and Personnel Office website (https://apo.ucla.edu/faculty-career-development/work-life-balance) or the UC Office of the President's website (https://www.ucop.edu/faculty-affairs-academic-programs/resources/family-friendly-practices-and-policies/family-friendly-policies-and-issues.html).
To ensure full consideration, the online application must be completed and submitted by November 9, 2026. Applications should include a cover letter, curriculum vitae, contact information for three recommenders, a statement focused on UCLA's mission of no more than three pages, a statement of teaching philosophy of no more than three pages, a statement on the applicant's vision for scholarly activities of no more than three pages, and a teaching portfolio that includes syllabi, evaluations, and instructional materials used in courses previously taught. Letters of recommendation will be requested at a later date from applicants who progress to a later stage of review. To learn about the required UCLA mission statement, please see the job posting at https://recruit.apo.ucla.edu/JPF11315.
The posted UC salary scales (https://www.ucop.edu/academic-personnel-programs/compensation/index.html) set the minimum pay determined by rank and step at appointment. See Table 1. The salary range for this position is $84,100-$108,900. “Off-scale salaries”, i.e. a salary that is higher than the published system-wide salary at the designated rank and step, are offered when necessary to meet competitive conditions.
Apply at the following website: https://recruit.apo.ucla.edu/JPF11315
The University of California is committed to creating and maintaining a community dedicated to the advancement, application, and transmission of knowledge and creative endeavors through academic excellence, where all individuals who participate in University programs and activities can work and learn together in a safe and secure environment, free of violence, harassment, bullying and other demeaning behavior, discrimination, exploitation, or intimidation. With this commitment as well as a commitment to addressing all forms of academic misconduct, UCLA conducts targeted employment reference checks for finalists to whom departments or other hiring units would like to extend formal offers of appointment into Academic Senate faculty positions. The targeted employment reference checks involve contacting the finalists' current and prior places of employment to ask whether there have been substantiated findings of misconduct that would violate the University's Faculty Code of Conduct. To implement this process, UCLA requires all applicants for Academic Senate faculty positions to complete, sign, and upload the form entitled “Authorization to Release Information” into RECRUIT as part of their application. If the applicant does not include the signed authorization to release information with the application materials, the application will be considered incomplete. As with any incomplete application, the application will not receive further consideration. Position description
Berkeley Law is one of the nation's great centers for legal education, ever exploring and pushing new intellectual boundaries while tackling urgent, real-world issues. The law school is also known for its vibrant and engaged community of students and scholars who are committed to providing leadership and making a difference on problems of local, national and global import. Currently ranked among the top law schools in the country, the School of Law has ambitious development goals as it looks to continue producing leaders in law, government, and society.
Berkeley Law invites applications for a full-time position on our clinical faculty, teaching in our Death Penalty Clinic. This faculty position entails membership in the Academic Senate with rights and responsibilities that are comparable to the standard professorial track, but with an emphasis on teaching, professional competence and activity, research and creative work, and University and public service.
Berkeley Law's Clinical Program includes seven in-house clinics: Environmental Law Clinic, Death Penalty Clinic, Global Rights Innovation Lab Clinic, Human Rights Clinic, Policy Advocacy Clinic, Samuelson Law, Technology & Public Policy Clinic, and Social Enterprise Clinic. The program also partners with the East Bay Community Law Center to offer community-based clinics: the Clean Slate Clinic, Community Economic Justice Clinic, Consumer Justice & General Clinic, Youth Defense Clinic, Education Justice Clinic, Health & Welfare Clinic, Housing Law Clinic, and Immigration Law Clinic.
The Death Penalty Clinic is dedicated to developing students' advanced legal advocacy skills while providing exceptional legal representation to individuals facing capital punishment. In response to the critical shortage of qualified and adequately funded counsel for people on death row, the clinic represents clients primarily in post-conviction proceedings, with a particular focus on jurisdictions that have the fewest legal resources. The clinic also tackles problems endemic to the administration of capital punishment. Through this work, students gain intensive, hands-on experience in complex litigation while contributing to high-quality representation in cases involving the most serious criminal penalties.
The mission of Berkeley Law's Clinical Program is to advance equal justice - racial, economic, and social justice - through three interrelated activities: preparing law students to address pressing societal problems and to become highly skilled, responsible, and reflective legal practitioners; providing first-rate legal services to underrepresented individuals, marginalized communities, and public-minded organizations––locally, nationally, and globally; and producing cutting-edge, interdisciplinary research to support litigation, inform public policy, and increase the effectiveness of our teaching and service.
Berkeley Law strives to educate responsible, effective, and forward-thinking advocates who serve the public through legal practice, public policy, academic scholarship, and related fields. In doing so, the school addresses some of society's most pressing challenges by leveraging its strengths in teaching and research to improve law, policy, and public institutions. At the heart of Berkeley Law's public mission is a commitment to access, affordability, and empowering students from all backgrounds to pursue impactful careers across a wide range of professional paths.
Berkeley Law is committed to addressing the family needs of faculty, including dual career couples and single parents. We are also interested in candidates who have had non-traditional career paths or who have taken time off for family reasons, or who have achieved excellence in careers outside academia. For information about potential relocation to Berkeley, or career needs of accompanying partners and spouses, please visit the Office for Faculty Equity and Welfare's website.

The College of Engineering (COE) at Western Carolina University (WCU) is growing!The University has received substantial support from the North Carolina legislature to expand engineering to meet the rapidly growing needs of the region and state. Our engineering and construction management programs feature project-based learning embedded throughout the curricula, preparing our students for professional practice and advanced study. Industry engagement is a hallmark of our programs, and we pride ourselves on having faculty with significant industry experience. Our culture embraces faculty-student interaction through experiences such as undergraduate research. We are committed to regional economic development and changing the lives of our students and their families through a transformative experience at our main rural campus setting in the mountains of western North Carolina, and at sites in Asheville and across western NC. The college's programs are instrumental to the economic vitality of the region and are advancing the university to be one of the nation's premier regional comprehensive institutions. We are creating leaders, innovators, and entrepreneurs with the foundation and skills needed for transformative careers in engineering and beyond.
The Department of Civil Engineering and Construction (CEC) invites applications for an Associate/Full Professor of Construction Management with an anticipated August 2027 start date. This is a nine (9) month, tenure-track position, with additional summer opportunities for research, teaching, and other professional endeavors. Successful candidates will be expected to teach at both the undergraduate and graduate levels, advise students, be involved in extra-curricular student engagement activities, develop a sustainable program of research and scholarship, and be engaged in university and professional service. Faculty pursue scholarship and research with external partners and with clients through our nationally recognized Rapid Center. Applied research that engages students, especially undergraduate students, is a hallmark of our program.
The Department of Civil Engineering and Construction houses on-campus undergraduate degree programs in Construction Management and Civil Engineering and an online non-thesis based graduate degree program in Construction Management. The College also has a Master of Engineering (MSE) and a Master of Engineering Technology (MSET) graduate program. Both the Construction Management and Civil Engineering programs are ABET accredited.

Have a minimum of three (3) or more years of U.S. project-based construction industry experience.
Upper-level management experience in the construction industry.

Demonstrated national standing or recognition in the construction education profession.

Job Details
The Department of Civil & Environmental Engineering at Stanford University invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the junior level (Assistant Professor). We seek applicants in support of the department's vision of creating solutions for cities, communities, and nature to thrive, with a particular focus on water or air quality (https://cee.stanford.edu/research-impact). While we give highest priority to the originality, quality, and potential impact of the candidate's work, we are especially interested in applicants whose research advances the characterization, assessment, and mitigation of risks to clean air and safe water in natural and engineered systems including resource recovery, physiochemical treatment systems, scalable water and wastewater services, and air quality engineering solutions linked to climate, energy use, and health outcomes, among others. Please visit our website for more information about the CEE Department at http://cee.stanford.edu/.
Applicants must have completed, or be completing, a Ph.D. in the advertised field or a closely related one. Evidence of the ability to pursue a program of research, and a strong commitment to graduate and undergraduate teaching are also required. A successful candidate will be expected to teach courses at the graduate and undergraduate levels and to build and lead a team of graduate students in PhD research.
Applications should include a resume, brief statements of research and teaching interests (3-5 pages total for both combined), and the names and e-mail addresses of 3-5 references. We will request letters of recommendation after candidates have been short-listed.
The Civil & Environmental Engineering Department, School of Engineering, Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability, and Stanford University value faculty who will help foster an open and respectful academic environment for colleagues, students, and staff with a wide range of backgrounds and perspectives. Candidates may choose to include as part of their research and teaching statements a brief discussion about how their work will further these values.
Applications will be accepted until November 1, 2026. Interviews will begin in the winter term, so applicants are encouraged to apply early. Please forward questions to ceefacultysearch@stanford.edu.
The expected base pay range for this position is:
Assistant Professor: $144,100- $163,766
This base pay range is for a nine-month academic appointment and does not include summer salary. For more information about compensation and our wide range of benefits, including housing assistance, please contact the hiring department.
Stanford University has provided a pay range representing its good faith estimate of what the university reasonably expects to pay for the position upon hire. The pay offered to the selected candidate will be determined based on factors including (but not limited to) the experience and qualifications of the selected candidate including years since terminal degree, training, and field or discipline; departmental budget availability; internal equity; and external market pay for comparable jobs.
Stanford is an equal employment opportunity and affirmative action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Stanford also welcomes applications from others who would bring additional dimensions to the University’s research, teaching and clinical missions.
Consistent with its obligations under the law, the University will provide reasonable accommodations to applicants and employees with disabilities. Applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation for any part of the application or hiring process should contact disability.access@stanford.edu.

About the Department:
Why ISE at NC State?
In ISE, you will be part of a department where innovative research happens both within and across disciplines. The Fitts Department of Industrial and Systems Engineering includes more than 25 faculty, 10 core staff, 350 undergraduate students, and 250 graduate students, including approximately 75 Ph.D. students. Our research spans advanced and biomedical manufacturing; health systems; human systems; supply chain and logistics; and systems analytics and optimization, along with interdisciplinary collaborations across the university and beyond. Our faculty are internationally recognized in their fields, with Fellows of IISE, INFORMS, SME, and other professional societies.
You will join a collaborative and collegial community where faculty work across traditional disciplinary boundaries and engage with researchers, medical schools, universities, industry, and government partners. The department leads three centers and multiple interdisciplinary graduate programs, creating opportunities to pursue research and educational collaborations well beyond ISE. In addition to degrees in ISE, the department leads the professional Master’s in Engineering Management program and collaborates on the graduate Operations Research program.The department houses two state-funded centers that are public-private partnerships: the Ergonomics Center of North Carolina, the only center of its kind at a U.S. public research institution, and the Center for Additive Manufacturing and Logistics, one of the most advanced manufacturing and 3D printing laboratories in the country. The newly established Bezos Center for Alternative Proteins is also led by an ISE faculty member. These centers provide additional opportunities to collaborate with industry and pursue research with real-world impact.
You will have access to world-class laboratory and research facilities supporting computing, manufacturing, human factors, and ergonomics research. These resources are complemented by Fitts-Woolard Hall, our state-of-the-art home on NC State’s Centennial Campus, located near the award-winning Hunt Library and numerous industry and government facilities. Centennial Campus provides a unique environment for university-industry collaboration and interdisciplinary research.At NC State ISE, our students “Think and Do” through active learning and real-world problems across the ISE discipline. You will have the opportunity to mentor and teach a diverse and growing student population and help prepare students to become leaders in academia, industry, and government. NC State is also investing significantly in engineering, with up to 40% growth in engineering faculty, staff, and undergraduate and graduate students expected over the coming years, creating new opportunities for collaboration, education, and research.
You will also benefit from being in Raleigh and the Research Triangle, one of the nation’s leading centers for technology, research, and innovation. NC State is located within close proximity to Duke University, the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, major research institutes, and a wide range of world-class companies. Raleigh offers an exceptional quality of life, with outstanding restaurants, cultural and recreational opportunities, and easy access to both the mountains and the coast.
At NC State ISE, you will join a nationally recognized department that values collaboration, innovation, and impact—and a university and community positioned for significant growth.
Wolfpack Perks and Benefits:
As a Pack member, you belong here, and can enjoy exclusive perks designed to enhance your personal and professional well-being. As you consider this opportunity, we encourage you to review our Employee Value Proposition and learn more about what makes NC State the best place to learn and work for everyone.

Essential Job Duties:
The Department of Industrial and Systems Engineering (ISE) at NC State University invites applications for open-rank, tenure-track faculty positions at all career stages. The department welcomes candidates whose research and teaching interests align with the broad field of Industrial and Systems Engineering, with particular interest in artificial intelligence and/or quantum computing for optimization; logistics and supply chain management; data science and analytics; and emerging areas of national and international importance. Appointments may be considered at the Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor level based on qualifications and career stage.
In this role, you will shape the future of Industrial and Systems Engineering through research, teaching, and collaboration. You will have the opportunity to establish a distinctive research agenda, pursue meaningful partnerships across disciplines, and translate your expertise into advances that address complex engineering challenges. Through your teaching and mentorship, you will help prepare the next generation of engineers, researchers, and leaders while contributing your perspective and expertise to the continued growth and excellence of ISE and NC State.
Key Responsibilities include and are not limited to the following:
Build and sustain an independent, externally funded research program that advances Industrial and Systems Engineering and contributes to emerging areas of national and international importance.
Conduct and disseminate high-impact research through scholarly publications, presentations, and other contributions to the field.
Develop interdisciplinary collaborations within NC State and with external academic, industry, government, and research partners to address complex engineering challenges.
Teach and develop courses at the undergraduate and graduate levels, creating engaging learning experiences that prepare students for the evolving field of Industrial and Systems Engineering.
Mentor and advise graduate students and support their academic, research, and professional development.
Contribute to the department, college, and university community through service, leadership, and activities that advance the mission and vision of NC State.
If you are an innovative researcher and educator ready to advance Industrial and Systems Engineering, collaborate across disciplines, and prepare the next generation of engineering leaders, we encourage you to apply.

Rank of Associate Professor – Recognized ability and potential for distinction, and demonstrated ability to direct activities, in the mutually agreed upon realms of responsibility; demonstrated ability and willingness to participate in department, college, and university affairs; a doctoral degree in Industrial Engineering or closely-related discipline.

Other Required Qualifications:

The Department of Health Sciences in the School of Education and Health Sciences at North Central College invites applications for a full-time, 9.5-month tenure-track faculty position in Health Science, to begin Fall 2027. This position includes a leadership appointment as Program Director of the undergraduate Health Science program.
The undergraduate Health Science program is one of the College’s largest and fastest-growing academic programs, serving more than 200 undergraduate majors. The successful candidate will provide visionary leadership to support the continued growth, quality, and innovation of the program while contributing to excellence in teaching, scholarship, and service.
As Program Director, the successful candidate will oversee the undergraduate Health Science program and collaborate closely with the department chair, college leadership, and external partners. Responsibilities may include, but are not limited to:
Providing leadership for the undergraduate Health Science program.
Leading curriculum development, review, and continuous program improvement.
Coordinating program assessment as applicable.
Advising and mentoring current and prospective Health Science students.
Managing program planning, budgeting, and resource allocation.
Developing the course schedule in collaboration with department chair and faculty.
Planning and facilitating program events that foster student engagement, professional development, and community within the major.
Building and maintaining relationships with healthcare organizations, community partners, and industry professionals to expand experiential learning opportunities.
Collaborating with graduate programs to develop and strengthen accelerated pathways and graduate education opportunities for Health Science students.
Supporting student recruitment, retention, and overall program visibility.
This tenure-track position carries a 20-credit annual teaching load, with a portion of teaching responsibilities reassigned to support Program Director duties. Teaching assignments will be based on departmental needs and the successful candidate’s expertise and may include undergraduate courses such as:
Introduction to Health Sciences
Community Health
Epidemiology in the Health Sciences
Evidence-Based Practice
Research Methods in the Health Sciences
Cultural Competency and Health Literacy
Health Systems and Informatics
In addition to program leadership and teaching, tenure-track faculty are expected to maintain an active program of scholarship, mentor undergraduate students, and contribute to the intellectual life of the College through departmental, school, and institutional service. Successful candidates will demonstrate a commitment to excellence in teaching, scholarly engagement, collaborative leadership, and fostering an inclusive learning environment.
QualificationsA doctoral degree (earned by the time of appointment) in Health Science or a closely related discipline is required. Candidates should demonstrate evidence of excellence in undergraduate teaching, a developing or established record of scholarship appropriate for a tenure-track appointment, and a commitment to student mentorship. Next Lives at the University of Cincinnati

UC's momentum has never been stronger as the anchor of the Cincinnati Innovation District, the oldest cooperative education (co-op) program in the country with students earning $94 million annually through paid experiences, an academic health system, and as a member of the Big 12 Conference. The university contributes $10.6 billion in economic impact to the city and $22.7 billion to the state of Ohio. At UC, next is all of us. Learn more at uc.edu.

About the Department of Philosophy
The Department of Philosophy is a PhD-granting department with strengths in philosophy of science, philosophy of cognitive science, and applied ethics and social/political philosophy. We comprise 14 full-time faculty, more than 25 active PhD students, and affiliated faculty across the University.
Department faculty lead the Center for Public Engagement with Science (PEWS), the UC Center for Humanities and Technology (CHaT), and the Cincinnati Ethics Center. The department also has close connections to the Institute for Research in Sensing (IRiS) and the Center for Cognition, Action, and Perception (CAP). Many department faculty pursue interdisciplinary or empirically informed research projects.
Job Overview
The Department of Philosophy in the College of Arts & Sciences at the University of Cincinnati invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor to begin in August 2027 with an Area of Specialization (AOS) in Ancient Philosophy and with an Area of Competence (AOC) in Comparative or Non-Western Philosophy or Ethics. The standard teaching load is 2-2.
Essential Functions
Teach courses in Philosophy, including introductory general education courses, upper-level undergraduate courses that serve the Philosophy BA program, and graduate seminars that serve the Philosophy PhD program.
Conduct and publish research in Philosophy in their AOS.
Advise graduate students and supervise Teaching Assistants.
Contribute service or committee work to the department (such as the Undergraduate or Graduate Studies Committee), college (such as grant or award review committees), and profession (such as peer review for journals or service in professional associations).
Minimum Requirements
Prior to effective date of appointment, all of the following:
A PhD in Philosophy or a closely related discipline
An Area of Specialization (AOS) in Ancient Philosophy
An Area of Competence (AOC) in Comparative or Non-Western Philosophy or Ethics
One semester of teaching experience at the college or university level, either as instructor or teaching assistant.
Application Process
Applicants must apply online at https://jobs.uc.edu (search requisition #104145 ). Candidates should submit a CV, cover letter, statement of research interests and plans, teaching dossier, and one writing sample. Because the application system does not manage confidential reference letters, candidates should arrange to have at least three confidential letters of recommendation sent via Interfolio, another dossier service, or by the letter writers themselves, to the Search Committee Chair at uc-phil-ancient@uc.edu.
Review of applications will begin on November 1, 2026. First round interviews will be held via Zoom in December 2026.
Compensation and Benefits
UC offers an exceptional benefits package designed to support your well-being, financial security, and work-life balance. (UC Benefits) Eligibility may vary by position and FTE status. Highlights include:
Comprehensive Tuition Remission
UC provides tuition remission for you and your eligible dependents, covering tuition costs for nearly all undergraduate and graduate programs offered by the university.
Robust Retirement Plans
As a UC employee, you won’t contribute to Social Security (except Medicare). Instead, you’ll choose between state pension plans (OPERS, STRS) or an Alternative Retirement Plan (ARP), with UC contributing 14–18% of your salary based on position.
Real Work-Life Balance
UC prioritizes work-life balance with a generous time-off policy, including:
Vacation and sick time
11 paid holidays and additional end-of-year paid time off (Winter Season Days)
6 weeks of paid parental leave for new parents
Additional Benefits Include:
Competitive salary based on experience
Comprehensive health coverage (medical, dental, vision, prescription)
Flexible spending accounts & wellness programs
Professional development & mentorship opportunities

jobs.description:
Job Details
Open Rank Position in Music Education, Natalie L. Haslam College of Music, Fall 2027
Location:
Knoxville, TN
Open Date:
Sep 22, 2026
Description:
Assistant, Associate or Full Professor; nine-month tenure-track appointment beginning Fall Semester, August 1, 2027. Salary and fringe benefits are competitive and commensurate with rank and experience.
The University of Tennessee's Natalie L. Haslam College of Music is seeking a dynamic music educator to join our faculty. The ideal candidate will demonstrate a collaborative spirit, bring expertise in elementary/general music education and contribute to our undergraduate and graduate music education offerings. The candidate should work collaboratively with other College of Music faculty to sustain and support the music education program, maintain a research/creative/scholarly activity profile commensurate with appointed rank, and demonstrate a commitment to forward-thinking curriculum development, innovation, and community engagement.
Primary responsibilities include teaching undergraduates in elementary music education, leading graduate courses in areas of expertise, coordinating field experience internships, and supervising student teachers/interns. The successful candidate will actively participate in professional development for elementary/general music educators, develop regional and national visibility as an elementary/general music educator, and develop and maintain positive relationships with inservice music educators. The candidate is also expected to serve on graduate committees and participate in various education and professional development opportunities including TMEA (ETGMEA), CNAfME, and NAfME.
Web Page: music.utk.edu
The University of Tennessee Natalie L. Haslam College of Music offers a broad and comprehensive professional music program at both the undergraduate and graduate levels and is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music. The College has approximately 65 faculty members and approximately 400 music majors.
General Information:
The University of Tennessee, Knoxville, is the state’s flagship research institution, a campus of choice for outstanding undergraduates, and a premier graduate institution. As a land-grant university, it is committed to excellence in learning, scholarship, and engagement with society. In all its activities, the university aims to advance the frontiers of human knowledge and enrich and elevate society. Knoxville’s cultural resources include a symphony orchestra, an opera company, a professional jazz orchestra, theatrical productions, ballet and modern dance, art galleries, and museums. Within an hour’s drive is the Great Smoky Mountains National Park with its scenic beauty and wide variety of recreational activities, plants, and wildlife.
Qualifications:
Required Qualifications:
1) Doctorate/PhD or ABD in music education or related area; 2) at least three years of successful public school experience; 3) an emerging and/or established (dependent on rank of appointment) record of research, presentations, or scholarly/creative activity; 4) demonstrated abilities in organization, communication and working effectively with faculty, students, colleagues, and administrators.
Preferred Qualifications:
1) Successful teaching experience in a music teacher education program; 2) ability to lead classes in secondary general music or other specializations such as music technology or popular music pedagogy; 3) experience teaching graduate online music education courses; 4) experience with elementary music teaching methodologies.
Candidates for the rank of Assistant Professor must:
Meet the qualifications for being an Assistant Professor within UTK’s faculty handbook and the Natalie L. Haslam College of Music bylaws; these are covered in the above Required Qualifications.
Candidates for the rank of Associate Professor must:
Meet the qualifications for being an Associate Professor within UTK’s faculty handbook and the Natalie L. Haslam College of Music bylaws; these qualifications normally include having served as an assistant professor for at least 5 years and having served as mentor to junior faculty.
Candidates for the rank of Full Professor must:
Meet the qualifications for being a Full Professor within UTK’s faculty handbook and the Natalie L. Haslam College of Music bylaws; these qualifications normally include having served as an associate professor for at least 5 years and having served as mentor to junior faculty.
Application Instructions:
Review of applications will begin on October 22, 2026 and continue until the position is filled. Applicants should submit a one-page letter of interest that summarizes qualifications and interest in working in a student-centered music education program at the University of Tennessee, a list of 3-5 references with contact information, curriculum vitae, and a statement of teaching philosophy. Select candidates may be asked to provide brief examples of research and videos of collegiate teaching.
Contact ahuntoon@utk.edu with any questions.

Location:
Hanover, NH
Open Date:
Sep 25, 2026
Close Date:
Jan 1, 2027
Description:
Dartmouth Engineering seeks to fill an instructional faculty position at the assistant or associate professor level. Instructional faculty positions are non-tenure-line, promotion and sabbatical eligible positions, with a renewable 3-year term, and the option of a rolling contract upon successful review after 6 years. Instructional faculty are expected to teach 4-5 courses each year, advise students, and take on service responsibilities. While conducting scholarship is encouraged, a research program is not required.
About Thayer
Thayer School of Engineering is a dynamic community of scholars and teachers committed to addressing critical societal needs and solving the world's most pressing challenges through ground-breaking research, technology innovation, and cultivating future generations of engineers and leaders via educational excellence in the classroom and the laboratory. As Dartmouth's engineering school, Thayer is responsible for undergraduate and graduate engineering degrees. Our engineering sciences major is distinguished by the close integration of diverse disciplines and the liberal arts, emphasizing hands-on experiential learning, and human-centered engineering. As a professional school of engineering, Thayer also offers an ABET-accredited Bachelor of Engineering degree, master degrees in engineering and engineering management and a PhD degree program.
Dartmouth is a member of the Ivy League and consistently ranks among the world's great academic institutions. Home to a celebrated liberal arts curriculum and pioneering professional schools, Dartmouth has shaped the education landscape and prepared leaders through its inspirational learning experience. Dartmouth has forged a singular identity, combining its deep commitment to outstanding education with distinguished research and scholarship in the arts and sciences and its three leading professional schools — Geisel School of Medicine, Thayer School of Engineering, and Tuck School of Business. Furthermore, Dartmouth's PhD Innovation (PhD-I) Program is the nation's first doctoral-level program aimed at providing PhD students the skills and support necessary to engage in enterprising research and translate their work into the commercial sphere. For more information see http://engineering.dartmouth.edu.
Qualifications:
Applicants should have a doctorate in engineering or a related field and a demonstrated potential to teach a range of mechanical engineering courses. Example areas of interest include, but are not limited to, systems, solid mechanics, mechanical design, and sustainable design. Candidates will be excellent teachers who embrace Thayer's interdisciplinary, collaborative, project-based approach to engineering education.
Application Instructions:
Interested candidates should submit a cover letter, CV, statement of teaching interests and philosophy, and contact information for three references via Interfolio at: https://apply.interfolio.com/193985. Applications will be reviewed as received, and the application portal will close on 1/1/2027.
Inquiries about the position should be directed to the search chair Professor Vicki May at faculty.hiring@thayer.dartmouth.edu.

Dartmouth College is an equal opportunity employer under federal law. We prohibit discrimination on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, disability, veteran status, marital status, or any other legally protected status. Applications are welcome from all.
Dartmouth is committed to accessibility for its community. If you are an applicant with a disability and would like to request a reasonable accommodation to aid in the job application and/or interview process, please email: ADA@Dartmouth.edu. In the subject line, please state application accommodations and include the job number or title. Someone from the ADA/504 Office will be in touch within 2 business days.
For additional employment opportunities at Dartmouth College, please visit the Dartmouth Interfolio Job Board, the Office of the Provost, and the Office of Human Resources.
Offers of employment are contingent upon consent to a pre-employment background check with results acceptable under Dartmouth policy. Please visit the Dartmouth policy portal for faculty handbooks and details of other Dartmouth policies.

jobs.description:
Job Details
Description
The Department of Architecture at the University of Virginia School of Architecture (arch.virginia.edu) welcomes applications for a tenure-track position at the rank of Assistant Professor. We seek candidates with a transformative vision for architecture, articulated through a portfolio of innovative architectural design, scholarship, and teaching. The successful applicant is expected to bring a strong pedagogical approach, the potential for design leadership within and beyond the discipline of architecture, a developing research agenda rooted in professional and/or academic practice, and a genuine interest in working and teaching across disciplinary boundaries.
The Department of Architecture's mission is to educate and inspire the next generation of architectural leaders who understand our discipline as inseparable from the landscapes, cultures, environments, and histories in which we are situated. We actively encourage collaboration across the School of Architecture's disciplines, including with the Departments of Landscape Architecture, Urban and Environmental Planning, and Architectural History, as well as with the larger university. As a vital member of this vibrant community, the successful candidate will advance these aims through teaching, research, and collaboration with faculty and students.
Qualifiations
This is a full-time appointment, with the expectation that faculty will reside in Charlottesville and actively engage with faculty, staff, and students at the University. Successful candidates must hold a terminal degree in Architecture (MArch) or a comparable degree in a related design field (such as MLA, MUD, PHD). Tenure-track faculty at UVA are expected to develop curriculum in collaboration with school leadership, serve on academic committees, support student success, and pursue an agenda of high-profile research, scholarship, or creative production. Candidates should show clear potential to develop a rigorous, design-driven body of research and creative work over the course of their career at UVA. Candidates will be expected to teach core architecture design studios and additional courses.
Application Instructions
To apply for this position, attach the following:
Cover letter. Brief statement that outlines creative practice/research objectives and teaching goals
CV. Full curriculum vitae
Portfolio. Digital, including examples of work and teaching (size limit: 100mb)
Teaching Proposal. A one-page statement describing courses you have taught and your teaching approach, and new courses or curricular directions you would develop here
References. Names of three people who can be contacted about your design/academic work
Applications reviews will begin in late November and will remain open until the position is filled. For questions regarding this position, please contact Search Committee Chairs, Associate Professor Katie MacDonald at kmacdonald@virginia.edu and Department Chair, Professor Jeana Ripple at ripple@virginia.edu. For Interfolio-related assistance, please contact UVA HR.

The Department of Architecture at the University of Virginia School of Architecture (arch.virginia.edu) invites applications for a tenured position at the rank of Associate or Full Professor: the Commonwealth Professor of Architecture and Artificial Intelligence. We seek a thought leader poised to define how artificial intelligence and advanced technology is transforming not only the tools of architectural practice, but the terms of the conversation itself. The successful candidate will demonstrate leadership in design, pedagogy, and research; work fluidly across disciplinary boundaries; and advance discourse on AI's use and consequence, both within the discipline and at the school.

Initiatives across the university that offer collaborative opportunities include the Digital Technology for Democracy Lab, the National Security Data and Policy Institute, the Digital Humanities Center, and the Environmental Institute. The School of Architecture looks to advance this work by interrogating assumptions that have long defined our field and exploring how AI is redrawing the boundaries of design process, authorship, ethic, analysis, environmental and energy systems, and spatial outcomes.

Position Summary:
The UNC Lineberger Comprehensive Cancer Center and the UNC School of Medicine’s Department of Neurosurgery seek a full-time physician scientist, open-rank, faculty member specializing in the treatment and research of brain tumors to lead the Neurosurgical arm of the UNC Neuro-Oncology program. Ideal candidates will be fellowship-trained in Neurosurgical Oncology.
The National Cancer Institute (NCI) first designated the UNC Lineberger Comprehensive Cancer Center in 1990. UNC is one of only 40 Comprehensive Cancer Centers nationwide, and UNC Lineberger is the only public Comprehensive Cancer Center in North Carolina to have this designation. UNC Lineberger has been rated ‘exceptional’ by the NCI in its most recent reviews. The opportunities for both clinical practice and research are extensive and also leverage the excellence and proximity of the UNC Eshelman School of Pharmacy and Gillings School of Global Public Health. UNC Lineberger is the academic home to the cancer programs, and the clinical home is the North Carolina Cancer Hospital, a 320,000 square-foot dedicated cancer hospital opened in 2009, and across the street from UNC Lineberger. UNC Lineberger physicians have been offering multidisciplinary, patient-centered care for more than a quarter century, giving patients access to medical and patient support specialists in one place, often in one visit. UNC’s system has been used as a model by other cancer centers and oncology programs nationwide.
The Neuro-Oncology program boasts an established clinical practice comprising Neuro-Oncologists and Neurosurgeons with special expertise and interest in brain tumors, and dedicated Radiation Oncologists with research and clinical expertise in fractionated and stereotactic radiosurgery, working closely within this multidisciplinary structure. There is a robust clinical trials portfolio, a centralized clinical trials office providing broad research support and access to the Brain Tumor Trials Collaborative and the Alliance for Clinical Trials in Oncology.

M.D. required.

Ideal candidates will be fellowship trained in Neurosurgical Oncology.

Not Applicable.

Position Summary:
The Department of Neurosurgery at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (UNC) invites applications for a fellowship-trained Stereotactic and Functional Neurosurgeon to join our growing multidisciplinary program. The successful candidate will join a dynamic academic environment comprising 12 neurosurgeons with expertise across subspecialties, supported by robust clinical, research, and educational infrastructure within the UNC School of Medicine and UNC Health.
Neurosurgery Services:
Our neurosurgery services include treatment for aneurysms and cerebrovascular disease, brain tumor treatment, epilepsy and functional neurosurgery, spine and head trauma, hydrocephalus, pituitary and skull base surgery, spinal neurosurgery, pediatric and fetal neurosurgery.
The department has expanded in recent years with new neurosurgical faculty, including surgeon-scientists, master clinicians, and an extraordinarily talented multimedia medical illustration team. There is a new neurosurgical outpatient center at the ACC. UNC Health has acquired the latest technology, including the LITT, Robot, and high/low-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU/LIFU), and the department has established a new peripheral nerve and spinal oncology program. The department generated $2.52M in grant funding and received $2.95M in philanthropic support. In the last few years, the department has improved its standing in Blue Ridge and US News & World Report rankings.
Primary Responsibilities:
Provide surgical care for patients with epilepsy and movement disorders, in close collaboration with neurologists specializing in these areas.
Participate actively in the education and mentorship of residents, fellows, and medical students.
Contribute to the department’s research mission, focusing on understanding the mechanisms of neurological disorders, the biologic and physiologic basis of neurosurgical interventions, and advancing surgical techniques for epilepsy and functional disorders.
Engage in interdisciplinary collaborations across UNC’s neuroscience, imaging, and engineering communities.
A research support package including start-up resources and protected time will be provided in proportion to the candidate’s experience, academic achievements, and funding history.
Minimum Education and Experience Requirements:
MD or MD/PhD (or equivalent) from an accredited institution.
Board-certified or board-eligible by the American Board of Neurological Surgery.
Fellowship training in stereotactic and functional neurosurgery.
The ability to work effectively with neurosurgical, critical care, and other clinician partners is paramount.
The position requires that the candidate have, or be able to obtain, a medical license in the state of North Carolina and be credentialed to practice medicine at UNC Health Care System.
Preferred Qualifications, Competencies, and Experience:
Demonstrated expertise in the evaluation and surgical treatment of epilepsy.
Demonstrated expertise in microelectrode-guided deep brain stimulation (DBS). Expertise also in asleep DBS preferred.
Evidence of a strong clinical track record and commitment to academic productivity.
For senior candidates, a record of extramural funding, innovation, and impactful publications is highly desirable.

Clinical services will be delivered primarily through outpatient care settings using both in-person and telehealth modalities. Faculty rank will be commensurate with experience.

Primary Purpose of Organizational Unit:
The Department of Biostatistics (BIOS) is internationally recognized as a leader in Biostatistics research and training. It is one of eight departments in the Gillings School of Global Public Health whose mission is to improve public health, promote individual well-being and eliminate health inequities across North Carolina and around the world. This mission is accomplished through an outstanding program of collaborative teaching, research and service. The Department of Biostatistics is one of the largest, most complex departments at UNC, receiving over $45 million in research funding in FY24. Currently BIOS includes approximately 288 students (84 undergraduate, 204 graduate), approximately 100 permanent staff members, and 40 faculty members (30 with primary appointments in BIOS), as well as an additional 20 adjunct faculty members. The Department of Biostatistics is housed in two different locations: administrative and faculty offices, including a suite of offices for graduate students, in McGavran-Greenberg Hall and the Collaborative Studies Coordinating Center at Carolina Square.
Position Summary:
The Department of Biostatistics in the Gillings School of Global Public Health at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (UNC) is seeking two tenure-track or tenured faculty members, starting in Fall 2027. These 12-month full-time positions may be filled at the rank of Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor, depending on qualifications and experience. The department seeks exceptional candidates who can contribute to its academic and research missions. Successful applicants will be expected to develop and maintain externally funded research programs and to engage in the teaching, mentoring, and service activities of the department.
One position is expected to be filled at the Full Professor rank and will include appointment as Director of the UNC Gillings Center for Artificial Intelligence and Public Health, with a secondary appointment in the Department of Computer Science. This position is part of a UNC cluster hire on Safeguarding Artificial Intelligence in Health: Foundations, Uncertainty, and High Stakes Decision Making that includes three jointly appointed positions within the Department of Biostatistics, the Department of Computer Science, and the Department of Statistics and Operations Research. This cluster hire is structured to strengthen collaboration across these departments. The ideal candidate will provide intellectual leadership in AI safety for biomedical and public health applications, building on existing strengths in statistical machine learning, causal inference, and high dimensional data analysis. This individual will play a central leadership role in research, mentoring, and interdisciplinary collaboration, and will contribute to the continued growth and national visibility of AI in public health at UNC.

Doctorate in Biostatistics or related field.

Applicants should have broad research and teaching interests, the potential to direct PhD-level research, and the ability to engage in collaborative research with other faculty members at the University. The applicant should have excellent communication skills. Candidates with expertise in statistical methods in artificial intelligence are particularly encouraged to apply.
Campus Security Authority Responsibilities:
Not Applicable.

Detailed Position Information
STEM-related: We seek candidates from all areas of STEM who are dedicated, innovative teachers and can offer courses in our transdisciplinary honors curriculum. Minimum qualifications include (1) an earned doctorate or other terminal degree in Mathematics, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Technology, Engineering, Bio/Tech-ethics, or other STEM-related field and (2) teaching experience at the college/university level. The degree must be completed by the start of the appointment.
Interdisciplinary/Open Field: We seek candidates who can contribute to strengthening our range of interdisciplinarity, especially social science, business, and STEAM-oriented course offerings. Applicants must also be innovative teachers able to offer courses in our transdisciplinary honors curriculum. Minimum qualifications include (1) an earned doctorate or other terminal degree appropriate to their discipline and (2) teaching experience at the college/university level. The degree must be completed by the start of the appointment.
Minimum Qualifications
Honors faculty are expected to have the skills and techniques necessary to manage highly collaborative, student-centered learning, and facilitate rigorous dialogue across differing perspectives, both in and out of the classroom. The successful candidates should be able to build creative, transdisciplinary syllabi, foster dialogue among students, and help individual students hone their skills as critical and creative thinkers, citizens, and leaders.
We especially welcome applications from candidates with a background in any one or more of the following areas: first-year experience, experiential education, research/creative development, leadership studies, and transdisciplinary methods. In addition, we encourage candidates with experience mentoring students through extracurricular and/or co-curricular programming to apply.
For both positions, the initial contract is three years, with review in the third year; rank promotion is possible. The normal teaching load is 12 credits per semester, with expectations for scholarship, committee service, and contributions to the overall academic and co-curricular life of the college. Scholarship may be in the areas of engagement, teaching and learning, and/or the applicant’s disciplinary area, including but not limited to public scholarship, innovative methodological/pedagogical approaches, peer-reviewed journal articles, books, book chapters, creative work, and conference presentations. While lab space and start-up packages are unavailable, successful candidates will receive other forms of support for research, teaching, and professional development.
Preferred Qualifications
Instructions and Required Materials for Application
Applicants should submit a cover letter expressing their interest in the specific position to which they are applying, teaching philosophy statement, CV, contact information for three academic references, and one to three recent teaching evaluations (if available). We will begin reviewing applications on October 23, 2026, and continue until the position is filled. Please direct questions to the search chair, Dr. Tara Mock, at tmock@ua.edu.
About the Division/College/School
The University of Alabama Honors College, ranked as one of the top 10 honors colleges in the nation, invites applications for two faculty positions at the rank of assistant professor of Honors: one STEM-related, one open specialty. These are full-time appointments at the level of Teaching Assistant Professor (non-tenured, renewable contract). They will be expected to teach a variety of honors classes and will have opportunities to develop and teach seminar classes based on their area of expertise.

Position Summary
The Department of Communication Studies in the College of Communication & Information Sciences at The University of Alabama invites applications for a nine-month tenure-track Assistant Professor in Organizational Communication, to begin August 2027. The Department of Communication Studies emphasizes a broad understanding of the power of communication by studying theory and practice in the areas of communication and culture, interpersonal communication, organizational leadership, and rhetoric and political discourse. We are committed to cultivating responsible, informed, and civically minded students who will be future leaders in their communities and workplaces.
Detailed Position Information
Organizational Communication research is strategically relevant with significant potential to enhance the national and international reputation of our university, college, and department via cutting-edge research and collaborations with our university’s new School of Leadership and Policy and our college’s Plank Center for Leadership in Public Relations. Applicants should pursue, or plan to pursue, external funding to support their research. This position is designed to elevate the department's research impact on the horizons of organizational communication and related interdisciplinary areas. This position also builds on the department's growing online MA program with an emphasis in organizational leadership and our current faculty strengths in organizational communication. The ideal candidate will advance a program of research in organizational communication and pursue extramural funding through foundation and corporate partnerships. We are particularly interested in applicants with expertise in areas such as:
● Leadership communication
● Organizational assessment/improvement
● Organizational resilience
● Executive communication
● GenAI, emerging technologies, and future of work in organizations
● Interdisciplinary areas that strengthen understandings of organizational communication
Candidates with other research interests related to organizational communication broadly are also encouraged to apply. Candidates with interdisciplinary interests should highlight their accomplishments for this position.
Applicants must display an ability to be an active and involved member of a highly collaborative faculty team. The successful hire will teach two courses each fall and spring semester, which may include undergraduate and master's-level courses, including contributions to the department's online MA program in organizational leadership. Our college has an interdisciplinary doctoral program and faculty have the opportunity to teach seminars and collaborate with doctoral students.
Minimum Qualifications
Applicants must have:
● Ph.D. in Communication or a related field completed by appointment start date. ABD at the time of application will be considered.

jobs.description:
Job Details
Job Title
Assistant Professor of Supply Chain Management
Agency
Texas A&M University - Central Texas
Department
College of Business Administration
Proposed Minimum Salary
Commensurate
Job Location
Killeen, Texas
Job Type
Faculty
Job Description
The College of Business Administration (COBA) at Texas A&M University-Central Texas welcomes highly qualified applicants to fill an immediate need for an Assistant Professor of Supply Chain Management starting in Fall 2027. This is a tenure-track faculty position. Application reviews will begin immediately. We are looking for a collegial teacher-scholar with a passion for teaching and a multi-faceted track record of excellence both within and beyond the classroom. Our greatest and immediate teaching need is for undergraduate courses in support of our brand-new BBA in Logistics & Supply Chain Management program. Our hope is that this faculty member will help establish this as a strong program with great student outcomes and robust regional industry connections. Courses at other levels and in other related areas may also be available on a limited basis depending on applicant qualifications and interest.
About Texas A&M University – Central Texas
Established as an independent member of the Texas A&M University System in 2009, A&M-Central Texas is a friendly and dynamic regional teaching institution that prides itself on excellence in instruction but also embraces a growing emphasis on research. A&M-Central Texas is truly unique in that it is an upper- and masters-level institution, offering only junior- and senior-level coursework needed to successfully complete baccalaureate degrees and all coursework leading to the completion of master’s degrees. As such, A&M-Central Texas maintains active partnerships with the major community colleges within the Greater Austin and Central Texas regions, as well as with Fort Hood, a premier outpost of the U.S. Army and one of the largest military installations in the world. Our multifaceted student demographic includes a significant proportion of first-generation college students, non-traditional learners, and military-affiliated personnel.
The College of Business Administration is accredited by AACSB, and we are eager to have energetic and collegial new faculty members partner with us in pursuit of our major strategic initiatives, of which there are many on the near horizon (most notably, a DBA program anticipated to launch Fall 2027 pending SACSCOC final approval). This is an exciting time of rapid change within the University and College that affords new faculty members many opportunities to make an immediate, significant, and lasting impact.
A&M-Central Texas is located on the southern edge of Killeen, TX, a city of approximately 150,000 located about halfway between Austin and Waco—about 60 miles either way. Our faculty members enjoy a wide variety of living options by virtue of the range of communities in the area—from quiet and rural to bustling and cosmopolitan. It is an easy drive to great art, food, shopping, and night life as well as to hunting, fishing, hiking, and camping for those who prefer the outdoors. Central Texas is a rapidly growing region with a booming economy, but is also a great place for families, with many options for schooling, worship, civic engagement, and recreation. It also has modest traffic and a reasonable cost of living. The major metropolitan areas of Houston, Dallas-Fort Worth, and San Antonio are all within a 3-hour radius of Killeen.
Responsibilities:
The candidate will be expected to provide quality, engaging instruction for typically three courses per term, primarily at the undergraduate level and in a variety of course delivery formats (face-to-face, online, or hybrid), with fully online being the most in-demand option at present. Candidates who possess exceptional skill at making technical content accessible to a broad audience are especially desired. The candidate will be expected to teach the following courses: LSCM 4321 Production and Operations Management, LSCM 4322 Business Process, Quality, and Lean Management, LSCM 4326 Global Procurement and Strategic Sourcing. Other assigned courses may include LSCM 4323 Supply Chain Management and BUSI 3311 Business Statistics. Additional summer teaching opportunities may be available depending on student demand and department needs.
Some scholarly contributions are also required. The candidate is expected have sufficient scholarly and/or professional activities to have “scholarly academic” status upon arrival per AACSB faculty classifications, and to have a healthy pipeline of works in progress toward publication, where health is measured more by viability and anticipated impact than by number and/or status. Scholarship is but one category of currency and impact with which faculty may engage: others include maintaining a recognized professional certification, presenting at academic conferences, engaging in consulting or other industry-related activities, and completing other relevant professional training and development activities. Professional development funds are available to support all of these endeavors, and faculty within the College frequently collaborate on research projects together.
In regard to service, faculty are expected to support their program(s), department, college, and/or university with committee work, but first-year faculty are exempt from this. In addition, faculty are expected to have some sort of service to their profession and/or to the community, but again, service contribution impact and quality are more important than the numbers of activities engaged in. Faculty generally have a lot of discretion in determining how best they can add value through their various service activities.
A Presidential Proclamation issued on September 19, 2025, imposes a $100,000 fee on all new H‑1B petitions filed after September 21, 2025, and Texas A&M University–Central Texas will not pay this fee. Additionally, a moratorium issued by Governor Abbott on January 27, 2026, restricts the filing of new H‑1B petitions unless approved by the Texas Workforce Commission. Accordingly, if you will now or in the future require sponsorship for employment visa status this moratorium may affect our ability to employ you should you be selected as the final candidate. Applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer.
Minimum Qualifications:
To be eligible to apply for this position, candidates should:
Possess a terminal degree (doctorate) in supply chain management or a closely related discipline from a regionally accredited university.
Be eligible for the AACSB “scholarly academic” faculty classification (two publications or relevant terminal degree completed since 2022, with viable works in progress).
Have a documented track record of successfully teaching supply chain or operations courses, including in fully online formats.
Be qualified to teach LSCM 4321, LSCM 4322, and LSCM 4326.
Preferred Qualifications:
The ideal candidate for this position would also possess:
At least three (3) years of full-time collegiate teaching experience.
Industry experience.
Experience developing industry connections in support of academic programs.
Proficiency in creating original and engaging online course instructional materials.
Qualifications to teach LSCM 4323 and BUSI 3311.
Great administrative, organizational, and interpersonal skills to support successful instruction to a largely non-traditional, first-generation, and military-affiliated student body.
Familiarity/experience with DBA programs and/or supervision of doctoral students.
Salary: Commensurate
Hours: Faculty hours; M-F; hours may vary by assignment and course modality.
To Apply:
Please apply directly on our Texas A&M University-Central Texas Job Site. Applicants are required to submit a cover letter, curriculum vitae (CV), and either the contact information for three professional references or three letters of recommendation. Additional materials, such as a teaching philosophy statement and transcripts, are optional but strongly encouraged.
All positions are security-sensitive. Applicants are subject to a criminal history investigation, and employment is contingent upon the institution’s verification of credentials and/or other information required by the institution’s procedures, including the completion of the criminal history check.
Equal Opportunity/Veterans/Disability Employer.

Job Summary
The Art program invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position in Animation at the rank of Assistant Professor or Associate Professor, contingent upon qualifications and professional experience. The successful candidate will begin employment on August 1, 2027. This position involves teaching animation courses across undergraduate levels, contributing to curriculum design and enhancement, supporting student success, participating in service activities, and maintaining an active research and creative agenda. We seek a dedicated educator who fosters creativity and innovation, promotes student growth, and integrates contemporary industry practices into both instruction and program development within this specialized area of study.
Commitment to Excellence: The successful candidate will contribute to a dynamic and evolving Animation program through outstanding teaching, student mentorship, creative scholarship, service, and engagement with both the university and broader community. The position offers an opportunity to help shape the future direction of animation education while preparing students for success in contemporary creative industries.
Responsibilities
Key responsibilities associated with this position include:
Teaching a range of Animation courses across all levels.
Advising and mentoring students regarding academic and professional development.
Developing and supporting internship opportunities that enhance student career readiness.
Contributing to program planning, assessment, and curriculum development initiatives.
Assisting with the recruitment and retention of a diverse student population.
Engaging with community partners and supporting outreach efforts.
Advancing the mission and goals of the Art Program and the University of West Georgia.
Assisting in the management of animation studios, labs, and related equipment.
Supervising and coordinating student employees.
Participating in departmental, college, and university service activities.
Required Qualifications
Required Qualifications:
A terminal degree in Animation or an equivalent field prior to August 2027.
Demonstrated proficiency with industry-standard animation software, technologies, workflows, and professional practices.
Extensive experience in animation fundamentals, including both traditional and digital approaches to animation.
Ideal Candidate Profile Preferred candidates will demonstrate expertise in two or more of the following areas:
2D Animation
3D Modeling and Animation
Stop-Motion Animation
Storyboarding
Digital Illustration
Character Design
Visual Storytelling
Animation Pipeline Development and Production Workflows Additionally, successful candidates should:
Demonstrate experience and/or a strong commitment to teaching and mentoring students from diverse backgrounds and demographics.
Possess substantial knowledge of the history of animation as well as current trends, issues, and developments within the field.
Show strong potential for excellence in teaching, service, student success initiatives, and research or creative scholarship.
Preferred Qualifications
Preferred Qualifications
Preference will be given to candidates with demonstrated experience in one or more of the following areas:
University-level teaching experience beyond graduate assistant responsibilities
Collaborative creative practice and/or collaborative teaching environments.
Curriculum design, development, and assessment.
Instruction in animation fundamentals, including both traditional methodologies and contemporary industry practices.
Application and integration of emerging technologies relevant to the animation discipline.
Proposed Salary
Salary is commensurate with experience.

Cover Letter
Curriculum Vitae Professional Portfolio
A single PDF containing:
Twenty (20) images or equivalent amount of time-based work.
Materials may include still frames, sketches, storyboards, illustrations, animation samples, or other examples demonstrating professional creative achievement.

Twenty (20) images or equivalent amount of time-based work created by students.

Note: When alternative presentation formats are necessary, applicants should include links within the PDF to external portfolio platforms such as Vimeo, YouTube, personal websites, or similar repositories. Any required passwords or access credentials should be provided.

Submit the following as three separate PDF documents:
Teaching Statement or Teaching Philosophy

Copies of all academic transcripts.
Official transcripts will be required from finalists.
