jobs.title: SUSMAT-RC - Assistant Professor in Bio Chemical Process Design and Engineering
jobs.description:
About Mohammed VI Polytechnic University (UM6P)
Mohammed VI Polytechnic University (UM6P) is an internationally oriented institution of higher learning, that is committed to an educational system based on the highest standards of teaching and research in fields related to the sustainable economic development of Morocco and Africa. UM6P is an institution oriented towards applied research and innovation. On a specific focus on Africa, UM6P aims to position these fields as the forefront and become a university of international standing.
More than just a traditional academic institution, UM6P is a platform for experimentation and a pool of opportunities, for students, professors and staff. It offers a high-quality living and study environment thanks to its state-of-the-art infrastructure. With an innovative approach, UM6P places research and innovation at the heart of its educational project as a driving force of a business model.
In its research approach, the UM6P promotes transdisciplinary, entrepreneurship spirit and collaboration with external institutions for developing up to date science and at continent level in order to address real challenges.
All our programs run as start-ups and can be self-organized when they reach a critical mass. Thus, academic liberty is promoted as far as funding is developed by research teams.
The research programs are integrated from long-term research to short-term applications in linkage with incubation and start-up ecosystems.
About the Chemical & Biochemical Sciences Green Process Engineering (CBS)
The Chemical & Biochemical Sciences Green Process Engineering Department (CBS) is a component of the Mohammed VI Polytechnic University (UM6P). The main objective of CBS is to set up a distinctive research-teaching program, of international level, to meet the research and teaching challenges of UM6P, in particular on green and environmental chemistry applied to all aspects of chemical sciences: organic and inorganic chemistry, analytical chemistry, chemical biology, biochemical and thermal reactions.
Research at CBS is organized around several major areas, which aim to answer challenging industrial questions, from complex chemical and biochemical reactions to scale-up and validation of process engineering. CBS projects aim at an in-depth understanding of the molecular mechanisms of all transformations in order to propose new original alternatives in terms of efficiency, environmental friendliness and sustainability.
Job description
The successful candidate will be responsible for designing, simulating, implementing and optimizing chemical and biochemical processes, especially continuous ones with applications in the chemical, agriculture, and biotechnological industries. SNG is looking for an enthusiastic, experienced, and entrepreneurial candidate to meet the goals of the research group. The incumbent will be expected to:
Lead the group s activities chemical process design, simulation, implementation, and optimization, at the macro-lab, pre-pilot, and pilot scales.
Closely interact with scientist, engineers, and entrepreneurs in the SNG and UM6P, as well as with external clients and collaborators.
Actively contribute to the entrepreneurial activities of the group. This is a unique and challenging opportunity to bridge R&D and entrepreneurship in a multidisciplinary and collaborative ecosystem, and to advance the development of use-inspired R&D at UM6P.
Proactively engage in collaborative R&D by providing solutions and demonstrating the potential bio/chemical process engineering in addressing important Moroccan technology challenges.
Supervise graduate students and/or postdoctoral fellows.
Prepare technical reports, manuscripts, and invention disclosures, and present results in relevant conferences.
Assist with the drafting of research proposals.
Assist with the management and administration of the SNG. The successful candidate will participate in progress review meetings, reports, and discuss results and explore opportunities for new activities consistent with the group s programmatic priorities.
Key duties
The successful candidate is expected to lead all aspects of bio/chemical process engineering, notably:
Develop new industrial processes and design new process plants and equipment or modify/optimize existing ones.
Test new processes, collect data required to make improvements and modifications, oversee the construction, supervise the operation of new pre-pilot/pilot plants, purchase and install equipment, and liaise with installation/project engineers and specialists.
Investigate and troubleshoot plant/process problems. Ensure that equipment works to its specification and to appropriate capacities
Assess safety and environmental issues and ensure safe working conditions and compliance with health and safety legislation.
Schedule and coordinate work to tight deadlines and within financial budgets.
Design and develop continuous manufacturing processes along with the layout and equipment for pre-pilot/pilot plants. This includes creating and setting specifications, developing, implementing, and monitoring this equipment as part of the manufacturing system.
Use of simulation software in the development of new processes
The successful candidate is also expected to:
Contribute to building a vibrant and sustainable entrepreneurial ecosystem at UM6P by translating, integrating, and assimilating sustainable academic innovations into commercial opportunities.
Deliver process engineering solutions to enable rapid evolution of academic research through the various TRL levels from innovation to product manufacturing (TRL 5-9).
Identify and engage potential partners to explore commercial opportunities for UM6P s entrepreneurial ecosystem by establishing good working relationships with collaborators, research institution, industry partners and government agencies.
Assist or lead the identification of new and more efficient bio/chemical processes.
Assist the PI and group members in writing manuscripts for publication, filing patents, and developing research proposals to acquire relevant equipment or expand research programs consistent with the programmatic priorities of the SNG.
Assist in the management and administration of the SNG. This activity may include several components, notably (a) collect, analyze, and summarize scientific literature relevant to a given project, (b) develop specific sections in relevant areas of expertise for a given proposal, (c) coordinate the organization of proposal applications in specific area of expertise.
Co-supervise research progress of graduate students, engineers, technicians, and/or postdoctoral fellows. This activity entails regular discussion with group members to ensure they are making progress in their research investigations, notably in the candidate s area of expertise. Discuss with the PI any challenges and roadblocks and ensure that the proposed solutions are implemented and followed upon.
Effectively communicate in English (verbally and in writing) to disseminate knowledge to group members, clients, and collaborators and/or to represent the SNG at conferences, meetings, and/or workshops.
Criteria of the candidate
R&D experience:
PhD in chemical engineering, materials engineering, mechanical engineering, or related areas from a recognized university with a focus on process engineering and its applications in the chemical, cements, fertilizers, and/or paints industries. Candidates with an engineering degree and at least 5 years of professional experience in R&D and process engineering may also apply.
Thorough knowledge of the key components of a bio/chemical process system (e.g. piping, pumps, tanks, flow valves, steam valves, temperature gauges, boilers, vessels, reactor vessels, crackers, distillation columns, heat exchangers, boilers, steam pipes, autoclaves, clarifiers, decanters, fluidised dryers, Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs), Proportional Integral Derivative (PID) Controllers).
Mastery of process simulation software (e.g. Aspen, ProSim, UniSim, ChemCAD, Mathworks) to work out the best production methods.
Knowledge of scientific principles related to magnitude, momentum, and heat transfer.
Thorough knowledge of analytical chemistry techniques with a demonstrated ability to solve highly technical problems.
Familiarity with process improvement methodologies (Six Sigma, lean manufacturing)
Ability to execute tasks with minimal oversight
Excellent publication (or patent) portfolio and R&D record.
Experience in supervising engineers, graduate students and/or postdoctoral fellows.
Demonstrated ability to organize/analyze/interpret results and assess whether additional investigations are necessary to reach the project s aims.
Evidence of collaboration with peers at national and/or international institutions.
Familiarity with some of the main Moroccan industries (notably chemical, cements, fertilizers, paints, recycling).
Teaching experience with the capacity to develop new courses (learning by doing) is desirable.
Entrepreneurial experience:
First-hand experience in entrepreneurship and awareness of the current Moroccan entrepreneurial ecosystem.
First-hand experience in market analysis, customer discovery, fundraising, developing business plans, developing IP strategy and new product certification for startups.
Experience in creating pitch decks for investors and potential customers.
Experience in launching technology start-ups including essential elements such as prototyping/product visualization and early-stage venture funding.
Evidence of participation in entrepreneurial programs.
Solid managerial skills and ability to take the initiative to advance the team s goals.
Awareness of Moroccan/African market and product development opportunities.
Experience with the incubation and start-up ecosystems in Morocco desirable.
Personal attributes
Understands and works towards team objectives.
Meets deadlines and displays strong administrative and organizational skills.
Strong initiative, self-motivated, and focused on achieving quality outputs (in R&D and entrepreneurship).
Ability to work effectively with a wide range of individuals, including faculty, students, industry executives, entrepreneurs, and investors.
Demonstrated ability to work on multiple projects at any given time.
Strong English and French communication skills, both verbal and written, are required.
While OCP group, a world leader in fertilizer production, is a privileged client for the University, a growing portfolio of clients is driving the development of a rich R&D ecosystem around the university. UM6P enjoys ample research funding, moderate teaching load, and excellent facilities. The university promotes multidisciplinary R&D, entrepreneurship and collaboration with external institutions and clients with the aim of advancing the Moroccan and African economies.
UM6P oﬀers highly competitive incentives to its current and future talented research staff.

Open Rank Position

Mohammed VI Polytechnic University (UM6P) is an internationally oriented institution of higher learning, that is committed to an educational system based on the highest standards of teaching and research in fields related to the sustainable economic development of Morocco and Africa. About the Sustainable Materials Research Center (SusMat - RC)
The Sustainable Materials Research Center (SusMat - RC) is a multidisciplinary research center engaged in the development of advanced biobased products and materials thereof using biotechnological, physical and chemical conversion strategies and engineering processes (b) understanding and controlling their underlying specific functionalities and the structure-properties relationship acting over multiple length scales from the molecular, nano to the macro level and their cross-interactions and (c) utilizing the gathered knowledge and the invented materials to address key technological challenges in Morocco and African continent and assist the transition toward a green and circular economy.
Job Description
The Sustainable Materials Research Center (SUSMAT-RC) at UM6P invites applications for a faculty position in Chemistry, Polymer Science, and Materials Science. Applicants with expertise in, but not limited to, Interface and Colloid Science, Emulsions, Coatings, Encapsulation, Surface Chemistry, Polymer Chemistry, and Molecular and Nanoscale Science are particularly invited to apply. The successful candidate will plan, develop and conduct applied research projects dedicated to Interfaces and Colloids in green chemistry and chemical engineering focusing on the synthesis, processing, and testing of new biobased monomers, polymers, and materials. As a rapidly growing research center, an ideal candidate for this role will be self-motivated, organized, and able to work in ambiguous and changeable situations. A minimum experience of 5 years after the completion of the PhD is required to be eligible for this position.
Key Duties
The successful candidate is expected to have:
Lead all aspects related to Interfaces and Colloids Science within SUSMAT RC.
Transfer the knowledge and findings related to interfaces and colloids to researchers at UM6P, external clients and/or collaborators when required.
Collaborate with SUSMAT RC researchers through the identification and development of new concepts to be applied to sustainable materials and derivatives and their industrial applications thereof.
Design and teach advanced courses related to interfacial chemistry, emulsions, colloids and interfaces for the benefit of Master and PhD students at UM6P,
Assist in the delivery of engineering solutions to enable the rapid evolution of applied research through the various TRL levels to development and manufacturing (TRL 3-9).
Work with members of SUSMAT RC, other faculty members, companies, and different consortia to identify concepts to rapidly test and translate research innovations to products and/or processes for commercialization.
Collaborate with other members of SUSMAT RC in writing manuscripts for publication, filing patents, and developing research proposals to expand research programs consistent with the strategic vision of the center.
Assist in the management and administration of the SUSMAT RC. This activity may include several components, notably (a) collect, analyze, and summarize scientific literature relevant to a given project/technology, (b) develop specific sections in relevant areas of expertise for a given proposal, (c) coordinate the organization of proposal applications in specific area of expertise.
Co-supervise research progress of graduate students and/or postdoctoral fellows. This activity entails regular discussion with group members to ensure they are making progress in their R&D investigations notably in the candidate s area of expertise.
Discuss with the director any challenges and roadblocks and ensure that the proposed solutions are implemented and followed upon.
Work with universities, companies, and different consortia to lead groundbreaking R&D for next generation sustainable materials.
Effectively communicate in English (verbally and in writing) to disseminate knowledge to group members, clients, and collaborators and/or to represent the SUSMAT RC at conferences, meetings, and/or workshops.
Proactively engage in collaborative R&D by providing solutions and demonstrating the potential of polymer science and engineering in addressing important Moroccan technology challenges.
Candidate Criteria
To be considered for this role, you will ideally have:
Educational background:
Ph.D. in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Polymer Science, Colloids and Interfaces Science, Soft Matter, or a closely related field
Experience and Skills:
At least 5 years of professional experience including post-doctoral with recognized expertise in Colloids and Interfaces Science, and industrial experience would be a strong asset.
Demonstrated skills in Interface and Colloid Science, Emulsions, Coatings, Surface Chemistry, Polymer Chemistry, and Molecular and Nanoscale Science.
In-depth knowledge of material rheology is essential
Good experience with (bio)polymer chemistry, nanocomposite science, and processing of (bio)polymers and (bio)composites.
Demonstrated ability to effectively develop, lead and maintain research programs.
Good teaching experience with the capacity to develop new courses and connect research to teaching (learning by doing) is desirable.
Good experience in the supervision of students from the M.Sc. and Ph.D. programs.
Good leadership and project management skills in driving the full project trajectory from conceptualization to implementation by applying managerial and scientific principles,
Evidence of collaboration with peers at national and/or international institutions,
Familiarity with the institutional and industrial ecosystem of Morocco,
First-hands experience in entrepreneurship, in launching technology start-ups including essential elements such as prototyping/product visualization and early-stage venture funding would be a strong asset,
First-hands experience in entrepreneurship or evidence of participation in entrepreneurial programs.
Awareness of Moroccan/African market and product development opportunities.
Personal Attributes
Be autonomous, detail-oriented, and possess strong organizational skills problem-solving attitudes
Strong initiative, self-motivated, and commitment to achieving quality outputs and excellence.
Demonstrated bounding to diversity and professional integrity.
Demonstrated excellent interpersonal skills and be a good team player
Ability to work effectively with a wide range of individuals, including university professors, industry executives, entrepreneurs, etc
Fluent in English and French, both spoken and written
Application and Selection:
The application folder must contain:
Detailed CV,
Cover letter along with a synthetic presentation of the background, research works, projects and activities, publications, key achievements,
Research and teaching plans, entrepreneurial ideas and concepts if any, and services to UM6P community: max 3-4 pages,
Contact information of 3 referees.
Our Offer
Very competitive salary and benefits package.
A unique set of research partners and collaborators.
Access to a pool of highly motivated and rigorously selected Master and PhD students with financial support.

jobs.title: Faculty Position in International Economics, Open Rank
jobs.description:
Faculty Position in International Economics, Open Rank
Location: Qatar
Open Date: Sep 22, 2026
Deadline:
Description
Georgetown University in Qatar (GU-Q) invites applications for one (1) open-rank core faculty position in International Economics.
We welcome applications from candidates in all fields of economics, with a preference for candidates conducting applied and empirically relevant research. This may include, but is not limited to, fields such as international economics, development economics, behavioral economics, labor economics, political economy, and applied microeconomics and macroeconomics. Applicants should demonstrate a strong research profile, evidenced by a substantial record of high-quality research accomplishments or, for more junior candidates, clear evidence of the potential to develop such a record. Candidates should also have an ambitious and active research agenda and a strong record of teaching excellence.
Appointment will be at the rank of Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, or Professor, depending on the candidate's experience and qualifications.
Qualifications
A Ph.D. in Economics.
A strong and active research agenda, with a demonstrated record of publication in leading economics journals or, for junior candidates, clear evidence of the potential to establish such a record.
A strong commitment to excellence in teaching and mentoring, demonstrated through previous teaching experience and, for senior candidates, a sustained record of teaching effectiveness and student mentorship.
Academic Environment and Faculty Support
GU-Q offers a rich academic setting supported by strong institutional resources to enable excellence in teaching and research. Faculty typically teach two courses (or 6 credit hours) per semester (a 2-2 load), supported by best-in-class instructional infrastructure. This includes the Global Classroom, which connects students in Doha with peers in Washington, D.C., for live, cross-campus engagement, and access to collaborative research centers such as the Center for International and Regional Studies (CIRS).
To advance faculty scholarship and professional development, GU-Q provides:
Access to GU-Q faculty research funds.
Eligibility for funding through the Qatar Research, Development, and Innovation Council (QRDI).
Eligibility to apply for a summer research supplement equivalent to 2/9 of base salary.
Generous conference travel funding and professional development resources.
Compensation and Benefits
GU-Q offers a highly competitive compensation package by U.S. academic standards, along with an exceptional expatriate benefits package that includes:
Fully furnished, high-quality housing.
Transportation allowance.
Annual family home leave.
Worldwide health insurance coverage.
Private school tuition support for accompanying children.
Additional relocation and onboarding assistance.
About Georgetown University in Qatar
GU-Q was established in 2005 alongside other elite international universities in Education City, in partnership with Qatar Foundation. GU-Q is an integral part of Georgetown University, delivering the renowned School of Foreign Service's Bachelor of Science in Foreign Service (BSFS) degree. Ranked first in the world in international relations by Foreign Policy magazine, this liberal arts program offers majors in International Politics, International History, Culture and Politics, International Economics, and Science, Technology, and International Affairs. The degree is awarded by Georgetown University in Washington, D.C. GU-Q is a research-focused, student-oriented institution with a globally competitive research and publications record. GU-Q values interdisciplinarity, and its faculty and students benefit from the opportunities offered by the wider academic ecosystem of Education City. For more information on GU-Q, see https://www.qatar.georgetown.edu.
Life in Qatar
Qatar offers a diverse, family-friendly living environment, with the cultural, educational, and recreational resources of a major global city. Public parks, beaches, sports facilities (including Education City's extensive sports venues), museums, cafes, and restaurants abound, and a state-of-the-art metro system connects all parts of Doha and nearby locations. Within Education City, the iconic Qatar National Library, designed by Rem Koolhaas, provides free membership to faculty and students. Faculty at GU-Q also benefit from a close-knit Georgetown community, strong institutional support, and regular coordination between Doha and Washington, D.C. While the early months of 2026 brought instability to the region, Doha remains one of the safest cities in the world, and Qatar continues to rank highly in the Global Peace Index. Doha is connected by direct flights to more than 160 destinations in 90 countries. This short video offers a glimpse of what it is like to teach and live in Qatar.
Application Process
Review of applications will begin on October 15, 2026, and continue until the position is filled. Applicants should provide a cover letter detailing teaching and research interests, curriculum vitae, the names and contact details of three scholarly references, and, if available, evidence of teaching excellence (such as recent student course ratings, peer observation reports, etc.).
All application materials must be submitted via Georgetown's online application management system at https://apply.interfolio.com/194081.
Questions about the online application system should be directed to Ms. Carina Lawson at cl978@georgetown.edu. Queries about the position should be directed to Professor Ramon Cobo Reyes Cano at rc1557@georgetown.edu. Please reference "International Economics" in the subject line.

You also can also contact the Office for Equal Opportunity Compliance at (202) 687-4798 or oeoc@georgetown.edu.

jobs.title: Tenure-Track Faculty 2026-2027
jobs.description:
Johns Hopkins University has made a major new investment in Data Science and AI. The investment will add 150 new faculty positions, including 30 Bloomberg Distinguished Professorships. The University has established the Data Science and AI Institute (DSAI Institute). A new half-million square foot building is being constructed and an unparalleled computational infrastructure is now operational . This expansion will establish Johns Hopkins as one of the largest and leading engineering schools with a top AI research program. The expansion will double the Department of Applied Mathematics and Statistics from 20 full-time regular faculty in 2023 to 40 by 2028.
This search is to fill faculty positions in the DSAI Institute. We invite applications for tenured or tenure-track faculty positions in all areas of the Mathematical Sciences. Preference will be given to candidates whose research has made an impact on data science, machine learning, and artificial intelligence. Outstanding candidates at all academic ranks will be considered. The successful candidate will have a tenure home in the Department of Applied Mathematics and Statistics. A joint appointment with another department is also possible. We anticipate making multiple offers.
Candidates must hold a Ph.D. in Applied Mathematics, Statistics, or related fields, and will be expected to establish a strong, independent, multidisciplinary, and internationally recognized research program. Commitment to teaching excellence at the undergraduate and graduate levels, and a dedication to creating an inclusive and supportive educational environment for all students is expected.
At Johns Hopkins, we value interdisciplinary collaboration. Faculty at the Whiting School of Engineering are united by a shared commitment to scientific discovery, teaching excellence, and transformative knowledge that contributes to the betterment of society. Successful candidates will find rich opportunities to engage with colleagues across the University, including the Data Science and AI Institute, the Mathematical Institute for Data Science, the SNF Agora Institute, the Carey Business School, Johns Hopkins School of Medicine, Krieger School of Arts and Sciences, Bloomberg School of Public Health, and Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory.
The expected salary range for this position is: Assistant Professors $160k-$200k, Associate Professors $180k-$250k, Full Professors $220k-$450k, for 12-month FTE. The referenced salary range is based on Johns Hopkins University's good faith belief at the time of posting. The actual compensation offered to the selected candidate may vary and will be based on factors including, but not limited to, the experience and qualifications of the selected candidate - e.g., years in rank, training, field, discipline, other work experience, and other similar factors; geographic location; internal equity; external market conditions; and other factors as reasonably determined by the University.
We offer dual career programs that support spousal/partner placement within the university and the broader Baltimore/Washington area.
All applicants should submit their application online at
https://apply.interfolio.com/194226
Electronic applications should include a cover letter describing the principal expertise of the applicant, a statement of teaching interests, a statement of research interests, a complete resume, and a publication list. Applications at the Assistant Professor level should also include at least three reference letters. Applications at the Associate or Full Professor levels need not include reference letters or names at this stage.
Applications submitted by December 1, 2026, will receive full consideration. The department will begin reviewing applications on November 1, 2026 and may take early action to schedule fall semester interviews.
Salary Range
The referenced salary range represents the minimum and maximum salaries for this position and is based on Johns Hopkins University's good faith belief at the time of posting. Not all candidates will be eligible for the upper end of the salary range. The actual compensation offered to the selected candidate may vary and will ultimately depend on multiple factors, which may include the successful candidate's geographic location, skills, work experience, internal equity, market conditions, education/training and other factors, as reasonably determined by the University.
Total Rewards

jobs.title: Teaching Faculty of Latin American, Latino & Iberian Studies
jobs.description:
Job Details
The Department of Latin American, Latino & Iberian Studies in the School of Arts & Sciences at the University of Richmond invites applications for a teaching faculty member to begin in the 2027-2028 academic year. This is a full-time, non-tenure-track, continuing position with benefits.
The candidate will teach 6 units per year, whereby 2 units often constitute a single intensive class that meets five times per week. The department's interdisciplinary curriculum highlights the cultural and linguistic diversity of the Spanish-speaking world and is committed to excellence in undergraduate teaching at all levels of the curriculum. The beginning and intermediate language courses that this candidate will teach develop students' linguistic and intercultural competence, thereby fulfilling an important requirement of our General Education curriculum, the Web of Inquiry, and prepare students for more advanced courses in support of the University's mission. While not required, the candidate will also have the occasional opportunity to teach more advanced Spanish courses with specific thematic foci (e.g. politics, media, literature), first year seminars in English, and the intensive intermediate Spanish courses taught abroad or on campus during the summer.
In addition to teaching, the candidate will co-direct the Spanish language program and serve on committees as needed. The candidate will work closely with a fellow co-director of the Spanish language program. Their shared duties include overseeing curricular development of beginning and intermediate Spanish courses, which are taught by full-time faculty members; advising students; and supervising the undergraduate assistant teachers who lead weekly practice sessions to build oral fluency. The candidate should bring creative and data-driven ideas and the administrative skills required to continually improve the language program. As both co-director and as language teacher, the candidate should have the knowledge and agility to respond thoughtfully to emerging technologies, including generative AI, as well as a commitment to improving students' ability to engage in uniquely human communication. The candidate will also be expected to build community and encourage belonging by connecting students from a wide range of linguistic and cultural backgrounds to opportunities across campus. There is no obligation to do research, but there are opportunities to do so.
Candidates must hold a Master's or doctoral degree in a relevant field such as Spanish, language program direction, second-language acquisition, or applied linguistics by the time of appointment. The candidate should have a record of excellence in teaching beginning and intermediate Spanish language courses at the college level. The ideal candidate will have experience in language program direction as well.
Applicants should apply online at https://jobs.richmond.edu and submit the following five documents: a one-page (single-spaced) cover letter; a curriculum vitae; a one-page (single-spaced) teaching statement; a one-page (single-spaced) program direction statement; and a single document, not to exceed five pages, containing evidence of teaching effectiveness. The teaching statement should describe the candidate's teaching philosophy and methods, including their approach to teaching a diverse student body, and provide context for the evidence of teaching effectiveness submitted. That evidence of teaching effectiveness could take the form of a syllabus, lesson plan, activity, assessment, or other material. The program direction statement should outline the candidate's experience and preparation for language program administration as well as their general approach to and vision for directing the Spanish language program at the University of Richmond.
Candidates for this position may be asked, at a later date, to provide a more comprehensive teaching portfolio, student evaluations, and the names and contact information for three references who will be asked to submit letters of recommendation. Review of applications will commence October 15, 2026 and continue until the position is filled. Please contact Elizabeth Kissling, department chair, with any questions. For more information on the department/school and its programs, please visit https://lais.richmond.edu/.
The starting salary for the position is budgeted at $77.000. Compensation is determined by the candidate's individual qualifications, experience, education, and skills.
The University of Richmond is a private university located just a short drive from downtown Richmond, Virginia. Through its five schools and wide array of campus programming, the University combines the best qualities of a small liberal arts college and a large university. With approximately 4,000 students, an 8:1 student-faculty ratio, and more than 90% of traditional undergraduate students living on campus, the University is remarkably student-centered.
The mission of the University of Richmond is to educate in an academically challenging, intellectually vibrant, and collaborative community dedicated to the holistic development of students and the production of scholarly and creative work. A Richmond education prepares students for lives of purpose, thoughtful inquiry, and responsible leadership in a diverse world. The University of Richmond's strategic priorities are academic excellence, belonging and community, access and affordability, well-being, and experiential learning and community engagement. The University seeks to model a relentlessly welcoming and inclusive campus community that values the expression of difference in ways that promote excellence in teaching, learning, personal development, and institutional success. Our academic community strongly encourages applications that are in keeping with this commitment.

Evidence of teaching/mentoring effectiveness

Job Description:
The Department of Media Production, Management, and Technology (MPMT) in the University of Florida's College of Journalism and Communications seeks to hire a tenure-track Assistant Professor with a demonstrated record of creative production to begin Fall 2027.
We seek a dynamic scholar/practitioner whose creative output advances storytelling through innovative media formats. We value candidates who push boundaries in media innovation and foster content that addresses contemporary social issues, cultural narratives, or technological disruptions.
The ideal candidate will demonstrate excellence in creative production while maintaining industry connections. Areas of expertise may include feature-length and short films, television series and specials, documentary filmmaking, emerging technologies such as augmented reality (AR) or virtual reality (VR), streaming series development and production, or hybrid formats that blend narrative with interactive elements. This role emphasizes a robust portfolio of creative work—such as films, documentaries, series, or interactive projects—alongside teaching and service contributions.
The MPMT department recognizes the critical importance of creative tenure tracks where artistic output is valued as highly as traditional scholarly research. Tenure evaluation will prioritize impactful creative scholarship, evidenced by honors and awards at nationally recognized film festivals, publications in creative outlets, peer-reviewed exhibitions, grants from bodies like the National Endowment for the Arts, or collaborations with industry leaders.
Responsibilities include teaching undergraduate courses in media production (for example, filmmaking techniques; camera and lens systems; documentary storytelling; VR/AR production; streaming content creation; mentoring students in hands-on projects; supervising capstone productions) and integrating emerging technologies into the curriculum. Candidates are expected to maintain an active agenda of original creative work, secure external funding, and disseminate outputs through festivals, broadcasts, online platforms, or academic conferences. Service duties include department and college committees, advising student media organizations, and contributing to college initiatives and other duties as assigned.

The Department of Media Production, Management, and Technology is one of the premier programs in offering courses related to mass media and emerging media. Our curriculum prepares students for the media industry through two specializations: Digital Film and Video Production, and Media Management and Technology. The department has about 500 student majors and 16 full-time faculty. Students from the department pursue careers in film production, TV program production, social media management, brand management, consumer analysis, UI/UX design, and digital marketing, among others. Media Production, Management, and Technology (MPMT) - UF College of Journalism and Communications
About the College of Journalism and Communications
We are recognized as a national leader in communication scholarship and professional skills development. Be part of an ambitious, progressive, and collaborative program at one of the top public research universities in the United States.
Accredited by ACEJMC, the college has earned its reputation for excellence over the last half-century on the strength of its programs, faculty, students, and alumni; the stories they tell; and the difference they make around the world. With over 70 full-time faculty members and 175 part- time instructors serving in four academic departments— Advertising; Journalism; Media Production, Management, and Technology; and Public Relations —we enroll about 2,500 undergraduates both in-person and online. Additionally, more than 700 graduate students are earning master's and doctoral degrees.
The College of Journalism and Communications offers multiple research and teaching environments, including the Atlas Lab for social media listening; the Consortium on Trust in Media and Technology; the STEM Translational Communication Center; the Center for Public Interest Communications; the Media, Effects, and Technology Lab; the Institute for Public Relations; The Agency, a full- service student-run advertising and public relations agency; the Innovation News Center; Division of Media Properties; and more. UF continues to expand its faculty ranks and the impact of its research and curriculum. UF faculty members annually generate more than $1 billion in research expenditures, with a comprehensive long-term AI initiative (https://ai.ufl.edu/about/) and access to state-of-the-art infrastructure, including one of the most powerful supercomputers in the U.S.

he University of Florida is situated in north-central Florida, a region renowned for its abundant natural beauty. Gainesville is within a two-hour drive of Tampa, Orlando, Jacksonville, the Atlantic Ocean, and the Gulf of Mexico.
About Gainesville
As home to Florida's largest and oldest university, Gainesville (http://cityofgainesville.org (http://cityofgainesville.org/)) is one of the state's centers of education, medicine, cultural events, and athletics. Gainesville and the surrounding area is home to about 250,000 people, a robust arts community, several museums, a world-class health care system anchored at UF, a downtown core known for its restaurants and brew pubs, excellent public and private schools, and abundant nature exemplified by clear, natural springs. Position description
The Department of Electrical Engineering & Computer Sciences (EECS) and the Center for Computational Biology (CCB) at UC Berkeley invite applications for one approved tenure-track position at the Assistant Professor level in the area of artificial intelligence (AI) for biology. Memberships in related institutes and initiatives or affiliations with other UC Berkeley departments or schools may also be considered. The EECS Department and the Center for Computational Biology have several related faculty positions open or opening soon. Please visit our EECS Faculty Positions website and the CCB Careers website to view these listings. If you are qualified for and wish to be considered for more than one position, please submit a separate application for each.
About the Department: The EECS department is part of the College of Engineering (COE) and the College of Computing, Data Science, and Society (CDSS). It offers one of the strongest research and instructional programs in this field anywhere in the world. The department's key strength is its array of cross-disciplinary, team-driven projects. The integration of EE and CS forms the core, with strong interactions that extend into many other disciplines.
About the Center: CCB is an academic unit under the College of Computing, Data Science, and Society (CDSS). It offers a PhD degree program, as well as interdisciplinary collaboration and research for diverse areas across computational biology. The center features distinguished faculty and graduate students from more than a dozen academic departments across six colleges at UC Berkeley.
About the Position: EECS and CCB are seeking applicants developing innovative AI and machine learning (ML) methods that significantly advance our understanding of complex biological systems and address high-impact problems in biology. Relevant research areas include, but are not limited to the following: AI/ML for predicting cellular phenotypes and responses to genetic, molecular, and environmental perturbations; modeling of molecular interactions, including interactions among proteins, nucleic acids, and small molecules; genotype-to-phenotype prediction across molecular, cellular, and organismal scales; AI/ML for genome and biomolecule engineering; and method development for computational genomics, including the integration of large-scale single-cell, spatial, imaging, and multimodal biological data. Across these areas, we are particularly interested in candidates who develop novel and broadly applicable AI/ML methodology for learning from complex biological data, with the potential to uncover fundamental biological principles and enable new approaches to understanding, predicting, and manipulating biological systems.

The Department of Aerospace Engineering at San Diego State University (SDSU) invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the Assistant Professor rank with expertise in aerospace engineering (CSU Working Title: Assistant Professor of Aerospace Engineering). The candidate is expected to teach aerospace engineering courses at the undergraduate and graduate levels and conduct cutting edge, externally funded research. An earned doctoral degree in Aerospace Engineering or a closely related field is required. A strong preference will be given to applicants who are advancing artificial intelligence and/or machine learning technologies in aerospace engineering. The current areas of expertise of the Department faculty include aerodynamics, computational and experimental fluid mechanics, propulsion, aerospace structures, aeroelasticity, non-destructive evaluation, guidance and control, and astrodynamics. Candidates that complement the existing department research programs and can collaborate are desired. The Department offers BS and MS degrees in Aerospace Engineering and participates in the Joint Doctoral Programs with the University of California, San Diego.
Required qualifications of the applicant by date of application:
A record of original research / scholarly accomplishments and demonstrated capacity and potential to a) develop a vigorous and independent program of research / scholarship activity and establish a high-quality extramurally-funded research program with leading expertise and vision in the field, b) excel at teaching and mentoring undergraduate and graduate students; and c) engage in both campus and professional service activities and work collaboratively with colleagues as a team member to advance the program.
Demonstration of past accomplishments and/or future plans in at least two (2) or more of the “Building on Inclusive Excellence” criteria (https://fs-diversity.sdsu.edu/recruitment/bie).
Required qualifications by date of hire:
Terminal degree in Aerospace Engineering or a closely related field with all degree requirements met.
The Department of Aerospace Engineering has nationally and internationally recognized research programs. A comprehensive aero lab consisting of a mid-size low speed wind tunnel, a Mach number 4.5 supersonic wind tunnel, and a pressurized water tunnel equipped with state-of-the-art flow diagnostic systems are operated within the department. Alumni from the department are among the best flying vehicle designers and notable industry leaders in the nation. In Aviation Week Network's 2017 Workforce Study, SDSU was identified as preferred suppliers and top providers of graduates for hiring within the global aerospace and defense industry. The department actively engages undergraduate students in faculty research and promotes extra-curricular professional activities as evident in the AIAA Design Build and Fly competition as well as successful rocket launches by the student-run SDSU Rocket Project. Notably, the undergraduate student body at the SDSU Aerospace Engineering Department has steadily increased from 100 students in year 2000 to over 600 students at present.
The College of Engineering is the fastest growing of SDSU's seven Colleges. The city of San Diego enjoys a renowned mild climate year-round and is a family-friendly urban environment. The metropolitan area is the hub of several leading industries, including major defense contractors and aerospace companies. San Diego and Southern California offer exceptional opportunities for research partnerships with the extensive local aerospace industry. For additional information about the department and the university, please visit http://aerospace.sdsu.edu and http://www.sdsu.edu.

Towson University:
Towson University (TU) is one of the nation’s top 100 public universities. Located north of Baltimore, TU currently enrolls over 19,000 students and is the second-largest university in the prestigious University System of Maryland. Towson University fosters a climate that is grounded in respect to cultivate the intellectual and personal growth of the entire university community.
Position:
The College of Fine Arts and Communication invites applications for a tenure-track, nine-month, full-time Assistant Professor of Music Theory in the Department of Music. The primary responsibility of this position is teaching music theory and musicianship. The Department seeks a student-centered educator able to bring professional experience and innovation to the undergraduate theory curriculum. Preferred candidates will be conversant with a wide range of musical practices and traditions. The preferred start date is August 2027.
Qualifications:
Applicants should hold a doctorate in music theory or a closely related field. ABD candidates will be considered but must have completed a doctoral degree prior to appointment. Candidates must demonstrate excellence in teaching theory and musicianship skills, a promising scholarly agenda, and capacity to serve the administrative needs of the Department of Music, the College of Fine Arts and Communication, and Towson University. Candidates with at least two years of university-level teaching experience are preferred.
Responsibilities:
Responsibilities of the position include 1) teaching undergraduate and graduate music theory and musicianship classes, with the possibility of contributing to the other areas of instruction based on candidate interest and experience; 2) maintaining a productive scholarly agenda consistent with Towson University’s reputation for excellence in interdisciplinary research; 3) contributing to the development of an innovative music curriculum; 4) demonstrating meaningful commitment to inclusive pedagogy and student engagement; 5) serving on department, college, and university committees; 6) participating in departmental recruitment activities; and 7) student advising.
The Department:
The Department of Music serves a community of over 200 music majors and graduate students, as well as offering courses and performance opportunities to students specializing in other fields. Towson students engage in a range of rigorous scholarly, creative, and collaborative work that reflects a broad base of musical interests. Our students have the valuable opportunity to work with a music faculty including internationally recognized composers, performers, scholars, and public intellectuals who prioritize student achievement, scholarly skills, creativity, and community. The Department regularly hosts guest artists for masterclasses and guest lectures and has a long history of philanthropic support to sponsor the educational needs of its students. TU alumni are nationally and internationally renowned composers and performers, educators in PreK-12 and university settings, technological innovators, entrepreneurs, and arts administrators.
The Department offers three undergraduate degree programs for music majors: the Bachelor of Science in Music, the Bachelor of Music (classical performance, jazz/commercial performance, or composition), and the Bachelor of Science in Music Education. The Department also offers minors in general music, music industry, jazz/commercial performance, and music technology. Graduate degrees include the Master of Science in Music Education, the Master of Music, the Master of Music in Music Pedagogy, and the Graduate Certificate in Applied Music.

A complete application portfolio includes 1) a letter of application addressing the candidate’s qualifications for the position; 2) a curriculum vitae; 3) a statement of teaching philosophy; 4) a statement of current and future scholarly research; 5) a recent video demonstration of classroom teaching; 6) three letters of recommendation; and 7) unofficial transcripts from all institutions of higher education attended (official transcripts will be required at time of hire).

jobs.title: Assistant Professor - Urban Analytics
jobs.description:
Job Details
Job no: 530167
Position Type: Faculty Full Time
Campus: UMass Boston
Department: UrbanPlanning&CommunityDevel
Pay Grade: 04

Job Description
The Department of Urban Planning and Community Development (UPCD) in the School for the Environment at the University of Massachusetts Boston (UMB) invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track Assistant Professor position in Urban Analytics and Artificial Intelligence (AI) beginning September 1, 2027.
We seek scholars whose research and teaching integrate urban planning, computational methods, and artificial intelligence to examine complex challenges facing communities, cities, and regions. The successful candidate will contribute to planning scholarship and practice through community engaged and innovative applications of urban analytics and AI that support more equitable, inclusive, and sustainable communities, cities, and regions.
About UMass Boston: UMass Boston is an urban public research university with a teaching soul, whose impact is both local and global. We are the third most diverse university in the country - more than 60% of our undergraduate students come from minoritized communities and groups and more than half of our students are the first in their families to attend a college or university. Thus, our students come to us from richly diverse life experiences and backgrounds; they bring to our classrooms and research settings the robust range of perspectives growing out of the socio-cultural, economic, and historical contexts in which they have lived, along with the challenges they encounter, engage, and strive to overcome. We invite applications from candidates who engage the diverse life experiences of our student body, who appreciate that students bring their holistic selves into the academic setting, and who recognize and articulate how their own life experiences and backgrounds have shaped their journeys, practices, and commitments as researchers, scholars, and educators.
About the School for the Environment (SFE): SFE is an interdisciplinary hub at UMass Boston that tackles the diverse challenges of the natural, built, and social environments through teaching, research, and outreach. SFE engages in innovative, equity-driven approaches that address environmental and societal problems, focusing on the health of communities and ecosystems in the Greater Boston area and beyond. SFE offers undergraduate, master’s, and PhD programs, with faculty expertise spanning environmental science, environmental studies, marine science, and technology. At SFE, faculty and students collaborate to pursue transdisciplinary research and solutions, fostering partnerships with communities, organizations, and government agencies.
About the Department of Urban Planning and Community Development (UPCD): UPCD is a mission-driven program grounded in the pursuit of the just city and region, with a strong emphasis on equity, community development, and applied planning practice. The department has experienced steady growth in enrollment across its BA, Minor, and MS programs in recent years, reflecting increasing student demand for planning education that integrates analytical, policy, and community-engaged approaches.
This position represents a strategic investment in the future of planning education. As AI-enabled tools and computational approaches increasingly shape planning research and professional practice, this hire will play an important role in equipping students with advanced analytical, spatial, and computational skills, strengthening the department’s urban analytics and AI curriculum, supporting interdisciplinary collaboration across the university, and preparing graduates for a rapidly evolving planning profession shaped by advances in urban analytics and artificial intelligence.
The successful candidate will also have opportunities to collaborate with campus initiatives such as the Paul English Applied AI Institute, the Urban Harbors Institute, the Sustainable Solutions Lab, and other centers across the university, and contribute to interdisciplinary teaching and research across the university.
Position Overview
We seek candidates with expertise in Urban Analytics, broadly defined as the application of computational, statistical, and spatial methods to urban systems and planning challenges. Candidates should demonstrate the ability to bridge technical methods and planning practice, with a focus on addressing inequities and sustainability challenges in communities, cities and regions.
Substantive areas of interest include, but are not limited to:
Climate, Public, and Municipal Finance (e.g., budget modeling, infrastructure finance, fiscal analytics)
Transportation and Mobility Systems (e.g., accessibility modeling, intelligent transportation systems, equity in mobility and access)
Environmental Planning and Urban Resilience (e.g., climate modeling, environmental justice analytics, risk assessment)
Land Use, Zoning, and Urban Development (e.g., zoning and entitlement analysis, land-use change, development patterns, spatial modeling, growth management)
We are particularly interested in candidates whose work critically engages how data and AI can both reproduce and mitigate structural inequities in urban systems.
The successful candidate will be expected to develop and sustain an independent, externally funded research program in urban analytics or a related field; publish in high-impact, peer-reviewed journals; and engage in collaborative, interdisciplinary research across the School for the Environment and the broader university, with a focus on advancing equity, and justice. The candidate will teach core and elective courses in the BA and MS programs, including urban analytics, GIS and spatial analysis, and AI applications in urban systems. In addition, the candidate will mentor undergraduate and graduate students through advising, research supervision, and career development. Service responsibilities include active participation in departmental, college, and university governance, engagement with community partners and public and nonprofit sectors, and contributions to UPCD’s mission of community-engaged and practice-oriented planning education.
Qualifications

jobs.description:
Open Rank of Occupational Therapy (Assistant, Associate, Full Professor or BCBS Distinguished Professorship)
Appalachian State University’s Master of Science in Occupational Therapy (MSOT) program was accredited by the Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education (ACOTE) in May 2026 and recently graduated its first cohort of students. The program seeks an experienced faculty member with established expertise, leadership, and scholarly perspective to join a collegial academic community committed to excellence in occupational therapy education, meaningful scholarship, and service to the profession and surrounding communities. As a faculty member, this individual will have opportunities to help shape the continued growth and direction of the occupational therapy program, mentor students and faculty, advance an established program of scholarship, and build interdisciplinary and community partnerships across the Beaver College of Health Sciences, the University, and region. Appalachian State University is classified as a Research 2- Doctoral University, characterized by high research spending and doctorate production by the Carnegie Classification of Institutions of Higher Education and has expanding opportunities for research and innovation.
For appointments at the rank of Associate Professor, candidates must demonstrate a documented record of effective teaching, student mentoring, and independent research in the area of expertise as evidenced by scholarly dissemination and pursuit of funding.
For appointments at the rank of Full Professor or Blue Cross Blue Shield of North Carolina Distinguished Professor, candidates must meet all departmental, university, and college requirements for appointment with tenure, including demonstrating a documented history of exemplary teaching, successful mentoring of students and other faculty, institutional and professional service, and an established program of research including dissemination and extramural funding. Candidates at this rank are also anticipated to have a record of successful mentoring of other faculty.
Highly qualified candidates whose experience and credentials demonstrate the capacity to provide leadership and vision will be considered for the Blue Cross Blue Shield of NC Distinguished Professorship. Competitive candidates will present:
A minimum of 5 years of experience in an occupational therapy educational program with a focus on student-and subject-centered pedagogy
Strong record of mentorship of both students and faculty
Evidence of an independent and sustained line of research

jobs.title: Assistant/Associate Professor in Communication Sciences and Disorders / Speech-Language Pathology
jobs.description:
Assistant/Associate Professor in Communication Sciences and Disorders / Speech-Language Pathology
The Department of Rehabilitation Sciences is searching for an Assistant/Associate Professors specializing in Communication Sciences and Disorders/Speech-Language Pathology.
An earned doctoral degree in speech-language pathology or related area is required.
ABD applications will be considered with initial appointment at the rank of Instructor. All degree requirements must be completed by February 28, 2028 for subsequent appointment at the rank of Assistant Professor.
Applications are encouraged from all qualified candidates. Applications are particularly encouraged from candidates with expertise in the areas of child language disorders, autism, literacy, cultural-linguistic variations, and/or complex communication needs.
For appointments at the rank of Assistant Professor, candidates must demonstrate the potential for effective teaching, student mentoring, and conducting research in the area of expertise.
For appointments at the rank of Associate Professor, candidates must demonstrate a history of successful teaching at the undergraduate and/or graduate levels, student mentoring, research productivity, and academic/professional service.
Responsibilities include teaching undergraduate and graduate courses, both face-to-face and online, conducting research and seeking external funding, and engaging in university and professional service. Opportunities for direct clinical service and clinical supervision may also be available.
The Department of Rehabilitation Sciences within the Beaver College of Health Sciences includes fully accredited graduate programs in Athletic Training, Speech-Language Pathology, and Occupational Therapy, an undergraduate program in Communication Sciences and Disorders, and minors in American Sign Language and Communication Sciences and Disorders. Our students are trained to empower people of all ages to improve/restore their functional abilities, fulfill their daily routines and roles, mitigate limitations or disabilities following injury or illness, and live full lives in the context of differing abilities. In addition, the department is home to the Charles and Geneva S. Scott Scottish Rite Communication Disorders Clinic, which provides speech-language pathology, audiology, and pediatric occupational therapy services as an outreach to the community and serves as a primary site for student clinical training. Department of Rehabilitation Sciences graduates transition into their respective positions as qualified healthcare practitioners with enhanced clinical skills, knowledge, and values. They will be well-prepared to improve the health and wellness of people across the region, state, and world. The department emphasizes interprofessional education, clinical-academic collaboration, and academic excellence.

Department of Mathematics
The Jess and Mildred Fisher College of Science and Mathematics
FCSM-4026
Towson University:
Towson University (TU) is one of the nation’s top 100 public universities. Located north of Baltimore, TU currently enrolls over 20,000 students and is the second-largest university in the prestigious University System of Maryland. Towson University fosters a climate that is grounded in respect to cultivate the intellectual and personal growth of the entire university community.

The Fisher College of Science and Mathematics invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Mathematics Education position in the Mathematics Department. Preferred start date August 2027.
Qualifications:
Candidates must possess a Ph.D. (or equivalent) in Mathematics Education, Mathematics (with significant work experience in Mathematics Education), Curriculum and Instruction (with focus in Mathematics Education), or a closely related field, before August 15, 2027. Candidates should have a strong research background, potential for external funding, and excellent teaching. Candidates in all mathematics education specialties (including elementary, middle school, secondary, and undergraduate mathematics education) are encouraged to apply.
Responsibilities:
Assistant Professors are assigned an instructional workload of five course units (three credit hours each) per academic year. Faculty members in mathematics education teach a broad spectrum of courses throughout the undergraduate curriculum and in the Master’s degree program in Mathematics Education. A strong commitment to excellence in teaching is essential. The successful candidate will establish a productive research program with a willingness to pursue external funding opportunities. The Department of Mathematics has 58 full-time faculty and over 130 math majors. We offer a Bachelor of Science degree in mathematics, with concentrations in Secondary Education, Actuarial Science, Applied Mathematics, and Pure Mathematics, as well as Master’s degrees in Mathematics Education, Actuarial Science and Predictive Analytics, and Applied and Industrial Mathematics. A criminal background investigation is required for the successful candidate, and results may affect employment.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor - Communication Sciences and Disorders
jobs.description:
The Department of Communication Sciences and Disorders, a CAA-accredited program in Speech-Language Pathology at the University of Houston, invites applications for a nine-month, tenure-track Assistant Professor position beginning Fall 2027.
Qualifications include an earned Ph.D. in Communication Sciences and Disorders or related field, potential for a strong record of research and scholarship, teaching experience, and a desire to contribute to a growing, innovative program. CCCs are strongly preferred. Areas of need include: dysphagia, speech sound disorders, audiology and aural rehabilitation, speech science, multilingualism, and social communication, though all strong applicants will be considered.
Responsibilities include teaching graduate and undergraduate courses in the candidate’s area of expertise, directing student research, participating in service at the department, university, and professional levels, and consulting with clinical educators as needed.
The University of Houston, a Carnegie-designated Tier One public research university, is centrally located in Houston, Texas. Situated within four miles of the Texas Medical Center, the world's largest medical complex, the university affords extensive opportunities for interdisciplinary research and clinical collaboration. As an expanding academic unit, the Department of Communication Sciences and Disorders (www.class.uh.edu/comd) is exceptionally well supported by the college as a center for high-impact research, rigorous education, and community clinical service.
We have approximately 300 undergraduate and 80 graduate students. Degrees offered include: B.A. and B.S. degrees in Communication Sciences and Disorders, an M.A. degree in Speech-Language Pathology, and a Ph.D. in Communication Sciences and Disorders. Additionally, the department offers a post-baccalaureate leveling program. Our on-campus clinic provides services to a broad demographic cross-section of the greater Houston area across a wide range of ages, disorders, and etiologies.
Review of applications will begin immediately and will continue until the positions are filled.
Applications must include a letter of interest with stated qualifications, a summary of research accomplishments and future goals, copies of representative work, a statement of teaching interests and philosophy, and a curriculum vitae. Summaries of teaching evaluations are welcome.
Questions regarding the application process or position may be directed to Dr. Amber Thiessen at althiess@central.uh.edu.
Employees are expected to have a home address in the state of Texas for the duration of their appointments.
Official transcripts are required for a faculty appointment and will be requested upon selection of the final candidates.
All positions at the University of Houston-System are security sensitive and will require a criminal history check. Individuals conducting research in critical infrastructure areas (i.e., communication infrastructure systems, cybersecurity systems, electric grid, hazardous waste treatment systems, and/or water treatment facilities) are subject to regular review to ensure the security and integrity of the research is maintained.
The University of Houston System and its universities are Equal Opportunity Institutions. Everyone is encouraged to apply.

jobs.title: Director of Faculty Affairs
jobs.description:
Director of Faculty Affairs
Georgetown University in Qatar (GU-Q) is dedicated to fulfilling Georgetown University's mission of promoting intellectual, ethical and spiritual understanding through serious and sustained discourse among people of different faiths, cultures, and beliefs. Embodying this spirit of the University, Georgetown's Qatar campus undertakes education, research, and service in order to advance knowledge and provide students and the community with a holistic educational experience that produces global citizens committed to the service of humankind. We demonstrate the values of Georgetown University; seek to build upon the world-class reputation of the Edmund A. Walsh School of Foreign Service; and work with our partner, Qatar Foundation, in its endeavors to achieve the Qatar National Vision 2030.
Requirements
Georgetown University in Qatar (GU-Q), located in Doha, is seeking Director of Faculty Affairs to oversee faculty recruitment, appointments, reappointments, promotions, and key academic administration and compliance processes. The role also serves as second-in-command to the Senior Associate Dean for Faculty and Academic Affairs, supporting academic decision-making, and departmental leadership.
The position is for a 3 year term, eligible for renewal.
Key Accountabilities:
Oversee the processes for recruitment, appointment, reappointment, and promotion of full-time core and teaching faculty, and the recruitment and appointment of adjunct faculty.
Communicate and advise faculty on relevant university policies and procedures, and assist the Associate Dean in tracking compliance.
Oversee and coordinate a high volume of administrative processes, including those related to promotion, reappointment, research leave, faculty merit, overload teaching, and course banking.
Serves as second-in-command to the Senior Associate Dean for Faculty and Academic Affairs, supporting high-level academic decision-making and departmental leadership.
Key Activities:
In consultation with the Dean, Associate Dean, and Faculty Chair, coordinate full-time faculty searches and oversee recruitment processes.
Manage the appointment processes for and support of visiting faculty, including from the main campus in Washington, DC, in consultation with curricular field chairs, the Faculty Chair, the Associate Dean, and the Dean.
Recruit and hire adjunct instructors, in consultation with the Dean, Associate Dean, Faculty Chair, and curricular field chairs.
Collaborate with other units to ensure the effective academic onboarding and orientation of new faculty.
In consultation with the Associate Dean and Faculty Chair, review faculty travel requests.
Oversee curricular activities fund and curricular group funding, ensuring usage of funds is in accordance with their respective policies.
Collaborate with the Office of Research to manage certain administrative aspects of research programs and processes (including summer supplement), like collecting and tracking proposals and overseeing payouts.
Support the Dean, Associate Dean, and Faculty Chair to ensure that all faculty meet workload standards.

Organizational Unit Overview:
Academic Affairs, led by the Provost and Senior Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs, comprises the university's colleges, schools and libraries, along with other academic support and administrative units. Academic Affairs works collaboratively to strengthen ECU's culture of academic excellence in line with our mission to be a national model for student success, public service and regional transformation.
The School of Dental Medicine is composed of ten administrative offices and four academic departments. The Administrative units include the Offices of the Dean, Vice Dean, Associate Dean for Student Affairs, Associate Dean for Research, Associate Dean for Clinical Affairs, Associate Dean for Extramural Clinical Practices, Assistant Dean for Dental Education and Informatics, Assistant Dean for Educational Support and Faculty Development, Assistant Dean for Academic Success and the Assistant Dean for Business Operations and Financial Affairs. The four academic departments are Surgical Sciences, Pediatric Dentistry, Orthodontics and Dentofacial Orthopedics, General Dentistry and Foundational Sciences.
Included in the mission of the School of Dental Medicine is to educate dental care providers (both dental students and dental residents) and to address the oral health care needs of the underserved population of North Carolina. The School of Dental Medicine meets these missions by operating dental clinics that provide both educational experiences for the dental students and residents and provide dental care to the residents of North Carolina. These clinics occur in both Ross Hall in Greenville, North Carolina, as well as Community Service-Learning Centers located throughout North Carolina. In order to operate these clinics, appropriate dental auxiliaries and clinical staff are needed.
Job Duties:
The ECU SoDM is seeking a part-time accomplished dental educator to support integration of the foundational biomedical sciences across the four-year predoctoral dental education program. The SoDM predoctoral biomedical science curriculum is multidisciplinary and includes both normal and abnormal functions of the human body with an emphasis on the oro-facial complex along with the scientific principles that underpin modern clinical dental practice. The dental faculty educator will actively participate in instruction and ensure that graduates are competent in the application of biomedical science knowledge in the delivery of patient care. The dental faculty educator will bring both clinical and biomedical science expertise to include one or more of the following scientific disciplines: general medicine, gross anatomy (including head and neck anatomy), molecular biology, neuroscience, general pathology, physiology, and/or pharmacology.
The position reports to the Chair of the Department of Foundational Sciences. Foundational Sciences is the home department at the SoDM for faculty in the areas of biological basic sciences, public health sciences, and behavioral sciences. The dental faculty educator will work closely with the Division Director of Basic Sciences and other faculty within the SoDM Department of Foundational Sciences. They will also work in close collaboration with SoDM clinical faculty from Departments of General Dentistry, Pediatric Dentistry, Orthodontics and Dentofacial Orthopedics, and Surgical Sciences. In addition, the dental faculty educator will work with faculty and staff in the Brody School of Medicine including the Department Chairs that are providing faculty instructors for the DMD curriculum.
Specific duties include:
Didactic teaching in course modules related to gross anatomy, physiology, pharmacology, general pathology, and medicine taught within the SoDM predoctoral curriculum.
Provide mentoring and oversight of problem-based learning within the Medical Case Seminar series and Foundations of Biomedical Sciences course.
Coordinate the anatomy and cellular biology modules and gross anatomy laboratory sessions.
Formulate new and innovative seminars or teaching methods to ensure continued learning and integration of the basic sciences within the clinical third and fourth years of the SoDM predoctoral dental curriculum.
Didactic and/or simulation teaching in preclinical course modules related to the candidate's clinical field or discipline.
Mentoring dental students in both the basic and clinical sciences related to teaching or research/scholarly activities.
Active participation in the editing current content and developing new materials involved in the delivery of instruction. This includes manuals, references, and presentation media.
Active participation in the developing and editing of content involved in the evaluation of student outcomes. This includes exams and Case-Based Learning (CBL).
Participate in program development, review processes, curricular changes, accreditation activities, and self-studies.
Participate in programs and activities for the American Dental Education Association (ADEA), American Association for Dental Oral and Craniofacial Research (AADOCR), International Association for Dental Research (IADR), and American Dental Association (ADA) to commensurate the role at the school.
Represent the department at internal and external academic communities, alumni, business and industry, government, foundations, patient and practitioner groups, and the general community.
Commitment to the Mission and Vision of the School of Dental Medicine including both a community-based and a generalist model of dental education.
Perform other duties as assigned by the Department Chair or Dean.

Background and expertise in both the basic biological and clinical sciences.

Research activities (except where appointment is strictly at Lecturer level, in which case research expectations are limited).
