Description of Work:
The Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the rank of Assistant Professor, with an anticipated start date in the 2027–2028 academic year.
The department seeks an outstanding candidate who will establish a nationally visible, externally funded research program in catalysis and contribute to excellence in undergraduate and graduate education. Catalysis is a core discipline in chemical engineering and a central enabling technology for advances in energy, sustainability, advanced materials, agriculture, and value-added chemical manufacturing.
Research areas of interest include, but are not limited to, heterogeneous and homogeneous catalysis; electrocatalysis and photocatalysis; biocatalysis; catalytic materials and interfaces; reaction engineering and kinetics; computational and data-enabled catalysis; integrated experimental–computational approaches; decarbonization; hydrogen technologies; carbon capture, utilization, and conversion; biofuels and biobased manufacturing; and catalysis for advanced manufacturing. Candidates whose work complements and expands existing departmental strengths are encouraged to apply.
The successful candidate will be expected to develop a strong scholarly record and externally funded research program; teach undergraduate and graduate courses in chemical engineering, including courses related to reaction engineering, kinetics, and catalysis as appropriate; mentor undergraduate and graduate students; and contribute to departmental, college, and university service. The position offers opportunities for collaboration with faculty engaged in experimental and computational catalysis and with campus research entities including the Nebraska Center for Materials and Nanoscience and the Nebraska Energy Sciences Research Center.
The Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering provides an outstanding environment for research and education, with opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration across the University of Nebraska–Lincoln and the broader University of Nebraska system. The department’s strategic growth in catalysis will support research and workforce development in areas important to Nebraska and the broader Midwest while enhancing competitiveness for federal and collaborative research initiatives.

A Ph.D. or equivalent terminal degree by the time of appointment. At least one degree (B.S., M.S., and/or Ph.D.) must be in chemical engineering.

Job Details:
The Department of Human-Centered Information Design & Technology in the School of Engineering at Mercer University invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor, to begin Fall 2027.
We seek a colleague whose teaching, scholarship, and/or professional experience reflect the evolving landscape of human-centered, technical, and professional communication in contemporary workplaces. We are particularly interested in candidates whose expertise engages the creation, evaluation, management, and governance of information in complex, technology-mediated, digital, and AI-supported environments.
Areas of Emphasis
Areas of emphasis should align with the department's strengths in technical communication, user experience, and artificial intelligence and may include one or more of the following:
Accessibility and inclusive design
Artificial intelligence and emerging communication technologies
Collaborative workflows and project management
Content strategy and User experience (UX)
Human-computer interaction (HCI) and/or human-robot interaction (HRI)
Information design and digital content practices
Instructional design and learning experience design
International and intercultural communication
Technical and professional communication in high-tech environments
Technical writing and editing
Web design, development, and docs as code
Position and Department
The Department of Human-Centered Information Design & Technology offers undergraduate and graduate programs that prepare students for careers in technical, professional, digital, and user-centered communication. Located within the School of Engineering, the department provides a distinctive interdisciplinary environment at the intersection of communication, design, technology, and applied problem-solving.
The department offers bachelor's and master's degree programs, as well as minors in technical communication, user experience, and artificial intelligence, and it provides service courses that support students across the School of Engineering. Faculty also contribute to a two-course sequence in professional and technical communication required for all engineering students.
We seek a faculty member who will contribute to a collaborative, collegial, and innovative department and help shape curricula for rapidly changing professional and technological contexts.
Responsibilities
Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in the department's programs
Contribute to service and support courses for the School of Engineering
Teach in face-to-face, hybrid, and online environments as needed
Maintain an active agenda of scholarship, creative activity, and/or professionally engaged work appropriate to rank
Contribute to curriculum development and revision in areas such as AI, UX, accessibility, content strategy, and digital communication
Advise and mentor students
Support student engagement in applied, research, and professional development opportunities
Participate in departmental, school, and university service, including assessment and committee work
Contribute to a team-oriented academic culture
Faculty in the department typically teach three courses each semester. Graduate teaching will include online delivery using university-supported platforms and tools. The department's laboratories, including usability and digital media labs, support teaching, student collaboration, and faculty-student research and applied project experiences.
Required Qualifications
A PhD in technical communication, professional communication, rhetoric, human-centered design, information design, UX, HCI, instructional design, or a closely related field from an accredited institution is required by the time of appointment.
Additionally, candidates should also have:
Evidence of or strong potential for excellence in teaching
Expertise in one or more of the areas listed above
Ability to teach effectively at the undergraduate level
Ability to teach graduate students, including in online or technology-supported environments
Ability to work collaboratively in a collegial department
Familiarity with current and emerging professional tools, practices, and technologies relevant to the field
An interest in engaging contemporary developments in AI and related communication technologies
Preferred Qualifications
A record of scholarly, professional, or applied work that demonstrates clear engagement with contemporary communication practice
Industry or other professional experience in technical, professional, digital, UX, or content-focused communication settings
Experience with accessibility standards, content systems, web technologies, technical editing, or AI-supported communication practices
Experience in curriculum innovation, interdisciplinary collaboration, or program development
About Mercer and HID
Mercer University is one of the few institutions with technical and professional communication offerings situated within a School of Engineering. This setting creates distinctive opportunities for interdisciplinary teaching, applied collaboration, and innovative program development. The department values human-centered approaches to communication and technology and is committed to preparing students for leadership in contemporary workplaces.
Application Materials
Applicants should submit:
A cover letter
Curriculum vitae
A list of references with current contact information
Additional materials may be requested from finalists, including unofficial transcripts, teaching materials, and/or samples of scholarly or professional work. Official transcripts will be required of the successful candidate.
Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled.
Selection of the final candidate is contingent upon successful completion of a criminal background check.
About Mercer University
Founded in 1833, Mercer University is a distinguished private institution recognized for its commitment to academic excellence, leadership development, and community engagement. With campuses across Georgia, Mercer's twelve schools and colleges offer a wide range of undergraduate, graduate, and professional programs. The university cultivates a close-knit, student-centered environment where innovation, service, and personal growth are deeply valued. Mercer's employees are at the heart of its mission, dedicated to advancing innovation, supporting student success, and strengthening both our local and global communities through service. At Mercer, we believe in the power of relationships and the importance of in-person collaboration. Accordingly, our employees are expected to serve in-person as it fosters real-time problem solving, mentoring, and the meaningful connections that strengthen both our work and service to our students and the broader university community.
Why Work at Mercer University
Mercer University offers a variety of benefits for eligible employees including comprehensive health insurance (for self and dependents), generous retirement contributions, tuition waivers, paid vacation and sick leave, technology discounts, schedules that allow for work-life balance, and so much more!
At Mercer University, a Bear is more than a mascot: it's a frame of mind that begins with a strong desire to make the most out of your career. Mercer Bears do not settle for mediocrity or the status quo. If you're seeking an environment where your passion and determination are embraced, then you want to work at Mercer University.

jobs.description:
Job Details
LEHIGH UNIVERSITY. The Department of Physics invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor with a specialization in Extragalactic Astrophysics, broadly defined, with an anticipated start date of July 1, 2027. We welcome candidates using observational, theoretical, computational, and/or data-intensive approaches.
The successful candidate will be expected to teach courses in astronomy and physics at the undergraduate and graduate levels, engage in scholarly activities, and participate in departmental, college, and university service. We are seeking candidates whose research will complement existing faculty expertise in observational stellar astrophysics, theoretical cosmology and string theory, and high energy physics. The successful candidate will demonstrate strong potential to develop a vibrant, externally-supported research program and a commitment to mentoring within our community of culturally diverse students.
The Department of Physics has established research programs in condensed matter physics, photonics, soft materials and biophysics, statistical physics, nuclear and particle physics, string theory, astrophysics, and atomic and molecular physics. The department offers a B.S. in Astrophysics and a B.A. in Astronomy, as well as M.S. and Ph.D. programs in Physics, providing opportunities to mentor undergraduate and graduate researchers and to teach and develop advanced courses in astronomy and astrophysics. Faculty have access to university high-performance computing and research-computing support, together with opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration through Lehigh’s Physics and Data Science programs and the Institute for Data, Intelligent Systems, and Computation. Lehigh also provides proposal-development and sponsored-program support, including services for early-career faculty, as well as competitive internal seed funding for new and collaborative research.
Founded in 1865, Lehigh University has combined outstanding academic and learning opportunities with leadership in fostering innovative research. Recognized among the nation's highly ranked research universities, Lehigh offers a rigorous academic community for over 7,500 students. Lehigh University has some 5,800 undergraduates, 1,800 graduate students, and nearly 600 full-time faculty members. Lehigh University is located in Bethlehem, PA, a vibrant and historic area. Over 840,000 people live in the Lehigh Valley, which is in close proximity to New York City and Philadelphia.
Qualifications
Candidates must have earned a Ph.D. in Astrophysics or a closely related field by the date of employment. The candidate must also demonstrate a record of publishing in top journals and experience teaching or mentoring in a university setting.
Application Instructions
Review of applications will begin on December 1, 2026 and will continue until the position is filled. For full consideration, applications should be received by December 1, 2026. Applicants should submit their materials at https://apply.interfolio.com/193844. Candidates should submit the following materials:
Cover letter
Curriculum vitae
Research statement that describes past scholarly contributions and future research directions
Teaching statement that describes instructional philosophy and courses that the candidate would want to teach or develop
A statement on Contributions to Lehigh’s Principles of Our Equitable Community that describes how your experiences, knowledge, and skills prepare you to effectively contribute to a learning and research community that holds these principles at its core (the Lehigh ADVANCE Center’s guide for understanding and preparing such statements is available here)
Names and affiliations of three references (letters will be requested later in the process)
Any inquiries regarding this search should be directed to Prof. M. Virginia McSwain, Chair of the search committee, at mcswain@lehigh.edu.
Equal Employment Opportunity Statement
Lehigh University is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital or familial status, national origin (including shared ancestry), pregnancy or related conditions, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, or veteran status. Lehigh University is committed to a culturally and intellectually diverse academic community and is especially interested in candidates who can contribute, through their research, teaching and/or service, to this mission. Lehigh University provides competitive salaries and comprehensive benefits, including domestic partner benefits, and supports faculty members’ work/life balance.

Relationship-building skills and knowledge of North Carolina communities are also preferred.

Be a Tar Heel!:
The Department of Statistics and Operations Research (STOR) in the College of Arts and Sciences, and the Department of Biostatistics in the School of Public Health at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill have an opening for a tenure-track position at the assistant professor level starting July 1, 2027. The departments are seeking candidates with a doctorate (or foreign equivalent) in statistics, biostatistics, operations research, artificial intelligence or a related field. This early career hire will focus on foundational statistical and optimization methods for safe and reliable AI, with applications in biomedicine and public health. Areas of interest include, but are not limited to, robust and stochastic optimization, generative and foundation models, reliable and robust machine learning, uncertainty quantification, sequential decision-making, and AI systems operating under uncertainty in high stakes environments. The secondary appointment in Biostatistics will facilitate close collaboration with applied researchers and provide pathways for translating methods into practice. Candidates are expected to highlight the connection between their research and their application focus in their cover letters. Duties of this position include teaching, research, and service. The hired candidate will be expected to teach courses at both undergraduate and graduate levels at the intersection of their expertise and the needs of the department. Screening of applications will begin November 9, 2026, on a rolling basis. Applicants are encouraged to apply by that date to be included in the initial review cycle; applications submitted afterward will continue to receive full consideration while the position remains open. The application package should include a cover letter, an up-to-date curriculum vitae, research and teaching statements, representative papers, and a list of relevant graduate courses taken. Applicants should also arrange for four letters of recommendation. At least one of the letters should include an evaluation of the applicant’s teaching ability. Application materials and letters of recommendation must be submitted in electronic form only; click on https://unc.peopleadmin.com/postings/ to apply for this position. This position is part of a cluster hire on Safeguarding Artificial Intelligence in Health: Foundations, Uncertainty, and High Stakes Decision Making, at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill that involves three jointly appointed positions with the Department of Biostatistics and the Department of Computer Science. This is structured to strengthen collaboration across these departments. The ideal candidate will have research and/or teaching interests that make substantive connections with related fields and would be excited to engage in cross-disciplinary conversations and collaborations. For inquiries, please contact STOR-Cluster@unc.edu . Further information about STOR is at http://stor.unc.edu, and about BIOS at https://sph.unc.edu/bios/biostatistics/.
Primary Purpose of Organizational Unit:
The primary mission of the Department of Statistics & Operations Research (STOR) in the College of Arts & Sciences is teaching, research, and service in statistics, operations research, probability, optimization, stochastic modeling, data science, analytics, and decision-making under uncertainty. The department is nationally recognized for graduate education and research; the College’s current rankings page lists Statistics at UNC-Chapel Hill as 11th nationally in U.S. News & World Report rankings, and the department’s research sits at the core of data science, machine learning/AI, analytics, network science, and related fields. The department administers graduate programs leading to the Ph.D. in Statistics and Operations Research and the M.S. in Statistics, Analytics and Data Science (STANDS), as well as undergraduate programs including the B.S. in Statistics and Analytics, the B.A. in Data Science, the undergraduate minor in Statistics and Analytics, and the Data Science minor. The Ph.D. program provides advanced training in statistics, optimization, probability, and stochastic modeling and typically requires four to five years of full-time graduate work; the M.S. program requires 30 credit hours of graduate coursework and a master’s essay and is normally completed in three to four semesters; the B.S. program requires four years of undergraduate study. In the most recent reporting year, the department awarded 223 B.S. degrees in Statistics and Analytics, 66 B.A. degrees in Data Science, 21 M.S. degrees, and 9 Ph.D. degrees. STOR also offers many high-demand courses serving students across the University in statistics, data science, optimization, analytics, probability, actuarial science, and quantitative reasoning. Historically, the department helped build the Research Triangle’s strength in the statistical and mathematical sciences through its support of the Center for Stochastic Processes, NISS, and SAMSI; today it continues this campus and regional role through interdisciplinary research, the UNC Statistical/Data Science Consulting Center, Data OPS, DataFest, industry/capstone activities, and participation in University initiatives in data science, AI, health systems engineering, and systems engineering. For more information about the department, please visit our website at https://stor.unc.edu/.

Primary Purpose of Organizational Unit:
Our primary mission is providing instruction of the highest quality in physics and astronomy to undergraduate and graduate students at UNC-CH. Training in physics is fundamental among the natural sciences because it provides understanding of the forces governing the structure of matter, from subatomic particles to the large-scale structure of the universe. Our departmental instructional mission spans all segments of the student community. Over 60% of all college graduates from UNC-CH have taken a course in our department. Among them: undergraduate liberal arts majors who should master the power of quantitative reasoning; undergraduates seeking a degree in another of the natural sciences, who need physics as a foundation for their advanced scientific training; the small number of undergraduates who major in physics, to whom we provide broad and rigorous training. Our graduate education and research advances frontiers of knowledge at the two extremes of space and time, from the very small (the realm of particle physics) to the very large (the realm of astronomy), while expanding the boundaries of knowledge in the many subfields spanning length scales between. Forefront physics and astronomy research requires access to well-equipped laboratories and extensive computing capabilities; it also must be supported by comprehensive and accessible library collections. Again, in research at this advanced level, the bridging aspect of physics provides basic interdisciplinary insight for many other sciences. This instructional mission is supported by a strong managerial, administrative, and technical staff. Duties of these employees range from budget planning and management for the numerous research grants held by faculty in the department to maintaining course and student records. These activities are usually accomplished in a standard 40- hour week schedule

The Department of Biology at UNC Chapel Hill (https://bio.unc.edu/) is searching to hire two tenure track Assistant Professors to study critical questions in Molecular, Cell, and Developmental Biology, broadly defined.
We seek candidates doing basic science driving at new fundamental discoveries using a variety of established, emerging, and new model systems. All candidates must have earned a Ph.D. or equivalent degree, have post-doctoral research experience, and be committed to teaching at the undergraduate and graduate levels. Successful candidates are expected to build an active research group, secure competitive external funding, and participate in the scientific community at UNC-CH. Therefore, a strong publication record and a track record of obtaining funding appropriate to career stage and eligibility will be considered favorably. Candidates are requested to specify in their cover letter what animal care facilities will be required to support their research program.
The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is a vibrant center of scientific discovery and innovation, with a commitment to collaboration. Our large research base spans many areas of biology and supports several outstanding graduate programs (including those in the Biological and Biomedical Science Program, https://bbsp.unc.edu/). The Department of Biology consists of over 50 faculty engaged in basic and interdisciplinary research, within the department and between other departments and schools at UNC.
Successful candidates will have opportunities for synergy with other units at UNC, including several UNC School of Medicine basic science departments and curricula (i.e., Genetics & Molecular Biology, Cell Biology & Physiology, Bioinformatics & Computational Biology, Pharmacology, Biochemistry & Biophysics, and Microbiology & Immunology). UNC also houses the Environment, Ecology, and Energy Program, the Department of Applied Physical Sciences, the School of Data Science and Society, the Institute of Convergent Sciences, The Galapagos Center, the Carolina Biodiversity Collaborative, the Integrative Program for Biological and Genome Sciences, and numerous other centers, programs, or institutes (e.g., the McAllister Heart Institute, the Lineberger Comprehensive Cancer Center, the Bowles Center for Alcohol Studies, and the Neuroscience Center).
UNC faculty, postdocs and graduate students routinely interact with colleagues at nearby Duke and North Carolina State Universities, and institutions in Research Triangle Park. The quality of life in North Carolina’s Triangle area is consistently rated among the highest in the nation.
Primary Purpose of Organizational Unit:
The Department of Biology at UNC-Chapel Hill is dedicated to the discovery and dissemination of new and existing knowledge in the broad discipline of Biology by maintaining a high-quality faculty who integrate cutting-edge research and student-focused teaching.
We are one of the largest academic departments in the College of Arts and Sciences. We have over 3,600 majors and 229 minors, and we enroll undergraduate students in over 8,000 seats in our classes each semester. Each fall or spring semester, we offer 52 classes (70 sections) and 13 lab courses (93 sections). Our average total annual expenditure exceeds $24 million, with nearly half of that coming from grant sponsored research. Our department has nearly $70 million in active grants to support our twin missions of research and teaching. Our large research base spans many areas of biology and supports several outstanding graduate programs. We consist of 48 tenure-track faculty, 11 teaching faculty, 5 research faculty, and numerous active adjunct and emeritus faculty who are engaged in basic and interdisciplinary research and teaching, both within the department and between other departments and schools at UNC.
We currently have 55 graduate students and 23 post-docs. We also employ approximately 85 additional graduate and undergraduate students from across the university to assist in our teaching and research missions. Further, we are supported by an administrative staff of 16, with an additional 15 staff directly supporting research.
Position Summary:
The Department of Biology at UNC Chapel Hill (https://bio.unc.edu/) is searching to hire a tenure track Assistant Professor to study critical questions in Molecular, Cellular, Developmental, or Microbial Biology.
We seek candidates who focus on molecular mechanisms that illuminate fundamental aspects of the biology of cells and organisms, including their interactions with the environment. We seek candidates who work across scales, using transdisciplinary approaches including genetic, molecular biology, cellular biology, biochemistry and/or genomic approaches. Research programs that leverage model experimental systems and/or have direct relevance to human disease are particularly desirable.

This is a 9-month tenure-accruing position that will be 20% teaching (College of Agricultural and Life Sciences), 80% research (Florida Agricultural Experiment Station), available in the Horticultural Sciences Department, Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences, at the University of Florida. This assignment may change in accordance with the needs of the unit. The programmatic emphasis for this position centers on the intersection of evolutionary plant genomics, and artificial intelligence to identify foundational gene networks underpinning maize domestication, anthropogenic improvement and adaptation to cultivated systems and environmental change. An expectation of this position is a leadership role in large-scale pangenomic initiatives to characterize the diversity of crops like maize and its wild relatives, providing critical crop agnostic resources for crop improvement and breeding.
Research areas of concentration include the following: Genetic architecture of adaptation: Investigating how maize adapts to diverse and changing environments, with a particular focus on adaptations to abiotic stresses from highlands across the Americas; Domestication and introgression: Analyzing the genomic signatures left by the domestication of teosinte and the subsequent gene flow between wild and domesticated varieties; Computational tool development: Creating and benchmarking artificial intelligence pipelines for de nova genome assembly, transposable element annotation, and genomic quality assessment. The expectation for this position includes successful acquisition of extramural funding from sources like NSF (PGRP, CNIC, etc.), FFAR, USDA-ARS, and/or industry partners sufficient to support the research program. Publications for this position are expected to appear in top 5% and Q1 journals as appropriate for the audience of the data including, Nature, Science, Nature Genetics, Genome Biology, Plant Cell and the Proceedings of the National Academy Sciences.

Job Details
LEHIGH UNIVERSITY. The Department of Community and Global Health (CGH) in the College of Health (COH) invites applications for an open rank Teaching Professor in Community-Engaged Methodologies, specializing in qualitative and community-engaged methodologies. The successful candidate will be expected to contribute to teaching and mentoring in the design, implementation, and evaluation of community-based health interventions, with particular attention to qualitative and mixed-methods approaches. In addition to teaching, the individual hired will be expected to mentor undergraduate and graduate students and participate in departmental, college, and university service. This is a renewable, fixed-term, full-time, non-tenure-track position. The initial term of appointment is 3 years, with an anticipated start date in July 2027. While the position is not tenurable, Teaching Assistant and Teaching Associate Professors who develop excellent records in teaching and service are expected to become eligible for consideration for promotion.
The mission of the College of Health is to contribute to a future in which health equity is achieved and communities thrive. Our graduates harness knowledge and innovation to lead advances in health and well-being. We are committed to developing sustainable solutions to improve lives and promote health, partnering with communities to advance health equity through interdisciplinary education and research, and data-driven and technological innovation. The COH offers undergraduate majors in Biostatistics/Health Data Science (BS), Population Health (BS), Community and Global Health (BA), Health, Medicine, and Society (BA), and Integrated Business and Health (BS). In addition, the COH offers a Master of Public Health (MPH), and PhD in Population Health. As our faculty grows, the COH will add a suite of graduate degrees in Biostatistics and Health Data Science (certificate, MS, PhD).
Founded in 1865, Lehigh University has combined outstanding academic and learning opportunities with leadership in fostering innovative research. Recognized among the nation's highly ranked research universities, Lehigh offers a rigorous academic community for over 7,500 students. Lehigh University has some 5,800 undergraduates, 1,800 graduate students, and nearly 600 full-time faculty members. Lehigh University is located in vibrant and historic Bethlehem, PA, one of the fastest growing regions in the US. Over 840,000 people live in the Lehigh Valley, which is in close proximity to New York City and Philadelphia.
Faculty Employment Prospectus
Qualifications
Candidates must have an earned doctorate in community and/or global health, or a closely related field such as public health, health promotion, health education, social and/or behavioral sciences, health communication, or medical or cultural anthropology by the date of employment. The successful candidate will play a pivotal role in delivering high-quality instruction to undergraduate students (B.S. in Population Health, B.A. in Community and Global Health) and graduate students (Master of Public Health - MPH). We seek an individual passionate about teaching and mentoring, with a focus on qualitative research design, mixed methods, community-based participatory research (CBPR), and/or program evaluation.

● Cover letter

Assistant or Associate Professor of Neuroscience
Job Description:
Open Rank Professor of Neuroscience
Since its founding in 1885, Goucher College has inspired global changemakers as a place of innovation and excellence. As a private, non-profit liberal arts college of approximately 1,000 undergraduate and 500 graduate students, Goucher is dedicated to teaching students to become complex problem-solvers prepared for the jobs of the future. Small class sizes, a rigorous curriculum, and dedicated faculty and staff allow for personalized mentorship of each student. Named one of the most innovative colleges in the country by U.S. News & World Report, Goucher is a leader in global education and was one of the first, and remains one of the only, colleges in the U.S. to provide 100% of its students with the opportunity to study abroad with no additional tuition surcharges.
The Department of Psychology at Goucher College invite applications for a tenure-track position in neuroscience at the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor to begin Fall 2027. We invite applicants who share Goucher’s commitment to fostering a vibrant undergraduate learning environment for all students. The position will support the new undergraduate Neuroscience major, which is housed jointly in the Departments of Psychology and Biological Sciences.
Applicants must have a Ph.D. in Neuroscience or a related field by the time of appointment; area of specialty is open (e.g., computational, cognitive, behavioral, systems, sensory). The ideal candidate will show a commitment to undergraduate education and demonstrate evidence of scholarship potential at a small liberal arts college. This research program should be viable without a dedicated wet lab or vertebrate facility. The candidate will be expected to teach 20 credits (the equivalent of five classes) per year, including Research Methods in Neuroscience, an intermediate-level course and an upper-level seminar in their area of expertise, a course that serves the Goucher Commons Curriculum, and rigorous mentoring of undergraduates on a research team. The successful candidate will play a vital role in the Neuroscience program by advising Neuroscience majors and helping to grow the program. Candidates should demonstrate a commitment to teaching students from a wide range of backgrounds and a dedication to engaged pedagogies that support student success.
Qualifications:
Required: Ph.D. in Neuroscience or related field at the time of appointment.
Preferred: Ph.D. and Postdoctoral training. Teaching experience and/or professional development at the undergraduate level.
Salary Ranges:
Assistant: $77,727-$86,364
Associate: $89,387-$99,319
Application Instructions:
Applicants are required to submit (1) a curriculum vita, (2) a cover letter, (3) a statement of teaching philosophy which speaks to the applicant’s pedagogical approaches to instruction, classroom practices and strategies, relevant teaching experience, and ability to teach to students from a wide range of backgrounds in a liberal arts college setting, and (4) a statement of research interests. In addition, three (3) confidential letters of recommendation will be requested from finalists.
Review of applications will begin October 19, 2026.
Goucher is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to increasing the equity of our community and seeking applicants dedicated to applying principles of equity and inclusion in all areas of the campus community.

Chartered by the state of Georgia in 1785, the University of Georgia is the birthplace of public higher education in America and is the state’s flagship university (https://www.uga.edu/). The University’s enrollment exceeds 41,000 students including over 31,000 undergraduates and over 10,000 graduate and professional students. The University of Georgia is the state’s flagship institution of higher

The School of Social Work serves more than 500 students through its CSWE-accredited B.S.W. and M.S.W. programs, Ph.D. program, and Master of Nonprofit Management and Leadership program. The School also offers joint M.S.W. degree programs with the School of Law, the College of Public Health, and the Terry College of Business through its M.B.A. program. Nationally and internationally recognized for excellence in research, teaching, public service, and international programs, the School of Social Work is committed to hiring faculty who work toward advancing social and economic disparities through scholarship/research, teaching, public service and/or administrative responsibilities.

Classification Title:

Faculty Rank:
Open Rank

Tenure Track or Tenured
Minimum Qualifications:
A Ph.D. in social work or cognate discipline (e.g. psychology, sociology, public health, neuroscience, economics).
Position Summary:
The University of Georgia School of Social Work invites applications for one tenure-track faculty position at the rank of assistant, associate, or full professor. The successful candidate will hold a joint appointment in the School of Social Work and the newly established School of Medicine.
We seek a scholar who will establish and lead an externally funded program of human-subjects research focused on the design, evaluation, implementation, and scaling of evidence-based digital interventions and clinical decision-support tools for prevention, treatment, and recovery. Areas of inquiry may include digital therapeutics; mobile- and web-based interventions; conversational agents for psychoeducation, screening, or triage; EHR-enabled measurement-based care; sensors and other digital biomarkers; and recovery platforms that connect individuals with treatment, peer support, and harm-reduction resources.
The successful candidate may employ rigorous and responsible artificial intelligence methods, including natural language processing, predictive modeling, risk stratification, relapse forecasting, recommender systems, and just-in-time adaptive interventions, to improve early detection, treatment engagement, care coordination, and sustained recovery. Related areas of research may include artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted clinical documentation and workflow optimization, digital phenotyping, integration of multimodal clinical and patient-reported data, and safe and transparent clinical decision support.
The joint appointment will create opportunities for close collaboration with clinical, behavioral, and data science investigators in the School of Medicine while advancing a Social Work research agenda focused on community-based implementation, behavioral health equity, practice integration, recovery-oriented care, and the ethical and responsible use of digital technologies and AI.
Teaching responsibilities may include undergraduate and graduate courses in digital behavioral health, SUD and co-occurring conditions, implementation science, research methods, and the ethical and equitable delivery of digitally enabled care. The faculty member will also contribute to the development of new curricula, certificates, and short courses that translate emerging research and technologies into practice-ready competencies.
The successful candidate will mentor students and trainees across social work, public health, medicine, nursing, informatics, and data science programs and support interdisciplinary research and career development. The faculty member will also be expected to build and sustain partnerships with hospitals, federally qualified health centers, health departments, community-based organizations, and peer-led recovery programs. Through these partnerships, the faculty member may co-design, pilot, implement, and evaluate digital interventions and lead dissemination activities that produce practical resources such as implementation toolkits, train-the-trainer materials, and evaluation dashboards.
The successful candidate will join an exceptionally talented and committed community of scholars and staff. Opportunities for collaboration within the School of Social Work include the Center for Human Trafficking Research & Outreach; the Center for Social Justice, Human and Civil Rights; and the Institute for Nonprofit Organizations. Across the University, faculty collaborate with colleagues in the College of Pharmacy, College of Public Health, newly established College of Nursing, College of Engineering, College of Family and Consumer Sciences, Mary Frances Early College of Education, and School of Law. Additional opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration are available through the Owens Institute for Behavioral Research, the Institute for Artificial Intelligence, and other university centers and institutes.
Faculty are expected to engage in teaching, research, field liaison duties and/or academic advising, and service. They may teach across the educational continuum at our Athens, Gwinnett, and Online campuses. The successful candidate is expected to share the University and School’s commitment to excellence in teaching, research, service, and engagement.
Additional Requirements:
Candidates for the Assistant Professor rank must have a Ph.D. in social work or cognate discipline (e.g. psychology, sociology, public health, neuroscience, economics).
Candidates for the Associate Professor rank must also be engaged in teaching, research, and service consistent with an appointment at the rank of associate professor.
Candidates for the Professor rank must also be engaged in teaching, research, and service consistent with a tenured faculty appointment at the rank of a tenured professor.
Tenure on appointment must be approved before hire, the faculty member must be appointed as an associate or full professor, must have already been tenured at a prior institution, and must bring a demonstrable national reputation to the institution.
Relevant/Preferred Education, Experience, Licensure, and/or Certification:
An M.S.W. degree with two years post master’s practice experience strongly preferred but not required.
We welcome applications from strong candidates in two areas: (1) Digital Mental Health and (2) Digital Behavioral Health for Substance Use Disorder (SUD).
Preferred Knowledge, Skills, Abilities and/or Competencies:
The candidate selected for this faculty position will be an outstanding scholar and teacher. Applicants must demonstrate exceptional research capacity and potential for external funding.
We welcome applications from scholars whose research advances digital behavioral health, withparticular attention to substance use disorders (SUD), co-occurring mental health conditions,and recovery across the lifespan.

You may also be subject to a pre-employment drug test for positions with high-risk responsibilities, if applicable. Please visit the UGA Background Check website.

California State University, Long Beach (CSULB) is a Hispanic Serving Institution (HSI) and an Asian American and Native American Pacific Islander-Serving Institution (AANAPISI). CSULB earned the prestigious Seal of Excelencia in 2023, joining a distinctive group of colleges and universities who have been recognized for its commitment to Latine/x student success. CSULB is committed to serving diverse students and has established and actively supports the Black Excellence Collegium, dedicated to promoting Black excellence and advancing Black Student Success, and El Concilio for Latinx Success at the Beach, whose mission is to build capacity and promote inclusive servingness across initiatives and efforts for the benefit of all students. The President’s Equity and Change Commission is dedicated to achieving inclusive excellence in our community and culture and throughout the university. CSULB’s Beach 2030 University Action Plans prioritize engaging all students; expanding access to higher education; promoting intellectual achievement; building community; and cultivating resilience.
College of Natural Sciences and Mathematics
Department of Biological Sciences
Required Qualifications:
Ph.D. in marine biology, zoology, ecology, evolution, or a related field
Postdoctoral research experience
Research experience in marine invertebrate zoology
A record of research productivity commensurate with experience level
Demonstrated potential for effectiveness and excellence in teaching and related areas such as research, scholarly and creative activities, etc.
Demonstrated commitment to working successfully with a diverse student population, including low socioeconomic and first-generation students
Preferred Qualifications:
At least two years of postdoctoral research experience or equivalent
Research experience (field and laboratory) studying marine invertebrate ecology. Topics may broadly include behavior, conservation biology, development, evolution, fisheries, genomics, physiology, and systematics
Demonstrated potential for establishing an externally funded research program
Demonstrated potential for developing an integrative research lab that studies regional or local fauna and ecosystems
Demonstrated interest in increasing the participation of underrepresented students in STEM fields through teaching and mentoring
Teaching experience at the college level, with the ability to teach invertebrate zoology, marine biology, ecology, evolution, and/or other courses in their area of specialty
Commitment to learning and incorporating pedagogical best practices to create equitable courses that promote student learning
Experience successfully working with populations demographically and/or socioeconomically similar to the CSULB student body
Experience mentoring or supporting students using inclusive and culturally relevant teaching strategies in a diverse classroom
Duties:
Develop and teach undergraduate and graduate courses in the core biology curriculum, core marine biology curriculum, courses in ecology and evolution, and/or other courses in their area of specialty. Teaching mode is at the discretion of the department. (Mode of instruction may include in-person, hybrid, online, and/or any combination thereof.)
Contribute to our efforts to diversify the scientific workforce by effectively training students both inside and outside the classroom
Develop and sustain an independent externally funded research program in marine invertebrate zoology that involves undergraduate and graduate (M.S.) students and leads to peer-reviewed publications with student co-authors
Participate in service to the department, college, university, and community
CSULB seeks to recruit faculty who enthusiastically support the University’s strong commitment to the academic success of all of our students, including students with disabilities, students who are first generation to college, veterans, students with diverse socio-economic backgrounds, and students of diverse sexual orientations and gender expressions. CSULB seeks to recruit and retain a diverse workforce as a reflection of our commitment to serve the People of California, to maintain the excellence of the University, and to offer our students a rich variety of expertise, perspectives, and ways of knowing and learning.
The College of Natural Sciences and Mathematics is a center of scientific learning in Long Beach offering excellent educational opportunities. Our student-centered instructional and research environment fosters equity, diversity, and access; mentors students for lifelong success by elevating character, skills, and mindset; creates scientific knowledge through research; and promotes science and mathematics in our community.
The College's mission is to educate the next diverse generation of scientists and mathematicians, as well as a science-literate citizenry, through inclusive teaching and research programs.
The Department of Biological Sciences has a strong record of graduating underrepresented and underserved students; at CSULB these efforts are supported by an extensive array of federal and state grants to support training of undergraduate and graduate students for a wide array of careers in the biological sciences.
Within the biology department relevant research facilities [https://www.csulb.edu/biological-sciences/marine-biology/facilities] include a dedicated research laboratory, access to departmental field vehicles and a fleet of small boats, dive facilities with a compressor and fill station, biological collections, and extensive shared molecular, imaging, and computational instrumentation [http://web.csulb.edu/colleges/cnsm/research/instruments/].
The CSULB Marine Biology Lab has two temperature-controlled recirculating seawater systems with mechanical and biological filtration and UV sterilization (6,000- and 8,000-L), an additional 24,000-L seawater storage tank, cold-room, aquaria and associated infrastructure for maintaining live organisms. CSULB is a member of the Southern California Marine Institute [https://www.scmi.net/who-we-are/], a consortium of 25 major institutions, colleges, and foundations in Southern California which maintains a marine lab facility located at the Port of Los Angeles that provides access to a variety of wet lab spaces, waterfront docks, and the 75’ research vessel RV Yellowfin. jobs.title: Faculty, English Language Learning & College Prep Center
jobs.description:
Job Details
Applications must be submitted by 12:01 a.m., October 12, 2026.
Thank you for your interest in a career at Northcentral Technical College (NTC).
NTC offers outstanding career opportunities on a modern campus with state-of-the-art technology that allows for a collaborative learning and work environment. Employees are offered an amazing Total Rewards package with competitive salaries, excellent benefits, and generous paid time off – including two paid closures for the winter holiday (Christmas – New Year) and summer (week of July 4th), for most full-time positions. NTC is “The College that Cares” and makes a difference in the lives of our employees and students. If you have the desire to help students while positively impacting the community, we’d love for you to join our team! See why our current employees did!
Salary is commensurate based on occupational experience and qualifications.
JOB SUMMARY, DESCRIPTION & QUALIFICATIONS:
Job Summary
The full-time faculty supports Northcentral Technical College’s College Prep Center/English Language Learning program by delivering high-quality instruction and fostering student success. This position is responsible for teaching courses within the program, developing and maintaining course materials, and aligning instruction with program objectives and evaluation procedures. Working 40 weeks within a 52-week academic year, faculty collaborates with colleagues, engages in professional development, and supports College initiatives to enhance the learning experience and achieve program goals.
Please Note: This is an in-person position located at NTC’s West Region campus locations.
The College Prep Center (CPC) Instructor plays a crucial role in providing comprehensive instruction and academic support to adult learners pursuing their educational, career, and personal goals. This position requires expertise in evidence-based instructional practices and the use of student data to guide individualized instruction in GED and HSED subject areas, including math, science, social studies, reading, language, health, civics, employability, and career awareness. CPC Instructors also support student development through instruction in financial literacy, life skills, and computer skills; provide instructional assistance to postsecondary students enrolled in college courses; and may provide English Language Learning (ELL) instruction to support the language and academic development of multilingual learners.
Essential Functions and Responsibilities
The following duties are primarily performed and are essential for this position. Employees are expected to be able to perform each of these job duties satisfactorily and successfully with or without reasonable accommodation.
Teaching & Student Success:
Facilitate student learning through engaging instructional strategies and methodologies across various modalities, including in-person, online, hybrid, and out-of-classroom activities, and mentoring students and peers.
Adhere to NTC’s academic calendar, Student Connect hours, teaching assignments, post and maintain office hours, and conduct assigned classes for the scheduled length of time in accordance with the faculty contract.
Assess and evaluate student performance by providing timely feedback and grades, maintaining accurate student records, attendance, and lab/clinical evaluations, in compliance with privacy laws, such as FERPA.
Develop and maintain course materials including outcome summaries, learning plans, Performance Assessment Tasks (PATs), syllabi, and online Learning Management System templates in the approved College format within designated timelines.
Select and utilize appropriate learning materials and resources including textbooks, library resources, equipment, and supplies to enhance learning.
Review, revise, and create curriculum in accordance with NTC academic standards and expectations.
Assist in planning, developing, implementing, and evaluating a new or modified course/certificate/program.
Stay current and focused on evolving learner needs and educational trends.
Provide written evaluations upon the student’s request.
Specific Instructional Program Duties:
Curriculum Development: Design and develop engaging and culturally relevant lesson plans and instructional materials tailored to the needs and proficiency levels of English language learners.
Instructional Delivery: Deliver dynamic and interactive English language lessons using a variety of teaching methods, technologies, and authentic materials to promote language acquisition and fluency.
Language Assessment: Administer and evaluate language assessments to determine students' proficiency levels, track progress, and identify areas for improvement.
Individualized Support: Provide personalized support and feedback to students through one-on-one tutoring sessions, language labs, and academic counseling to address specific language challenges and foster academic success.
Cultural Competency: Foster an inclusive and supportive learning environment that respects and celebrates students' diverse cultural backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives.
Collaboration: Collaborate with faculty, staff, and other stakeholders to integrate language learning strategies across the curriculum and support students' academic and professional goals. Provide guidance and support to program staff in grant management, reporting, and compliance activities.
Professional Development: Stay abreast of current trends, research, and best practices in English language teaching and participate in professional development opportunities to enhance instructional effectiveness and student outcomes.
Administrative Duties: Maintain accurate records of student attendance, progress, and performance assessments, and assist with program planning, evaluation, and accreditation processes as needed.
College/Program Area Support:
Maintain program documentation as required by accreditation, program, or clinical sites standards, if applicable.
Coordinate with instructional support services to address student accommodation and modification needs, fostering an inclusive learning environment.
Engage and participate in faculty development training, professional day activities, College in-service events, commencement, team time, and other designated College activities.
Assist in onboarding and orienting new full-time, part-time, adjunct faculty, and other employees within the program or content area.
Actively participate in institutional, advisory and program team, and committee meetings.
Attend College Open Houses (on-campus and off-campus, set-up and take down) to assist with student recruitment and in support of Student Services activities.
Build and maintain collaborative relationships with business and industry partners, community organizations, and K-12 partners to strengthen program connections.
Assist, participate, support, and carry out all duties as assigned.
Professional Development:
Maintain Wisconsin Technical College System (WTCS)/Faculty Quality Assurance Standards (FQAS) and Higher Learning Commission qualification and meet requirements, accreditation or licensing standards, as applicable to program areas.
Maintain professional certifications, licensures, and credentials as required by the specific program area.
Remain up-to-date professionally in the area of content expertise and the teaching profession.
Minimum Qualifications Required
In limited circumstances, NTC may consider a combination of education, training, and experience which provides the necessary knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform the duties of this position.
Education: Bachelor's Degree
Preferred Dual-Qualification (CPC + ELL): Instructors teaching English Language Learning (ELL) / English as a Second Language (ESL) courses must have one of the following:
A Bachelor’s degree or higher with a major in one of the following:
Teaching English as a Foreign Language (TEFL)
Teaching English as a Second Language (TESL)
Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages (TESOL)
Foreign Language
Linguistics
Bilingual Education
OR
A Bachelor’s degree or higher with a combination of at least 20 semester credits in one or more of the following areas:
Teaching English as a Foreign Language (TEFL)
Teaching English as a Second Language (TESL)
Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages (TESOL)
Linguistics
Bilingual Education
Degrees That Commonly Satisfy These Requirements
BA/BS Teaching English as a Foreign Language (TEFL)
BA/BS Teaching English as a Second Language (TESL)
BA/BS Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages (TESOL)
BA/BS Linguistics
BA/BS Applied Linguistics
BA/BS Bilingual Education
BA/BS Foreign Language Education
BA/BS English (with ESL/ELL-focused coursework)
BA/BS Education (any level—Elementary/Secondary/Special Education/Alternative Education—with ESL/ELL or language acquisition emphasis AND/OR passing score on Praxis English to Speakers of Other Languages (ESOL) test/DPI licensure)

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Marketing
jobs.description:
Job Details
The College of Business at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln seeks applicants for a tenure-track, Assistant Professor level position starting Fall 2027. Applicants should demonstrate the ability and qualifications commensurate with the rank of Assistant Professor. Upon hiring, they are also expected to show successful and ongoing involvement in the Department and the College’s research, service, and teaching (undergraduate and graduate programs).
Qualifications
Applicants must have a Ph.D. in marketing or a related discipline from an AACSB or equivalent accredited School or College of Business at the time of the appointment. Additional requirements include a demonstrated ability to conduct high-quality research aimed at top-tier marketing journals, research in the domain of managerial marketing (e.g., marketing strategy, B2B, sales), the ability to teach at the undergraduate and graduate levels, and experience and credentials commensurate with the rank of Assistant Professor.
Preference will be given to candidates who have either manuscripts published or with invited revisions in top-tier marketing journals.
Application Process
For full consideration, applications should be received by October 30, 2026, although applications will be accepted until the position is filled. To apply, go to https://employment.unl.edu, requisition F_260097 and click “Apply for this Job.” Complete the faculty information form and attach the following documents:
Letter of interest.
A detailed resume or CV that includes information on education, experience, research publications/working papers, and teaching experience, if applicable (including title and levels of courses taught and a summary of teaching evaluations).
A list of three references with complete contact information.
One published or working research paper (optional).
Additional supporting material that the candidate may want to submit (optional).
Combine the research paper and supporting materials (items 4 and 5) into a single document for upload. The application must be complete before it can be evaluated. For questions about the application process, please email Michelle Jacobs (mjacobs1@unl.edu). For questions about the position, email the chair of the search committee, Dr. Sajeesh Sajeesh (ssajeesh2@unl.edu).
About the Department of Marketing
The Department of Marketing (https://business.unl.edu/marketing/) has 15 faculty members. It provides a very collegial environment for research and teaching. The Agribusiness Program and the Center for Sales Excellence are also housed in the department, offering resources and opportunities for collaboration with industry partners.
About the College of Business
The College of Business drives discovery, creates opportunity, and empowers its record-breaking 4,534 students to lead the future of business. Programs include 12 undergraduate majors and numerous graduate programs, including our highly ranked online MBA, three online master of science degrees, and two Ph.D. programs. Established in 1913, it is the only doctorate granting business college in Nebraska. Howard L. Hawks Hall, located at 14th and Vine Streets, has been home to the college since 2017. Hawks Hall features interactive learning in state-of-the-art classrooms, cutting-edge technology and one-stop student support services, including free one-on-one tutoring and coaching. For more information, visit https://business.unl.edu/.
About the University of Nebraska–Lincoln
We are proud to be consistently recognized by Forbes as a top employer and certified as a Family Friendly Workplace. We are known for our welcoming, supportive environment, commitment to professional growth, and outstanding benefits. UNL isn’t just a workplace; it’s a place to build your career and make a meaningful impact in Nebraska.
About Lincoln, Nebraska
Home to the University of Nebraska–Lincoln, the city of Lincoln consistently ranks one of the happiest cities in America and highest for livability thanks to a low cost of living, great schools and friendly, community-minded residents. Set amidst a big sky and open landscape, the state’s capital city is simple to navigate with a nationally noted low crime rate, a wide range of housing choices and a reliable public transit system. As one of the fastest growing metro areas in the Midwest, Lincoln boasts a growing technology sector, more parkland per capita than all but a few U.S. cities, an extensive bike trail network, and numerous options for recreational and personal interest activities. It’s easy to feel at home here.
The University of Nebraska does not discriminate based on race, color, ethnicity, national origin, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, disability, age, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, and/or political affiliation in its programs, activities, or employment. See https://equity.unl.edu/notice-nondiscrimination/.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Sociology
jobs.description:
Job Details
Job Title: Assistant Professor of Sociology
Location: Kennesaw, Georgia
Regular/Temporary: Regular
Full/Part Time: Full-Time
Job ID: 304034
About Us
For more than 60 years, Kennesaw State University has been known for its entrepreneurial spirit and sense of community. A leader in innovative teaching and learning, Kennesaw State is located just north of Atlanta and combines a suburban setting on two metro-Atlanta campuses in Kennesaw and Marietta. As one of Georgia's largest universities, Kennesaw State offers undergraduate and graduate degrees to over 50,000 students. Our high-impact research and Division I athletics also draw students from throughout the region and across the globe. A member of the University System of Georgia, Kennesaw State is a Carnegie-designated doctoral research institution (R2) committed to becoming a world-class academic institution positioned to broaden its academic and research missions and expand its scope on a local, regional, and national level.
Our university's vibrant culture, career opportunities, rich benefits, and values of respect, integrity, collaboration, inclusivity, and accountability make us an employer of choice. As part of the University System of Georgia, Kennesaw State exemplifies the power and promise of a student-centered, research-driven university. In addition, Kennesaw State supports the University of Georgia's core values of accountability, excellence, integrity, and respect. We are searching for talented people to join Kennesaw State University in our vision. For more information, visit the Kennesaw State University website.
Location
Our Kennesaw campus is located at 1000 Chastain Road NW, Kennesaw, GA 30144. Our Marietta campus is located at 1100 South Marietta Parkway, Marietta, GA 30060.
Department Information
We are a collective of interdisciplinary and community-engaged scholars committed to investigating and addressing social problems, which are broadly defined as conditions or behaviors that have a negative impact on society. We examine and understand these problems using scientific approaches, including applied, theoretical, and evaluation research. Faculty expertise broadly includes sociological, criminological, and criminal justice research areas related to social harms, social organization and disorganization, policing, courts, and correctional systems, life course sociology and criminology, causes and correlates of crime and deviance, responses to crime, laws, policies, and practices, and myriad forms of inequality. Finally, SCJ faculty are scholars and teachers committed to excellence in teaching and mentorship to ensure our graduates are ready for life and work after college. Faculty in the department engage in multiple forms of experiential education and high-impact practices to synthesize their teaching, research, and service roles.
With more than 400 full-time faculty and 8,100 degree-seeking students, the Norman J. Radow College of Humanities & Social Sciences is dedicated to pioneering workforce readiness in the humanities and social sciences. By staying true to our Liberal Arts values and integrating practical knowledge and experiential learning into our curriculum, we empower our students to become responsible citizens ready for the demands of the modern workplace. The home of three schools and eight departments, the College offers more than 80 graduate and undergraduate programs of study in both traditional and interdisciplinary fields. These programs enable students to develop leadership, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills, as well as a strong sense of civic engagement.
The College is committed to the success of our students, faculty, staff and communities. We seek candidates whose experience has prepared them to fulfill that commitment and engage our students, partners, and stakeholders effectively.
Job Summary
Kennesaw State University is now accepting applications for a full-time, tenure track faculty position as Assistant Professor of Sociology in the Department of Sociology and Criminal Justice with a preferred start date of August 2027. This is a nine-month contracted position and is for work to be performed in the state of Georgia.
Responsibilities
Maintain a productive, high-impact program of research and scholarship.
Pursue external funding in support of research and scholarly activity.
Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in research methods and statistics in the Department of Sociology and Criminal Justice, including in the M.S. in Criminal Justice program, along with introductory and substantive courses aligned with the candidate's expertise and departmental needs.
KSU uses a differentiated workload model. The baseline teaching workload is 9 credit hours (i.e., 3 courses) per semester.
Teach courses across varying modalities (face-to-face, hybrid and online) and class sizes (including large class sizes) on the Kennesaw and/or Marietta campuses.
Engage and mentor undergraduate and graduate students in research that supports their academic and professional development.
Contribute service to the department, college and university, including committee work and shared governance.
Teaching assignments will be based on earned degrees and SACSCOC Faculty Credentials Guidelines.
Required Qualifications
An earned doctoral degree, or the foreign equivalent, in Sociology or a related discipline is required at the time of hire.
Demonstrated training and expertise in quantitative research methods and applied statistics, as evidenced by graduate coursework, publications, presentations or teaching.
Demonstrated experience teaching research methods and/or statistics, or demonstrated preparation to do so.
Demonstrated productivity in research and scholarship, as evidence by publications, presentations and/or scholarly work.
Preferred Qualifications
Evidence of effective teaching across multiple modalities (face-to-face, online, and hybrid).
A program of research employing advanced quantitative or computational methods (e.g., hierarchical modeling, structural equation modeling, causal inference, longitudinal, spatial or network methods).
A substantive research agenda in one or more subfields: medical sociology, demography/population studies, public health or criminology.
Demonstrated potential for, or a record of, securing external research funding.
A record of publishing scholarship in reputable outlets.
Ability to teach courses that serve both the Sociology and Criminal Justice programs, including at the graduate (MSCJ) level.
Required Documents to Attach
CV
Cover Letter (3 page max) outlining how the candidate meets the required and preferred qualifications, as well as their (a) research interests and futureresearch plans, (b) teaching philosophy, and (c) evidence of teaching effectiveness other efforts to facilitate student success.
Unofficial Transcripts (Official Transcripts and Official International Course-by-Course Evaluations Due Upon Hire)
Names, phone numbers, and email addresses of at least 3 references
The full text of up to 3 representative publications, preprints, or scholarly works in progress (Upload as Writing Sample)
Incomplete applications will not be considered.
Apply Before Date
Review of applications will begin immediately.For full consideration, please apply by November 1, 2026.
USG Core Values
The University System of Georgia is comprised of our 25 institutions of higher education and learning as well as the System Office. Our USG Statement of Core Values are Integrity, Excellence, Accountability, and Respect. These values serve as the foundation for all that we do as an organization, and each USG community member is responsible for demonstrating and upholding these standards. More details on the USG Statement of Core Values and Code of Conduct are available in USG Board Policy 8.2.18.1.2 and can be found on-line at https://www.usg.edu/policymanual/section8/C224/#p8.2.18_personnel_conduct.
Additionally, USG supports Freedom of Expression as stated in Board Policy 6.5 Freedom of Expression and Academic Freedom found on-line at https://www.usg.edu/policymanual/section6/C2653.
Equal Employment Opportunity
Kennesaw State University is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. The University is committed to maintaining a fair and respectful environment for living, work and study. To that end, and in accordance with federal and state law, Board of Regents policy, and University policy, the University prohibits harassment of or discrimination against any person because of race, color, sex (including sexual harassment, pregnancy, and medical conditions related to pregnancy), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, ethnicity or national origin, religion, age, genetic information, disability, or veteran or military status by any member of the KSU Community on campus, in connection with a University program or activity, or in a manner that creates a hostile environment for members of the KSU community.
For additional information on this policy, or to file a complaint under the provisions of this policy, students, employees, applicants for employment or admission or other third parties should contact the Office of Institutional Equity at English Building, Suite 225, eeo@kennesaw.edu.
Background Check
Per the University System of Georgia background check policy, all final candidates will be required to consent to a criminal background investigation. Final candidates may be asked to disclose criminal record history during the initial screening process and prior to a conditional offer of employment. Applicants for positions of trust with screening results which confirm a disqualifying criminal history will be immediately disqualified from employment eligibility.
All applicants are required to include professional references as part of their application process. Some positions may require additional job based screenings such as motor vehicle report, credit check, preemployment drug screening and/or verification of academic credentials. https://www.usg.edu/hr/assets/hr/hrap_manual/HRAP_Background_Investigation_Employment.pdf

Description:
About Us
The Office of the Vice-Provost, Faculty & Academic Life (VPFAL) is the institutional office responsible for providing academic human resources services in relation to faculty members and librarians across the University. It provides advice, support, and/or approval to Divisions and divisional academic human resources teams and the senior administration on a broad range of matters related to the academic life cycle. The office also serves as the primary point of contact for engagement with the University of Toronto Faculty Association, including in relation to salary, benefit and workload negotiations, investigations, policy revision and development, as well as grievances and arbitration.
Your Opportunity
Under the general direction of the Associate Director, and working in collaboration with a wide range of offices both internal and external to the University, the Faculty Relations Consultant will provide a broad range of support in respect of academic human resources and faculty/labour relations activities across the University of Toronto, with a primary focus on negotiations with the UTFA and case management of grievances and workplace complaints involving faculty members and librarians. These include complaints regarding alleged incidents of bullying, harassment, discrimination, sexual violence, and complaints from students regarding their experience with graduate supervision. The incumbent will also provide support on related governance processes (i.e., bringing matters through Governing Council processes for information or approval).
The role requires strong skills and knowledge in employee and labour relations, issue assessment, case management, stakeholder consultation, conflict resolution, policy interpretation, collective agreement administration, and handling highly sensitive and confidential workplace matters.
Key responsibilities:
Advising on the interpretation and application of agreements, policies and procedures; case management from a VPFAL perspective of workplace and student complaints, and grievances, involving faculty members and librarians; drafting letters; providing support to University bargaining committees and the process of implementation of agreements; producing a variety of reports in support of faculty relations and bargaining with UTFA; and providing related administrative support including note-taking in meetings, preparing speaking notes and keeping track of deadlines, including governance timelines.
Qualifications Required:
Education:
University degree in a relevant discipline and course work in the Human Resources field with particular focus on labour relations/faculty relations; or equivalent combination of education and experience.
An MIR/MIRHR is considered an asset.
Experience:
Minimum three (3) years' related human resources experience with an emphasis on collective agreement and employment policy interpretation and application, grievance/arbitration processes, and workplace complaints and investigations.
Experience in Academic HR in a university context is considered an asset.
Demonstrated experience advising internal clients in policy interpretation and with employee investigations and case management.
Knowledge of labour and employment law, including the Ontario Human Rights Code.
Experience working with diverse populations including demonstrated effective consultation skills with designated groups.
Sound knowledge of human resources best practices and familiarity with public sector employment.
Must have previous experience data management.
Significant knowledge of HR principles and practices and, preferably, knowledge of the University’s policies and practices as they pertain to faculty members and librarians.
Skills:
Computer experience including word processing, spreadsheet applications, database management, and scheduling software (e.g, Outlook).
Internet research skills required.
Other:
Excellent oral and written communication, interpersonal and organizational skills.
Excellent analytical skills.
Ability to exercise tact, independent judgement and discretion.
Ability to handle sensitive client interactions effectively and with professionalism.
Ability to maintain strict confidentiality and to handle sensitive information in an appropriate manner.
Ability to understand and synthesize information and statistics.
Demonstrated ability to prioritize a fluctuating workload, under pressure, and to meet deadlines.
Accuracy and attention to detail essential.
Ability to work both independently and within a team environment.
