Description:
The Department of Mathematics at the University of Pennsylvania invites applications for one tenure-track Assistant Professor position in Algebra or Analysis. Responsibilities include teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in Mathematics and conducting research in their field.
We are a collaborative and interactive department. We pursue original investigations in Differential Geometry, Partial Differential Equations, Functional Analysis, Mathematical Physics, Algebraic Topology, Algebraic Geometry and Algebraic Number Theory, Combinatorics and Algorithms, Category Theory, Logic and its applications to Computer Science, and several other areas of current mathematical development. The Mathematics Department is housed within the School of Arts & Sciences, which is comprised of the College of Arts and Sciences, the Graduate Division, and the College of Liberal and Professional Studies. Interdisciplinary research and collaboration are supported by the breadth and depth of academic pursuits at Penn as well as the proximity of resources on our contiguous green urban campus in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. We promote and encourage curiosity, intellectual engagement, and discovery among all our students and faculty. University, School, and departmental resources that support our efforts include but are not limited to: the Offices of the Vice Provost for Faculty and Vice Provost for Research, PennGlobal, Wellness at Penn, the Center for Excellence in Teaching, Learning and Innovation, the Penn Center for Undergraduate Research and Fellowships, and Penn Human Resources.
The department offers an undergraduate major that provides students an understanding of the modern discipline of mathematics. More generally, we teach hundreds of undergraduate students and sixty grad students each year. Our graduate students often go on to become postdocs and faculty in academic institutions, and to work as applied research mathematicians for government agencies, as industry scientists working in data analysis, and as researchers in biotech companies. Our department also participates in cross-disciplinary efforts, many faculty interacting with adjacent undergraduate programs such as computer science, physics, systems and mechanical engineering, and operations research and statistics in the business school.

● Capacity for teaching at both the graduate and undergraduate levels and mentoring and supporting a diverse student body

We welcome teacher-scholars whose work applies emerging technologies to questions in nutrition, dietetics, and health. Relevant areas may include digital health, artificial intelligence and machine learning, nutrition informatics, health data science, computational or precision nutrition, mobile and wearable technologies, technology-supported nutrition care or education, and other related applications. We welcome work spanning clinical, community, public health, foodservice, behavioral, population, and educational contexts.
The Department of Nutrition, Food Science, and Packaging at San José State University is a dynamic, interdisciplinary academic community committed to preparing students for professional leadership in nutrition, dietetics, food science, food management, and packaging through high-quality teaching, applied research, experiential learning, and engagement with community and industry partners. Established in 1911, the department was the first nutrition department in the California State University system and today offers a B.S. in Nutritional Science with concentrations in Dietetics, and Applied Nutrition and Food Sciences; a B.S. in Packaging; M.S. programs in Nutritional Science and Packaging; the Spartan Accelerated Graduate Education (SAGE) Scholars Program in Nutritional Science and Packaging; an ACEND-accredited Didactic Program in Dietetics; and a Dietetic Internship. A distinctive strength of the department is its Packaging program, one of only a small number of packaging degree programs in the United States, which combines science, engineering, design, and business and benefits from SJSU’s location in Silicon Valley and strong connections with the medical device, pharmaceutical, food, technology, and packaging industries.
The department provides students with hands-on learning through laboratories, applied research, internships, professional experiences, and community-based activities, while fostering a diverse, inclusive, and collaborative environment in which faculty, staff, and students work across disciplinary boundaries. Recent student accomplishments in academic, professional, and culinary competitions reflect the department’s emphasis on student achievement and professional preparation. Faculty joining the department will have opportunities to contribute to innovative undergraduate and graduate education, mentor a diverse student population, develop interdisciplinary and applied research programs, collaborate with colleagues and external partners throughout Silicon Valley and the greater Bay Area, and help shape the continued growth of programs addressing evolving challenges in nutrition, food systems, health, and sustainable and innovative packaging. Current Registered Dietitian Nutritionist (RDN) credential or evidence to be credentialed by August 17, 2027.

Record of scholarly publications or strong potential for a productive scholarly agenda.

Expertise or an emerging research program in health technology, artificial intelligence, digital health, nutrition informatics, health data science, computational nutrition, or related applications to nutrition and dietetics, particularly work that advances ethical, equitable, and evidence-based uses of technology.

Position Description
The School of Information at San José State University is pleased to announce a search for Assistant Professor of Cultural Heritage Informatics, AI/Digital Transformation, and Critical Technology Studies beginning in August 2027. We especially welcome applicants whose work advances the emerging field of Critical Technology Studies, investigating how technological systems shape knowledge production, cultural memory, access to information, social equity, democratic participation, and institutional practice.
The School of Information (iSchool - SJSU - School of Information - Information Science School) prepares professionals who organize, preserve, analyze, protect, teach, and improve access to information across communities and institutions. Our new faculty member will join a scholarly community with:
thousands of students and a broad global alumni community;
one of the largest and most diverse schools in the information field;
fully online graduate programs that support working professionals;
an ALA-accredited MLIS program;
an emphasis on access, equity, community service, digital literacy, and ethical technology; and
a commitment to working on problems connected to information access, AI literacy, digital preservation, cybersecurity, and social justice.
The School of Information and San José State University value institutional excellence and are committed to advancing equity through research, teaching, and service. We enroll more than 40,000 students, many of whom are historically underserved; approximately 45% of our undergraduate students are first-generation college students and 38% are Pell Grant recipients. In addition, we are both a Hispanic Serving Institution (HSI) and an Asian American and Native American Pacific Islander Serving Institution (AANAPISI). SJSU aspires to create holistic learning environments that facilitate both individual and collective transformation. We seek teacher-scholars who cultivate inclusive, empowering spaces for mutual learning, skill-building, and knowledge exchange for all students. Our commitment to lifelong learning supports meaningful connections among faculty, staff, students, alumni, and the broader communities we serve.
We invite all applicants to include a Statement of Institutional Excellence (or incorporate it into your cover letter) to share how your lived and professional experiences will contribute to the SJSU community—particularly in relation to student success. A guide to writing this statement can be found at SJSU Institutional Excellence Statement Guidelines.

Earned doctorate in Library and Information Science, Information Studies, Informatics, Archives, Museum Studies, Digital Humanities, Science and Technology Studies, Computer Science, Data Science, or a closely related field by the time of appointment.

Evidence of scholarship, teaching, or professional practice related to digital transformation, emerging technologies, or critical technology studies.

About Binghamton University:
Binghamton University is a premier public R1 research institution in the State University of New York (SUNY) system that unites more than 130 broadly interdisciplinary educational programs with some of the most vibrant research in the nation. Our unique character - shaped by our mission, outstanding academics, facilities, and community life - promotes extraordinary student success, research, and service; Binghamton University is where our students, faculty and staff thrive.
Working at Binghamton University is more than about having a great job - it is about having the opportunity to flourish in an exciting, engaging environment. Our faculty and staff appreciate Binghamton's collegial and inclusive culture and its commitment to excellence, education, innovation, and civic engagement. Our diverse campus community contributes to our success.
Binghamton merges rigorous academics, distinguished faculty who value cutting-edge, and community-engaged research, teaching and service, exceptional staff, and ultramodern facilities to engage and challenge its 18,000+ students. Our high-achieving student body represents diverse experiences from first-generation college-goers to international students. Beyond their talent, these classmates share a desire to shape the future through technology, insight, intellectual exploration, and community service.
Job Description:
Department Overview:
The Biomedical Engineering (BME) Department is particularly strong in advanced biomanufacturing, biomaterials, biomechanics, cardiovascular engineering, nanomedicine, neuroengineering, organ-on-a-chip, stem cells, tissue engineering/regenerative medicine, and wearable biosensors. The BME Department is the home of the Center of Biomanufacturing for Regenerative Medicine (CBRM), and the Department has recently formed a joint Institute for Regenerative Medicine with the Upstate Medical University. The Department has recently launched a workforce training program partnered with the School of Management to develop a Biomanufacturing Project Management Certificate Program funded by BioMADE. For more information, please visit our website. Funding from private operational support and public capital investment has allowed Binghamton University to establish the New York Center for AI Responsibility and Research, one of the nation's first centers aimed at ethical AI research. The Center will serve as a premier AI research hub for the entire State University of New York system and focus on developing novel technical innovations related to the safety and security of artificial intelligence models and systems.
Job Description:
As part of the strategic plan for expanding biomedical and health science research in emerging fields, the Department of Biomedical Engineering in the Watson College, Binghamton University (BU), State University of New York (SUNY), invites applications for one tenured faculty position at the full professor level with an expected start date of September 1, 2027.
We are seeking a well-established biomedical engineer who has a successful track record in funding, scholarship, teaching, and service. We seek applications from candidates in all areas of biomedical engineering; however, we are particularly interested in the following areas: Artificial Intelligence (AI), Data Science, or Controls in Biomedical Engineering (brain-computer interface, computer vision, machine learning, digital pathology, biomedical big data, cell/tissue/organ atlas, AI-empowered cell biomanufacturing and tissue biofabrication). Candidates with a demonstrated commitment to diversity and inclusiveness are preferred.
Responsibilities of the position include:
Developing and implementing a robust plan that synergizes and accelerates our strategic research partnerships with Upstate Medical University and the CBRM.
Augmenting existing capabilities and expertise in AI, data science, and controls in Biomedical Engineering at Binghamton University and Upstate Medical University, building on ongoing research at both campuses, and further strengthening and growing cross-institutional collaborations.
Making significant contributions to Binghamton University's New York Center for AI Responsibility and Research.
The successful candidate will receive a comprehensive startup package including competitive salary compensation and benefits commensurate with qualifications and experience.
Requirements:
Required Qualifications:
PhD degree in biomedical engineering or a closely related discipline
Proven research leadership
Record of scholarship as evidenced by peer-reviewed publications and citations
Successful record of securing external funding
Experience as an effective educator and research mentor
Preferred Qualifications:
Background in AI, Data Science, or Controls in Biomedical Engineering
Demonstrated commitment to diversity and inclusiveness

Job Details
Assistant Professor - Special Education **FACULTY VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT** Lehman College, of The City University of New York, ranks among the top five institutions in the nation for fostering social mobility. A four-year Hispanic-Serving Institution in the Bronx, Lehman offers bachelor’s, master’s, and advanced degrees and certificate programs in the Liberal Arts, sciences, and professions. The College’s community-driven mission and notable academic programs attract a diverse, international enrollment of over 15,000 students who take courses on its 37-acre, tree-lined campus and online degree programs. Many thousands more community members benefit yearly from its active cultural, educational, health, and economic outreach programs and services. The School of Education (SOE) is one of the six schools within Lehman College. SOE reflects the mission of the college in serving the Bronx, New York City, and surrounding region as an intellectual, economic, and cultural center. As the only public higher education school of education in the Bronx, SOE embrace’s a vision of preparing future educators to meet the needs of increasingly diverse student population who themselves represent a racial, ethnic, cultural, and linguistic spectrum that remains one of the strengths of our state and community. SOE is organized in three departments: Early Childhood and Childhood Education; Counseling, Leadership, Literacy, and Special Education (CLLSE); and Middle and High School Education. SOE offers initial preparation programs that include Early Childhood Education, Childhood Education, English Education, Foreign Language, Science Education, Mathematics Education, Social Studies Education, TESOL, Literacy, and Special Education across grades. Bilingual Extensions in most certification areas is also offered. SOE also collaborates with the schools of Arts and Humanities and Health Sciences, Human Services, and Nursing in offering initial preparation programs in Music Education, Art Education, and Health Education. SOE offers two advanced preparation programs in Literacy Studies, Mental Health and Educational Leadership, including a doctorate in Organizational Leadership. SOE houses several institutes and centers to advance educator preparation, professional development, and school–community engagement. CLLSE houses a variety of outstanding and nationally accredited graduate degree programs, with each culminating in a doctoral degree, or master’s degree, or an advanced certificate, and most leading to New York State Certification. Our faculty are committed to excellence in scholarship and teaching and are recognized for their work with Bronx and urban schools, districts, nonprofits, and other community organizations, and strive to provide transformational learning experiences for our graduate students. They are experienced in meeting the needs of adult learners and are dedicated to mentoring, motivating, and supporting our graduate students through consistent advisement, engaging instruction, continuous program improvement, and career placement. The Department of Counseling, Leadership, Literacy, and Special Education (CLLSE) in the School of Education at Lehman College, City University of New York (Bronx, New York City) invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor in Special Education. The successful candidate must demonstrate excellence in teaching, service, advocacy, and research in the field of Special Education to engage and inspire our economically, culturally, and linguistically diverse candidates, colleagues, and P–20 schools. The successful candidate will be expected to demonstrate knowledge and skills for teaching graduate-level courses (on campus and online) in multiple modalities within the Special Education curriculum. Candidate may also be assigned to teach undergraduate courses and advise undergraduate students. The successful candidate will be expected to advise students, engage in and maintain an active program of research, scholarly work (including professional publications and presentations), service, and overall, maintain professional identity as a Special Educator. Excellent administrative and interpersonal skills are required. Familiarity with accreditation at the higher education level is helpful. This position reports directly to the chairperson of CLLSE. **Position Responsibilities:** Responsibilities include maintaining a teaching load of 18 credits per 9-month academic year. Teaching assignments include graduate-level and undergraduate courses delivered on campus and online across multiple instructional modalities within the Special Education curriculum. The successful candidate will share responsibility for continuous program improvement and program accreditation, academic advisement, and department assignments, including administrative duties, program and course development. Faculty are expected to maintain a regular on campus presence for teaching, office hours, departmental and other activities. In addition to eighteen (18) teaching hours per year, you are required to engage in research, scholarship, and service. You may be assigned to teach evenings and/or weekends, and/or online, either synchronously or asynchronously. This is not a remote position. Other responsibilities include: + Engage in student recruitment, application review, and admissions processes + Engage in program assessment, accreditation activities, and ongoing program development and improvement initiatives + Support department and program operations and clinical coordination to ensure effective student placement and supervision + Collaborate with faculty and staff across departments and schools to advance interdisciplinary and sponsored program initiatives + Pursue external funding opportunities to support research, program innovation, and continuous improvement efforts + Develop and maintain articulation agreements and educational partnerships with schools and other external organizations and institutions. + Engage in service to the university, college, school, and department through committee membership and related professional contributions + Assist with program hiring, staffing, mentoring, and supervision of part-time and adjunct faculty. + Perform other related duties as assigned in support of program and institutional goals **QUALIFICATIONS** Required Qualifications • Ph.D. in Special Education or related degree + Demonstrated excellence in graduate-level teaching through in-person and online modalities. + Experience working with diverse student populations. Strong commitment to social justice, anti-racism, and anti-oppression, diversity, equity, and inclusion + Ongoing record of scholarship. + Strong organizational and interpersonal skills and the ability to work collegially as a team member. **COMPENSATION** $89,777 - $105,588. CUNY offers faculty a competitive compensation and benefits package covering health insurance, pension and retirement benefits, paid parental leave, and savings programs. We also provide mentoring and support for research, scholarship, and publication as part of our commitment to ongoing faculty professional development. **HOW TO APPLY** Visit www.cuny.edu, access the employment page, log in or create a new user account, and search for this vacancy using the Job ID or Title. Select "Apply Now" and provide the requested information. Candidates must attach a resume, cover letter, and three professional references (name, title, organization, and contact information). **CLOSING DATE** The review of applications will begin on October 20th, 2026 until a candidate is identified. **JOB SEARCH CATEGORY** CUNY Job Posting: Faculty **EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY** CUNY encourages people with disabilities, minorities, veterans and women to apply. At CUNY, Italian Americans are also included among our protected groups. Applicants and employees will not be discriminated against on the basis of any legally protected category, including sexual orientation or gender identity. EEO/AA/Vet/Disability Employer. Advertised Job Summary:
Under limited supervision of the Principal Investigator (PI), this individual will conduct research on the synthesis of single crystal and polycrystalline materials, thin-film deposition, and micro/nano fabrication; characterizing these materials using laboratory-based techniques to measure their electrical, magnetic, optical, and thermal properties; and collaborating with experimental and theoretical researchers to develop structure-property relationships and novel functional materials.
Job Related Minimum Required Education and Experience:
Applicants must hold a PhD in condensed matter physics or closely related field and have postdoctoral experience in material synthesis, thin film fabrication, characterization, and theoretical modeling.
Knowledge/Skills/Abilities:
Expertise in material synthesis, thin film fabrication, characterization, and theoretical modeling.
Required to conduct business lawfully and ethically by consistently adhering to compliance policies, procedures, and regulations.
Job Duty:
Synthesis of single crystal and polycrystalline materials, thin-film deposition and micro/nano fabrication: To successfully accomplish the proposed research objectives, it is essential to hire a qualified candidate with expertise in the synthesis of single-crystal and polycrystalline materials, thin-film deposition, and micro/nanofabrication. These activities require specialized technical knowledge, extensive hands-on experience, and the ability to operate sophisticated research equipment that is critical to the project. The research involves the controlled growth of high-quality single-crystal and polycrystalline materials with precise control over composition, crystallinity, and defect density. In addition, the project requires the deposition of thin films using advanced techniques while maintaining stringent control over film thickness, uniformity, and interface quality. The fabrication of micro- and nanoscale devices further demands expertise in cleanroom processes, including photolithography, electron-beam lithography, etching, deposition, and device integration. These tasks are highly specialized and require trained personnel to ensure reproducibility, reliability, and high-quality experimental outcomes. The individual hired will be responsible for designing and optimizing material synthesis protocols, performing thin-film growth and characterization, carrying out micro/nanofabrication processes, maintaining laboratory and cleanroom equipment, troubleshooting fabrication challenges, documenting experimental procedures, and training junior researchers and students as needed. The researcher will also collaborate with other team members to integrate synthesized materials into functional devices and accelerate the overall research progress. Hiring a dedicated expert will significantly improve research efficiency, reduce experimental errors, minimize equipment downtime, and ensure compliance with laboratory safety and cleanroom operating procedures. Their specialized expertise will enable the project to meet its technical milestones on schedule while producing high-quality, reproducible results suitable for publication and future technology development.
Essential Function:
Yes
Percentage of Time:
45
Job Duty:
Characterizing materials using laboratory-based techniques (including national user facilities) to measure their electrical, magnetic, optical, and thermal properties; collaborating with experimental and theoretical researchers to develop structure–property relationships and novel functional materials: The success of the proposed research depends on comprehensive characterization of synthesized materials to establish the relationships between their structure, composition, and functional properties. To achieve these objectives, it is necessary to hire a qualified candidate with expertise in advanced materials characterization, data analysis, and collaborative research involving both experimental and theoretical approaches. The project requires systematic characterization of materials using a wide range of laboratory-based techniques, as well as specialized instrumentation available at national user facilities. These measurements include electrical, magnetic, optical, and thermal property characterization, together with complementary structural, chemical, and microstructural analyses. The hired researcher will be responsible for planning and conducting characterization experiments, preparing samples for analysis, operating and coordinating access to advanced characterization facilities, analyzing and interpreting complex datasets, and integrating experimental results with theoretical modeling. The individual will also collaborate closely with experimentalists and computational researchers to develop quantitative structure–property relationships, identify the mechanisms governing material performance, and guide the design and optimization of novel functional materials. In addition, the researcher will coordinate user-facility proposals, manage experimental campaigns at national laboratories, maintain detailed documentation of characterization results, and assist in preparing publications, presentations, and technical reports. Hiring a dedicated expert will ensure that characterization activities are performed efficiently and at the highest technical standard, maximizing the scientific value of both laboratory and user-facility measurements. Their expertise will accelerate the discovery and optimization of functional materials, strengthen collaborations across experimental and theoretical teams, improve the reproducibility and rigor of the research, and help the project achieve its scientific milestones within the proposed timeline.
Essential Function:
Yes
Percentage of Time:
45
Job Duty:
Mentoring other group members, including postdocs, graduate students, and undergraduate researchers: A dedicated research scientist is essential not only to advance the technical objectives of the proposed project but also to provide consistent mentorship and training for postdoctoral researchers, graduate students, and undergraduate researchers. As the research program expands in scope and complexity, effective supervision and knowledge transfer are critical to maintaining high-quality research, ensuring reproducible results, and fostering the professional development of junior researchers. The hired researcher is expected to provide guidance on experimental design, laboratory techniques, instrumentation, data analysis, and scientific problem-solving. They will train new group members in laboratory safety, standard operating procedures, equipment operation, and best practices for data management and documentation. In addition, they will assist trainees in troubleshooting experiments, interpreting results, preparing manuscripts and conference presentations, and developing independent research skills. The research scientist will also coordinate collaborative activities within the research group, facilitate communication among experimental and computational team members, and help ensure that projects progress efficiently toward established milestones. Their regular interaction with trainees will promote a collaborative research environment, improve productivity, and enable more effective use of laboratory and shared research facilities. Hiring an experienced researcher with strong mentoring capabilities will strengthen the group’s research infrastructure by providing sustained technical leadership and continuity across multiple projects. This role will enhance the quality of training for students and postdoctoral researchers, accelerate their development as independent scientists, and increase the overall productivity and impact of the research program while allowing the principal investigator to focus on strategic research direction, external collaborations, and project management.
Essential Function:
Yes

10

For more than 60 years, Kennesaw State University has been known for its entrepreneurial spirit and sense of community. Location
Our Kennesaw campus is located at 1000 Chastain Road NW, Kennesaw, GA 30144. Our Marietta campus is located at 1100 South Marietta Parkway, Marietta, GA 30060.
Department Information
We are a collective of interdisciplinary and community-engaged scholars committed to investigating and addressing social problems, which are broadly defined as conditions or behaviors that have a negative impact on society. We examine and understand these problems using scientific approaches, including applied, theoretical, and evaluation research. Faculty expertise broadly includes sociological, criminological, and criminal justice research areas related to social harms, social organization and disorganization, policing, courts, and correctional systems, life course sociology and criminology, causes and correlates of crime and deviance, responses to crime, laws, policies, and practices, and myriad forms of inequality. Finally, SCJ faculty are scholars and teachers committed to excellence in teaching and mentorship to ensure our graduates are ready for life and work after college. Faculty in the department engage in multiple forms of experiential education and high-impact practices to synthesize their teaching, research, and service roles.
With more than 400 full-time faculty and 8,100 degree-seeking students, the Norman J. The home of three schools and eight departments, the College offers more than 80 graduate and undergraduate programs of study in both traditional and interdisciplinary fields. These programs enable students to develop leadership, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills, as well as a strong sense of civic engagement.

Teach courses across varying modalities (face-to-face, hybrid and online) and class sizes (including large class sizes) on the Kennesaw and/or Marietta campuses.

Teaching assignments will be based on earned degrees and SACSCOC Faculty Credentials Guidelines.
Required Qualifications
An earned doctoral degree, or the foreign equivalent, in Sociology or a related discipline is required at the time of hire.
Demonstrated training and expertise in quantitative research methods and applied statistics, as evidenced by graduate coursework, publications, presentations or teaching.
Demonstrated experience teaching research methods and/or statistics, or demonstrated preparation to do so.
Demonstrated productivity in research and scholarship, as evidence by publications, presentations and/or scholarly work.

The University of Pennsylvania School of Nursing, one of 12 Schools in a highly ranked institution, is dedicated to the integration of interdisciplinary research, education, and practice.

The Nurse-Midwifery program prepares graduates for midwifery practice focused on providing family-centered, comprehensive care for fundamentally healthy people and their families. The BSN and MPN programs both include courses focused on sexual reproductive health and nursing of women and infants.

The School of Art + Art History in the College of the Arts seeks an Assistant Professor of Studio Art with expertise in printmaking in the expanded field to join our forward-looking interdisciplinary program at a top-ranked public university. We seek an innovative artist-educator to lead the development of printmaking curricula in the expanded field. The ideal candidate has an active studio practice that engages the complex materiality, history, and theories of printmaking, as well as emerging technologies and methods, and their creative research is informed by contemporary art theories and practice. They will have a strong knowledge of historical and contemporary reproductive and fabrication media that they present as a vibrant and relevant technology. The successful candidate will demonstrate a clear commitment to interdisciplinary artistic practices with an emphasis on printmaking, including DIY strategies, 'maker tools,' and historical and future-focused print methods and ideas.
The University of Florida College of the Arts intends to be a transformative community, responding to and generating paradigmatic shifts in the arts and beyond. As artists and scholars, we embrace the complexity of our evolving human experience and seek to empower our students and faculty to shape that experience fearlessly through critical study, creative practice, and provocation. We seek a colleague who identifies as a change-maker. We seek a colleague who will position emerging artists and researchers as catalysts for justice on local and global levels.
This position is covered by the United Faculty of Florida Contract. You can view this employment union contract here https://admin.hr.ufl.edu/compliance/employee-relations-and-ethics/union-negotiations/united-faculty-of-florida-contract/.

Teach a 2/2 course load at the undergraduate and graduate levels in printmaking in the expanded field in an interdisciplinary studio art curriculum.
Course assignments may also include Studio Art foundations and non-majors courses, including courses in the university's General Education curriculum.
Course assignments may also include interdisciplinary graduate courses, such as a seminar for first-year MFA in Art students or a team-taught critique seminar.
Mentor and advise graduate students and supervise graduate committees.
Maintain an active profile of creative research, consistent with the expectation of tenure and promotion
Collaborate with staff in shared supervision of the printmaking facilities.
Actively participate in our learning community and in shared governance through service to the school, college, university, and profession.
SCHOOL OF ART + ART HISTORY: The School of Art + Art History (SAAH) believes that art, design, and scholarship are critical to the cultural life and creative advancement of our local, national, and international communities. We empower each of our 360 undergraduate and 130 graduate students with knowledge, skills, and curiosity to engage thoughtfully and courageously with our changing world. The school offers BA, BFA, MA, MFA, and PhD programs, both residential and online, and students can study art education, art history, curatorial studies, graphic design, design & visual communications, museology (museum studies), and studio art. The 4Most Gallery and the three University Galleries provide exhibition space for international contemporary art and student work. The school has facilities in three on-campus buildings, and three off-campus sites. SAAH is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Art and Design.
The School of Art + Art History nurtures a culture of critical inquiry in our scholarly and creative work. The school has 38 full-time (including one director) and 11 part-time faculty, plus 11 staff members. The faculty publish, present, curate, and exhibit widely and internationally at the highest level. They bring their scholarship and creative work into their teaching, offering innovative learning experiences to their students. The school's programs have a focus on experiential learning and research that engages with our global and local communities. The school's four galleries serve as a laboratory where students can participate in the lifecycle of the work of art, as artists who display their work, as curators who organize exhibitions, and as historians and critics who articulate what they see. The galleries hosted 26 exhibitions last academic year with dozens of additional exhibitions displayed in other school spaces. The school's programs in art and design view their work as interdisciplinary and often collaborative with other disciplines across campus. The school's innovative and growing design program aims to use the State of Florida as a laboratory to develop solutions to real-world problems. The endowed Harn Eminent Scholar in Art History Chair and partially endowed Visiting Artist Series sponsored lectures, masterclasses, and studio visits from 20 artists, scholars, and designers last year, with an additional 30+ paying virtual visits to SAAH classrooms. The annual SAAH New York and Museum Studies trips connect students to alumni and other industry professionals who are thriving in their careers.
THE COLLEGE OF THE ARTS: The College of the Arts is an engine of transformation that generates paradigmatic shifts in the arts and beyond, while nurturing adaptability, innovation, and excellence. We foster an environment where novel creative practice, leading research, and experiential learning thrive. Our students, faculty, and staff interrogate and respond to the ever-changing relationship between technology and the human spirit. We prepare future leaders in artistic professions and creative industries, while developing student capacity for interdisciplinary scholarship that serves and engages local and global communities. The College offers baccalaureate, masters, and doctoral degrees. Approximately 1,600 students are pursuing majors in degrees offered by the College of the Arts under the direction of 150 faculty members in its three accredited schools— the School of Art + Art History, the School of Music, and the School of Theatre + Dance, and in the Center for Arts in Medicine, the Digital Worlds Institute, and the Center for Arts, Migration, and Entrepreneurship. In addition, the college comprises the University Galleries, and the University level of the New World School of the Arts in Miami.
The University of Florida: The University of Florida is a comprehensive learning institution built on a land grant foundation. We are The Gator Nation, a diverse community dedicated to excellence in education and research and shaping a better future for Florida, the nation and the world. Our mission is to enable our students to lead and influence the next generation and beyond for economic, cultural and societal benefit. UF is a graduate research institution with more than 50,000 students and membership in the prestigious Association of American Universities. Gainesville, which is consistently ranked as one of the nation's most livable cities, is located midway between the Gulf of Mexico and the Atlantic Ocean. Together, the University and the community comprise the educational, medical and cultural center of North Central Florida.
In addition to salary, the University of Florida (UF) offers low cost State Health plans, a number of Dental plans to fit you and your family's needs, and Vision. Domestic partner coverage through GatorCare is also available. Optional plans such as life, disability, legal and accident insurance are also available.

Job Description:
The University of Florida has pioneered the effort to integrate AI education in every major and every college. The College of Education seeks a tenure-track Assistant or Associate Professor in AI-based Quantitative Research Methods in Education. This faculty member will join the Research and Evaluation Methodology program (REM; https://education.ufl.edu/research-evaluation-methods), a productive and collegial community of scholars committed to high-quality teaching, research, and service. In addition, this faculty member will have the opportunity to collaborate with researchers in a variety of units centered around AI and technology-enhanced learning, such as the Institute for Advanced Learning Technologies (https://ialt.education.ufl.edu).
Successful applicants for the tenure-track Assistant or Associate Professor position are expected to develop and maintain a clear, systematic line of methodology-focused research; vigorously pursue external research funding; publish in top-tier methodological journals or proceedings; present research findings at meetings of professional associations; and contribute to advising and teaching graduate students. Additionally, candidates will engage in service to the program, school, college, university, and profession in general. The nine-month, tenure-accruing faculty appointment begins August 2027. Salary is negotiable, highly competitive, and commensurate with qualifications and experience.
Potential areas of expertise and scholarship may include:
AI-enhanced psychometrics, Computational Psychometrics, Digital-based assessment, and related areas
Causal machine learning for designing and analyzing experimental and quasi-experimental studies
Reinforcement Learning (RL) in educational research
Natural Language Processing (NLP)-based methods in educational assessment, measurement, and quantitative analysis
Issues of validity, reliability, and heterogeneous impacts in AI-enhanced quantitative methodology
Integration of machine learning and Bayesian or frequentist statistical approaches
Advancements to educational quantitative research methodology through AI
Responsibilities:
Conduct scholarly activities commensurate with expectations of a tenure-track assistant or associate faculty member at a research-intensive university
Build a collaborative and diverse community of scholars among colleagues within and outside of the college, especially within UF's AI research community
Vigorously pursue external funding opportunities with the support of the College's Office of Educational Research
Publish in top-tier refereed methodological journals or proceedings
Advise, engage, and mentor graduate students on research activities and theses and dissertations.
Design and teach advanced methodological courses (face-to-face, blended, and/or online) for graduate students and, potentially, undergraduate students
Provide service to the university and the profession
ABOUT THE COLLEGE: The College of Education at the University of Florida, founded in 1906, has consistently been ranked No. 1 and No. 2 in the nation in Online Graduate Education for the last nine years, No. 2 nationally for undergraduate education and 6th nationally among public and private education schools (U.S. News & World Report). Three of the College's academic programs occupy top-20 spots in the U.S. News rankings: Counselor Education (1st), Special Education (4th), and Elementary Education (14th). Cutting-edge interdisciplinary research and public scholarship—often conducted in partnership with other UF colleges, school districts and communities across the state and nation—are yielding powerful learning systems and models that are helping to transform education in today's changing world, starting with our youngest learners. Faculty researchers last year garnered more than $150.3 million in external awards supporting studies and projects addressing education's most critical issues. With both on campus and online options, the college offers 29 bachelor's and advanced degree programs and concentration areas, within nine academic specialties. To sustain the college's innovative edge, heightened emphasis on emerging technologies, student experience and interdisciplinary research will effectively prepare tomorrow's leaders in all education disciplines. The College's educator preparation programs have been continuously nationally accredited since 1954. Follow us: @UF_COE (X), @uf_coe (Instagram), @university-of-florida-college-of-education (LinkedIn), and @UF.COE (Facebook)

U.S. News & World Report ranks UF 7th among public universities. National rankings such as 1st by the Wall Street Journal and 4th by Forbes in their respective lists of Public Universities are a result of UF's commitment to provide the highest quality education at the best value. UF is home to 16 colleges and more than 200 research, service and education centers, bureaus and institutes, and boasts more than 6,600 faculty members, 60,000 students and 405,000 living alumni. Faculty scholars last year generated more than $1.26 billion in research awards. UF recently launched a $70 million AI partnership with NVIDIA, taking the first step toward ensuring equitable access to bringing AI to students and faculty from across campus and the state. The Florida Legislature designated UF as a “preeminent'' state university in 2013.
ABOUT THE AREA: UF is situated in Gainesville in North Central Florida, a vibrant college town that blends big-city cultural and athletic offerings with small-town friendliness and charm, along with excellent schools. Gainesville, located about halfway between the Atlantic Ocean and Gulf of Mexico, is often recognized as one of America's best college towns and is easily accessible to three major metropolitan areas (Jacksonville, Orlando and Tampa). The National Arbor Day Foundation has recognized Gainesville as a “Tree City USA” every year since 1982. USA Today ranked Gainesville as the number one place to move in the Sunshine State. Add the allure of Florida's famous sunshine, tropical breezes, and abundant wilderness, springs, rivers and seashores nearby, and it is little wonder that top-caliber faculty and students find our College and University to be the perfect balance of premier academics and a fulfilling lifestyle.

The successful candidate will play a key leadership role in advancing SPOHP's mission of teaching, training, research, and public engagement. The candidate will also contribute to the Department of History's vibrant intellectual community and commitment to innovative, student-centered teaching.
Drawing on expertise in oral history, public history, and United States history, the successful candidate will teach a 2-2 course load that includes courses in oral history methodology, public history, and areas of U.S. history that complement SPOHP's mission and support the curricular needs of the Department. jobs.description:

Job No: 541425
Work Type: Full Time
Location: Main Campus (Gainesville, FL)

Department: 18050000 - ED-STL SCHL-TEACH - LEARN
Job Description
Classification Title:
AST/ASO
Classification Minimum Requirements:
Candidates for Assistant Professor shall hold the highest degree appropriate to their field or possess equivalent qualifications based on professional experience. A candidate shall be expected to demonstrate successful experience pertinent to the position they are being recommended and have demonstrated qualities relevant to the goals of the academic unit in which they will be employed.
Candidates for Associate Professor shall hold the highest degree appropriate to their field or possess professional qualifications above those equivalent to the highest degree relevant to their field. They are expected to have produced creative work, professional writing, or research and successful teaching or professional experience. A candidate for this rank must have a distinguished record of achievement beyond the assistant professor level.
Job Description:
The College of Education at the University of Florida seeks a 9-month assistant or associate tenure-track faculty with expertise in artificial intelligence (AI) in education. This position will be part of the Educational Technology or Research and Evaluation Methodology academic program and UF's Institute for Advanced Learning Technologies.
The faculty member will join a dynamic community of scholars and engage in collaborative work with colleagues across UF and beyond, including but not limited to: the AI2 Center, the UF Artificial Intelligence and Informatics Research Institute, Computer & Information Science & Engineering, Digital Worlds Institute, UF Libraries, McKnight Brain Institute, Neuroscience, Psychology/Cognitive Sciences, Florida Museum of Natural History, Harn Museum of Art and UF Online.
Potential areas of expertise and scholarship include:
Generative AI in teaching and learning
AI and professional learning
AI and educational assessment
AI literacy for learning and instruction across formal and informal education contexts
AI for inclusive and accessible education
AI ethics and policy
Other innovative areas of inquiry related to AI and other emerging learning technologies
Responsibilities:
Conduct scholarly activities commensurate with expectations of tenure-track faculty at an AAU research-intensive university
Vigorously pursue external funding to enhance research and development
Publish in respected refereed scholarly journals salient to the candidate's line of research
Present research at national and international conferences
Advise, engage, and mentor graduate students in research and teaching activities
Teach courses (face-to-face, blended, and/or online)
Provide service to the program, school, college, university, and the profession
ABOUT THE COLLEGE: Founded in 1906, the College of Education at the University of Florida has a long history of mission-driven excellence, working to advance research, prepare the next generation of educators and solve society's most pressing challenges. The college is No. 2 in the nation among all Graduate Education Schools, according to U.S. News & World Report. In Online Graduate Education, the college has ranked No. 1 or No. 2 for the last 11 years. Among specialty rankings, both the Counseling (No. 2) and Special Education (No. 5) programs have maintained top-five designations for the past four years. In total, the college ranks top 20 in six program areas including Elementary Teacher Education (No. 12), Curriculum and Instruction (No. 17), Educational Administration (No. 19) and Higher Education (No. 19). Novel interdisciplinary research and public scholarship—in collaboration with other UF colleges, school districts, communities and education partners across the nation—are yielding powerful real-world results in teaching and learning. Last year, faculty researchers tallied more than $133.4 million in research expenditures supporting studies and projects addressing education's most challenging issues. To sustain the college's innovative edge and societal benefit, heightened emphasis on AI and emerging technologies, student experience and interdisciplinary research will effectively prepare tomorrow's leaders in all education disciplines. With both on-campus and online options, the college offers a variety of bachelor's and advanced degree programs and concentration areas within nine academic specialties. The college's educator preparation programs have been accredited by CAEP and NCATE since 1954. Follow us: @UF_COE (X), @uf_coe (Instagram), @university-of-florida-college-of-education (LinkedIn), and @UF.COE (Facebook)
ABOUT THE UNIVERSITY: The University of Florida, founded in 1853, is a public land-grant, sea-grant and space-grant research university and one of the most academically diverse universities in the nation. U.S. News & World Report ranks UF No. 7 among public universities. National rankings such as No. 1 for Online Bachelor's by U.S. News and No. 1 by the Wall Street Journal are a result of UF's commitment to provide the highest-quality education at the best value. UF is a Carnegie R1 institution, home to 16 colleges and more than 200 research, service and education centers, bureaus and institutes. The university boasts more than 6,100 faculty members, 63,000 students and 525,000 living alumni. Faculty scholars last year generated more than $1.25 billion in research awards. UF recently expanded its $70 million AI partnership with NVIDIA, adding an additional $24 million investment to make AI accessible to students and faculty across campus and the state. The Florida Legislature designated UF as a "preeminent'' state university in 2013.
ABOUT THE AREA: UF is situated in Gainesville, a vibrant college town in North Central Florida that blends big-city cultural and athletic offerings with small-town friendliness and charm, along with excellent schools. Gainesville, located about halfway between the Atlantic Ocean and Gulf of America, is recognized as one of the nation's best college towns and is easily accessible to three major metropolitan areas (Jacksonville, Orlando and Tampa). The National Arbor Day Foundation has recognized Gainesville as a "Tree City USA" every year since 1982. Livability ranked Gainesville as one of the Best Places to Live in the U.S. Add the allure of Florida's famous sunshine, tropical breezes, and abundant wilderness, springs, rivers and seashores nearby, and it is little wonder that top-caliber faculty and students find our university to be the perfect balance of premier academics and a fulfilling lifestyle.

Salary is commensurate with qualifications and experience.
Required Qualifications:
Doctorate in relevant academic discipline
Expertise in AI associated with education and one or more of the areas mentioned above
Record of scholarship as demonstrated through publications and presentations at national conferences (commensurate with experience)
Record of relevant teaching experience with diverse populations (commensurate with experience)
Technical skills related to area of expertise
Ability to positively contribute to the degree programs within the UF Ed Tech or the Research and Evaluation Methodology program and to the advancement of IALT

Ability to positively contribute to national visibility, reputation, and success of UF

Experience working in an interdisciplinary higher education environment

Evidence of outreach and dissemination of research via creative and non-traditional channels

Position description
The University of California, Berkeley invites applications for an approved faculty position at either the non-tenured (tenure-track) Assistant Professor level or the tenured Associate Professor level in the area of Electronic, Functional, and Quantum Materials. Rank will be determined based on qualifications and experience. This appointment will be a joint 50% Materials Science and Engineering / 50% Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences appointment.
The EECS Department has several related faculty positions open or opening soon. Please visit our EECS Faculty Positions webpage to view these listings. To be considered for multiple positions, please submit a separate application for each one.
About the Departments:
The MSE department is part of the College of Engineering (COE) and maintains close ties with Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (LBNL). It advances the understanding and design of materials through an interdisciplinary blend of chemistry, physics, and engineering, pairing rigorous fundamentals with modern, application-driven approaches. Our key strength is our collaborative, cross-disciplinary research community, with abundant opportunities for students and collaborators across campus and beyond.
The EECS department is part of the College of Engineering (COE) and the College of Computing, Data Science, and Society (CDSS). It offers one of the strongest research and instructional programs in this field anywhere in the world. Our key strength is our array of cross-disciplinary, team-driven projects. The integration of EE and CS forms the core, with strong interactions that extend into many other disciplines.
About the Position:
We seek applicants interested in the science and engineering of electronic and functional materials, from fundamental discovery through synthesis, characterization, and integration into device platforms. Areas of interest include, but are not limited to, wide-bandgap and ultrawide-bandgap semiconductors; materials for energy-efficient microelectronics and low-power AI hardware, including materials for neuromorphic and in-memory computing; ferroelectric, multiferroic, and magnetic materials for logic and memory; photonic and optoelectronic materials; quantum materials; and heterogeneous integration and advanced processing of emerging materials with established device platforms. All areas within Electronic, Functional, and Quantum Materials are of interest, and candidates across this breadth are encouraged to apply.
UC Berkeley values the family needs of faculty, including dual career couples, single parents, or those who may have taken time off for family reasons. For information about potential relocation to Berkeley, or career needs of accompanying partners and spouses, please visit the Office for Faculty Equity and Welfare's website.

The Department of Sociology and Criminology & Law at the University of Florida, College of Liberal Arts and Sciences invites applications for a full-time, nine-month, tenure-accruing position beginning August 16, 2027, at the rank of Assistant Professor with specialization in population health broadly defined. We seek scholars whose research examines the social, economic, political, environmental, and/or demographic factors that shape population health outcomes and health inequalities. We also offer minors in Sociology of Social Justice & Policy and Environmental Justice & Policy. Job Details
Position OverviewThe Department of Design at the University of Kansas is seeking a faculty member at the Assistant Teaching Professor level to work with undergraduate students in its newly established program in Animation.
We are looking for an enthusiastic and engaging design thinker and maker with a passion for visual storytelling, character animation, and the development and exploration of animation tools and techniques, who is interested in working closely with our faculty to build this new program. Candidates with experience in teaching, curriculum development, and robust professional practice will stand out. We also encourage recent master’s degree graduates eager to launch a career in animation education, or education and mentorship minded industry professional to apply.
Candidates must be able to demonstrate professional level skills in 2D or 3D animation practice with a focus on narrative and character animation, complemented by a strong historical familiarity with the medium, and a passion for educating students in these areas.
Candidates should also have a strong background in industry standard production tools and methods, and current professional practice standards.
Ideal candidates will demonstrate a proficiency in one or more of the following areas:
2D and/or 3D character animation – body mechanics, acting, dialogue, character animation workflow and tools.
Directing for animation – storyboarding, visual storytelling.
3D Skills – modeling, rigging, texturing, or lighting for animation and games.
Animation production and project management.
This position is subject to a collective bargaining agreement between The University of Kansas and United Academics, United Academics of KU, AAUP, or AFT. UAKU is the exclusive representative. As the State of Kansas is a right to work state, you have the right to be a member or not be a member of a union without fear of personal or professional repercussions.
About the Department of Design
The Department of Design, housed in Chalmers Hall, prepares animators, illustrators, experience designers, graphic designers, marketing creatives, motion designers, product designers, UX/UI developers, and other multidisciplinary communicators to thrive as innovative practitioners, and socially engaged leaders, in an ever-changing professional field. Design students have access to studio spaces, computer labs, a letterpress lab, a Riso lab, and digital fabrication labs. Students gain insights from lectures and workshops with world-renowned designers, collaborations with industry partners, and opportunities to participate in short-term study abroad programs and semester-long internships in the US and abroad.
Students earn a BFA in Design with programs in Animation, Illustration, Industrial Design, Visual Communication Design, and Interaction Design. The Bachelor of Fine Arts in Design is a four-year, 120-credit-hour degree program. All design students spend the first semester in general design foundation courses and in the second semester begin taking foundation courses in their chosen major.
KU’s excellence is a result of the rich tapestry of experiences, perspectives, and backgrounds of our faculty, staff, students, and colleagues from across our nation and the globe. At KU, we invest in continuous learning and growth by creating a climate where people engage in respectful dialogue and debate, and support each other’s success. We foster a culture of care where each person is seen, heard and valued. When people feel a true sense of belonging, we believe they are better able to reach their full potential and achieve remarkable things. This is a non-tenure position with up to a 3-year limited term contract, which has the possibility of renewal based upon a comprehensive evaluation.

Applications will continue to be accepted until this date.
Position description
The Berkeley School of Education invites applications for a tenure track position at the assistant professor level in the area of Civics Education, with a focus on civic learning and democratic engagement. We welcome applicants from education as well as a range of connected disciplinary and interdisciplinary spaces, including but not limited to political science, public policy, history, ethnic studies, and data science. The candidate should have research, publication, and teaching and/or mentoring experience in Civics Education with undergraduate and graduate students appropriate to rank. Preference will be given to scholars whose work centers K–12 classrooms and youth civic development.
The applicant's research focus should explore the teaching and learning of civics and advancing learning theory to address the challenges and possibilities of public democratic life. Across the United States and globally, young people express deep concern about polarization, misinformation, civic exclusion, and the fragility of democratic institutions. We seek a scholar whose research program explores Civics Education in ways that respond to these realities and who designs innovations that help educators meet the needs, interests, and aspirations of students. Given the increasing importance of digital citizenship, information literacy, and the civic implications of technology, we would expect the candidate to have some expertise in these areas.
About UC Berkeley School of Education
In the Berkeley School of Education, we educate like democracy depends on it– because it does. In a fast-changing, polarized world where inequalities and existential threats multiply, education remains an essential lynchpin for fostering human potential, achieving generational progress, and nurturing civic engagement. Together our research, teaching, and practice supports a vision of public education that has as its goal equity and inclusion at all levels - classroom, school, community, district, state, nation, and globe. Our students arrive with exceptional academic talent and professional experience, driven to make a meaningful impact as researchers, educators, leaders, and innovators. Together, faculty and students engage with pressing questions, from how children, youth, and adults learn across varied contexts, to how schools, communities, and societies can expand opportunities and advance educational equity. Through effective and equity-informed education, the BSE helps people and communities learn to dialogue across difference, use critical thinking to make informed decisions, and advance both individual achievement and progress for the benefit of society. As a world leader in public education, guided by a commitment to excellence in scholarship, teaching, innovation, and leadership, our professional and academic programs help prepare the next generation of educators, leaders, scholars, and policymakers, while contributing to transformative knowledge creation and the public good.
