jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Biology (Anatomy and Physiology)
jobs.description:
Salary Range $60,000 - $70,000
Assistant Professor of Biology (Anatomy and Physiology)
The Department of Biological Sciences at Randolph College seeks applicants for a tenure-track assistant professor in anatomy and/or physiology to begin in August of 2027. The position requires experience in and commitment to teaching, research, and service in a small-liberal arts setting. The position is an academic (9-month) tenure-track appointment with a teaching load of six courses per year. The successful candidate will teach courses in Anatomy & Physiology, introductory biology, biology senior program, and develop new courses in the candidate’s area of expertise to complement existing course offerings.
We welcome applicants from a variety of subfield backgrounds related to vertebrate anatomy and physiology but would be especially enthusiastic about candidates with teaching and research experience in embryology/developmental biology, animal physiology, animal nutrition, and/or mammalogy.
The successful candidate will be expected to develop an active and independent research program focusing on any level of biological organization in animal physiology, commensurate with the needs and resources of the department. Service to the department and the institution, including undergraduate academic advising and committee work, is also required.
Review of applicants will begin on November 2, 2026, and continue until the position is filled. Candidates chosen to be interviewed will be contacted by email.
More information about the Department of Biological Sciences at Randolph College can be found here: https://www.randolphcollege.edu/biology/
Primary responsibilities
Teach six courses per academic year, including Anatomy and Physiology. Additional courses may include Introductory Biology, Senior Program, and lectures and/or laboratory courses in the candidate’s area of expertise. Typical teaching load is 3 courses per semester in our innovative Take2 curricular model where courses are offered in two 7-week sessions each semester. Maintain regular weekly office hours to provide academic support and guidance to students enrolled in assigned courses. Serve as an academic advisor to assigned undergraduate students (majors and non-majors). Develop and maintain an active research program that includes undergraduate students and is commensurate with the needs and resources of the department. Randolph College has established undergraduate research funding such as the Randolph Innovative Student Experience (RISE) grant, the Randolph Summer Research Program (SRP) to support summer student research, and the annual Randolph Symposium of Artists and Scholars. There are also funds available to support faculty and student travel to conferences. Start-up funds are available for this position. Serve on college-wide committees focused on faculty governance, curricular development, and enhancing campus-wide excellence. Participate in faculty meetings focused on departmental operations and planning, faculty development, pedagogical strategies, and student support initiatives.
Required qualifications for tenure-track assistant professor
A Ph.D. in biology, physiology, cell biology, or a closely related field by August 2027. Demonstrated or evidence of potential excellence in undergraduate instruction (in-person). A commitment to inclusive learning, active teaching strategies, and student-centered pedagogy, as demonstrated by experience, expertise, and/or formal training. Evidence of active research and scholarship. A commitment to inclusive undergraduate teaching in a liberal arts setting and a willingness to engage with institutional student success initiatives. Must be available and willing to teach in-person, on-campus courses held in a 7-week format.
Preferred education and experience
Teaching experience at the undergraduate level, including Human Anatomy and Physiology lecture and laboratory. Research experience that includes mentoring undergraduate students from diverse backgrounds. Experience creating a student-centered learning environment, including evidence of teaching effectiveness and/or training in pedagogical strategies. Record of publication in peer-reviewed journals, including first-authored papers. Record of acquiring extramural research funds to support the candidate's research.
How to apply
To apply, please send the following materials to: biologysearch@randolphcollege.edu
a cover letter addressing all position responsibilities and qualifications, including familiarity with the small liberal arts collect environment; a current curriculum vitae; a statement of teaching philosophy that includes evidence of teaching effectiveness, describes experience creating and maintaining an inclusive learning environment, and addresses ability to teach content areas in the accelerated TAKE2 learning format. an unofficial graduate transcript (official transcript required for employment); and names and contact information of three professional references (only references of finalists will be contacted).
Only complete applications submitted electronically will be considered. Finalists will be required to submit to a background investigation and provide official graduate transcripts.
Review of applicants will begin on November 6, 2026 and continue until the position is filled. Candidates chosen to be interviewed will be contacted by email. Questions about this position may be directed to Dr. Amanda Rumore (arumore@randolphcollege.edu).
Affirmative Action/EEO statement
Randolph College is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate or allow discrimination on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, sex (including pregnancy), gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, veteran status, political beliefs, or any other classification protected by applicable law. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including but not limited to hiring, promotion, termination, placement, transfer, layoff, recall, compensation, and training.
About the Department of Biological Sciences at Randolph College
Our department focuses on integrative biology and emphasizes evolution across our curriculum. The department consists of six faculty and a full-time laboratory technician. Members of the department have access to teaching and research lab space in the newly-renovated Martin Science Building, the Randolph College Natural History and Archaeology Collections, and multiple college-owned nature preserves. More information about our department can be found here: http://www.randolphcollege.edu/biology/
About Randolph College
Randolph College, founded in 1891 as Randolph-Macon Woman’s College, is a traditional small liberal arts college with a longstanding reputation for excellence in teaching and an appreciation for and commitment to inclusivity. In the College’s unique TAKE2 curricular model, students take two courses in seven-week sessions with two sessions per semester. The result is a curriculum that provides time for students to focus on two courses, while balancing other important aspects of the college experience: internships, extracurricular activities, athletics, and jobs. More information about Randolph College can be found here: http://www.randolphcollege.edu/
About Lynchburg, VA
Lynchburg, VA is located near the geographic center of Virginia, at the edge of the Blue Ridge Mountains. Its expanding population supports a vibrant downtown, and offers a variety of cultural, educational, and recreational opportunities, making it an attractive destination for both residents and visitors. The city boasts ample outdoor activities such as hiking, swimming, boating, skiing, and access to a municipal park system with urban trails, playgrounds, and swimming pools. Lynchburg is also known for its strong educational presence, housing five colleges and universities. The city's arts and theater scene is lively, complemented by museums and a minor league baseball team. Lynchburg is a city with a growing number of employers and businesses, but a low cost of living compared to the nearby cities of Charlottesville and Roanoke. Located approximately 180 miles from Washington, D.C., Lynchburg is accessible via an Amtrak station and regional airport.

jobs.title: Assistant Director for Human Resources and Faculty Affairs
jobs.description:
Job Details
This position has been deemed critical by the Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability Dean’s Office and is exempt from the hiring pause.
This position is based on Stanford’s main campus with consideration given to the option for a hybrid work schedule (partially onsite 3 or more days a week), subject to operational need. Interested candidates must include a resume and cover letter to be considered for this position.
Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa.
About Us
The Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability (SDSS) strives to create a future when humans and nature thrive in concert and in perpetuity. The school is made up of a three-part structure to drive global impact: Our academic departments and programs educate students and create new knowledge across areas of research that are crucial for advancing the long-term prosperity of the planet and people; Institutes bridge scholarship at Stanford and beyond, bringing multiple viewpoints to bear on urgent challenges; The Sustainability Accelerator drives new policy and technology solutions through a worldwide network of partners who work with our teams to develop solutions at a global scale. The school is dedicated to creating and supporting a community with the richness of experience and background needed to create solutions that benefit all people, particularly those most affected by environmental damage and climate change.
For more information on the school, click here.
The Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability (Dean’s Office) has a unique job opportunity for a senior human resources professional who is looking for a challenging position supporting academic, non-academic staff, and faculty in the school. This position will be part of a small team, reporting to the Director for Human Resources and Faculty Affairs and be responsible for Human Resources (HR), and Faculty Affairs (FA) functions for assigned client groups. Since most FA issues tie closely to HR issues, we are confident that an experienced HR professional will be able to easily transfer their knowledge to FA work.
Your responsibilities include:
Collaborate closely with leadership, managers and employees to provide expert advice, counsel and management on all aspects of the HR/FA functions including but not limited to organizational development and change management, employee relations; classification and compensation; recruitment and retention; performance management and staff development.
Collaborate closely with school leadership, department managers and others in the management of the faculty search, appointment and promotion process. Oversee appointment processes for visiting and consulting faculty, academic staff-teaching and visiting scholars; ensure accuracy and compliance with school and university policies and guidelines.
Lead the implementation of HR/FA processes and strategize solutions on HR/FA issues for an assigned client group. Provide expert HR/FA consultation and guidance to managers, faculty, and senior leaders.
Review and approve employment transactions and academic appointments, ensuring alignment with university and school policies and guidelines. serve as the primary point of contact for reviewing materials for faculty, academic staff, visiting and adjunct faculty, and other teaching titles.
Provide administrative and operational support and guidance for faculty employment activities, including searches, appointments, reappointments, promotions, sabbaticals, leaves, retirements, and recalls.
Support senior leadership in local and university-wide initiatives, including the development and implementation of communication strategies.
In addition to the minimum qualifications listed below, our preferred qualifications include:
Knowledge of faculty affairs process at Stanford is highly desired but a willingness to learn them is critical. Most FA issues tie closely to HR issues and while the population is different, the judgment, rationale and processes involved are analogous. Therefore, a strong HR professional should be able to easily transfer those skills to faculty affairs.
Demonstrated ability to exercise sound judgment, discretion, and diplomacy when handling highly sensitive and confidential employee and faculty matters.
Requires excellent problem-solving, organization, prioritization, and follow-through to successfully manage workload that is subject to conflicts, competing priorities, and constant interruptions.
10 or more years of progressive HR experience, particularly in higher education or large organizations.
Proven experience in coaching, training, educating, and influencing managers and senior leadership.
Experience working in an academic environment and/or with faculty appointment and promotion processes.
The expected pay range for this position is $160,000 to $190,000 per annum.
Responsibilities
Core Duties:
Lead strategic planning and analysis for complex functions or programs with significant business, regulatory and/or technical challenges requiring subject matter expertise. May provide development of program or function from initial concept to implementation.
Manage the administration and evaluation of programs or functions. Oversee the interpretation, implementation and compliance with policies and regulations. Recommend actions and/or resolve complex issues that often span organizational boundaries.
Represent the program or function at the university level and/or to external/internal stakeholders and constituencies.
Develop and manage outreach strategy that includes relationship development, communications, and compliance.
Oversee or supervise staff in the development and implementation of programs or functions.
May develop and/or oversee budgets; manage finances including monitoring, analyzing, forecasting, and reporting.
Minimum Education and Experience
Bachelor’s degree and eight years of relevant experience, or combination of education and relevant experience.
Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:
Demonstrated leadership skills and ability to influence and motivate constituencies which could span multiple organizational boundaries.
Demonstrated excellent planning, organizational and analytical skills.
Demonstrated ability to make sound business decisions using good business judgment and innovative and creative problem-solving.
Demonstrated ability to manage financial, organizational and staff resources.
Excellent interpersonal and communications skills with the ability to cultivate professional and business partnerships.
Relevant subject matter expertise.

jobs.title: Faculty Appointment in International Security
jobs.description:
Job Details
Stanford University seeks an expert in international security affairs to be appointed as Senior Fellow in the Freeman Spogli Institute for International Studies at the Center for International Security and Cooperation (CISAC). Faculty from the social sciences are particularly encouraged to apply.
Senior Fellows at Stanford University are full members of the Academic Council, with a rank equivalent to tenured associate or full professor.
The successful candidate for this position will be an internationally recognized scholar with an interest and expertise in contemporary threats and challenges in the domain of international security affairs. They may well have other significant interests and expertise as well that would add to Stanford’s faculty community working on a variety of security issues. In addition, they may also have a record of policy relevant publication, teaching, or public service.
Applicants should possess an exceptional record of research and publication and be committed to teaching at the undergraduate and graduate levels and training pre- and post-doctoral fellows at CISAC to become the next generation of scholars on international security policy. Applicants might also have substantial interest or proven expertise in making, advising or implementing national or international security policy. The successful candidates will be expected to provide leadership for the study of international security issues at Stanford University.
Application packages should be submitted online and include the following documents: 1) a curriculum vitae with complete bibliography; 2) a research statement (up to 2 pages); 3) a statement of teaching interests (1 page); 4) up to three examples of scholarly publications; and 5) a cover letter.
Review of application files will start from October 19, 2026. Questions regarding this application may be directed to Patrick Laboon.
Stanford is an equal employment opportunity and affirmative action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Stanford welcomes applications from all who would bring additional dimensions to the University’s research, teaching and clinical missions.
Consistent with its obligations under the law, the University will provide reasonable accommodations to applicants and employees with disabilities. Applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation for any part of the application or hiring process should contact disability.access@stanford.edu.
The expected base pay range for this position is:
Senior Fellow: $186,000 - $285,000

jobs.title: Assistant Professor Of Physics
jobs.description:
Job Details
LEHIGH UNIVERSITY. The Department of Physics invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor with a specialization in Extragalactic Astrophysics, broadly defined, with an anticipated start date of July 1, 2027. We welcome candidates using observational, theoretical, computational, and/or data-intensive approaches.
Candidates must have earned a Ph.D. in Astrophysics or a closely related field by the date of employment. The candidate must also demonstrate a record of publishing in top journals and experience teaching or mentoring in a university setting.
The successful candidate will be expected to teach courses in astronomy and physics at the undergraduate and graduate levels, engage in scholarly activities, and participate in departmental, college, and university service. We are seeking candidates whose research will complement existing faculty expertise in observational stellar astrophysics, theoretical cosmology and string theory, and high energy physics. The successful candidate will demonstrate strong potential to develop a vibrant, externally-supported research program and a commitment to mentoring within our community of culturally diverse students.
The Department of Physics has established research programs in condensed matter physics, photonics, soft materials and biophysics, statistical physics, nuclear and particle physics, string theory, astrophysics, and atomic and molecular physics. The department offers a B.S. in Astrophysics and a B.A. in Astronomy, as well as M.S. and Ph.D. programs in Physics, providing opportunities to mentor undergraduate and graduate researchers and to teach and develop advanced courses in astronomy and astrophysics. Faculty have access to university high-performance computing and research-computing support, together with opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration through Lehigh’s Physics and Data Science programs and the Institute for Data, Intelligent Systems, and Computation. Lehigh also provides proposal-development and sponsored-program support, including services for early-career faculty, as well as competitive internal seed funding for new and collaborative research.
Founded in 1865, Lehigh University has combined outstanding academic and learning opportunities with leadership in fostering innovative research. Recognized among the nation's highly ranked research universities, Lehigh offers a rigorous academic community for over 7,500 students. Lehigh University has some 5,800 undergraduates, 1,800 graduate students, and nearly 600 full-time faculty members. Lehigh University is located in Bethlehem, PA, a vibrant and historic area. Over 840,000 people live in the Lehigh Valley, which is in close proximity to New York City and Philadelphia.
Review of applications will begin on December 1, 2026 and will continue until the position is filled. For full consideration, applications should be received by December 1, 2026. Applicants should submit their materials at https://apply.interfolio.com/193844. Candidates should submit the following materials:
Cover letter
Curriculum vitae
Research statement that describes past scholarly contributions and future research directions
Teaching statement that describes instructional philosophy and courses that the candidate would want to teach or develop
A statement on Contributions to Lehigh’s Principles of Our Equitable Community that describes how your experiences, knowledge, and skills prepare you to effectively contribute to a learning and research community that holds these principles at its core (the Lehigh ADVANCE Center’s guide for understanding and preparing such statements is available here)
Names and affiliations of three references (letters will be requested later in the process)
Any inquiries regarding this search should be directed to Prof. M. Virginia McSwain, Chair of the search committee, at mcswain@lehigh.edu.
Lehigh University is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital or familial status, national origin (including shared ancestry), pregnancy or related conditions, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, or veteran status. Lehigh University is committed to a culturally and intellectually diverse academic community and is especially interested in candidates who can contribute, through their research, teaching and/or service, to this mission. Lehigh University provides competitive salaries and comprehensive benefits, including domestic partner benefits, and supports faculty members’ work/life balance.

jobs.title: Associate or Full Professor in Scoring for the Screen
jobs.description:
Job Details
Associate or Full Professor
(Tenured)
Department of Radio/Television/Film & The Bienen School of Music
The Department of Radio/Television/Film explores the history, theory, and production of media—from cinema to television to sound design to interactive media and emerging technologies. We value originality, critical analysis, creativity, and vision in both scholarly research and creative work. Our programs, courses, and research opportunities focus on the history of film, television, sound, and interactive media as well as the critical analysis of media texts, technologies, and cultures. Our faculty explore the social and cultural impact of media—and use media to convey their own messages to the world. All are dedicated to integrating the theory and the practice of media, participating in interdisciplinary dialogue, and fostering a spirit of creativity and collaboration. This prepares students who are eager to pursue careers in the media industries as writers, directors, producers, and managers who inspire, persuade, and educate their audiences.
The Department, in joint effort with the Bienen School of Music, aims to build a new focus on musicians in the film and television industry. The schools seek to hire an accomplished creative at the rank of Associate or Full Professor with expertise in scoring for the screen. Radio/Television/Film has launched a new curricular track in “Composing for the Screen” and holds the state-of-the-art Hobson-Lucas Recording Studio designed to support recording processes. MFA students in the department’s Documentary Media and Writing for the Screen and Stage MFA programs often collaborate with student musicians in the Bienen School of Music for their films. This senior faculty member would address this collaborative student demand across programs and facilitate exciting initiatives, such as: an ongoing series of cross-school film screenings with live music; a program pairing student filmmakers with student composers; shared events featuring top composers for film, TV, and videogames; industry outreach and professional development for musicians, composers, and sound artists.
This position is 100% in person and located on Northwestern University’s Evanston campus in the greater Chicago area.
Employment term: This is a full-time continuing senior faculty appointment, service of 9 months paid over 12. The hire would be subject to Northwestern’s tenure approval process.
Salary Range: The salary range is $140,000-$160,000, competitive based upon experience.
Preferred Start: September 1, 2027.
Closing Date: October 16, 2026. Review of applications will begin on October 19, 2026.
Primary Responsibilities:
Research and creative work in the area of scoring for the screen Undergraduate and graduate student instruction Supervision of student thesis projects Service to the department, school, university, and profession
Minimum Qualifications:
Terminal degree appropriate to the field, i.e. MFA in film and media production, music composition, or similar credentials, and/or equivalent industry experience
Application Documents:
Applications will be accepted via Northwestern Careers. For full consideration, please be sure to include the following materials in your application:
• Cover letter describing relevant interests, preparation, and experience; candidates should specifically address how previous experiences relate to qualifications for the role and how they see themselves contributing to both the School of Communication and the Bienen School of Music
• Statement on teaching philosophy and creative practice
• Current CV, including links to creative works
• Three (3) contacts for letters of recommendation, of which at least one should address teaching qualifications
Forward questions regarding the position to search chair, Professor Jacob Smith (jacobsmith@northwestern.edu.). For more information about the Department, please visit the department’s website.
The Schools:
The School of Communication has five departments and offers a suite of interdisciplinary undergraduate, professional, and graduate programs. The departments span the communication arts and sciences including the Department of Radio-Television-Film, the Roxelyn and Richard Pepper Department of Communication Sciences and Disorders, the Department of Communication Studies, the Department of Performance Studies, and the Department of Theatre (which includes music theatre and dance). The school offers instruction to roughly 900 undergraduate majors and 650 graduate and professional students. Founded nearly 150 years ago, the School has been a leader in developing the communication disciplines and professions, and continues to be a center of excellence in the communication arts and sciences. Our current Dean is E. Patrick Johnson.
Northwestern University’s Henry and Leigh Bienen School of Music ranks as one of the nation’s leading music institutions. For more than a century, the Bienen School has offered a unique combination of conservatory-level musical training with the academic rigor of a top-tier research institution. Through exceptional training and dedicated, collaborative teaching, Bienen faculty prepare students to excel in the ever-changing music world and forge new paths in both the performance and academic arenas.
The University:
Northwestern University is one of the nation’s largest private research universities. Located on the shore of Lake Michigan, the main campus is in Evanston and the medical campus is 12 miles south in downtown Chicago. There is continuing expansion of University facilities and programs, particularly in the sciences and medicine. Diverse cultural, social, and recreational activities abound on and near each campus. We are committed to supporting a strong campus community.
Benefits:
At Northwestern, we are proud to provide meaningful and competitive benefits. The available benefits package for this position will include health, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance; paid medical/sick and parental leave; tuition benefits for the employee and dependents; pre-tax and flex spending accounts for commuting and dependent care; generous retirement savings options; and wellness programs. For a comprehensive overview of available benefits, including eligibility details, visit us at https://www.northwestern.edu/hr/benefits/index.html to learn more.
Northwestern University has provided a pay range representing its good faith estimate of what the university reasonably expects to pay for the position. The pay offered to the selected candidate will be determined based on factors including (but not limited to) the experience and qualifications of the selected candidate including years since terminal degree, training, and field or discipline; departmental budget availability; internal comparators; and external market pay for comparable jobs.

jobs.description:
Assistant/Associate Professor in National Defense & Security - Engineering
Purdue Engineering invites applications for tenure/tenure-track positions at Assistant or Associate ranks in all engineering disciplines. Purdue University seeks to attract multiple exceptional candidates with interests and expertise related to relevant Defense and security related fields, including but not limited to directed energy, hypersonics, integrated sensing, electronic warfare, energetic materials, propulsion, space technology, microelectronics, cybersecurity, biotechnology, quantum science, future generation wireless technology, advanced materials, trusted AI and autonomy, integrated network systems-of-systems, human-machine interfaces, supply-chain logistics, and manufacturing. Successful candidates will be expected to collaborate across disciplines in the defense or security area. US citizenship is not required to apply for this position; however, many of the externally funded national defense-related research opportunities require US citizenship.
Successful candidates must hold a Ph.D. degree in Aeronautics and Astronautics, Electrical and Computer Engineering, Materials Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a closely related discipline by the employment start date. Early-career applicants must show evidence of initiating independent research, while mid-career applicants should demonstrate a sustained record of independent research within academic or industrial organizations, and contributions to education and/or mentoring. Successful candidates will conduct original research, advise graduate students, teach undergraduate and graduate level courses, be active in professional organizations, and perform service at the School/Department, College, and University levels. While the focus in this search is on candidates with potential tenure homes appointments in the Schools of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Electrical and Computer Engineering, Materials Engineering, Chemical Engineering, and Mechanical Engineering, applicants interested in other Purdue engineering schools are welcome to apply.
Purdue Engineering is renowned for top-notch faculty and students, unique research facilities and innovations, and a culture of collegiality and persistent pursuit of preeminence. As one of the top ranked and largest engineering colleges in the nation, we are the first among U.S. engineering colleges in annual graduates and market demand, and have 9 degree programs ranked in the top 10 nationally. Purdue Engineering furthermore continues to be a top-ranked college for patents and translation of our research activities to practice in the state, nation, and world. More than 70 Purdue Engineering faculty and alumni are National Academy of Engineering members, and we look to continue bringing outstanding faculty to campus, and remaining the leader in affordable excellence at scale by guiding strategic growth through investment in people, exciting initiatives, and remarkable facilities.
To apply, please submit application to this site https://careers.purdue.edu/job/AssistantAssociate-Professor-in-National-Defense-&-Security-Engineering/44145-en_US/ including (1) cover letter, (2) a complete curriculum vitae, (3) teaching plan (2 pages), (4) research plan (2 pages), and (5) names and contact information for at least 5 references. The search committee may contact references to request letters. For information/questions regarding applications contact the Office of Academic Affairs, College of Engineering, at coeacademicaffairs@purdue.edu. Review of applications will begin on October 24, 2026 and will continue until the position is filled. A background check is required for employment in this position.
Purdue and the College of Engineering have a Concierge Program that provides dual career assistance and relocation services.
Purdue University is an equal opportunity/equal access university.

Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in economics and finance, such as microeconomics, macroeconomics, economics of financial literacy, corporate finance, financial markets and institutions (money and banking), and courses in our certified financial planner program.
Maintain an active program of scholarly research resulting in peer-reviewed publications, conference presentations, and other professional contributions.
Participate in departmental, college, and university committees and service activities.

After receiving feedback on formative reviews in the second, third, and fourth years of employment, a case for tenure and promotion is submitted in the fall of the sixth year.
Tenure track faculty are eligible for sabbatical following six complete academic years of full-time service and every seven years thereafter. Additional professional development opportunities include the possibility of start-up funds and the potential for junior faculty leave. The Thorpe Center for Curricular and Faculty Development supports faculty in their teaching and scholarly work including peer-to-peer mentoring, workshops, internal grants, and assistance with instructional design and technology.
About IWU: Founded in 1850, Illinois Wesleyan University is a nationally ranked, small, private undergraduate liberal arts university with highly selective admission criteria and a tradition of teaching excellence emphasizing the integration of the liberal arts and professional education. We are located in Bloomington, IL, a metro area of 190,000 people, which is about a two or three hour drive from Chicago, St. Louis, and Indianapolis. We offer BBA and MBA degrees in eight active concentrations as well as an Executive MBA for working professionals. New Mexico represents a wide range of perspectives with a rich cultural heritage. The MIDS Department faculty supports existing BBA and MBA programs, including concentrations in MIS, and an MS in Cybersecurity and Business Analytics. Teaching responsibilities for this position include undergraduate and graduate courses in Management Information Systems (preferably in Cybersecurity).
The Marketing, Information Systems, and Decision Sciences group is a small, cohesive group seeking colleagues who demonstrate a willingness to make a commitment to maintaining and building a strong MIS area within the Ellis School of Business Leadership.

Evidence of or promise of a significant program of research and scholarship in cybersecurity and/or Management Information Systems Evidence of excellence or promise of achieving excellence in teaching MIS core and elective courses at the undergraduate and graduate levels, with emphasis on cybersecurity. Description
The San Diego State University Civil, Construction and Environmental Engineering (CCEE) seeks to hire a tenure-track assistant professor with expertise in construction planning, execution and management of resilient infrastructure.
This position targets individuals who understand how large-scale infrastructure projects—such as highways, bridges, airports, mass transit, and utility networks—are planned, built, delivered, and maintained. The successful candidate will advance research and teaching in heavy civil construction operations and methods, constructability, project delivery methods, risk management of infrastructure projects, and related areas.
Infrastructure resilience: Climate adaptation, disaster recovery, resilient supply chains, risk-based infrastructure planning.
Infrastructure Constructability: Emphasis on the design-construction interface for improved constructability (project safety, risk, cost, schedule, etc.)
Construction Operations & Methods: innovative construction methods for infrastructure construction.
Project Delivery & Heavy Civil Management: Project delivery system to support infrastructure project objectives (Design-Build, Integrated Project Delivery (IPD), Public-Private Partnerships (P3), infrastructure asset management)
Risk management of infrastructure projects
Resilient Construction Execution: Field-level adaptation strategies for building in extreme environments, constructing under active climate threats, and scheduling around severe weather disruptions.
Workforce & Safety Systems: safety management systems, heavy-equipment and operational safety, and workforce training for heavy civil construction.
Apply via PageUp by December 7, 2026.
The CCEE department offers four undergraduate majors: Civil Engineering, Construction Engineering, Environmental Engineering, and Construction Management. Campus: St. George (Downtown Toronto)

POSITION DESCRIPTION
The Department of Mechanical & Industrial Engineering in the Faculty of Applied Science & Engineering at the University of Toronto invites applications for a full-time tenure stream position in Operations Research. The appointment will be at the rank of Associate Professor or Professor, with an anticipated start date of July 1, 2027.
Areas of interest include, but are not limited to, continuous and/or discrete optimization, online algorithms and sequential decision-making, (algorithmic) game theory, mechanism and market design, decision-focused learning, and other emerging and related areas at the intersection of Operations Research and Artificial Intelligence.
REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS
Candidates must have earned a PhD degree in Operations Research, Industrial Engineering, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, or related areas, with a clearly demonstrated record of excellence in research and teaching. We seek candidates whose research and teaching interests complement and enhance our existing departmental strengths. Ideally, candidates should also demonstrate an awareness of modern machine learning and AI in their research.
Candidates must provide evidence of research excellence which can be demonstrated by a record of sustained high-impact contributions and publications in top-ranked and field relevant journals, the submitted research statement, presentations at significant conferences, awards and accolades, and other noteworthy activities that contribute to the visibility and prominence of the discipline, as well as strong endorsements from referees.
Evidence of excellence in teaching will be provided through teaching accomplishments, the teaching dossier submitted as part of the application (with required materials outlined below), as well as strong letters of reference.
RESPONSIBILITIES
Candidates will have an established international reputation and will be expected to sustain and lead innovative and independent research, and to maintain an outstanding, competitive, and externally funded research program.
In addition, the successful candidate will be assigned a teaching and service load.
HIRING SALARY RANGE
The rank and salary will be commensurate with qualifications and experience. The upper end of the salary range for this position exceeds $200,000 CAD per annum. Negotiations beyond this salary range will be considered for exceptionally qualified candidates.
ABOUT US
Established in 1827, and located in vibrant downtown Toronto, the University of Toronto is Canada's largest university, recognized as a global leader in research and teaching. U of T's distinguished faculty, institutional record of groundbreaking scholarship and wealth of innovative academic opportunities attract outstanding students and academics from around the world. The Department of Mechanical & Industrial Engineering at the University of Toronto is home to the top mechanical and industrial engineering programs in Canada. a teaching dossier which includes a teaching statement, sample course materials, and teaching evaluations; and

jobs.description:
Job Details
Assistant, Faculty Development & Support
Date Posted: 09/29/2026
Req ID:50344
Faculty/Division: Faculty of Arts & Science
Department: Academic Human Resources
Campus: St. George (Downtown Toronto)
Existing Vacancy: Yes
Description:
The Faculty of Arts & Science is the heart of Canada’s leading university and one of the most comprehensive and diverse academic divisions in the world. The strength of Arts & Science derives from our combined teaching and research excellence in the humanities, sciences and social sciences across 29 departments, seven colleges and 46 interdisciplinary centres, institutes and programs.
We can only realize our mission with the dedication and excellence of engaged staff and faculty. The diversity of opportunities and perspectives within the Faculty reflect the local and global landscape and the need for curiosity, innovative thinking and collaboration. At Arts & Science, we take pride in our legacy of innovation and discovery that has changed the way we think about the world.
The University of Toronto is committed to recruiting and retaining outstanding faculty and academic staff. The Academic Human Resources Office provides support and expertise to academic units on the interpretation and application of policies and procedures governing academic appointments. The development of faculty and academic leadership contributes to the Academic Human Resources Offices’ efforts to recruit and retain excellent faculty and academic administrators by promoting a positive and highly collegial working environment, supporting faculty as they transition through career stages, and by guiding faculty in navigating the complexities of a large, decentralized university.
The Academic Human Resources Office supports academic administrators and their staff on the full spectrum of Academic HR matters, including recruitment, appointments, tenure, continuing status, promotion, leaves, workload, PTR and retirement. This office also supports academic units in respect of academic unionized employee groups including Teaching Assistants and Course Instructors (CUPE 3902, Unit 1), Sessional Lecturers and Writing Instructors (CUPE 3902, Unit 3) and Postdoctoral Fellows (CUPE 3902, Unit 5). The Academic Human Resources Office's Faculty Development and Support team works closely with the Vice-Dean, Faculty & Academic Life to implement a range of programming that supports faculty engagement, professional development, and system navigation.
Your opportunity:
Reporting to the Coordinator, Faculty Development the incumbent is responsible for performing timely day-to-day administrative activities that assist in the smooth and efficient operation of the Faculty Development and Support team and the Academic Human Resources Office. The incumbent works in a complex environment that requires a high degree of sensitivity, responsiveness, independent judgment, and a need to maintain absolute confidentiality regarding sensitive issues. The Assistant, Faculty Development and Support will make all administrative arrangements, and provide support, for all faculty development programming and events, including mental health workshops and training; assist with the documentation, collection and coordination of data; assist with confidential HR filing systems and records; screen visitors; monitor and respond to email; order supplies and process invoices. The incumbent provides a broad range of timely project, programming, communication and administrative support to the Faculty Development and Support team and the Academic Human Resources team in general. They are required to use initiative and exercise sound judgment in facilitating referrals and/or directing mental health training participants to appropriate resources and supports.
General Responsibilities:
Programming and day-of event support for Faculty Development team, including booking venue, registration, liaising with participants, event set up, preparing materials, order catering, and IT support.
First point of contact for screening visitors and referring appropriately.
Responding to enquiries within the defined scope of the role and redirecting as appropriate.
Responsible for office administration including monitoring the general inbox, responding to incoming email and processing invoices.
Organizing and maintaining complex electronic files.
Maintaining the SharePoint site.
Entering data and pulling reports from HRIS.
Collating and organizing data for ad hoc requests.
Drafting internal and external communications.
Updating website.
Proofreading and fact-checking content.
Essential Qualifications:
Education: University degree and courses leading to completion of CHRP or an acceptable equivalent of education and experience.
Experience: Two years' relevant office administration experience. Experience coordinating and planning complex event logistics. Knowledge of mental health and related health promotion concepts and practices. Experience providing support to a team including dealing with frequent interruptions and multi-tasking work priorities. Experience organizing and maintaining files. Demonstrated experience dealing with a diverse client group.
Skills: Advanced computer skills including proficiency with Microsoft 365 products (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint, Forms, Teams) ); PDF creation software (Adobe Acrobat Professional). Strong organizational and interpersonal skills; strong administrative skills; and excellent web administration skills.
Other: Familiarity with human resources protocols and practices; ability to communicate effective both orally and in writing; ability to take initiative and work independently; strong attention to detail and strong organizational skills; tact, care and discretion in dealing with difficult or sensitive situations; ability to set own work priorities based on an understanding of the priorities of the office. Works cooperatively with others as part of a team. Must be able to maintain confidentiality. Strong understanding and interest in faculty development and mental health.
Assets: Completion of Applied Suicide Intervention Skills Training (ASIST) training; familiarity with human resources protocols and practices; experience working with HRIS software. Project management experience. Experience with Microsoft Power Platform.
Internal applicants may request for a job description at adminhr.artsci@utoronto.ca

Job Details
Assistant/ Associate/ Professor - Hematological Pathologist
Date Posted: 09/30/2026
Closing Date: 11/04/2026, 11:59PM ET Open until Filled
Req ID: 50386
Job Category: Faculty - Clinical
Faculty/Division: Faculty of Medicine

Description:
The Department of Laboratory Medicine and Pathobiology, Temerty Faculty of Medicine at the University of Toronto and the Laboratory Medicine Program at the University Health Network (UHN) are seeking to recruit a Hematological Pathologist at the rank of Assistant, Associate or Full Professor. The candidate is expected to have diagnostic and research training/expertise in Hematopathology and Laboratory Hematology. The expected start date is March 1, 2027 or mutually agreed upon.
We are seeking an academic hematopathologist who will foster excellence in hematopathology and laboratory hematology clinical practice, teaching and research at the hospital. The successful candidate must be an experienced academic hematopathologist with established track record and will join a large academic laboratory faculty with diverse diagnostic expertise, teaching responsibilities, basic and clinical research activities. Expertise in lymph node/lymphoma pathology is required. The department has a high volume of interesting and challenging cases and utilizes leading edge technologies, including molecular diagnostics and cancer cytogenetics. Participating in diagnostic service for UHN and its client facilities is also expected; and after hours on-call. Participation and leadership in collaborative or independent research and publishing scholarly work is expected. The successful candidate must show evidence of excellent and innovative scholarship in teaching and education in undergraduate, post-graduate, fellowship, and continuing education.
The successful applicant must hold a medical degree, certification in Hematological Pathology from the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada or its equivalent, and be eligible for registration with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario. This full time, permanent position (37.5 hours per week) offers an annual salary of $232,500 as well as a competitive benefits package.
Applications will be accepted until November 4, 2026, or until the position is filled. Only short-listed applicants will be contacted.
Interested applicants should send their curriculum vitae, a brief statement of their career plans, and the names of three referees via email to:
Dr. Jan Delabie
Division Head, Department of Laboratory Hematology
University Health Network
Laboratory Medicine Program
200 Elizabeth Street, 11E-444
Toronto, Ontario M5G2C4
E-mail: Jan.Delabie@uhn.ca

University Health Network is one of Canada's largest acute care teaching organizations with 1000 beds and nine priority programs in Transplantation, Advanced Medicine & Surgery, Oncology and Blood Disorders, Neural and Sensory Science, Heart & Circulation, Musculoskeletal Health and Arthritis, Laboratory Medicine, Diagnostic Imaging and Community & Population Health. It maintains a major commitment to excellence in healthcare delivery, research and teaching. University Health Network is the primary teaching hospital for the University of Toronto. For more information about UHN, please visit www.uhn.ca
As one of the largest departments of its kind, the Department of Laboratory Medicine and Pathobiology (LMP) has more than 450 faculty including basic scientists, pathologists, laboratory physicians and scientists. By combining research with clinical practice, we are uniquely positioned to translate new findings into reality. As a result, we are known as leaders in diagnosing and treating patients and populations, making an impact locally, nationally and internationally. For more information about the Department of Laboratory Medicine and Pathobiology, University of Toronto please visit our website at www.lmp.utoronto.ca

jobs.description:
The Department of International Literary and Cultural Studies (ILCS) at Tufts University in Medford, Massachusetts invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor in East Asian Comparative Literature/Film/Cultural Studies, to begin September 1, 2027.
The successful candidate will join a diverse faculty dedicated to understanding the complexities of a changing world through literary, cinematic, and other expressions of human consciousness. We work collaboratively across our various language/culture areas and with other departments and programs, including International Relations, International Literary and Visual Studies, Film and Media Studies, and the School of the Museum of Fine Arts. For more information about our department, see https://as.tufts.edu/ilcs.
Requirements
We give priority to scholars of Chinese who also work in Japanese or Korean but are also open to scholars who combine a specialization in Chinese with interests in other non-regional literary traditions. A PhD in a related humanities field completed by time of hire. Record of success as a college/university-level teacher, with publications in peer-reviewed venues preferred.
Responsibilities
Producing outstanding scholarship in areas related to the department and its programs. Teaching courses in support of both single-language/area-focused programs and our comparative track. Advising and mentoring of students, especially in theses and independent research projects. Service to the department, to the Chinese Program, and to the University. Building collaborative relationships with other academic programs and departments to foster cross-disciplinary exchange.
Application Instructions
Please submit the following via Interfolio to https://apply.interfolio.com/194577 1) A letter of application and CV; 2) a brief writing sample (10- to 20-pages); 3) two-page statements on i) research interests, and ii) teaching; and 4) three confidential letters of recommendation uploaded directly by recommenders to Interfolio. Review will begin on October 21, 2026 and continue until the position is filled.
Questions should be addressed to Susan Napier at susan.napier@tufts.edu or Markus Wilczek at markus.wilczek@tufts.edu.

jobs.title: Tenure Track Faculty in Mechanical Engineering and Engineering Design for 2027-2028
jobs.description:
Rose-Hulman is searching for inspiring educators who share our passion for teaching undergraduate engineering students. Our mission is “to provide students with the world’s best undergraduate science, engineering, and mathematics education in an environment of individual attention and support.” If this resonates with you, then we think you’ll love what we have to offer.
We welcome applications for multiple tenure-track positions at the Assistant Professor rank, to begin in the Fall of 2027. Primary teaching responsibilities will involve undergraduate engineering education in areas aligned with the candidate's expertise and departmental needs, including contributions to Mechanical Engineering and multidisciplinary Engineering Design experiences. Candidates with advanced experience may be considered for appointment at a higher academic rank.
Essential job responsibilities include teaching and advising students, continued professional development, and service to the department, Institute, and professional community. Applicants should demonstrate a strong commitment to undergraduate engineering education, including laboratory instruction and lifelong personal and professional development. Research and scholarship remain part of the role — professional development at Rose-Hulman is defined broadly as continued intellectual growth throughout one's career, which may include scholarship of discovery, integration, application, teaching, or learning, often carried out in partnership with undergraduate students — but it supports the teaching mission rather than competing with it.
Requirements include a doctoral degree (by the start of employment) in engineering, engineering education or closely related field. While we welcome candidates from any specialty within Mechanical Engineering or closely adjacent engineering disciplines to apply, experience that supports our dynamics, mechanics, and design curriculum is strongly desired. We also welcome candidates with expertise in cutting-edge ME technologies. Candidates with experience that supports our Engineering Design program are also strongly desired.
The department and institute place a high value on supporting all our students; candidates who are excited to enhance student engagement and community are especially encouraged to apply.
Applicants must submit the following items to https://jobs.rose-hulman.edu/:
A cover letter that addresses:
Your interest in a faculty position at Rose-Hulman and your commitment to undergraduate engineering education.
The engineering, engineering science, engineering mechanics, and/or engineering design courses you would be most interested in teaching at Rose-Hulman. Identify at least four Rose-Hulman courses. Please visit our Academic Catalog at https://catalog.rose-hulman.edu/ for descriptions of courses in the Mechanical Engineering and Engineering Design curricula.
Any interest in teaching within Rose-Hulman's multidisciplinary Engineering Design program, including studio-based instruction, design education, project-based learning, community- or client-engaged experiences, and interdisciplinary collaboration through team teaching and partnerships with faculty across engineering, computer science, and the humanities.
A teaching statement that:
Describes your teaching philosophy and teaching accomplishments.
Demonstrates your commitment to teaching, mentoring, and supporting undergraduate students.
Discusses how your teaching philosophy and experiences inform your approach to undergraduate engineering education.
Provides specific examples illustrating how your approach promotes student learning, engagement, and success.
A professional development statement that:
Discusses your professional development objectives. Note that Rose-Hulman broadly defines professional development as “continued intellectual growth throughout one’s career.” Professional development may include scholarship in all its forms, including the scholarships of discovery, integration, application, teaching, and learning.
An updated Curriculum Vitae
Finalist candidates will also be asked to provide contact information for at least three professional references capable of commenting on the appropriateness of your candidacy at Rose-Hulman.
Rose-Hulman’s Mechanical Engineering Department has established itself as one of the top ME programs in the nation. See what the media and our peer institutions have said by visiting https://www.rose-hulman.edu/about-us/rankings-and-distinction.html. Our scenic campus in Terre Haute, IN is home to an increasingly diverse student body of 2,100 students who are as passionate to learn and create as we are to guide them. Our facilities include modern classrooms, state-of-the-art instructional laboratories, and design-focused innovation centers. Walking the halls, you can’t miss the effect that our open-door culture has on the relationships between our faculty, staff, and students. At Rose-Hulman, education extends beyond the classroom.
Additional information on Rose-Hulman and the Mechanical Engineering Department is available from https://www.rose-hulman.edu/ME. Job Details

Description:
The Knoxville campus of the University of Tennessee seeks candidates who have the ability to promote an atmosphere where all members of the university community feel welcome and can thrive.
The Natalie L. Haslam College of Music invites applications for a 9-month tenure-track position at the Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor level in Music, Science, and Health. This is a rare and forward-looking appointment designed for a scholar-teacher who believes that a fuller understanding of music — how we hear it, perform it, feel it, analyze it, and create it — is enriched by understanding the human brain, human behavior, and the science behind how we interact with the art of music and human health.
The successful candidate will occupy a distinctive role at the intersection of music, medicine and health, neuroscience, psychology, cognitive science, or other theoretical and applied sciences, contributing to both the core curriculum of the College and to an emerging cross-disciplinary research culture. The candidate will work in the Natalie L. Haslam College of Music with potential for collaboration with other colleges, and relevant health organizations.The successful candidate is expected to have either existing or strong potential for obtaining extramural funding.
Teaching Responsibilities may include:
Core lab-sequence instruction in music integrated with perspectives from the natural or social sciences appropriate to the candidate's expertise
Seminars in areas such as music and health, music perception and psychoacoustics, the neuroscience of musical experience, and other topics relevant to the candidate’s field
Student mentorship and research supervision in the candidate’s core field and related interdisciplinary fields
Online course development and delivery, with interest in expanding the College's reach into digital learning environments
Research Profile
We seek a candidate with an active research agenda that intersects with one or more of the following areas:
Scientific applications of health, wellbeing, and/or and human development, including scientific approaches to understanding music’s role in health-related outcomes.
The neuroscience of musical experience, including brain-music interaction, with particular attention to musical and cognitive aspects such as rhythm, harmony, melody, tonality, memory, and emotion.
Computational, data-driven, and/or psychological approaches to music perception, emotion, musical structure, and performance, with a focus on their relationships to human health
Machine learning and artificial intelligence applications for understanding how music interacts with human health, behavior, and perception
Web Page: www.music.utk.edu
The University of Tennessee Natalie L. Haslam College of Music offers a broad and comprehensive professional music program at both the undergraduate and graduate levels and is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music. The College has approximately 65 faculty members and approximately 400 music majors.
General Information:
The University of Tennessee, Knoxville, is the state’s flagship research institution, a campus of choice for outstanding undergraduates, and a premier graduate institution. As a land-grant university, it is committed to excellence in learning, scholarship, and engagement with society. In all its activities, the university aims to advance the frontiers of human knowledge and enrich and elevate society. Knoxville’s cultural resources include a symphony orchestra, an opera company, a professional jazz orchestra, theatrical productions, ballet and modern dance, art galleries, and museums. Within an hour’s drive is the Great Smoky Mountains National Park with its scenic beauty and wide variety of recreational activities, plants, and wildlife.

PhD or related doctorate in a health-related science, neuroscience, psychology, cognitive science, or a closely related field (ABD considered with degree conferred by August 1, 2027)
Emerging or established national visibility in the field as appropriate to rank
Demonstrated research activity and publication in relevant areas
Demonstrated ability to communicate, organize work effectively, and collaborate productively with faculty, staff, and students.
Candidates for the rank of Assistant Professor should demonstrate a credible plan for developing an externally funded research program. Associate and Full Professor candidates should demonstrate a record of obtaining and/or leading external funding appropriate to their field.
Preferred Qualifications
Evidence of successful teaching at the college/university level.
Candidates for the rank of Assistant Professor must:
Meet the qualifications for being an Assistant Professor within UTK’s faculty handbook and the Natalie L. Haslam College of Music bylaws; these are covered in the position's Required Qualifications.

Meet the qualifications for being an Associate Professor within UTK’s faculty handbook and the Natalie L. Haslam College of Music bylaws; these qualifications normally include having served as an assistant professor for at least 5 years and having served as mentor to junior faculty.

Cover letter detailing your interests and qualifications relating to research, teaching, and service.
Current CV

Teaching and mentoring philosophy
Two-three representative publications
Contact information for three references listing names, email addresses, and phone numbers

jobs.description:
Associate/Full Professor – Finance
Position Summary:
The Crummer Graduate School of Business at Rollins College in Winter Park, Florida offers a unique opportunity to qualified applicants with expertise in corporate finance and/or investments. If you share our passion for outstanding teaching, consider joining our faculty as an Associate/Full Professor of Finance in Fall 2027. Applicants should have a Ph.D. in Finance from an AACSB-accredited school. A professional certification (i.e., CFA) is desirable.
We hire experienced faculty, many of whom have won teaching awards before joining Crummer. If you enjoy teaching and aspire to expand your teaching skills, this is the position for you. A successful candidate will demonstrate a strong commitment to teaching MBA students in both traditional and blended formats and have at least four years of teaching experience at an AACSB-accredited school.
At Crummer, you will have the opportunity to teach students with varying ages and levels of experience, ranging from recent college graduates to senior executives. Our students demand much of us; they challenge and stimulate us as much as we do them. Crummer faculty are all dedicated to providing our students with an integrated, experiential educational environment. As a result, we have tremendous collaboration among the various disciplines. We are nimble and operate with little bureaucracy. All new Crummer faculty come without tenure and have three to four years to qualify for tenure based on teaching, research, and service.
Teaching: To be successful at Crummer, you must be dedicated to great teaching. Crummer School faculty members take great pride in their teaching. We attract outstanding students who are motivated, eager to learn, and deeply engaged in our programs. We are looking for faculty who have already won teaching awards, especially at the MBA level. Fifty percent of your annual performance at Crummer will come from your teaching, as evaluated by colleagues and students. Finance faculty must teach the core finance course in the MBA program, as well as electives that match their background. Crummer faculty are encouraged to develop elective courses that bring their research interests and professional experiences into the classroom.
Research: The Crummer faculty recognize that a broad range of research contributes to management practice. Thirty percent of your annual performance evaluation will come from your research at Crummer. Our faculty handbook spells out the exact requirements.
Service: Crummer has 18 faculty members who collaborate between and among various disciplines. The remaining twenty percent of your annual performance evaluation is based on your service activities. We practice faculty governance without rancor and most of our decisions are unanimous. You will find collegiality one of the best parts of life at Crummer.
Because we are unique, the Crummer School is not for everyone. If you are just starting your academic career, Crummer is not for you. If teaching is your primary motivation, you will likely find a good fit at Crummer. We are looking for a candidate who has already made a significant mark in research and is ready to transition to a program that truly does emphasize teaching. We also value practical professional experience as well as prior engagements with executives through teaching and/or consulting.
Crummer is a great place to work-great students, wonderful colleagues, and a stimulating intellectual climate. We are an AACSB accredited, nationally ranked MBA-only graduate business school attached to a highly ranked undergraduate liberal arts college.

Position Summary:
The Crummer Graduate School of Business at Rollins College invites applications for a tenure-track
faculty position at the rank of Associate or Full Professor in the area of operations and supply chain management beginning in September 2027. We are seeking a seasoned educator and thought leader who combines a strong academic foundation with a passion for shaping practice-oriented insights for today's business leaders.
We are seeking a seasoned educator and thought leader who combines a strong academic foundation with a passion for shaping practice-oriented insights for today's business leaders. This is not a traditional operations management role. We are looking for someone who brings a systems thinking perspective to operations that emphasizes helping leaders understand how operational choices create second- and third-order effects across interconnected value chains and organizations. We are particularly interested in candidates exploring technology's evolving role in operations ranging from business analytics and automation to AI-enabled decision-making, including how large language models and domain-specific AI shape operational resilience and performance. While this position emphasizes practical impact and executive education, we remain an AACSB-accredited institution with high standards for research productivity. Candidates must have a distinguished record of publishing in peer-reviewed academic journals as well as demonstrated excellence in teaching. However, this role is ideal for a scholar who has excelled in traditional academic research and MBA teaching and is now seeking to broaden their focus toward executive education, applied research, and practitioner-oriented thought leadership.
We especially welcome candidates who:
Have published in respected peer-reviewed journals and built a strong scholarly reputation, but also seek to translate those insights into frameworks, tools, and programs that impact practicing managers and executives.
Can connect systems thinking and foresight to operational strategy, helping organizations navigate uncertainty, interconnected risks, and emerging technologies.
Have experience engaging with business leaders or industry forums and can design executive education offerings that elevate Crummer's presence in practice-oriented learning.
Are collaborative and thrive in Crummer's interdisciplinary, small-school environment, which emphasizes applied learning, close student-faculty engagement, and strong industry connections.

The Department of Political Science at Clemson University is conducting a search for an assistant professor with a research agenda applying quantitative research methods to topics in comparative politics or international relations. This is a nine-month, tenure-track position with an August 2027 start date.The Department of Political Science is part of the College of Behavioral, Social, and Health Sciences at Clemson University. It includes 25 full-time faculty members supported by two full-time staff members and offers B.A. and B.S. degrees in political science, a master's degree in public administration, and a Ph.D. in policy studies. Its strategic plan-Clemson Elevate-articulates three dynamic goals: delivering the #1 student experience in the nation, doubling research productivity by 2035, and transforming lives statewide and beyond. The Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences (PES) at Clemson University is seeking applicants for the Gregory Distinguished Endowed Professorship in Urban Entomology, a 12-month, tenure-track position at the level of Associate Professor. The appointment will include responsibilities in Extension (60%) and research (40%) and will be located on the Clemson University main campus in Clemson, SC. The successful candidate will be an integral part of the Extension, research, and educational programs of PES. The PES department is a dynamic unit within the College of Agriculture, Forestry, and Life Sciences (CAFLS), with a strong commitment and contribution to the Land-Grant mission of Clemson University. The PES department encompasses 59 faculty with various specializations, including, but not limited to, entomology, plant pathology, horticulture, soil science, weed science, and agronomy. It houses 150 undergraduates across three programs (Horticulture, Plant and Environmental Sciences, and Turfgrass) and 112 graduate students in M.S. and Ph.D. granting programs (Entomology and Plant and Environmental Sciences). The faculty and graduate student populations are diverse and cosmopolitan, involved in projects across the state, region and the globe. The successful candidate will assume leadership of Clemson University's Extension, outreach, and community engagement in the management of household and structural pests and will be expected to develop a nationally and internationally recognized, externally funded program that addresses the needs of stakeholders regarding pests in urban and built environments. The successful candidate will participate actively in undergraduate and graduate education by chairing and serving on graduate committees, supervising thesis, dissertation, and undergraduate research, and authoring Extension and research publications with students. Job Details

Clemson University: Harvey S. Peeler Jr. College of Veterinary Medicine
Location: CVM - COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE HUB(001184) BLDG001184
