Description
The Clemson University Harvey S. Peeler Jr. College of Veterinary Medicine (PCVM) is seeking applicants for several full-time positions to serve as Small Animal Educators. These faculty positions will play a pivotal role in the development and implementation of the Clemson DVM curriculum (https://www.clemson.edu/veterinary-medicine/students/curriculum.html). The successful candidates will have a primary instructional role in developing and delivering small animal medicine and / or surgery content in the integrated Clemson DVM curriculum. These faculty members will teach with a dynamic, collaborative team consisting of experienced general practice clinicians, boarded specialists, and education specialists. The small animal medicine and surgery course series is designed to be an integrated, systems-based approach for conditions common to small animal general practice. This role is designed to attract outstanding educators and experienced clinicians who are passionate about teaching diagnostic medicine and small animal surgery in a practical, integrated fashion. Board certification in small animal internal medicine, small animal surgery, or ABVP certification is encouraged but not required. The Clemson DVM curriculum is based upon integrative, collaborative team teaching in which faculty with varying backgrounds can work together to offer students an inclusive and innovative learning environment. The Small Animal Educators will collaborate with our other teaching faculty to facilitate vertical and horizontal integration for the delivery of core small animal internal medicine and surgery principles. Utilizing state of the art classrooms and teaching technology, this faculty member will be asked to adopt an integrated educational approach to provide students with a strong foundation of cognitive, clinical, and professional competencies in preparation for entry into the partially distributive model of clinical training in the fourth year. This position will consist primarily of didactic and small group instruction, along with some instruction in teaching laboratories. While the PCVM will not have a specialty referral hospital, it will have a fully staffed Community Practice as well as a robust Shelter Medicine spay-neuter program. The Small Animal Educators will work closely with the Community Practice and Shelter Medicine clinicians to integrate classroom concepts that translate seamlessly into real world experiences. A clinical service commitment is not required; however, interested individuals are encouraged to engage in teaching activities in our Community Practice. Additionally, these faculty members will engage in scholarly activity, which can include curriculum development, programmatic or curricular assessment, scholarship of teaching and learning, and other similar activities. Finally, a hybrid academic appointment will be considered for a boarded small animal specialist (internal medicine and / or surgery). If desired, this individual may seek a combination of a part-time academic appointment at Clemson while also having a part-time position in private referral practice. The possibility of a 9-month to 12-month contract are options that can be discussed with the Department Chair. Overview of Clemson and the PCVM Located in South Carolina's beautiful and fast-growing Upstate, Clemson University is the land-grant university of South Carolina and ranks among the country's top 50 national public universities in the U.S. News & World Report. The University has nearly 23,400 students (including nearly 18,600 undergraduates) who can select from 80 undergraduate and 110 graduate degree programs. Clemson employs over 1,150 full-time faculty and has an annual budget expenditure of over $900M. Clemson University maintains its status as an R1 Carnegie Research Institution while maintaining a strong focus on undergraduate education. The PCVM is currently seeking accreditation by the American Veterinary Medicine Association-Council on Education to offer the Doctor of Veterinary Medicine degree to approximately 80 students per cohort which started in August 2026). The PCVM plans to utilize a partial distributive model of clinical training for students. Its brand-new state of the art campus will reside in Pendleton, SC, near the T. Ed Garrison Arena, will house research and teaching labs, and utilize both ambulatory services as well as teaching sites at the Clemson University Equine Center, Lamaster Dairy Cattle Center, and other locations for education in the field. In 2023, the Board of Trustees approved Clemson Elevate, the university's new strategic plan. Clemson Elevate is built on 3 pillars: deliver the #1 student experience, double research by 2035, and transform lives statewide and beyond. The PCVM was named as a strategic priority for the university, demonstrating the importance of the new college to the future of the university and the state. We are excited to attract a team of top talent as we build the new college. Overview of the Position Reporting to the Department Chair and working closely with the Foundational Sciences and Clinical Skills Leads, the small animal medicine educator will: Create and deliver the small animal content in the team-taught systems-based courses in the curriculum. Participate in teaching laboratories as agreed upon with colleagues and the department chair Develop assessment strategies in alignment with the overall competency-based curriculum. Collaborate with other faculty members to ensure integration of knowledge and skills across years and courses. Actively and effectively engage in student-centered instruction, coaching, and mentorship. Collaborate closely with the Clemson University Community Practice and with our partner clinics. Serve on PCVM and campus committees as an appointed or elected member. Additionally, the faculty member must have the ability to: Emulate our PCVM cultural values including integrity, authenticity, respect, welcoming, trust, and collaboration. Work independently and collaboratively as part of a team, possess exemplary verbal and written communication skills, with exceptional organizational skills and attention to detail. Prioritize and manage multiple tasks, meet deadlines, and function independently with limited supervision and guidance. Work in partnership with faculty and staff across multiple disciplines and functions across the college and university. Participate in research and scholarship initiatives designed to improve educational and professional outcomes. Demonstrate a commitment to the core values of Clemson University and specifically to community, engagement, belonging and accessibility (CEBA).
Qualifications
DVM or equivalent with 3+ years of relevant experience.
Applicants must demonstrate a strong foundation in small animal practice and the ability to teach clinical skills to veterinary students in classroom and laboratory/skills settings
Board certification is not required; board-eligible/board-certified candidates are encouraged to apply.
Commitment to excellence and creativity in education.
Licensed or eligible for licensure to practice veterinary medicine in South Carolina and ability to obtain a DEA license.
Preferred qualifications include:
5+ years of relevant experience in veterinary medicine or education.
Experience in clinical skills education, simulation pedagogy, and/or competency-based assessment.
Demonstrated experience mentoring learners (students, interns, residents, or technicians).
Board certification or residency training in small animal medicine (ACVIM, ECVIM), small animal surgery (ACVS, ECVS) or American Board of Veterinary Practitioners (ABVP).

https://apply.interfolio.com/194184
and submit a cover letter, resume, and contact information for three references by 10/23/26 to assure full consideration.

Sarah Lawrence College invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track faculty position in clinical psychology beginning in the fall of 2027. Competitive candidates may have a research and practice focus primarily in adult and/or in child clinical psychology. Candidates are expected to be able to teach in both areas. Intersections with contemporary social, cognitive, and affective neuroscience are especially welcome. The ideal candidate will be able to connect their research and teaching to different cultural/global contexts. Competitive candidates might have experience working with qualitative, quantitative, mixed methods, and/or community-based participatory research methods.

A full-time position involves teaching two 5-credit courses per semester. Seminar courses are typically capped at 15 students and include a seminar class and biweekly meetings with individual students to develop a semester-long independent project which usually takes the form of a substantial literature review or other form of independent research project conducted under the instructor's guidance. The position is teaching-intensive, involving two courses per semester. Description
The University of Virginia Department of Pediatrics and Division of Neonatology invite applications for a Neonatology faculty member at the Assistant or Associate Professor level. This position can be tenure-eligible (Clinical Educator Track) or tenure-ineligible (Clinical Faculty Track). The ideal candidate for this position is a board certified/board eligible Neonatologist with strong clinical skills and a career focused on education, quality improvement, or other academic pursuits. Special consideration is given to those with expertise in neonatal hemodynamics and POCUS.
The UVA NICU is a 64 bed level IV unit with approximately 950 admissions per year with plans to expand to 90+ beds by 2028. Approximately 30% of admissions are born at outside hospitals from across Virginia and the mid-Atlantic region and many have complex multisystem conditions. We care for pre-op cardiac patients and perform ECMO within the NICU.
The UVA Neonatology faculty is comprised of 16 neonatologists and a PhD with a broad range of academic interests including bench research, clinical research, quality improvement and education. Our Neonatology Fellowship program includes 9 fellows and we have a large and growing group of APPs in addition to residents and medical/APP students.
We have a telehealth program that complements our Neonatal Emergency Transport System (NETS) providing consultations and transports for sick infants, as well as an active NICU follow-up program, run by Developmental Pediatrics. Members of our Neonatology Division have a collaborative relationship with members of other Divisions in Pediatrics, with all subspecialties represented. We also have an excellent relationship with our obstetric and Maternal-Fetal Medicine colleagues. UVA has approximately 2500 deliveries per year, many of them high risk. We have a busy Fetal Care Center and an MFM fellowship training program.
UVA Health Children’s lives within UVA Health Medical Center, a world-class academic medical center and health system. UVA Health Children’s is the number 1 rated Children’s Hospital in Virginia for 6 consecutive years by US News & World Report. In 2026, 9 pediatrics subspecialties were ranked including Neonatology at #41. UVA Health’s footprint encompasses 4 hospitals and 2 physician groups with an integrated network of primary and specialty care clinics throughout Charlottesville, Albemarle, Nelson and Augusta counties, Culpeper, and Northern Virginia. Through its teaching and research, UVA Health continues to innovate and advance medicine while providing high-quality care.
Qualifiations
Applicants must be board eligible or board certified in Neonatology and have an M.D. or D.O. degree, and must be eligible for medical licensure in Virginia.
Candidates requiring visa sponsorship will not be considered for this position.

jobs.description:
Job Details
Description
The University of Virginia’s Department of Pediatrics, Division of Pediatric Allergy, Immunology, and Rheumatology is searching for a full-time Pediatric Allergist/Immunologist faculty member at rank of Assistant or Associate Professor on the Clinical Faculty (non-tenure) track. Rank, tenure status, and salary are dependent upon qualifications. The appointee will focus on the clinical care of children with pediatric allergic disorders including asthma, allergic rhinitis, atopic dermatitis, and urticaria, as well as children with a variety of immunodeficiency concerns. This position also affords the appointee a unique and exciting opportunity to participate in the newly approved UVA Food and Digestive Allergic Diseases Center of Excellence, by expanding access to world-class food allergy clinical care in Charlottesville and across the Commonwealth of Virginia, including supervising oral immunotherapy (OIT) and oral food challenges. Interest and/or experience in the multidisciplinary care of patients with Eosinophilic Gastrointestinal Disorders (EGIDs) is also preferred. Satellite clinic opportunities may also be explored. The appointee will also perform inpatient consults at UVA in collaboration with the Division of Asthma, Allergy, and Immunology in the Department of Medicine, and is expected to be proficient in the evaluation and management of pediatric immunodeficiency and immunodysregulatory disorders. The appointee will be a collaborative member of the Division and be positioned to succeed in a dynamic academic environment and advance the clinical, educational, and scholarly goals we offer. Other duties will include the teaching and supervision of GME trainees and medical students.
In addition to the nationally recognized food allergy and EGID programs within the new Center of Excellence, the Division boasts a nationally recognized primary immunodeficiency program, a multidisciplinary high-risk asthma clinic, a unique multidisciplinary GI-Allergy clinic focused on FPIES and Alpha-Gal Syndrome, a rapidly growing Rheumatology program, and a drug allergy assessment program, all with exciting and diverse clinical research opportunities. Numerous collaborations with the Division of Asthma, Allergy, and Immunology in the Department of Medicine in basic science and translational research, as well as the teaching and training of allergy/immunology fellows, are also available, and make for a ripe academic environment and potential for exciting future research opportunities, if interested.
The University of Virginia School of Medicine and affiliated UVA Health System form the premier medical and research institution in the Commonwealth of Virginia and has a rich tradition of discovery, translational, clinical and health services/outcomes-based research grounded in a culture of collaboration and service. US News and World Report once again ranked the UVA Children’s Hospital the #1 children’s hospital in Virginia, and our group has a long history of pioneering asthma and allergy-related research. The University is located in Charlottesville, VA, situated in the picturesque Shenandoah Valley just 100 miles from Washington, DC. Our region boasts outstanding opportunities for outdoor recreation year round, including hiking, water-based activities as well as skiing and snowboarding. We are just a short drive to Virginia Beach and the Outer Banks of North Carolina to the east and the Blue Ridge mountains to the west. Some of the state’s finest restaurants and music are showcased on the Downtown Mall, the longest contiguous outdoor mall in the US. Charlottesville is also host to many award-winning vineyards and is routinely listed among the most desirable cities in which to live, raise a family, and retire.

Prior to the start of employment, qualified applicants must:
Have a medical doctorate degree or equivalent
Hold or be eligible for medical licensure in the Commonwealth of Virginia
Have completed an ACGME-accredited Allergy/Immunology training program and be Board eligible or certified in Allergy/Immunology

The Department of Psychology and Neuroscience in the College of Arts and Sciences at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill invites application for a tenure track faculty position at the rank of Assistant Professor, to begin July 2027. We seek an outstanding researcher with expertise at the intersection of AI and cognition. Areas of research may include, but are not limited to, the effects of AI on learning, language processing, and other cognitive tasks; the development of AI-assisted technologies to measure cognitive processes; human-computer interactions; AI-informed brain-computer interfaces; or AI models of attention, language, and memory. The position will build on existing expertise in our department in the areas of complex human capabilities and how they change as a result of human experience.
The successful candidate will join the Cognitive Psychology program within the Department of Psychology and Neuroscience. UNC Chapel hill offers opportunities for exciting collaboration and innovation, both across the six programs in the department as well as with UNC’s new School of Data and Information Sciences, the UNC School of Education, the UNC Health Care System’s new Aging Brain Clinic, the School of Public Health, the Frank Porter Graham Child Development Institute, the Biomedical Research Imaging Center, the School of Social Work, and the School of Medicine.
Primary Purpose of Organizational Unit:
The primary purpose of the Psychology and Neuroscience Department is to provide excellent education, research and service in the field. This goal breaks down into four important components: 1) to teach psychology and neuroscience to undergraduates in a manner that will introduce them vigorously to its broad scope; 2) to offer scientific and professional training to graduate students in the areas of behavioral and integrative neuroscience, clinical, cognitive, developmental, quantitative, and social psychology; 3) to carry out cutting-edge research in these areas, and 4) to provide consulting and administrative support services to the science and profession of psychology as well as to the university, the community, the state, and the nation.
The Department consists of six programs: behavioral and integrative neuroscience; clinical psychology; cognitive psychology; developmental psychology; quantitative psychology, and social psychology. Each program is designed to acquaint the student thoroughly with the theoretical and research content of the specialty and to provide training in the research skills needed to become a competent and creative investigator. In addition, the programs focus on the development of appropriate professional skills.
The Department of Psychology and Neuroscience currently ranks 2nd in the College in grant funding with over $15 million annually in awarded grants and approximately $20 million annually in expenditures from all funds. The Department of Psychology and Neuroscience has the largest undergraduate major in the College of Arts and Sciences with approximately 1900 majors, and one of the largest graduate Ph.D. programs with approximately 140 graduate students. The Department is also home to the UNC Psychology and Neuroscience Community Clinic, which provides therapeutic treatment and assessment services to a variety of constituencies on campus and in the community.
Position Summary:
Primary responsibilities of the position will include conducting high-quality research, mentoring doctoral student research, publishing in peer reviewed journals and broader dissemination, seeking external funding for research, teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in cognitive psychology, and engaging in departmental, university, and professional service activities.
Minimum Education and Experience Requirements:
Ph.D. in Psychology, Neuroscience or a related field by date of appointment
Preferred Qualifications, Competencies, and Experience:
We are seeking candidates with a strong record of (or potential for) cutting edge research productivity, the potential to develop an independent, externally funded research program that is internationally recognized, and a commitment to teaching and mentoring at the undergraduate and graduate levels.
Campus Security Authority Responsibilities:
Not Applicable.
Special Instructions:
The application should include the following: cover letter explaining how you can support the department’s mission in the three areas of research, teaching and service (https://psychology.unc.edu/); curriculum vitae; research and teaching statements; up to 4 reprints, preprints or working papers, and the names of four professionals familiar with your work who can submit recommendation letters for you. If you do not yet have your Ph.D. but expect to have it by the time of appointment, please indicate this in the cover letter.
Please use the Research Statement option to upload research and teaching statements in a combined pdf.
Please use Research/Writing Sample and/or Other Document options to upload papers.

The Department of Psychology and Neuroscience at the University of North Carolina (UNC) at Chapel Hill invites applications for two tenure-track positions at the Assistant Professor level in the field of Behavioral and Integrative Neuroscience, with appointments to begin July 2027.
We seek outstanding candidates in each of the following areas:
(1) Human Neuroscience of Substance Use Disorders. We seek candidates conducting human-subjects research focused on the neural mechanisms of substance use disorders. Relevant research may address risk factors, development, maintenance, recovery, and treatment. Relevant approaches may include neuroimaging, computational modeling, functional neural network analyses, fNIRS, EEG/ERP, noninvasive brain stimulation, machine learning approaches or other related methodologies that provide mechanistic insight to advance our understanding of substance use disorders.
(2) Pre-Clinical Neuroscience of Substance Use Disorders. We seek candidates investigating the neural and cellular mechanisms underlying substance use disorders using pre-clinical animal models. Relevant approaches include, but are not limited to, circuit, cellular, molecular, and systems neuroscience approaches, as well as the integration of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, computational methods, New Approach Methodologies (NAMs), human iPSC-derived neural systems or organoids, and advanced behavioral and physiological analyses.
Successful applicants will join the Behavioral and Integrative Neuroscience program within the Department of Psychology and Neuroscience, which has longstanding strengths in the neurobiology of reward, addiction, and motivated behavior and a collaborative research environment including the UNC Bowles Center for Alcohol Studies, the UNC Neuroscience Center, the Biomedical Research Imaging Center, the School of Medicine, and other programs across campus. Candidates who leverage innovative computational, methodological and quantitative, approaches to address questions related to alcohol and substance use disorders are especially encouraged to apply.
Primary Purpose of Organizational Unit:
The primary purpose of the Psychology and Neuroscience Department is to provide excellent education, research and service in the field. This goal breaks down into four important components: 1) to teach psychology and neuroscience to undergraduates in a manner that will introduce them vigorously to its broad scope; 2) to offer scientific and professional training to graduate students in the areas of behavioral and integrative neuroscience, clinical, cognitive, developmental, quantitative, and social psychology; 3) to carry out cutting-edge research in these areas, and 4) to provide consulting and administrative support services to the science and profession of psychology as well as to the university, the community, the state, and the nation.
The Department consists of six programs: behavioral and integrative neuroscience; clinical psychology; cognitive psychology; developmental psychology; quantitative psychology, and social psychology. Each program is designed to acquaint the student thoroughly with the theoretical and research content of the specialty and to provide training in the research skills needed to become a competent and creative investigator. In addition, the programs focus on the development of appropriate professional skills.
The Department of Psychology and Neuroscience currently ranks 2nd in the College in grant funding with over $15 million annually in awarded grants and approximately $20 million annually in expenditures from all funds. The Department of Psychology and Neuroscience has the largest undergraduate major in the College of Arts and Sciences with approximately 1900 majors, and one of the largest graduate Ph.D. programs with approximately 130 graduate students. The Department is also home to the UNC Psychology and Neuroscience Community Clinic, which provides therapeutic treatment and assessment services to a variety of constituencies on campus and in the community.

In July 2026, UNC Chapel Hill launched the Division of Data Science and Society within the School of Data and Information Sciences (SDIS), a division devoted to data science teaching, research, scholarship, service, and creativity. DSS’s vision is to be a leader in shaping the field of data science through an interdisciplinary and rigorous grounding in theory and methods with a human centric approach to the entire data life cycle.
The mission of DSS is to empower a diverse community of faculty conducting research in the fundamentals and/or the applications of data science. The Division is training undergraduate, graduate, and professional students to be the next generation of data science leaders with the knowledge and skills to thrive in this data-driven world. The Division will serve the state, the nation, and the world through premier data science educational programs and innovative research directed to advancing the public good with human centric and ethical applications.
The core elements of SDIS include porous borders: leveraging our low walled collaborative Carolina culture to solve major societal problems. Interdisciplinary research clusters that cross Division and School boundaries are a vital element of our Scholarly community. The School of Data and Information Sciences is focused on students and education – the emphasis is not just on data science majors but on all students becoming data literate. The school’s culture has an open and transparent structure, governance, and business model.
Position Summary:
The Division of Data Science and Society (DSS) at UNC-Chapel Hill’s School of Data and Information Sciences (SDIS) is excited to announce a full-time Professor of the Practice position in data science. This position provides academic leadership for the culminating capstone experience in the school’s graduate data science programs – the online Master of Applied Data Science (MADS) and the residential Master of Science in Data Science (MS) – and serves as the faculty lead for MADS. The successful candidate will orchestrate the delivery of the graduate capstone course, serve as instructor of record for the MADS capstone, and teach additional DATA courses in the MADS program as program needs require. Primary responsibilities include:
* Orchestrate the delivery of the graduate capstone course by vetting projects in conjunction with the school’s Office of Cross-Sector Partnership, overseeing and grading student work, and communicating with the external clients of capstone projects.
* Teach a wide range of the DATA courses offered in the MADS program, including the culminating capstone experience, in coordination with other teaching faculty.
* Serve on the Admissions Committee for MADS, reviewing candidates who meet program qualifications and making admission decisions.
* Collaborate with school staff on curricular improvements to ensure the online program management vendor delivers services that meet university academic standards.
* Oversee continuous quality improvement of the curriculum by reviewing instructor and student feedback and implementing changes.
* Take an active role in planning and carrying out the optional on-campus immersion held during the summer.
* Participate in virtual student recruitment sessions four times a year.
Professors of the practice at SDIS bring deep professional and pedagogical expertise into the classroom and play a central role in connecting students with real-world practice. Working closely with teaching faculty, program staff, the Office of Cross-Sector Partnership, and the school’s external partners, the Professor of the Practice will ensure that data science master’s students complete a rigorous, client-facing capstone experience that translates classroom learning into professional practice. We invite you to join the DSS faculty and be part of this mission.
Minimum Education and Experience Requirements:
The applicants must have a Ph.D. in data science, statistics, computer science, or a related field, or a master’s degree in a related field accompanied by substantial professional experience in the practice of data science.

Minimum Qualifications:

Position Summary:
The Franklin College of Arts and Sciences at the University of Georgia (UGA) invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Design Anthropology in the Department of Anthropology, beginning August 1, 2027. The successful candidate will contribute to the development of design anthropology as an area of research and teaching within the Department of Anthropology while creating opportunities for interdisciplinary connections across UGA, including with the interdisciplinary Museum Studies Program.
Areas of specialization within design anthropology are open and may engage material, visual, digital, or multimodal forms; technologies and infrastructures; museum anthropology, exhibition practice, and collections; or other designed environments and systems. Relevant work may employ ethnographic, participatory, collaborative, or experimental approaches to investigate the social, cultural, political, and ethical dimensions of design and to engage processes of making, intervention, community engagement, and imagining possible futures.
The successful candidate will have opportunities to collaborate with faculty across anthropology and to develop research and teaching connections with UGA’s museums, collections, laboratories, public-facing institutions, and community partners, including the interdisciplinary Museum Studies Program, Georgia Museum of Natural History, Laboratory of Archaeology, Georgia Museum of Art, Lamar Dodd School of Art, College of Environment and Design, and other relevant programs and units across campus. These settings offer opportunities to approach museums, collections, and other public-facing environments not simply as repositories or sites for presenting knowledge, but as spaces of encounter, ethnographic inquiry, collaborative experimentation, design, imagination, and public engagement. The successful candidate will be expected to develop an independent research program with strong potential for extramural support.
The successful candidate will contribute to the Department of Anthropology’s undergraduate and graduate programs and develop courses in design anthropology and the candidate’s areas of expertise that can also create interdisciplinary connections with Museum Studies and other programs across UGA. Teaching will include one large-enrollment undergraduate course per year as well as upper-level undergraduate and graduate courses.
This position is for a tenure-track Assistant Professor. This is a full-time equivalent position with a 50% instruction (12 credit hours), 45% research, and 5% service effort expectation per academic year.
Additional Requirements:
The qualifications and academic expectations for ranks as well as the guidelines for promotion and tenure at the University of Georgia can be found at https://provost.uga.edu/faculty-affairs/promotion-tenure/.
Preferred Knowledge, Skills, Abilities and/or Competencies:
We seek an anthropologist whose research and teaching explore relationships among people, culture, design, and material, visual, digital, spatial, or experiential forms of knowledge and practice.
We welcome candidates whose anthropologically grounded research examines how people imagine, make, use, experience, and transform objects, technologies, environments, institutions, and systems, and how anthropological knowledge and methods can contribute to processes of design, representation, experimentation, and public engagement. We seek scholars who approach design not only as an object of anthropological analysis but also as a mode of inquiry and collaboration.
Applicants should demonstrate potential for excellence in teaching and mentoring and for engaging students in anthropological approaches to design, ethnography, material and visual culture, museums, technology, environments, and public-facing scholarship.

Position Summary:
The University of Georgia School of Social Work invites applications for one tenure-track faculty position at the rank of assistant, associate, or full professor. The successful candidate will hold a joint appointment in the School of Social Work and the newly established School of Medicine.
We seek a scholar who will establish and lead an externally funded program of human-subjects research focused on the design, evaluation, implementation, and scaling of evidence-based digital interventions and clinical decision-support tools for prevention, treatment, and recovery. Areas of inquiry may include digital therapeutics; mobile- and web-based interventions; conversational agents for psychoeducation, screening, or triage; EHR-enabled measurement-based care; sensors and other digital biomarkers; and recovery platforms that connect individuals with treatment, peer support, and harm-reduction resources.
The successful candidate may employ rigorous and responsible artificial intelligence methods, including natural language processing, predictive modeling, risk stratification, relapse forecasting, recommender systems, and just-in-time adaptive interventions, to improve early detection, treatment engagement, care coordination, and sustained recovery. Related areas of research may include artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted clinical documentation and workflow optimization, digital phenotyping, integration of multimodal clinical and patient-reported data, and safe and transparent clinical decision support.
The joint appointment will create opportunities for close collaboration with clinical, behavioral, and data science investigators in the School of Medicine while advancing a Social Work research agenda focused on community-based implementation, behavioral health equity, practice integration, recovery-oriented care, and the ethical and responsible use of digital technologies and AI.
Teaching responsibilities may include undergraduate and graduate courses in digital behavioral health, SUD and co-occurring conditions, implementation science, research methods, and the ethical and equitable delivery of digitally enabled care. The faculty member will also contribute to the development of new curricula, certificates, and short courses that translate emerging research and technologies into practice-ready competencies.
The successful candidate will mentor students and trainees across social work, public health, medicine, nursing, informatics, and data science programs and support interdisciplinary research and career development. The faculty member will also be expected to build and sustain partnerships with hospitals, federally qualified health centers, health departments, community-based organizations, and peer-led recovery programs. Through these partnerships, the faculty member may co-design, pilot, implement, and evaluate digital interventions and lead dissemination activities that produce practical resources such as implementation toolkits, train-the-trainer materials, and evaluation dashboards.
The successful candidate will join an exceptionally talented and committed community of scholars and staff. Opportunities for collaboration within the School of Social Work include the Center for Human Trafficking Research & Outreach; the Center for Social Justice, Human and Civil Rights; and the Institute for Nonprofit Organizations. Across the University, faculty collaborate with colleagues in the College of Pharmacy, College of Public Health, newly established College of Nursing, College of Engineering, College of Family and Consumer Sciences, Mary Frances Early College of Education, and School of Law. Additional opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration are available through the Owens Institute for Behavioral Research, the Institute for Artificial Intelligence, and other university centers and institutes.
Faculty are expected to engage in teaching, research, field liaison duties and/or academic advising, and service. They may teach across the educational continuum at our Athens, Gwinnett, and Online campuses. The successful candidate is expected to share the University and School’s commitment to excellence in teaching, research, service, and engagement.
Additional Requirements:
Candidates for the Assistant Professor rank must have a Ph.D. in social work or cognate discipline (e.g. psychology, sociology, public health, neuroscience, economics).
Candidates for the Associate Professor rank must also be engaged in teaching, research, and service consistent with an appointment at the rank of associate professor.
Candidates for the Professor rank must also be engaged in teaching, research, and service consistent with a tenured faculty appointment at the rank of a tenured professor.
Tenure on appointment must be approved before hire, the faculty member must be appointed as an associate or full professor, must have already been tenured at a prior institution, and must bring a demonstrable national reputation to the institution.
Relevant/Preferred Education, Experience, Licensure, and/or Certification:
An M.S.W. degree with two years post master’s practice experience strongly preferred but not required.
We welcome applications from strong candidates in two areas: (1) Digital Mental Health and (2) Digital Behavioral Health for Substance Use Disorder (SUD).

The candidate selected for this faculty position will be an outstanding scholar and teacher. Applicants must demonstrate exceptional research capacity and potential for external funding.
We welcome applications from scholars whose research advances digital behavioral health, withparticular attention to substance use disorders (SUD), co-occurring mental health conditions,and recovery across the lifespan.

Position Summary
The Department of Theatre and Dance invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in Dance.
Detailed Position Information
The Department of Theatre and Dance invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in Dance. The successful candidate will engage with students across the MFA and BA dance programs through teaching, mentoring, research and creative activity, and service. The faculty member will teach a combination of dance studies and studio courses, which may include dance pedagogy, graduate research methods, graduate dance seminars, and improvisation and composition, in addition to all levels of technique in the candidate’s area of expertise. While we are particularly seeking candidates with experience teaching all levels of jazz and/or ballet techniques, additional expertise in dance forms such as Hip Hop, House, Street Style, or Latin forms, and in dance technology and digital media, will be considered an asset. The position also offers opportunities to contribute to the reimagining of curricular initiatives and the development of new courses. The faculty member will mentor graduate and undergraduate students in teaching, choreography, and research.
Research and creative activity are integral components of the position. The faculty member is expected to develop and maintain a compelling creative research agenda with demonstrated potential to impact the field. This is an exciting time for creative work within the department, and in Fall 2027, we will open the Smith Family Center for the Performing Arts, a new performing arts center featuring four venues including the dedicated 450-seat Eliza P. Culverhouse Dance Theatre. Creative research opportunities on campus include choreographing for the pre-professional company Alabama Repertory Dance Theatre, contributing other departmental productions, and collaborative, interdisciplinary arts research opportunities through CARI, the Collaborative Arts Research Initiative, among others.
Additional responsibilities include student recruitment, mentorship of student dance concerts, and service to the department, college, and university. The faculty member will also advise and mentor students at both the graduate and undergraduate levels, contributing to their artistic, academic, and professional development throughout their time in the program.
Minimum Qualifications
Master of Fine Arts or PhD in Dance or related field. Record of successful teaching at the college and/or university level. Candidates should demonstrate a clear commitment to inclusive pedagogical approaches and a record of work using various and collaborative perspectives. Good communication and organizational skills are imperative.
Preferred Qualifications
3-5 years of university teaching experience and evidence of potential to impact the field through creative activity and research.

This position begins on August 16, 2027. To apply, go to careers.ua.edu/jobs/search/AS. Review will begin November 15 and remain open until filled. The University of Alabama Honors College is hiring a full-time Teaching Assistant Professors of Honors in an open specialty. Candidates should be innovative teacher-scholars who work across disciplines and support the College’s Honors Forward strategic plan. This initiative emphasizes small classes, individualized faculty interaction, first-year experiences, experiential and community-engaged learning, and research or creative projects.
Detailed Position Information
The University of Alabama Honors College, ranked as one of the top 10 honors colleges in the nation, invites applications for a faculty positions at the rank of assistant professor of Honors with open specialty. This is full-time appointments at the level of Teaching Assistant Professor (non-tenured, renewable contract). They will be expected to teach a variety of honors classes and will have opportunities to develop and teach seminar classes based on their area of expertise.
Guided by a newly implemented strategic plan, Honors Forward, the College seeks an innovative teacher-scholar with experience working across, between, and especially beyond disciplinary boundaries. Honors Forward encapsulates the College’s mission to cultivate students who are exceptional thinkers, citizens, and leaders. With an emphasis on smaller classes and one-on-one interactions with faculty, a first-year experience, experiential and community-engaged learning, and research/creative activity that culminates in a signature project, Honors Forward is designed to help students chart their own path to academic excellence. This faculty search is one of several hiring initiatives for the College, designed to expand resources and enhance the Honors experience for the College’s 7,000+ students.
The initial contract is three years, with review in the third year; rank promotion is possible. The normal teaching load is 12 credits per semester, with expectations for scholarship, committee service, and contributions to the overall academic and co-curricular life of the college. Scholarship may be in the areas of engagement, teaching and learning, and/or the applicant’s disciplinary area, including but not limited to public scholarship, innovative methodological/pedagogical approaches, peer-reviewed journal articles, books, book chapters, creative work, and conference presentations. While lab space and start-up packages are unavailable, successful candidates will receive other forms of support for research, teaching, and professional development.
Minimum Qualifications
We seek candidates who can contribute to strengthening our range of interdisciplinarity, especially social science, business, and STEAM-oriented course offerings. Applicants must also be innovative teachers able to offer courses in our transdisciplinary honors curriculum. Minimum qualifications include (1) an earned doctorate or other terminal degree appropriate to their discipline and (2) teaching experience at the college/university level. The degree must be completed by the start of the appointment.
Preferred Qualifications
Honors faculty are expected to have the skills and techniques necessary to manage highly collaborative, student-centered learning, and facilitate rigorous dialogue across differing perspectives, both in and out of the classroom. The successful candidates should be able to build creative, transdisciplinary syllabi, foster dialogue among students, and help individual students hone their skills as critical and creative thinkers, citizens, and leaders. We especially welcome applications from candidates with a background in any one or more of the following areas: first-year experience, experiential education, research/creative development, leadership studies, and transdisciplinary methods. In addition, we encourage candidates with experience mentoring students through extracurricular and/or co-curricular programming to apply.
Instructions and Required Materials for Application
Applicants should submit a cover letter expressing their interest in the specific position to which they are applying, teaching philosophy statement, CV, contact information for three academic references, and one to three recent teaching evaluations (if available). We will begin reviewing applications on October 23, 2026, and continue until the position is filled. Please direct questions to the search chair, Dr. Tara Mock, at tmock@ua.edu.

The Department of Art and Art History at The University of Alabama invites applications for a full-time, nine-month, tenure-track, Assistant Professor position in Graphic Design beginning fall semester 2027. The ideal candidate will demonstrate commitment to creative activity, teaching excellence, scholarship, and university and community service.
The successful candidate will teach courses at the undergraduate level and will serve on the graduate faculty. This position includes teaching and research responsibilities. The candidate's primary creative engagement should be within the graphic design field. While a broad range of skills is required, one or more of the following focus areas are sought, but not limited to: interactive design, motion design, print media, branding/identity, packaging design, graphic design history, and commercial/industry practices. The applicant should be well-versed in the theory of graphic design pertaining to contemporary practice, as both a fine art and applied discipline. The individual will work with other faculty members in the area on curriculum development, facilities management, coordination of instructors, and scheduling. Other responsibilities include: participation in departmental duties such as student advising and mentorship; program assessment and management; service to departmental, college, and university committees; and participation in community outreach and program recruitment.
Importantly, the candidate should demonstrate an ability to conduct a sustained program of creative research and production. An established record of creative activities, awards, and/or industry recognition that demonstrates a high level of professional engagement with contemporary practice is essential.
The Department of Art and Art History offers the BA and MA degrees in Art History and the BA, BFA, MA, and MFA degrees in Studio Art, and the BFA in Graphic Design. Important resources include the Sarah Moody Gallery of Art, the Sella-Granata Art Gallery, the Paul R. Jones
Collection of American Art, and the UA Gallery at the Dinah Washington Cultural Arts Center. The University of Alabama, the state's flagship public research university, is located in Tuscaloosa, about 50 miles southwest of Birmingham. UA's enrollment is diverse, drawing from the state of Alabama, the Southeast region, and the nation, and increasingly from around the world. These include the Barna Theatre, the Dinah Washington Cultural Arts Center, the Tuscaloosa Amphitheatre, as well as many galleries both on campus and off. Across the Black Warrior River, Northport is home to the Kentuck Arts and Crafts Center. Each year, the Kentuck Arts Festival brings together over 270 nationally and internationally acclaimed folk artists. Throughout the year there are many festivals and events in the city which make Tuscaloosa a culturally vibrant location to live. Additionally, Tuscaloosa is in the middle of a busy interstate corridor, close to Birmingham, Nashville, New Orleans, and Atlanta.

Georgia Tech is a top-ranked public research university situated in the heart of Atlanta, a vibrant city with great economic and cultural strengths. The Institute is a member of the University System of Georgia, the Georgia Research Alliance, and the Association of American Universities. Job Summary
The Jimmy and Rosalynn Carter School of Public Policy (https://spp.gatech.edu) at the Georgia Institute of Technology invites applications for a tenure-track assistant professor position. We seek a philosopher specializing in the philosophy of science and technology, political philosophy, practical ethics, or social epistemology, whose research and teaching addresses the ethical, legal, social, or policy implications of artificial intelligence (AI) and related technologies.
We welcome candidates with an appreciation of the historical development of AI and related technologies as well as those with strong perspectives on the future development of this technology. The successful candidate will be prepared to teach AI Ethics and Policy to Georgia Tech undergraduate and graduate students in a wide range of disciplines and to develop new courses to expand the Carter School's curricular offerings in this area. They will also be expected to develop a nationally recognized research program and contribute to teaching and mentoring at the undergraduate and graduate levels. We are especially interested in candidates whose research and teaching interests relate to and could contribute to one or more of the School's strengths in energy and environmental policy, health policy, information and communications (ICT) policy, science and technology policy, and social and urban policy.
Required Qualifications
An earned doctorate is required by the start of the appointment.
Required Documents to Attach
Applicants should submit:
A cover letter
Curriculum vitae
Up to three publications
A research statement, including descriptions of future research plans
A teaching statement, including descriptions of teaching interests
Contact information for three academic references
Apply Before Date
The committee will begin reviewing applications on October 26, 2026 and applicants are encouraged to apply by this date for optimal consideration; however, the search will continue until the position is filled.
Contact Information Please contact Dr. Justin B. Biddle for additional information at justin.biddle@pubpolicy.gatech.edu

Atlanta, Georgia
Department Information
About the School of Office of Information Technology at the Georgia Institute of Technology
Located in the heart of vibrant Atlanta, Georgia, the Partnership for an Advanced Computing Environment (PACE) team defines and manages centralized research computing services at the Georgia Institute of Technology. We facilitate research efforts and foster strategic partnerships to provide Georgia Tech researchers with an unrivaled advantage, empowering them to lead their disciplines for the advancement of science and society across the globe. In addition to high-performance computing, we incorporate emerging cloud, network, data analytics, and storage technologies. Our growing team directly supports faculty, students, and other researchers resulting in a dynamic environment filled with intellectual stimulation and continuous innovation.
Job Summary
The OIT (Office of Information Technology) department at the Georgia Institute of Technology in Atlanta, Georgia, invites applications for the Partnership for Advanced Computing Environment (PACE). Applications will be considered at all ranks. The Partnership for Advanced Computing Environment (PACE) seeks a skilled junior or mid-career Research Scientist to join us. The successful candidate will join the Research Software Engineer (RSE) team in PACE, in collaboration with other teams, and play a key role in building and operating an AI-centric platform, facilitating AI workflow porting on the PACE environment, and developing internal tools to enhance the efficient operation and researchers' scientific/AI workflow. This role will work closely with the Platform and Architecture (Platform) and Cyberinfrastructure (CI) Teams to support GT faculty on research projects and evaluate underlying technologies.
This role requires strong software engineering expertise, system integration experience, excellent communication skills, and the ability to bring innovative solutions to researchers' projects and implement them into deliverables.
Georgia Institute of Technology Research Computing PACE (The Partnership for Advanced Computing Environment) Center is pleased to announce an exciting career opportunity as a Research Software Engineer focused on building and operating AI-centric platforms. This role emphasizes scalable, secure, multi-tenant infrastructure for AI/ML workloads (e.g. JupyterHub, MLflow) supporting everything from interactive development to model training, tracking, and deployment on scalable compute backends (HPC cluster). This position will also serve as a consulting role, collaborating with domain scientists to develop scientific/AI workflows on the PACE system.
This role requires software engineering expertise, system integration experience, excellent communication skills, and the ability to bring innovative solutions to researchers' projects and implement them as deliverables. This role enables reliable, secure, and efficient use of PACE resources for AI/ML workloads by delivering shared platforms, reference workflows, and automation that improve researcher productivity, reproducibility, and operational stability at scale.
Responsibilities
AI-centric Platform Engineering: Build and operate shared AI-centric platforms (e.g., JupyterHub, MLflow) and associated services to enable secure, multi-tenant AI environments for researchers. Integrate identity management, resource quotas, and policy controls; support experiment tracking and reproducibility.
Reliability & Performance: Monitor and improve performance, scalability, and stability of AI services in production. Establish service-level objectives (SLOs) where appropriate; tune systems for GPU utilization, throughput, and latency; and help diagnose workload bottlenecks across compute, storage, and networking.
MLOps & Deployment Enablement: Enable repeatable workflows for training, evaluation, artifact management, and (when applicable) model serving. Define reference patterns for packaging (containers), configuration, and environment management to support reproducible research and reliable rollout of services.
Maintain the user-facing scientific and engineering software stack, including AI, data analytics, and modelling/simulation applications: Develop and optimize the central software stack on the target architecture using containers and/or the automatic software building tool e.g. Spack, EasyBuild.
Documentation & Operational Readiness: Produce clear technical documentation, runbooks, and architecture notes. Communicate progress, risks, and tradeoffs to both technical and non-technical stakeholders; contribute to operational processes.
Stay abreast of Technical Trends: Acquire knowledge through independent study, consultation of textbooks and research papers, and engagement with online training resources relevant to required problem domains.
Work in partnership with other GT Colleges IT groups to support the deployment of scientific/AI applications and workflows for researchers on PACE systems
Closely work with other internal PACE units, including the Platform and Architecture (Platform), Cyberinfrastructure(CI), and Research Computing Facilitation (RCF) Teams, to address researchers needs
Author and publish scientific papers, reports, and presentations to communicate research results and findings to internal and external audiences
Any other task assigned by the supervisor
Required Qualifications
This position vacancy is an open rank announcement. Final job offer will be dependent on candidate qualifications in alignment with Research Faculty ranks as outlined in section 3.2.1 of the Georgia Tech Faculty Handbook (https://www.policylibrary.gatech.edu/faculty-handbook/3.2.1-research-faculty-hiring-and-promotion-guidelines)
Research Scientist I
Bachelors Degree in Computer Science, or related area
Research Scientist II
A Master's degree and three (3) years of relevant full-time experience after completion of that degree, or
A Master's degree and five (5) years of relevant full-time experience after completion of a Bachelor's degree, or
A Doctoral degree in Computer Science, or related area
Preferred Qualifications
The preferred candidate will have:
Master in computational science or related fields.
Excellent written and oral communication skills, with the ability to communicate complex engineering concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences
Proven ability to work independently and as part of a team, with a strong sense of initiative and drive for results
Proficiency in Python and shell scripting (e.g., Bash) for automation and tooling.
Experience with (Nvidia and/or AMD) GPUs and distributed concepts (CUDA stack basics, multi-GPU/multi-node computation) and debugging common performance/failure patterns.
Experience with profiling and troubleshooting tools (e.g., performance analyzers, debuggers) and basic observability concepts (metrics, logs, traces).
Experience with Linux-based compute environments. Familiarity with HPC concepts (schedulers, shared filesystems) and/or distributed AI training is a plus.
Familiarity with complex AI software tool chain building on Linux environment.
Additionally, they will have demonstrated experience in (one or more of the following areas:
Experience with containerization technologies (e.g., Docker, Apptainer, Podman)
Experience with data management, databases (SQL/NoSQL), and distributed systems; comfort designing and operating internal services and APIs.
Experience with AI/ML frameworks such as PyTorch, Ultralytics, and LangChain/LangGraph.
Experience with common AI/ML workflows such as training, fine-tuning, image detection/segmentation, retrieval-augmented generation, and/or agentic workflows.
Experience with inference backend e.g. vLLM, Ollama and Triton
Experience contributing to or supporting open-source software, including PR and code review.
Experience working in developing software for research applications
Experience in software development lifecycle.
Experience in writing and publishing research papers at conferences and journals.
Improving team processes through documentation, automation, and knowledge sharing.
Proposed Salary
Proposed Salary: $53,204 - $110,000. Commensurate with education and experience.
Required Documents to Attach
Applicants should submit the following:

Location: Atlanta, Georgia
Regular/Temporary: Regular
Full/Part Time: Full-Time
Job ID: 304246
About Us
Georgia Tech prides itself on its technological resources, collaborations, high-quality student body, and its commitment to building an outstanding and diverse community of learning, discovery, and creation. We strongly encourage applicants whose values align with our institutional values, as outlined in our strategic plan. These values include academic excellence, diversity of thought and experience, inquiry and innovation, collaboration and community, and ethical behavior and stewardship. Georgia Tech has policies to promote a healthy work-life balance and is aware that attracting faculty may require meeting the needs of two careers.
About Georgia Tech
Georgia Tech is a top-ranked public research university situated in the heart of Atlanta, a diverse and vibrant city with numerous economic and cultural strengths. The Institute serves more than 45,000 students through top-ranked undergraduate, graduate, and executive programs in engineering, computing, science, business, design, and liberal arts. Georgia Tech's faculty attracted more than $1.4 billion in research awards this past year in fields ranging from biomedical technology to artificial intelligence, energy, sustainability, semiconductors, neuroscience, and national security. Georgia Tech ranks among the nation's top 20 universities for research and development spending and No. 1 among institutions without a medical school.
Georgia Tech's Mission and Values
Georgia Tech's mission is to develop leaders who advance technology and improve the human condition. The Institute has nine key values that are foundational to everything we do:
1. Students are our top priority.
2. We strive for excellence.
3. We thrive on diversity.
4. We celebrate collaboration.
5. We champion innovation.
6. We safeguard freedom of inquiry and expression.
7. We nurture the wellbeing of our community.
8. We act ethically.
9. We are responsible stewards.
Over the next decade, Georgia Tech will become an example of inclusive innovation, a leading technological research university of unmatched scale, relentlessly committed to serving the public good; breaking new ground in addressing the biggest local, national, and global challenges and opportunities of our time; making technology broadly accessible; and developing exceptional, principled leaders from all backgrounds ready to produce novel ideas and create solutions with real human impact.
Location
Atlanta, GA
Department Information
The Institute for Matter and Systems is one of Georgia Tech's Interdisciplinary Research Institutes. IMS brings together researchers across fields and operates shared fabrication and characterization facilities with more than 250 instruments, including more than 23,000 square feet of cleanroom space. The facilities serve users from academia, industry, and government and are part of the NSF-funded National Nanotechnology Coordinated Infrastructure.
Job Summary
The Institute for Matter and Systems is seeking a Research Engineer to serve as a technical leader within its shared microelectronics research infrastructure. The position owns and advances research capabilities in semiconductor fabrication and process integration, advanced packaging and heterogeneous integration, and device and interconnect characterization.
The Research Engineer develops new processes and methods, ensures that IMS capabilities produce reliable and research-quality results, supports facility users, collaborates on challenging academic and externally sponsored research, and provides opportunities to pursue independent applied research in a highly dynamic academic environment. The role combines hands-on experimental work with technical leadership, user development, applied research, and responsibility for helping IMS determine where to build future capability.
Responsibilities
Own and Advance Research Capabilities
Serve as the technical authority for semiconductor fabrication and process integration, advanced packaging and heterogeneous integration, and device and interconnect characterization. Define validated methods, baseline processes, performance metrics, and reproducibility standards, and integrate tools into reliable workflows for semiconductor devices, MEMS, photonics, sensors, advanced materials, and wide-bandgap research.
Develop New Processes Methods and Technology Platforms
Lead experimental development beyond standard equipment recipes. Use feasibility studies and designed experiments to define technical limits and advance successful methods through characterization, qualification, documentation, and user deployment.
Areas may include:
Semiconductor fabrication and process integration. Develop integrated process flows using photolithography, direct-write lithography, RIE, ICP, DRIE, PVD, CVD, ALD, thermal and wet processing, and metallization.
Advanced packaging and heterogeneous integration. Develop workflows for redistribution layers, electroplating, TSV/TGV integration, wafer bonding, die attach, lamination, metallization, wafer-level processing, and heterogeneous integration.
Device interconnect and package characterization. Develop electrical testing and validation methods using probe stations and parameter analyzers, including interconnect and package characterization, reliability assessment, and failure analysis.
Pursue Collaborative or Independent Research
Collaborate with Georgia Tech faculty, students, startups, industry, government laboratories, and sponsored research teams to translate research questions and device requirements into executable experiments. Select methods, integrate techniques, troubleshoot failures, interpret results, and contribute to proposals, reviews, reports, presentations, and publications. Pursue independently funded research aligned with IMS priorities.
Steward Scientific and Technical Performance
Maintain the scientific integrity, readiness, and performance of assigned capabilities. Lead acceptance, qualification, calibration, baseline monitoring, and root-cause troubleshooting. Define requirements for maintenance, repairs, upgrades, and process changes, coordinating with IMS staff, vendors, service engineers, and research partners as needed.
Train, Mentor and Sustain Institutional Knowledge
Train and qualify students, researchers, staff, and internal and external users in experimental design, process integration, measurement, troubleshooting, and reproducible use of shared infrastructure. Maintain standard operating procedures, recipes, training materials, baseline data, best practices, and troubleshooting guidance so institutional knowledge remains accurate and transferable.
Shape Future IMS Technical Direction
Identify emerging needs and technology trends to guide IMS capability roadmaps and investments. Recommend and commission new equipment, methods, and platforms; support proposals and partnerships; and build faculty and external collaborations. Initiate applied research aligned with IMS priorities in fabrication, packaging, integration, and characterization
Required Qualifications
This position vacancy is an open rank announcement. Final job offer will be dependent on candidate qualifications in alignment with Research Faculty ranks as outlined in section 3.2.1 of the Georgia Tech Faculty Handbook (https://www.policylibrary.gatech.edu/faculty-handbook/3.2.1-research-faculty-hiring-and-promotion=-guidelines)
Research Engineer I
Bachelor's Degree in engineering/science or related field.
Research Engineer II
A master's degree in science, engineering or related area, and three (3) years of relevant full-time experience after completion of that degree, or
A master's degree in science, engineering or related area, and five (5) years of relevant full-time experience after completion of a bachelor's degree, or
A Doctoral degree
Senior Research Engineer
A Master's degree and seven (7) years of relevant full-time experience after completion of that degree, or
A Master's degree and nine (9) years of relevant full-time experience after completion of a Bachelor's degree, or
A Doctoral degree and four (4) years of relevant full-time experience after completion of a Bachelor's degree.
Preferred Qualifications
Significant hands-on experience in semiconductor fabrication, micro/nanofabrication, or semiconductor process integration.
Demonstrated experience in experimental research, process development, experimental design, data analysis, and technical problem-solving.
Experience operating in cleanroom or advanced semiconductor fabrication environments.
Ability to work collaboratively with faculty, graduate researchers, technical staff, and external research partners.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to effectively engage diverse technical users and multidisciplinary research teams.
Research experience in semiconductor devices, MEMS, photonics, sensors, advanced materials, wide-bandgap semiconductors, or related micro/nanotechnology areas.
Experience developing fabrication processes using lithography, plasma etching, thin-film deposition, metallization, thermal processing, or wafer-level process integration.
Experience in advanced packaging, wafer-level packaging, electroplating, RDL, TSV/TGV processing, wafer bonding, or heterogeneous integration.
Experience in semiconductor device electrical characterization, packaging validation, reliability testing, or failure analysis.
Experience independently developing new experimental methodologies, research capabilities, or technology platforms.
Experience contributing to multidisciplinary research projects, sponsored research programs, technical publications, conference presentations, or research proposals.
Experience working in shared research facilities, university core laboratories, national laboratories, or semiconductor industry R&D environments.
Demonstrated ability to independently drive technical projects while collaborating effectively within multidisciplinary research teams.
Required Documents to Attach
Please provide three professional references.

About Us
Middle Georgia State University (MGA), a multi-campus, baccalaureate and graduate degree-granting public institution, is the most affordable public state university in Georgia. MGA has five campuses-Macon, Cochran, Dublin, Eastman, and Warner Robins, all located in central Georgia-and global outreach through its fully-online campus. Its enrollment of 8,400 students is largely comprised of students from most of Georgia's 159 counties. The University has six academic schools, including Georgia's flagship aviation program, that support its mission to educate and graduate inspired, lifelong learners whose scholarship and careers enhance the state.

The Department of Information Technology has programs that prepare students to solve problems and apply new technologies within an increasingly interconnected and changing global environment. They emphasize career success through lifelong learning and professional development at all levels of the curriculum. The Department offers a Bachelor of Science (BSIT), Master of Science (MSIT), and Doctor of Science (DScIT) in Information Technology. Middle Georgia State¿s Bachelor of Science in Information Technology program is accredited by ABET. MGA is also designed as a National Center of Academic Excellence in Cyber Defense Education (CAE-CDE) by the National Security Agency.

The Department of Information Technology within the School of Computing at Middle Georgia State University is seeking candidates for an Assistant Professor of Information Technology. This is a ten-month tenure track which involves teaching, scholarship, and service.
Responsibilities
Teaching responsibilities will be at the undergraduate and graduate level (Master and Doctoral) programs. Candidates should be able to teach a variety of IT cores and elective courses within the IT program (http://www.mga.edu/it). Teaching responsibilities may include day and/or evening classes. Travel between campuses (Cochran, Dublin, Macon and Warner Robins) will be required. Online teaching experience is required. In addition to teaching, job requirements include service to the institution; an active research and scholarly activities leading to publication in peer-reviewed journals.

jobs.title: Biology Faculty
jobs.description:
Job Details
SUMMARY
South Texas College is a comprehensive institution, which places primary emphasis on excellence in classroom instruction. Faculty members are expected to demonstrate and maintain competence in each of the following areas throughout their employment at the College.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES include the following. Other duties may be assigned.
1. Mastery of Subject Matter:
Demonstrates a thorough and accurate knowledge of the field or discipline
Possesses appropriate educational/professional credentials to teach in field or discipline
Attempts to connect subject matter with related fields
Maintains currency in subject matter through professional development
2. Teaching Performance:
Plans and organizes instruction in ways which maximize student learning
Effectively employs teaching and learning strategies that promote student engagement
Modifies instructional methods and strategies to meet students' needs
Effectively employs available instructional technology when appropriate
Encourages the development of communication skills and higher order thinking skills through appropriate assignments
Effectively communicates subject matter content to student
Contributes to the selection and development of instructional materials
3. Evaluation of Student Learning:
Participates in the development, implementation, and assessment of departmental student learning outcomes
Develops and uses evaluation methods, which fairly measures student progress toward outcomes
Evaluates and expeditiously returns student work to promote maximum learning
Maintains accurate records of student progress
Submits final grade rosters and supporting documents according to established deadlines
4. Support of College Policies and Procedures:
Maintains familiarity with and adheres to College Policies and Procedures
Fulfills requirements of Faculty as set forth in the letter of employment
Maintains regular office hours to ensure accessibility to students and colleagues
Prepares, distributes, and submits syllabi and approved course outlines for all assigned sections in accordance with program, division and College procedures
Prepares and submits Financial Aid Attendance Rosters, Census Rosters, Progress Reports and Learning Outcome Data, by the respective deadlines each semester
Assures confidentiality
5. Participation in College, Division, and Program Activities:
Serves on College, divisional, and program committees, teams and task forces as assigned.
Attends meetings and events as required by College administration.
Participates in professional activities which contribute to the educational goals of the College and its constituents
Responds in a timely fashion to information requests from College and division administrators and program chairs
Fosters and maintains effective working relationships with students, colleagues, and supervisors
Assists the chair in developing, reviewing, and revising curriculum
6. Contribution to the Growth and Enhancement of College Mission and Programs:
Participates in student advising
Maintains familiarity with College goals, mission, and long-range plans
Contributes to planning and development processes through appropriate channels
Performs professional responsibilities in accordance with pertinent goals, mission, and plans of College, division, and program
Facilitates recruitment and retention of students
7. Performs other duties as assigned
QUALIFICATIONS
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
1. Must possess appropriate academic preparation
2. Must be able to provide official transcripts and/if transcripts are earned from a foreign teaching institution, then must be able to provide an evaluation indicating that this education is equivalent to or beyond the qualifications required This evaluation must be from an approved evaluation service
3. Excellent communication skills, both oral and written; excellent interpersonal skills
4. Excellent organizational skills
5. Commitment to the community college philosophy of education
EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE
Applicant must meet the STC credential requirements as per Board Policy DBA - Employment Requirements and Restrictions: Credentials and Records located at https://pol.tasb.org/PolicyOnline/PolicyDetails?key=632&code=DBA#localTabContent
Doctorate or Master's degree in Biology or a related field from a regionally accredited institution, doctorate (Ph.D.) preferred;
or a Doctorate or Master's degree with a minimum of 18 graduate semester hours in the Biology from a regionally accredited institution.
Credentials must meet requirements of 18 graduate hours in discipline from a regionally accredited institution.
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
Applicant should have a minimum of two years recent teaching experience at college/university level
Two or more years of recent prior Microbiology and/or Anatomy and Physiology teaching experience
Coursework and/or teaching experience sufficient to teach Microbiology and/or Human Anatomy and Physiology
Coursework and/or teaching experience sufficient to also teach other Biology courses in our curriculum
Experience using a variety of teaching technologies and methodologies
Demonstrated current and ongoing professional growth
Experience teaching diverse student population
Experience using Learning Management System (Blackboard)
Online Teaching experiences

About UofSC
From the Upstate to the Lowcountry, the University of South Carolina system is transforming the lives of South Carolinians through the impact of our eight institutions and 20 locations throughout the state.
