In addition, our Palmetto College campuses in Salkehatchie, Union, Lancaster and Sumter enable students to earn associate or bachelor's degrees through a combination of in-person, online or blended learning. All of our system institutions place strong emphasis on service — helping to build healthier, more educated communities in South Carolina and beyond.
Advertised Job Summary
The Department of Geography in the McCausland College of Arts and Sciences at the University of South Carolina invites applications for a full-time, nine-month tenure track faculty position at the rank of Assistant Professor in GIScience, with an anticipated start date of August 16, 2027.
We seek an emerging scholar whose research and teaching engage the frontiers of GIScienceand cutting-edge geospatial technologies. Areas of interest that advance GIScience concepts, theories and/or methods include, but are not limited to, GIS modeling, digital cartography, geo-visualization, spatial statistics, GeoAI and Geospatial Intelligence, with potential topical applications in environmental hazards, human-environment interactions, sustainable development, spatial inequities, health, energy, urban planning and related fields. The successful candidate will be expected to continue the department's strong tradition of leadership in the field, contribute to a collaborative research environment, and foster partnerships across campus and beyond. We are interested in a candidate who wishes to play a leading role in the future of GIScience.
Teaching responsibilities will include supporting and advancing fundamental GIS courses at the undergraduate and graduate levels, supporting the Geospatial Intelligence (GEOINT) certificate, as well as developing new courses in the candidate's area of expertise. The successful candidate will teach four courses per academic year (two per semester) and is expected to participate in graduate student recruitment and supervision.
The Department currently comprises nineteen tenured/tenure-track faculty and one full-time instructor. Faculty research interests span resource politics, environmental hazards, human rights, coastal geomorphology, energy geographies, health, GIS and remote sensing, biogeography, migration, and climate change, with collaborations across the college, university, and beyond. In addition, the Department faculty lead several institutes and centers including the Hazards, Vulnerability and Resilience Institute (HVRI), Walker Institute of International and Area Studies, and the Center for GIScience and Geospatial Big Data. The Department offers PhD, MS, MA, BS, and BA degrees. For more information about the Department of Geography, please visit https://sc.edu/study/colleges_schools/artsandsciences/geography.

R0011115
Tampa

Position Details
The University of Tampa Department of Music seeks a qualified candidate for a tenure-track position as Assistant Professor of Voice/Musical Theatre to join its robust voice program, which serves approximately 100 voice majors. We seek a faculty member with strong professional expertise in both teaching and performance and a genuine commitment to mentoring aspiring singers and maintaining a high-quality vocal program within a collaborative and professionally rigorous academic environment. The successful candidate will also be expected to participate in recruitment and outreach activities both on and off campus and to maintain an active scholarly and creative agenda.
The primary responsibilities of this position are to teach musical theatre and classical voice majors and minors, with a strong foundation in healthy vocal development and vocal pedagogy, and to direct a musical theatre ensemble. We are committed to developing well-rounded artists who graduate ready to thrive professionally in any area of the performing arts or to advance toward a career in academia.
The Music Department offers BA, BM, and BME degrees, and the Theatre and Dance Department offers a BFA degree in Musical Theater; both departments are housed in the College of Arts and Letters. The vocal program at The University of Tampa is thriving, and our students have opportunities to perform in Musical Theatre and Opera Scenes productions, as well as the Master Series and choirs, in our state-of-the-art facilities, including Falk Theatre, Gordon Theatre in the Ferman Center for the Arts, Sykes Chapel, and other performance venues in historic Plant Hall.
The University delivers challenging and high-quality educational experiences to a diverse group of learners. The University has a strong core curriculum rooted in the liberal arts, an enduring commitment to internationalization that has garnered the Senator Paul Simon Award, and a practical, experiential approach to learning. The University offers more than 200 areas of study, including majors in our colleges of Arts and Letters, Business, Natural and Health Sciences and Social Sciences, Math and Education and 18 master's programs, and 3 professional doctoral programs.
The College of Arts and Letters (CAL) is a place where theory meets practice and expression meets experience. Guided by faculty who are talented artists and distinguished scholars, students come to CAL to study everything from fleeting snaps to enduring works of classic literature. The College is home to eight collaborative and innovative academic departments: Art and Design, Communication, English and Writing, Film, Animation and New Media, Languages and Linguistics, Music, Philosophy and Religion, and Theatre and Dance.
As a community of scholars and artists, the College of Arts and Letters engage in cutting-edge creative work, technological innovation, critical scholarly practice, and dialogue with diverse communities. Faculty and students across CAL work with emerging technologies in cutting-edge facilities including the stunning new Ferman Center for the Arts, the Bailey Art Studios and FabLAB, the historic Falk Theatre, the Sykes Chapel and Center for Faith and Values, and the Cass media production facilities.

-Mezzo-sopranos, Tenors, Baritones, and Basses are especially encouraged to apply

-Evidence of and/or commitment to outreach and recruitment

jobs.title: Open Rank Tenure or Clinical Faculty - Large Animal & Ambulatory Services
jobs.description:
Job Details
Open Rank Tenure or Clinical Faculty - Large Animal & Ambulatory Services
Clemson University: Harvey S. Peeler Jr. College of Veterinary Medicine
Location: CVM - COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE HUB(001184) BLDG001184
Open Date: Jul 21, 2026
Description
The new Clemson University Harvey S. Peeler Jr. College of Veterinary Medicine (CVM) is seeking applicants for a full-time faculty position to help establish the new Clemson CVM Large Animal and Ambulatory Service. The primary responsibilities of this position are focused on clinical service, teaching, and research. Academic rank would be commensurate with experience. Wellness and faculty support are important to Clemson University; faculty benefits can be found here.Part of the mission of the Clemson CVM is to promote animal and human health in the state of SC through the education of the next generation of veterinary clinicians and scientists with an emphasis on large animals (including cattle, sheep, goats, and horses), general practice and population medicine. The position is designed for an individual committed to this mission by providing large animal clinical service, teaching, and research in both the clinical and pre-clinical curriculum of the developing Clemson DVM program. This individual will work with students, other faculty, staff, and large animal clients in local communities. The service will have four new fully equipped trucks based out of a dedicated ambulatory services building on the new Clemson CVM Campus, enabling faculty members to deliver an exceptional client and patient experience while educating students in this core student-led ambulatory service rotation. The ambulatory service building will maintain a full complement of diagnostic analyzers, and each fully equipped, state-of-the-art ambulatory truck will have a dedicated ultrasound and access to patient-side bloodwork analyzers, flexible endoscopy, mobile hoof trimming and squeeze chutes, and digital radiography. Clinical skills laboratories with low and high-fidelity large animal simulation models and live animal teaching facilities on site at the Lamaster Dairy and Clemson Equine Unit will support additional educational experiences for clinical rotations. The clinical service will have referral relationships with several area referral hospitals, as a referral hospital facility is not currently planned for the Clemson CVM Campus. Clemson CVM specialists are available for case consultation in areas such as pathology, large animal internal medicine, preventive medicine, and equine surgery. Support from the Clemson University State Diagnostic Laboratory in Columbia, SC will help ambulatory clinicians engage with pathologists for clinical diagnostic needs. Clemson CVM faculty and staff experts in teaching and learning will help the successful candidate in developing curriculum for the ambulatory clinical rotation, providing student feedback, and assessing students. Department and faculty expertise will provide support for candidates who wish to complete an ABVP or ACVPM certificate. Clinical assignments will include after-hours emergency duty, shared by the four full-time members of the ambulatory service team. Emergency case load will consist of mixed large animal/production species including equine. Phone consultation and in person support via Clemson faculty and colleagues for daytime and after-hours cases are available and encouraged to help successful applicants build comfort with multiple species. Individual and collaborative research is also encouraged, with mentorship and support available. The first three years of the position will be focused on building the ambulatory practice. Engaging with extension agents across the state and developing relationships with local and regional producers and producer groups will enable the practice to accept fourth year Clemson veterinary students in 2029. Collaborations with Clemson Extension and Clemson School of Nursing-Rural Health will also be part of the planned relationship building, as engagement with regional producers and rural communities will enhance the educational experience for fourth year students. Fourth year students from regional veterinary schools will be accepted for elective rotations prior to 2029. Species PercentagesAs this is a new clinical service, case load numbers have not yet been generated. Anderson County, where the CVM is located, leads the state in cattle and sheep numbers and ranks second in horse numbers. Nearby counties of Oconee, Laurens, Saluda, and Abbeville are also strong in animal agriculture sectors, particularly in cattle, small ruminants, horses, and poultry. The ambulatory service will support backyard poultry and swine operations only, with a likely focus on 4-H animals and individual or small herd care. One of the four ambulatory trucks is designated as a regional herd health truck, intended to seek out larger regional farms for herd health management educational experiences, working with local veterinarians and extension agents to promote producer efficiency, food quality, and food safety within the state of South Carolina. Overview of the Position Reporting to the Department Chair academically and the Head of Veterinary Services for clinical service, the faculty member will work as part of a dynamic team to: • Establish and maintain a large animal clientele in the upstate of SC and surrounding areas; • Provide routine and emergency care to animals in the Clemson Piedmont Research and Education Center facilities, including dairy, beef, sheep, horses, and poultry species. • Engage with the Clemson Farm managers in each of the units to support best practices in preventative health care for the relevant species; • Establish best practices and standards of care for the service; • Build the inventory and equipment needed to establish a successful practice; • Expand education and outreach programs for producers and producer groups to ensure a productive, safe and healthy livestock and poultry industry; • Provide comprehensive routine and emergency care to large animal patients (including cattle, sheep, goats, and horses) in a field setting; • Lead and participate in curriculum design and development for the student-led ambulatory rotation; • Engage in teaching and assessment of clinical skills and professional development of students across all years of the DVM curriculum; • Serve on CVM and campus committees as appointed or elected; and • Develop and participate in a collaborative research program. Additionally, the faculty member must have the ability to: • Work independently and collaboratively as part of a team; • Demonstrate exemplary verbal and written communication skills, with exceptional organizational skills and attention to detail; • Provide the #1 experiential learning experience for Clemson CVM students; • Prioritize and manage multiple tasks, meet deadlines, and function independently with limited supervision and guidance; • Work in partnership with faculty and staff across multiple disciplines and functions across the college and university; • Participate in research and scholarship initiatives designed to improve educational and professional outcomes; • Commit to ongoing professional development and staying current with advancements in veterinary medicine; • Demonstrate a commitment to the core values of Clemson University Overview of Clemson and the CVM Located in South Carolina's beautiful and fast-growing Upstate, Clemson University is the land-grant university of South Carolina and ranks among the country's top 50 national public universities in the U.S. News & World Report. The University has nearly 23,400 students (including nearly 18,600 undergraduates) who can select from 80 undergraduate and 110 graduate degree programs. Clemson employs over 1,150 full-time faculty and has an annual budget expenditure of over $900M. Clemson University maintains its status as an R1 Carnegie Research Institution while maintaining a strong focus on undergraduate education. The CVM has received a letter of reasonable assurance from the AVMA-Council on Education to offer the Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM) degree and will admit the first class of 80 students in 2026. The CVM plans to utilize a semi-distributive model of clinical training for students. Its brand-new, state-of-the-art campus will reside in Pendleton, SC, near the T. Ed Garrison Arena, will house research and teaching labs, and utilize both ambulatory services as well as teaching sites at the Clemson University Equine Center, Lamaster Dairy Cattle Center, and other locations for education in the field. In 2023, the Board of Trustees approved Clemson Elevate, the university's new strategic plan. The CVM was also named as a strategic priority for the university, and the CVM ambulatory service will provide many areas of alignment: Excellent experiential learning experiences for Clemson CVM students Collaborative partnership opportunities for impactful research in rural animal agriculture Improvements in quality, quantity and safety of food; enhance competitiveness of South Carolina food producers Expansion of education and outreach programs to ensure a productive, safe, and healthy livestock and poultry industry Impacts on the health and lives of rural communities and animals in South Carolina through service to the community
Qualifications
DVM or equivalent
Three to five years of relevant experience in multispecies large animal or rural ambulabory practice
Experience in herd health management, specifically development of preventive programs in line with different types of producer goals and development of programs aligned with individual animal care goals for small hobby farms or food animal species kept as companion animals.
Valid veterinary licensure or the ability to obtain a license for SC, GA, and NC.
Preferred qualifications include:
Ability to provide veterinary services with multiple species.
Experience in formal veterinary education, veterinary extern education, or producer education
Board certification or interest in pursuing board certification, including ABVP and ACVPM credentials

jobs.title: ASSISTANT PROFESSOR, ENVIRONMENTAL ENGINEERING
jobs.description:
Job Details
ASSISTANT PROFESSOR, ENVIRONMENTAL ENGINEERING
Job Description Summary, Duties and Responsibilities, Required Qualifications and Preferred Qualifications
Search will be open until filled. First consideration will be given to applications received by 11/15/2026. Applications received after 11/15/2026 may be reviewed depending on search progress and needs but are not guaranteed full consideration.
________________________________________________________________________________________________________
URI is Rhode Island's flagship public research university. In 2025, URI achieved Carnegie R1 status, placing it among the nation's highest research activity universities. URI was also ranked the No. 1 public university in New England by The Wall Street Journal/College Pulse. The Kingston campus is located near Narragansett Bay and the Atlantic coast, with access to Providence, Boston, New York, and the coastal communities of southern Rhode Island. Rhode Island is also an EPSCoR-eligible jurisdiction, providing faculty with access to targeted federal funding opportunities that support research capacity, collaboration, and innovation.
________________________________________________________________________________________________________
The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering at the University of Rhode Island invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the assistant professor level in environmental engineering. The anticipated start date is August 2027.
We seek an outstanding scholar and educator with the potential to build a nationally prominent, externally funded research program. This is a broad search, and candidates from all areas of environmental engineering are encouraged to apply.
The department is interested in reviewing applications from candidates whose work touches on air pollution, indoor air quality, links between climate and air quality, atmospheric chemistry, and ocean-atmosphere interactions; however, candidates from all areas of environmental engineering are encouraged to apply and will receive full consideration.
The successful candidate will contribute to the growth of environmental engineering research at URI and help advance the launch and long-term success of URI's new Bachelor of Science degree program in Environmental Engineering.
THE POSITION IS IN-PERSON
POSITION SUMMARY:
The successful candidate will be expected to develop a nationally recognized and externally funded research program; publish high-impact scholarship; teach undergraduate and graduate courses; mentor undergraduate and graduate students; contribute to the new BS Environmental Engineering curriculum; and participate in service to the department, college, university, profession, and broader community.
Applicants are expected to hold a terminal degree in environmental engineering, civil engineering, chemical engineering, environmental health engineering, or a closely related field by the time of appointment. Required qualifications include evidence of potential for excellence in research and teaching; a strong record of scholarly activity appropriate to career stage; effective written and oral communication skills; and the ability to work effectively with students, faculty, staff, and external partners. Preferred qualifications include evidence of potential for external research funding; experience advising or mentoring students; ability to teach core undergraduate or graduate environmental engineering courses; interest in program development; and Professional Engineering licensure or the ability to pursue licensure.
The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering is housed within URI's College of Engineering and is entering an exciting period of growth. The department offers undergraduate and graduate programs in civil and environmental engineering and is launching a new BS degree in Environmental Engineering. The successful candidate will join URI at a pivotal moment, with opportunities to help shape a new undergraduate degree program while expanding the department's research impact in environmental engineering.
Faculty and students in the College of Engineering work in the Fascitelli Center for Advanced Engineering (FCAE), a 190,000-square-foot facility designed to support interdisciplinary engineering research and education. Research in the facility is organized around themes that include clean water, sensors and instrumentation, alternative energy, advanced materials, robotics, biomedical technology, and nanotechnology. FCAE also houses the Shimadzu Analytical Core, the RI Water Resources Center, and the RI Consortium for Nanoscience and Nanotechnology.
________________________________________________________________________________________________________
KEY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
• Develop a nationally recognized, externally funded research program in
environmentalengineering.
• Publish high-impact scholarship.
• Teach undergraduate and graduate courses.
• Mentor undergraduate, M.S., and Ph.D. students.
• Contribute to the development and success of the B.S. in Environmental
Engineeringcurriculum.
• Participate in service to the department, college, university, profession, and broadercommunity.
OTHER DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
Perform other duties as required.
LICENSES, TOOLS, AND EQUIPMENT:
Personal computers, printers, word processing, database management,
and spreadsheet software.
ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS:
This position is not substantially exposed to adverse environmental conditions.
________________________________________________________________________________________________________
QUALIFICATIONS
REQUIRED:
1. A terminal degree in environmental engineering, civil engineering, chemical engineering, environmental health engineering, or a closely related field by the time of appointment.
2. Evidence of potential for excellence in research and teaching.
3. A strong record of scholarly activity appropriate to the candidate's career stage.
4. Effective written and oral communication skills.
5. Ability to work effectively with students, faculty, staff, and external partners.
PREFERRED:
1. Evidence of potential to secure external research funding.
2. Experience advising or mentoring students.
3. Ability to teach core undergraduate and/or graduate environmental engineering courses.
4. Interest in Environmental Engineering B.S. degree program development.
5. Professional Engineering licensure or the ability to pursue licensure.
________________________________________________________________________________________________________

jobs.description:
Job Details
Job Title: Assistant Professor or Associate Professor of Public History
Location: Kennesaw, Georgia
Regular/Temporary: Regular
Full/Part Time: Full-Time
Job ID: 303951
About Us
For more than 60 years, Kennesaw State University has been known for its entrepreneurial spirit and sense of community. A leader in innovative teaching and learning, Kennesaw State is located just north of Atlanta and combines a suburban setting on two metro-Atlanta campuses in Kennesaw and Marietta. As one of Georgia's largest universities, Kennesaw State offers undergraduate and graduate degrees to over 50,000 students. Our high-impact research and Division I athletics also draw students from throughout the region and across the globe. A member of the University System of Georgia, Kennesaw State is a Carnegie-designated doctoral research institution (R2) committed to becoming a world-class academic institution positioned to broaden its academic and research missions and expand its scope on a local, regional, and national level.
Our university's vibrant culture, career opportunities, rich benefits, and values of respect, integrity, collaboration, inclusivity, and accountability make us an employer of choice. As part of the University System of Georgia, Kennesaw State exemplifies the power and promise of a student-centered, research-driven university. In addition, Kennesaw State supports the University of Georgia's core values of accountability, excellence, integrity, and respect. We are searching for talented people to join Kennesaw State University in our vision. For more information, visit the Kennesaw State University website.
Location
Our Kennesaw campus is located at 1000 Chastain Road NW, Kennesaw, GA 30144. Our Marietta campus is located at 1100 South Marietta Parkway, Marietta, GA 30060.
Department Information
The History and Philosophy Department prepares students for adaptable, fulfilling careers by teaching a core set of transferable knowledge and skills through research, analyzing and assessing evidence, and articulating sound conclusions both orally and in writing. Students learn about the larger world by studying societies, cultures, and economies across a broad chronological and geographical spectrum, which makes them better global citizens, problem solvers, and communicators.
With more than 400 full-time faculty and 8,100 degree-seeking students, the Norman J. Radow College of Humanities & Social Sciences is dedicated to pioneering workforce readiness in the humanities and social sciences. By staying true to our Liberal Arts values and integrating practical knowledge and experiential learning into our curriculum, we empower our students to become responsible citizens ready for the demands of the modern workplace. The home of three schools and eight departments, the College offers more than 80 graduate and undergraduate programs of study in both traditional and interdisciplinary fields. These programs enable students to develop leadership, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills, as well as a strong sense of civic engagement.
The College is committed to the success of our students, faculty, staff and communities. We seek candidates whose experience has prepared them to fulfill that commitment and engage our students, partners, and stakeholders effectively.
Job Summary
Kennesaw State University is now accepting applications for a full-time, tenure track faculty position as Assistant Professor or Associate Professor of Public History in the Department of History and Philosophy with a preferred start date of August 2027. This is a nine-month contracted position and is for work to be performed in the state of Georgia.
Responsibilities
Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in public history and history, such as Introduction to Public History, Documentation and Interpretation of Historic Sites, Historic Preservation, Oral History, Museum Education, Historical Archaeology, and related courses, according to expertise and program needs. Faculty are expected to teach courses of variable size and modalities, including large class sizes when necessary, and on Kennesaw and/or Marietta campuses.
Produce and disseminate high-quality, meaningful scholarship in public history, history, or a closely related field. Research agenda may include traditional scholarship as well as peer-reviewed public scholarship in the form of National Register nominations, exhibitions, and other forms of scholarly work made available to the public.
Seek external funding to support research and scholarly activity.
Coordinate the undergraduate public history minor and undergraduate internships for the Department of History & Philosophy.
Collaborate with the Department of Museums, Archives and Rare Books (MARB) to coordinate student projects, work with campus and community partners on public history initiatives, and serve on the University Architectural Review Committee. KSU's Department of Museums, Archives & Rare Books serves as a unique learning lab for students, offering undergraduate research and internship opportunities and support for Honors and capstone projects. With several public history resources, the Williams Rare Book Museum, the Museum of History and Holocaust Education, and the KSU Archives--the Public History Program works closely with MARB and receives support for projects that serve the on and off campus community.
Teaching assignments will be based on earned degrees and SACSCOC Faculty Credentials Guidelines.
Required Qualifications
Ph.D. degree, or the foreign equivalent, in History or Public History, or a closely related field, is required at the time of hire
AND
For Assistant Professors:
Demonstrated potential for excellence in teaching, mentorship, and promoting student success at the university level, such as, but not limited to, teaching success in public history courses
Demonstrated potential for excellence in research and scholarship within the discipline, such as, but not limited to, peer-reviewed publications, academic presentations, and external funding applications.
Demonstrated potential for service to university, profession, and community, such as, but not limited to, collaboration on public history projects across academic units and with stakeholders beyond the university.
For Associate Professors
Demonstrated record of excellence in research and scholarship within the discipline, such as, but not limited to, peer-reviewed publications, academic presentations, digital or physical exhibits, and external funding applications
Demonstrated record of excellence in teaching, mentorship, and promoting student success at the university level, such as, but not limited to, teaching succession public history courses.
Demonstrated record of service to university, profession, and community, such as, but not limited to, collaboration on public history projects across academic units and with stakeholders beyond the university
Preferred Qualifications
Demonstrated record of success in teaching at the undergraduate level in public history.
Evidence of a sustained research agenda in history, history education, or a closely related field
Experience applying for or working with extramural funding to support research
Demonstrated interest in or experience with digital humanities projects
Successful experience managing public history projects such as exhibitions, oral history projects, National Register nominations, and historic site surveys.
Effectiveness in teaching in different modalities and different course sizes, including large classes, if necessary, on Kennesaw and Marietta campuses
Demonstrated record of collaboration, partnerships, and/or community engagement
Required Documents to Attach
CV
Cover Letter addressing experience in teaching, public history, collaboration, and scholarship, as well as research agenda going forward
Unofficial Transcripts (Official Transcripts and Official International Course-by-Course Evaluations Due Upon Hire)
Names, phone numbers, and email addresses of at least 3 references.
Portfolio of Scholarship and Creative Activity should include a research statement and examples of scholarly publications and/or public history projects
Incomplete applications will not be considered.
Apply Before Date
Review of applications will begin immediately.For full consideration, please apply by October 31, 2026.
Contact Information
For questions about this faculty opening, please contact David Parker, dparker@kennesaw.edu.
For technical support or assistance completing a job application, please contact the Shared Services Center at (877) 251-2644 or support@usg.edu.
For questions about a specific job posting at Kennesaw State University, please contact the search chair listed under the contact information section on each posting. For general questions about faculty jobs please email facultyjobs@kennesaw.edu.
USG Core Values
The University System of Georgia is comprised of our 25 institutions of higher education and learning as well as the System Office. Our USG Statement of Core Values are Integrity, Excellence, Accountability, and Respect. These values serve as the foundation for all that we do as an organization, and each USG community member is responsible for demonstrating and upholding these standards. More details on the USG Statement of Core Values and Code of Conduct are available in USG Board Policy 8.2.18.1.2 and can be found on-line at https://www.usg.edu/policymanual/section8/C224/#p8.2.18_personnel_conduct.
Additionally, USG supports Freedom of Expression as stated in Board Policy 6.5 Freedom of Expression and Academic Freedom found on-line at https://www.usg.edu/policymanual/section6/C2653.
Equal Employment Opportunity
Kennesaw State University is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. The University is committed to maintaining a fair and respectful environment for living, work and study. To that end, and in accordance with federal and state law, Board of Regents policy, and University policy, the University prohibits harassment of or discrimination against any person because of race, color, sex (including sexual harassment, pregnancy, and medical conditions related to pregnancy), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, ethnicity or national origin, religion, age, genetic information, disability, or veteran or military status by any member of the KSU Community on campus, in connection with a University program or activity, or in a manner that creates a hostile environment for members of the KSU community.
For additional information on this policy, or to file a complaint under the provisions of this policy, students, employees, applicants for employment or admission or other third parties should contact the Office of Institutional Equity at English Building, Suite 225, eeo@kennesaw.edu.
Background Check
Per the University System of Georgia background check policy, all final candidates will be required to consent to a criminal background investigation. Final candidates may be asked to disclose criminal record history during the initial screening process and prior to a conditional offer of employment. Applicants for positions of trust with screening results which confirm a disqualifying criminal history will be immediately disqualified from employment eligibility.
All applicants are required to include professional references as part of their application process. jobs.title: Assistant/Associate Professor, Painting
jobs.description:
Job Details
Winthrop University invites applications for an Assistant or Associate Professor of Fine Arts specializing in Painting. This is a full-time, nine-month, tenure-track appointment in the Department of Fine Arts, part of the College of Visual and Performing Arts. The College also includes the departments of Design, Arts Administration, Theatre and Dance, and Music and also the Winthrop University Galleries.
Winthrop’s beautiful campus is located in Rock Hill, South Carolina, within the rapidly growing Charlotte metropolitan region and approximately 20 minutes from Charlotte, North Carolina. The area offers a thriving arts and cultural scene as well as convenient access to Charlotte Douglas International Airport.
We seek a dynamic and forward-looking artist-educator who will contribute to Winthrop’s commitment to rigorous study of image-making, material exploration, and technical excellence while helping advance the curriculum in contemporary painting practices. The successful candidate will be prepared to teach both traditional and contemporary approaches to painting using a wide range of media and substrates.
Teaching responsibilities will span all undergraduate levels, from foundational studies in pictorial composition to advanced and interdisciplinary studio practices, including senior-level mentorship within the Bachelor of Fine Arts program.
Position Responsibilities
The successful candidate will:
Teach 3 studio courses each fall and spring semesters, with primary responsibility for undergraduate painting courses at the beginning, intermediate, and advanced levels.
Teach foundational studio courses as needed, which may include Drawing, 2D Design, Media Studies, and related foundation-level offerings. The ability to teach introductory printmaking courses is an asset, but not required.
Provide instruction in both traditional and contemporary approaches to painting, including technical proficiency with oil, acrylic, water-based, and other media; preparation and construction of painting surfaces and supports; and conceptually driven approaches to studio practice.
Develop and regularly update course content to provide rigorous instruction in painting while engaging historical and contemporary practices, material exploration, technical proficiency, formal visual principles, and interdisciplinary approaches to studio art.
Advise and mentor undergraduate Fine Arts majors, including supporting students in portfolio development, professional preparation, advanced studio work, and senior capstone exhibitions.
Maintain an active record of creative and scholarly activity consistent with expectations for tenure and promotion, demonstrated through exhibitions, juried or curated opportunities, professional presentations, publications, commissions, residencies, or other relevant forms of professional engagement.
Contribute to the continued development of the Painting area, including curriculum, teaching and learning spaces, studios, equipment, and related resources in response to evolving pedagogical and program needs.
Participate in departmental and programmatic responsibilities, including curriculum development, annual assessment, accreditation activities, and other initiatives supporting the academic mission of the department.
Actively support and participate in student recruitment and retention efforts, including portfolio reviews, prospective-student events, and other departmental outreach activities.
Contribute professional service to the Department of Fine Arts, College of Visual and Performing Arts, University, discipline, and broader community.
Support the effective and safe operation of studio facilities and equipment and maintain appropriate office hours and availability for students.
Assume other responsibilities consistent with departmental needs and the candidate’s areas of expertise.
About the College
To learn more about the College of Visual & Performing Arts please visit: https:/ www.winthrop.edu/cvpa/.
About Winthrop University
Founded in 1886, Winthrop University in Rock Hill, South Carolina, offers its 5,200-plus undergraduate and graduate students an educational experience that blends liberal arts, professional programs, global awareness, and civic engagement. In its colleges of Arts and Sciences; Business and Technology; Education, Sport, and Human Sciences; and Visual and Performing Arts, Winthrop embraces only those programs and activities that can be delivered at an exemplary level. Winthrop University is achieving national stature as a competitive and distinctive co-educational, public, residential, comprehensive, values-oriented institution. The values of service, excellence, community, and leadership provide the foundation for Winthrop’s continuing development and shape Winthrop’s continuing success. Numerous national accolades reflect the sustained high quality and value of the Winthrop Experience, including the most recent U.S. News & World Report’s ranking of Winthrop as one of the top-10 public comprehensive universities in the South. Winthrop is an active member of the Rock Hill community and recognized as a key component of the region’s economic resurgence. Approximately 20 minutes from Charlotte, North Carolina, Winthrop has direct access to and is engaged in a broad and expansive regional business community. Winthrop’s beautiful campus encompasses a rich architectural blend of neo-Georgian buildings and is included in the National Register of Historic Places. The attractive recreational and research complex area that surrounds Winthrop Lake is home to Winthrop’s 18 Division I men’s and women’s sports.
Benefits
At Winthrop University, we are proud to offer a comprehensive benefits package that significantly enhances the total compensation for our employees. In partnership with the State of South Carolina and the Public Employee Benefit Authority (PEBA), our benefits include health and life insurance, generous paid leave, parental leave, and retirement programs. These benefits reflect our commitment to supporting the well-being and financial security of our employees. For more information please visit: https://www.winthrop.edu/hr/employee-benefits.aspx.
Background Check
Winthrop University is committed to providing a safe campus community. Winthrop conducts background investigations for applicants being considered for employment. Background investigations include reference checks, a criminal history record check, and when appropriate, a financial (credit) report or driving history check.
Position Availability: 08/16/2027
Required Qualifications
Master of Fine Arts (MFA) in Painting or Studio Art
Minimum of 2 to 3 years of successful college-level teaching experience (full-time or adjunct), supported by a portfolio of student work, personal work, and a robust personal exhibition record.
Extensive mastery of traditional oil, acrylic, water-based, and mixed-media painting techniques, alongside proficiency in structural drawing and design principles.
Exceptional grasp of studio pedagogy, objective grading standards, and formal design elements.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills required for rigorous student evaluation and collaborative faculty governance.
Preferred Qualifications
Familiarity with and the ability to teach introductory printmaking courses.
Employment Conditions: Full time, tenure-track, 3/3 teaching load
Application Instructions
Applicants should submit the following materials in PDF Format:
Curriculum vitae (CV), including the names, phone numbers, and e-mail addresses of three (3) professional references from whom letters of recommendation have been requested.
Cover Letter (addressing how the candidate’s qualifications align with position responsibilities)
Statement of Teaching Philosophy
Portfolio of 20 student works (provide project brief and course name, date, materials used, etc.)
Personal Artist Statement including a portfolio of 20 images of professional work (title, date, materials, short description of the work)
Portfolio of up to 20 examples of the candidate’s professional, creative, or scholarly work, submitted as a PDF or URL.
Transcript and evidence of highest degree achieved (unofficial transcripts are acceptable for the initial review; official transcripts must be provided for a final appointment)
Three letters of recommendation will be requested from semifinalists at a later date. (The CV must include the names, phone numbers, and e-mail addresses of all references.)
Questions about the position and applications should be directed to Department of Department of Fine Arts, Mark Hamilton, chair, hamiltonm@winthrop.edu.

jobs.title: Health & Human Physiological Sciences Faculty Position (Tenure-Track, Open Rank)
jobs.description:
Job Details
Summary
The Health and Human Physiological Sciences (HHPS) Department invites applications for a full-time open-rank tenure-track faculty position in HHPS to begin in the fall of 2027. The HHPS Department is located in the recently opened Billie Tisch Center for Integrated Sciences, a state-of-the-art teaching and research facility that fosters unique interdisciplinary connections across the sciences. The HHPS Department has a suite of laboratories for conducting sophisticated, in-depth research from the molecular/cellular level to applied physiology in animal and human models. Our suite of laboratories allows for research interests across a breadth of areas including environmental/occupational physiology, cardiovascular physiology, endocrinology, and metabolism. Responsibilities include undergraduate teaching within the department and as part of the College’s first-year experience program; developing and implementing a research program that involves undergraduates and competes for national grants (e.g., NIH-AIREA); advising/mentoring students; and serving the department, the college, and broader profession.
Applicants should embrace the teacher-scholar model and demonstrate a strong commitment to undergraduate teaching and mentoring within a liberal arts environment. Candidates should have expertise in exercise physiology or a closely related area of human physiology and health, with the potential to contribute to courses across the HHPS curriculum. Areas of scholarly interest may include, but are not limited to, exercise physiology, integrative physiology, physical activity and health, nutrition, or other biomedical and health-related fields.
Candidates should demonstrate the potential to develop an active and sustainable research program that meaningfully engages undergraduate students in the research process. We particularly value candidates who view teaching and scholarship as complementary activities and who are enthusiastic about mentoring students as developing scientists and health professionals. Experience in teaching, postdoctoral research, and pursuit of extramural funding are highly desirable.
We are seeking an energetic teacher/scholar who embraces interdisciplinary work in a creative and supportive environment. We are expressly interested in faculty with expertise in exercise physiology, broadly, and/or areas complementary to existing faculty expertise in the department.
Responsibilities
Teach 18 contact hours per academic year (~5 classes) including: Introduction to Exercise Physiology, Human Anatomy & Physiology, Research Techniques in Human Physiology/Exercise Testing and Prescription, Human Nutrition, Advanced Exercise Physiology, Research Design, and special topics upper-level courses. Responsibilities will also include occasionally teaching a first-year seminar course in the College’s first-year experience seminar course.
Conduct and disseminate research with HHPS students. Pursue funding through governmental, professional organizations, and/or industry partners. Dissemination of research through presentations at scientific conferences and publications in peer-reviewed journals.
Act in service to the department, college, and broader professional community.
This is a 9-month per academic year position with benefits eligibility and salary paid over 12-months per year.
Qualifications
A Ph.D. or similar degree in the area of exercise/applied physiology/kinesiology or a related field (ABD considered).
Preference will be given to candidates with undergraduate teaching experience, postdoctoral fellowship experience, active research agendas, and those with experience in pursuing extramural research funding.
Salary: $80,000 - $120,000 depending on rank.
Skidmore College offers a comprehensive benefits package, including a relocation stipend and a lab startup package. Tenure-track faculty (assistant professors) are eligible for a pre-tenure research leave in their fourth year at the college. Our benefits plans provide choice and flexibility to support our employees' needs and those of their families.
Benefits information: www.skidmore.edu/benefits
Application Instructions:
Applicants should submit the following materials to the HR application portal:
A cover letter outlining your interest and ability to fulfill the position outlined above
Curriculum vitae
A teaching statement that outlines your experience and describes your teaching style, instructional techniques, and general pedagogical approach.
A research statement outlining your research experience and goals, including potential avenues to pursue funding.
Contact information for 3 professional references
Applications will be reviewed starting October 30th 2026.
Apply online: www.skidmore.edu/hr
Questions? Please contact Steve Ives, Professor and Chair of Health & Human Physiological Sciences, sives@skidmore.edu or T.H. Reynolds, Professor and Associate Chair of Health & Human Physiological Sciences, treynold@skidmore.edu
About Skidmore College:
Skidmore is a highly selective liberal arts college that fosters creative approaches to teaching and learning. Skidmore’s faculty of teacher-scholars are devoted to the instruction and mentoring of approximately 2500 talented undergraduates. With its relatively small size and student-faculty ratio, the College is a close-knit academic community situated in a beautiful and historic setting.
Employment at Skidmore College is contingent upon an acceptable post-offer background check result.
Equal Employment Opportunity Statement
Skidmore College is committed to being an inclusive campus community and, as an Equal Opportunity Employer, does not discriminate in its hiring or employment practices on the basis of race, color, creed, religion, gender, age, national or ethnic origin, physical or mental disability, military or veteran status, marital status, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, genetic information, predisposition or carrier status, domestic violence victim status, familial status, dating violence, or stalking, or any other category protected by applicable federal, state or local laws.

Areas of particular interest include, but are not limited to: Biopolitics, Gender/Sexuality/Queer Studies, and/or Sociolinguistics. Ph.D. (or ABD status with Ph.D. completed by start date) in Spanish or Hispanic Studies is required. A selective liberal arts college located on Chicago’s North Shore, Lake Forest College enrolls approximately 1,800 students from more than 40 states and from more than 100 countries. jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Judicial Politics
jobs.description:
Job Details
The Department of Political Science at West Virginia University seeks to hire a full-time, tenure-track Assistant Professor with a specialization in judicial politics, law and courts, and/or public law. The preferred start date is August 13, 2027. We welcome applications that can contribute broadly to the judicial politics curriculum.
The Department of Political Science offers a full range of academic programs (B.A., M.A., and Ph.D.) and has 14 full-time faculty, 36 graduate students, and about 400 undergraduates, many of whom are in the Pre-Law Area of Emphasis. The department faculty are active in research on American and state politics, class politics, comparative elections, computational methods, conflict analysis, congressional politics, international relations, political and economic inequality, public opinion, public policy, racial and ethnic politics, religion and politics, representation, and state courts. The department’s methodologically rigorous doctoral program offers fields in American politics, comparative politics, international politics, and public policy. Additionally, the department houses the International Studies program, which is an interdisciplinary undergraduate major focusing on national security, diplomacy, and development.
Responsibilities:
The person hired in this position will maintain an active research agenda that advances the department’s program in the area of judicial politics. They will be expected to regularly publish in high-quality peer-reviewed journals. The teaching load is two courses per semester. The successful candidate will be expected to teach classes that complement the department’s current offerings at both the graduate and undergraduate levels, develop new course offerings, and mentor students. They must have the ability to teach effectively the department’s undergraduate judicial politics introductory course and advanced undergraduate courses on constitutional law and civil liberties. They may also be asked to develop advanced undergraduate judicial politics classes in their area(s) of expertise. The candidate will also be expected to serve the department, university, and profession.
Professional Qualifications:
The successful candidate must have a Ph.D. in Political Science, Government, or Public Policy. We will consider ABD candidates, but the Ph.D. must be conferred by the start date. In addition, the candidate must demonstrate evidence of the following: potential to develop an active research agenda that will secure external funding; appropriate methodological skills; evidence of and commitment to establishing an excellent record of teaching and mentorship; and excellent communication skills.
To apply, please visit https://careers.wvu.edu/career-opportunities and upload the following:
1. Cover letter.
2. Curriculum vitae.
3. Research statement: Describes past scholarly contributions, current work, and future research directions.
4. Teaching statement: Describes teaching, learning, and mentoring philosophy, as well as teaching evaluations and courses that the candidate would want to teach or develop.
5. Samples of written work.
6. Complete contact information for three professional references. Letters of recommendation from professional references will only be requested from finalists.
For more information, please visit our website https://politicalscience.wvu.edu. Questions regarding this position may be directed to the chair of the search committee, Dr. Matthew Jacobsmeier (matthew.jacobsmeier@mail.wvu.edu). Review of applications will begin on November 6, 2026, and will continue until the position is filled.
Affirmative Action
Morgantown, WV is a growing university city. The area offers abundant outdoor recreation and the cultural opportunities of a college town. It is within easy driving distance of Pittsburgh, PA (70 mi) and is within a day's driving distance to Washington DC and Columbus, OH (200 mi). West Virginia University is a place of purpose and community. We take pride in our profound impact on the state of West Virginia and are committed to the personal and professional growth of our employees. From the groundbreaking R1 research at our flagship campus in Morgantown to the career-oriented programs at WVU Potomac State in Keyser, and the technology-intensive programs at WVU Tech in Beckley, the contributions of WVU employees resonate across the state, touching lives and shaping futures. At WVU, you will discover a supportive community that champions work-life balance and fosters a collaborative atmosphere. Our core values — service, curiosity, respect, accountability and appreciation — unite us as Mountaineers. Join us at West Virginia University, where your work will make a lasting impact. To learn more about WVU, visit wvu.edu.
West Virginia University is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We invite all qualified applicants regardless of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, or Veteran status.

The School of Teacher Education (STE) in the Anne Spencer Daves College of Education, Health, and Human Sciences (Anne’s College) and the Florida Center for Reading Research (FCRR) at the Florida State University invite applications for a nine-month, tenured or tenure-earning assistant or associate professor of Reading Education or Special Education. The position will involve teaching, research, and service within STE, and will include a joint appointment with FCRR. The position carries a reduced teaching assignment with correspondingly high expectations for research productivity.
The successful candidate will have a tenure home in one of two majors within STE: Reading Education or Special Education. These majors work closely together in STE and FCRR, so a collaborative orientation is desired. The candidate will be expected to maintain a rigorous grant writing and research program, including competitive externally funded research grants. The candidate will also teach undergraduate, masters, and/or doctoral level classes within their program, and train doctoral students through active participation in their research program. The candidate will also be expected to participate in university governance in the department, college, and FCRR, at a level that is commensurate with their rank.
The candidate will join an interdisciplinary group of colleagues and students at STE, Anne’s College, and FCRR. Drawing from multiple disciplines, FCRR investigates all aspects of reading and reading-related skills across the lifespan. Through rigorous and robust research, innovation, and engagement, FCRR advances the science of reading to improve learning and achievement from birth through adulthood. Meanwhile, Anne’s College advances society and enriches our community through support and education, while enhancing the quality of life of all our students, faculty and staff. Through meaningful collaborations, commitment to public scholarship, and integration of research, practice and policy, Anne’s College addresses America’s urgent education challenges in the innovative manner characteristic of FSU.
The roots of FSU’s Anne Spencer Daves College of Education, Health, and Human Sciences date back to the university’s establishment, and it is the oldest college of its kind in Florida. The College is home to six academic departments united through a common goal to maximize human potential. In total, the College includes the Department of Educational Leadership & Policy Studies, Department of Educational Psychology & Learning Systems, Department of Human Development & Family Sciences, Department of Health, Nutrition & Food Sciences, Department of Sport Management, School of Teacher Education, numerous research centers, and three laboratory schools (Florida State University School, FSU Pembroke Pines Charter School, and The Collegiate School at FSU Panama City). General Description:
The Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry is seeking to hire a 9-month, tenure earning faculty at the rank of Assistant Professor of Organic Chemistry. We seek collaborative and innovative scientists and educators who will contribute to our growing research and teaching missions.
UNF is a Carnegie R2 institution, reflecting our commitment to high-impact research while maintaining our tradition of excellence in undergraduate teaching. We are proud to support active faculty researchers and offer competitive startup packages. The department is also conducting simultaneous searches in other subdisciplines of chemistry; scientists working at the interface of these areas are encouraged to apply to the position most aligned with their teaching strengths.
Position Highlights:
Research Expectations: Establish a research program, focusing on organic chemistry related topics, that actively involves undergraduate students and/or master’s students. This will include continually pursuing extramural grant support, disseminating research results in presentations at professional conferences, and publishing manuscripts in peer-reviewed journals. We encourage applications with research programs across the organic chemistry spectrum.
Teaching Load: Four–six courses per academic year, with a reduced load (two per semester) for the first three years. Continued course reductions are available for faculty with strong research productivity aligned with the UNF Strategic Plan.
Courses Taught: Organic Chemistry I & II (both lecture and lab), lower-level courses (such as General Chemistry), and upper-level electives in the candidate’s area of expertise.
Mentorship and Service: Participate in departmental governance, advise and mentor students, and contribute to our service mission at the department, college, and university levels.
Supervisor: This position reports to the Department Chair, Dr. Hannah Malcolm.
Working Hours: Varies
Supervision Exercised: Yes
Required Licensure: N/A
Required Qualifications:
Ph.D. in Chemistry, Biochemistry, or related discipline.
Excellence in research as demonstrated by a strong publication record in peer-reviewed journals and proposals for future work.
A strong commitment to undergraduate research and teaching.
Preferred Qualifications/Skills:
UNF seeks to attract faculty of the highest caliber, who are skilled in the scholarship of teaching, discovery, application, and integration of knowledge in organic chemistry.
Commitment to excellence in teaching undergraduate courses within the chemistry/biochemistry department curriculum, specifically Organic Chemistry I and II, as well as organic chemistry electives and lower-level courses.

Towson University fosters a climate that is grounded in respect to cultivate the intellectual and personal growth of the entire university community.
Position: The College of Education invites applications for a tenure-track, 9-month Assistant Professor position in the Department of Elementary Education with three years PreK-12 grade teaching experience in public schools. Faculty with expertise in elementary education curriculum and instruction with demonstrated knowledge and experience in reading instruction and assessment, writing instruction, and supporting multilingual learners are encouraged to apply. Preferred begin date is August 2027.
Qualifications: Applicants should have a doctoral degree in Curriculum and Instruction or an education-related field. ABD applications will be considered, but the appointment will be at the instructor rank, and all degree requirements must be completed by August 1, 2027. Candidates should have a strong commitment to teaching and working with teacher candidates and novice teachers; expertise in elementary education literacy curriculum, instruction, and assessment; demonstrated knowledge and experience supporting multilingual learners and/or urban schools; a promise high-quality research; the ability to work in a collaborative manner with colleagues and school-based partners, and commitment to working across programs, disciplines, and cultures to strengthen the field.
Responsibilities: Primary responsibilities include: (1) Teaching and Supervising: Research-active instructors teach/supervise 6 course units (equivalent to 18 credits) over a 9-month academic year in our student-focused programs, providing high-quality instruction at the undergraduate and graduate levels in a variety of literacy courses, (2) Scholarship: Development/continuation of a focused area of research that includes peer-reviewed publications, professional presentations, grant funding, and involvement in scholarly projects with students; and (3) Service: Active service participation at the department, college, university, community, and professional levels.
The Department: The Department of Elementary Education currently has 28 full time-time faculty members and offers four programs. The programs include: one undergraduate elementary education program and three graduate programs (M.Ed. in Reading Education, M.Ed. in Elementary Education, and M.A.T. in Elementary Education). jobs.description:
Job Details
The Engineering & Mathematics Department of the School of Science, Technology, Engineering & Mathematics (STEM) at the University of Washington Bothell (UWB) invites applications for a faculty position at the rank of Assistant Teaching Professor in Electrical Engineering, with an anticipated start date of September 16, 2027. We seek applicants who demonstrate commitment to excellence in teaching, scholarship, and service in a diverse and inclusive academic community. The successful candidate will join our faculty on a full-time (100% FTE) basis for a nine-month academic appointment (3-year term, renewable) beginning September 16, 2027.
The base salary range for this position will be $11,365-$11,964 per month during the nine-month academic year ($102,285-107,676 annually), commensurate with experience and qualifications, or as mandated by a U.S. Department of Labor prevailing wage determination.
The successful candidates will be expected to contribute to success of the program in several ways including teaching a wide range of undergraduate courses (spanning from circuits, devices, digital circuit design, signal & systems and their laboratories) , teaching graduate courses in areas of expertise, supervising laboratory sessions and capstone projects, engaging in scholarship, and through service to the program, department, and school.
Candidates will be considered across a range of research and teaching interests in electrical engineering. Current needs are greatest in power electronics and circuit design.
The Electrical Engineering program is part of the Department of Engineering and Mathematics, which is housed in the School of STEM. In addition to Electrical Engineering, the department has programs in mechanical engineering, computer engineering, and Mathematics. The program offers a BS in Electrical Engineering, a BS in Computer Engineering (jointly run with the Department of Computer Systems and Software (CSS), an MS in Electrical and Computer Engineering, and a Graduate Certificate in Electrical and Computer Engineering Foundation. The Electrical Engineering program is comprised of 8 full-time and several part-time faculty, with vast academic and industrial experience. The EE faculty have expertise in a broad range of areas, including power systems, signal processing, communication systems, power electronics, embedded systems, design of organic cells, AI and machine learning, etc. The program has well-equipped labs and facilities to conduct teaching and research.
The School of STEM is the largest school at UW Bothell, and we are a school committed to attracting faculty and staff who create an exceptional student experience in support of our core values of Collaboration, Opportunities, Responsibility, and Engagement. Our faculty members are dynamic educators who engage in innovative, evidence-based pedagogies. We offer seventeen degrees (fourteen undergraduate, three graduate), eleven minors, and two graduate certificates across four Departments (Biological Sciences, Computing and Software Systems, Engineering & Mathematics, Physical Sciences). The school is housed in several buildings on a vibrant campus collocated on a restored 100-acre wetland with an active salmon stream, including the 74,000 square-foot Discovery Hall teaching and laboratory facility, and our new 80,000 square-foot STEM building, Innovation Hall – the first shared academic building between a community college and university in the country.
Located in the heart of the Puget Sound region, the University of Washington Bothell is one of the most dynamic public universities in the state of Washington. UW Bothell is a student-centered campus known for engaging students through classes, team projects, and research in which students connect what they learn or create in the classroom with the broader community. This is achieved through close relationships with faculty members as teachers and mentors, and staff dedicated to student success. The academic work of the campus focuses on cross-disciplinary research, connected learning, and community engagement, and prepares students for leadership in the state of Washington and beyond.
The campus offers more than 55 undergraduate and graduate degree programs in five schools. Current UW Bothell enrollment is over 6,000 students. More than 90% of undergraduates are from Washington State, and approximately 40% are first-generation college attendees. The priorities of the University’s current Strategic Plan – “Expanding Access, Achieving Excellence”, are to enhance community and campus engagement, and advance cross disciplinary teaching and scholarship. In addition to award winning faculty and staff, UW Bothell has been recognized for innovations in academic programming and support services designed to help students graduate on time and debt-free. It has also earned both recognition and awards for its work in the area of environmental sustainability and is just one of twelve institutions selected to join the launch cohort of the Postsecondary Data for Action Network (PDAN), a new national initiative co-led by the Institute for Higher Education Policy (IHEP) and the Association for Institutional Research (AIR). This selection places UW Bothell among a small group of colleges and universities collectively committed to using data in smarter, more student-centered ways.
All University of Washington faculty are expected to engage in teaching, scholarship, and service.
Qualifications
Applicants for this position must meet the following minimum qualifications:
PhD (or foreign equivalent) in Electrical Engineering or closely related fields by time of appointment.
Candidates may be considered for an Acting Assistant Teaching Professor pending PhD title if they have not yet completed their doctoral research. When the degree is conferred, the title changes to an assistant professorial appointment in the corresponding track. Doctoral degree must be completed within 2 years.
Application Instructions
To ensure full consideration of your application, please submit all materials no later than October 31, 2026. Priority will be given to those applications received by October 31, 2026. Applications will only be accepted via Interfolio: https://apply.interfolio.com/194000. The position will remain open until filled.
If you have a question about the details of this search/position, or about Interfolio, please contact the search committee at uwbmath@uw.edu.
Applications should include the following materials:
a cover letter of no more than two pages detailing your interest in the position, relevant qualifications, and experiences
a curriculum vitae
transcripts showing all graduate level coursework (unofficial transcripts are acceptable)
teaching statement that includes any available evidence of teaching excellence, reflection on previous teaching and how that informs current and future teaching plans.
Applicants should articulate how their past experiences and/or future plans in teaching, mentoring, and/or service promote a sense of belonging and foster a welcoming and inclusive environment.
Please also include contact information for at least three referees who are prepared to provide letters of recommendation upon request.
Equal Employment Opportunity Statement
Equal Opportunity
The University of Washington is committed to fostering an inclusive, respectful and welcoming community for all. As an equal opportunity employer, the University considers applicants for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, national origin, citizenship, sex, pregnancy, age, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, genetic information, disability, or veteran status consistent with UW Executive Order No. 81.
Benefits Information
The University is committed to providing excellent benefits to our faculty. For a summary of available benefits, please see UWHR benefits information.
Privacy Notice
Your application materials may be used for employment consideration and shared in accordance with UW’s Privacy Policy.
Disability Services
The University of Washington is committed to providing access and reasonable accommodation in its services, programs, activities, education, and employment for individuals with disabilities. To request disability accommodation in the application process, contact the Disability Services Office at 206-543-6450 or dso@uw.edu.
