Job Title:Assistant Professor - Environmental Humanities with Area Studies Expertise in Eastern Europe and Eurasia
Department:Arts and Sciences | Slavic and East European Languages and Cultures
Transnational World Language Studies
Environmental Humanities with Area Studies Expertise in Eastern Europe and Eurasia
Rank: Tenure-Track Assistant Professor
Department of Slavic and East European Languages and Cultures
College of Arts and Sciences
Position Overview
The Department of Slavic and East European Languages and Cultures (SEELC) at The Ohio State University invites applications for a Tenure-Track Assistant Professor position in Transnational World Language Studies in the area of interdisciplinary Environmental Humanities beginning August 15, 2027. We aim to hire a dynamic scholar who will contribute to the vibrant and collegial intellectual communities of our department by engaging with interdisciplinary research, innovative teaching, program development, community engagement, and service.
This is one of three tenure-track hires in Transnational World Language Studies, the other two being in the departments of East Asian Languages and Literatures and Spanish and Portuguese. We are also conducting searches for three Postdoctoral Scholar to Tenure-Track Assistant Professor positions in Humanities-based Interdisciplinary World Languages and Cultures in the departments of French and Italian, Germanic Languages and Literatures, and Near Eastern and South Asian Languages and Cultures.
In keeping with the department’s commitment to interdisciplinarity, we are especially interested in scholars who examine the complex relationships among environment, society, culture, politics, and technology across the region, with particular attention to contemporary environmental challenges and their historical, cultural, and geopolitical dimensions. This position builds on current departmental strengths in interdisciplinary world languages and cultures, including in environmental and transnational indigenous studies, transnational media literacy, intercultural competency and global security, experiential learning, and community engagement.
The position is grounded in the broad field of environmental humanities and welcomes applicants from disciplines such as cultural and literary studies, media and technology studies, anthropology, environmental studies, area studies, or related interdisciplinary fields. The successful candidate will demonstrate a strong research and teaching agenda that advances understandings of how regional and transnational environmental transformations shape intercultural, economic, and social processes across Eastern Europe and Eurasia.
The successful candidate will contribute to interdisciplinary scholarship and teaching on environmental issues affecting Eastern Europe, Russia, Central Asia, the Caucasus, the Arctic, and neighboring regions— a vast geographical area that is central to global discussions about climate change, environmental transformations, and sustainability. This centrality has only intensified amid the ongoing environmental and human impacts of military conflicts and security concerns. We are especially interested in applicants whose research engages one or more of the following areas: climate change and climate adaptation; energy sources and transitions; climate security in the Arctic and Eurasia; migration and environmental displacement; environmental impacts of war and conflict; energy geopolitics; environmental justice; resource extraction; sustainability; and/or the intersections of environment, technology, and society in a regional and transnational frame.
As global climate and security crises become increasingly intertwined, transnational interdisciplinary linguistic and cultural expertise in Eastern Europe and Eurasia is essential for advancing public understanding of some of the most pressing challenges facing societies worldwide. We seek candidates who can translate their expertise beyond the academy, as well as for current and emerging careers that require skills in humanistic inquiry, global fluency, and multi-disciplinary literacies.
Successful candidates would be charged with conducting research and creating courses that engage their discipline beyond national borders from the perspective of intercultural competence and global fluency.
Partial startup for the Transnational World Language Studies tenure-track positions is funded by the Mellon Foundation grant “Global Fluency, Career Agility: Transforming World Languages at Ohio State.” The new hires will participate in the activities within the Department and have designated faculty mentors who are engaged in research on topics relating to transnational world language education, global fluency and intercultural competence, and to their area of specialization.
Performance Objectives
Maintain an active scholarship program.
Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in Environmental Humanities, East European and Eurasian Studies, and related interdisciplinary fields.
Advance the Mellon-funded Transforming World Languages at OSU initiative by collaborating with faculty and staff across disciplines, contributing to innovative programming, and creating new courses that strengthen students’ global fluency and intercultural competence.
Mentor students in engaged research and career pathways.
Develop innovative courses that bridge departments and programs.
Contribute to departmental service.
Foster innovative collaboration across units engaged in interdisciplinary environmental studies, international studies, media and technology, energy and climate research, and/or security studies broadly understood.
Education and Experience Qualifications
Required
PhD in disciplines such as cultural studies, literature & culture, anthropology, media studies, area studies, or related interdisciplinary fields is required at the time of appointment which is August 15, 2027. ABDs are welcome to apply.
Native or near-native fluency in one language from the multilingual environment of Eastern Europe and Eurasia is required.
Candidates must demonstrate achievement or strong promise of scholarly success.
Desired:
Experience in and/or commitment to public-facing or community engaged scholarship, teaching, and/or service.
Competency in one additional language of the region.
Engagement with ethical AI and/or media.
Ohio State provides access to a depth and breadth of opportunities and resources. Starting your first day, Ohio State offers you a comprehensive benefits package.
How to Apply
To be considered, please submit your application via Workday. https://osu.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/OSUCareers/job/Columbus-Campus/Assistant-Professor---Environmental-Humanities-with-Area-Studies-Expertise-in-Eastern-Europe-and-Eurasia_R160296-1
Application period closes November 19, 2026.
Inquiries may be directed to SEELC (interim) Chair, Dr. Jennifer Suchland (suchland.15@osu.edu) and the search committee Chair Dr. Alex Burry (burry.7@osu.edu).
You will be presented with the opportunity to attach up to FIVE individual documents in the Application Documents section. Please include the following:
Attachment 1: Cover Letter: 1-2 page letter, which should include a brief summary of your academic background and why you are interested in this opportunity.
Attachment 2: CV (Curriculum Vitae): Detailed overview of your scholarly experience, including your research experience, teaching and mentoring experience, service, engagement, and publications.
Attachment 3: Research Statement: Summary of your past research accomplishments, current work/research, and proposal for your future research plan as a faculty member.
Attachment 4: Teaching Statement: A statement of your approaches, experience and philosophy regarding your teaching, learning, and mentoring.
Attachment 5: A writing sample.
Candidates selected to move forward in the process will be asked to provide three letters of reference at a later date.
Application Deadline is November 19, 2026
Additional Information:
The College
With more than 80 majors and 100 minors, the College of Arts and Sciences is the academic heart of the university. The Arts and Sciences provides extraordinary opportunities to collaborate across disciplines, blending creativity and analysis to truly be at the forefront of thought. The breadth and depth of knowledge in the college gives students and researchers the critical thinking and adaptability essential for a lifetime of success.
Department Information
Established in 1962, the Department of Slavic and East European Languages and Cultures is dedicated to researching and teaching the languages, literatures, and cultures of the East, Central, and Southeast European nations and peoples. From the outset, the department has embraced the identity of a genuinely "Slavic and East European" (rather than "Russian”) department and has maintained that broad scope ever since. We value interdisciplinarity and serve a broad body of undergraduate students with interests in a variety of disciplines outside the Humanities. In addition, our faculty and curriculum include non-Slavic cultures of the region from an interdisciplinary perspective. Our graduate program supports interdisciplinarity and pedagogical training in communicative methods.

Department:Arts and Sciences | Physics Administration
Theoretical High Energy Physics with connection to Astrophysics
Department of Physics

Position Overview
The Department of Physics at The Ohio State University announces an opening for a tenure-track faculty position for a theoretical physicist working at the intersection of high energy physics and astrophysics. The open rank appointment, with the Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, or Professor title depending on qualifications, will start in Autumn 2027. We seek a candidate whose work complements that of the high energy physics and astrophysics efforts at Ohio State and/or helps initiate new research directions at their intersection. Our high energy theory group is interested in all aspects of particle physics, quantum field theory and string theory, and is currently focused on quantum chromodynamics (QCD), physics beyond the Standard Model, and black holes. A non-exhaustive list of points of possible connection to astrophysics includes neutrinos, dark matter, inflation, gravitational waves, dark energy, and early- or late-universe cosmology. The successful candidate will work to advance the Department’s mission in research, teaching, and service and is anticipated to become a member of the Ohio State Center for Cosmology and AstroParticle Physics (CCAPP).

Applicants should demonstrate the potential to be a recognized leader in theoretical high energy physics, who will develop a productive, well-funded, and internationally prominent research program. Successful candidates will be expected to:
foster cross-disciplinary research with sustained impact;
develop and maintain an extramurally funded research program;
have a strong commitment to excellence in teaching and mentoring; and
contribute to the teaching (graduate and undergraduate) and service missions of the University.

Assistant or Associate Professor in Subsurface Energy Engineering
POSITION SPECIFICS
The John and Willie Leone Family Department of Energy and Mineral Engineering (EME) in the College of Earth and Mineral Sciences at The Pennsylvania State University invites applications for a tenure-line faculty position at the Assistant or Associate Professor rank with a research focus in Subsurface Energy Engineering. The appointment will be made at a rank commensurate with the successful candidate's qualifications and experience.
We seek an exceptional scholar who will contribute to and strengthen the department's leadership in subsurface energy engineering through innovative, interdisciplinary research addressing critical challenges in subsurface energy production and storage and flow in porous media. Areas of interest include, but are not limited to, all traditional petroleum engineering disciplines, including reservoir engineering; drilling and completions engineering; production and operations engineering; formation evaluation and petrophysics, as well as related and emerging areas such as enhanced geothermal systems; nuclear waste disposal; subsurface recovery of critical minerals; microfluidics and lab-on-a-chip technologies; and AI-, data-, and computationally enabled approaches to subsurface engineering.
EME is a dynamic, multidisciplinary department that thrives on collaboration and impact-driven research, fostering partnerships across academia, industry, and government. Penn State provides exceptional opportunities for collaboration through its renowned interdisciplinary institutes, offering access to world-class resources and networks.
Competitive applicants for the rank of Assistant Professor must possess a Ph.D. in an engineering field directly related to their research area before beginning employment at Penn State. Candidates should demonstrate strong potential to establish an externally funded experimental, computational, or integrated research program that strengthens EME's Subsurface Energy Engineering research area. Candidates must also demonstrate a commitment to excellence in education and mentoring, including teaching undergraduate and graduate courses across EME programs, advising and mentoring graduate students, and contributing service to the Department, College, University, and profession.
Candidates for the rank of Associate Professor must meet the qualifications for Assistant Professor and additionally demonstrate excellence in teaching and mentoring, a strong record of research, publications, and external funding, and an established national or international reputation for scholarly or professional achievement. The successful candidate will play a key role in advancing interdisciplinary research within the department and college and to serve as a collaborative leader who contributes to innovation and excellence across the department.
To apply, submit the following materials:
A cover letter describing the candidate's principal research interests and providing the names and contact information of four references;
A complete curriculum vitae, including a full list of publications;
A research statement of no more than three pages describing the candidate's research vision and future directions and explaining how their program would strengthen and expand EME's research leadership;
A teaching statement of no more than one page describing the candidate's approach to teaching and mentoring and identifying courses within the EME undergraduate and graduate curriculum, as well as curricular areas, in which the candidate could make the greatest contributions; and
Two published journal articles that the candidate considers their most impactful scholarly contributions.
Applications received by November 27, 2026 will receive full consideration. Review of applications will continue until the position is filled. Please direct inquiries and nominations to Prof. Sanjay Srinivasan, Chair of the Search Committee, at szs27@psu.edu.

The University of Pennsylvania School of Nursing, one of 12 Schools in a highly ranked institution, is dedicated to the integration of interdisciplinary research, education, and practice.
The Family and Community Health (FCH) Department in the School of Nursing seeks candidates for an associated faculty position on the non-tenure practice track. We invite individuals prepared at the doctoral level (PhD or DNP) to apply to the Associated faculty (Practice Track at rank of Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor).
Applicants must have content expertise in sexual reproductive health, women’s health, and/or nurse-midwifery. Teaching responsibilities may include courses in the Women’s Health Gender Related (WHGRNP) Nurse Practitioner program, Nurse-Midwifery program, and our BSN and MPN programs.
The Women’s Health/Gender-Related Nurse Practitioner program focuses on the primary, sexual, and reproductive health care needs of women from adolescence through the advanced years, concentrating on promoting and maintaining wellness. The Nurse-Midwifery program prepares graduates for midwifery practice focused on providing family-centered, comprehensive care for fundamentally healthy people and their families. The BSN and MPN programs both include courses focused on sexual reproductive health and nursing of women and infants.
The Practice Professor may have teaching responsibilities in both the entry-to-practice (BSN & MPN) and graduate programs. Experience in academic program leadership, curriculum development/evaluation, academic teaching using multiple modalities (didactic, online) and working with an interprofessional audience of physicians and nurses is preferred. Strong analytical skills with the ability to assimilate numerous sources of complex information is required. Excellent writing skills are essential. Strong interpersonal and organizational skills needed.

Current national board certification is required. For those who will teach in the Nurse-Midwifery Program, the candidate must be licensed as a Certified Nurse-Midwife (CNM) in Pennsylvania or be eligible for licensure, with acquisition of the CNM license within the first semester of employment. jobs.title: Professor and Director, Dr. Yvette Kanouff School of Data, Mathematical and Statistical Sciences
jobs.description:
Job Details
The Opportunity
The College of Sciences at the University of Central Florida (UCF) invites applications for a full-time, 12-month, position of tenured professor and director of the newly formed School of Data, Mathematical, and Statistical Sciences with an anticipated start date on May 1, 2027. The successful candidate will serve as the inaugural Director of the School. The director is the unit head, provides leadership for the school, and is essential to the decision-making and administrative functions within the unit, including academic programs, budget, hiring, evaluations, and facilities. This appointment offers an opportunity to strengthen connections across the disciplines in the school and support their distinctive strengths. Nominations of ideal candidates can be communicated to the Committee Chair, Dr. Brett McCollum (brett.mccollum@ucf.edu).
The Dr. Yvette Kanouff School of Data, Mathematical, and Statistical Sciences (Kanouff School) is a new interdisciplinary unit within the College of Sciences formed from the merger of the Department of Mathematics and the Department of Statistics and Data Science. The new school has a growing, innovative population of faculty and students carrying out theoretical and applied research in Mathematics, Statistics, Data Science, Actuarial Science, and Artificial Intelligence / Machine Learning. The school’s undergraduate academic programs include degrees in Data Science, Actuarial Science, Mathematics, and Statistics. Graduate programming includes a M.S. degree in Statistics and Data Science with two tracks in Data Science and Statistical Computing and a SAS certificate program, a M.S. degree in Mathematical Science including tracks in Industrial Mathematics and Financial Mathematics, a Ph.D. in Mathematics including a track in Financial Mathematics, and a Ph.D. in Big Data Analytics including a track in Statistics. The Ph.D. in Big Data Analytics is the first Ph.D. program of its kind in the state of Florida and only one of a few across the globe and has been ranked #4 nationally by TechGuide’s Best Data Analytics Ph.D. programs in 2025.
With 70 full-time faculty, The Kanouff School serves over 120 graduate students and 800 program majors, provides prerequisite courses for colleges such as Engineering & Computer Science and Medicine, and offers General Education courses that support the broader undergraduate student community. As a significant service teaching unit, the school annually supports roughly 4,000 undergraduate FTE across more than 600 course sections of various class sizes. It is a collegial academic unit with broad representation that values collaborations and mentorship across subdisciplines. The school faculty collaborate with faculty from across the College of Sciences as well as the Institute of Artificial Intelligence, the National Center of Forensic Science, the Nanoscience and Technology Center, the College of Optics and Photonics, the College of Engineering and Computer Science, the College of Medicine, the College of Nursing, and the College of Community Innovation and Education, thus preparing our students for complex problem solving in an interdisciplinary world. For more information, visit https://sciences.ucf.edu/sdmss/.
The UCF College of Sciences (COS) is the largest college at the university and a powerhouse for the regional and national STEM workforce, spanning the natural, computational, physical, and social sciences and housing centers, institutes and initiatives that serve as hubs for research and innovation. Through sharing and applying knowledge, COS is cultivating pathways for students to solve our world’s most pressing and complex problems. With a mission to provide a world-class education in an environment where faculty, staff, and students thrive, research flourishes, and our community prospers; a number of COS academic programs are among those nationally ranked by U.S. News and World Report, Princeton Review, and others. For more information, please visit https://sciences.ucf.edu.
UCF, named one of the most innovative public universities in the nation by U.S. News & World Report, is located in Orlando, Florida and is classified as a Very High Research Activity university by the Carnegie Foundation. With more than 70,000 students, UCF is one of the largest universities in the country, offering more than 240 degree programs. UCF is an economic engine, attracting and supporting industries vital to the region's future while providing students with real-world experiences that help them succeed after graduation. For more information, visit http://www.ucf.edu.
Minimum Qualifications:
A Ph.D. in Data Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Actuarial Science, or a closely related field, from an accredited institution. In addition, to be eligible for appointment as a tenured professor upon hire, the successful applicant must have a distinguished record commensurate with a tenured faculty member at the rank of professor within the Kanouff School with respect to teaching, research, and service. Candidates will have a demonstrated record of administrative leadership in a university or similar setting for at least 2 years.
Preferred Qualifications:
Preference will be given to candidates who have demonstrated experience in:
handling faculty matters,
supervising staff,
managing budgets,
using strong communication skills,
having a distinguished record of teaching at the undergraduate and graduate levels, and
having a strong publication record reflecting experience conducting research within the disciplines of the school.
Additional Application Materials Required:
UCF requires all applications and supporting documents be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/ . In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following materials: (1) a current CV, and (2) a 2-to-3-page letter of interest that addresses the qualifications, research and leadership experience, teaching philosophy, and vision for the school.
NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.
The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.
Review of applications will begin on November 16, 2026, and will continue until the position is filled.
Questions regarding the position should be directed to Dr. Brett McCollum, Search Committee Chair, at brett.mccollum@ucf.edu.
Special Instructions to the Applicants:
All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. H-1B visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H-1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.
Job Close Date:
Open until filled.
Note to applicants: Please keep in mind that a job posted as “Open until filled” may close at any time without notice. As such, we encourage you to submit your application and all required documentation as quickly as possible to ensure consideration for the posted position.
Are you ready to unleash YOUR potential?
As a next-generation public research university and Forbes-ranked top employer in Florida, we are a community of thinkers, doers, creators, innovators, healers, and leaders striving to create broader prosperity and help shape a better future. No matter what your role is, when you join Knight Nation, you’ll play an integral role at one of the most impactful universities in the country. You’ll be met with opportunities to connect and collaborate with talented faculty, staff, and students across 13 colleges and multiple campuses, engaging in impactful work that makes a positive difference. Your time at UCF will provide you with many meaningful opportunities to grow, you’ll work alongside talented colleagues on complex projects that will challenge you and help you gain new skills and you’ll have countless rewarding experiences that go well beyond a paycheck.

Department Overview:
A premier public R1 research institution, Binghamton University contributes over $1.2 billion annually to the regional economy. The recent $113 million research award from Economic Development Agency (EDA) for battery technology innovation speaks to the university's leadership on knowledge transfer and partnerships across industrial and academia to advance technology development and innovation in science and engineering. The university attracts outstanding students and is home to award-winning faculty, many of whom are ranked in the top 2% of researchers in their respective fields, including the 2019 Nobel Laureate Dr. Stanley Whittingham in the field of Chemistry.
The Biomedical Engineering Department is particularly strong in advanced biomanufacturing, biomaterials, biomechanics, cardiovascular engineering, nanomedicine, neuroengineering, organ-on-a-chip, stem cells, tissue engineering/regenerative medicine, and wearable biosensors. The Department has recently launched a workforce training program partnered with the School of Management to develop a Biomanufacturing Project Management Certificate Program funded by BioMADE. The Department also runs a National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) PREP postdoc and graduate training program. For more information, please visit our website.
Job Description:
The Thomas J. Watson College of Engineering and Applied Science at Binghamton University invites applications for a tenured Full or Associate Professor position with an expected start date of September 1, 2027, in regenerative medicine. We are seeking national leaders in stem cell science, cell therapy, and biomanufacturing with special focus in pancreatic islet development, islet biomanufacturing, islet biology, and islet transplantation to be part of a collaborative research and education alliance between Binghamton University and Upstate Medical University. This position will carry the title of SUNY Empire Innovation Professor and is supported in part by the State University of New York (SUNY)'s Empire Innovation Program (EIP), a key initiative to recruit and retain outstanding faculty with an established track record of research and scholarship in areas of strategic priority.
We are seeking exceptional and well-established experts with outstanding track records of funded research, scholarship, teaching and service. Applications are invited from candidates in all areas of regenerative medicine, biomaterials, and tissue biofabrication. However, human pancreatic islet development, islet biomanufacturing, islet biology and islet transplantation are areas of particular interest.
Successful candidates will augment existing capabilities and expertise in regenerative medicine at Binghamton University and Upstate Medical University, build on ongoing research at both campuses and further strengthen and grow cross-institutional collaborations. They will develop and implement a robust plan to synergize and accelerate research partnerships between the Center of Biomanufacturing for Regenerative Medicine (CBRM) led by Watson College's Biomedical Engineering Department and the Basic Science and Clinical Departments at Upstate Medical University.
Successful candidates will receive a comprehensive startup package including competitive salary compensation and benefits commensurate with qualifications and experience.

We seek a scholar whose research and teaching focus on Spanish literature of the sixteenth and/or seventeenth centuries and who can contribute broadly to our undergraduate and graduate curriculum in Spanish literature and culture.
The successful candidate will be prepared to teach courses in Golden Age literature, including works by major authors such as Miguel de Cervantes, Pedro Calderón de la Barca, Garcilaso de la Vega, Luis de Góngora, Lope de Vega, Tirso de Molina, and Francisco de Quevedo. The teaching load for this position is two Spanish courses per semester.
The Department of Romance Languages consists of 30 faculty members across Spanish, French, and Italian. Our department teaches more than 1,000 students each semester and offers a variety of extracurricular programs for additional exposure to language and culture outside the classroom. Students can major or minor in any of our languages. Our Spanish division also offers three distinct courses for heritage speakers of the language. Within Harpur College of Arts and Sciences, Spanish is the second most commonly declared minor among students. We offer a range of graduate options, including 4+1 and traditional Master of Arts degrees in each of our languages, as well as a Master of Arts in Teaching in Spanish and French. Our faculty regularly collaborate with other units on campus, including the Center for Medieval and Renaissance Studies, the Translation Research and Instruction Program, the Latin American and Caribbean Studies Program, and the Linguistics Program. jobs.description:
Job Details
Job no: 530274
Position Type: Faculty Full Time
Campus: UMass Boston
Department: Nursing
Pay Grade: 05
Date opened: 01 Oct 2026 Eastern Daylight Time
Applications close:
Job Description:
The Opportunity
The Department of Nursing in the Manning College of Nursing and Health Sciences (MCNHS) at the University of Massachusetts Boston invites applications for an appointment at the rank of Associate Professor or Professor beginning September 1, 2027.
This position offers the opportunity to join a diverse community of scholars whose research is advances health equity across local and global settings. We seek an accomplished investigator with an established, externally funded program of research who will sustain and extend that work at UMass Boston, provide scholarly leadership within the Department, and mentor doctoral students and early-career faculty. The successful candidate will benefit from an established culture of collaboration and strong research infrastructure.
Our Scholarship
Nursing scholarship at UMass Boston is grounded in health equity. Our faculty conduct research where health is shaped and delivered, collaborating with communities to address health challenges locally and globally. We welcome applicants whose scholarship aligns with or expands our strengths in areas such as, aging and gerontology, maternal and child health, community-engaged research, and clinically focused science, including cardiovascular health, diabetes, and oncology.
What You Will Do
The successful candidate will:
Sustain and expand an externally funded program of research as principal investigator,
Teach and mentor student, including chairing and serving on dissertation committees
Mentor early-career faculty in research development, grant proposal preparation, and scholarly productivity
Provide leadership and service to the Department, College, University, and profession
Build and sustain research collaborations across the University and with our community partners
What You Will Bring
Required
An earned research doctorate (PhD or equivalent) in nursing or a related field
Eligibility for RN licensure in Massachusetts
A record of research, teaching, and service that merits appointment at the rank of Associate Professor or Professor with tenure at the University of Massachusetts Boston
Current extramural funding as principal investigator that can be transferred to or sustained at UMass Boston, or a clearly articulated plan to secure such funding upon arrival
Demonstrated experience mentoring doctoral students, postdoctoral fellows, and/or early-career faculty
Teaching experience in higher education
Appointment at the rank of Professor additionally requires a national or international reputation in the candidate’s area of science and a sustained history of continuous, competitive extramural funding as principal investigator. Rank and tenure status will be commensurate with the successful candidate’s record and determined through the University’s review process.
Preferred
An active award that is transferable to UMass Boston
Experience leading research teams, centers, cores, or training grants
A record of mentoring colleagues in grant proposal and manuscript development
Doctoral-level teaching and leadership of dissertation or capstone committees
What We Offer
The Manning College and its Office of Research provide internal and external mentoring for faculty, including structured support for grant proposal and manuscript preparation, alongside a wide range of multidisciplinary and interdisciplinary collaborative research opportunities. Faculty appointed at senior rank receive a competitive start-up package, and the College’s pre- and post-award research administration team supports the transfer and ongoing management of existing extramural awards.
Our faculty collaborate with major academic and medical institutions in and around Boston, including the Dana-Farber/Harvard Cancer Center, UMass Chan Medical School, Boston Children’s Hospital, the Massachusetts Department of Public Health, and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, as well as with community, public, and private health care agencies across the region. The National Cancer Institute funds the University of Massachusetts Boston–Dana-Farber/Harvard Cancer Center partnership; this longstanding collaboration has enabled faculty at both institutions to strengthen and extend partnerships for research on health disparities, PhD training, and community outreach.
Our Programs
The BS, MS, and DNP nursing programs are accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE). The MS and DNP programs prepare Family Nurse Practitioners and Adult/Gerontological Nurse Practitioners. The PhD program focuses on health equity, broadly defined.
Across all programs, our teaching addresses health across the life course among diverse populations, with a sustained focus on improving health equity for populations at risk for health care disparities. For more information, please visit https://www.umb.edu/nursing-health-sciences/
Our students
The University of Massachusetts Boston is the third most diverse university in the country, with more than 60% of our undergraduate students coming from minoritized communities and groups and more than half of our students the first in their families to attend a college or university. Our students come to us from richly diverse life experiences and backgrounds; they bring to our classrooms and research settings the robust range of perspectives growing out of the socio-cultural, economic, and historical contexts in which they have lived, along with the challenges they encounter, engage, and strive to overcome. Faculty are expected to engage and support students with diverse backgrounds and lived experiences through inclusive teaching, advising, and mentoring practices.
How To Apply
To apply, please submit the following: i) cover letter; ii) curriculum vitae (CV); iii) a statement of current and future research plans, including a summary of current and pending extramural support; iv) a statement on teaching philosophy and experience v) a minimum of three professional references, including names and contact information.
The position will remain open until filled. Questions are welcome at any point in the process. Please contact Dr. Rosemary Samia (rosemary.samia@umb.edu), Chair, Nursing Faculty Search Committee.
UMass Boston expects to pay within an approximate range between $118,500 and $190,000 for this position.
The specific pay for this position will be determined by the University based on the consideration of all relevant factors when and if it decides to extend an offer of employment.
UMass Boston is committed to the full inclusion of all qualified individuals. As part of this commitment, we will ensure that persons with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations for the hiring process. If reasonable accommodation is needed, please contact HR@umb.edu or 617-287-5150.

jobs.title: Multiple Faculty Searches
jobs.description:
Multiple Faculty Searches
Department of Physics - UC Berkeley
The Physics Department at the University of California, Berkeley is actively recruiting for multiple tenure track Assistant Professor positions. These searches are in the following areas:
​
● Atomic, Molecular, & Optical (AMO) Physics Theory: We welcome applicants from across the full range of theoretical AMO subfields, especially those who will make fundamental contributions to theory and exhibit strong synergy with experimental AMO research. Candidates from subfields in quantum simulation, many-body quantum mechanics, emergent phenomena and entangled systems, connections to quantum information science, quantum optics, precision measurement and tests of fundamental physics, ultracold molecules and chemistry, ultrafast optics, and others are encouraged to apply.
● Condensed Matter Experiment: We welcome applicants across all areas, including but not limited to, quantum magnetism, topological phases, unconventional superconductivity, spintronics, and novel quantum order arising in exotic materials in three dimensional and low dimensional systems, such as van der Waals and layered heterostructures. Areas of expertise of interest include, but are not limited to, the synthesis of bulk and thin film materials, advanced spectroscopic and scattering techniques, quantum and mesoscopic transport, and microscopic imaging and scanning probe techniques. We also encourage applications at the interface of condensed matter physics and quantum information science.
● Open Search: We welcome applicants in a broad open search in space sciences, astrophysics, and experimental nuclear and particle physics. Areas of emphasis include space sciences, theory or experiment, including space and solar plasma physics, gravitational waves, black hole imaging, gamma ray astrophysics, multi-messenger astronomy, radio cosmology, cosmic rays, and dark matter; astrophysics experiment, including gravity wave detection and space plasma physics; observational and theoretical astrophysics focused on the use and development of data science techniques and machine learning; and experimental nuclear and particle physics focused on fundamental symmetries of nature, including CP and time reversal symmetry, family and lepton number symmetries, and matter-antimatter symmetry.
Applicants must submit a separate application to each position of interest.
Berkeley Physics and its partners are committed to establishing cultures that nurture scientific identity and remove barriers to entry, in order to strengthen pathways into careers. To that end, we strive to work and learn together in a positive and inclusive environment. Please visit UC Berkeley Physics' Equity & Inclusion website for more information.
Berkeley Physics has a long history of excellence in teaching, research, and service, as well as a culture that values and promotes interdisciplinarity. It has a compelling record of national and global engagement, and benefits from strong relationships with Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and other research labs and industry.
Berkeley Physics is committed to addressing personal and family needs of faculty. For more information, refer to OFEW New Faculty site.
The University of California is committed to creating and maintaining a community dedicated to the advancement, application, and transmission of knowledge and creative endeavors through academic excellence, where all individuals who participate in university programs and activities can work and learn together in a safe and secure environment, free of violence, harassment, discrimination, exploitation, or intimidation. Consistent with this commitment, UC Berkeley requires all applicants for Senate faculty positions to complete, sign, and upload an Authorization of Information Release form into AP Recruit as part of their application. If an applicant does not include the signed authorization, the application will be considered incomplete, and as with any incomplete application, will not receive further consideration. Although all applicants for faculty recruitment must complete the entire application, applicants will only be subject to reference checks if and when they are selected as the candidate to whom the hiring unit would like to extend a formal offer. More information is available on this website.
Qualifications: PhD (or equivalent international degree) or enrolled in PhD or equivalent international degree-granting program at the time of application.
To apply:

● Open Search in Physics: https://aprecruit.berkeley.edu/JPF05524
To guarantee full consideration, applications must be received by November 15, 2026. All reference letters will be treated as confidential per University of California policy and California state law. Please refer potential referees, including when letters are provided via a third party (i.e., dossier service or career center), to the UC Berkeley Confidentiality Policy prior to submitting their letters.
Please direct questions to our Academic Personnel Office at PhysicsAP@berkeley.edu

Paid parental leave after 12 months of continuous service.
WCU offers an abundance of training and development programs, certifications, workshops and conferences – many of which are offered free of charge.
Position Summary: The primary location of this position is on the main Cullowhee, NC campus.
The Psychology Department at Western Carolina University (WCU) invites applications for a 9-month, full-time, tenure-track position at the Assistant Professor level. The projected begin work date is August 2027.
The typical teaching load for a tenure-track faculty is a 3-3 (Fall/Spring), consisting of both undergraduate and graduate courses. The area of expertise is open, but the successful candidate will show evidence of or potential for success in the teaching of general psychology, research methods, and courses in the faculty member's area of expertise. Based on department needs and faculty interest and expertise, opportunities to teach careers and issues, senior seminar, or a graduate course may also be available.
As a teacher-scholar, the successful faculty member is expected to maintain a program of meaningful disciplinary research that is engaging to both undergraduate and graduate students. Consistent with this expectation, willingness to supervise directed study courses (PSY 280/480/680), graduate thesis and dissertation research is important to this position. To support research, the psychology department has three dedicated spaces for research, including a lab with EEG equipment, as well as access to an undergraduate research participant (SONA) pool. Opportunities for collaboration within the department, college, and across the university are also encouraged and supported. Faculty in the department hold expertise in a wide range of subdisciplines within psychology, including but not limited to social psychology, developmental-, rural-, and clinical health psychology, neuroscience, cognitive psychology, human sexuality, and forensic psychology. Please see our faculty website for more information on faculty research areas and labs.
In terms of location within the university, the Psychology department is located in the College of Education and Allied Professions (CEAP). WCU is committed to the Boyer model of scholarship, stewardship of place, integrated learning, and engagement. The Psychology department is known for its engaged teaching. We pride ourselves in offering high impact practices and engagement with our surrounding community, including service learning opportunities, internships, and research collaboration. At the undergraduate level, the psychology major is one of the largest on campus, with approximately 600 students. The department is home also to three residential graduate programs in Health Service (PsyD), School (SSP), and Clinical (MA) psychology, respectively. In addition, the department contributes to the interdisciplinary minor in neuroscience. Applicants are encouraged to visit the WCU website (www.wcu.edu) and read more about the university's mission, vision, and core values.

PhD in Psychology or closely related field from an accredited institution.

Preferred Qualifications:
Position Type: Permanent Full-Time

letter of application,
current CV,
research statement
teaching statement
list of three professional references with complete contact information,
unofficial transcripts showing degree conferral dates for all degrees at the master's degree level and higher*
optional materials (e.g., evidence of teaching effectiveness, a representative publication)

Employees of WCU are provided a comprehensive benefits package as well as other resources, policies and programs to ensure a happy and healthy work/life balance. Benefit eligible employees have access to dental, vision and health insurance plans – eligibility begins on the first of the month following date of hire. Retirement plan contributions begin on the eligibility date following election and include employer contributions for either a defined contribution or a defined benefit plan. Eligible employees have access to tuition waivers for up to three courses per academic year; employee may enroll at any of the constituent UNC System campuses. Also offered are free group exercise classes multiple times per week, a discounted membership to the campus recreation center, free vaccine and booster shots offered on campus, pretax flexible spending accounts, 12 paid holidays and 24 hours of paid community service leave each year. Leave earning employees (staff and 12-month faculty) who work at least half of the working days of their first month of employment will begin accruing vacation and sick leave immediately. Paid parental leave after 12 months of continuous service.
WCU offers an abundance of training and development programs, certifications, workshops and conferences – many of which are offered free of charge.
Position Summary: The primary location of this position is on the main Cullowhee, NC campus.
The Psychology Department at Western Carolina University (WCU) invites applications for a 9-month, tenure-track faculty position at the Assistant or Associate professor level. Rank to be determined at the time of hire. Anticipated begin work date of August 2027. The typical teaching load is 3-3 (Fall/Spring), consisting of both undergraduate and graduate courses. Supervision of graduate students in the McKee Clinic and External Practicum is included in the 3/3 teaching load.
The successful candidate will show evidence of or potential for success in the teaching and supervision of students in our APA accredited post-masters Doctor of Psychology (PsyD) in Health Service Psychology program and our scientist-practitioner oriented MA program in clinical psychology. Each of these residential programs has a theoretical orientation consistent with behavioral/cognitive-behavioral foundations and accept typically 6 to 8 students per cohort. The preparation of psychologists who can serve the region, as well as expanding access to evidence-based services for those living in rural communities, is an important part of our mission. Relevant to this faculty position is our department's state-of-the art, public-facing McKee Assessment and Psychological Services Clinic, dedicated to providing advanced assessment and psychotherapy training for our graduate students (PsyD, SSP, MA) through affordable comprehensive services to individuals, families, and schools in our community. In addition to supervision of graduate students, the successful candidate would have an opportunity to teach seminar style courses in the MA and PsyD programs, and teach in the undergraduate program. Course assignments are decided based on department and program needs, as well as faculty interests and experience. To this end, the eligible candidate needs to have earned a doctorate (PhD or PsyD) in clinical or health service psychology from an APA-accredited program and be able to supervise graduate trainees as part of the teaching load. Being licensed or license eligible (near completion of post-doctoral hours) as a psychologist in North Carolina is preferred. The typical breakdown for faculty workload is 60% teaching, 20% research, and 20% service.
As a teacher scholar, the successful faculty member is expected to maintain a program of meaningful disciplinary research that is engaging to both undergraduate and graduate students. The area of research is open, however, interest and expertise in neurodevelopmental disorders such as Autism or Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), or child and adolescent psychopathology more broadly, may fill an important need in the department. In addition, the department has dedicated research spaces ('labs') for Cognitive Science, Human Neuroscience (with EEG equipment), and Health Psychology, respectively, as well as faculty expertise in substance use, maternal mental health, forensic psychology, traumatic stress, human sexuality, psycholinquistics, and developmental psychology (childhood, adolescence, and aging focus), to name a few. Additionally, the faculty member would enjoy also the many opportunities for partnering with colleagues across campus, and connect with schools-, hospitals-, non-profit organizations, research consortiums, and other service providers in the region.
At the undergraduate level, the psychology major is one WCU's largest majors with approximately 500 students. The department, college, and university offer faculty internal funding opportunities to support scholarship, conference travel, and professional development. Moreover, WCU is a 12,000-student regional comprehensive university in the University of North Carolina system. The university offers 115 undergraduate programs and more than 40 graduate programs. The campus is located in the picturesque Cullowhee valley between the Great Smoky and Blue Ridge Mountains, just minutes from the town of Sylva, public schools, recreation centers, trails, and rivers. Campus is midway between Charlotte and Atlanta, 50 miles west of Asheville, NC, a city with vibrant art, entertainment, food, and culture scenes, and 20 miles west of Waynesville, NC, the largest town in Western North Carolina with many options for dining, shopping, entertainment, and craft breweries. The entire region is noted for its excellent quality of life and access to outdoor activities.
The Department of Psychology is located in the College of Education and Allied Professions (CEAP). Psychology, CEAP, and Western Carolina University holds inclusive excellence as a core value, and we work together to foster a welcoming community, where all are respected and know they belong.

Doctorate (PhD or PsyD) in clinical or health service psychology or closely related field from an APA-accredited program.

Workload for NTL faculty includes teaching 12 credits each semester in the area of expertise and based on department needs, and fulfilling service and advising obligations each semester.

The Department of Geography in the McCausland College of Arts and Sciences at the University of South Carolina invites applications for a full-time, nine-month tenure track faculty position at the rank of Assistant Professor in GIScience, with an anticipated start date of August 16, 2027.
We seek an emerging scholar whose research and teaching engage the frontiers of GIScienceand cutting-edge geospatial technologies. Areas of interest that advance GIScience concepts, theories and/or methods include, but are not limited to, GIS modeling, digital cartography, geo-visualization, spatial statistics, GeoAI and Geospatial Intelligence, with potential topical applications in environmental hazards, human-environment interactions, sustainable development, spatial inequities, health, energy, urban planning and related fields. The successful candidate will teach four courses per academic year (two per semester) and is expected to participate in graduate student recruitment and supervision.
The Department currently comprises nineteen tenured/tenure-track faculty and one full-time instructor. Faculty research interests span resource politics, environmental hazards, human rights, coastal geomorphology, energy geographies, health, GIS and remote sensing, biogeography, migration, and climate change, with collaborations across the college, university, and beyond. In addition, the Department faculty lead several institutes and centers including the Hazards, Vulnerability and Resilience Institute (HVRI), Walker Institute of International and Area Studies, and the Center for GIScience and Geospatial Big Data. The Molinaroli College of Engineering and Computing (MCEC) at the University of South Carolina (USC) in Columbia, SC is seeking a qualified applicant for an Assistant Professor Tenure-Track faculty position to support its Mechanical Engineering program. USC andMCEC pursue a bold vision of supporting the state’s growing aerospace, manufacturing, technology, and nuclear industries while experiencing sustained growth in student numbers and research output. We aim to hire innovative and bold thought leaders focused on student success, outstanding research, and the motivation and drive to support the US and SC economy and industrial base. This 9-month faculty Assistant Professor position is tenure track with an anticipated start date of August 16, 2027.Applicants for the Assistant Professor rank should possess a PhD degree in Mechanical Engineering or closely related field, a demonstrated record of research accomplishments, and an outstanding capacity for teaching undergraduate and graduate courses. Candidates with a strong vision for the future of engineering education are highly encouraged to apply.Successful candidates will be expected to develop internationally recognized, externally funded research programs in cutting edge areas of mechanical engineering. In particular, candidates with a strong track record of research and teaching in the broad field of solid mechanics and mechanics of materials are encouraged to apply. Areas of particular interest include, but are not limited to, mechanics for extreme environments and nuclear applications; mechanics-informed advanced manufacturing; integrated experimental and computational mechanics; fracture, damage, and failure; and transformative AI-enabled advances that deliver fundamentally new capabilities in these areas or in solid mechanics more broadly.The successful candidates must have the ability to (1) teach and develop Mechanical Engineering curriculum (including lecture, laboratory, or design courses) at the undergraduate and graduate levels, (2) develop and sustain an independent, nationally recognized research program, (3) collaborate within multi-disciplinary teams of faculty and other researchers across colleges and institutions, and (4) be engaged in professional activities.USC is a Flagship, R1 research university experiencing sustained growth in number of students and research. The Molinaroli College of Engineering and Computing has seven academic departments with over 40 academic programs, more than 3,600 undergraduate students, and received over $73m of competitive federal sponsored research awards in 2025. jobs.title: Assistant Professor in Mechanical Engineering
jobs.description:
Job Details
Position OverviewThe University of Kansas (KU) Department of Mechanical Engineering (ME) is seeking outstanding candidates for multiple tenure-track faculty positions at the rank of Assistant Professor. We seek dynamic and innovative scholars who are passionate about collaborative research, excellence in teaching, and advancing the field of mechanical engineering through impactful research and education.
The department welcomes applicants whose research complements and expands existing strengths within the department. The examples below illustrate areas of potential interest.
Mechanics, materials, and manufacturing: solid and computational mechanics, advanced materials, advanced manufacturing
Energy and transport: energy systems, thermal and fluid sciences, sustainability
Robotics and intelligent systems: robotics, autonomous vehicles, controls
Emerging and interdisciplinary areas: research connecting mechanical engineering with health, climate, infrastructure, or other fields
Outstanding candidates in other mechanical engineering fields may also be considered. Candidates whose work bridges traditional mechanical engineering disciplines or promotes interdisciplinary collaboration are especially encouraged to apply.
The Assistant Professor position is subject to a collective bargaining agreement between The University of Kansas and United Academics. UAKU is the exclusive representative for the bargaining unit, and it is the candidate’s right to be a member or not be a member of a union without fear of personal or professional repercussions.
Applications are sought from candidates with earned doctorates in mechanical engineering or closely related fields by the time of appointment. Successful candidates are expected to contribute to the development of academic programs and a strong research program. Successful candidates will be results-oriented, have a record of superior scholarship, have demonstrated potential to develop an externally-funded research program, and teach high-quality courses at both the undergraduate and graduate levels. The KU ME Department currently has programs leading to bachelor's, master's, and doctoral degrees. Increasing research innovation and collaborations to make a difference in the world are priorities in the department.
The KU School of Engineering has embarked on a strategic plan that leads to significant expansion while maintaining and improving the existing high-quality student programs. This approach drives growth in facilities, faculty, students, leadership, and research as it helps industry partners find the new talent, designs, and techniques they need to fuel economic growth and business success. The KU School of Engineering is most interested in applicants committed to excellence who can contribute to the University’s innovative, collaborative, and multidisciplinary initiatives to educate leaders, build healthy and vibrant communities, and make discoveries that will change the world.Job DescriptionPosition Overview continued:
KU's main campus is considered one of the most beautiful in the nation; located in Lawrence, a thriving city of 97,000, 30 minutes west of Kansas City in the forested hills of eastern Kansas. At KU we make it our mission to educate leaders, build healthy communities, and make discoveries that change the world. We aspire to be an exceptional learning community that lifts each other and advances society. KU’s strategic plan Jayhawks Rising is focused on objectives to accomplish this vision through three mission-based priorities of student success, healthy and vibrant communities, research, and discovery. KU’s excellence is a result of the rich tapestry of experiences, perspectives, and backgrounds of our faculty, staff, students, and colleagues from across our nation and the globe. At KU, we invest in continuous learning and growth by creating a climate where people engage in respectful dialogue and debate, and support each other’s success. We foster a culture of care where each person is seen, heard and valued. When people feel a true sense of belonging, we believe they are better able to reach their full potential and achieve remarkable things. The successful candidate must be eligible to work in the U.S. by the effective date of the appointment.
Screening of applications will begin on November 9, 2026 and continue until a qualified pool of applicants is received. The target start date is August 18, 2027.

jobs.title: Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor of Pathology (Molecular Genetic Pathology)
jobs.description:
Job Details
The Stanford Department of Pathology seeks an outstanding MD, MD/PhD, or PhD with expertise in Molecular Genetic Pathology for appointment at the rank of Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor in the University Medical Line or Clinician Educator Line. Board eligibility or equivalent training in Molecular Genetic Pathology or Laboratory Genetics and Genomics is required. The successful candidate will participate in the clinical reporting of high complexity molecular tests predominantly for solid tumors and hematologic neoplasms. The MGP faculty contribute to the education of pathology residents and fellows, including up to four Molecular Genetic Pathology fellows and two Laboratory Genetics and Genomics fellows each year. Opportunity is available to participate in test development toward a shared vision of comprehensive somatic and germline testing for serving our patients.
Stanford Medicine leads the biomedical revolution in precision health and recognizes that continued success will require world-leading innovation in patient care across all aspects of pathology. The Department of Pathology fully embraces this inspired vision as we collaborate closely with our colleagues in Stanford Health Care, Stanford Children’s Health, and Stanford University School of Medicine. We seek experienced and ambitious colleagues who are enthusiastic about our vision and commit to our collaborative culture. If you are interested in advancing precision health at one of the greatest universities in the world, situated in the most dynamic and entrepreneurial region of the U.S., and currently undergoing major inpatient and outpatient expansions, then join us.
The major criteria for appointment for faculty in the University Medical Line shall be excellence in the overall mix of clinical care, clinical teaching, scholarly activity that advances clinical medicine, and institutional service appropriate to the programmatic need the individual is expected to fulfill. The major criterion for appointment as Clinician Educators is excellence in the overall mix of clinical care, teaching, administrative and/or scholarship appropriate to the programmatic need the individual is expected to fulfill. Academic rank and line will be determined by the qualifications and experience of the successful candidate.
Successful candidates will join the faculty in the Department of Pathology, which currently includes a Nobel laureate, multiple members of the National Academies, and many other investigators with national and international distinctions. In conjunction with its outstanding research program, the Department of Pathology educates outstanding graduate students, residents and fellows and is responsible annually for over 20 million laboratory tests and over 200,000 anatomic pathology specimens spanning 12 subspecialties.
Applicants should submit a curriculum vitae, cover letter, brief description of plans for future research, and a list of 3 references to Faculty Positions Application Link. Letters should be addressed to Thomas J. Montine, MD, PhD, Chair, Department of Pathology.

jobs.title: Open Rank Faculty Position in Smart Manufacturing
jobs.description:
Job Details
The School of Engineering (https://engineering.stanford.edu/) at Stanford University invites applicants for an all-ranks faculty search in the area of Smart Manufacturing. The appointment will be at the tenure-track assistant professor, tenure-track or tenured associate professor, or tenured full professor rank. The primary home department will be one of the nine departments in the School of Engineering (https://engineering.stanford.edu/faculty-research/departments) and will be determined during the search process.
Manufacturing is being transformed by the convergence of advances in sensing, autonomy, materials science, data infrastructure, artificial intelligence, optimization, and human-machine collaboration. These technologies are reshaping how physical products are designed, produced, monitored, and improved, blurring the boundary between the digital and physical worlds. This shift is enabling new levels of automation, adaptability, and sustainability across the manufacturing lifecycle from individual unit processes to entire supply networks, creating rich opportunities for cross-disciplinary collaboration across engineering and beyond.
We invite applications from individuals pursuing research in Smart Manufacturing, broadly defined to include topics such as advanced and additive manufacturing, in-situ sensing and closed-loop process control, AI-driven design and defect detection, digital twins, robotics and automation, cyber-physical production systems, industrialized construction, sustainable and circular manufacturing, and data-driven operations and supply chains. Candidates can be conducting this work in the context of any engineering discipline.
Successful candidates should be conducting world-class research and translating their results into real-world impact in their domain (or, for junior candidates, have demonstrated potential to do so). In addition to excellence in research, we expect candidates to be or become educational leaders in advanced manufacturing topics and to effectively communicate the role of advanced and smart technologies in shaping the future of manufacturing, including considering its broader societal impacts.
Applicants must have completed, or be completing, a Ph.D. in the advertised field or a closely related one. Evidence of the ability to pursue a program of research, and a strong commitment to graduate and undergraduate teaching are also required. A successful candidate will be expected to teach courses at the graduate and undergraduate levels and to build and lead a team of graduate students in Ph.D. research.
The School of Engineering and Stanford University value faculty who will help foster an open and respectful academic environment for colleagues, students, and staff with a wide range of backgrounds and perspectives. Candidates may choose to include as part of their research and teaching statements a brief discussion about how their work and experience further these values.
Applications should include the following materials:
Cover letter
CV
Brief statements of research and teaching interests (3-5 pages total for both combined). Candidates are encouraged to describe not only their accomplishments but also specific planned research projects and courses that they might like to teach.
Two representative publications
Names and e-mail addresses of 3-5 references. If a candidate currently holds a tenured faculty appointment, their references will only be contacted if they are short-listed. For all other applicants, references will be contacted immediately upon the submission of the application.
In the cover letter, applicants should identify potential home department(s) in the School of Engineering. In addition to applying to this search, if a potential home department has an active search at their rank, applicants should also apply to the departmental search and indicate in that application that they have also applied to the Smart Manufacturing search.

The Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Temerty Faculty of Medicine at the University of Toronto, and the Division of Gynecologic Oncology at Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre are seeking a full-time Gynecologic Oncologist. The successful candidate will have an academic position description as a Clinician Investigator, Clinician Educator, or Clinician Quality Improvement and must be eligible for a full-time clinical academic appointment at the rank of Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, or Professor at the University of Toronto. The anticipated start date is July 1, 2027, or another mutually agreeable date.
The University of Toronto Division of Gynecologic Oncology provides comprehensive, multidisciplinary care to patients with gynecologic malignancies and is committed to excellence in clinical care, teaching, clinical trials, and research. The Division includes more than 20 Gynecologic Oncologists across four affiliated cancer centres, serving a metropolitan population of more than 6.5 million people.
The successful candidate will join an established team of six Gynecologic Oncologists based at Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre, a fully affiliated teaching hospital of the University of Toronto and home to the Odette Cancer Centre and Sunnybrook Research Institute.
As a member of an accomplished interprofessional team, the successful candidate will demonstrate a strong commitment to collegial and collaborative practice, with excellent communication skills and a passion for delivering outstanding patient care in a multidisciplinary environment. We are seeking a candidate with an excellent track record of academic productivity and peer-reviewed publications who will continue to contribute to a strong and sustained research program. The successful candidate will also demonstrate advanced surgical skills, including expertise in open and minimally invasive (laparoscopic and robotic) surgery.
Enthusiastic participation in all levels of our teaching and education mandate, including undergraduate, residency, and fellowship education, is expected. The successful candidate will promote and demonstrate excellence in professional practice and conduct.
Candidates must be licensed, or eligible for licensure with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario. Qualified applicants must be certified, or eligible for certification, in the subspecialty of Gynecologic Oncology by the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada (RCPSC), or have completed equivalent regulated subspecialty training in Gynecologic Oncology, in addition to an MD degree.

This unique position provides an exceptional opportunity for a dynamic researcher to thrive in a collaborative environment at the forefront of nuclear science.
In this role, your professional efforts will be split between the Facility for Rare Isotope Beams (FRIB) at Michigan State University (MSU) and the local facilities at NC State and the Triangle Universities Nuclear Laboratory (TUNL), located in Durham, North Carolina. jobs.title: Assistant/Associate Professor of Philosophy, Fall 2027
jobs.description:
Job Details
Assistant/Associate Professor of Philosophy, Fall 2027
Location:
Knoxville, Tennessee
Open Date:
Oct 1, 2026
Description:
The Department of Philosophy at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville invites applications for a tenure-line position at the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor, beginning Fall 2027. The Knoxville campus of the University of Tennessee is on the academic semester system, and the default teaching load is two courses per semester, totaling four per year. Research and teaching expectations are high. Tenure-line faculty in the department are highly research-active. Teaching expectations include undergraduate courses at all levels, graduate teaching in area(s) of specialization and competence, and mentoring of student research at all levels, including directing theses and serving on thesis committees. Faculty are also responsible for service to the department, university, and profession, of a kind and degree appropriate to rank. Interest in exploring the possibility of developing a new logic lab on campus would be desirable. UTK is a land-grant university and values publicly-engaged research, teaching, and service, and considers evidence of commitment to public engagement in the records of applicants.
Qualifications:
PhD in Philosophy must be completed by the position start date, 8/1/2027. Some preference will be given to candidates at the advanced Assistant or early Associate level. Candidates for appointment at the Assistant Professor level must demonstrate potential to develop a sustained record of excellence in teaching and research. Candidates for appointment at the Associate Professor level must demonstrate a sustained record of excellence in teaching and research, as well as a record of significant service.
Area of Specialization: Philosophy of Language or Logic
Area of Competency: Open but ability to teach PHIL 235 (Formal Logic) is required. Highly desirable would be one or more of (i) ability to teach PHIL 435 (Intermediate Formal Logic, required for all Ph.D. students); (ii) ability to contribute to some interdisciplinary area (e.g. linguistics, neuroscience, AI, game development); (iii) ability to contribute to the department's degree concentrations in Legal and Political Philosophy or Philosophy of Science and Medicine.
This position is part of UTK's "Envisioning and Narrating Emerging Futures" hiring constellation; for details see https://artsci.utk.edu/about/employment/
Application Instructions:
Please submit (i) a cover letter, which should include some discussion of possible service contributions to the department; (ii) a CV; (iii) a fully anonymized research statement; (iv) a fully anonymized writing sample of 5000-10000 words; (v) at least three letters of recommendation; and (vi) a teaching portfolio that includes a teaching statement, representative syllabi in the candidate's AOS, and other evidence of teaching effectiveness. About Murray State:
Murray State blends educational opportunities found at research institutions with collaborative interactions among students, faculty and staff found at smaller universities. Students receive personalized attention from supportive faculty and staff as the University offers a 16:1 student-to-faculty ratio. Murray State University places our highest priority on student learning and excellent teaching, blending the range of educational opportunities often experienced at research institutions with the nurturing student-teacher interactions usually found at smaller universities.
Located in the West Kentucky region, Murray State University is a public, comprehensive University which offers a low cost of living, low property taxes, and a four-season climate. Murray has a friendly, small-town atmosphere with locally-owned specialty shops and restaurants, an acclaimed community theater, art guild and award-winning public schools. The area is home to Kentucky Lake and Land Between the Lakes, a 170,000-acre National Recreation Area, which offers a wide-range of activities and amenities for residents and visitors alike. jobs.description:
Job Details
EEO Statement :
The University of Nebraska does not discriminate based on race, color, ethnicity, national origin, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, disability, age, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, and/or political affiliation in its programs, activities, or employment. See: Notice of Nondiscrimination
Working Title:
Open Rank Professor - Plant Metabolism
Department:
Biochemistry-0831
Requisition Number:
F_260106
Posting Open Date:
10/01/2026
Application Review Date: (To ensure consideration, please submit all application materials before review date):
11/02/2026
Open Until Filled:
Yes
Description of Work:
The Department of Biochemistry and the Center for Plant Science Innovation at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln (UNL) invite applications for a tenure-track nine-month (academic year) faculty position of open rank (assistant/associate/full professor). This appointment is apportioned as 80% research and 20% teaching. Applicants are sought who will develop a vigorous, internationally recognized research program that seeks to identify novel metabolic pathways, regulatory mechanisms and/or biological processes with the goal of translating findings into strategies for crop improvement and/or bio-based products that support sustainable agriculture and biotechnology to enhance human health. Researchers will be able to leverage UNL’s extensive research infrastructure that includes the Plant Transformation Core Research Facility (PTCRF), multi-location biotech fields, and advanced field and greenhouse phenotyping platforms, to validate and scale their discoveries.
The Department of Biochemistry provides a robust environment for molecular research, offering access to state-of-the-art resources through shared equipment and the Nebraska Center for Biotechnology. Candidates will have the opportunity to utilize the UNL Cryo-EM facility for structural biology, mass spectrometry for metabolomics and proteomics, and bioinformatics and systems biology computational resources.
The university offers a highly collaborative environment to develop plant-focused research programs with affiliated resources provided by the University Research Centers (Center for Plant Science Innovation, Center for Integrated Biomolecular Communication, Redox Biology Center, Center for Virology), Holland Computing Center, the Quantitative Life Sciences Initiative, Nebraska Innovation Campus and the Center for Biological Chemistry and Complex Biosystems graduate training programs. The University Research Centers and UNL provide cutting-edge research facilities that support multiple-omics, bioinformatics, supercomputing, flow cytometry, confocal microscopy, TEM, SEM, and metabolic engineering. A competitive start-up package and appropriate laboratory and office space will be offered.
About Us
To learn about UNL benefits and your total compensation, please see: https://go.unl.edu/aboutus.
To learn more about Lincoln, NE at About Lincoln | Nebraska.
Minimum Required Qualifications:
Ph.D. or equivalent degree in biochemistry, plant science, or a related field.
Two or more years of postdoctoral experience.
Strong record of original research in plant biochemistry as evidenced by peer-reviewed publications.
Preferred Qualifications:
Experience in grant writing.
Experience teaching in biochemistry or related fields.
Experience with mentoring students.
Excellent communication skills.
Expertise in integrated biochemical, structural, and molecular genetic approaches in plant metabolism.
Demonstrated potential for collaborative research.
Work Location (City, State):
Lincoln, NE
How to Apply:
Click “Apply for this Job” and then “Faculty Application.” Complete the application and attach the following documents:
A letter of interest that describes your qualifications for the job and anticipated contributions.
Your curriculum vitae.
Contact information for three professional references.
