jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Mathematics, Academic General Faculty
jobs.description:
Job Details
Description
The University of Virginia’s Department of Mathematics invites applications for an Assistant Professor (General Faculty) expected to begin August 10, 2027. We are particularly interested in candidates whose career focus is on teaching and learning mathematics and are prepared to contribute to the leadership of our teaching mission in our lower division. The core responsibilities of this position include teaching six courses per year (three each during the spring and fall terms). Additional duties will include serving as a mentor for graduate TAs, providing leadership in our teaching mission, and coordinating the department’s Calculus I & II course offerings. This is a continuing three-year, tenure-ineligible appointment with the possibility but not the guarantee of renewal.
The Department of Mathematics' General Faculty team is a dynamic group that works together to implement evidence-based teaching practices to improve student outcomes in coordinated introductory mathematics courses. Opportunities to participate in graduate TA professional development and/or re-design efforts to improve existing courses may be available.
Qualifiations
Minimum qualifications
By the start of the appointment, applicants must hold a Ph.D. in Mathematics, Mathematics Education, or a related field and have at least 2 years of college-level teaching experience in Mathematics, inclusive of teaching done as a graduate student.
Preferred qualifications.
Desirable qualifications include experience coordinating multi-section courses, experience working in a team environment, experience working with students from a wide variety of backgrounds, experience mentoring/developing graduate TAs, and familiarity with the Scholarship of Teaching and Learning (SoTL) in mathematics.
Application Instructions
To apply, click on Interfolio and submit the following documents:
1. A cover letter describing your skills and experience in the teaching and learning of mathematics and why you are interested in this position. (1-2 pages)
2. A curriculum vitae with the contact information for at least three references.
3. A teaching portfolio. The portfolio should include a statement of your teaching philosophy and provide the committee with a clear picture of your approach to teaching and student learning. Additional materials that illustrate their experience and development as educators are welcome. This might include brief descriptions of curriculum or course design, teaching practices, approaches to assessment, or other examples of effective teaching and learning.
4. Contact information for 3 references.
In addition, please submit the following required documents electronically through www.MathJobs.org:
1. A cover letter describing your skills and experience in the teaching and learning of mathematics and why you are interested in this position.
2. An AMS Standard Cover Sheet.
3. A curriculum vitae.
4. A teaching portfolio that will help the committee understand your approach to teaching andlearning. This should contain a personal teaching philosophy. It could include brief descriptions of curriculum design and/or other teaching and learning innovations and practices that reflect who you are.
5. Three letters of reference that address teaching.
Review of applications begins on December 6th and will continue until the position is filled. We will only consider complete applications.
The university will perform background checks on all new hires prior to employment.
Questions about this position should be directed to Professor James Rolf at jsr2pz@virginia.edu

Candidates should utilize interdisciplinary humanities approaches for analyzing, participating, and creating in games studies.
We welcome approaches that engage in games studies’ major intellectual strands, such as game narratives and narrative critique, game aesthetics, ludology, critical making, design, technology studies, or the rhetoric of games and gaming.
We seek candidates who are confident in producing cross-disciplinary, collaborative, and experimental games research. Strong evidence of leadership and participation in game studies programs and initiatives will show a collaborative model for academic work. Public outreach, the sharing of resources, and community building will demonstrate generosity and engagement.
Candidates who apply for this position should demonstrate the traits described above and have a significant investment in critical game studies. They will work regularly with hands-on games studies methods, have a strong record of collaboration and working across disciplinary areas, and read and produce critical game studies scholarship. They may also have expertise in a complementary area of interest that would find a home in a department of English and comparative literature.

The Department of Epidemiology is one of the eight departments located in the Gillings School of Global Public Health, the number one ranked public school of Public Health in the US. The achievements of our faculty, staff, students, and alumni contribute to the department’s standing among the leading academic departments of epidemiology in the world. Position Summary:
Application review will begin September 15 and continue until positions are filled.
One or two full-time tenure-track faculty positions in the rank of Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor (open rank) in the Department of Epidemiology.
Competitive candidates will demonstrate strong capacity for research that impacts public health, advances the field of epidemiology, and contributes to the department’s teaching mission. As members of the Department of Epidemiology at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, faculty are expected to develop independently funded research portfolios, contribute impactful scholarly products, mentor master’s and doctoral students, and teach core epidemiology methods and/or substantive area courses in epidemiology.
The department’s primary focus is the development and application of research methods to understand the patterns and causes of health and disease, and the application of that knowledge to improving the health of populations. The department provides strong training in research methods and opportunities to apply epidemiology to a wide range of health problems.
Minimum Education and Experience Requirements:
PhD or equivalent degree in Epidemiology or a closely related field prepared to conduct independent research, contribute high-quality teaching, and mentor student training in epidemiology research.
Preferred Qualifications, Competencies, and Experience:
Tenure-track faculty at all levels are expected to demonstrate excellence in teaching, service and scholarship through their scholarly contributions to science, capacity to obtain extramural funding that supports independent research, classroom instruction, and mentoring master’s and doctoral students. Candidates for the rank of Associate Professor must additionally demonstrate research leadership through funded epidemiologic research (in the role of PI/MPI role on grants or contracts) and a track record for training graduate students (demonstrated through both mentoring and teaching). Candidates for the rank of Full Professor must further demonstrate excellence in scholarship with national or international recognition, research leadership with sustained research funding (in the role of PI/MPI on grants or contracts).

Applications should be submitted electronically through the following website: https://unc.peopleadmin.com/postings/323620

Job Details
Assistant Professor of Criminal Justice
Job ID: 304032
Location: Kennesaw, Georgia
Full/Part Time: Full Time

About Us
For more than 60 years, Kennesaw State University has been known for its entrepreneurial spirit and sense of community. A leader in innovative teaching and learning, Kennesaw State is located just north of Atlanta and combines a suburban setting on two metro-Atlanta campuses in Kennesaw and Marietta. As one of Georgia's largest universities, Kennesaw State offers undergraduate and graduate degrees to over 50,000 students. Our high-impact research and Division I athletics also draw students from throughout the region and across the globe. A member of the University System of Georgia, Kennesaw State is a Carnegie-designated doctoral research institution (R2) committed to becoming a world-class academic institution positioned to broaden its academic and research missions and expand its scope on a local, regional, and national level.
Our university's vibrant culture, career opportunities, rich benefits, and values of respect, integrity, collaboration, inclusivity, and accountability make us an employer of choice. As part of the University System of Georgia, Kennesaw State exemplifies the power and promise of a student-centered, research-driven university. In addition, Kennesaw State supports the University of Georgia's core values of accountability, excellence, integrity, and respect. We are searching for talented people to join Kennesaw State University in our vision. For more information, visit the Kennesaw State University website.
Location
Our Kennesaw campus is located at 1000 Chastain Road NW, Kennesaw, GA 30144. Our Marietta campus is located at 1100 South Marietta Parkway, Marietta, GA 30060.
Department Information
We are a collective of interdisciplinary and community-engaged scholars committed to investigating and addressing social problems, which are broadly defined as conditions or behaviors that have a negative impact on society. We examine and understand these problems using scientific approaches, including applied, theoretical, and evaluation research. Faculty expertise broadly includes sociological, criminological, and criminal justice research areas related to social harms, social organization and disorganization, policing, courts, and correctional systems, life course sociology and criminology, causes and correlates of crime and deviance, responses to crime, laws, policies, and practices, and myriad forms of inequality. Finally, SCJ faculty are scholars and teachers committed to excellence in teaching and mentorship to ensure our graduates are ready for life and work after college. Faculty in the department engage in multiple forms of experiential education and high-impact practices to synthesize their teaching, research, and service roles.
With more than 400 full-time faculty and 8,100 degree-seeking students, the Norman J. Radow College of Humanities & Social Sciences is dedicated to pioneering workforce readiness in the humanities and social sciences. By staying true to our Liberal Arts values and integrating practical knowledge and experiential learning into our curriculum, we empower our students to become responsible citizens ready for the demands of the modern workplace. The home of three schools and eight departments, the College offers more than 80 graduate and undergraduate programs of study in both traditional and interdisciplinary fields. These programs enable students to develop leadership, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills, as well as a strong sense of civic engagement.
The College is committed to the success of our students, faculty, staff and communities. We seek candidates whose experience has prepared them to fulfill that commitment and engage our students, partners, and stakeholders effectively.
Job Summary
Kennesaw State University is now accepting applications for a full-time, tenure track faculty position as Assistant Professor of Criminal Justice in the Department of Sociology and Criminal Justice with a preferred start date of August 2027. This is a nine-month contracted position and is for work to be performed in the state of Georgia.
Responsibilities
Teach required undergraduate and graduate courses in criminal justice in the Department of Sociology and Criminal Justice, including in the M.S. in Criminal Justice program, along with elective courses aligned with the candidate's expertise and departmental needs.
KSU uses a differentiated workload model. The baseline teaching workload is 9 credit hours (i.e., 3 courses) per semester.
Teach courses across varying modalities (face-to-face, hybrid and online) and class sizes (including large class sizes) on the Kennesaw and/or Marietta campuses.
Maintain a productive, high-impact program of research and scholarship.
Pursue external funding in support of research and scholarly activity.
Engage and mentor undergraduate and graduate students in research that supports their academic and professional development.
Contribute service to the department, college and university.
Teaching assignments will be based on earned degrees and SACSCOC Faculty Credentials Guidelines.
Required Qualifications
An earned doctoral degree, or the foreign equivalent, in Criminal Justice, Criminology, or a closely related discipline is required at the time of hire.
Demonstrated training and expertise in the criminal justice system, as evidenced by graduate coursework, publications, and/or presentations.
Demonstrated experience teaching criminal justice courses and/or data analytics/statistics, or demonstrated preparation to do so.
Demonstrated productivity in research and scholarship, as evidenced by publications, presentations and/or scholarly work.
Preferred Qualifications
A substantive research agenda in one or more subfields: policing, data analytics & visualization, criminal justice policy.
Demonstrated potential for, or a record of, securing external research funding.
Ability to teach courses that serve undergraduate and graduate Criminal Justice programs.
Demonstrated record of effective teaching across multiple modalities (face-to-face, online and hybrid).
Required Documents to Attach
CV
Cover Letter (3 page max) outlining how the candidate meets the required and preferred qualifications, as well as their (a) research interests and future research plans and (b) teaching philosophy, evidence of teaching effectiveness, and efforts to facilitate student success.
Unofficial Transcripts (Official Transcripts and Official International Course-by-Course Evaluations Due Upon Hire)
Names, phone numbers, and email addresses of at least 3 references
The full text of up to 3 representative publications, preprints, or scholarly works in progress (Upload as Writing Sample)
Incomplete applications will not be considered.
Apply Before Date
Review of applications will begin immediately. For full consideration, please apply by November 1, 2026.

For questions about this faculty opening, please contact Dr. James McCafferty, jmccaff4@kennesaw.edu.
For technical support or assistance completing a job application, please contact the Shared Services Center at (877) 251-2644 or support@usg.edu.
For questions about a specific job posting at Kennesaw State University, please contact the search chair listed under the contact information section on each posting. For general questions about faculty jobs please email facultyjobs@kennesaw.edu.
USG Core Values
The University System of Georgia is comprised of our 25 institutions of higher education and learning as well as the System Office. Our USG Statement of Core Values are Integrity, Excellence, Accountability, and Respect. These values serve as the foundation for all that we do as an organization, and each USG community member is responsible for demonstrating and upholding these standards. The Institute serves more than 45,000 students through top-ranked undergraduate, graduate, and executive programs in engineering, computing, science, business, design, and liberal arts. Georgia Tech's faculty attracted more than $1.4 billion in research awards this past year in fields ranging from biomedical technology to artificial intelligence, energy, sustainability, semiconductors, neuroscience, and national security. Georgia Tech ranks among the nation's top 20 universities for research and development spending and No. 1 among institutions without a medical school.
Georgia Tech's Mission and Values
Georgia Tech's mission is to develop leaders who advance technology and improve the human condition. The Institute has nine key values that are foundational to everything we do:
1. Students are our top priority.
2. We strive for excellence.
3. We thrive on diversity.
4. We celebrate collaboration.
5. We champion innovation.
6. We safeguard freedom of inquiry and expression.
7. We nurture the wellbeing of our community.
8. We act ethically.
9. We are responsible stewards.
Over the next decade, Georgia Tech will become an example of inclusive innovation, a leading technological research university of unmatched scale, relentlessly committed to serving the public good; breaking new ground in addressing the biggest local, national, and global challenges and opportunities of our time; making technology broadly accessible; and developing exceptional, principled leaders from all backgrounds ready to produce novel ideas and create solutions with real human impact.
Department Information
The Office of the Vice Provost for AI in Education at the Georgia Institute of Technology (https://provost.gatech.edu) in Atlanta, Georgia invites applications for an open-rank Academic Professional position in Academic AI. Applicants will be considered at all ranks.
The Director of Academic AI serves as the senior operating leader of the Office of the Vice Provost for AI in Education and partners closely with the Vice Provost to execute Georgia Tech's Academic AI Strategy. The position leads the office's governance architecture, directs a portfolio of initiatives from incubation through pilot implementation to institutional adoption, and oversees the reporting cycle through which progress is communicated to the Provost. The Director facilitates collaboration and shared processes with key institutional partners, including the Office of Information Technology, Communications, Legal and Compliance, Procurement, the Center for Teaching and Learning, and college leadership.
The Director provides strategic decision support related to process design, prioritization, and resource allocation within the Office of the Vice Provost and represents the office in the Vice Provost's absence. The successful candidate will contribute substantively to the intellectual and operational work of the unit by developing frameworks, authoring guidance and analyses, and building institutional capabilities that advance the effective and responsible integration of artificial intelligence in education.
Candidates are expected to demonstrate an exceptional commitment to the teaching and mentoring of students.
Georgia Tech prides itself on its technological resources, collaborations, high-quality student body, and its commitment to building an outstanding community of learning, discovery, and creation. We strongly encourage applicants whose values align with our institutional values. These values include academic excellence, freedom of expression and inquiry, innovation, collaboration, and ethical behavior and stewardship. Georgia Tech has policies to promote a healthy work-life balance and is aware that attracting faculty may require meeting the needs of two careers.
Responsibilities
Strategic Leadership and Planning
Support implementation of the Academic AI Strategic Plan, translating goals into sequenced work with named owners, milestones, and measures of success.
Advise the Vice Provost on priorities, tradeoffs, and risks, and prepare the analysis on which consequential decisions rest.
Identify where strategy, policy, or capacity is missing and develop proposals to address it; contribute to drafting institutional guidance on academic uses of AI.
Governance Leadership
Direct the unit's governance apparatus (a Steering Committee, initiative groups, and working subcommittees on a staggered monthly cadence), setting agendas with the Vice Provost and authoring the substantive pre-reads while delegating scheduling, rosters, and production to program support staff.
Document decisions and unresolved disagreements, and drive action items to completion across units whose owners do not report to this position.
Resolve questions of process independently; escalate matters of institutional policy, novel precedent, or significant resource commitment.
Portfolio Leadership: Incubator, Accelerator, and Adoption
Manage the pipeline through which AI proposals move from inquiry to pilot to adoption, including entry criteria, stage gates, and exit decisions.
Recommend which projects receive funding, credits, staffing, or sponsorship, and make the case to governance bodies; administer microgrant and seed funding programs.
Identify appropriate metrics for pilot projects, lead evaluation sessions, and recommend continuation, scaling, or discontinuation.
Maintain the Incubator resource toolbox (credits, tooling, student talent, compliance requirements, approval pathways) so routine inquiries resolve without convening committees.
Institutional Partnership and Representation
Collaborate with counterparts in OIT, Communications, Legal and Compliance, Procurement, CTL, and college leadership, negotiating shared processes and resolving jurisdictional questions.
Represent the office in institutional committees and briefings where the Vice Provost is not present, and Georgia Tech in consortia and peer networks.
Equip college representatives for their liaison and change management roles with materials, FAQs, and consistent messaging; contribute to the professional record through presentations or practitioner publications.
Assessment and Reporting
Manage the reporting cycle through which goal and objective owners report progress to the Steering Committee and institutional leadership.
Author consolidated analyses for provost-level review that render judgment: what is working, what is not, and what should change.
Identify the measures by which the strategy is evaluated, and flag gaps, duplicated effort, and emerging risks to those positioned to act.
Required Qualifications
This position vacancy is an open rank announcement. The final job offer will be dependent on candidate qualifications in alignment with Non-tenure Track Academic Faculty ranks as outlined in section 3.2.2 of the Georgia Tech Faculty Handbook: https://www.policylibrary.gatech.edu/faculty-handbook/3.2.2-non-tenure-track-academic-faculty-members-hiring-and-promotion-guidelines
Academic Professional
Terminal degree.
Quality of performance and potential development must be recognized by peers.
Senior Academic Professional
Terminal degree.
Evidence of superior performance in the chosen field.
Recognition by peers (whether national, regional, or local).
Successful and measurable related experience.
Five (5) years or more as an Academic Professional (or equivalent rank).
Principal Academic Professional
Terminal degree.
Evidence of superior performance in the chosen field.
Recognition by peers (whether national, regional, or local).
Successful and measurable related experience supervising others' work.
Successful and measurable related experience in a position of significant responsibility and authority within a program area.
Demonstrated impact.
Six (6) years or more as a Senior Academic Professional (or equivalent rank).
Preferred Qualifications
Demonstrated success working across organizational units without formal authority over participants, and building programs where the structure did not previously exist rather than administering established ones
Supervisory experience, including hiring, onboarding, and managing staff or student employees
Working fluency with generative AI tools and the AI in higher education landscape sufficient to evaluate proposals and advise faculty credibly
Writing and analytic skill sufficient to produce governance documentation and institutional analysis for senior leadership with minimal revision
Experience with formal governance bodies at the institutional level
Familiarity with institutional procurement, IT security review, or research compliance processes
Experience in a startup or newly established unit within a large institution
Teaching, instructional design, or program evaluation experience
Experience managing budgets, grant programs, or seed funding portfolios
Record of external presentation or publication on AI or higher education administration
Required Documents to Attach
Applicants should submit CV or Resume and Cover Letter.
Application materials should be submitted as .PDF files via https://hr.gatech.edu/careers/.
Requests for information may be directed to David Joyner (david.joyner@gatech.edu).

The School's Strategic Vision is available at https://www.ce.gatech.edu/strategic-vision The 2027 U.S. News and World Report rankings place both the Civil Engineering and the Environmental Engineering undergraduate programs at #1 in the country. The 2027 graduate program rankings will not be released for some time, but in 2026 the corresponding graduate programs were ranked #3 and #4, respectively.
We are a vibrant and intellectually diverse School, with people who are using new technologies to expand the notion of what it means to be civil and environmental engineers in the 21st Century. We teach our students the engineering fundamentals needed to be successful at the interface of the built and the natural worlds. Our program focuses on learning how to think, how to solve problems, and how to impact society for the better. We provide rigorous learning environments, together with out-of-the-classroom and overseas experiences challenging our students to reach their highest potential.
Job Summary
The School of Civil and Environmental Engineering (CEE) (https://ce.gatech.edu) at the Georgia Institute of Technology in Atlanta, GA invites applications for multiple tenure-track faculty positions in the areas of Geosystems Engineering and Transportation Systems Engineering. Applicants will be considered at all ranks, with a preference for the Assistant Professor rank, in the following particular areas:
The Geosystems Engineering (GEO) program seeks forward-thinking faculty who are advancing the frontiers of the field in areas such as multiphysics and multiscale studies of coupled processes in geomaterials, mining geoengineering, engineered geomaterials, sensing and continuous monitoring, data-driven design, energy geoengineering, climate-adaptive coastal geotechnics, and planetary geotechnics. We welcome candidates who bring innovative approaches, interdisciplinary perspectives, and a compelling vision for the future of geosystems engineering in response to pressing societal and technological challenges.
The Transportation Systems Engineering (TSE) program seeks candidates with research and teaching emphases in one or more of the areas of travel demand and human behavior, multimodal transportation systems, regional-scale planning and policy, and/or the future of transportation technology. We seek candidates whose research advances understanding how people, vehicles, infrastructure, and emerging technologies interact across transportation systems, including (but not limited to) areas such as activity-based modeling, attitudinal influences, mobility analysis, public transit, connected and automated vehicles, sensor-enabled infrastructure, asset management, and AI methods to solve real-world transportation problems. We are especially interested in candidates whose research and teaching incorporates contemporary computational tools, artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled methods, field validation, and multimodal systems thinking to address current and emerging transportation challenges. As transportation systems engineering continues to evolve, the successful candidate will leverage advances in AI and related methods to strengthen the field's core focus on the transportation problems that arise from interactions among people, infrastructure, operations, economics, technology, and policy.
In addition, the College of Engineering is advertising ( https://coe.gatech.edu/faculty-job-opportunities) multiple tenured/tenure-track faculty positions (at all ranks) across two multidisciplinary themes, one of which Energy and Sustainability is particularly relevant to the GEO and TSE areas of CEE. Potential candidates for these hires are asked to apply directly to the most appropriate School (CEE, in our case), but should clearly indicate in their cover letter that they are interested in the cross-cutting Energy and Sustainability theme, if applicable. Joint appointments (across two Schools) are possible, as appropriate.
Outstanding faculty candidates in other areas of Civil and Environmental Engineering including Construction and Infrastructure Systems Engineering (CISE), Environmental Engineering (ENVE) Structural Engineering, Mechanics and Materials (SEMM); and Water Resources Engineering (WRE) will also be considered.

Georgia Tech is aware that attracting faculty may require meeting the needs of two careers..
Responsibilities CEE faculty are expected to lead independent research at the cutting edge of their field and build a strong, extramurally funded research program and national/international recognition. In addition, they are expected to teach both undergraduate and graduate level courses, mentor a diverse student body, and conduct service to the school, institute, and profession.
Required Qualifications An earned doctorate is required by the start of the appointment.
Preferred Qualifications Successful candidates will have demonstrated an exemplary track record of research accomplishments and/or the ability to develop a strong, externally funded research program, which addresses emerging domain-specific challenges while maintaining a foundation in core domain-specific engineering principles. The successful candidate must also demonstrate a passion for teaching and mentoring a diverse student body at the undergraduate and graduate levels in civil and environmental engineering and help prepare students for a profession evolving at an ever-increasing pace, shaped by artificial intelligence, new technologies, data-intensive methods, and rapidly changing employer needs. Successful candidates will further display a degree of service engagement appropriate to their career stage.

A cover letter of application indicating the area of interest

In four pages or less, a statement of research interests

jobs.title: Director, Faculty Professional Integrity (School of Medicine - Office of Faculty)
jobs.description:
The School of Medicine, Office of Faculty is seeking a Director, Faculty Professional Integrity. The core values of Johns Hopkins Medicine include integrity, respect, and collegiality. The Office of Faculty is responsible for developing and implementing policies that promote faculty professionalism, responsible conduct, and accountability.
The Director of Faculty Professional Integrity is a newly established position responsible for fostering a culture of professionalism, integrity, and accountability among faculty throughout the School of Medicine (SOM). Reporting to the Vice Dean for Faculty, the Director will support the development and implementation of policies, educational initiatives, and operational processes that promote professional conduct and strengthen institutional integrity. The Director will also oversee the institutional processes for reviewing allegations of faculty professional misconduct in accordance with applicable policies, procedures, and regulations.
The Director will work closely with the Director of Research Integrity and collaborate with School of Medicine leadership and institutional partners across Johns Hopkins.
Specific Duties & Responsibilities
Implements policies addressing faculty professionalism, professional conduct, and misconduct, and develops associated procedures and standard operating procedures.
Develops and continuously improves operational processes, including recordkeeping, tracking systems, and other tools to support effective management of professional integrity matters.
Develops and delivers educational programs and training for faculty, department leaders, and administrators related to professionalism, responsible conduct, and institutional expectations.
Serves as a resource to School of Medicine leadership regarding issues related to faculty professionalism, professional conduct, and the appropriate application of institutional policies.
Collaborates with institutional partners to ensure policies and procedures remain current with applicable regulations and national best practices.
Works closely with the Office of General Counsel, Human Resources, the Office of Institutional Equity, the Office of Research Integrity, and other institutional partners to promote a culture of professionalism and integrity.
Oversees assessments, inquiries, and investigations of allegations of faculty professional misconduct in accordance with institutional policies and procedures.
Coordinates inquiry and investigation committees and prepares objective, thorough reports summarizing allegations, evidence, interviews, findings, and recommendations.
Ensures appropriate application of institutional policies, procedures, and relevant regulations throughout the review process.
Maintains confidential records of professional integrity matters and prepares reports for School of Medicine leadership.
Supports the School of Medicine Standing Committee on Discipline.
Performs other duties as assigned.
Additional knowledge, skills, and abilities
Demonstrated integrity, sound judgment, professionalism, and discretion.
Excellent analytical, critical thinking, investigative, and problem-solving skills.
Outstanding written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
Ability to manage highly sensitive and confidential matters with professionalism and impartiality.
Ability to work independently, prioritize competing demands, and manage multiple complex matters simultaneously.
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
Ability to build collaborative relationships and work effectively with faculty, administrators, and institutional leaders.
Experience developing policies, procedures, educational programs, and process improvements.
Ability to facilitate educational and training sessions.
Knowledge of professional integrity and/or research integrity regulations and standards.
Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor's Degree.
Five years of progressively responsible professional experience in faculty affairs, compliance, research integrity, legal affairs, human resources, academic administration, investigations, or a related field.
Additional education may substitute for required experience, and additional related experience may substitute for required education beyond a high school diploma/graduation equivalent, to the extent permitted by the JHU equivalency formula.
Preferred Qualifications
Master's Degree, Doctoral Degree, JD, or other advanced professional degree in science, law, business, public policy, higher education administration, healthcare administration, or a related field.

About Binghamton University:
Binghamton University is a premier public R1 research institution in the State University of New York (SUNY) system that unites more than 130 broadly interdisciplinary educational programs with some of the most vibrant research in the nation. Our unique character - shaped by our mission, outstanding academics, facilities, and community life - promotes extraordinary student success, research, and service; Binghamton University is where our students, faculty and staff thrive.
Working at Binghamton University is more than about having a great job - it is about having the opportunity to flourish in an exciting, engaging environment. Our faculty and staff appreciate Binghamton's collegial and inclusive culture and its commitment to excellence, education, innovation, and civic engagement. Our diverse campus community contributes to our success.
Binghamton merges rigorous academics, distinguished faculty who value cutting-edge, and community-engaged research, teaching and service, exceptional staff, and ultramodern facilities to engage and challenge its 18,000+ students. Our high-achieving student body represents diverse experiences from first-generation college-goers to international students. Beyond their talent, these classmates share a desire to shape the future through technology, insight, intellectual exploration, and community service.
Job Description:
Department Overview:
BU is ranked one of the top 50 public universities and is a premier R1 research university. The University's direct impact on the regional economy has reached $1.2 billion. The recent $113 million research award from the Economic Development Administration (EDA) further catalyzes and fosters knowledge transfer and partnerships across industries and academia to advance technology development and innovation in science and engineering, and a $160 million NSF ENGINE grant helps the university to build ecosystems for science discovery and technology advancement. The university attracts outstanding students and award-winning faculty, including 2019 Nobel Laureate Dr. Stanley Whittingham, who are partners in active discovery. The Department has recently launched a workforce training program partnered with the School of Management to develop a Biomanufacturing Project Management Certificate Program funded by BioMADE. The Department also runs a National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) PREP postdoc and graduate training program.
The Biomedical Engineering (BME) Department is particularly strong in advanced biomanufacturing, biomaterials, biomechanics, cardiovascular engineering, nanomedicine, neuroengineering, organ-on-a-chip, stem cells, tissue engineering/regenerative medicine, and wearable biosensors. The BME Department is the home of the Center of Biomanufacturing for Regenerative Medicine (CBRM), and the Department has recently formed a joint Institute for Regenerative Medicine with Upstate Medical University. For more information, please visit our website. Funding from private operational support and public capital investment has allowed Binghamton University to establish the New York Center for AI Responsibility and Research, one of the nation's first centers aimed at ethical AI research. The Center will serve as a premier AI research hub for the entire State University of New York system and focus on developing novel technical innovations related to the safety and security of artificial intelligence models and systems.
Job Description:
As part of the strategic plan for expanding biomedical and health science research in emerging fields, the Department of Biomedical Engineering in the Thomas J. Watson College of Engineering and Applied Science at Binghamton University invites applications for one tenure-track faculty position at the Assistant Professor level with an expected start date of September 1, 2027.
We seek applications from candidates in all areas of biomedical engineering; however, we are particularly interested in the areas of biomedical robotics and embodied intelligence for health and medicine. Areas of interest include, but are not limited to, artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled physiological monitoring, biomechatronics, digital twins, human-machine interfaces, intelligent medical devices and instrumentation, implantable and wearable sensors and devices, rehabilitation and assistive technologies, and surgical and image-guided robotics. Candidates with a demonstrated commitment to diversity and inclusiveness are preferred.
Responsibilities of the position include:
Expand existing institutional capabilities in biomedical robotics and embodied intelligence for health and medicine through innovative research and external funding.
Drive research initiatives and foster interdisciplinary collaborations within Binghamton University's New York Center for AI Responsibility and Research.
Develop new undergraduate and graduate courses, teach and mentor students, and contribute to departmental growth.
The successful candidate will receive a comprehensive startup package including competitive salary compensation and benefits commensurate with qualifications and experience.
Requirements:
Required Qualifications:
PhD degree in biomedical engineering or a closely related discipline
Preferred Qualifications:
Background in biomedical robotics
Industry or national laboratory experience
Teaching experience
Demonstrated commitment to diversity and inclusiveness
Please be advised that H1B visa sponsorship may not be available for this position.

Job Details
Introduction
Nationally recognized as a Great College to Work For, TTUHSC provides much more than just a job! Enjoy excellent benefits, including paid leave, retirement plans, wellness programs, health insurance and so much more. Ready to start building a rewarding career in a positive environment where you can develop and thrive? Join us as we change the future of health care.
About TTUHSC
Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center is enriching the lives of others by educating students, providing excellent patient care, and advancing knowledge through innovative research. TTUHSC graduates more health care professionals than any other health care institution in the state, conferring 24.2% of all degrees and certificates awarded from health-related institutions in Texas. By providing comprehensive clinical services to more than 10 million individuals across 121 counties, TTUHSC is dedicated to advancing the health of people throughout Texas and beyond. This is where world-class education meets compassionate patient care – and we believe that our people are the reason for our institution’s lasting success and bright future.
Being part of the TTUHSC team means being part of an innovative and supportive community that empowers each individual to do their best work. Through our values-based culture, TTUHSC is committed to cultivating an exceptional workplace community with a positive culture that puts people first.
Visa Information
TTUHSC, at its sole discretion, may initiate new H-1B I-129 visa petitions in accordance with the directive issued by Governor Abbott. Approval from the Texas Workforce Commission is required. On a limited, case-by-case basis, the institution may also sponsor eligible individuals for change-of-status or change-of-employer petitions for qualifying positions. TTUHSC will not pay the $100,000 fee, if applicable.
Position Description
Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center (TTUHSC) Permian Basin Department of Surgery. Our program is rooted in a rigorous, evidence-based educational environment that emphasizes clinical excellence, surgical proficiency, and continuous professional development. As part of our surgery residency program, we are committed to cultivating surgeons who are very technically skilled, as well as focusing on professionalism, exemplifying integrity, inclusivity, and the highest standards of patient-centered care with compassion and kindness.
Located in the heart of the Permian Basin—the nation’s largest petroleum-producing region and one of its fastest-growing populations—our department plays a vital role in expanding and strengthening the surgical workforce to meet the urgent healthcare needs of this underserved area. Our mission is to train surgeons who are equipped to serve diverse communities with empathy, cultural competence, and clinical excellence in the Permian Basin or any other community.
The General Surgeon will have block time scheduled with our community hospital(s), participating in call coverage rotation and maintaining clinical time for pre and post surgical consultation. Opportunities for GME leadership with the Residency and Clerkship Programs. Da Vinci Robot opportunities at community hospitals.
Major/Essential Functions
Diagnose and manage a broad array of medical conditions through preoperative, operative and postoperative care.
Provide inpatient and outpatient care of surgical patients.
Procedures to include both emergent and non-emergent conditions.
Collaborate with a multidisciplinary team and refer patients as appropriate.
Educate patients on treatment plans, medications and pre and post operation care.
Complete medical records accurately and completely in a timely manner.
Participate in the training of medical students and residents.
Required Qualifications
MD/DO or equivalent,
Completion of, or in the process of completing an ACGME accredited General Surgery Residency,
Ability to obtain a TX medical license,
Foreign Medical Graduates Only: ECFMG Certification OR Equivalency Certification.
Required Attachments
Resume / CV
Optional Attachments
Professional/Personal Reference
Benefits
TTUHSC is committed to creating an environment where our team members can do their best work, with programs and benefits to support head-to-toe well-being. Explore just a few of the advantages of being a TTUHSC team member:
Health Plans + Supplemental Coverage Options – Individual health insurance provided at no cost for full-time team members
Paid Time Off – Including holidays, vacation, sick leave and more
Retirement Plans
Wellness Programs
Certified Mother-Friendly Workplace
Additionally, TTUHSC invests in the success of our team members by providing opportunities for personal and professional growth, including lifelong learning programs, recognition programs, and health and wellness initiatives. Team members also enjoy a variety of other perks, such as special membership rates at local gyms and golf courses, access to state-of-the-art software and facilities, and discounts on travel, technology, entertainment and more.

Full Time

Monthly

Salary commensurate with related education, experience and/or skills

Compensation is commensurate upon the qualifications of the individual selected and budgetary guidelines of the hiring department, as well as the institutional pay plan. For additional information, please reference the institutional pay plan website at https://app4.ttuhsc.edu/payplan.

No

No

jobs.description:
Job Details

Position Type: Faculty Full Time
Campus: UMass Boston
Department: Mathematics
Date opened: 02 Oct 2026 Eastern Daylight Time
Applications close:
Job Description
The Department of Mathematics at the University of Massachusetts Boston (UMass Boston) invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professorship in Mathematics beginning September 1, 2027. The research area of interest is in applied mathematics with a preferred emphasis in scientific and mathematical Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Applied Statistics, and related areas at the intersection of mathematics, statistics, machine learning, artificial intelligence, and data science. We are especially interested in candidates whose research combines rigorous mathematical and computational methodologies with impactful applications, preferably in biotechnology, biomedicine, neuroscience, or related scientific domains. Exceptional candidates from other areas of applied mathematics are encouraged to apply.
The Mathematics Department at UMass Boston is a vibrant and collegial group of faculty with research interests spanning the spectrum of pure and applied mathematics including Geometry and Symplectic Topology; Representation Theory; and Applied Mathematics, Data Science, and Mathematical Biology, and it pursues an important teaching mission. The College of Science and Mathematics is committed to inclusive excellence in research and education. We are a highly collaborative college of STEM including departments of Biology, Chemistry, Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics and Physics, and strong interdisciplinary Ph.D. programs. State-of-the-art research computing facilities, including high-performance computing clusters, are available to UMass Boston researchers. Partnerships and collaborations with academic institutions and industry research laboratories in the Greater Boston area offer substantial opportunities for collaboration.
The successful candidate must possess a PhD degree in mathematics, statistics or related fields and must have a robust research program and strong potential to secure extramural funding. The successful candidate will have an opportunity to expand and strengthen the research within the department and college. All candidates must exhibit a clear commitment to advancing the university's teaching mission through their participation in on-going student success initiatives in the department and the university. The successful candidate will also have the capacity to contribute to broad departmental and college service. A teaching load reduction to root a strong research program will be provided. For more information about the department see https://www.umb.edu/science-mathematics/academic-departments/mathematics/.
UMass Boston is an urban public research university with a teaching soul, whose impact is both local and global. We are the third most diverse university in the country - more than 60% of our undergraduate students come from minoritized communities and groups and more than half of our students are the first in their families to attend a college or university. Thus, our students come to us from richly diverse life experiences and backgrounds; they bring to our classrooms and research settings the robust range of perspectives growing out of the socio-cultural, economic, and historical contexts in which they have lived, along with the challenges they encounter, engage, and strive to overcome. We invite applications from candidates who engage the diverse life experiences of our student body, who appreciate that students bring their holistic selves into the academic setting, and who recognize and articulate how their own life experiences and backgrounds have shaped their journeys, practices, and commitments as researchers, scholars, and educators.
Application instructions:
Please submit (i) a cover letter, and (ii) a curriculum vitae to (APPLICATION LINK). Additionally, applicants are strongly encouraged to submit supplemental materials to MathJobs.org at the following link: [MathJobs Link]. These materials should consist of the following: (i) a cover letter; (ii) a curriculum vitae; (iii) a standard AMS cover sheet; (iv) a statement of current research, vision, and future research plans; (v) a description of teaching philosophy and experience. In addition, you should arrange for four (4) writers to submit letters of recommendation to MathJobs.org, with one of these letters addressing teaching. Please note that applications are considered incomplete (and will not be considered) unless the cover letter and curriculum vitae are submitted to (PageUp LINK). For full consideration, applications should be received by November 1, 2026. For inquiries, email: math@umb.edu.
UMass Boston expects to pay within an approximate range between $80,000 and $97,817 for this position.
The specific pay for this position will be determined by the University based on the consideration of all relevant factors when and if it decides to extend an offer of employment.
UMass Boston is committed to the full inclusion of all qualified individuals. As part of this commitment, we will ensure that persons with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations for the hiring process. If reasonable accommodation is needed, please contact HR@umb.edu or 617-287-5150.

jobs.title: AI Faculty Strategist
jobs.description:
Indiana Tech is a thriving, independent, teaching-oriented university that delivers career-oriented programming in a wide variety of disciplines that includes business, engineering, computer sciences, criminal justice, cybersecurity, marketing, health sciences, communication and helping professions. Indiana Tech enrolls nearly 1,500 students in its traditional undergraduate programs on its picturesque main campus, and nearly 5,000 students in its adult and online program. We offer degrees at the associate, bachelor’s, master's, and doctoral levels and undergraduate and graduate certificates.
Over 41% of our students are either globally or domestically diverse; this contributes to our unique vibrant and inclusive campus community. All academic programs are designed to provide students with relevant and practical experiences, including an emphasis on internships. The university is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission.
Indiana Tech is committed to fostering a welcoming and respectful environment for all. We actively support the recruitment, engagement, and retention of students, faculty, and staff from a wide range of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives. We believe that creating a sense of connection and support across our campus community plays an essential role in preparing students to succeed and contribute in a global society.
Indiana Tech has big plans for its future. Learn more at Indiana Tech Strategic Plan or strategicplan.indianatech.edu.
Indiana Tech is seeking an innovative, collaborative, and faculty-centered leader to serve as its AI Faculty Strategist. Reporting to the Executive Director of the AI Institute, with a dotted-line relationship to the Vice President for Academic Affairs, this position serves as the university’s primary faculty consultant for artificial intelligence pedagogy and instructional innovation. The AI Faculty Strategist leads Indiana Tech’s faculty-facing initiative for teaching AI within the curriculum and helps faculty build the knowledge, confidence, and instructional judgment needed to effectively integrate AI into teaching and learning.
Serving concurrently as Director of the Teaching Excellence Center, the AI Faculty Strategist plays a central role in advancing Indiana Tech’s institutional AI strategy by helping faculty navigate the rapidly evolving landscape of artificial intelligence in higher education. This position works closely with the Warrior AI Readiness Manager, the Director of Curriculum Design & AI Integration, academic deans, instructional designers, and faculty across disciplines to move instructors from AI awareness to meaningful course and program transformation.
The AI Faculty Strategist serves as the primary point of contact for faculty seeking guidance on AI pedagogy, instructional design, assessment redesign, and responsible AI integration. The successful candidate will provide individual consultation, facilitate professional development opportunities, mentor faculty participating in AI innovation initiatives, and help faculty identify opportunities for course redesign and instructional improvement. Faculty projects selected for full redesign and implementation will be carried out in partnership with the Curriculum Design team.
Additional responsibilities include developing and facilitating workshops, seminars, communities of practice, and faculty-development programs focused on AI in higher education. The Strategist will use institutional readiness data to identify coaching opportunities, contribute faculty-focused programming to university-wide AI initiatives, create instructional resources and teaching guides, support grant-related activities, and represent Indiana Tech’s AI efforts at institutional, regional, and national conferences.
Required Skills and Experience
The ideal candidate will possess a master’s degree in education, educational technology, instructional design, higher education, computer science, artificial intelligence, business, or a related discipline, along with a minimum of five years of higher-education teaching experience.
Candidates must demonstrate a strong understanding of artificial intelligence applications in higher education, including their impact on teaching, learning, assessment, curriculum design, and student engagement. The successful candidate will have a record of instructional innovation and experience integrating emerging educational technologies into academic programs and classroom environments.
The position requires demonstrated excellence in college teaching, outstanding written and verbal communication skills, and the ability to engage faculty from a wide variety of academic disciplines. Candidates must possess strong consultation, facilitation, coaching, and presentation skills and be able to foster collaboration while supporting faculty through instructional change and innovation.
Experience in designing and facilitating faculty development programs, workshops, training sessions, or professional learning initiatives is required. Candidates should also demonstrate the ability to translate complex AI concepts into practical instructional strategies that can be implemented effectively in diverse academic settings.
Preferred Skills and Experience
A doctoral degree in education, instructional design, higher education, educational technology, artificial intelligence, computer science, business, or a related discipline is preferred.
Preferred candidates will have scholarship related to teaching and learning, educational technology, instructional innovation, or artificial intelligence. Experience supporting online education, digital learning environments, and faculty adoption of emerging technologies is also highly desirable.
Additional preferred qualifications include experience leading institutional teaching and learning initiatives, developing instructional resources and toolkits, presenting at professional conferences, managing faculty innovation programs, or supporting grant-funded educational projects.
Opportunity and Impact
This is an exciting opportunity for a passionate educator and thought leader to help shape the future of teaching and learning at Indiana Tech. The AI Faculty Strategist will play a critical role in helping faculty understand, evaluate, and responsibly integrate artificial intelligence into their courses while strengthening student learning outcomes and preparing graduates for an AI-enabled workforce.
Success in this role will be reflected through increased faculty participation in AI professional development, growth in faculty consultations and curriculum redesign activity, development of instructional resources and teaching guides, improvement in AI-informed teaching practices, scholarly contributions, conference presentations, and achievement of grant-supported initiatives.
Why Indiana Tech?
Indiana Tech is a private, nonprofit university dedicated to innovation, collaboration, and student success. As part of the AI Institute and Teaching Excellence Center, the AI Faculty Strategist will have the opportunity to influence teaching practices across the university and help position Indiana Tech as a leader in responsible and effective AI integration in higher education.
Ready to help faculty transform teaching and learning for the age of artificial intelligence? Apply today and join Indiana Tech in shaping the future of higher education through innovation, collaboration, and instructional excellence.
**Application materials must include Vita and unofficial transcripts. Applicants must be prepared to provide a written response to Tech's mission and vision. The position remains open until filled; a review of candidates will commence as application materials are received.

Job Posting Title:
Faculty, Mental Health Lead Counselor
Job Description Summary:
Under the direction of the Senior Director of Mental Health Counseling Services, the Faculty, Mental Health Counselor Lead provides clinical and administrative leadership for counseling operations at Austin Community College (ACC). This role ensures the delivery of high-quality, ethical, and accessible mental health services that support student well-being,
retention, and academic success to a multicultural student population. The position balances direct mental health care services with clinical oversight, including clinical supervision of counseling staff, coordination of clinical operations, and leadership in crisis response, outreach, and
campus collaboration. The Counselor Lead will serve as a key support to the Senior Director of Mental Health Services and the Director of Wellness, Outreach & Prevention, assisting with departmental operations, strategic initiatives, and continuity of leadership functions that advances departmental goals focused on persistence, retention, and student engagement that align with ACC's mission along with professional standards from Council for the Advancement of Standards in Higher Education.
Job Description:

jobs.title: Faculty Affairs Administrator 2
jobs.description:
Job Details
The Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences in the Stanford University School of Medicine is seeking a Faculty Affairs Administrator 2 to oversee faculty affairs activities for our Clinician Educator and Instructor faculty. With the third-largest faculty population in the School of Medicine, our department is a large and dynamic academic community whose mission is to advance mental health and well-being through innovative research, exceptional clinical care, education and training, community engagement, and leadership. This administrative position plays a key role in supporting our faculty throughout their careers at Stanford. The position provides significant exposure to department-level decision-making and the opportunity to develop broad expertise in academic faculty affairs within a complex and highly collaborative environment. The Faculty Affairs Administrator 2 serves as a trusted and knowledgeable resource for faculty, department leaders, and staff; coordinates faculty appointments, reappointments, promotions, and other personnel actions; and helps ensure that faculty affairs processes are efficient, responsive, and consistent with School of Medicine and University policies.
Responsibilities
Core Duties:
Provide operational support and guidance to search/review committees and make recommendations for process improvement.
Document and interpret policies and processes for contributors to the appointment/promotion form (chair, faculty lead, and candidate).
Manage review, promotion, and search processes, including marketing, recruiting, preparing committee reports. Create agenda, prepare, and edit documents and forms for faculty review including recommendations.
Identify problematic information in letters and advise on how to resolve the problem. May provide first level approval for appointments and reappointments.
Prepare offer letters, as needed, for the chair or dean, which may include gathering and synthesizing information from other offices.
Serve as primary point of contact, as needed, in onboarding and orienting new faculty to the department, school, and university. Oversee all faculty visa matters and advise on application of policy, as needed. Troubleshoot issues as they arise.
Assist in ensuring compliance with faculty related policies as led by the Office of Faculty Advancement.
Minimum Education:
Bachelor's degree
Minimum Experience:
Three years of experience working with administrative processes, or combination of education and relevant experience.
Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:
Elevated level of attention to detail and accuracy.
Ability to track, monitor and adhere to deadlines.
Ability to learn university systems.
Experience working with databases and Microsoft Office suite.
Excellent communication skills.
Demonstrated ability to act with tact and maintain confidentiality.
Demonstrated problem solving and analytical skills.
Demonstrated ability to work well with Stanford colleagues and clients and with external organizations.
Demonstrated commitment to personal responsibility and value for safety, shown through communication of safety concerns and use and promotion of safe behaviors based on training and lessons learned.

jobs.title: Open Rank Professor - Educator, Medical Laboratory Science Program, College of Allied Health
jobs.description:
Current UC employees must apply internally via SuccessFactors
Faculty rank and compensation will be based on experience and academic credentials.
Next Lives at the University of Cincinnati
Founded in 1819, the University of Cincinnati ranks among the nation’s best urban public research universities. Home to more than 53,600 students, 12,000 faculty and staff, and over 360,000 living alumni, UC, a Carnegie 1 institution, combines research prowess with a physical setting The New York Times has called “the most ambitious campus design program in the country." UC's momentum has never been stronger as the anchor of the Cincinnati Innovation District, the oldest cooperative education (co-op) program in the country with students earning $94 million annually through paid experiences, an academic health system, and as a member of the Big 12 Conference. The university contributes $10.6 billion in economic impact to the city and $22.7 billion to the state of Ohio. At UC, next is all of us. Learn more at uc.edu.
UC is a mission-driven organization where we are committed to student success and positively transforming the community through scholarship and service. We thrive on innovation, making an impact, and fostering an environment where staff and faculty are key contributors to UC’s success.
The Department of Clinical and Health Information Sciences
The Department of Clinical and Health Information Sciences (CHIS) is one of the academic units in the College of Allied Health Sciences. The department offers undergraduate degrees in Medical Laboratory Science, Respiratory Therapy, Health Information Management, and Advanced Medical Imaging Technology. The department also has four graduate programs in Medical Laboratory Science Leadership, Respiratory Therapy, Health Informatics and the Doctor of Clinical Laboratory Science.
Job OverviewThe University of Cincinnati’s Medical Laboratory Science Graduate Programs is searching for a full-time Educator Track faculty member who will contribute to the department’s teaching, service and scholarship. This role encompasses teaching responsibilities across both Master's and Doctoral Medical Laboratory Science programs, with a primary emphasis on masters-level coursework. This is a 12-month position with rank commensurate with education and experience.
Medical Laboratory Science ProgramsThe UC MS-MLSL (Master of Medical Laboratory Science Leadership) program offers a two-year program designed primarily for working adults using an asynchronous distance learning approach. The program enrolled its first students in the spring of 2021. The curriculum focuses on a leadership core along with concentrations in health administration and management, higher education, molecular diagnostics and immunohematology. A portion of the MS-MLSL curriculum forms the foundation for the DCLS curriculum; providing a bridge for career and academic advancement.
The UC DCLS (Doctor of Clinical Laboratory Science) program offers a three-year, plus one semester program designed for working adults using asynchronous distance learning courses with a clinical residency requirement and culminating experience. The highly competitive DCLS program enrolled the first co-hort of students in the fall of 2025. The mission of the DCLS program is to provide broad-based knowledge and skills to prepare students for advanced careers in clinical laboratory sciences, such as consulting with physicians and diagnostic management teams to improve test selection, utilization, and result interpretation, patient and healthcare provider education on laboratory related issues, performing evidence-based research to support changes in the role of the laboratory in patient care, improve patient safety, and reduce costs.
Essential Functions
This position is primarily responsible for teaching and service in the MS-MLSL program, the Clinical and Health Information Sciences Department and College of Allied Health Sciences with the possibility of teaching roles in the DCLS program.
Teaching and service responsibilities include, but are not limited to, course development and curriculum assessment; primary instruction of didactic courses using online delivery modalities; leadership with and mentoring of adjunct faculty; student advising and mentoring, including capstone, service on program committees; and tasks as assigned.
While online teaching and service are central to this position, scholarship activities are also required consistent with the mission of the program and the University.
Minimum Requirements
Doctor of Philosophy in education or a health-related field or discipline and appropriate allied health credentials.
Candidates currently enrolled in a terminal degree program are welcome to apply, but the doctorate must be completed prior to the start date.
Demonstration of teaching experience as an adjunct instructor for at least 3 months per year for a minimum of two years, OR one year of full-time teaching at the College level.
Three (3) years of experience within the field of medical laboratory science in a leadership role
Teaching experience to include on-line teaching and use of learning management systems
Demonstrated experience in curriculum development and assessment
Current knowledge and skill in the use of computer technology and educational learning
Nationally certified as a medical laboratory scientist generalist (ASCP, AMT or equivalent)
Additional Qualifications Considered
Five (5) years of experience within medical laboratory science in clinical practice, industry, administration, or leadership.
Prior scholarly works published or presented
Active in professional activities at local, state, and/or national levels
Demonstrated student mentorship experience and commitment to student success
Strong organizational skills
Ability to work independently
Interest and ability to collaborate with an interdisciplinary team
Excellent written and oral communication skills with the ability to present complex material to students unfamiliar with a subject.
Application Process
Interested and qualified applicants must apply online and include:
A Cover Letter of interest
Statement of teaching philosophy and research plan
Updated CV/Resume
A list of three (3) professional references with contact information
Teaching evaluations will be requested from applicants who have prior teaching experience if selected for an on-campus interview
Applicants without a Cover Letter or CV/Resume will not be considered.
Compensation and Benefits
UC offers an exceptional benefits package designed to support your well-being, financial security, and work-life balance. (UC Benefits) Eligibility may vary by position and FTE status. Highlights include:
Comprehensive Tuition Remission
UC provides tuition remission for you and your eligible dependents, covering tuition costs for nearly all undergraduate and graduate programs offered by the university.
Robust Retirement Plans
As a UC employee, you won’t contribute to Social Security (except Medicare). Instead, you’ll choose between state pension plans (OPERS, STRS) or an Alternative Retirement Plan (ARP), with UC contributing 14–18% of your salary based on position.
Real Work-Life Balance
UC prioritizes work-life balance with a generous time-off policy, including:
Vacation and sick time
11 paid holidays and additional end-of-year paid time off (Winter Season Days)
6 weeks of paid parental leave for new parents
Additional Benefits Include:
Competitive salary based on experience
Comprehensive health coverage (medical, dental, vision, prescription)
Flexible spending accounts & wellness programs
Professional development & mentorship opportunities
To learn more about why UC is a great place to work, please visit our Careers Page.

The Department of Biological Sciences in the School of Arts and Sciences at the Lebanese American University (LAU) invites applications for three full-time, tenure-track faculty positions at the rank of Assistant Professor in the fields of Immunology/Biotechnology, Computational Biology, and Ecology/Environmental Biology.
We seek highly motivated and innovative scholars who will contribute to the department’s vibrant and interdisciplinary research and teaching community. Candidates in Immunology/Biotechnology should demonstrate expertise in experimental or applied areas relevant to human health and disease; those in Computational Biology should have a strong background in bioinformatics, systems biology, or data-driven approaches to molecular and cellular processes; and those in Ecology/Environmental Biology should bring expertise in biodiversity, environmental systems, conservation, or ecological modeling.
We particularly encourage applicants whose research complements the department’s strengths in genomics, systems biology, neuroscience, or cancer biology. Successful candidates will have opportunities to collaborate with experimental biologists and clinical researchers across LAU, contributing to a growing interdisciplinary research environment.
In addition to establishing an active and externally funded research program, successful candidates will play a key role in developing and teaching undergraduate and graduate courses within their areas of expertise, mentoring students, advising capstone projects and master’s theses, and engaging in service at the departmental and university levels.
Beyond excellence in research and teaching, the appointed faculty members are expected to contribute to program development and assessment, academic advising, and institutional or community service initiatives. These positions offer a unique opportunity to join a dynamic, collaborative, and forward-looking department dedicated to advancing knowledge and fostering positive societal impact through education and research.
Responsibilities:
Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in general biology and computational biology
Advise and mentor undergraduate and graduate students
Oversee senior year projects
Engage in scholarly work and research
Be actively involved in supporting and developing the program's main research tracks
Engage in service to the department, the university and the profession
Additional duties may be set by the department in light of departmental needs and priorities.
Qualifications:
Minimum Qualifications:
A Ph.D. in Immunology, Ecology, Biotechnology, Computational Biology, Bioinformatics, Systems Biology, or a closely related field.
At least two years of postdoctoral research experience.
A strong record of research accomplishments, including publications in peer-reviewed, high-impact journals, and demonstrated potential for securing external research funding.
For computational and quantitative fields:
expertise in one or more of the following areas is highly desirable — genomics and transcriptomics, systems biology, machine learning and AI applications in biology, network biology, or computational modeling and simulations.
Proficiency in programming languages such as Python, R, or MATLAB, and experience analyzing large biological datasets.
Demonstrated excellence or strong potential in teaching at the undergraduate and graduate levels, particularly in computational or quantitative biology.
Commitment to mentoring students, fostering diversity, and contributing to an inclusive and collaborative academic environment.
Interest in interdisciplinary collaboration with biologists, computer scientists, and clinicians within LAU and with external partners globally.
The Department:
The Department of Biological Sciences is one of the eight departments of the School of Arts and Sciences at LAU. It offers a Bachelor of Science (B.S.) in Biology and a Master of Science (M.S.) in Biological Sciences with additional programs upcoming in the near future.
The University:
The Lebanese American University is an Equal Opportunity Employer operating in Lebanon under a charter from the Regents of the State University of New York. Information about the University can be found at http://www.lau.edu.lb.
Application requirements:
Prospective candidates should apply electronically by sending a letter of interest including a statement of teaching and research interests, and an updated CV by email to: soas.careers@lau.edu.lb . The CV should include the names, emails and phone numbers of three references. The university reserves the right to contact additional references with notice given to the candidates at an appropriate time in the process.
Candidates must refer to position no. AS-28-02, in the subject line of the email.
