jobs.description:
Job Description
SCHOOL OF CHINESE MEDICINE
Research Assistant Professor (26270219)
Applications are invited for a Research Assistant Professor position in the School of Chinese Medicine (SCM), Hong Kong Baptist University. The SCM is committed to advancing translational research that integrates Chinese Medicine, musculoskeletal research, immunity and targeted therapy, promoting innovative translational discoveries that address major chronic diseases.
HKBU provides a vibrant research environment that bridges traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) with state-of-the-art biomedical sciences, fostering unique opportunities for interdisciplinary innovation in musculoskeletal research, immune regulation and precision medicine. The ideal candidate is expected to advance the SCM s strategic priorities by investigating mechanisms of musculoskeletal diseases, with particular interest in autoimmune and degenerative arthritis; elucidating pathways underlying immune dysregulation and inflammation; defining the biological basis of inflammation and tissue degeneration across musculoskeletal diseases; applying cutting-edge multi-omics technologies such as single-cell sequencing and spatial transcriptomics to translational research; and developing novel therapeutic strategies and biomarkers that integrate Chinese medicine concepts with modern biomedical science.
Responsibilities:
Conduct research on musculoskeletal biology, immune dysregulation and inflammation;
Lead translational projects employing single-cell sequencing and molecular biology to uncover pathomechanisms and therapeutic targets in musculoskeletal diseases;
Develop innovative research directions in musculoskeletal diseases, including novel diagnostic or therapeutic strategies inspired by herbal medicine, natural products, emerging targeted therapeutic modalities or immune-cell engineering;
Collaborate with clinical and industry partners to translate research findings into practical applications;
Supervise postgraduate students and research staff, and contribute to the academic activities of the SCM; and
Prepare competitive research grant proposals and publish high-quality scientific papers.
Requirements:
A PhD in Biology, Immunology, Biomedical Sciences, Chinese Medicine, or related disciplines;
A strong publication record in well-regarded international journals, with demonstrated leadership in research on the pathogenesis of musculoskeletal diseases, targeted therapeutic development, and immune-cell engineering;
Proven experience in experimental animal models, targeted therapy, immune-cell engineering, molecular and cellular biology, and the mechanistic study of musculoskeletal diseases;
Demonstrated ability to conduct independent research and secure competitive funding; and
Excellent written and oral communication skills; strong enthusiasm for interdisciplinary collaboration.
The initial appointment will be made on a fixed-term contract of up to three years. Re-appointment thereafter is subject to mutual agreement.
Salary will be commensurate with qualifications and experience.
Application Procedure:
Applicants are invited to submit their applications at the HKBU e-Recruitment System. All applicants should send in their teaching evaluation results of last three years and samples of publications, preferably three best ones out of their most recent publications. Applicants should also request two referees to send in confidential letters of reference, with Job Identification number (stated above) quoted on the letters, to the Human Resources Office (Email: recruit@hkbu.edu.hk) direct. Applicants who are not invited for interview 4 months after submission of application may consider their applications unsuccessful. All application materials including publication samples, scholarly/creative works will not be returned after the completion of the recruitment exercise unless upon request. Details of the University's Personal Information Collection Statement can be found at https://hro.hkbu.edu.hk/en/worklife-at-hkbu/employee-favourable-environment.html#privacy-policy.
The University reserves the right not to make an appointment for the posts advertised, and the appointment will be made according to the terms and conditions applicable at the time of offer.
Review of applications is ongoing until the position is filled.

jobs.title: SUSMAT RC - Assistant Professor in Bio-Chemical Process Design
jobs.description:
About Mohammed VI Polytechnic University (UM6P)
Mohammed VI Polytechnic University (UM6P) is an internationally oriented institution of higher learning, that is committed to an educational system based on the highest standards of teaching and research in fields related to the sustainable economic development of Morocco and Africa. UM6P is an institution oriented towards applied research and innovation. On a specific focus on Africa, UM6P aims to position these fields as the forefront and become a university of international standing.
More than just a traditional academic institution, UM6P is a platform for experimentation and a pool of opportunities, for students, professors and staff. It offers a high-quality living and study environment thanks to its state-of-the-art infrastructure. With an innovative approach, UM6P places research and innovation at the heart of its educational project as a driving force of a business model.
In its research approach, the UM6P promotes transdisciplinary, entrepreneurship spirit and collaboration with external institutions for developing up to date science and at continent level in order to address real challenges.
All our programs run as start-ups and can be self-organized when they reach a critical mass. Thus, academic liberty is promoted as far as funding is developed by research teams.
The research programs are integrated from long-term research to short-term applications in linkage with incubation and start-up ecosystems.
About the Chemical & Biochemical Sciences Green Process Engineering (CBS)
The Chemical & Biochemical Sciences Green Process Engineering Department (CBS) is a component of the Mohammed VI Polytechnic University (UM6P). The main objective of CBS is to set up a distinctive research-teaching program, of international level, to meet the research and teaching challenges of UM6P, in particular on green and environmental chemistry applied to all aspects of chemical sciences: organic and inorganic chemistry, analytical chemistry, chemical biology, biochemical and thermal reactions.
Research at CBS is organized around several major areas, which aim to answer challenging industrial questions, from complex chemical and biochemical reactions to scale-up and validation of process engineering. CBS projects aim at an in-depth understanding of the molecular mechanisms of all transformations in order to propose new original alternatives in terms of efficiency, environmental friendliness and sustainability.
Job description
The successful candidate will be responsible for designing, simulating, implementing and optimizing chemical and biochemical processes, especially continuous ones with applications in the chemical, agriculture, and biotechnological industries. SNG is looking for an enthusiastic, experienced, and entrepreneurial candidate to meet the goals of the research group. The incumbent will be expected to:
Lead the group s activities chemical process design, simulation, implementation, and optimization, at the macro-lab, pre-pilot, and pilot scales.
Closely interact with scientist, engineers, and entrepreneurs in the SNG and UM6P, as well as with external clients and collaborators.
Actively contribute to the entrepreneurial activities of the group. This is a unique and challenging opportunity to bridge R&D and entrepreneurship in a multidisciplinary and collaborative ecosystem, and to advance the development of use-inspired R&D at UM6P.
Proactively engage in collaborative R&D by providing solutions and demonstrating the potential bio/chemical process engineering in addressing important Moroccan technology challenges.
Supervise graduate students and/or postdoctoral fellows.
Prepare technical reports, manuscripts, and invention disclosures, and present results in relevant conferences.
Assist with the drafting of research proposals.
Assist with the management and administration of the SNG. The successful candidate will participate in progress review meetings, reports, and discuss results and explore opportunities for new activities consistent with the group s programmatic priorities.
Key duties
The successful candidate is expected to lead all aspects of bio/chemical process engineering, notably:
Develop new industrial processes and design new process plants and equipment or modify/optimize existing ones.
Test new processes, collect data required to make improvements and modifications, oversee the construction, supervise the operation of new pre-pilot/pilot plants, purchase and install equipment, and liaise with installation/project engineers and specialists.
Investigate and troubleshoot plant/process problems. Ensure that equipment works to its specification and to appropriate capacities
Assess safety and environmental issues and ensure safe working conditions and compliance with health and safety legislation.
Schedule and coordinate work to tight deadlines and within financial budgets.
Design and develop continuous manufacturing processes along with the layout and equipment for pre-pilot/pilot plants. This includes creating and setting specifications, developing, implementing, and monitoring this equipment as part of the manufacturing system.
Use of simulation software in the development of new processes
The successful candidate is also expected to:
Contribute to building a vibrant and sustainable entrepreneurial ecosystem at UM6P by translating, integrating, and assimilating sustainable academic innovations into commercial opportunities.
Deliver process engineering solutions to enable rapid evolution of academic research through the various TRL levels from innovation to product manufacturing (TRL 5-9).
Identify and engage potential partners to explore commercial opportunities for UM6P s entrepreneurial ecosystem by establishing good working relationships with collaborators, research institution, industry partners and government agencies.
Assist or lead the identification of new and more efficient bio/chemical processes.
Assist the PI and group members in writing manuscripts for publication, filing patents, and developing research proposals to acquire relevant equipment or expand research programs consistent with the programmatic priorities of the SNG.
Assist in the management and administration of the SNG. This activity may include several components, notably (a) collect, analyze, and summarize scientific literature relevant to a given project, (b) develop specific sections in relevant areas of expertise for a given proposal, (c) coordinate the organization of proposal applications in specific area of expertise.
Co-supervise research progress of graduate students, engineers, technicians, and/or postdoctoral fellows. This activity entails regular discussion with group members to ensure they are making progress in their research investigations, notably in the candidate s area of expertise. Discuss with the PI any challenges and roadblocks and ensure that the proposed solutions are implemented and followed upon.
Effectively communicate in English (verbally and in writing) to disseminate knowledge to group members, clients, and collaborators and/or to represent the SNG at conferences, meetings, and/or workshops.
Criteria of the candidate
R&D experience:
PhD in chemical engineering, materials engineering, mechanical engineering, or related areas from a recognized university with a focus on process engineering and its applications in the chemical, cements, fertilizers, and/or paints industries. Candidates with an engineering degree and at least 5 years of professional experience in R&D and process engineering may also apply.
Thorough knowledge of the key components of a bio/chemical process system (e.g. piping, pumps, tanks, flow valves, steam valves, temperature gauges, boilers, vessels, reactor vessels, crackers, distillation columns, heat exchangers, boilers, steam pipes, autoclaves, clarifiers, decanters, fluidised dryers, Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs), Proportional Integral Derivative (PID) Controllers).
Mastery of process simulation software (e.g. Aspen, ProSim, UniSim, ChemCAD, Mathworks) to work out the best production methods.
Knowledge of scientific principles related to magnitude, momentum, and heat transfer.
Thorough knowledge of analytical chemistry techniques with a demonstrated ability to solve highly technical problems.
Familiarity with process improvement methodologies (Six Sigma, lean manufacturing)
Ability to execute tasks with minimal oversight
Excellent publication (or patent) portfolio and R&D record.
Experience in supervising engineers, graduate students and/or postdoctoral fellows.
Demonstrated ability to organize/analyze/interpret results and assess whether additional investigations are necessary to reach the project s aims.
Evidence of collaboration with peers at national and/or international institutions.
Familiarity with some of the main Moroccan industries (notably chemical, cements, fertilizers, paints, recycling).
Teaching experience with the capacity to develop new courses (learning by doing) is desirable.
Entrepreneurial experience:
First-hand experience in entrepreneurship and awareness of the current Moroccan entrepreneurial ecosystem.
First-hand experience in market analysis, customer discovery, fundraising, developing business plans, developing IP strategy and new product certification for startups.
Experience in creating pitch decks for investors and potential customers.
Experience in launching technology start-ups including essential elements such as prototyping/product visualization and early-stage venture funding.
Evidence of participation in entrepreneurial programs.
Solid managerial skills and ability to take the initiative to advance the team s goals.
Awareness of Moroccan/African market and product development opportunities.
Experience with the incubation and start-up ecosystems in Morocco desirable.
Personal attributes
Understands and works towards team objectives.
Meets deadlines and displays strong administrative and organizational skills.
Strong initiative, self-motivated, and focused on achieving quality outputs (in R&D and entrepreneurship).
Ability to work effectively with a wide range of individuals, including faculty, students, industry executives, entrepreneurs, and investors.
Demonstrated ability to work on multiple projects at any given time.
Strong English and French communication skills, both verbal and written, are required.
While OCP group, a world leader in fertilizer production, is a privileged client for the University, a growing portfolio of clients is driving the development of a rich R&D ecosystem around the university. UM6P enjoys ample research funding, moderate teaching load, and excellent facilities. The university promotes multidisciplinary R&D, entrepreneurship and collaboration with external institutions and clients with the aim of advancing the Moroccan and African economies.
UM6P oﬀers highly competitive incentives to its current and future talented research staff.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Basic Medical Sciences - One Health
jobs.description:
As part of Purdue University’s strategic investment in One Health – Intelligent Medicines, the Department of Basic Medical Sciences in the College of Veterinary Medicine invites applications for a tenure-track or tenured faculty position at the Assistant or Associate Professor level. We seek innovative scientists whose research addresses fundamental mechanisms of cancer and disease at the intersection of tumor biology, neuroscience, immunology, regenerative biology, and the skeletal system.
We welcome investigators who leverage comparative, translational, and cross-species approaches to understand how interactions among tumors, neural circuits, immune cells, stem cell niches, and tissue microenvironments influence disease initiation, progression, metastasis, and therapeutic response.
Leveraging Purdue's strengths in comparative medicine and naturally occurring disease models, successful candidates will have unique opportunities to pursue translational discovery across species and advance One Health solutions relevant to both animal and human health. Candidates may utilize naturally occurring disease in veterinary patients, experimental model systems, organoids, or emerging computational and AI-enabled approaches to address questions relevant to both animal and human health.
Areas of Research Interest
We welcome candidates pursuing innovative research in:
Cancer Neuroscience and Tumor-Neural Interactions: Neural regulation of cancer initiation, progression, metastasis, treatment response, and cancer-associated symptoms.
Bone Metastasis and Skeletal Tumor Biology: Mechanisms governing tumor-bone interactions, metastatic colonization, dormancy, and skeletal remodeling.
Neuro-Immune and Bone-Immune Crosstalk: Interactions among neural, immune, and skeletal systems that shape tumor progression and anti-tumor responses.
Innovative Models and Technologies: Comparative animal models, organoids, spatial and single-cell biology, advanced imaging, computational approaches, AI/ML, and other emerging technologies for studying complex biological systems.
Purdue's One Health Initiative
This strategic recruitment will help advance Purdue’s One Health Initiative which seeks to tackle complex challenges with real-world impact at the intersection of human, animal, and plant health. This recruitment initiative builds on previous strategic faculty recruitment initiatives in: (1) Integrated Health; (2) AI-Driven Biomolecular Design, and (3) Advanced Chemistry. In addition, a parallel strategic faculty recruitment initiative in Healthy and Resilient Living Systems is ongoing. Through academic programs, research, facility infrastructure and industry partnerships, Purdue is making giant leaps in improving health outcomes for all living things and driving economic growth regionally and globally. This strategic faculty recruitment initiative focused on Intelligent Medicines is expected to build on prior recruitment initiatives and existing Purdue research and academic strengths, to transform research and impact human, animal and environmental health by bridging silos and fostering collaboration across disciplines.
The Intelligent Medicines theme seeks to create a framework that improves human, animal, and environmental health through the integration of technology, data, and systems thinking. This faculty recruitment initiative is disease agnostic and aims to establish new capabilities in AI-enabled therapeutic development, non-animal models of disease, advanced manufacturing, intelligent health systems, digital twins, robotics, human factors, supply chain resilience, and health technology innovation. By combining strengths in device innovation, computational intelligence, manufacturing systems, and healthcare operations, Purdue intends to create a highly visible flagship that strengthens industry engagement, expands workforce development opportunities, and attracts significant external funding.
Qualifications
A Ph.D. in a biological science and a minimum of 2 years relevant post-doctoral experience.
A record of research excellence and productivity commensurate with rank.
Demonstrated potential or record of interdisciplinary collaboration and impactful scholarship.
Commitment to teaching and student mentorship.
Faculty Responsibilities
Establish a vigorous, externally funded research program.
Teach courses in undergraduate or professional programs, mentor students, and train graduate students and postdoctoral fellows.
Engage in service to the Department, College, and University.
Collaborate across disciplines to solve complex global one health challenges.
Integration within the Purdue One Health Community
Collectively, the strategic faculty recruitment initiatives represent a forward-thinking investment in Purdue’s research infrastructure and academic excellence. Faculty hired as part of these One Health strategic faculty recruitment initiatives will be supported as part of the overall One Health community. Together, these faculty members are expected to work across diverse disciplines, enhance Purdue’s external funding potential, and drive innovation at the intersection of health, environment, food, and economics. In addition to joining an academic unit, faculty hired under this initiative will have the opportunity to join a vibrant ecosystem of interdisciplinary centers and institutes, that span the hard tech corridor between Indianapolis and West Lafayette including:
Center for Health Analytics and Therapeutic Intelligence
Purdue Institute for Cancer Research (PICR)
Purdue Center for Musculoskeletal Engineering (PCME)
The integrated, cross-disciplinary nature of One Health is essential for addressing today’s most urgent health challenges and ensuring Purdue’s continued leadership in research, education, and community impact.
Application Process
To apply, please submit a cover letter, complete curriculum vitae, 2–3 page description of current and future research, teaching statement, and contact information for at least three references. Review of applications will begin on November 2, 2026 and continue until positions are filled. Applications should be submitted at: https://careers.purdue.edu/job/Assistant-Professor-of-Basic-Medical-Sciences-One-Health/44286-en_US/. A background check is required for employment in this position.
Purdue is an equal opportunity/equal access university.

Job Details
Teaching Professor - Systems Engineering
Systems Engineering
Cornell University
The Cornell Systems Engineering Program is experiencing significant growth, driven by strong recognition through innovative industry collaborations and honors from leading professional societies. AI is increasingly becoming a critical subsystem within engineered products and systems. Systems engineering provides the framework needed to architect, integrate, and manage it within complex systems. To meet this need, we are inviting applications for a new faculty position at the rank of Assistant, Associate or Full Teaching Professor. We seek a candidate with expertise in artificial intelligence who can teach engineers to design, deploy, and oversee AI within larger systems, addressing challenges such as data dependence, model updates, and human–AI interaction. This position offers the opportunity to help shape the future of systems engineering across domains, from energy and infrastructure to biotechnology and healthcare. It's part of a broader effort spanning multiple disciplines and key industry collaborations, including Lockheed Martin, Intel, Arm, and more. We are especially interested in candidates with expertise in at least one of the following areas:
Digital twins
AI-service integration
Embedded, Edge, and Physical AI systems
AI security and resilient systems
AI for infrastructure, energy, and transportation
AI for biotechnology and life sciences
Human-AI systems and decision making
AI4SE & SE4AI
This is an open-rank, full-time, on-campus, non-tenure-track position with a long-term, renewable appointment. The role focuses primarily on teaching three courses and advising Master of Engineering projects annually. Candidates must hold a doctoral degree (Ph.D. or equivalent). Academic ranks of Assistant, Associate, or Full Teaching Professor will be determined based on experience and qualifications. Teaching Professors are expected to deliver high-quality classroom instruction, contribute to curriculum development, advance pedagogical practices, and mentor other educators. Initial appointments are for up to three years for Assistant Teaching Professors and up to five years for Associate and Full Teaching Professors.
The Systems Engineering Program at Cornell builds upon the broad expertise of its faculty to deliver unique, transdisciplinary master’s and doctoral education. It attracts a diverse cohort of students from multiple disciplines, industries, and countries. The faculty member appointed to this position will play a pivotal role in shaping the future of the program and will actively participate in strategic planning and operational decisions. As a core member of the Systems faculty, the successful candidate is expected to contribute to the program’s educational mission by teaching a select number of well-established, analytically focused graduate-level courses; ensuring course content remains current and relevant by engaging with ongoing research in Systems; and advising graduate students on systems-related projects.

Please explain how you found out about this listing

Prior relevant work or industry experience.

The UF College of Medicine, the largest college within UF's academic health center, is currently the highest-ranked medical school in Florida. UF Health Shands, UF Health's private, not-for-profit hospital system, includes seven hospitals, a state-designated Level I trauma center, a Level IV neonatal intensive care unit, a regional burn center, and an emergency air and ground transport program.
The Department of Pediatrics clinical services are delivered at UF Health Shands Children's Hospital, which was named one of the best Children's Hospital in Florida in the 2025-26 U.S. News & World Report rankings. Nationally ranked in four pediatric specialties, UF Health Shands Children's Hospital provides the full spectrum of pediatric specialty services and is among the top children's hospitals in the Southeast US. UF Health Shands Children's Hospital provides care for the children of Florida and is a major destination center for pediatric patients, who require specialized attention for complex medical problems.
UF Health Shands Children's Hospital represents the only quaternary-care academic pediatric center in North Florida. The children's hospital has 208 beds, including fully-equipped pediatric and neonatal intensive care units. UF Health Shands Children's Hospital is part of the Children's Miracle Network's alliance of premier hospitals for children.
The Department of Pediatrics is committed to fostering innovation and advancing discovery in the biomedical and psychosocial aspects of child health and human development, educating and training pediatric scientists, and directly translating basic scientific discoveries into new patient-oriented therapies. In the most recent fiscal year, the department was home to over $30.5M in sponsored research.
UF Health faculty work in multidisciplinary teams with researchers in the five other Health Science Center colleges, as well as those from across the University. The focus of team efforts is often grown out of the Centers and Institutes, including the Evelyn F. and William L. McKnight Brain Institute, the UF Genetics Institute, the Powell Gene Therapy Center, and the UF Health Cancer Center.
Gainesville, Florida
Gainesville, FL, is a vibrant city that offers a mix of culture, outdoor beauty, and a dynamic community atmosphere. The city, touted as one of the more affordable cost-of-living communities in Florida, is surrounded by stunning natural attractions like the Florida Museum of Natural History, Paynes Prairie Preserve, crystal clear freshwater springs, and several scenic parks, making it ideal for outdoor adventures. Gainesville also has a strong sense of community and is recognized for its festivals, farmer's markets, and various dining options downtown. The historic Hippodrome Theatre is the perfect place to indulge in live performances or independent films. Sports enthusiasts can enjoy many Division I NCAA sports (Go Gators).

jobs.title: Open Rank Clinical Track Faculty in Clinical Mental Health Counseling
jobs.description:
The College of Education at the University of Iowa is making a major investment in addressing critical mental health needs. The Department of Counselor Education is committed to advancing mental health services statewide, with particular attention to rural communities. We are seeking a dedicated and student-centered clinical faculty member to help lead our growing Clinical Mental Health Counseling (CMHC) MA Program.
Position
The Department of Counselor Education at the University of Iowa invites applications for an open rank clinical-track, academic year faculty position in the Clinical Mental Health Counseling Program. Starting date for the successful candidate is negotiable, but no later than August 18, 2027, ahead of the Fall 2027 semester.
We seek an individual with demonstrated excellence in teaching, clinical supervision, and program leadership, as well as experience relevant to clinical mental health counseling, rural communities, and counselor education.
This individual should have demonstrated:
Skills in effective teaching and clinical supervision.
Skills as an effective instructor at the undergraduate and/or graduate level.
Leadership experience, e.g., as a program coordinator in clinical mental health counseling or counselor education
A strong record of professional service that advances the research, training, and clinical work intended to improve and support individual’s mental health including those in rural communities.
Experience collaborating with colleagues and communities from a variety of backgrounds and perspectives.
The successful candidate will serve as a core faculty member and Program Coordinator for our Clinical Mental Health Counseling Program. This individual may also join in partnership with the Scanlan Center for School Mental Health. The program, following College of Education trends, has strong department, college, university, and clinical community support, and is committed to an environment that values diversity and collegiality. The preferred candidate will have a strong commitment to student-centered practice and will be experienced in implementation of CACREP accreditation standards in mental health counselor education.
Responsibilities
Being a core faculty member in the Clinical Mental Health Counseling MA program, Teaching courses, in the Clinical Mental Health Counseling MA program, in areas consistent with the candidate’s interests and department needs, Serve as program coordinator for the Clinical Mental Health MA program, Engage in a professional agenda that advances the research, training, or clinical work intended to improve the lives of individuals in need of clinical mental health services, Support program initiatives that enhance the instructional and clinical experiences of our CMHC students, Advising students, Engage in professional, university, collegiate, and departmental service that advances the research, training, and clinical work intended to improve the lives of individuals in need of clinical mental health services.
Education Requirement
Prospective candidates must have:
An earned doctorate in Counseling from a CACREP accredited program,
OR
An earned doctorate in a closely related field with a master’s degree in Clinical Mental Health from a Council on Accreditation of Counseling and Related Educational Programs (CACREP) accredited program.
Required Qualifications
Concentration or specialization in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, Experience in teaching undergraduate/graduate courses, Experience in program leadership, (e.g., curriculum coordination, program administration) Experience in providing clinical supervision reflective of CACREP standards and practices, Demonstrated commitment to create positive relationships with community counseling providers including school settings, Be a National Certified Counselor, NCC, or certification eligible, Experience contributing to a welcoming and respectful academic environment
Desirable Qualifications
Eligible for LMHC in the State of Iowa, Established Teaching, Research, and Service record reflective of expected requirements for appointment at the rank of Clinical Associate or Clinical Full Professor, respectively, Experience in the practice of clinical mental health counselor, Be LMHC, LPC or eligible for counselor licensure, Experience teaching in a CACREP accredited graduate program,
Salary
Competitive and commensurate with qualifications and experience. Excellent benefits, and professional development support.
Applications
Candidates must submit a letter addressing all qualifications noted above; a curriculum vitae; and contact information for three references.
To apply for this position, visit https://jobs.uiowa.edu/content/faculty/ and search requisition number 75898.
Inquiries
Direct general questions about the position to Dr. Isak Kim, Search Committee Chair (isak-kim@uiowa.edu), and questions about the application procedure to Rachel Wallace (rachel-wallace@uiowa.edu), Faculty Affairs Manager.
Screening
Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled.
Additional Information
Successful candidates will be required to disclose any misconduct history or pending research misconduct investigation including but not limited to sexual misconduct in prior employment and provide a related release and will be subject to a criminal background and credential check.
Persons with disabilities who need assistance or accommodations with the application or interview process may contact University Human Resources/Faculty and Staff Disability Services at (319) 335-2660 or fsds@uiowa.edu.
If your H-1B petition is subject to the September 19, 2025, Presidential Proclamation, please note that the department will NOT cover the $100,000 payment associated with H-1B sponsorship, either at the time of hire or for international travel purposes. We encourage you to explore alternative pathways for work authorization. Our team is available to help identify options that may be suitable for your situation.
The University of Iowa is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply and will receive consideration for employment free from discrimination on the basis of race, creed, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, pregnancy (including childbirth and related conditions), disability, genetic information, status as a U.S. veteran, service in the U.S. military, sexual orientation, or associational preferences.
Why Join Us?
At the University of Iowa, you’ll thrive in a collaborative, welcoming, and intellectually rich environment. As a Big Ten, R1 institution, we offer the resources of a major university with the personal connections of a close-knit academic community. Our faculty are supported at every stage of their careers through mentorship, professional development, and leadership opportunities. Located in Iowa City, one of the most livable cities in America, you’ll enjoy a vibrant cultural scene, top-rated schools, and a welcoming community that values creativity, innovation, and work-life integration. Learn more about this community and resources at WorkLife at Iowa.
About the College
Recognized as the State of Iowa’s top College of Education, we offer more than 80 undergraduate and graduate degree programs, including licensure, endorsement, and certificate programs, many of which are regularly ranked among the best in the nation. Students study with our world-renowned faculty who are the leaders in their fields. Our college is comprised of four departments: Educational Policy and Leadership Studies, Psychological and Quantitative Foundations, Counselor Education, and Teaching and Learning. The College houses several Centers that support work in critical areas of education, including UI REACH, Iowa Reading Research Center, Scanlan Center for School Mental Health, and the Belin-Blank Center for Gifted Education and Talent Development. The College is guided by a Strategic Plan which defines our mission and the vision and values that bolster it.
About the Department
The Department of Counselor Education develops exceptional and ethical mental health advocates, counselors, and counselor educators for ever-changing communities. Our MA programs in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, Rehabilitation Counseling, School Counseling, and our PhD in Counselor Education and Supervision, contribute to the profession through the creation and dissemination of knowledge, skills, and attitudes appropriate for the development of ethical and culturally sensitive counseling professionals. Our programs continue to be nationally ranked with our Rehabilitation Counseling Program recognized as the nation’s 4th top program.

jobs.title: GSMI - Professor in Geotechnics and Geomechanics
jobs.description:
About UM6P:
Mohammed VI Polytechnic University (UM6P) is an internationally oriented institution of higher learning, that is committed to an educational system based on the highest standards of teaching and research in fields related to the sustainable economic development of Morocco and Africa. UM6P is an institution oriented towards applied research and innovation. On a specific focus on Africa, UM6P aims to position these fields as the forefront and become a university of international standing. More than just a traditional academic institution, UM6P is a platform for experimentation and a pool of opportunities, for students, professors and staff. It offers a high-quality living and study environment thanks to its state-of-the-art infrastructure. With an innovative approach, UM6P places research and innovation at the heart of its educational project as a driving force of a business model. In its research approach, UM6P promotes transdisciplinary, entrepreneurship spirit and collaboration with external institutions for developing up to date science and at continent level in order to address real challenges. All our programs run as start-ups and can be self-organized when they reach a critical mass. Thus, academic liberty is promoted as far as funding is developed by research teams. The research programs are integrated from long-term research to short-term applications in linkage with incubation and start-up ecosystems.
Areas of research and Expertise:
The Geology and Sustainable Mining Institute (GSMI) is seeking an Assistant professor of Geomechanics. The ideal candidate will have extensive expertise in:
Rock mechanics, ground control, and geotechnical engineering in mining.
In-situ geotechnical characterization and risk assessment.
Job Description:
The Geology and Sustainable Mining Institute at Mohammed VI Polytechnic University invites applications for a full-time, permanent position in Geomechanics.
We are looking for candidates with a strong research focus on the design of underground and open-pit mining operations and geomechanics.
The successful candidate will be responsible for:
Conducting research and development in geomechanics, focusing on rock mechanics, slope stability, and ground control.
Developing and implementing numerical models to predict and analyze the mechanical behavior of rock masses in mining environments.
Exploring innovative solutions for ground control techniques to enhance safety and efficiency in mining operations.
Studying the behavior of rock masses under extreme conditions, such as high-stress environments, deep mining, and weak rock formations.
Conducting experimental research to better understand rock behavior, including field-based investigations at real mining sites.
Integrating environmental, social, and governance (ESG) considerations into geotechnical risk management and sustainable mining practices.
Recruiting and supervising graduate students and research assistants in mining and geomechanics projects.
Designing and performing laboratory and field experiments to assess rock properties and behavior under various mining conditions.
Building research projects related to geomechanics and applying for funding opportunities to support research activities.
Securing research funding through grant applications and industry partnerships.
Publishing research findings in high-impact journals and presenting results at industry conferences and academic seminars.
Fostering collaboration with interdisciplinary teams and external partners.
Translating research insights into actionable solutions in collaboration with industry stakeholders.
Teaching courses related to geomechanics and rock stability.
Qualifications:
Ph.D. in mineral engineering, geological engineering or a closely related field.
Proven track record of securing research funding
Experience in supervising graduate students and leading research teams.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
An engineering degree in mining engineering is a plus.
Application Process:
Interested candidates should submit the following documents:
A cover letter detailing their research interests and relevant experience.
A curriculum vitae (CV) including a list of publications if they exist.
Contact information for two professional references.
Statement of research and teaching.
Other documents that the candidate considers important for the recruitment process.
Applications should be submitted electronically with all documents attached in a single file or zipped in a single folder with the mention Geomechanics in the subject.

jobs.title: GSMI - Professor in Economic Geology
jobs.description:
Job Description
The Geology and Sustainable Mining Institute (GSMI) of University Mohammed VI Polytechnic (UM6P) invites applications for a full-time Professor position in the field of Economic Geology specializing Base and Precious-Metal Deposits, with an expected start as soon as possible. The appointment will be at the Professor level depending on the curriculum vitae and past experience of the successful candidate.
This position targets internationally renowned candidates with proven Metallogeny, Ore Mineralogy and Isotope Geochemistry preferably in combined field and analytical research applied to Base and Precious-Metal Deposits (Cu, Ni, Sn, Pb, Zn, Au, Ag, Pt etc) . We require experience in a range of metallic ore deposits including magmatic, metamorphic and basin-hosted deposits including MVTs, SEDEX and Carlin-type deposits. A strong background on African geology and related metal ores would be a significant advantage. The candidate also should demonstrate excellence in teaching on Bachelor, Master and PhD levels to establish a vibrant program of teaching at the interface between geology and mineral resources. Experience in the acquisition and/or management of third-party funded projects along with excellent written and verbal communication skills and academic self-administration are highly appreciated. The candidate is expected to prove ability to design, coordinate, and organize scientific events and research projects, as well as establish intra and extramural funded research programs. The ability to develop partnerships with industry and state entities is highly desirable.
The candidate must have experience working in a team of geoscientists and engineers to advance the understanding of Base and Precious-Metal ore exploration and valorization, and achieve the objectives of grant-funded research programs. Additionally, the candidate should have demonstrated good skills for meeting and conferring with others, and potential for academic and scientific leadership. Excellence in teaching at the undergraduate and graduate levels is also expected.
A Ph.D. in Geology of Base and Precious-Metal Deposits, metallogeny, economic geology or related specialization. In addition to convincing and stimulating research and teaching plans, the candidates must provide evidence of excellence in research as demonstrated by a record of sustained high-impact publications in top-ranked, field-relevant journals, presentations at significant conferences, distinguished awards and accolades, and other noteworthy activities that contribute to the visibility and prominence of the discipline.
Required documents include:
An application letter,
A Curriculum Vitae,
A description of the most significant scientific achievements, as well as a statement of research and teaching interests and plans,
A digital copy and summary of the PhD thesis,
Written references from 2 persons and contact details of them, Other documents that the candidate considers important for the recruitment process.
About the employer
Mohammed VI Polytechnic University is an institution dedicated to research and innovation in Africa and aims to position itself among world-renowned universities in its fields. The University is engaged in economic and human development and puts research and innovation at the forefront of African development. A mechanism that enables it to consolidate Morocco's frontline position in these fields, in a unique partnership-based approach and boosting skills training relevant for the future of Africa. Mohammed VI Polytechnic University aspires to leave its mark nationally, continentally, and globally. UM6P is located in the municipality of Benguerir, in the very heart of the Green City and only 70 km away from Marrakech. Thanks to its prestigious architectural landscape and modern equipment, the UM6P offers premium conditions for a desirable lifestyle.
Salary scales and allowances are competitive, meet international standards, and are commensurate with experience. Subject to certain conditions, the UM6P provides practical assistance in relocating and accommodation.

University Background:
The mission of California Lutheran University is to educate leaders for a global society who are strong in character and judgment, confident in their identity and vocation, and committed to service and justice. Founded in 1959 in beautiful Ventura County, the university has an enrollment of about 3,500 undergraduate and graduate students who come from across the nation and around the world from a diversity of backgrounds, cultures and faiths. As a federally recognized Hispanic-Serving Institution, Cal Lutheran is looking for candidates with a dedication to and success in working in diverse communities. The university is committed to an inclusive learning and work environment that values individual differences and respects each person's dignity.
Basic Function:
Under the direction of the Dean and the Department Chair, the Assistant Professor is responsible for providing academic instruction to students for the assigned undergraduate courses. The Assistant Professor is also to serve as an academic mentor to students; serve on faculty or university committees; and engage in scholarly activities, and/or creative endeavors which contribute to the academic mission of the University, as outlined in the faculty handbook.
The Music Department at California Lutheran University invites applicants for a tenure-track Assistant Professor whose primary responsibility will be to conduct the university choirs (including an all-student SATB mixed choir and treble choir), guide all vocal-related activities, and teach courses in the Music Department beginning in Fall 2027. The successful candidate will be a visionary, enthusiastic, and collaborative choral pedagogue and musician committed to building and maintaining a vibrant choral and vocal program. Proven or potential success with recruitment is expected. Teaching responsibilities include coursework in the candidate's secondary areas of expertise and may include music theory, music history, conducting, private vocal lessons, or other subjects. Additional responsibilities involve the planning and performance of the annual Christmas Concerts.
California Lutheran University is a Hispanic Serving Institution. We seek candidates with experience or sensitivity to working with students from underrepresented ethnic and racial backgrounds and educational attainment, including first-generation and/or immigrant students. The successful candidate will have a record of and a commitment to diversity, inclusion, equity, justice, and belonging, and who can serve as a mentor for African-American, Latina/o, and/or Native American students.
The Music Department is a student-centered learning community that prides itself on providing a strong music education within a nurturing atmosphere. Faculty members are experienced professionals who are committed to teaching excellence. The music program is widely respected for its performance ensembles, its classroom teaching, and its studio instruction. Cal Lutheran's majors have gone on to be successful performers, educators, composers, conductors and music-industry specialists. We embody the spirit of a strong conservatory education within a liberal arts setting.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Criminology and Criminal Justice
jobs.description:
Assistant Professor of Criminology and Criminal Justice
Position Category: Faculty
FLSA: Exempt
FTE: .75 (academic year full-time)
Location: Thousand Oaks
University Background:
The mission of California Lutheran University is to educate leaders for a global society who are strong in character and judgment, confident in their identity and vocation, and committed to service and justice. Founded in 1959 in beautiful Ventura County, the university has an enrollment of about 3,500 undergraduate and graduate students who come from across the nation and around the world from a diversity of backgrounds, cultures and faiths. As a federally recognized Hispanic-Serving Institution, Cal Lutheran is looking for candidates with a dedication to and success in working in diverse communities. The university is committed to an inclusive learning and work environment that values individual differences and respects each person's dignity.
Basic Function:
Under the direction of the Dean and Department Chair, the Assistant Professor is responsible for providing academic instruction to students in assigned undergraduate courses. The Assistant Professor is to serve as an academic advisor to students; contribute to department and university activities; serve on faculty or university committees; engage in scholarly activities; and/or participate in creative endeavors.
Cal Lutheran's Department of Criminology and Criminal Justice (Crim. Dept.) invites applicants for a tenure-track faculty position beginning in Fall 2027. Candidates will apply at the rank of Assistant Professor and must hold a doctorate in Criminology, Criminal Justice, or a related field. ABD status will also be considered.
The successful candidate will be able to teach a variety of undergraduate courses in criminology and criminal justice. Area of teaching and research specialization is open, with potential areas including, but not limited to, criminal law and procedure; policing and procedural justice; criminal and forensic investigation and evidentiary processes; crime analysis and data science; juvenile justice and delinquency; and evaluation research.
Applicants with expertise in the empirical study of crime and justice, evidence-based approaches to improving criminal justice systems, or innovative approaches to teaching and mentoring undergraduate students are especially encouraged to apply. Professional experience in the criminal justice system is desirable but not required. Experience mentoring undergraduate research or engaging students in scholarly, community-based, or applied research is highly desirable.
A full-teaching load is 3 courses per academic semester and 6 per academic year. Primary teaching responsibilities will be based on departmental needs and may include undergraduate courses such as Introduction to Criminal Justice, Criminal and Procedural Law, Critical Issues in Policing, Juvenile Delinquency, Research Methods & Statistics, and with the ability to develop additional courses relevant to their specialization. The successful candidate may also have opportunities to contribute to interdisciplinary programs, experiential learning initiatives, internships, and curriculum development.
The mission of the Criminology and Criminal Justice program is to develop and share knowledge about crime, criminal behavior, victimization, criminal law and procedure, and the institutions and processes of the criminal justice system through teaching, research, and service. We provide students with theoretical knowledge, research and analytical tools, ethical grounding, and practical skills that prepare them for meaningful professional pathways and lifelong learning. We aim to educate future leaders in criminal justice practice, policy, research, and related fields who will make informed and constructive contributions to a more equitable and just society. https://www.callutheran.edu/college-arts-sciences/criminal-justice/
In sum, the successful candidate will demonstrate excellence in undergraduate teaching, maintain an active program of scholarship appropriate for a teaching-focused institution, mentor and advise students, and contribute meaningful service to the department, university, and broader community.
Representative Duties:
Teach undergraduate courses in criminology and criminal justice, normally 24 units per academic year. Teaching assignments will be based on departmental needs and may include Introduction to Criminal Justice, Introduction to Law and Legal Processes, Critical Issues in Policing, Research Methods and Statistics, and courses aligned with the successful candidate's expertise.
Provide engaging academic instruction through lectures, interactive discussions, applied activities, and other inclusive, evidence-based teaching practices in classroom, individual, and technology-mediated settings. Create assignments and activities that develop students' cognitive abilities, communication skills, and higher-order thinking skills.
Develop course curricula, syllabi, assignments, and learning activities that strengthen students' substantive knowledge, research and analytical abilities, communication skills, ethical reasoning, and higher-order thinking.
Observe and evaluate student performance in meeting course objectives and student learning outcomes through assignments, projects, discussions, examinations, presentations, and other appropriate measures; respond to student inquiries and provide prompt, constructive feedback in class, online, and during established consultation or office hours.
Maintain current and accurate records of course enrollment, attendance, student academic progress, and course curriculum; prepare and submit grades, assessment data, and required reports in a timely manner.
Teach and hold regular office hours in person on campus at least four days per week.
Provide students with a course syllabus within the first week of each course, as outlined in the Faculty Handbook.
Mentor and advise students regarding course selection, major requirements, academic progress, applied skill development, internships, career pathways, graduate or professional education, and other post-graduate plans.
Supervise and collaborate with students on undergraduate research and facilitate experiential and applied learning opportunities that connect criminological theory and empirical research with criminal justice policy and practice.
Maintain an active program of scholarship appropriate for a teaching-focused institution, including research, publication, conference participation, and other scholarly, professional, or creative activities in criminology and criminal justice.
Adhere to the responsibilities related to teaching, advising, service, and scholarly, professional, and creative activities for Assistant Professors as outlined in the Faculty Handbook.
Adhere to the responsibilities related to teaching, advising, service, and scholarly, professional, and creative activities as outlined in the Faculty Handbook.
Attend and participate on committees and in department, division, campus, and University meetings.
Contribute to professional and community engagement through collaborative research, public scholarship, internships, applied learning, or partnerships with criminal justice practitioners, public agencies, and community organizations.
Evening and weekend hours may be required.
Perform related duties as assigned based on departmental and University needs.
Knowledge Of:
Current theory, empirical research, policy, and professional practice in criminology and criminal justice.
The organization, operation, and contemporary challenges of criminal justice institutions, including law enforcement agencies, courts, and related legal and community organizations.
Criminal justice professional pathways and the knowledge and applied competencies students need to pursue careers or graduate and professional education in the field.
Quantitative, qualitative, and applied research methods, including methods of gathering, analyzing, interpreting, presenting, and preparing data and conducting program evaluation.
Principles and best practices of effective, inclusive, and evidence-based undergraduate teaching.
Student learning outcomes, curriculum development, and methods of assessment.
Effective practices in undergraduate mentoring, advising, and research supervision.
Experiential and applied learning practices, including internships, community-based learning, undergraduate research, and practitioner partnerships.
University curricula and the role of the major within a liberal arts education.
Community and campus resources, services, programs, and professionals available to support student success.
Modern computing technology, including current and emerging instructional technologies, analytical software, data tools, and other technologies relevant to teaching and scholarship.
Ethical, legal, and professional standards related to teaching, research, criminal justice practice, student privacy, and the responsible collection and use of data.
Recordkeeping requirements and techniques related to student enrollment, attendance, grades, academic progress, course curriculum, and program assessment.
Ability To:
Demonstrate thorough and accurate knowledge of criminology and criminal justice.
Design and deliver accessible, engaging, and academically rigorous course curricula using varied and inclusive teaching approaches that address different learning styles.
Connect criminological theory and empirical research with criminal justice policy, institutional practice, and professional pathways.
Translate empirical evidence and data into meaningful classroom, research, and applied learning experiences.
Develop curricula, assignments, and assessments aligned with course and program learning outcomes.
Develop students' research literacy, analytical abilities, ethical reasoning, communication skills, and applied criminal justice competencies.
Mentor and advise students regarding academic progress, undergraduate research, internships, career preparation, and post-graduate planning.
Supervise and collaborate with undergraduate students in scholarly, community-based, or applied research.
Use quantitative, qualitative, or applied research methods appropriate to the candidate's area of scholarship.
Integrate current and emerging instructional delivery technologies, analytical software, and research tools into the learning process to enhance teaching, scholarship, and the educational experience.
Exhibit sensitivity to and understanding of the diverse academic, social, economic, cultural, racial, and ethnic backgrounds of University students.
Exhibit sensitivity to and understanding of the needs of students with disabilities.
Maintain professional and ethical standards that protect student confidentiality and ensure the responsible use of information and data.
Communicate effectively, both orally and in writing, using tact, patience, and courtesy with students, colleagues, practitioners, community partners, and other constituencies.
Establish and maintain effective and collaborative working relationships with students, faculty, staff, criminal justice practitioners, public agencies, and community organizations.
Work constructively with colleagues and treat faculty, staff, administrators, and students with respect and professionalism.
Analyze situations accurately and adopt effective courses of action.
Demonstrate a commitment to professional excellence and continuous growth within criminology and criminal justice, including teaching, scholarship, advising, and service.
Satisfactorily fulfill a faculty member's duties and responsibilities and make significant contributions to the University community.
Analyze situations accurately and adopt practical courses of action.
Minimum Qualifications:
Possession of a Ph.D. in Criminology, Criminal Justice, or a closely related field from an accredited institution is required for appointment at the rank of Assistant Professor. Candidates who are ABD will be considered but will be appointed at the rank of Instructor until completion of the doctorate. A J.D. alone is not sufficient unless the candidate also possesses a Ph.D. in Criminology, Criminal Justice, or a closely related field.
Preferred Qualifications:
Licenses and Other Requirements:
None
Physical Abilities:
Detect to understand appropriate written correspondence; communicate clearly to exchange information in person and via the telephone or video; operate a computer and other office productivity machinery; stationary position for extended periods of time; move or transport light objects; position self to store and/or retrieve files.
Working Environment:
Indoor classroom environment; subject to visiting a variety of classroom sites on campus.
Hiring Range $73,000 - $82,000
Posting Number: Faculty001262020
Open Date: 08/10/2026
Close Date: 11/01/2026
Application Procedure/Special Instructions We look forward to reading your application.
Please include the following materials with your application:
1. Cover Letter: Please tell us about yourself and explain how you meet the qualifications for the position. Please also describe how you plan to support the mission and Hispanic-Serving Institution designation of California Lutheran University. Two pages maximum.
2. Curriculum Vitae or Resume: Please provide a curriculum vitae or resume detailing your educational background, professional experience, teaching experience, publications, service, appointments or positions, honors, awards, and other relevant accomplishments.

Shouldering our social responsibility of Serving Macao, Integrating into the Greater Bay Area , our mission is to nurture high-calibre professionals to meet the evolving needs of Macao and the broader region. Eligible appointees may apply under the Macao Talent Programme. In March 2026, CityU Macau established an advanced research institute and a knowledge transfer centre in the Guangdong Macao In-Depth Cooperation Zone in Hengqin, offering faculty a platform for industry academia collaboration and research translation.

Civil and Commercial Law
Job Description
Successful candidates are expected to contribute significantly to the Faculty s programme development and will be responsible for teaching, research, and the supervision and coordination of students professional practice and dissertations.
Job Requirements

Ability to teach in English and Chinese;
Assistant Professor: strong research potential and quality publications. Associate Professor: a sustained record of high-quality publications, experience in teaching and postgraduate supervision, and a track record of competitive research grants. Professor: international academic standing and leadership, with the ability to lead discipline development;
Preference will be given to candidates with full-time university teaching experience or teaching awards, national or provincial research projects, or substantial industry experience;
Preference will be given to Macao residents under the same conditions.

Enquiries (not applications) may be sent to jobs@cityu.edu.mo. The position will remain open until filled.
The following documents should be uploaded to the online application platform:
Resume
Personal Identification Document
Graduation Certificates
Cover Letter (clearly indicating the position, reference code and academic unit you are applying for)
Contact information for three referees
Review of applications will commence immediately. Applicants who are not invited for an interview within three months of submission should consider their applications unsuccessful. The successful candidate is expected to assume duty in December 2026 or mid-August 2027.
Personal data provided by applicants will be kept confidential and used for recruitment purposes only.

jobs.description:
The College of Nursing at Taipei Medical University invite applications for Assistant, Associate, or Professor position in the International Ph.D. Program in Gerontology and Long-Term Care.
Contract type: Full-time
Job Description-
Taipei Medical University (TMU) is seeking a highly motivated scholar with a Ph.D. and an outstanding record of academic achievement in healthcare or a related discipline. Applicants must hold a doctoral degree from an accredited public, private, or foreign university, college, or institution recognized by the Ministry of Education (R.O.C.).
The successful candidate is expected to contribute to TMU s international research profile and engage in interdisciplinary research and collaboration within a dynamic academic environment.
The successful candidate will be appointed to the College of Nursing at Taipei Medical University.
Salary
$83,720NTD~ $198,770NTD per month + benefits
Selection Criteria
Qualifications
Applicants must hold a Ph.D. in a healthcare-related field or a related discipline, with outstanding academic achievements, from a public or accredited private university or independent college, or from a foreign university or independent college recognized in accordance with the regulations of the Ministry of Education, Taiwan.
Candidates should demonstrate strong research potential or established scholarly achievements in one or more of the following areas: Aging and Public Health Policy, Geriatrics and Long-Term Care, Health Promotion and Healthy Aging, and Digital Health and AI for Aging.
Proficiency in English and the ability to teach courses using English as a Medium of Instruction (EMI) are required.
Candidates should demonstrate the ability to secure competitive research funding, with experience in research proposal development, conducting large-scale research projects, independent research, and international research collaboration.
Candidates should demonstrate the ability to innovate in teaching and research and to work effectively in interdisciplinary and collaborative teams.
Candidates with prior teaching experience will be given preference.
Candidates should demonstrate a strong commitment to teaching, mentoring, and talent development.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, strong teamwork capabilities, and demonstrated experience in international academic exchange and collaboration are highly desirable.
Candidates should demonstrate strong research motivation, academic professionalism, and the ability to contribute to an international and interdisciplinary academic environment.

A photocopy of education and working experience diploma (any foreign diploma should be verified in advance by the overseas office, Republic of China (Taiwan)
Publication list (including thesis credit chart, journal publications, and SCI journal rankings)

Two letters of recommendation

Description
The Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) area within the Computing and Mathematical Sciences Division at Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI) invites applications for tenured/tenure-track faculty positions at the Associate and Full Professor ranks.
We seek an established academic leader who positions technical data visualization as the core engine for human-AI collaboration, reasoning, and multi-stakeholder sensemaking. Leveraging deep technical expertise to expose internal system dynamics, the successful candidate will translate computational complexity into human legibility equipping diverse stakeholders to reason and decide together.
The ideal candidate will bring an internationally recognized research track record showing how interactive, dynamic visual interfaces ground human reasoning and decision making and enable oversight in complex computational systems. Candidates should demonstrate an active research agenda (commensurate with rank) that establishes visual interfaces as the framework for collaborative sensemaking and systems oversight. The successful candidate will contribute to our growing graduate degree programs, mentor exceptional graduate students, and leverage MBZUAI s world-class compute resources and interdisciplinary environment to drive global impact in human-centered AI.

Description
The Statistics and Data Science Area within the Division of Humanities, Social and Management Sciences at Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI) focuses on the rigorous statistical and probabilistic foundations of machine learning and data science. We emphasize computational methods for large-scale data and scalable inference techniques. Our current research includes areas such as statistical learning theory, high-dimensional statistics, causal inference, uncertainty quantification, fairness, and interpretability in AI. We encourage interdisciplinary research, integrating statistical innovation with decision sciences, healthcare, climate science, and computational biology. Faculty members will have ample opportunities to collaborate with industry partners, government agencies, and research institutions to develop AI-driven solutions for real-world challenges.
The successful candidate will be responsible for delivering high-quality instruction, mentoring of students, contributing to curriculum development, and will also have the opportunity to collaborate with leading AI researchers. We are seeking faculty at all levels (Assistant, Associate, Full Professor).
Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI) is a world-leading university dedicated to advancing AI as a global force for good. The UAE s visionary leaders established MBZUAI to educate and develop top talent, conduct advanced research, foster an innovation ecosystem, and act as a strategic think tank for the public and private sectors.
The University attracts world-class thinkers and doers in computer science, AI, bioscience, humanities and beyond. Our groundbreaking academic research initiatives are working on developing future solutions that will impact the world and change the way we imagine things.
Why Join MBZUAI?
Top-Tier Compensation: Competitive salaries aligned with leading global academic institutions
Funding: MBZUAI empowers researchers with resources and academic freedom, fostering groundbreaking AI advancements in an environment of innovation and independent inquiry.
Exceptional Benefits:
Comprehensive health & life insurance
Relocation support for international faculty
Build State-of-the-Art Research Facilities: Cutting-edge AI labs and high-performance computing
Live in Abu Dhabi: World s safest city, year-round sunshine, rich culture, and modern amenities
Industry & Government Collaborations: Work with top AI researchers, leading tech firms, and policymakers
Qualifications
This position requires a PhD in Statistics, Computer Science, or a closely related field. Applicants from all areas of statistics are encouraged to apply, particularly those working at the intersection of statistics and machine learning. The ideal candidate will be an innovative scholar, advancing both statistical theory and its applications in AI-driven contexts.
Application Instructions
To apply for this position, please submit the following items:
Cover Letter
Curriculum Vitae
Statement of research vision and interests
