List of your three most significant publications from the past five years, along with your Google Scholar h-index
Reference Letters or Name and contact details for three referees (Referees will be contacted during the recruitment process to upload their reference letter via Interfolio)

jobs.title: Political Science Faculty Member
jobs.description:
Job Details
About Holyoke Community College:
Holyoke Community College is housed on a multi-million-dollar, 135-acre campus, equipped with state-of-the art technology in specialized learning facilities. HCC serves over 9,000 students annually, and provides a variety of recreational and cultural activities, from sports programs to music festivals, for students and community members alike. The college's strongest assets continue to be an innovative spirit, a sincere concern for students and a commitment to strive for even greater success. These are the values which have created a tradition of excellence spanning more than six decades, and which are enabling Holyoke Community College to meet today's challenges.
Mission:Educate. Inspire. Connect.
Values: Kindness, Inclusion, Trust, Innovation & Collaboration
Kindness, inclusion and trust are the foundation of the work that we do together. Innovation and collaboration enable us to explore and implement the ideas that will shape our future.
The Critical Social Thought (CST) Department at Holyoke Community College seeks a full-time tenure-track faculty member to bring vision and innovation to Political Science courses within the department’s CST Option. We seek candidates who will bring a broad grounding in US Political Science to the department, and who can enhance our course offerings with specialized areas of expertise. Candidates with research or teaching in US National Politics, State and Local Politics, Civics, Civil Liberties, Immigration, Transnational Politics, and Latinx Politics are particularly encouraged to apply. Our ideal candidate will continue the department’s tradition of interdisciplinary teaching with colleagues across campus and engaging with the external community via community-based learning. As part of the college’s efforts to ensure equitable outcomes for all HCC students, candidates must bring a demonstrated commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion in their teaching practice, as well as a record of excellence in college-level instruction.
Primary responsibilities include: teaching lecture classes on general US Political Science topics as well as electives that serve the needs of students in our program as well as other degree programs; strengthening the ongoing development of our CST academic program via assessment and curriculum development; participating in college governance, recruitment and retention efforts; and professional development.
In addition to teaching experience, candidates should also demonstrate a commitment to student-centered advising, and to building partnerships that will enhance students’ opportunities for career and transfer. Such partnerships may include internal collaborations with colleagues in the CST department and in the Latinx Studies program as well as external collaborations to expand career and transfer opportunities for students who major in CST and Latinx programs.
Although hybrid teaching options may be available, this position will require a substantial amount of in-person, on-campus work with students, faculty, and community partners.
Teaching US Political Science lecture courses, in particular general US National as well as State and Local Politics surveys, and courses that address specific subfields in Political Science relevant to the faculty member’s expertise. Ability to teach Immigration, Transnational Politics, and Latinx Politics is of particular interest.
Working closely with colleagues in Critical Social Thought Department and across campus, develop innovative teaching methods; expand community-engaged learning initiatives; continue a commitment to innovative, inclusive, discovery-based and critically engaged curricula; incorporate technology in the classroom; develop and implement new courses as appropriate that serve the students’ academic needs, and strengthen the ongoing development of our CST academic program.
Advising students in the CST program and related majors.
Meeting with and assisting students during regular office hours.
Actively participating in department, division, and professional staff meetings as well as other components of college governance.
Maintaining professional expertise in areas of specialization.
Participating in college programs and activities.
Assisting the Dean, Associate Dean, and Chair of the Critical Social Thought Department to establish and maintain existing academic partnerships with related college programs as well as expand articulation agreements with external college and university programs.
Providing college service as required by the MCCC contract, including participation in shared governance committees, sub-committees, or task forces.
Minimum Qualifications:
Master’s degree in Political Science or closely related field, with the ability to teach standard survey courses (US National, State and Local Government, Civil Liberties) as well as specialized courses within US Political Science and across disciplines;
Teaching experience in higher education, specifically as instructor of record;
Demonstrated excellent teaching skills including interactive teaching, varied pedagogical strategies, and culturally responsive pedagogies;
Experience using instructional technology across teaching modalities (i.e. in physical, hybrid, and online classes) to enable student success;
Experience working successfully with a diverse student body, staff, and faculty;
Effective communication skills and ability to work collaboratively on projects and initiatives.
Equivalency Statement:
We welcome and encourage applicants who do not meet the qualifications as stated above, to put in writing precisely how their background and experience have prepared them for the responsibilities of this position. It is preferred that this document be uploaded separately from the resume, cover letter, and references. Preferred Qualifications:
A record of teaching excellence in Political Science at a community college or at the first year/sophomore college level;
Ph. D in Political Science or closely related field;
Interest in promoting and participating in interdisciplinary learning;
Ability to provide leadership within an academic department that will contribute to growth, innovation, and excellence in alignment with institutional goals;
Bilingual (English/Spanish).
Full-Time, Tenure-Track MCCC/MTA Position:
Salary Range: $58,722.00 - $70,786.00. Actual salary will be commensurate with education and experience in accordance with MCCC/MTA Collective Bargaining Agreement. Full State benefits.
Funding: State.
Start Date: Fall, 2027.
Additional Details:
Applicants must include a CV, cover letter, and syllabus in one of the following areas: US National Government, State & Local Government, or Civil Liberties.
A teaching demonstration is a required part of the interview process.
Disability Accommodations:
Holyoke Community College is committed to the full inclusion of individuals with disabilities and will ensure the availability of reasonable accommodations. If a reasonable accommodation is needed to participate in the job application or interview process, please contact the Office of People and Talent at (413) 552-2554.
Background Check:
Employment is contingent upon the successful completion and review of a background check which will include CORI (Criminal Offender Record Information) and SORI (Sex Offender Registry Information).
All candidates must have legal authorization to work in the United States. HCC is not sponsoring H1B Visa.
Holyoke Community College is an affirmative action/equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, disability, religion, age, veteran status, genetic information, gender identity or sexual orientation in its programs and activities as required by Title IX of the Educational Amendments of 1972, the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, and other applicable statutes and college policies. The College prohibits sexual harassment, including sexual violence. Inquiries or complaints concerning discrimination, harassment, retaliation or sexual violence shall be referred to the College’s Affirmative Action and/or Title IX Coordinator, the Massachusetts Commission Against Discrimination, the Equal Employment Opportunities Commission or the United States Department of Education’s Office for Civil Rights.

jobs.title: Assistant / Associate Professor of English – Anglophone African Literature
jobs.description:
Assistant / Associate Professor of English – Anglophone African Literature
The Department of English in the College of Arts and Sciences (CAS) at American University of Sharjah (AUS) invites applications for a full-time faculty position at the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor with a specialization in Anglophone African Literature to begin August 2027.
The successful candidate should have an active program of scholarly output in their field and a demonstrated commitment to excellence in undergraduate teaching. We are open to candidates with a wide range of approaches within the field of Anglophone African Literature. We are particularly interested in candidates who possess expertise in course and program development. Additional preferred qualifications include a minimum of three years’ experience teaching in North American-style higher education institutions and experience with international student populations.
Teaching responsibilities include a six-course annual load (3/3) in introductory and advanced literature, as well as academic writing and communication courses. Additional responsibilities include contributing to the intellectual life of the department and university through meaningful service, including student mentoring, enrichment events, and participation in shared governance responsibilities.
New faculty at AUS benefit from robust institutional support, including opportunities for internal grants, professional development support, and interdisciplinary collaboration. The Department of English is a diverse and dynamic community with wide-ranging teaching and research interests, including literary studies, linguistics, composition, and education. The department delivers the foundational university writing program, and offers a Bachelor of Arts in English Language and Literature and a Master of Arts in TESOL. For more information about the Department of English, please visit https://www.aus.edu/cas/department-of-english
Required Qualifications:
PhD in Literature (or a closely related discipline), with a research focus on Anglophone African Literature Record of high-quality publications commensurate with rank Teaching experience at the university level
Preferred Qualifications:
A minimum of three years’ experience teaching in North American-style higher education institutions Experience with international student populations
AUS is fully committed to equal opportunity at all levels without discrimination on the basis of race, gender, religion, age, family status, or national origin.
Positions are subject to budgetary approval.
About American University of Sharjah
American University of Sharjah (AUS) invites applications from accomplished scholars committed to excellence in teaching, learning and research within an American-style, globally recognized institution. Successful candidates will be offered a salary commensurate with experience, along with free housing, paid utilities and other attractive benefits.
As a comprehensive, independent, non-profit, coeducational university, AUS is consistently ranked among the top 10 universities in the Arab region and among the top 17 percent of ranked universities in the world (QS, 2027). The university fosters a diverse community of over 6,000 students from more than 100 nations, with English as the language of instruction and the workplace.
Located in Sharjah's University City, AUS is directly adjacent to the Sharjah Research, Technology and Innovation Park, providing faculty with significant opportunities to engage in interdisciplinary research and contribute directly to the UAE’s rapidly expanding innovation ecosystem. The campus is set in a vibrant and cosmopolitan area, offering abundant opportunities for travel, entertainment and cultural experiences, with Sharjah International Airport minutes away and Dubai International Airport only 30 minutes from campus. A number of schools aligned with various international curricula are located nearby.
AUS is licensed and its programs are accredited by the Commission for Academic Accreditation of the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research of the United Arab Emirates. AUS has been accredited in the United States of America by the Middle States Commission on Higher Education (1007 North Orange Street, 4th Floor, MB #166, Wilmington, DE 19801 USA) since June 2004.
For more information, please visit www.aus.edu.
Application Instructions
To apply, candidates should include the following in their online application, submitted to https://acg-apps1.aus.edu/cas/empapp/apply.php?p=ENG-27-01.
Cover letter detailing teaching experience and research activities (2-3pp) Current curriculum vitae including the names and contact details of three references
The submission deadline for full consideration is December 7, 2026. Incomplete applications will not be considered. Only candidates advancing in the selection process will be contacted. The committee expects to schedule interviews in late-January; at that time three letters of recommendation, a sample syllabus, and a writing sample will be requested.

jobs.title: Faculty Position in Ethics of Technology at the Ecole polytechnique fédérale de Lausanne
jobs.description:
The College of Management of Technology (CDM) at EPFL invites applications for a faculty position in Ethics of Technology, broadly construed. We seek an outstanding scholar whose research examines ethical questions raised by technology, its role in society, and its regulation. The position is open to candidates from a broad range of fields including computer science, cognitive science, economics, engineering, life sciences, statistics and related disciplines. The appointment will be at the Associate or Full Professor level with an expected start date in September 2027 (or mutually agreed upon).
The successful candidate will be based in the College of Management of Technology and contribute to its mission of advancing research and education at the interface of technology, organizations, economy, and society. The position is intended to provide intellectual leadership across EPFL on the ethical and societal dimensions of technology. The successful candidate will be expected to develop an ambitious research and teaching program that connects to scientific and technological domains across campus. They must have a strong commitment to excellence in teaching and contribute to CDM’s education programs at the undergraduate and graduate levels.
EPFL ranks among the world’s leading universities and offers internationally competitive salaries, generous research support, significant start-up resources, and excellent research infrastructure. The successful candidates will join an internationally oriented and research-active faculty and benefit from opportunities for collaboration across EPFL.
EPFL is located in Lausanne, Switzerland, a beautiful and vibrant city in an Alpine setting on the shores of Lake Geneva, in the heart of Europe. Switzerland offers an exceptionally high standard of living and Lausanne is a highly international city.
The application package should include the following documents in pdf format: cover letter including a statement of motivation; curriculum vitae; publication list; research statement; statement of teaching interests; as well as the names and contact of five to seven references who are ready to supply a letter upon request.
Application deadline: November 15, 2026.
Applications should be uploaded to the EPFL recruitment page:
https://facultyrecruiting.epfl.ch/position/65044492
Inquiries can be addressed to:
Prof. Daniel Kuhn
Director of the Management of Technology & Entrepreneurship institute
Chair of the Search Committee
E-mail: cdm_erecruiting@epfl.ch
Further information on EPFL and CDM is available at epfl.ch and cdm.epfl.ch
EPFL is an equal opportunity employer and family friendly university. It is committed to increasing the diversity of its faculty. It strongly encourages women to apply.

jobs.title: Associate Professor/Professor - Indigenous Knowledge Systems
jobs.description:
Job Details
Associate Professor/Professor - Indigenous Knowledge Systems
Date Posted: 10/05/2026
Closing Date: 11/11/2026, 11:59PM ET
Req ID: 48735
Job Category: Faculty - Tenure Stream (continuing)
Faculty/Division: Faculty of Arts & Science
Department: Centre for Indigenous Studies
Campus: St. George (Downtown Toronto)
Existing Vacancy: Yes
POSITION DESCRIPTION
The Centre for Indigenous Studies in the Faculty of Arts & Science at the University of Toronto invites applications for a full-time tenure stream position in the area of Indigenous Knowledge Systems. The appointment will be at the rank of Associate Professor or Professor, with an anticipated start date of July 1, 2027.
Preference will be given to candidates who self-identify as Indigenous. Recognizing that there are a variety of terms that potential candidates may use to self-identify, the University uses the term “Indigenous” in this search, which forms part of the U of T Response to Canada’s Truth and Reconciliation Commission, to encompass the people of Turtle Island, including those who identify as First Nations, Métis, Inuk (Inuit), Alaska Native, Native American, and Native Hawaiian people.
REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS
Applicants must have earned a PhD degree in Indigenous Studies or a related area, with a clearly demonstrated record of excellence in research and teaching in Indigenous Knowledge Systems. Candidates must have an established international reputation. We seek candidates whose research and teaching interests complement and enhance our existing departmental strengths.
The candidate will have a deep understanding of the Indigenous Knowledge systems and pedagogies of their own people, community, or Nation, including knowledge gained through sustained community relationships and culturally grounded practices of teaching and learning. The candidate must also demonstrate the ability to teach Indigenous and non-Indigenous students how Indigenous Knowledge systems and pedagogies shape Indigenous Studies and other academic disciplines. Knowledge of one or more Indigenous languages is also an asset.
Candidates must provide evidence of research excellence, as demonstrated by a record of sustained high-impact contributions and publications in top-ranked and field-relevant journals; the submitted research statement; presentations at significant conferences; awards and accolades; other noteworthy activities that contribute to the visibility and prominence of the discipline; and strong endorsements from referees.
A demonstrated record of experience and engagement, including relationship-building, long- standing relationships, and work with community leaders and Elders/Knowledge Holders, is required. Candidates must also demonstrate long-term experience and ethical engagement with Indigenous organizations and institutions and evidence of understanding the importance of consensus-building relationships.
Evidence of excellence in teaching will be demonstrated through teaching accomplishments, the teaching dossier (including the required materials outlined below), and strong letters of reference.
RESPONSIBILITIES
Candidates will be expected to sustain and lead innovative and independent research, and to maintain an outstanding, competitive, and externally funded research program.
In addition, the successful candidate will be assigned a teaching and service load.
The Centre for Indigenous Studies is in the process of developing a graduate program and the successful candidate will have the opportunity to be fully engaged in the development and implementation of the program.
HIRING SALARY RANGE
The rank and salary will be commensurate with qualifications and experience. The upper end of the salary range for this position exceeds $200,000 CAD per annum.
ABOUT US
Building upon the expertise of our faculty and the extensive resources of the University, the Centre for Indigenous Studies houses an interdisciplinary program within the Faculty of Arts & Science and is uniquely positioned to nurture critical scholarship and teaching. We draw faculty members and students from across the world and are situated in one of the most diverse metropolitan regions in North America, on the traditional land of many Indigenous nations, including the Wendat, the Seneca (Haudenosaunee), and the Mississaugas of the Credit.
For more information on working at the University of Toronto, please visit https://www.utoronto.ca/research-innovation/working-at-uoft.
APPLICATION PROCESS
All application materials, including recent reference letters, must be received by November 11, 2026.
All qualified candidates are invited to apply online by clicking the link below. Your CV and cover letter should be uploaded into the dedicated fields. Please combine additional application materials into one or two files in PDF/MS Word format. Applicants must submit the following materials:
a cover letter;
a current curriculum vitae;
a research statement outlining current and future research interests;
one recent publication;
a teaching dossier, includinga teaching statement,
sample course materials, and
teaching evaluations; and
the name and contact information of three references.
Equity, diversity and inclusion are essential to academic excellence as articulated in University of Toronto’s Statement on Equity, Diversity and Excellence. We seek candidates who share these values and who demonstrate throughout the application materials their commitment and efforts to advance equity, diversity, inclusion, and the promotion of a respectful and collegial learning and working environment.
Applicants must arrange to have three letters of reference (on letterhead, dated and signed) sent directly by the referee via email to indigenousstudies.admin@utoronto.ca by the closing date. Reference letters should be addressed to Professor Susan Hill, Director, Centre for Indigenous Studies.
If you have any questions about this position, please contact Susan Hill at indigenousstudies.admin@utoronto.ca.
The University of Toronto has adopted the AAU Principles on Preventing Sexual Harassment in Academia, including the requirement that applicants release personnel information from prior employers regarding sexual misconduct. Full details and requirements can be found here.
Please note: Artificial intelligence (AI) tools may be used in the initial screening or assessment of applications; however, all final assessments and hiring decisions are made by the search committee members.
All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply; however, Canadians and permanent residents will be given priority.
Diversity Statement
The University of Toronto embraces Diversity and is building a culture of belonging that increases our capacity to effectively address and serve the interests of our global community. We strongly encourage applications from Indigenous Peoples, Black and racialized persons, women, persons with disabilities, and people of diverse sexual and gender identities. We value applicants who have demonstrated a commitment to equity, diversity and inclusion and recognize that diverse perspectives, experiences, and expertise are essential to strengthening our academic mission.
As part of your application, you will be asked to complete a brief Diversity Survey. This survey is voluntary. Any information directly related to you is confidential and cannot be accessed by search committees or human resources staff. Results will be aggregated for institutional planning purposes. For more information, please see http://uoft.me/UP.
Accessibility Statement
The University strives to be an equitable and inclusive community, and proactively seeks to increase diversity among its community members. Our values regarding equity and diversity are linked with our unwavering commitment to excellence in the pursuit of our academic mission.
The University is committed to the principles of the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA). As such, we strive to make our recruitment, assessment and selection processes as accessible as possible and provide accommodations as required for applicants with disabilities.
If you require any accommodations at any point during the application and hiring process, please contact uoft.careers@utoronto.ca.

POSITION DESCRIPTION
The Department of Language Studies at the University of Toronto Scarborough (UTSC) invites applications for a full-time teaching stream position in Linguistics. The appointment will be at the rank of Assistant Professor, Teaching Stream, with an anticipated start date of July 1, 2027.
This search aligns with the University’s commitment to strategically and proactively promote diversity among our community members (Statement on Equity, Diversity & Excellence). Recognizing that Black, Indigenous, and other Racialized communities have experienced inequities that have developed historically and are ongoing, we strongly welcome and encourage candidates from those communities to apply.
In addition, the University of Toronto Scarborough is implementing its Strategic Plan: Inspiring Inclusive Excellence. Consistent with the values and objectives in that plan, we especially welcome candidates who self-identify as Indigenous or those who have lived experience in Black or other racialized (persons of colour) communities. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to be connected with colleagues from under-represented groups, including those hired through targeted efforts in recent years across departments spanning the Sciences, Social Sciences, and Humanities.
REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS
Applicants must have earned a PhD degree in Linguistics or a related area by the time of appointment, or shortly thereafter, with a demonstrated record of excellence in teaching Linguistics in a degree-granting program. We seek candidates whose teaching interests complement and enhance our existing departmental strengths.
Candidates must have teaching experience in a degree-granting program, including lecture preparation and delivery, curriculum development, and development of online material/lectures. Additionally, candidates must possess a demonstrated commitment to excellent pedagogical inquiry and innovative teaching practices such as Experiential Learning, as well as a demonstrated interest in teaching-related scholarly activities in Linguistics. Candidates must also demonstrate the ability to teach a range of class sizes and course levels, and an interest in developing a long-term career in teaching and related scholarly activity in Linguistics. We are looking for a colleague who specializes in sound systems (phonetics/phonology), with preference given to candidates with a secondary specialization in language acquisition, speech-language disorders, or documentation.
Evidence of excellence in teaching and a commitment to excellent pedagogical inquiry will be demonstrated through teaching accomplishments, awards and accolades, presentations at significant conferences, the teaching dossier (including the required materials outlined below), and strong letters of reference.
Candidates must also show evidence of a commitment to equity, diversity, inclusion, and to the promotion of a respectful and collegial learning and working environment, as demonstrated through the application materials.
RESPONSIBILITIES
The successful candidate will be assigned a teaching and service load.
HIRING SALARY RANGE
The salary range is $115,000 - $135,000 CAD per annum, depending on experience. Negotiations beyond this salary range will be considered for exceptionally qualified candidates.
ABOUT US
The Department of Language Studies, located at the University of Toronto Scarborough (UTSC), offers a rich selection of undergraduate programs in Linguistics, French, and English & Chinese Translation. Our faculty are internationally recognized scholars whose research encompasses a wide range of fields, including language acquisition, multilingualism, psycholinguistics, translation, discourse analysis, language documentation and revitalization, sociolinguistics, French language and literature, and English and Chinese translation.
We are a collaborative and intellectually dynamic academic community where excellence in research and teaching go hand in hand. Our faculty are dedicated to creating an inclusive, engaging, and supportive learning environment that encourages intellectual curiosity, critical inquiry, and experiential learning. Through innovative teaching and active scholarship, we prepare students to become thoughtful, adaptable, and globally engaged graduates.

POSITION DESCRIPTION
The Centre for Indigenous Studies in the Faculty of Arts & Science at the University of Toronto invites applications for a full-time tenure stream position in the area of Indigenous Knowledge Systems. The appointment will be at the rank of Assistant Professor, with an anticipated start date of July 1, 2027.
Preference will be given to candidates who self-identify as Indigenous. Recognizing that there are a variety of terms that potential candidates may use to self-identify, the University uses the term “Indigenous” in this search, which forms part of the U of T Response to Canada’s Truth and Reconciliation Commission, to encompass the people of Turtle Island, including those who identify as First Nations, Métis, Inuk (Inuit), Alaska Native, Native American, and Native Hawaiian people.
REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS
Candidates must have earned a PhD degree in Indigenous Studies or a related area by the time of appointment, or shortly thereafter, with a demonstrated record of excellence in research and teaching in Indigenous Knowledge Systems. We seek candidates whose research and teaching interests complement and enhance our existing departmental strengths. The candidate will have a deep understanding of the Indigenous Knowledge systems and pedagogies of their own people, community, or Nation, including knowledge gained through sustained community relationships and culturally grounded practices of teaching and learning. The candidate must also demonstrate the ability to teach Indigenous and non-Indigenous students how Indigenous Knowledge systems and pedagogies shape Indigenous Studies and other academic disciplines. Knowledge of one or more Indigenous languages is also an asset.
Candidates must provide evidence of research excellence which can be demonstrated through a record of publications in top-ranked and field-relevant journals or forthcoming publications that meet high international standards; the submitted research statement; presentations at significant conferences; awards and accolades; and strong endorsements from referees.
Candidates should have teaching experience in a degree-granting program, including lecture preparation and delivery, curriculum development, and development of online material/lectures. A demonstrated record of experience and engagement, including relationship-building, long- standing relationships, and work with community leaders and Elders/Knowledge Holders, is required. Candidates must also demonstrate long-term experience and ethical engagement with Indigenous organizations and institutions and evidence of understanding the importance of consensus-building relationships. Engagement with Indigenous communities will be demonstrated through reference letters and other application materials.
Evidence of excellence in teaching will be demonstrated through teaching accomplishments, the teaching dossier (including the required materials outlined below), and strong letters of reference.
RESPONSIBILITIES
The successful candidate will be expected to pursue innovative and independent research, and to establish an outstanding, competitive, and externally funded research program.
In addition, the successful candidate will be assigned a teaching and service load.

The expected salary range is $120,000 - $160,000 CAD per annum, depending on experience. Negotiations beyond this salary range will be considered for exceptionally qualified candidates.

We draw faculty members and students from across the world and are situated in one of the most diverse metropolitan regions in North America, on the traditional land of many Indigenous nations, including the Wendat, the Seneca (Haudenosaunee), and the Mississaugas of the Credit.
For more information on working at the University of Toronto, please visit https://www.utoronto.ca/research-innovation/working-at-uoft.

POSITION DESCRIPTION:
The Department of Health and Society (DHS) at the University of Toronto Scarborough (UTSC) invite applications for a full-time tenure stream position in Climate and Community Health Equity. The appointment will be at the rank of Assistant Professor, with an anticipated start date of July 1, 2027.
This position part of the Canada Excellence Research Chair’s Network for Equity in Sustainability Transitions (CERC NEST). The CERC NEST uses a transdisciplinary, comparative and action-centred approach with communities and city actors in Toronto and internationally to examine how to enhance participation in decision-making, address inequities in regulations and investments, and ensure fair distribution of benefits, livability and a good life for all.
REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS
Candidates must have earned a PhD degree in a related discipline (e.g., Sociology, Engineering, Public Health, Environmental Sciences, etc.) by the time of appointment or shortly thereafter with a demonstrated record of excellence in research and teaching. We seek candidates whose research and teaching interests complement and broaden our existing departmental strengths, dovetail with CERC NEST research vision and methodologies, and enhance the campus strengths and priorities.
The successful candidate will have mixed or multi-methods research experience relevant to sustainability transitions by focusing on the human health and community equity implications of climate-related issues, such as extreme heat, air pollution (indoor and ambient), and energy use in cities. Grounded in the CERC-NEST goal of co-producing knowledge to foster equity in sustainability transitions, this hire will take an integrated approach to community health equity. Teaching experience is essential, and experience in curriculum or course development will be considered an asset. Strong professional, research, and academic networks are also advantageous.
Candidates must provide evidence of research excellence which can be demonstrated through a record of publications in top-ranked and field-relevant journals or forthcoming publications that meet high international standards; the submitted research statement; as well as presentations at significant conferences; awards and accolades; and strong endorsements from referees of high standing.
Demonstrated teaching ability across a range of courses is required, including areas such as climate change mitigation and adaptation in cities, community health equity, and health across diverse communities throughout the lifespan. Evidence of excellence in teaching will be demonstrated through teaching accomplishments, the teaching dossier (including the required materials outlined below, as well as evidence of superior performance in other teaching-related activities), and strong letters of reference. Other teaching-related activities can include performance as a teaching assistant or course instructor, experience leading successful workshops or seminars, student mentorship, or excellent conference presentations or posters.
Equity and diversity are essential to academic excellence. We seek candidates who value diversity and whose research, teaching, and service commit to equity, diversity, inclusion and to the promotion of a respectful and collegial learning and working environment, as demonstrated through the application materials. Candidates are asked to submit a 1–2-page statement of contributions to equity and diversity, which might cover topics such as (but not limited to): research or teaching that incorporates a focus on underrepresented communities, the development of inclusive pedagogies, or the mentoring of students from underrepresented groups.
RESPONSIBILITIES
The successful candidate will be expected to pursue innovative and independent research, and to establish an outstanding, competitive, and externally funded research program. The successful candidate is also expected to establish strong connections particularly within Scarborough and between DHS, the CERC NEST, and the new Scarborough Academy of Medicine and Integrated Health (SAMIH).
In addition, the successful candidate will be assigned a teaching and service load.
HIRING SALARY RANGE
The salary range is $145,000 - $165,000 CAD per annum, depending on experience. Negotiations beyond this salary range will be considered for exceptionally qualified candidates.
ABOUT US
The University of Toronto offers the opportunity to conduct research and creative practice, teach, and live in one of the most diverse cities in the world. The appointment is at the University of Toronto Scarborough, which is a research-intensive campus with an interdisciplinary commitment, a multicultural student body, and a modern campus. Within the University of Toronto Scarborough, the Department of Health and Society is home to a diverse community of students, teachers, and researchers. Members of our growing department ask cutting-edge questions about health, disability, illness, and disease, locally and globally and from a range of disciplinary perspectives. For more information about the Department of Health and Society at the University of Toronto Scarborough, please visit our website.

jobs.description:
Job Details
Posting Number:
PG194875EP
Internal Recruitment :
No
Working Title:
Open Rank Teaching Faculty
Anticipated Hiring Range:
Commensurate with education and experience: (Asst Teaching Professor: $120,000 – $130,000; Assoc Teaching Professor: $130,000 – $145,000; Teaching Professor: $145,000 – $160,000)
Work Schedule:
Monday through Friday, 8 am to 5 pm (additional work outside of standard hours may be required due to business needs)
Job Location:
Raleigh, NC
Department :
Institute for Advanced Analytics
About the Department:
Established in 2007, the NC State University Institute for Advanced Analytics (IAA) is a global leader in graduate analytics education. The Institute prepares future analytics professionals through an immersive, interdisciplinary curriculum integrating statistics, data science, artificial intelligence, machine learning, operations research, and business strategy. The Institute’s flagship Master of Science in Analytics (MSA) program is complemented by a growing portfolio of professional education and online certificate programs designed to meet the evolving workforce needs of industry.
The Institute maintains strong partnerships with corporate, government, and nonprofit organizations to provide applied learning experiences that prepare graduates and working professionals to solve complex, data-driven business challenges.
Wolfpack Perks and Benefits:
As a Pack member, you belong here, and can enjoy exclusive perks designed to enhance your personal and professional well-being. As you consider this opportunity, we encourage you to review our Employee Value Proposition and learn more about what makes NC State the best place to learn and work for everyone.
What we offer:
Medical, Dental, and Vision
Flexible Spending Account
Retirement Programs
Disability Plans
Life Insurance
Accident Plan
Paid Time Off and Other Leave Programs
12 Holidays Each Year
Tuition and Academic Assistance
And so much more!
Attain Work-life balance with our Childcare benefits, Wellness & Recreation Membership, and Wellness Programs that aim to build a thriving wolfpack community.
Disclaimer: Perks and Benefit eligibility is based on Part-Time or Full-Time Employment status. Eligibility and Employer Sponsored Plans can be found within each of the links offered.
Essential Job Duties:
The Institute for Advanced Analytics invites applications for an open-rank Assistant, Associate, or full Teaching Professor. This 12-month non-tenure-track faculty position will play a central role in developing, delivering, and continuously improving the Institute’s portfolio of online professional certificate programs and graduate instruction.
As a faculty member, you will shape how working professionals and graduate students learn and apply analytics in a rapidly evolving field. You will bring your expertise in analytics, artificial intelligence, machine learning, and data science into the classroom while creating practical, technology-enabled learning experiences that connect academic knowledge to real-world challenges. Through teaching, mentoring, curriculum innovation, and collaboration with faculty and industry partners, you will help prepare learners to apply emerging tools and insights in their professional work.
Key Responsibilities fall within the following functional areas:
Online Curriculum Development and Teaching:
Lead the design, development, delivery, and continuous improvement of online certificate and graduate courses, creating engaging content and assessments that support meaningful learning outcomes.
Create engaging asynchronous and synchronous learning experiences using modern educational technologies and evidence-based instructional practices.
Continuously strengthen curriculum by incorporating advances in analytics and emerging technologies and using student feedback and assessment data to improve learning experiences.
Partner with faculty, instructional designers, educational technology professionals, and media specialists to deliver high-quality online learning experiences.
Deliver graduate and professional education courses in analytics and related disciplines.
Student Engagement and Applied Learning:
Mentor graduate students through industry-sponsored projects, connecting them with corporate partners and guiding teams from planning through final deliverables.
Provide academic and professional advising through regular student engagement and office hours.
Supervise graduate teaching assistants as assigned.
Foster a collaborative learning environment that supports student growth and professional development.
Program Development and Professional Engagement:
Help shape professional education offerings in response to emerging workforce needs and opportunities.
Partner with faculty, Institute leadership, and industry stakeholders to strengthen curriculum and experiential learning.
Contribute to program assessment, accreditation, recruitment, outreach, and executive education activities.
Build relationships with industry partners that expand learning and professional opportunities for students.
Service and Scholarly Engagement:
Contribute to Institute and university committees, admissions, curriculum planning, and faculty governance.
Maintain current expertise through professional development in analytics education, instructional technology, and industry trends.
Pursue scholarly and professional activities aligned with your expertise and rank, including applied research, presentations, publications, consulting, or industry collaboration.
If you are energized by helping learners translate analytics and emerging technologies into meaningful solutions, we invite you to bring your expertise to a faculty community committed to innovation, applied learning, and the evolving needs of today’s workforce.
Other Responsibilities:
n/a
Minimum Education and Experience:
Assistant Teaching Professor
Doctoral degree, equivalent degree, or equivalent professional experience in analytics, data science, statistics, computer science, information systems, operations research, business analytics, artificial intelligence, or a closely related discipline.
Expertise in one or more areas of analytics or data science.
Teaching, training, or curriculum development experience with graduate-level courses.
Ability to communicate complex analytics concepts effectively with students, faculty, and industry partners.
Associate Teaching Professor: In addition to the qualifications for Assistant Teaching Professor:
Established record of teaching experience in higher education, executive education, or professional training.
Record of developing curriculum or educational programs.
Leadership in professional practice, industry, or applied analytics.
Demonstrated contributions to academic service or program leadership.
Teaching Professor: In addition to the qualifications for Associate Teaching Professor:
National or international recognition as a leader in analytics or a related field.
Distinguished record of curriculum innovation, educational programs, or industry initiatives.
Sustained impact through teaching, professional engagement, and service.
Proven leadership that advances analytics in higher education, industry, or both.
Other Required Qualifications:
n/a
Preferred Qualifications:
Background in designing and teaching fully online or hybrid courses.
Experience with learning management systems such as Moodle or Canvas.
Industry expertise applying analytics, artificial intelligence, machine learning, or data science to business challenges.
Knowledge of online instructional design and quality frameworks, such as Quality Matters.

Essential Job Duties:
The Assistant Professor of Population Medicine and Career Success specializes in Large Animal Population Medicine and Veterinary Education Scholarship. This dynamic role is designed for an innovative educator and researcher ready to shape the future of veterinary medicine by blending cutting-edge clinical instruction with ground-breaking educational research. This position plays a central role in delivering our core DVM curriculum while building a nationally recognized research program that drives innovation in farm animal health, AI integration, immersive learning, and student well-being.
Teaching:
Based on specific focus, this faculty member will contribute to population medicine and career readiness teaching in existing core, elective and selective courses. The faculty member will also have the option to participate in teaching and/or proposing new selective, elective or special topics courses. Interested individuals may contribute to ongoing development of house officer and graduate student competency-based training programs and trainee assessments.
Research:
This position is expected to establish an impactful, nationally recognized research program at the intersection of Large Animal Population Medicine and Veterinary Education Scholarship. This dual-focus program will address critical gaps in population health education by actively developing, implementing, and evaluating novel teaching methods. This position will focus on discovery that interrogates, innovates and transforms farm animal population health and career readiness training in veterinary education. The research will address gaps in knowledge and pivotal questions including, but not limited to, the following examples:
Immersive Technologies and Virtual Reality (VR): Investigating the design, implementation, and educational efficacy of immersive virtual environments—such as “digital twin” models of production facilities, processing plants, or pasture ecosystems. This research will leverage VR to simulate complex, high-stakes population medicine scenarios (e.g., biosecurity breaches, foreign animal disease outbreaks, and large-scale herd epidemiology mapping). The focus will be on assessing how immersive environments support rapid systemic decision-making, epidemiological risk assessment, and spatial problem-solving without inducing real-world biosecurity or animal welfare risks.
Competency-Based Veterinary Education (CBVE) & Advanced Assessments: Developing and validating robust, outcomes-based assessment methodologies. This includes creating standard-setting tools that reliably evaluate both technical execution (e.g., simulation-based herd analytics or theriogenology models) and non-technical professional competencies (e.g., communication, animal welfare advocacy, and One Health system collaboration).
Experiential, Simulation, and Community-Engaged Learning: Evaluating the educational efficacy and scalable impact of ambulatory training and community-partnered outreach to bridge the gap between tertiary referral environments and general production practice. Comparing student learning outcomes relevant to population medicine in different clinical settings.
Professional Identity Formation (PIF) and Career Sustainability: Investigating the longitudinal development of professional identity in DVM students and its explicit correlation to post-graduation career satisfaction, practitioner retention, and mental well-being. This research will evaluate how educational interventions, mentorship, and hidden curricula influence the psychological transition from student to clinician. Specifically, it will look at how to cultivate a resilient, “challenge-focused” professional identity within large animal and population medicine—equipping graduates to find career satisfaction while navigating the unique systemic, environmental, and socio-economic pressures intrinsic to production animal practice.
Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Digital Literacy: Investigating the integration of generative AI, intelligent tutoring systems, and clinical decision support models into the DVM curriculum. Research will evaluate how to foster AI literacy and “appropriate skepticism” while examining the cognitive risks of overreliance, algorithmic bias, and data privacy in production animal surveillance.
This individual will join existing large and farm animal faculty and staff currently teaching population medicine and epidemiology in DVM years 1-4.

Essential Job Duties:
The Assistant Professor of Large Animal Clinical Skills and Career Success will join a dedicated group of faculty and staff currently teaching large animal clinical skills, medicine and surgery. A combination of models, simulations and farm animals at the Teaching Animal Unit and Reedy Creek Farm are used to facilitate assessments that can be used to develop skills portfolios and investigate best practices in feedback and remediation of clinical skills.
Teaching:
This faculty member will contribute to clinical skills, large animal and career readiness teaching in existing core, elective and selective courses. The faculty member will also have the option to participate in teaching and/or proposing new selective or elective courses. Interested individuals may contribute to ongoing development of house officer and graduate student competency-based training programs and trainee assessments.
Research:
This faculty member will establish an impactful and nationally recognized research program dedicated to advancing Large Animal Clinical Skills educational research. As veterinary curricula globally evolve to meet changing technological, societal, and agricultural needs, this position will drive evidence-based advancements in how veterinary students acquire, refine, and maintain large animal technical and clinical competencies. The faculty member will be expected to investigate current high-priority areas and address critical, unmapped gaps in knowledge within veterinary medical education. The prospective areas of educational research supported by this position include, but are not limited to:
Simulation-Based Learning & Physical Model Innovation: Developing, validating, and optimizing large animal (equine, bovine, and production animal) procedural models, simulators and assessments (i.e. OSCEs, mini-CEX, etc.). A primary research gap in this domain is the critical lack of longitudinal data assessing the long-term transferability of skills from synthetic simulators to live animal clinical scenarios to practice, as well as addressing the historical “small animal bias” in existing commercial simulation tools.
Artificial Intelligence (AI) & Digital Workflow Integration: Exploring the integration of generative AI, multimodal large language models, and AI-standardized stakeholders within clinical training and communication workflows. Research will target how to teach students to utilize AI safely, ethically, and responsibly for diagnostic reasoning and uncertainty management, while addressing student adoption challenges, cognitive overreliance, and technological biases.
Competency-Based Veterinary Education (CBVE) & Assessment: Designing, implementing, and validating objective, standardized assessment instruments and grading frameworks for psychomotor skills. Research will focus on mapping competencies to pedagogical combinations that offer the highest cost-benefit ratios and efficacy for equine and production animal training.
Remediation Strategies & Cognitive Load Management: Developing evidence-based intervention and remediation strategies for students experiencing difficulties with technical proficiency. This includes studying methods to lower student anxiety and ensure safety during the high-stakes transition from low-stress models to live, potentially unpredictable large animals.
Spectrum of Care, Ethics, & Community-Engaged Learning: Investigating educational frameworks that prepare students to practice quality medicine across a spectrum of care, particularly in resource-limited, rural, or underserved environments. Research could address how experiential learning in these settings impacts clinical skill acquisition and influences veterinary workforce shortages in production animal medicine.
Community-based Education Models & Educator Development: Assessing how the pedagogical characteristics, instructional proficiency, professional identity and career satisfaction of clinical educators affect student learning in off-campus clinical teaching environments. Research will target frameworks for standardizing educator professional development and mentoring ability among non-faculty clinical preceptors.
Pipeline Development, Admissions Predictors, & Career Sustainability: Investigating the correlation between holistic DVM admissions criteria (e.g., non-cognitive attributes, rural or agricultural backgrounds, specific pre-veterinary experiences) and long-term career commitment to large animal and food supply veterinary medicine. Research in this domain will target the critical “pipeline leak”—the documented decline in large animal career interest that occurs over the course of the four-year professional curriculum. Prospective studies will explore how educational interventions, early tracking pathways, mentorship frameworks, and systemic support systems can mitigate burnout, bridge the pay-to-debt gap, and ensure the geographic and economic sustainability of the large animal veterinary workforce in rural and underserved areas.
Wellbeing, Professional Identity, & Veterinary Humanities: Evaluating the intersections of clinical skills mastery with veterinary humanities, ethical reasoning, and professional identity formation. The program will examine how early, structured competence in large animal handling correlates with student self-care, resilience, and long-term career sustainability.

Position Details
The Department of Health Sciences and Human Performance within the College of Natural and Health Sciences at The University of Tampa invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position with expertise in Exercise Science, beginning in August 2027.
We seek a highly qualified and motivated faculty member to complement and enhance our undergraduate Human Performance and graduate Exercise and Nutrition Science programs.
Teaching: The ideal candidate will be committed to teaching a variety of courses in exercise science, nutrition, and human performance. Depending on the candidate's expertise and departmental needs, teaching responsibilities may include, but are not limited to, undergraduate and graduate nutrition courses, Introduction to Exercise Science, Senior Seminar, Practicum in Exercise Science, and Internship supervision. The successful candidate may also teach other graduate-level courses in the Exercise and Nutrition Science program, including courses delivered in hybrid formats (i.e., online and face-to-face instruction). Experience with program accreditation processes is desirable. Faculty members are expected to create engaging and inclusive learning environments that challenge students to reach their full potential.
Responsibilities will include a teaching load of 12 credit/contact hours per semester at the undergraduate and graduate levels.
Service and Student Involvement: We expect our colleagues to fully engage with the institution by providing and/or developing expertise that serves the broader needs of the institution as a requirement for this position. Community and professional service are also valued contributions, particularly where relevant to the discipline. Successful colleagues engage undergraduate and graduate students in a variety of activities as a means of providing greater depth and opportunity to the educational experience at the university. Faculty members also advise students each semester, providing important guidance for enrollment as well as career advice. Service: Experience with the program accreditation process would be desirable.
Scholarship: Candidates are expected to maintain an active scholarly agenda appropriate to their field and the resources available at The University of Tampa. Scholarly activities should contribute to the candidate's currency in their field and are considered in the tenure evaluation process. The exact nature and extent of scholarly expectations may vary by department and should be discussed with the department chair and dean. Start-up funds and research spaces are available but limited compared to research-intensive institutions. As one of the largest departments in the University, ample opportunities exist for collaboration within the department, and our faculty are routinely successful at securing internal grant funds to support research. Assistance is available to identify external grant sources, grant writing, and additional sources of funding for equipment that cannot be purchased with start-up funds.
Qualifications: Applicants must have a Ph.D. in Health Sciences and Human Performance or related discipline by August 2027. Candidates holding certifications as a Certified Strength Conditioning Specialist (NSCA) and/or Certified Exercise Physiologist (ACSM-EP) are desirable.
The candidate is expected to engage in scholarly activity, advise/mentor students, and participate in service to the department, college, University, and broader community.
The salary for this position is competitive and commensurate with qualifications and experience.

The University is ideally situated on a beautiful 110-acre campus next to the Hillsborough River, adjacent to Tampa's dynamic central business district, which is a growing, vibrant, diverse metropolitan area. UTampa reflects this vibrancy; with 30 consecutive years of enrollment growth UTampa boasts 260 student organizations, a multicultural student body from 50 states and more than 100 countries, and "Top Tier" ranking in U.S. News and World Report.
The University delivers challenging and high-quality educational experiences to a diverse group of learners. The University has a strong core curriculum rooted in the liberal arts, an enduring commitment to internationalization that has garnered the Senator Paul Simon Award, and a practical, experiential approach to learning. The University offers more than 200 areas of study, including majors in our colleges of Arts and Letters, Business, Natural and Health Sciences and Social Sciences, Math and Education, 18 master's programs, and 3 professional doctoral programs.
The College of Natural and Health Sciences offers rigorous, high quality curricula in biology, marine science, environmental science, chemistry, biochemistry, physics, forensic science, exercise science, public health, allied health, sport management and nursing; all designed to prepare students for challenges and opportunities that lie ahead. Our faculty are excellent teachers, both in the classroom and working with students on an individual basis. UT has invested heavily in the development of our college's teaching and research facilities and laboratories. Our college continually fosters relationships with organizations in the greater Tampa Bay area and elsewhere to provide students with the opportunity to pursue an internship, volunteer, or interact with professionals working in their chosen field. Each department also offers study abroad courses that students can take for credit toward their degree. For more information, see: https://www.ut.edu/academics/college-of-natural-and-health-sciences.

Job Posting Title:
Faculty, Korean
Job Description Summary:
The Department of World Languages (WOLA) faculty supports student learning across on-campus and distance learning modalities. This position is a Korean teaching role with opportunities to teach additional languages offered within the department if SACSCOC credentialing criteria are met. Faculty prepare and deliver engaging, innovative coursework aligned with the ACTFL World-Readiness Standards. A successful candidate will bring strong communication skills, a collaborative spirit, and a commitment to student success in an environment that promotes belonging for all. This position begins in August 2027.
Job Description:
The World Languages Department offers credit courses across 10 languages of instruction leading to an Associate of Arts degree in both on-campus and online formats. Recognized for excellence, our department has earned an "Exemplary" assessment rating for 10 consecutive years and is home to several award-winning faculty members. Our faculty actively engage in innovative practices in language pedagogy, second-language acquisition, and multi linguistic, with opportunities to participate in service learning and global learning experiences, including study abroad. Above all, advancing a deep appreciation and understanding of global cultures remains a foundational commitment of our department.
Principal Responsibilities and Duties
Prepare and teach courses in the field of Korean language to a multicultural student population based on the department's approved course learning outcomes, utilizing a variety of instructional strategies appropriate to the needs of community college students and the standards of the discipline.
Participate actively in departmental responsibilities and departmental governance, including curriculum review and revision, program review, assessment of student learning outcomes at the course and program level, and other departmental activities.
Administer and evaluate departmental Course Challenge Exams in Korean and maintain and revise Course Challenge Exam materials to ensure alignment with departmental curriculum and learning outcomes.
Evaluate student progress and provide clear, timely feedback reflecting program learning outcomes and departmental expectations.
Serve as a mentor to students in the Korean program.
Provide teaching and mentoring services to students in a manner which does not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, age, protected veteran status, political affiliation, or other protected categories.
Remain current in the field through a variety of professional development activities.
Support division and department goals through active and collegial engagement in decision-making and unit-level planning.
Serve on collegewide and departmental committees, councils, work groups, and task forces.
Perform other related tasks as assigned by the department chair, dean, and/or associate vice chancellor, vice chancellor, executive vice chancellor.
Technology
Demonstrated proficiency using computer applications, online resources, and other technologies for the classroom.
Demonstrated proficiency using an online learning management system such as Blackboard to develop and build course content and perform administrative duties (posting office hours, syllabi, etc.)
Principal Professional Standards
Appropriate use of the college's learning management system.
Meet deadlines for attendance certification and submission of final course grades.
Participate in graduation, general assembly, and other official college functions.
Maintain regular office hours to assist students and improve student retention and success.
Attend and participate in collegewide, campus, department, or other activities and meetings.
Recognize and reflect standards of civility and collegiality in all interactions.
Comply with published college policies and procedures and meet professional standards for teaching in a community college.
Required Education
Master's degree in Korean, or
Master's degree with 18 graduate hours in Korean
In accordance with Southern Association of College and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC) requirements. SACSCOC requirements may differ depending on the courses taught within the discipline.
Preferred Education
In addition to meeting the required education qualifications in Korean, a minimum of 18 graduate semester hours in one of the following languages is preferred: Arabic, Chinese, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Latin, Russian, or Spanish.
This list reflects the additional languages offered by the Department of World Languages.
​
Qualities of a Successful Candidate
Ethics, integrity, and sound professional judgment.
A commitment to establishing and maintaining positive working relationships with students, colleagues, and staff representing multicultural and socioeconomic backgrounds.
Dynamic, non-traditional instructional delivery methods to teach students of widely varying levels of proficiency and from various backgrounds and abilities.
Appropriate and up-to-date knowledge of the discipline and subject matter.
Experience using technology as an instructional aide where appropriate to enhance learning.
Documented experience with active and applied teaching and learning methodologies.
A strong commitment to teaching in a community college setting, including teaching practices that reflect an understanding of the multicultural classroom and the benefits of cultural awareness and sensitivity in the classroom and the workplace.
Commitment to a culture of care for all.
Commitment to the comprehensive mission of Austin Community College and to the principles and practices associated with Servant-Leadership.
Ability to communicate effectively with students with a wide range of skills and backgrounds.
Strong interpersonal skills and ability to work with varied populations from the local community as well as students, staff, faculty, and administration.
Strength in communication media, both verbal and written, as well as listening.
Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, ability to maintain an established schedule, including evenings and weekends, including possible multiple campus locations that may vary by semester.
Commitment to maintaining confidentiality of student information.
Understanding of what it means to teach in a community college environment that serves often underprepared and underserved students.
Application Requirements
1. Upload the following documents to your application:
Unofficial/copy of transcripts
Updated Curriculum Vitae (C.V.) or Résumé
Cover letter explaining interest in the position
One representative teaching artifact, such as a syllabus, lesson plan, course activity, assessment, or other instructional material that reflects your approach to language teaching

6101 Highland Campus Dr., Bldg 3000, Suite 3.2224
Austin, TX 78752

Work is routinely performed in an office/classroom environment.
Subject to standing, walking, sitting, bending, reaching, kneeling, pushing, and pulling.
Ability to lift up to 10 pounds.
Work safely and follow safety rules. Report unsafe working conditions and behavior. Take reasonable and prudent actions to prevent others from engaging in unsafe practices.

The Department of Pediatrics at the Medical College of Georgia at Augusta University in Augusta, Georgia is actively seeking a full-time faculty member at the rank of Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, or Professor, to serve in the Division of Pediatric Critical Care Medicine. This position will provide clinical care in the Wellstar Golisano Children's Hospital of Georgia, in addition to education for pediatric fellows, residents, and medical students at the Medical College of Georgia at Augusta University. This position does not meet the requirements to be on a tenure track.
Responsibilities
Patient Care/Service - 87%
Become board certified in Pediatric Critical Care Medicine by year four (4)/maintain board certification.
Provide high-quality, comprehensive care in Pediatric Critical Care Medicine in an effort to improve quality, safety and patient experience.
Be clinically productive through the provision of clinical services at Wellstar MCG Health and the Wellstar Golisano Children's Hospital of Georgia.
Participate in on-call duties with other faculty. Nights, weekends, holidays.
Meet all metrics associated with Ongoing Professional Practice Evaluation (OPPE).
Become increasingly productive through the provision of clinical services in Pediatric Critical Care Medicine.
Meet and maintain wRVU productivity targets as set forth by the department chair and MCG Dean's Office through clinical services provided. Productivity targets are subject to change.
Support departmental efforts in promoting good professional relationships with AU physicians and physicians outside of AU (referring physicians in community, region and state).
Provide prompt feedback to referring physicians.
Teaching/Instruction - 13%
Provide education and training to residents, medical students and staff in pediatric critical care medicine which includes but is not limited to: clinical supervision, consultation and didactics.
Achieve and maintain teaching evaluation scores at or above the department mean.
Attend 50% or more weekly pediatric Grand Rounds presentations and monthly faculty meetings.

MD, DO or equivalent from an appropriately accredited institution and be board certified/eligible in Pediatric Critical Care Medicine. Must have or be able to obtain a State of Georgia Medical License, federal DEA, and be PALS/CPR certified.
Assistant Professor- Early level career as a faculty member with appropriate post graduate training.

Professor- Senior level career faculty member with at least five years at the rank of Associate Professor or comparable training, background, and experience.

The intended work commitment or full-time equivalent (FTE) for this position is 1.0 and considered full-time.

Associate Professor- Salary and compensation is commensurate with education, experience, and achievements. The salary is subject to availability of funds.
Professor- Salary and compensation is commensurate with education, experience, and achievements. The salary is subject to availability of funds.

https://www.augusta.edu/faculty-affairs/promotionandtenure.php

The MCG educational experience is anchored by the main campus in Augusta, with regional clinical campuses for third- and fourth-year students across the state, and two four-year campuses located in Athens (in partnership with the University of Georgia) and in Savannah (in partnership with Georgia Southern University). MCG's expanding partnerships with physicians and hospitals across Georgia currently provide more than 350 sites where students can experience the full spectrum of medicine, from complex care hospitals to small-town solo practices. The Department of Theatre at the University of Tennessee invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant/Associate Professor specializing in Acting (Stage & Screen). The successful candidate will be a accomplished acting teacher with extensive training in one or more recognized approaches to actor training and significant professional experience in theatre. The ideal candidate will have demonstrated excellence teaching acting at the university, conservatory, or equivalent professional-training level, with experience teaching both undergraduate and graduate actors. Experience in acting for the camera and/or performance in emerging media and/or filmmaking is required.
Duties include active participation in both graduate and undergraduate programs, service to the department, university, and profession, and creative activity and/or research. The faculty member will teach courses in acting, including advanced scene study and advanced scene study. Other classes may include acting for the camera, audition technique, performance across emerging media, on-camera technique for non-majors or other areas of expertise. The successful candidate will contribute to the continued development of a rigorous, sequential actor-training curriculum and mentor students preparing for professional careers across stage and screen.
The faculty member will contribute as a company member to the Clarence Brown Theatre, a LORT D professional theatre in residence, as an actor, director, or in other capacities based on their expertise. UTK is a land-grant university and values engaged forms of research/scholarship/creative activity, teaching, and service and considers evidence of these commitments in the records of applicants. The University is engaged in a next-level initiative aimed both at substantially elevating the University's national reputation for impactful research, scholarship, and creative activity and at assembling a roster of faculty committed to delivering one of the nation's best educational experiences for undergraduate and graduate students.
This position is part of a new constellation of interdisciplinary faculty positions in the UT College of Arts and Sciences emphasizing Envisioning and Narrating Emerging Futures (ENEF). We are seeking tenure-line faculty who will have overlapping interests that foster faculty development and collaboration. The goal is to bring together and invest in faculty across departments whose research, scholarship and creative work is linked through this initiative and to attract scholars who can bring different perspectives to an important issue or area.
Qualifications:
Minimum qualifications include an MFA or equivalent terminal degree, or at least five years of professional experience at the regional theatre level or above, and a demonstrated record of, or potential for, excellence in teaching. Candidates must also demonstrate professional experience in theatre and experience in acting for the camera, filmmaking, and/or performance in emerging media.
Candidates for appointment at the Assistant Professor level must demonstrate the potential to develop a sustained record of excellence in teaching and professional creative activity and/or research appropriate to a tenure-track faculty appointment.
Candidates for appointment at the Associate Professor level must demonstrate a substantial and sustained record of excellence in teaching and professional creative activity and/or research, along with a record of service and professional accomplishment commensurate with appointment at the rank of Associate Professor.
