jobs.title: Sponsored Programs Administrator - Open Rank
jobs.description:
Job Details
Overview
POSITION SUMMARY:
Under the general direction of the Associate Director or designee, the Sponsored Programs Administrator provides program support to principal investigators, administrators and staff regarding the timely completion of required documents for institutional approval of sponsored programs applications. The Sponsored Programs Administrator will also provide direction and assistance in all sponsored programs processes while adhering to sponsor, institutional, state, and federal guidelines.
This is an open-rank posting (there are 4 levels of Sponsored Programs Administrator) - candidates will be hired into the level commensurate with their experience.
Responsibilities
ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:
Sponsored Programs Administrator I:
Handle a standard project portfolio involving the life cycle of a grant from proposal to closeout
Review and verify all aspects of sponsor and institutional forms related to applications/proposals and amendments.
Assess award documents and recommend changes to ensure compliance with award terms and conditions, University policy, State and Federal laws and regulations
Negotiate incoming and execute outgoing sub-awards. Audit sub-recipient status and debarment review
Accountable for accurate demographic data, budget, and research compliance within electronic records
Collaborate with post-award staff in account set-up of proposals, new awards and modifications to track and report awards and sub-award activity
Disseminate changes in federal, state, and institutional policies, rules, and regulations and ensure organizational participation in compliance
Perform other duties as required.
Sponsored Programs Administrator II:
Duties noted above plus:
Handle a project portfolio of significant complexity for high profile departments with multiple component budgets involving the life cycle of a grant from proposal to closeout
Develop and present training materials and serve as a resource to both internal and external colleagues
Evaluate pre-award research administration internal procedures and recommend improvements
Assess award documents and recommend changes to the sponsor to ensure compliance with award terms and conditions, University policy, State and Federal laws and regulations
Accountable for accurate demographic data, budget, and research compliance in electronic records as the formal institutional system of record
Sr Sponsored Programs Administrator:
Duties noted above plus:
Handle a project portfolio of significant complexity for high profile departments with multiple component budgets and atypical projects involving the life cycle of a grant from proposal to closeout
Assist with the innovation, development, and implementation of special projects
Evaluate pre-award research administration procedures, recommend improvements, and participate in implementation of new practices
Prepare and participate in agency inspections and audits
Participate in the implementation of interdepartmental policies and procedures and systems for grants and contract administration
Responsible for secondary review of proposals ensuring accuracy with sponsor guidelines
Disseminate changes in federal, state, and institutional policies, rules, and regulations. Recommend methods to ensure organizational participation in compliance
Team Lead Sponsored Programs Administrator:
Duties noted above plus:
Leadership:
Responsible for leading a team of SPAs and managing their workloads.
Responsible for identifying, balancing, and tracking assignments and overall workload for the team; adjusting assignments as appropriate.
Monitor performance of team members and provide feedback to Associate Director for staff performance reviews. Identify weaknesses and strengths of team members and propose recommendations to Associate Director.
Support the professional development of team members through mentorship.
Participate in the development and implementation of initiatives to improve internal processes and maximize team performance.
Serve as a facilitator in the University’s Research Administration Program, develop educational materials and coordinate workshops and seminars on sponsored research topics for faculty members, department administrators and the research community at large, in conjunction with the Training Coordinator.
Assist (and lead) in the development, implementation, and integration of standard operating procedures and best practices.
Portfolio Management
Responsible for a project portfolio of significant complexity for high profile departments with multiple component budgets and atypical projects involving the life cycle of a grant from proposal to closeout
Serve as institutional representative with federal grants management and sponsoring agencies and officials
Negotiate, analyze and interpret award documentation and legally binding terms and conditions of grant and contract agreements, seeking additional legal or technical guidance when necessary.
Develop and present training materials for both internal and external constituents in research administration and research systems
Evaluate pre-award research administration procedures, recommend improvements, and participate in implementation of new policies, procedures and practices
Provide guidance and assistance to principal investigators, faculty and staff related to proposal development, budgeting, grant compliance and technical requirements
Assess, negotiate and interpret award documentation and legally binding terms and conditions of grant and contract agreements, seeking additional legal or technical guidance when necessary.
Prepare for, gather data and participate in sponsoring agency and federal audits, desk reviews and site visits
Contribute to the development and implementation of interdepartmental policies and procedures and systems for grants and contract administration
Provide leadership in the expansion of pre-award electronic systems, including evaluating upgrade and interface opportunities, testing and development of reporting
Mentor and provide direction to less seasoned personnel involved in the development of grant proposals, award modifications, technical systems and reporting
Responsible for final secondary review of proposals ensuring accuracy with sponsor guidelines and requirements
Review, verify and certify all aspects of sponsor and institutional data related to applications/proposals and amendments
Accountable for accurate research compliance, budget and administrative and demographic data within electronic records
Provide support to the innovation, development, and implementation of special projects
Interpret and disseminate changes in federal, state, and institutional policies, rules, and regulations. Recommend methods to ensure organizational participation in compliance
Qualifications
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:
Sponsored Programs Administrator I:
Bachelor's degree in Business, Research Administration, a related field, or equivalent experience
0-1 years of business-related experience
Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite
Excellent interpersonal, verbal and writing skills needed to present and communicate effectively with a diverse population of stakeholders.
Demonstrated time management and problem-solving skills with ability to organize and prioritize workload, identify problem areas and take action to meet deadlines.
Previous experience in an Institution of Higher Education working in Research Administration preferred.
Familiar with OMB Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, And Audit Requirements for Federal Awards preferred.
Familiarity with NIH Grants Policy Statement preferred.
Sponsored Programs Administrator II:
Requirements noted for SPA I plus:
1 - 3 years of business-related experience
Professional Certification in Research Administration (Certified Research Administrator; CRA/CPRA) preferred.
Sr Sponsored Programs Administrator:
Requirements noted for SPA I plus:
3-5 years of business-related experience
Demonstrated ability to coordinate a team workload and operationalize a high-risk sponsored research portfolio.
Professional Certification in Research Administration (Certified Research Administrator; CRA/CPRA) or Master’s Degree in Research Administration preferred.
Knowledge of OMB Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards preferred.
Extensive knowledge of NIH Grants Policy Statement preferred.
Team Lead Sponsored Programs Administrator:
Requirements noted above plus:
10 years of research administration or similar business-related experience
Knowledge of Huron Pre-Award System preferred.

jobs.title: Clinical Faculty
jobs.description:
Job Description:
Reporting to the Associate Dean for Clinical Education and this role will function as member of a collaborative teaching team in the development and delivery of a curriculum for osteopathic students in biomedical and clinical sciences to prepare them to advance to the graduate medical education portion of their professional development and education. Offering clinical insights combined with scientific information to develop in students the ability to effectively integrate medical decision making based on scientific outcomes and standards with the application of the art and science of medical care needed to provide patient centered medical care to advance the health and wellness of patients. We are seeking a professional with community-based practice experiences, including those training in areas of specialty including but not limited to, internal medicine, family medicine, geriatrics, pediatrics, women’s health, and general surgery.
SPECIFIC RESPONSIBILITIES:
Teaching (70%)
Utilization of diverse, novel and innovative teaching modalities in the delivery of patient and population based medical cases to MS I and MS II medical students
Case presentations
Small group discussions
Development of student assessments
Utilization of diverse, innovative, and evidence-based teaching modalities to enhance the delivery of health care education, including interprofessional education, professional identity formation, systems-based practice, and self-directed learning and discovery.
Assist in the development and delivery of didactic educational modules and activities for MS III and MS IV students
Collaborate with the clinical skills education team to develop and facilitate osteopathic clinical skills courses including;
Effective communication to facilitate accurate history taking and sensitive delivery of information (ICS);
Conduct of appropriately thorough physical examinations in a respectful, efficient, and skillful manner (PC);
Approach diagnoses with the ability to extract critical information, a thorough knowledge of disease presentations, and rational use of laboratory tests (MK);
Consider the impact of culture, age, gender, sexual orientation, risk perception, and personal values on patients needs (PC);
Identify, define, and understand ethical issues in medicine, in order to provide health care in a morally responsible manner (MK, Prof);
Develop the skills and knowledge required for effective and appropriate medical decision-making for the care of the patient;
Maintain skills for continuous education, and competence in obtaining and critically appraising new information from diverse sources (MK, PBLI);
Gain the ability to integrate research procedures and protocol into the clinical care of the patient;
Recognize the importance of their own well-being, and employ effective responses to challenges, stress, and fatigue (Prof, Prof Identity, SBP);
Be skilled in accurate, responsible, and respectful communication with other personnel involved in health care delivery (ICS, Prof, SBP);
Administration (10%)
Serve as course director or coordinator for educational offerings for students in either biomedical courses or clinical courses;
Assist with interviewing and hiring of department faculty as requested
Participate in the peer evaluation of department faculty
Promote scholarly activity and research by KHSU faculty and students with outcomes of public dissemination of scholarship
Collaborate with Assistant Dean of Outcomes & Assessment (ADOA) on all evaluations of all courses, laboratory, service and scholarly activities, ensuring formal after-action reporting, curriculum inventory and mapping at least annually (or as additionally requested)
Collaborate with COM leadership, ADOA on evaluation of osteopathic student readiness to advance to next level of curriculum in accord with KansasCOM policy
Service (10%)
Participate in student interviewing, mentorship, and career counseling
Foster a positive culture amongst the students, faculty, and KHSU-KansasCOM staff.
Serve on selected committees at the discretion of the Dean.
Assist the Senior Associate Dean for Academic Affairs in accreditation functions to include document creation, data collection, data entry, education of faculty on accreditation, and other accreditation-related functions at the discretion of the Dean.
Perform other related duties, as assigned
Research and Scholarly Activity (10%)
Promote student Research
Participate in scholarly activity with outcomes of public dissemination of scholarship
SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES:
N/A
QUALIFICATION(S):
A clinician educator with a track record of proven effective academic and administrative experience in Medical education.
A doctoral degree as a DO or MD degree with clinical or educational experience.
Current, unrestricted medical license
Eligible for professional malpractice coverage by the COM’s agent and agency
Current Board Certification in specialty
Good standing with all regulatory and governmental boards and agencies
Experience preferred applying teaching methods which might include team-based learning, ‘flipped classroom’, problem-based learning, distance learning, interactive large group presentation, audience response systems, curriculum delivery systems (e.g. Canvas), and proficiency in exam item (COMLEX and/or USMLE) writing
A substantial record of success as an educator, and of managing personnel.
Experience in publication/national presentations.
KEY COMPETENCIES:
Leadership abilities in influencing and shaping performance
Strong interpersonal skills and enthusiasm to contribute to organizational growth and development
Strong knowledge base in medical education assessment
Strong team & people management skills
Familiarity with AOA COCA requirements
Strong, effective, and diplomatic oral and written communication skills
Excellent public speaking skills
Excellent service skills relevant to supervisor, peers, direct reports, medical students, and faculty
Experience with medical school accreditation and reporting
The essential physical and mental requirements described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the job's essential functions. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

They are not to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required of personnel so classified. All personnel may be required to perform duties outside of their normal responsibilities from time to time, as needed.

KHSU-KansasCOM is committed to complying with all applicable laws regarding equal employment opportunities. KHSU-KansasCOM strives to create and maintain a work environment in which people are treated with dignity, decency, and respect. All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply.

Responsibilities
Florida State University College of Medicine (FSU MED) invites applications for the position of Director of Clinical Foundations within the Office of Medical Education.
This faculty leadership position provides strategic and operational leadership for the implementation, management, assessment, and continuous improvement of the first two years of the undergraduate medical education curriculum. The Director is responsible for supporting academic excellence, curricular integration, educational innovation, and the successful transition of medical students from the pre-clerkship curriculum to their clinical education.
This is a faculty position reporting to the Associate Dean for Undergraduate Medical Education, with responsibility for leading the implementation, management, assessment, and continuous improvement of the M1 and M2 curriculum. The Director works collaboratively with course directors, faculty, staff, and medical education leadership to promote academic excellence, curricular integration and innovation, and alignment with the College's educational program objectives, mission, and applicable Liaison Committee on Medical Education (LCME) accreditation standards.
The Director oversees the planning, delivery, and evaluation of the pre-clerkship curriculum, including curricular activities, educational assessments, course and examination processes, and student learning outcomes. The Director serves as Chair of the Year 1 & 2 Subcommittee of the Curriculum Committee and as an ex-officio member of the Year 3 & 4 Subcommittee and Curriculum Committee, providing leadership for course review, curricular evaluation, outcomes assessment, continuous quality improvement, and accreditation activities. Responsibilities also include oversight and analysis of National Board of Medical Examiners (NBME) examinations, the Comprehensive Basic Science Examination (CBSE), and USMLE (United States Medical Licensing Examination) Step 1 preparation and outcomes.
The Director will also oversee the College of Medicine Course Master Schedule with support from MED Administrative Services, as needed. The Director provides leadership and supervision for Office of Medical Education staff supporting the pre-clerkship curriculum and supports the development of course directors and faculty. Working with medical education leadership and other College programs, the Director contributes to strategic planning and integration of the four-year undergraduate medical education curriculum, supports students' successful transition to the clinical years, and represents the College on appropriate committees and initiatives related to medical education.
The successful candidate will be considered for appointment at the Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, or Professor level, with academic rank determined based on qualifications and experience and in accordance with College and University criteria.
Qualifications
Ph.D., M.D., D.O., M.D./Ph.D., or other appropriate terminal degree from an accredited university in a discipline relevant to medical education and the responsibilities of the position.
For physician candidates, board certification or board eligibility and eligibility for medical licensure in the State of Florida, as applicable.
Demonstrated record in undergraduate medical education, including experience with curriculum development, course leadership, educational assessment, program administration, or related medical education activities.
Demonstrated leadership experience within a school of medicine, academic health center, or comparable academic environment.
Strong organizational, interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills, with demonstrated ability to manage multiple complex academic initiatives and priorities.
Preferred Qualifications
Demonstrated commitment to academic excellence, professional development, collaboration, stakeholder engagement, and fostering an educational environment that supports the College of Medicine's mission.
Previous experience as a medical school course director, curriculum director, or in another significant leadership role within undergraduate medical education.
Demonstrated record of teaching, educational scholarship, scholarly activity, and/or service appropriate to the academic rank sought.
Knowledge of LCME accreditation standards and experience supporting accreditation, continuous quality improvement, or institutional medical education program evaluation.
Experience with educational program evaluation, assessment of learner outcomes, and continuous quality improvement.
Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with faculty, staff, students, academic leaders, and other stakeholders across organizational and disciplinary boundaries.
Experience with competency-based medical education, curricular mapping, educational program objectives, and horizontal and vertical curriculum integration.
Experience with NBME examinations, CBSE, USMLE Step 1 outcomes, or other medical student assessment programs.
Experience leading multidisciplinary teams and supervising professional staff in an academic or medical education environment.

General Description:
This is a 9-month, tenure-earning, Assistant Professor of Physical Chemistry position in the Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry, in the College of Arts and Sciences. We seek collaborative and innovative scientists and educators who will contribute to our growing research and teaching missions.
UNF is a Carnegie R2 institution, reflecting our commitment to high-impact research while maintaining our tradition of excellence in teaching. We are proud to support active faculty researchers and offer competitive startup packages. The department is also conducting a simultaneous search in other subdisciplines of chemistry; scientists working at the interface of these areas are encouraged to apply to the position most aligned with their teaching strengths.

Research Expectations: Establish a research program, focusing on physical chemistry related topics, that actively involves undergraduate students and/or master’s students. Job Description
The College of Business Administration (COBA) at Texas A&M University-Central Texas welcomes highly qualified applicants to fill an immediate need for an Assistant Professor in Management / Leadership starting in Fall 2027. This is a tenure-track faculty position. Application reviews will begin immediately. We are looking for a dynamic and collegial teacher-scholar with a passion for teaching and a multi-faceted track record of excellence both within and beyond the classroom. This faculty member would be expected to teach leadership-related courses at a variety of levels and in a variety of modalities. Assigned courses will include undergraduate leadership and one or more of the following graduate courses: organization development and change (masters), cross-sector partnerships (masters), global leadership theory and practice (masters), leadership formation and development (masters), and any one of the in-development doctoral courses that would support our DBA leadership emphasis area (still pending final SACSCOC approval). Other courses may also be available on a limited basis depending on applicant qualifications and interest.
While this position is being advertised at the rank of Assistant Professor, we warmly welcome applications from candidates with distinguished records and broader experience. Depending on institutional needs and individual qualifications, consideration may be given for credit toward years of service and/or appointment at the rank of Associate Professor. Please note that tenure upon hire is possible but atypical and is determined on a case-by-case basis in consultation with the Provost.
About Texas A&M University – Central Texas
Established as an independent member of the Texas A&M University System in 2009, A&M-Central Texas is a friendly and dynamic regional teaching institution that prides itself on excellence in instruction, but also embraces a growing emphasis on research. A&M-Central Texas is truly unique in that it is an upper- and masters-level institution, offering only junior- and senior-level coursework needed to successfully complete baccalaureate degrees and all coursework leading to the completion of master’s degrees. As such, A&M-Central Texas maintains active partnerships with the major community colleges within the Austin and Central Texas region, as well with Fort Hood, a premier outpost of the U.S. Army and one of the largest military installations in the world. Our multifaceted student demographic includes a significant proportion of first-generation college students, non-traditional learners, and military-affiliated personnel.
The College of Business Administration is accredited by AACSB, and we are eager to have dynamic and collegial new faculty members partner with us in pursuit of our major strategic initiatives, of which there are many on the near horizon (most notably, a DBA program anticipated to launch Fall 2027 pending SACSCOC final approval). This is an exciting time of rapid change within the College that affords new faculty members many opportunities to make an immediate, significant, and lasting impact.
A&M-Central Texas is located on the southern edge of Killeen, TX, a city of approximately 150,000 located about halfway between Austin and Waco—about 60 miles either way. Our faculty members enjoy a wide variety of living options by virtue of the culture in the area—from quiet and rural to bustling and cosmopolitan. It is an easy drive to great art, food, shopping, and night life as well as to hunting, fishing, hiking, and camping for those who prefer the outdoors. Central Texas is also a great place for families, with many options for schooling, worship, civic engagement, and recreation. It also has light traffic and a reasonable cost of living. The major metropolitan areas of Houston, Dallas-Fort Worth, and San Antonio are all within a 3-hour radius of Killeen.
Responsibilities
The candidate will be expected to provide quality, engaging instruction for typically three courses per long term in a variety of course delivery formats (face-to-face, online, or hybrid), with fully online being the most in-demand option at present. Summer teaching opportunities may also available as dictated by student demand and department needs.
Some scholarly contributions are also required. The candidate is expected have sufficient scholarly and/or professional activities to have “scholarly academic” status upon arrival per AACSB faculty classifications, and to have a healthy pipeline of works in progress, where health is measured more by viability and impact than by volume. Scholarship is but one category of currency and impact with which faculty may engage: others include maintaining a recognized professional certification, presenting at academic conferences, engaging in consulting or other industry-related activities, and completing other relevant professional training and development activities. Professional development funds are available to support all of these endeavors, and faculty within the College frequently collaborate on research projects together.
In regard to service, faculty are expected to support the department, college, and university with committee work, but first-year faculty are exempt from this. In addition, faculty are expected to have some sort of service to their profession and/or to the community, but again, service contribution impact and quality are more important than the number of activities engaged in. Faculty (in consultation with the department chair) generally have a lot of discretion in determining how best they can add value through their various service activities.
A Presidential Proclamation issued on September 19, 2025, imposes a $100,000 fee on all new H‑1B petitions filed after September 21, 2025, and Texas A&M University–Central Texas will not pay this fee. Additionally, a moratorium issued by Governor Abbott on January 27, 2026, restricts the filing of new H‑1B petitions unless approved by the Texas Workforce Commission. Accordingly, if you will now or in the future require sponsorship for employment visa status this moratorium may affect our ability to employ you should you be selected as the final candidate. Applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer.
Minimum Qualifications:
To be eligible to apply for this position, candidates should:
Possess a terminal degree (doctorate) in management / leadership or a closely-related discipline from a regionally accredited university
Be eligible for the AACSB “scholarly academic” faculty classification
Have a documented track record of successfully teaching leadership courses, including in fully online formats
Preferred Qualifications:
The ideal candidate for this position would also possess:
At least three (3) years of full-time collegiate teaching experience
Experience working with doctoral students
Industry experience, including ongoing connections
Proficiency in creating original, dynamic, and engaging online course instructional materials
Great administrative, organizational, and interpersonal skills to support successful instruction to a largely non-traditional, first-generation, and military-affiliated student body
Salary: Commensurate
Hours: Faculty hours; M-F; hours may vary by assignment and course modality.
To Apply:
Please apply directly on our Texas A&M University-Central Texas Job Site. Applicants are required to submit a cover letter, curriculum vitae (CV), and either the contact information for three professional references or three letters of recommendation. Additional materials, such as a teaching philosophy statement and transcripts, are optional but strongly encouraged.
All positions are security-sensitive. Applicants are subject to a criminal history investigation, and employment is contingent upon the institution’s verification of credentials and/or other information required by the institution’s procedures, including the completion of the criminal history check.
Equal Opportunity/Veterans/Disability Employer.

Job Title:Assistant Professor - Empire and Environment in Latin America
Department:Arts and Sciences | Spanish and Portuguese
Transnational World Language Studies
Empire and Environment in the Spanish and Portuguese-Speaking Worlds
Rank: Tenure-Track Assistant Professor
Department of Spanish and Portuguese
College of Arts and Sciences
Position Overview
The Department of Spanish and Portuguese (SPPO) at The Ohio State University invites applications for a Tenure-Track Assistant Professor position in Transnational World Language Studies in the area of Empire and Environment in the Spanish and/or Portuguese-Speaking areas of Latin America and the Caribbean beginning August 15, 2027. We aim to hire a dynamic scholar who will contribute to the vibrant and collegial intellectual communities of our department by engaging with interdisciplinary research, innovative teaching, program development, community engagement, and service.
This is one of three tenure-track hires in Transnational World Language Studies, the other two being in the departments of East Asian Languages and Literatures and Slavic and East Europeans Languages and Cultures. We are also conducting searches for three Postdoctoral Scholar to Tenure-Track Assistant Professor positions in Humanities-based Interdisciplinary World Languages and Cultures in the departments of French and Italian, Germanic Languages and Literatures, and Near Eastern and South Asian Languages and Cultures.
In keeping with the department’s commitment to interdisciplinarity, we are especially interested in scholars who demonstrate an interdisciplinary research profile that examines the historical and contemporary relationships among empire, environment, extraction, race, indigeneity, migration, and ecological justice across the Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking world. We seek scholars whose research approaches environmental questions through the lenses of, for example, cultural studies, literary studies, Indigenous studies, Latinx studies, decolonial studies, critical geography, environmental humanities, media studies, visual culture, or public humanities. Areas of specialization may include colonial ecologies; extractivism and resource frontiers; environmental injustices; Indigenous and Black Atlantic environmental knowledge; climate migration; food systems; water politics; energy humanities; environmental media; or the historic and cultural dimensions of planetary crisis.
The successful candidate will build on SPPO's existing strengths in Latin American, Latinx, Brazilian, Andean, Iberian, and community-engaged scholarship and will contribute to strengthening connections across world languages while helping to cultivate a more unified intellectual identity around themes of global relevance.
Partial startup for the Transnational World Language Studies tenure-track positions is funded by the Mellon Foundation grant “Global Fluency, Career Agility: Transforming World Languages at Ohio State.” The new hires will participate in the activities within the Department, create new courses, and have designated faculty mentors who are engaged in research on topics relating to transnational world language education, global fluency and intercultural competence, and their area of specialization.
Performance Objectives
Develop and maintain an active, nationally and internationally recognized research agenda on empire, environment, and transnational cultural dynamics in the Spanish- and/or Portuguese-speaking world.
Teach and mentor undergraduate and graduate students in Spanish and/or Portuguese while contributing to curriculum development in areas such as environmental humanities, climate justice, coloniality, ecology, and transnational cultural studies.
Advance the Mellon-funded Transforming World Languages at OSU initiative by collaborating with faculty and staff across disciplines, contributing to innovative programming, and creating new courses that strengthen students’ global fluency and intercultural competence.
Foster connections across languages, disciplines, and communities through collaborative research, public-facing scholarship, and/or community-engaged activities.
Participate in departmental service.
Education and Experience Qualifications
Required:
PhD in Spanish, Portuguese, Latin American Cultural Studies, or related field required at time of appointment which is August 15, 2027. ABDs welcome to apply.
Native or near-native fluency in Spanish and/or Portuguese
Candidates must demonstrate achievement or strong promise of scholarly success.
Research agenda that connects multiple methods and/or theoretical approaches to the study of empire and environment in the Americas.
Desired:
Experience and/or commitment to public-facing or community engaged scholarship, teaching and/or service.
Demonstrated ability to contribute to and strengthen transdisciplinary and translingual collaborations in environmental humanities scholarship.
Knowledge of French, Haitian Kreyòl/Creole, and/or Francophone Caribbean contexts, particularly in dialogue with Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking worlds.
Ohio State provides access to a depth and breadth of opportunities and resources. Starting your first day, Ohio State offers you a comprehensive benefits package.
How to Apply
To be considered, please submit your application via Workday. https://osu.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/OSUCareers/job/Columbus-Campus/Assistant-Professor---Empire-and-Environment-in-Latin-America_R160266
Application period closes November 9, 2026. Inquiries may be directed to Laura Podalsky, podalsky.1@osu.edu.
You will be presented with the opportunity to attach up to FIVE documents in the Application Documents section. Please include the following:
Attachment 1: Cover Letter: 1-2 page letter, which should include a brief summary of your academic background and why you are interested in this opportunity.
Attachment 2: CV (Curriculum Vitae): Detailed overview of your scholarly experience, including your research experience, teaching and mentoring experience, service, engagement, and publications.
Attachment 3: Research Statement: Summary of your past research accomplishments, current work/research, and proposal for your future research plan as a faculty member.
Attachment 4: Teaching Statement: A statement of your approaches, experience and philosophy regarding your teaching, learning, and mentoring.
Attachment 5: A writing sample.
Candidates selected to move forward in the process will be asked to provide three letters of reference.
Application period closes November 9, 2026

Job Title:Assistant Professor - Musicology
Department:Arts and Sciences | Music
Position Overview
The Music Theory and Musicology Area in the School of Music at The Ohio State University is searching for a tenure-track Assistant Professor in musicology and/or ethnomusicology. Areas and topics of specialization are open, but the successful candidate will have a scholarship and teaching profile that complements and expands existing faculty expertise in our Area, which includes faculty members in both musicology and music theory. We are especially interested in candidates whose work advances fine-grained analysis of music and sound within communities of practice.
The Music Theory and Musicology Area prides itself on constructive collaboration across the disciplines of musicology, ethnomusicology, and music theory. The successful candidate should evidence interest in and engagement with music studies, broadly defined, in terms of scholarly output, curriculum development, public outreach, and student recruitment. Finally, the candidate will teach within and further develop musicology’s core undergraduate and graduate curricula. Undergraduate core courses include European art music traditions, African American musical traditions, musical citizenship (the intersection of music, politics, and civics globally), and global music histories. Graduate courses include disciplinary surveys (in “musicology” and “ethnomusicology”), methodological training (historical and ethnographic), and specialized seminars.
Performance Objectives
The successful candidate will evidence:
A scholarship and teaching profile that complements and expands existing faculty expertise in musicology and music theory at in the School of Music and related units at Ohio State.
Scholarship that advances fine-grained analysis of music and sound within communities of practice.
A scholarship, teaching, and service profile that demonstrates interest in and engagement with music studies, broadly writ (including musicology, ethnomusicology, and music theory), in terms of scholarly output, curriculum development, public outreach, and student recruitment.
A teaching profile that demonstrates the ability and desire to teach within and further develop the Musicology Area’s core undergraduate and graduate curricula in the School of Music.
Education and Experience Requirements
Required:
Ph.D. in Musicology, Ethnomusicology, or a comparable and relevant humanistic discipline.
Earned doctorate by the time of appointment is required.
ABD candidates with an expected graduation date prior to August 15, 2027, will be considered.
Desired:
Scholarship that complements and expands existing expertise in musicology and music theory.
Demonstrated engagement with interdisciplinary music studies.
Experience in curriculum development, public outreach, and student recruitment.

jobs.description:
Job Details
Assistant or Associate Professor in City and Regional Planning
Location:
Philadelphia, PA
Open Date:
Oct 5, 2026
Description:
The Department of City & Regional Planning at the Stuart Weitzman School of Design at the University of Pennsylvania seeks an outstanding scholar for a full-time, tenure-track position with responsibilities for teaching, research, and service. Candidates at the assistant and associate professor levels will be considered for the position.
We seek an exceptional scholar and educator whose research and practice contribute to our department in one or more of the following areas: Urban and Regional Economics; Public Finance; Real Estate and Housing Economics and/or Finance; Housing Planning and/or Policy; and Land Use Planning. The successful candidate will have: 1) a proven track record of scholarly research in one or more of these areas; 2) connections to the broader field of city and regional planning; 3) the ability to teach existing and new courses relevant to the core or concentrations in their area of urban planning specialty; 4) the ability and desire to lead a departmental concentration, certificate program, and/or perform similar administrative duties; 5) leadership experience or potential, including the ability to collaborate and make connections across departments/programs/schools/centers.
The Weitzman School of Design includes City and Regional Planning, Architecture, Fine Arts, Historic Preservation, and Landscape Architecture. The Department of City and Regional Planning offers a two-year Master of City Planning degree, a one-year Master of Urban Spatial Analytics, and a PhD. We welcome the new faculty member to participate in the various research centers located at the School and University.
Qualifications:
Minimum qualifications: a PhD in Urban Planning or a related field by the start of employment.
Application Instructions:
Applicants should submit a statement of interest that describes their relevant experience, a research statement outlining their agenda for research and scholarship, a curriculum vitae, two recent publications or writing samples, a teaching statement, and the names and contact information for three references who will be contacted at a later date. Please keep the statement of interest under 500 words and the research and teaching statements under 1,000 words each.
Review of applications will begin on November 1, 2026 and will continue until the position is filled. The position will begin on July 1, 2027, or on a mutually agreed date thereafter.
Applications should be addressed to the Search Committee, Department of City & Regional Planning. Questions should be directed to Kate Daniel, Department Coordinator, City & Regional Planning, at katf@design.upenn.edu.

The Department of Speech, Language and Hearing Sciences at Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center (TTUHSC) invites applications for a 12-month, non-tenure track position for the Doctor of Audiology program. Candidates must have expertise and qualifications in assessing and treating disorders of hearing and balance. This position will require the individual to provide and supervise clinical services for patients in the TTUHSC Speech, Language and Hearing Clinic and possibly other settings (e.g., schools) in Lubbock, Texas. Rank of Assistant Professor/Associate Professor/Professor and applicable salary are dependent upon candidate's qualifications and experience.
Major/Essential Functions
Supervise and mentor graduate student clinicians in various settings.
Provide clinical services to patients in various settings.
Provide service to the department, university and profession.
Participate in clinical simulations.
Provide clinically relevant didactic instruction.
Participate in professional development.
Required Qualifications
Au.D. degree or higher in Audiology.
Evidence of at least three (3) years of clinical practice.
ASHA certification (CCC-A).
State of Texas licensure or eligibility to obtain Texas licensure.
Preferred Qualifications
Recent and consistent experience supervising graduate student clinicians in direct clinical service within the last three years.
At least 5 years of current, direct audiology service provision to clients, including adult and pediatric diagnostics.
Teaching experience.
Experience with vestibular testing.

Cover Letter, Resume / CV

Assistant Professor in Violin
Job No: 541607
Work Type: Full Time
Location: Main Campus (Gainesville, FL)
Categories: Education/Training/Instructional Design, Humanities
Department: 13030100 - COTA-MUSIC-DIRECTOR
Job Description
Classification Title:
AST PROF
Classification Minimum Requirements
Candidates for this rank must hold the highest degree appropriate to their field or possess equivalent qualifications based on professional experience. A candidate shall be expected to demonstrate successful experience pertinent to the position they are being recommended and have demonstrated qualities relevant to the goals of the academic unit in which they will be employed.
Job Description:
The University of Florida School of Music in the College of the Arts invites applications for a full-time, 9-month Assistant Professor of Violin. We seek an accomplished performer and pedagogue who will contribute to the continued success and growth of our BM, BA, MM, and DMA programs in violin. The successful candidate will recruit and teach a full studio of applied violin students. Other responsibilities could include teaching violin pedagogy, violin literature, or chamber music.
The University of Florida College of the Arts intends to be a transformative community, responding to and generating paradigmatic shifts in the arts and beyond. As artists and scholars, we embrace the complexity of our evolving human experience and seek to empower our students and faculty to shape that experience fearlessly through critical study, creative practice, and provocation. We seek a colleague who identifies as a change-maker. We seek a colleague who will position emerging artists and researchers as catalysts for justice on local and global levels.
The University of Florida is an equal opportunity institution.
This position is covered by the United Faculty of Florida Contract. You can view this employment union contract here https://admin.hr.ufl.edu/compliance/employee-relations-and-ethics/union-negotiations/united-faculty-of-florida-contract/.
Responsibilities
Recruit, maintain, and teach a successful full violin studio of undergraduate and graduate level students, including weekly private instruction of applied violin curriculum, studio class, and participation in area recitals/juries. (Additional responsibilities may include coaching chamber and/or teaching courses in the candidate's area(s) of expertise.)
Maintain professional activities at the regional and national level as a performing artist consistent with the expectation of tenure and promotion
Service to the String area, School of Music, University, and the profession as consistent with expectation of tenure and promotion
SCHOOL OF MUSIC: Organized within the College of the Arts, the School of Music plays an important role in the academic and cultural life of the University, the College's Creative Campus initiative and the community. The School has 40 full-time and nine adjunct faculty, serving some 200 graduate and 200 undergraduate music majors. Degree programs include B.S., B.A., B.M., M.M., D.M.A., and the Ph.D. in music education, composition, ethnomusicology, and historical musicology. Program emphases include performance, music education, theory, composition, music history and literature, ethnomusicology, conducting, and sacred music. The School of Music is also home to the UF Bands program, which includes “The Pride of the Sunshine” Gator Marching Band. School of Music facilities include the School of Music Building and Steinbrenner Band Hall, among others. The University of Florida is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges and is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music. jobs.description:
Salary Range or Pay Grade
Assistant Professor: $108,000-$115,000, Associate Professor: $115,000-$135,000
Field of Specialization
Any Medium/Discipline
The Visual Arts Program in the School of the Arts at Columbia University invites applications for a position at the rank of Assistant Professor/Associate Professor of Visual Arts (tenure-track) specializing in any medium or discipline, effective July 1, 2027.
The successful candidate will be innovative and passionate, and have a significant exhibition record and advanced technical skills grounded in the history of their respective medium(s) and possess strong leadership qualities. Appointees must have a thorough knowledge of contemporary art discourse and a demonstrated ability to mentor and engage critically with our diverse student population regardless of medium. A minimum of three years teaching experience at both the undergraduate and graduate level, full-time or adjunct, strongly preferred.
Columbia’s Visual Arts Program is interdisciplinary and fosters rich creative work at both the graduate (MFA in Visual Arts) and undergraduate (BA with Visual Arts major) levels in the areas of Moving Image, Painting, Photography, Printmaking, Sculpture, and Expanded practice. The Visual Arts Program, in collaboration with the Department of Music and the Computer Music Center, also offers a course of study in the discipline of Sound Art which leads to an MFA in Visual Arts. The Program offers undergraduate studio classes in all areas mentioned, enrolling over 700 registrations each school year, and offers a major in Visual Arts leading to a BA awarded by Columbia College or the School of General Studies.
The appointee will teach graduate students across all mediums as well as undergraduate studio courses, advise students at both the graduate and undergraduate levels, lead Grad Studio or Group Critiques, oversee MFA theses, and mentor postgraduate careers. The full-time teaching load consists of four classes each school year, and Independent Study at faculty’s discretion. Participation is required in rotating service and leadership roles, including committee work in collaboration with other programs in the School. A fully engaged presence on campus is expected along with a willingness to collaborate with peers to help shape the future of the Visual Arts Program and the School of Arts at both the graduate and undergraduate levels.
Candidates for Assistant Professor or Associate Professor (tenure-track position) must have demonstrated and shown promise of the capacity for creative work and the accompanying pedagogy qualifying them for future nomination to tenure.
Rank and salary commensurate with experience.
Review of applications will begin January 10th, 2027 and continue until the position is filled.
Qualifications
Minimum degree required: BA or equivalent
Preferred degree: MA or MFA strongly preferred
Teaching experience: Minimum of three years teaching at the undergraduate and graduate level strongly preferred.

All applications must be made through Columbia University’s Academic Search and Recruiting (ASR) system. Please upload the following required materials: cover letter, CV, teaching philosophy, contact information for three referees, and samples of your work, provided through a word or PDF document with a live URL link to a website with a minimum of 15 work sample images (No slideshows or PowerPoints accepted).

jobs.description:
Assistant Professor of Human Development and Family Studies
with a specialization in Marriage and Family Therapy
The Department of Human Development and Family Studies, College of Human Environmental Sciences at The University of Alabama, seeks applicants for a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Human Development and Family Studies with a specialization in Marriage and Family Therapy. The position is for a core faculty member in the COAMFTE-accredited master’s Marriage and Family Therapy Program. We place priority on the selection of an applicant with an active research agenda, as demonstrated by a strong record of peer-reviewed research publications and/or involvement in externally funded research. The successful candidate will be expected to develop a robust scholarly research program with external support; teach graduate courses in the marriage and family therapy program; provide clinical supervision for students in the marriage and family therapy program; mentor undergraduate and graduate students; and engage in professional service at the campus, community, state, and/or national level.
Minimum Qualifications
A doctorate in Marriage and Family Therapy, Couple and Family Therapy, or a related field with an emphasis in Marriage and Family Therapy; ABD applicants will be considered provided the doctorate is completed by the August 16, 2027 start date.
Evidence of an active research agenda, including peer-reviewed publications and/or presentations and involvement in grant submissions or externally funded research projects;
Teaching experience in higher education;
Clinical supervision experience; and
Strong interpersonal skills, including effective oral and written communication skills.
Preferred qualifications: Degree from a COAMFTE-accredited Program, Active or license-eligible status in Marriage and Family Therapy and AAMFT Approved Supervisor or AAMFT Supervisor Candidate designation.
Instructions and Required Materials for Application
Complete application on-line at https://facultyjobs.ua.edu
Your application should include:
Application Letter (Cover Letter)
Curriculum Vitae
Research Statement
Teaching Statement
Clinical Supervision Statement
List of Professional References
Review of candidates will begin immediately with a posting close date of 11/1/2026.
Applicants with questions should contact Dr. Blake Berryhill at mbberryhill@ua.edu.
About the College
At the College of Human Environmental Sciences, we empower students to bring about positive change in the world. Our faculty conduct advanced research, provide outreach and prepare a new generation of professionals with a shared goal of improving lives.
CHES brings together a wide range of disciplines which focus on the interaction between individuals, families and the environment. Five distinct departments cover a multitude of human science programs that help individuals across the lifespan improve their mental, physical and financial well-being. We touch people’s lives in the home, at school, in the workplace, at the dinner table, on the athletic field, and in a myriad of other arenas.
About the University
The University of Alabama is located in Tuscaloosa, Alabama, named one of Travel + Leisure’s 25 Best College Towns and Cities in the U.S. As one of the nation’s premier universities, UA offers bachelor’s, master's and doctoral degrees in nearly 200 fields of study. With more than 1,400 acres of tree-lined academic core campus and over 300 state-of-the art facilities, UA has been ranked among the most beautiful and most impressive college campuses in the South, in the state of Alabama and in the nation.
In Fall 2023, the Capstone set a new enrollment record with more than 39,000 students, including more than 8,200 in the freshman class. The current enrollment includes students from every county in Alabama, every state in the nation and 92 countries around the world. More than 1,100 National Merit Scholars are currently enrolled, making UA one of the largest enrolling institutions of the scholars in the country.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor, Criminal Justice
jobs.description:
Job Details
Job Summary
This is a nine-month, tenure-track faculty appointment requiring regular on-campus presence to fulfill teaching, research, advising, service, and departmental responsibilities. The position encourages active engagement in scholarly research, externally funded projects, proposal development, grant management, and community or agency partnerships.
Special Note: We are unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position. Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States without the need for sponsorship now or in the future.
Essential Job Functions
Teaching:
The successful candidate will develop and teach undergraduate and graduate courses in Criminal Justice, with particular emphasis on homeland security and emergency management.
Teaching responsibilities may also include courses in criminal justice policy, security studies, law enforcement, corrections, cybersecurity, research methods, or other areas consistent with the candidate’s expertise and departmental needs.
The candidate will be expected to provide high-quality instruction, academic advising, and mentorship to students in both face-to-face and online learning environments.
The Department values innovative, student-centered teaching practices that promote critical thinking, professional development, applied learning, and academic success.
Service:
The successful candidate will contribute to the service needs of the Department, College, University, and profession. Service responsibilities may include committee work, curriculum development, assessment and accreditation-related activities, student recruitment and retention, community engagement, professional service, and participation in academic governance.
The candidate will also be expected to support departmental outreach efforts and represent the Department of Criminal Justice at university, community, and professional events.
Research:
The successful candidate will be expected to establish and maintain an active research agenda in criminal justice, homeland security, emergency management, security studies, or a closely related area.
Expectations include publishing in peer-reviewed scholarly outlets, presenting research at professional conferences, pursuing internally and/or externally funded research opportunities, and contributing to the advancement of knowledge in the field.
The Department especially welcomes candidates whose research has applied, interdisciplinary, policy-relevant, or community-engaged dimensions. Opportunities may exist to collaborate with faculty across disciplines and to build partnerships with local, state, federal, and community-based agencies.
Minimum and Desired Qualifications
Minimum Qualifications:
An earned Ph.D. in Criminal Justice, Criminology, Sociology, Public Administration, Homeland Security, Emergency Management, Security Studies, or a closely related field by the time of appointment.
Candidates currently holding the rank of Associate Professor who seek appointments at the same rank must have a record of teaching, scholarship, and service that meets the Lamar University Department of Criminal Justice’s standards for tenure and promotion to Associate Professor.
A demonstrated academic focus or research/teaching expertise in homeland security, emergency management, security studies, or a closely related area.
Demonstrated potential for effective teaching, advising, and mentoring of undergraduate and graduate students.
Evidence of scholarly productivity or strong potential for an active research agenda.
Excellent oral and written communication skills.
Demonstrated potential for interdisciplinary teaching, research, applied collaboration, or professional engagement.
Desired Qualifications:
Experience teaching in face-to-face and/or online environments.
Ability to teach courses in homeland security, emergency management, security studies, criminal justice policy, cybersecurity, or related areas.
Ability to teach and support undergraduate and graduate Criminal Justice programs.
Experience mentoring students.
Evidence of scholarly activity, including publications, research, or grant development.
Experience integrating technology into teaching, research, or practice.
Experience working with criminal justice, public safety, homeland security, emergency management, or community organizations.
Ability to support interdisciplinary research and partnerships.
Supplemental Information
Key Competencies:
Ability to teach undergraduate and graduate Criminal Justice courses.
Expertise in homeland security, emergency management, security studies, or arelated field.
Commitment to student learning, mentoring and advising.
Potential for a productive research agenda and scholarly activity.
Strong oral and written communication skills
Ability to collaborate with colleagues, students, practitioners, and communitypartners.
Commitment to service, curriculum development, and program growth.
Ability to work effectively in an interdisciplinary academic environment.
Physical Requirements: Ability to perform the essential functions of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation, including occasional lifting of up to 25 pounds and movement between classrooms, laboratories, offices, and field locations.
Job Conditions: Work is primarily performed in classroom, office, online instructional, and meeting settings, with occasional community, professional, or field-based activities. The position may involve evening, weekend, or travel commitments related to teaching, research, student support, recruitment, outreach, professional conferences, or service activities.
Pay Range: Commensurate
Required Documents: These documents are required for your application to be considered complete.
Cover Letter
Curriculum Vita
Statement of teaching philosophy
Research statement
Contact information for three professional references
Unofficial graduate transcripts
Three Recommendation Letters

Applicants are required to sign an authorization for release of prior employment records to Lamar University. We will only contact prior employers and off-list references for finalists.

Home to more than 18,000 students, Lamar University is among the fastest growing Texas colleges and universities. LU is a member of The Texas State University System, which is the first higher education system of Texas and maintains the lowest average tuition and fees of any university system in Texas. With more than 120-degree options and a community that cares, Lamar students are always proud to be Cardinals. jobs.description:
Job Details
Job Summary
The Assistant Professor of Scenic and Lighting Design is a full-time faculty position within the Department of Theatre & Dance, responsible for teaching undergraduate courses, supporting departmental productions, and contributing to the academic and artistic mission of the university. This position integrates classroom instruction with hands-on production work, emphasizing student mentorship, collaboration, and safe technical practices. The role requires close coordination with faculty, staff, and the Technical Director to support scenic, lighting, and props design areas, manage production-related resources, and ensure high-quality educational and performance outcomes. In addition to teaching and production responsibilities, the position includes service and administrative support activities consistent with faculty expectations at a state-supported institution.
Special Note: We are unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position. Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States without the need for sponsorship now or in the future.
Essential Job Functions
Teaching and Instruction:
Teaches a range of undergraduate courses in theatre design and production, including but not limited to Stagecraft, Production, Scenic Design, Lighting Design, Introduction to Design, and Theatre Appreciation. Develops course syllabi, instructional materials, and assessments; evaluates student performance; maintains office hours; and supports student learning outcomes consistent with departmental and university standards.
Scenic and Lighting Design & Production Support:
Serves as scenic and/or lighting designer for Department of Theatre & Dance productions or supervises guest artists and student designers for the departmental season, which includes four plays, two dance concerts, and additional student-produced works. Mentors students through all phases of the design and production process and supports experiential learning in production-based courses.
Technical Coordination, Safety, and Facilities Support:
Coordinates with the Technical Director in managing the scene shop and overseeing the props design area within production classes. Ensures proper use, maintenance, and replacement of tools and equipment; enforces safety standards and best practices in all technical and production activities; and promotes a safe learning and working environment for students and staff.
Budgeting and Administrative Support:
Assists in preparing and managing production budgets for departmental shows. Completes required paperwork including purchase requisitions, time sheets, and related documentation. Helps coordinate and supervise production strikes and load-outs.
Service, Collaboration, and Student Engagement:
Demonstrates a willingness and ability to work with the undergraduate student population. Participates in departmental activities, meetings, and service as assigned. Collaborates effectively with faculty, staff, and students to support the mission and goals of the Department of Theatre & Dance and the university.
Minimum and Desired Qualifications
Minimum Qualifications:
Master of Fine Arts (M.F.A.) in Theatrical Design or a closely related field.
Demonstrated proficiency in scenic and lighting design.
Knowledge of current trends, tools, technologies, and safety standards in scenic and lighting design.
Ability to mentor, supervise, and instruct undergraduate students in classroom and production-based settings.
Ability to collaborate effectively with faculty, staff, students, and guest artists.
Desired Qualifications:
At least three (3) years of teaching experience at the college or university level.
Professional experience in scenic and/or lighting design.
Experience working within an academic theatre production environment.
Supplemental Information
Key Competencies:
Strong instructional, mentoring, and student engagement skills.
Working knowledge of scenic and lighting technologies, tools, and equipment.
Effective written, oral, and interpersonal communication skills.
Ability to manage multiple productions, priorities, and deadlines simultaneously.
Commitment to excellence and working with the undergraduate student population.
Physical Requirements:
Ability to stand, walk, and move for extended periods.
Ability to lift, carry, push, or pull materials and equipment associated with theatrical productions.
Ability to safely use tools, ladders, lifts, and technical equipment common to theatre and scene shop environments.

Position Description:
The Department of Curriculum and Instruction at Texas State University invites applications for one full-time, nine-month faculty position in Special Education. The position may be filled at the rank of tenure-track Assistant Professor or Associate Professor with tenure, or Professor with tenure beginning fall 2027.
We seek a scholar with a clearly identifiable program of research focused on Special Education and improving educational opportunities and outcomes for individuals with disabilities. The successful candidate should be able to contribute to teaching across multiple Special Education program areas (i.e., Special Education generalist). Candidates from all areas of Special Education are encouraged to apply.
The successful candidate will contribute to the undergraduate and graduate Special Education programs and to the preparation of Special Education teachers and other professionals who serve individuals with disabilities. The candidate will teach courses at the undergraduate and graduate level, maintain an active program of research, advise and mentor students, contribute to program development, and provide service and leadership within the program, department, university, and profession. Courses are offered on campus, hybrid, and online (synchronous and asynchronous) during the day and in the evening.
Appointment at the Associate Professor or Professor rank will require meeting Texas State University and Department of Curriculum and Instruction standards for appointment with tenure.
RESPONSIBILITIESKey responsibilities include:
Teaching undergraduate and graduate Special Education courses, including courses supporting teacher preparation and certification, across in-person, hybrid, and online modalities; developing or revising courses as program needs arise.
Supervising teacher candidates in field-based or clinical teaching experiences.
Maintaining an active and focused program of research that results in peer-reviewed publications and professional presentations.
Seeking external funding to support research and/or personnel-preparation activities, as appropriate.
Advising and mentoring undergraduate and graduate students.
Contributing to the continued development and improvement of the Special Education programs.
Supporting program activities related to educator preparation, state requirements, accreditation, and alignment to professional standards.
Providing service and leadership to the Special Education program, Department of Curriculum and Instruction, College of Education, university, and profession.
ABOUT THE DEPARTMENTThe Department of Curriculum and Instruction is located within the College of Education at Texas State University. The department offers undergraduate and graduate programs that prepare educators and other professionals to support learning and student success across educational settings. Additional information about the Department of Curriculum and Instruction is available at https://www.education.txst.edu/ci/.

Evidence of peer-reviewed scholarly productivity.
Evidence of effective university teaching.
Evidence of the ability to contribute to undergraduate and graduate Special Education programs, including Special Education teacher preparation.

A clearly identifiable and sustained program of research focused on Special Education or the education of individuals with disabilities.
A record of sustained peer-reviewed scholarly productivity.
A record of effective university teaching.
A record of contributing to Special Education teacher preparation or other educator-preparation programs.
A record of professional service.
Current rank of Associate Professor or Professor
Accomplishments sufficient to meet Texas State University and Department of Curriculum and Instruction standards for appointment at the Associate Professor or Professor rank with tenure.

Evidence of potential for securing external funding for research or personnel preparation.
Experience contributing to educator-preparation or teacher-certification programs.
Experience developing or participating in partnerships with schools, districts, or other educational organizations.

Experience providing leadership in educator preparation, program development, accreditation, or teacher certification.
Experience developing and sustaining partnerships with schools, districts, educational agencies, or professional organizations.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Management
jobs.description:
Job Details
Position Title:
Assistant Professor of Management
Job Posting Number:
2027028TTL
Job Location:
Round Rock, San Marcos
Department:
Department of Management
Position Description:
The Department of Management in the McCoy College of Business at Texas State University invites applications for a recently approved, tenure-track position at the rank of Assistant Professor to begin in Fall 2027. The successful candidate for this position will regularly publish high-quality research in the management/supply chain domain.
A successful candidate will also teach undergraduate and/or graduate management/supply chain courses while engaging in service appropriate for this rank. Additionally, a successful candidate will have an interest in supporting initiatives of the university, college, and department.
About the Department of Management
The Department of Management is a highly collegial and intellectually vibrant group of approximately 41 full-time faculty. The department offers a B.B.A. in Management (with concentrations in Entrepreneurial Studies, Human Resources, Leadership and Decision-Making, and Supply Chain Management); offers a university-wide minor in Innovation & Entrepreneurship; supports the college’s face-to-face and online M.B.A. programs as well as the college’s D.B.A. program; and serves as the home of the Center for Student Entrepreneurship.
About the McCoy College of Business
The McCoy College of Business provides student-centered undergraduate, master’s, and doctoral programs that produce graduates with the skills and experience to compete responsibly, professionally, and successfully in dynamic business environments. Nationally acclaimed faculty, extraordinary community partners, and industrious students collaborate to solve business challenges through applied research. As an AACSB-accredited institution with over 6,700 students, the McCoy College of Business emphasizes innovation, experiential learning, student-focused engagement, research, and service as it educates the next generation of global business leaders. The McCoy College of Business is home to the #1 Sales Program (worldwide), ranked #4 in family business research productivity (United States), ranked among the Top 30 Best Business Schools (among US public universities), and offers a Tier 1 MBA program. In recent years, the part-time MBA program was ranked among the best part-time MBA programs in the nation by U.S. News & World Report.
About Texas State University
Texas State University, located along the beautiful San Marcos River, is in the center of the Texas Innovation Corridor. The city of San Marcos is home to the university, which is 25 miles south of Austin and 60 miles north of San Antonio. Nestled in the Texas Hill Country, the campus enjoys a beautiful setting along the banks of the San Marcos River and nearby access to two major airports.
Texas State is driving what’s next in research, academic excellence, and student success. The promising students, inspiring faculty, dedicated staff, and new graduates are primed to have an impact, change lives, and make a difference in the world. As a national research university with a Carnegie classification of Doctoral University: High Research Activity, Texas State is committed to world-class research and scholarly activities that span all disciplines, create new knowledge, and advance economic, cultural, and technological progress to address real-world issues. Texas State is on a trajectory to become a “Tier One” research university.
With more than 48,000 students, Texas State is among the 50 largest public universities in the nation. Students choose from over 200 bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral degree programs offered by nine colleges. Texas State’s enrollment of minority students accounts for over 50% of the student population, and Hispanic-student enrollment accounts for over 35% of the student body. The university is a federally designated Hispanic Serving Institution and is one of 30 institutions nationally to receive the prestigious Seal of Excelencia in recognition of efforts to accelerate the success of Hispanic students in higher education. Additionally, Texas State has been named by Forbes as a Best Employer, and Best Employer for Women. The university is also regularly ranked as a Best College for Veterans.
Additional Details about the Position
The following details are offered as general information to applicants. Please note that the information below is subject to change.
Salary: The salary is competitive and commensurate with experience and qualifications.
Location: San Marcos campus (while the majority of courses are taught at the San Marcos campus, there may be a future need for teaching at the Round Rock campus).
Support: Includes the potential for summer support, other research support, and a professional development budget for research use and conference attendance.
Other Information about Why to Choose Texas State: https://www.hr.txst.edu/talent-acquisition/why-choose-txst.html
Benefits: Numerous benefits are offered (see https://www.hr.txst.edu/benefits.html for an overview).
The Department of Management seeks a collegial faculty member to advance the department and college as the university transitions to a top-tier research institution while maintaining a strong commitment to teaching. Candidates with supply chain management expertise and interests in emerging areas such as AI applications in supply chain are encouraged to apply.
This position is subject to the availability of funds.
Required Qualifications:
Successful applicants must possess the following qualifications:
A Ph.D. in Supply Chain, Business Administration, or a related business field, from an AACSB-accredited institution by the date of hire.
A history of, or strong potential for, publishing in high-quality, peer-reviewed business journals commensurate with rank.
Experience in high-quality teaching of Supply Chain Management courses at the undergraduate or graduate level commensurate with rank.
A record of service commensurate with rank.
Preferred Qualifications:
Successful applicants may also possess the following desirable qualifications:
Evidence of publishing in top-tier scholarly business journals, according to the Australian Business Deans Council (ABDC) Journal Quality List or the Chartered Association of Business Schools (CABS) Academic Journal Guide.
Evidence of high-quality teaching of Supply Chain Management or related courses (include a summary of teaching evaluations).
Evidence of a research interest in Supply Chain Management.
Evidence of a commitment to high-quality professional and institutional service activities.
Evidence of related industry experience.
Application Procedures:
Only applications submitted for this specific posting through the Texas State University website will be accepted and considered: https://jobs.hr.txstate.edu/postings/58684.
To ensure full consideration, please submit the following by 11/5/2026:
Cover letter (that clearly describes how each required qualification is met).
Curriculum vitae with references.
Research statement (that details research program and goals).
Evidence of teaching effectiveness (a summary of teaching evaluations is preferred).
Unofficial transcripts (all in one document).
The selected candidate will be required to provide official transcripts from all degree-granting universities.
Questions may be directed to Dr. Indu Ramachandran, Search Committee Chair (i_r38@txstate.edu)

From the Upstate to the Lowcountry, the University of South Carolina system is transforming the lives of South Carolinians through the impact of our eight institutions and 20 locations throughout the state. More than 50,000 students are enrolled at one of eight institutions, including the research campus in Columbia and comprehensive four-year universities in Aiken, Upstate and Beaufort. In addition, our Palmetto College campuses in Salkehatchie, Union, Lancaster and Sumter enable students to earn associate or bachelor’s degrees through a combination of in-person, online or blended learning.
