FACULTY VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT
The Department of Media Culture at the College of Staten Island, City University of New York, invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor in Cinema Studies, with an anticipated start date of Fall 2027. The Department offers bachelor's degrees in Cinema Studies (with tracks in Production and Critical Studies) and Communication (with tracks in Corporate Communication, Design and Digital Media, Journalism, and Media Studies). The Department has a strong commitment to interdisciplinary inquiry and welcomes candidates whose work crosses traditional boundaries.
We seek a candidate with the range to teach across both production and critical studies, grounded in a strong command of film and media history and theory. Given the rapidly evolving digital media landscape, the ideal candidate engages with diverse modes of production and brings a deep understanding of the craft alongside its social, cultural, political, and aesthetic dimensions. Candidates whose scholarship focuses on national, global, diasporic, African American, or LGBTQ+ cinemas are also welcome to apply.
QUALIFICATIONS
Candidates must hold an MFA or PhD. ABD candidates are eligible provided the degree is conferred prior to appointment.
Preferred qualifications include:
The successful candidate will have a demonstrated commitment to excellence in undergraduate teaching as well as an active and developing research and creative practice. Candidates must demonstrate the ability to teach and mentor students in narrative, documentary, and experimental film and video production. The successful candidate will be expected to teach across these areas, advise senior production projects, and contribute actively to curriculum development and program review.

$73,294 - $85,556
CUNY offers faculty a competitive compensation and benefits package covering health insurance, pension and retirement benefits, paid parental leave, and savings programs. We also provide mentoring and support for research, scholarship, and publication as part of our commitment to ongoing faculty professional development.

Description
The San Diego State University (SDSU) invites applications for a full-time tenure-track position in AI Security at the rank of Assistant Professor with an expected start date of Fall 2027. The Assistant Professor will be a member of the interdisciplinary Cybersecurity Research and Education Center (CCRE; https://cyber.sdsu.edu), with an academic appointment in the Management Information Systems (MIS) department within the AACSB International-accredited Fowler College of Business. Apply via PageUp by December 11, 2026 for full consideration.
SDSU is an R1 institution with a strategic initiative to develop world-leading research and education in cybersecurity and privacy. The CCRE is home to faculty conducting state-of-the-art research in critical infrastructure protection, cyber-physical systems, network security and privacy, and cybersecurity operations and management. The MIS Department has faculty expertise in information systems, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, data science, and supply chain management, and interdisciplinary initiatives with CCRE and the Silberrad Center for Artificial Intelligence. The MIS Department offers Master of Science in Cybersecurity Management (MSCM) and Master of Science in Supply Chain Innovation (MSSCI) degrees.
The center seeks candidates working in AI security to complement its existing research activity and curricula. Qualified applicants will have demonstrated expertise in trustworthy and secure AI, AI security governance and policy, AI privacy, and/or AI/ML supply-chain security. This search specifically emphasizes the security of AI systems rather than the application of AI techniques to conventional cybersecurity problems.

A record of original research / scholarly accomplishments and demonstrated capacity to
Develop a vigorous and independent program of research and scholarship in AI security, cybersecurity, secure and trustworthy AI, or closely related areas.
Teach graduate and/or undergraduate courses;
Demonstration of past accomplishments and/or future plans in at least two (2) or more of the “Building on Inclusive Excellence” criteria.
Required qualifications by date of hire
Terminal PhD degree in Information Systems, Computer Science or Electrical or Computer Engineering, or a closely related field, with all degree requirements met.
Preferred qualifications:
Strong understanding of statistical machine learning, large language models, generative AI, model protection, adversarial machine learning, and agent security.
Experience in adversarial machine learning, agent security, federated learning, and model protection
Strong record of peer-reviewed publications, presentations, and/or funding
Preparation for teaching students from diverse backgrounds
Demonstrated potential to develop and sustain externally funded cybersecurity research, including support from U.S. government agencies, the Departments of Defense, Energy, and War, and military sponsors, subject to applicable sponsor eligibility requirements.

Cover letter, including information indicating how the applicant meets or will meet required qualifications, preferred qualifications, and “Building on Inclusive Excellence” criteria
Curriculum vita
Research statement

Letters from three references

Director & Faculty (Rank TBD)
Job No: 541627
Work Type: Full Time
Location: Main Campus (Gainesville, FL)
Categories: Engineering
Department: 19010520 - EG-LEADERSHIP PROGRAMS
Job Description
Classification Title:
Director & Faculty (Rank TBD)
Classification Minimum Requirements:
• Master's degree in engineering
• Experience in successfully leading organizations (industry and/or academic) and partnering with external advisory boards
• Experience in successful stakeholder engagement activities (external and internal), including nurturing donor relationships and fundraising
• Maintains key personal qualities as a good communicator with good presence and high energy
Job Description:
ELI, located in the UF Wertheim Laboratory for Engineering Excellence, offers both undergraduate and graduate coursework and certificate programs in engineering leadership, engineering project management, and engineering and AI ethics and safety. Since its inception in 2011, over 16,000 students have completed coursework in ELI and almost 1,000 students have graduated with earned academic certificate credentials in engineering leadership or engineering project management. With three other permanent staff, dedicated adjunct instructors (many of whom are practicing engineers), a committed Advisory Board, faculty fellows, affiliates and partners, and shared support of the core values and expectations of ELI faculty and students, ELI is now poised to further enrich the education of engineering students through new academic programs, enhanced engagement programming for current and former students, and educational outreach to external partners.
The responsibilities of the ELI Director include but are not limited to the following:
Ensuring fulfillment of ELI's vision and mission and regular communication of the vision to internal and external stakeholders.
Overseeing curriculum enhancement and the creation of innovative degree initiatives and academic programs through strong collaboration with the HWCOE leadership, ELI Advisory Board, and college/university units and individuals.
Ensuring the relevance of all ELI curriculum by evaluation and application of career-readiness competencies, assessment at the course and program levels, and surveying of current and former students and employers.
Partnering with HWCOE Advancement officers in developing ELI donor relationships and active fundraising for existing and visioned ELI activities.
Leading grant proposal writing and submissions to enhance funding for ELI activities and initiatives.
Supporting development and implementation of leadership training programs for external non-UF entities.
Closely partnering with the ELI Advisory Board, meeting on a semesterly basis and engaging members in events and other activities.
Leading, mentoring, supporting, and building camaraderie among ELI staff, which currently include 3 other permanent faculty members and 14 additional supporting personnel.
Performing administrative duties that include reporting to the Florida Board of Governors, UF Office of Institutional Planning and Research, UF Advancement, and the Commission on Colleges and Universities.
Serving as a primary contributor in planning ELI events, which include the Linda Parker Hudson Leader-in-Residence Program.
Managing the ELI budget and leading fiscal planning activities for ELI.
Actively engaging in teaching ELI courses, ideally in the areas of project management, leadership, or professional development for doctoral students.
Actively engaging in the American Society of Engineering Education LEADs Division activities.
Administering the ELI Faculty Fellows, ELI Partners, and Kirkland Engineering Leadership Professor Programs by selecting participants, holding regular meetings, and intentionally building a coalition of internal and external collaborators who will further the mission of ELI.
Collaborating closely with HWCOE partners, including the Engineering Innovation Institute, Department of Engineering Education, faculty throughout HWCOE, and academic advisors, through meetings (as needed) and their participation in ELI events and activities.
Meeting regularly with the HWCOE Senior Associate Dean (and Dean) as required.
Supporting expansion of extracurricular student programming and alumni outreach activities.
Expected Salary:
Commensurate with Education and Experience
Required Qualifications:
• Master's degree in engineering
• Experience in successfully leading organizations (industry and/or academic) and partnering with external advisory boards
• Experience in successful stakeholder engagement activities (external and internal), including nurturing donor relationships and fundraising
• Maintains key personal qualities as a good communicator with good presence and high energy
Preferred:
Experience in teaching undergraduate and graduate students
Experience in proposal writing and fundraising
Experience in building and infusing organizational culture
Maintains a program/project manager mentality
UF HWCOE graduate
Special Instructions to Applicants:
The search committee will begin reviewing applications immediately and will continue to review applications until the position is filled. You must apply by submitting an application through UFCareers via https://jobs.ufl.edu/. (Job 541627) The application consists of attached PDF files of the following required documents: 1. Cover letter (summary, introduction related to hiring-emphasis areas) 2. Resume or curriculum vitae (including a 1-page CV highlights) 3. Names, addresses, phone numbers, and email addresses of no less than three and up to five references. Additional documents should be uploaded as one PDF to the “other documents” selection in the application. 4. A personal leadership experience summary detailing previous leadership roles and outcomes achieved. 5. A vision statement for leading ELI into the future, including short- and long-term goals and identifying synergies of these goals with previous leadership-related curriculum and programming activities. 6. A personal leadership philosophy statement.
The anticipated start date for this position is January 2, 2027. For further questions, please contact Search Committee Chair and Senior Associate Dean Dr. John Shea at jmshea@ufl.edu or Acting ELI Director, Mr. Bill McElroy, P.E. at mcelrowj@ufl.edu.
The University of Florida (UF) is the flagship campus of the State of Florida university system and is consistently ranked among the nation's top public universities. UF is home to HiPerGator, the fastest AI supercomputer in higher education, and the Herbert Wertheim College of Engineering is undergoing a major expansion in faculty, research, and facilities with a strong focus on artificial intelligence. In Fall 2023, UF opened Malachowsky Hall for Data Science & Information Technology, a 260,000-square-foot facility that serves as the hub for AI.

Work Type: Full Time

Job Description
Classification Title:
AST PROF
Classification Minimum Requirements
Candidates for this rank shall hold the highest degree appropriate to their field or possess equivalent qualifications based on professional experience. A candidate shall be expected to demonstrate successful experience pertinent to the position they are being recommended and have demonstrated qualities relevant to the goals of the academic unit in which they will be employed.
Job Description:
The University of Florida School of Music in the College of the Arts invites applications for a full-time, 9-month Assistant Professor in the Bands area with an appointment starting August 16, 2027. We seek an accomplished pedagogue who will contribute to the continued success and growth of a comprehensive band program. The successful candidate will instruct concert and athletic ensembles, bringing a dynamic personality and enthusiasm for teaching to our existing community of outstanding scholars and musicians.
The University of Florida College of the Arts intends to be a transformative community, responding to and generating paradigmatic shifts in the arts and beyond. As artists and scholars, we embrace the complexity of our evolving human experience and seek to empower our students and faculty to shape that experience fearlessly through critical study, creative practice, and provocation. We seek a colleague who identifies as a change-maker. We seek a colleague who will position emerging artists and researchers as catalysts for justice on local and global levels.
This position is covered by the United Faculty of Florida Contract. You can view this employment union contract here https://admin.hr.ufl.edu/compliance/employee-relations-and-ethics/union-negotiations/united-faculty-of-florida-contract/.
Responsibilities:
Tenure Accruing Responsibilities
• Collaborate with the Director of Bands and Associate Director of Bands in the day-to-day operations of the band program, ensuring effective rehearsals, performances, and administrative coordination.
• Assist with the planning, preparation, and execution of performances, including concerts, athletic events, tours, and special programs.
• Conduct and rehearse assigned concert bands, athletic bands, and related ensembles in support of the artistic and educational mission of the band program.
• Teach undergraduate conducting courses.
• Collaborate with band faculty and staff on scheduling, equipment coordination, and ensemble logistics.
• Support recruitment, retention, and outreach activities for the band program and School of Music.
• Participate in service activities appropriate to a tenure-accruing faculty appointment, including faculty meetings and School of Music events.
• Perform additional duties as assigned in support of the mission and goals of the band program and School of Music.
Summer Faculty Appointment Responsibilities
• Beginning on the first day of each Summer B session and continuing through the start of Fall classes, assist with planning and preparations for the band program.
SCHOOL OF MUSIC: Organized within the College of the Arts, the School of Music plays an important role in the academic and cultural life of the University, the College's Creative Campus initiative and the community. The School has 40 full-time and nine adjunct faculty, serving some 200 graduate and 200 undergraduate music majors. Degree programs include B.S., B.A., B.M., M.M., D.M.A., and the Ph.D. in music education, composition, ethnomusicology, and historical musicology. Program emphases include performance, music education, theory, composition, music history and literature, ethnomusicology, conducting, and sacred music. The School of Music is also home to the UF Bands program, which includes “The Pride of the Sunshine” Gator Marching Band. School of Music facilities include the School of Music Building and Steinbrenner Band Hall, among others. The University of Florida is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges and is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music. For more information, visit www.arts.ufl.edu/music.
THE COLLEGE OF THE ARTS: The College of the Arts is an engine of transformation that generates paradigmatic shifts in the arts and beyond, while nurturing adaptability, innovation, and excellence. We foster an environment where novel creative practice, leading research, and experiential learning thrive. Our students, faculty, and staff interrogate and respond to the ever-changing relationship between technology and the human spirit. We prepare future leaders in artistic professions and creative industries, while developing student capacity for interdisciplinary scholarship that serves and engages local and global communities. The College offers baccalaureate, masters, and doctoral degrees. Approximately 1,600 students are pursuing majors in degrees offered by the College of the Arts under the direction of 150 faculty members in its three accredited schools— the School of Art + Art History, the School of Music, and the School of Theatre + Dance, and in the Center for Arts in Medicine, the Digital Worlds Institute, and the Center for Arts, Migration, and Entrepreneurship. In addition, the college comprises the University Galleries, and the University level of the New World School of the Arts in Miami.
The University of Florida: The University of Florida is a comprehensive learning institution built on a land grant foundation. We are The Gator Nation, a community dedicated to excellence in education and research and shaping a better future for Florida, the nation and the world. Our mission is to enable our students to lead and influence the next generation and beyond for economic, cultural and societal benefit. UF is a graduate research institution with more than 50,000 students and membership in the prestigious Association of American Universities. Gainesville, which is consistently ranked as one of the nation's most livable cities, is located midway between the Gulf of Mexico and the Atlantic Ocean. Together, the University and the community comprise the educational, medical and cultural center of North Central Florida.
In addition to salary, the University of Florida (UF) offers low cost State Health plans, a number of Dental plans to fit you and your family's needs, and Vision. Domestic partner coverage through GatorCare is also available. Optional plans such as life, disability, legal and accident insurance are also available.
UF provides a variety of leave programs including vacation, sick leave, 11 paid holidays, personal leave days, and family medical leave. Nine-month faculty employees accrue approximately 13 sick days annually, and 4 personal leave days, typically used during the holiday closing period (accruals based on full-time employment). UF also provides you the flexibility to deal with life's challenges by offering paid family leave, eight full weeks of leave over a 24-month period.
Build a retirement roadmap with competitive pension plans, investment accounts and a host of voluntary add-ons, such as 457 deferred compensation and 403(b) plans.
UF Employees are also eligible for the GatorPerks discount program, which provides big savings at various business and retailers!

Doctorate or ABD in music (Instrumental Conducting or Music Education)

POSITION DESCRIPTION:
The Department of Psychology at the University of Toronto Scarborough (UTSC) invites applications for a full-time tenure stream position in the area of Clinical Psychology. The appointment will be at the rank of Assistant Professor, with an anticipated start date of July 1, 2027.
REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS
Candidates must have earned a PhD degree in Clinical Psychology from a Canadian Psychological Association (CPA), American Psychological Association (APA), or an equivalently accredited clinical psychology program by the time of appointment or shortly thereafter, and conduct research in adult and/or emerging adult populations, with a demonstrated record of excellence in research and teaching in Clinical Psychology. The candidate must also be eligible for registration or currently registered with the College of Psychologists and Behaviour Analysts of Ontario. We seek candidates whose research and teaching interests complement and enhance our existing departmental strengths in Clinical Psychology. Particular consideration will be given to candidates whose research incorporates functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) methodologies, as well as electroencephalography (EEG).
Candidates must provide evidence of excellence in research, which can be demonstrated through a record of publications in top-ranked and field-relevant journals or forthcoming publications that meet high international standards; the submitted research statement; presentations at significant conferences, awards and accolades, and strong endorsements from referees.
Evidence of excellence in teaching will be demonstrated through teaching accomplishments, the teaching dossier (including the required materials outlined below, as well as evidence of superior performance in other teaching-related activities), and strong letters of reference. Other teaching-related activities can include performance as a teaching assistant or course instructor, experience leading successful workshops or seminars, student mentorship, or excellent conference presentations or posters, or clinical teaching, supervision, or mentorship of trainees in applied or clinical settings.
RESPONSIBILITIES
The successful candidate will be expected to pursue innovative and independent research at the highest international level and to establish an outstanding, competitive, and externally funded research program.
In addition, the successful candidate will be assigned a teaching and service load. They must also provide evidence of readiness as a research supervisor, as they will be expected to undertake undergraduate and graduate research supervision and teaching, and to perform standard professional and administrative activities typical of a research-intensive university-level department.
Equity and diversity are essential to academic excellence. We seek candidates who value diversity and whose research, teaching and service bear out our commitment to equity. Candidates must also show evidence of a commitment to equity, diversity, inclusion and to the promotion of a respectful and collegial learning and working environment, as demonstrated through the application materials. Candidates are asked to submit a 1- to 2-page statement of contributions to equity and diversity, which might cover topics such as (but not limited to): research or teaching that incorporates a focus on underrepresented communities, the development of inclusive pedagogies, or the mentoring of students from underrepresented groups.
This search aligns with the University’s commitment to strategically and proactively promote diversity among our community members (Statement on Equity, Diversity & Excellence). Recognizing that Black, Indigenous, and other Racialized communities have experienced inequities that have developed historically and are ongoing, we strongly welcome and encourage candidates from those communities to apply.
In addition, the University of Toronto Scarborough is implementing its Strategic Plan: Inspiring Inclusive Excellence. Consistent with the values and objectives in that plan, we especially welcome candidates who self-identify as Indigenous or those who have lived experience in Black or other racialized (persons of colour) communities. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to be connected with colleagues from under-represented groups, including those hired through targeted efforts in recent years across departments spanning the Sciences, Social Sciences, and Humanities.
HIRING SALARY RANGE
The expected salary range is $140K to $170K CAD per annum, depending on experience. Negotiations beyond this salary range will be considered for exceptionally qualified candidates.
ABOUT US
As part of University of Toronto’s tri-campus structure, the University of Toronto Scarborough offers the opportunity to conduct research, teach, and live in one of the most diverse cities of the world. The successful candidate will be a member of the Department of Psychology at UTSC, which includes faculty members with interests in clinical, developmental, social, cognitive, and behavioral neuroscience. The successful candidate will also be affiliated with the Graduate Department of Psychological Clinical Science, which is housed within the Department of Psychology at UTSC and offers a CPA-accredited MA/PhD program in Clinical Psychology, grounded in the clinical science model. The program integrates scientific research with clinical practice. It fosters a rigorous and supportive training environment focused on evidence-based practice, interpersonal and metacognitive competencies, and collaborative clinical education.
The successful candidate will benefit from access to outstanding research infrastructure within the newly opened Myron and Berna Garron Health Sciences Complex, home to the Scarborough Academy of Medicine and Integrated Health (SAMIH). As part of the Department's strategic investments in neuroscience and mental health research, researchers have access to state-of-the-art neuroimaging and electrophysiological research facilities, including advanced fMRI and EEG infrastructure. Applicants whose research programs incorporate neuroimaging methodologies are particularly well positioned to take advantage of these resources and the opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration they support.

All qualified candidates are invited to apply online by clicking the link below. Your CV and cover letter should be uploaded into the dedicated fields. Please combine additional application materials into one or two files in PDF/MS Word format. Applicants must submit the following materials:
a cover letter;
a current curriculum vitae;

three recent or forthcoming publications;
and a teaching dossier including
a teaching statement,
sample course materials,
and teaching evaluations or evidence of superior performance in other teaching-related activities as listed above;
the name and contact information of three references;
as well as an EDI statement as described above.
Applicants who have a PhD from a program that is not accredited by the CPA or APA must demonstrate equivalency of their clinical psychology degree in the cover letter and append any supporting documents.

Description:
The Department of Medicine, Temerty Faculty of Medicine, University of Toronto and the Division of General Internal Medicine, Department of Medicine at Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre are inviting applications for the position of an Academic General Internist. This full-time appointment will be eligible for an academic appointment at the University of Toronto with a position description as a Clinician in Quality Improvement (CQI) or a Clinician Teacher (CT), at the rank of Assistant, Associate or Full Professor. It is expected that the position will be approximately 70% clinical and 30% related to quality improvement or teaching, respectively, for CQI or CT. Expected start date is July 1, 2027, or another mutually agreeable date thereafter.
We are seeking a physician who will deliver and foster excellence in academic general internal medicine. The successful candidate will join the Division of General Internal Medicine, which currently has 21 full-time members. The successful candidate will be expected to participate in general internal medicine clinical activities in both the inpatient and outpatient settings. They will also be expected to participate in the educational activities of the Division and provide exceptional undergraduate and postgraduate teaching. The primary location of practice is Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre, 2075 Bayview Avenue, Toronto, Ontario, Canada. Proficiency in English is required.
The successful candidate must hold an MD degree, have or be eligible for certification in Internal Medicine by the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada, and have or be eligible for medical licensure by the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario. Subspecialty certification in General Internal Medicine is preferred. The successful applicant will have a proven academic record of excellence in quality improvement, teaching, and/or education. Advanced training in quality or innovation with evidence of scholarship (such as peer-reviewed publications, presentations, or awards) is required for a CQI position. Advanced training and demonstrated achievement in teaching is required for a CT position (such as a strong track record of teaching, awards, or education scholarship).
Estimated compensation will be in the range of $250,000 to $300,000 commensurate with academic rank, qualifications and experience. The successful candidate will be eligible for membership in the Sunnybrook Department of Medicine Association through which clinical billings and benefits will be administered. The candidate will also be able to participate in the department’s group medical, dental and life insurance benefit plans.
Applications will be accepted until November 13, 2026. Please be explicit as to which type of position (CQI or CT) you are applying for. Toronto, Ontario, Canada, M4N 3M5

North Carolina State University is a research-focused (R1) institution located in the Research Triangle Area, in Raleigh, North Carolina. As a public land-grant institution, NC State has a duty not only to conduct research but also to provide accessible education and to serve the public through extension. Housed in the College of Humanities and Social Sciences, the School of Social Work offers undergraduate and graduate education to over 300 students.
The BSW generalist social work curriculum prepares students for entry-level social work practice, leadership, and the delivery and evaluation of health and human services, as well as future graduate study. The MSW curriculum prepares students for advanced generalist practice, including leadership in planning, developing, managing, and evaluating culturally relevant services for individuals, families, groups, organizations, and communities. NC State is committed to excellence in research, scholarship, teaching, and community extension and engagement.
The School of Social Work is accredited by the Council on Social Work Education (CSWE). CSWE’s Commission on Accreditation is the sole body authorized to accredit BSW and MSW programs in the United States.

Essential Job Duties:
The Assistant/Associate Professor of Population Medicine and Career Success specializes in Large Animal Population Medicine and Veterinary Education Scholarship. This dynamic role is designed for an innovative educator and researcher ready to shape the future of veterinary medicine by blending cutting-edge clinical instruction with ground-breaking educational research. This position plays a central role in delivering our core DVM curriculum while building a nationally recognized research program that drives innovation in farm animal health, AI integration, immersive learning, and student well-being.
Teaching:
Based on specific focus, this faculty member will contribute to population medicine and career readiness teaching in existing core, elective and selective courses. The faculty member will also have the option to participate in teaching and/or proposing new selective, elective or special topics courses. Interested individuals may contribute to ongoing development of house officer and graduate student competency-based training programs and trainee assessments.
Research:
This position is expected to establish an impactful, nationally recognized research program at the intersection of Large Animal Population Medicine and Veterinary Education Scholarship. This dual-focus program will address critical gaps in population health education by actively developing, implementing, and evaluating novel teaching methods. This position will focus on discovery that interrogates, innovates and transforms farm animal population health and career readiness training in veterinary education. The research will address gaps in knowledge and pivotal questions including, but not limited to, the following examples:
Immersive Technologies and Virtual Reality (VR): Investigating the design, implementation, and educational efficacy of immersive virtual environments—such as “digital twin” models of production facilities, processing plants, or pasture ecosystems. This research will leverage VR to simulate complex, high-stakes population medicine scenarios (e.g., biosecurity breaches, foreign animal disease outbreaks, and large-scale herd epidemiology mapping). The focus will be on assessing how immersive environments support rapid systemic decision-making, epidemiological risk assessment, and spatial problem-solving without inducing real-world biosecurity or animal welfare risks.
Competency-Based Veterinary Education (CBVE) & Advanced Assessments: Developing and validating robust, outcomes-based assessment methodologies. This includes creating standard-setting tools that reliably evaluate both technical execution (e.g., simulation-based herd analytics or theriogenology models) and non-technical professional competencies (e.g., communication, animal welfare advocacy, and One Health system collaboration).
Experiential, Simulation, and Community-Engaged Learning: Evaluating the educational efficacy and scalable impact of ambulatory training and community-partnered outreach to bridge the gap between tertiary referral environments and general production practice. Comparing student learning outcomes relevant to population medicine in different clinical settings.
Professional Identity Formation (PIF) and Career Sustainability: Investigating the longitudinal development of professional identity in DVM students and its explicit correlation to post-graduation career satisfaction, practitioner retention, and mental well-being. This research will evaluate how educational interventions, mentorship, and hidden curricula influence the psychological transition from student to clinician. Specifically, it will look at how to cultivate a resilient, “challenge-focused” professional identity within large animal and population medicine—equipping graduates to find career satisfaction while navigating the unique systemic, environmental, and socio-economic pressures intrinsic to production animal practice.
Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Digital Literacy: Investigating the integration of generative AI, intelligent tutoring systems, and clinical decision support models into the DVM curriculum. Research will evaluate how to foster AI literacy and “appropriate skepticism” while examining the cognitive risks of overreliance, algorithmic bias, and data privacy in production animal surveillance.
This individual will join existing large and farm animal faculty and staff currently teaching population medicine and epidemiology in DVM years 1-4.

Essential Job Duties:
The Assistant/Associate Professor of Large Animal Clinical Skills and Career Success will join a dedicated group of faculty and staff currently teaching large animal clinical skills, medicine and surgery. A combination of models, simulations and farm animals at the Teaching Animal Unit and Reedy Creek Farm are used to facilitate assessments that can be used to develop skills portfolios and investigate best practices in feedback and remediation of clinical skills.
Teaching:
This faculty member will contribute to clinical skills, large animal and career readiness teaching in existing core, elective and selective courses. The faculty member will also have the option to participate in teaching and/or proposing new selective or elective courses. Interested individuals may contribute to ongoing development of house officer and graduate student competency-based training programs and trainee assessments.
Research:
This faculty member will establish an impactful and nationally recognized research program dedicated to advancing Large Animal Clinical Skills educational research. As veterinary curricula globally evolve to meet changing technological, societal, and agricultural needs, this position will drive evidence-based advancements in how veterinary students acquire, refine, and maintain large animal technical and clinical competencies. The faculty member will be expected to investigate current high-priority areas and address critical, unmapped gaps in knowledge within veterinary medical education. The prospective areas of educational research supported by this position include, but are not limited to:
Simulation-Based Learning & Physical Model Innovation: Developing, validating, and optimizing large animal (equine, bovine, and production animal) procedural models, simulators and assessments (i.e. OSCEs, mini-CEX, etc.). A primary research gap in this domain is the critical lack of longitudinal data assessing the long-term transferability of skills from synthetic simulators to live animal clinical scenarios to practice, as well as addressing the historical “small animal bias” in existing commercial simulation tools.
Artificial Intelligence (AI) & Digital Workflow Integration: Exploring the integration of generative AI, multimodal large language models, and AI-standardized stakeholders within clinical training and communication workflows. Research will target how to teach students to utilize AI safely, ethically, and responsibly for diagnostic reasoning and uncertainty management, while addressing student adoption challenges, cognitive overreliance, and technological biases.
Competency-Based Veterinary Education (CBVE) & Assessment: Designing, implementing, and validating objective, standardized assessment instruments and grading frameworks for psychomotor skills. Research will focus on mapping competencies to pedagogical combinations that offer the highest cost-benefit ratios and efficacy for equine and production animal training.
Remediation Strategies & Cognitive Load Management: Developing evidence-based intervention and remediation strategies for students experiencing difficulties with technical proficiency. This includes studying methods to lower student anxiety and ensure safety during the high-stakes transition from low-stress models to live, potentially unpredictable large animals.
Spectrum of Care, Ethics, & Community-Engaged Learning: Investigating educational frameworks that prepare students to practice quality medicine across a spectrum of care, particularly in resource-limited, rural, or underserved environments. Research could address how experiential learning in these settings impacts clinical skill acquisition and influences veterinary workforce shortages in production animal medicine.
Community-based Education Models & Educator Development: Assessing how the pedagogical characteristics, instructional proficiency, professional identity and career satisfaction of clinical educators affect student learning in off-campus clinical teaching environments. Research will target frameworks for standardizing educator professional development and mentoring ability among non-faculty clinical preceptors.
Pipeline Development, Admissions Predictors, & Career Sustainability: Investigating the correlation between holistic DVM admissions criteria (e.g., non-cognitive attributes, rural or agricultural backgrounds, specific pre-veterinary experiences) and long-term career commitment to large animal and food supply veterinary medicine. Research in this domain will target the critical “pipeline leak”—the documented decline in large animal career interest that occurs over the course of the four-year professional curriculum. Prospective studies will explore how educational interventions, early tracking pathways, mentorship frameworks, and systemic support systems can mitigate burnout, bridge the pay-to-debt gap, and ensure the geographic and economic sustainability of the large animal veterinary workforce in rural and underserved areas.
Wellbeing, Professional Identity, & Veterinary Humanities: Evaluating the intersections of clinical skills mastery with veterinary humanities, ethical reasoning, and professional identity formation. The program will examine how early, structured competence in large animal handling correlates with student self-care, resilience, and long-term career sustainability.

About UC Blue Ash
The University of Cincinnati Blue Ash College is one of the largest regional colleges in Ohio, providing an accessible pathway to higher education for students from all backgrounds. The college is located fifteen miles north of the main uptown campus, on 135 acres in a park-like setting. We offer primarily associate degrees in career and transition programs, as well as general education courses and technical baccalaureate degrees to approximately 5,100 students. The college is a recipient of the Cincinnati Business Courier 2021 Best Places to Work award and, in 2025, earned national recognition for student opportunity and success, being named Opportunity Colleges and Universities, a distinction awarded to institutions that serve as national models for advancing student success.
The Department of Mathematics, Physics and Computer Science (MPCS) has 31 full-time faculty members, including six teaching physics. We value excellent teaching and personalized student support to help students achieve their goals, whether the goal is to enter a career or to continue their education.
Job Overview
The University of Cincinnati Blue Ash College Department of Mathematics, Physics, and Computer Science (MPCS) invites applications for a tenure-track position at the rank of Assistant Professor in Physics, intended to begin August 15, 2027.
Expectations for this position include consistently effective teaching, incorporating pedagogical strategies to improve student learning, and contributing to the advancement of teaching through professional activities.
Essential Functions
The successful candidate will be required to:
Teach physics courses as assigned by the academic unit head. These courses may include, but are not limited to, Concepts in Physics, Introductory Physics, Algebra-based General Physics, Calculus based College Physics, Introductory Astronomy, Sustainable Energy and associated labs. The standard teaching load is 12 credit hours per semester. Instructors are required to teach in-person classes, which may include evening courses. Some classes may also be offered with online, hybrid or hyflex options. Class sizes normally range from 15-30 students.
Engage in professional activities that support the University of Cincinnati Blue Ash College's mission and vision, including its commitment to excellent and accessible, student-centered education and exceptional teaching, innovative scholarship, and service. Such activities may include, but are not limited to, physics and/or physics education research, participation and leadership in professional organizations, attending and presenting at workshops, seminars, and conferences, and publishing works based on research and/or creative activities in peer-reviewed journals. Examples of creative activities include the design of instructional materials and demonstrations, innovative approaches to introducing physics concepts, and laboratory and hands-on experiences.
Participate in service or assignments which contribute to the goals of the Department, College, University and/or Community Service such as, but not limited to, serving on committees, evaluating/supporting student and academic activities, and professional service based on expertise.
Use the university course management system (Canvas) and other relevant classroom technologies.
Hold regular office hours to meet with students.
Minimum Requirements
Prior to the effective date of the appointment, all of the following are required:
Master's degree in Physics, Physics Education, or a related field.
One (1) academic year of experience teaching Physics or related courses at the College/University level, which could have been as a teaching assistant, adjunct, or full-time faculty.
Application Process
Applicants must apply online to Requisition 104336 at jobs.uc.edu. Applicants must electronically submit the following to their application:
A curriculum vitae,
A cover letter which describes in detail how the educational background and experience of the candidate make him/her qualified for the position,
A statement of teaching experience and philosophy,
A copy of graduate transcripts,
A list of at least three (3) references, including complete contact information, who can address the candidate's qualifications for this position, with at least one that can address the candidate's teaching experience.
Applications will be reviewed beginning January 10, 2027, but the position will remain open until it is filled.

jobs.description:
Job Details
Assistant Professor in Socio-Cultural Anthropology - Fall 2027
Location:
UTK
Open Date:
Oct 7, 2026
Description:
The Department of Anthropology at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville invites applicants for a full-time tenure-track position in Socio-Cultural Anthropology at the rank of Assistant Professor beginning August 1, 2027. The position will focus on food sovereignty in relation to indigenous or other marginalized communities. The University is engaged in a next-level initiative aimed both at substantially elevating the University’s national reputation for impactful research, scholarship, and creative activity and at assembling a roster of faculty committed to delivering one of the nation’s best educational experiences for undergraduate and graduate students.
Qualifications:
We seek to hire a scholar with broad training in socio-cultural anthropology or closely related disciplines with a strong background in ethnographic methods and community engagement. While regional expertise is open, we seek a scholar whose regional focus complements those of existing faculty. This position is part of a new College-wide faculty hiring constellation intended to bring together tenure-line faculty members whose research, scholarship, and creative activity can help bring new, interdisciplinary perspectives to the area of Societal Resilience to Environmental Hazards. Candidates who can contribute to this interdisciplinary constellation will be preferred.
The Department of Anthropology at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville is a three-field department that includes cultural anthropology, anthropological archaeology, and biological anthropology. The Department of Anthropology hosts the Disaster, Displacement and Human Rights Program and collaborates with interdisciplinary programs on campus like Native American and Indigenous Studies, Latin American, Caribbean and Latinx Studies, and Africana Studies. We are seeking a scholar who strengthens the department’s socio-cultural anthropology subfield and can offer courses of relevance to students across the department and university.
The successful candidate will be expected to teach two courses per semester, maintain a robust research profile, and contribute to departmental and university service.
An earned doctorate in Socio-Cultural Anthropology or a closely related field must be in hand by the time of appointment.
Required Qualifications
Ph.D. in Cultural Anthropology, Social Anthropology, Socio-Cultural Anthropology, or a closely related field.
Ph.D. in hand before the start date of August 1, 2027.
Use of ethnographic field methods for research.
Research focus on food sovereignty and/or indigeneity.
Ability to teach upper-division undergraduate and graduate courses in cultural anthropology, specifically in ethnographic methods and theory.
Preferred Qualifications
Ability to teach courses focused on the geographical area of their expertise.
Ability to teach courses pertinent to themes such as vulnerability and resilience in the context of environmental hazards, climate change impacts on vulnerable communities, environmental justice and indigenous societies.
Application Instructions:
Applicants should submit a cover letter that addresses relevant research and teaching experience, a CV, research statement, and the names and contact information of three referees. Letters of reference, sample syllabi, and a statement of teaching philosophy will be requested at a later stage.
Please submit application materials via Interfolio at https://apply.interfolio.com/194222. Review of applications will begin on November 15, 2026, and will continue until the position is filled. Preference will be given to applications received before the November 15 deadline. Direct any questions to Dr. Arsalan Khan, Search Committee Chair, at akhan53@utk.edu.

The new hire will be joining an active faculty at the University of Tennessee – Knoxville, a research-intensive university with more than 31,000 undergraduate and 7,000 graduate students. The city of Knoxville was recently named by Trip Advisor as a “Top Ten Destination on the Rise,” boasting an attractive and walkable downtown that hosts celebrated restaurants, shopping venues, and year-round cultural events and community-gathering activities. The Knoxville metropolitan area has a population of nearly 700,000 and is within easy driving distance to Atlanta, Nashville, Asheville, Cherokee, Cincinnati, and the Great Smoky Mountains National Park.

Description:
The College of Nursing at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville, seeks an innovative and compelling Clinical Assistant, Associate or Full Professor to contribute to educating the next generation of health care professionals. With a longstanding tradition of excellence in nursing education, research, and clinical practice, we are proud to be a guiding force in healthcare education. We embrace innovation while honoring the values that have shaped our success. By offering cutting-edge academic programs, supporting impactful research, and forging strong community partnerships, we prepare healthcare professionals who deliver high-quality, culturally responsive care in a diverse and ever-changing world. The ideal candidate will have a record that demonstrates excellent teaching potential with expertise in teaching topics in nursing. Additionally, the ideal candidate should have a strong commitment to teaching and service and should thrive in a diverse and intellectually stimulating environment.
Duties:
Participate in the ongoing development, implementation, evaluation, and enhancement of nursing academic programs:
Participate in program and course revisions.
Revise assigned courses to reflect program outcomes, AACN essentials, state board of nursing minimum standards, current evidence, and best practice.
Collaborate with emphasis area coordinators, clinical concentration coordinators, program directors, and the Associate and Assistant Deans to identify the types of clinical experiences and sites needed for optimal clinical education of students.

Participate in the development of academic policies affecting the admission, progression, graduation and dismissal of students.

Description of Work:
The Psychology Department at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln is recruiting a tenure-track Assistant Professor in Addiction Science who studies antecedents, processes, and/or consequences of substance use and/or misuse. Potential areas of interest include but are not limited to developmental trajectories and/or aging processes; biological and neurobehavioral mechanisms, including human or animal models; social and interpersonal processes; addiction-related cognition and decision-making; risk and resilience factors such as trauma, stress, or comorbidity with mental health disorders; and addiction-related prevention, treatment, policy, and laws. Experience with advanced quantitative approaches is welcome but not required for the position.
Responsibilities include maintaining an active research program, including the pursuit of external funding, and teaching graduate and undergraduate courses in addiction and substance use. Given that addiction and substance use are integral to a number of other disciplines, the successful candidate could be a valuable contributor to multidisciplinary research efforts involving multiple units on campus (e.g., Center for Brain, Biology & Behavior; Rural Drug Addiction Research Center; Minority Health Disparities Initiative; Nebraska Athletic Performance Lab; Center for Research on Children, Youth, Families, and Schools; Center on Children, Families, and the Law; the College of Education and Human Sciences; the Law School). The Department of Psychology values a collegial and supportive working environment in which a range of experiences and perspectives strengthens research and teaching, and we welcome applicants who will contribute to that environment.
Minimum Required Qualifications:
Ph.D. in psychology or a related field is required by the start date.
Research experience in addiction science and/or substance use.
A successful history of scholarly publications in peer-reviewed journals.
Research interests that connect to the Rural Drug Use Addiction Research Center.
Teaching experience in psychology or related areas.
Evidence of the ability to work effectively with students from a wide range of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives.
Preferred Qualifications:
Relevant experience post-Ph.D.
Experience with advanced quantitative approaches.
Research interests that complement current faculty expertise (e.g., cognitive psychology, clinical psychology, developmental psychology, law-psychology, neuroscience, or social psychology).

Teaching experience in the field of addiction science or substance use.

Description of Work:
Position Overview
We seek a collaborative technical leader with comprehensive expertise in scenic construction and engineering, rigging and safety, fabrication, and related production disciplines, along with experience with contemporary entertainment technologies such as Vectorworks and/or AutoCAD, automation and show-control systems, CNC fabrication, and 3D printing.
The successful candidate will be committed to practice-based learning and understand how foundational craft knowledge informs and enhances technological innovation. They will bring a passion for interdisciplinary collaboration and preparing students for current and future career paths across the entertainment industry. We seek a colleague who is curious about new technologies and methodologies, comfortable working in an evolving educational and production environment, and interested in contributing to the continued development of the School’s curriculum and pedagogical approaches.
The successful candidate will have experience managing complex technical operations; demonstrated project-management and leadership skills; and the ability to work collaboratively with students, faculty, staff, guest artists, and industry partners.
Key Responsibilities
Technical Leadership and Production
Oversee the physical construction and engineering aspects of School productions, including rigging, fabrication, and safety.
Develop and implement technical systems supporting both conventional and emerging production methodologies.
Integrate new production technologies into existing production processes and workflows.
Provide technical leadership and problem-solving across the School’s production activities.
Collaborate with faculty and staff across Entertainment Design & Production, Theatre, Film, and Emerging Media Arts to develop shared technical resources and workflows.
Maintain and advance professional standards for safety, fabrication, rigging, and technical production.
Teaching and Mentorship
Teach and mentor students in technical theatre, entertainment technology, fabrication, and evolving production methodologies. Depending upon curricular needs and the candidate’s areas of expertise, courses may include:
Computer-Aided Drafting
Automation and Computer-Controlled Systems
Rigging
Special Effects
Metalworking
Entertainment Engineering
Advanced Materials and Fabrication
Advanced Carpentry
CNC and Dimensional Printing Technologies
The successful candidate will mentor students through hands-on, practice-based learning and help them connect foundational construction and fabrication skills with contemporary entertainment technologies.
Curriculum and Interdisciplinary Collaboration
Develop course work within the curricular structure that connects traditional craft, fabrication, engineering, and emerging production technologies.
Foster interdisciplinary learning opportunities across theatre, film, and emerging media.
Explore new technologies, methodologies, and teaching approaches as entertainment production continues to evolve.
Contribute, as appropriate, to online and digitally supported curriculum development.
Facilities and Technical Resources
Contribute to the strategic development of technical facilities supporting the School’s expanding curricular and production needs.
Help oversee scene shops, fabrication spaces, prop and storage areas, and associated making and production facilities.
Ensure that facilities and technical practices meet current safety standards while supporting innovative production practices.
Participate in planning for equipment, technologies, and infrastructure supporting Entertainment
Design & Production and interdisciplinary production.
Professional and Industry Engagement
Maintain active engagement with current practices and emerging technologies within the entertainment industry.
Help develop student connections to internships, apprenticeships, professional opportunities, and industry partners.
Represent the School through appropriate professional organizations, conferences, and industry engagement.
Contribute to conversations about the changing nature of technical production and entertainment education.
Minimum Required Qualifications:
BFA in Technical Theatre or a related field with significant professional experience in lieu of a terminal degree.
Minimum two years of professional experience in technical direction or related production work for live entertainment.
Demonstrated expertise in traditional theatrical craft, construction, fabrication, and contemporary entertainment technology.
One year of collegiate teaching experience or equivalent professional training, mentorship, or instructional experience.
Demonstrated project-management and leadership skills.
Preferred Qualifications:
MFA in Technical Theatre or a related field.
Five or more years of professional experience in technical direction or related entertainment production.
Two or more years of teaching experience in higher education.
Experience with emerging technologies such as automation, virtual production, motion capture, real-time systems, interactive media, or advanced digital fabrication.
Experience in film production, themed entertainment, immersive experiences, live events, or other forms of mediated entertainment.
Professional connections across entertainment technology, themed entertainment, live performance, film, or related industries.
Experience developing curriculum, including online or digitally supported modalities.
Professional certifications in relevant software, safety practices, rigging, fabrication, or technical systems.

The Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering at UNL is seeking applicants for a tenure-line position at the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor with a focus in computer engineering systems, computer architecture, or networking, including connections to systems engineering. The person hired into this position is expected to develop a nationally recognized research program and contribute to academic programs in computer engineering, with opportunities to support interdisciplinary systems engineering research and education.
Research and educational activities may include:
Developing an externally funded research program in computer engineering systems, computer architecture, or networking.
Developing and teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in these areas to prepare students for careers in industry, research, and academia.
Mentoring undergraduate and graduate students and advancing collaborative research, capstone projects, and industry partnerships.
The position will be based on the Scott Campus in Omaha, NE, and housed in the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, with opportunities to support teaching and research on UNL’s City Campus in Lincoln. This location will facilitate collaboration with faculty across Nebraska Engineering, the University of Nebraska at Omaha, and relevant industry and government partners.
Candidates are expected to have an outstanding publication record, a history of funded research, and a strong national/international reputation in the area of computer and system engineering and related topics. Preference will be given to candidates with experience building higher education degree programs.
As part of this initiative, the Department of Electrical & Computer Engineering (https://ece.unl.edu) invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the Assistant/Associate Professor level that will provide a nucleus for further hiring in this technical area. The Department of Electrical & Computer Engineering consists of approximately 35 tenured/tenure-track faculty, 400 undergraduate students, and 120 graduate students co-located in two cities, Lincoln and Omaha, Nebraska. An outstanding infrastructure exists for conducting research, including central facilities housing state-of-the-art instrumentation and computing, including the Holland Computing Center (https://hcc.unl.edu). Opportunities for collaborations across the University of Nebraska include the University of Nebraska Medical Center; the University of Nebraska-Omaha College of Information Science & Technology; the Nebraska Center for Energy Sciences Research; the Center for Brain, Biology, and Behavior; the Nebraska Athletic Performance Laboratory; the Midwest Roadside Safety Facility; Innovation Campus; and other state- and federally-funded research centers and programs.

Our new colleague will be joining a dynamic and committed community of scholars in the department and a collaborative faculty group in elementary education. Description of Work:
The Department of Biochemistry and the Center for Plant Science Innovation at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln (UNL) invite applications for a tenure-track nine-month (academic year) faculty position of open rank (assistant/associate/full professor). This appointment is apportioned as 80% research and 20% teaching. Applicants are sought who will develop a vigorous, internationally recognized research program that seeks to identify novel metabolic pathways, regulatory mechanisms and/or biological processes with the goal of translating findings into strategies for crop improvement and/or bio-based products that support sustainable agriculture and biotechnology to enhance human health. Researchers will be able to leverage UNL’s extensive research infrastructure that includes the Plant Transformation Core Research Facility (PTCRF), multi-location biotech fields, and advanced field and greenhouse phenotyping platforms, to validate and scale their discoveries.
The Department of Biochemistry provides a robust environment for molecular research, offering access to state-of-the-art resources through shared equipment and the Nebraska Center for Biotechnology. Candidates will have the opportunity to utilize the UNL Cryo-EM facility for structural biology, mass spectrometry for metabolomics and proteomics, and bioinformatics and systems biology computational resources.
The university offers a highly collaborative environment to develop plant-focused research programs with affiliated resources provided by the University Research Centers (Center for Plant Science Innovation, Center for Integrated Biomolecular Communication, Redox Biology Center, Center for Virology), Holland Computing Center, the Quantitative Life Sciences Initiative, Nebraska Innovation Campus and the Center for Biological Chemistry and Complex Biosystems graduate training programs. The University Research Centers and UNL provide cutting-edge research facilities that support multiple-omics, bioinformatics, supercomputing, flow cytometry, confocal microscopy, TEM, SEM, and metabolic engineering. A competitive start-up package and appropriate laboratory and office space will be offered.

Position Summary:
The Division of Hematology and the UNC Blood Research Center (BRC) at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill seek an accomplished physician-scientist to serve as Director of the UNC Blood Research Center. Candidates should be nationally recognized leaders in benign/classical hematology and eligible for appointment as Associate Professor or Professor on the tenure track.
The UNC Blood Research Center is a multidisciplinary research organization focused on basic, translational, clinical, and population-based investigation of benign hematologic disorders. The Center serves as the scientific home for benign hematology research across UNC and fosters collaboration from laboratory discovery through clinical implementation.
The successful candidate will have a strong record of scientific leadership, high-impact publications, and sustained extramural funding. Areas of interest include thrombosis and hemostasis, sickle cell disease and hemoglobinopathies, hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia, hematopoiesis, iron metabolism, vascular biology, gene and cell therapies, and related blood disorders.
The Division of Hematology includes physician-scientists, clinical investigators, and basic scientists engaged in research spanning laboratory discovery through clinical investigation. The Division maintains nationally recognized programs in sickle cell disease, bleeding disorders, and hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia, with close collaboration across adult and pediatric hematology programs. Clinical and research activities are housed within the Eastowne Medical Office Building, which includes dedicated clinical research infrastructure.
The Blood Research Center includes more than 40 investigators from multiple disciplines and benefits from strong collaborations across UNC, including the Lineberger Comprehensive Cancer Center, Gillings School of Global Public Health, Eshelman School of Pharmacy, and Biomedical Engineering. The Francis Owen Blood Research Laboratory further strengthens the Center’s translational research capabilities.
The Director will provide scientific and strategic leadership for the Blood Research Center and advance its mission as a premier center for benign hematology research. Responsibilities include:
* Developing and implementing a strategic vision for growth in basic, translational, and clinical research.
* Fostering multidisciplinary collaborations across UNC and with external partners.
* Promoting translation of scientific discoveries into diagnostics, therapeutics, and clinical trials.
* Supporting faculty development, mentoring junior investigators, and strengthening training pathways.
* Serving as Program Director of the NIH-supported T32 training program and overseeing research training initiatives.
* Leading recruitment of physician-scientists, translational investigators, and basic scientists.
* Overseeing research space, shared resources, and Center finances.
* Partnering with institutional leadership to enhance the national visibility and impact of benign hematology research at UNC.
The Director will report to the Chief of the Division of Hematology and serve as the principal advocate for benign hematology research. Academic rank, leadership responsibilities, and compensation will be commensurate with the candidate’s experience, accomplishments, and national stature.
Academic rank will be commensurate with the candidate’s experience and accomplishments. The successful candidate will be expected to meet UNC criteria to be appointed on the tenure track.
Minimum Education and Experience Requirements:
MD, DO or MD/PhD. Individuals should preferably be board certified in Hematology. Clinical background and training in benign hematology. Active research program with track record of external funding.
Preferred Qualifications, Competencies, and Experience:
Demonstrated success in leading multidisciplinary research programs and mentoring investigators across career stages. A sustained record of NIH or equivalent extramural funding, experience building collaborative research initiatives, and a commitment to fostering inclusive and innovative research environments are highly desirable. Candidates should have the ability to engage in clinical activities within benign hematology and participate in educational programs for residents, fellows, graduate students, and postdoctoral trainees.

Not Applicable.

The Department of Radiology at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is seeking a Cardiothoracic Radiologist to join the Cardiothoracic Imaging Division. This position supports the clinical, educational, and collaborative missions of the department within a high volume academic medical center.

The division is responsible for interpretation of portable and conventional chest radiographs, thoracic computed tomography (CT) examinations, cardiac CT and MRI studies, and the performance of chest fluoroscopy. The service functions in close collaboration with pulmonology, oncology, internal medicine, cardiology, and cardiac and thoracic surgical services.

The Department of Communication at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill seeks to hire a Professor of the Practice (teaching track) to join our expanding Screenwriting Minor. Primary Purpose of Organizational Unit:
The Department of Communication is one of 44 departments and curricula in the College of Arts & Sciences. As the largest unit on campus, the College of Arts & Sciences forms the academic core of the Carolina experience. Through teaching, research, and service, the Department of Communication addresses how communication functions to create, sustain, and transform personal life, social relations, political institutions, economic organizations, and cultural and aesthetic conventions in society. Faculty conduct research and teach within a broad range of communication disciplines, including performance studies, media and technology studies, rhetoric, media arts production and new media, and organizational and interpersonal communication. Recognized for significant contributions to the profession, University, state, and nation, the Department houses a PhD program, a major in Communication, an interdisciplinary major in Cultural Studies, and a minor in Screenwriting. It serves as the intellectual home for 26 faculty members, 45 graduate students, and nearly 700 undergraduates. The Department’s doctoral program offers a theoretically rich, interdisciplinary, problem-based approach to education and research that enables graduate students to define their own research in response to the changing demands of a constantly evolving communicative and cultural world. The Department’s majors, as well as the hundreds of pan-University non-majors seek out our classes for a set of critical capacities that contribute to an engaged, creative, and critical 21st century citizen. The department’s website provides a detailed look at our activities, mission, and values.
Position Summary:
The Department of Communication at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill seeks to hire a Professor of the Practice (fixed-term) in Screenwriting. The successful candidate will teach six undergraduate courses in screenwriting per year, including at least four sections of Intro to Writing for Film and Television. Courses may include small seminars and medium-to-large lecture courses.

Master’s degree in screenwriting or another discipline, or equivalent professional experience.

Minimum 1 year of teaching at the University level or comparable; record of optioned or produced screenplays (independent or studio).

Primary Purpose of Organizational Unit:
The School of Government at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill works to improve the lives of North Carolinians by engaging in practical scholarship that helps public officials and citizens understand and improve state and local government. As the largest university-based local government training, advisory, and research organization in the United States, the School of Government offers up to 300 courses, webinars, and specialized conferences for more than 14,000 public officials each year. In addition, faculty members annually publish approximately 50 books, manuals, reports, articles, bulletins, and other print and online content related to state and local government. The School is also home to a nationally ranked graduate program in public administration.
For more information about the School, visit sog.unc.edu.
Position Summary:
The UNC School of Government seeks an attorney with a commitment to public service, a desire to teach, and a strong interest in legal research and writing to serve as an Assistant Professor of Public Law and Government with a primary focus on public employment law.
Every unit of government is an employer and must meet the legal obligations related to employment that employers generally must meet. In addition, governments as employers have constitutional and other constraints related to their employment obligations that employers in the private sector do not face. North Carolina public employers look to the School for guidance on the law of employment generally and for help with individualized situations particularly.
The faculty member in this tenure track position will provide research, training, and advising to state and local government officials on topics of public employment law, including constitutional protections including free speech in the government workplace and statutory requirements, including the Fair Labor Standards Act, the Family and Medical Leave Act, the Americans with Disabilities Act and workers compensation, as well as the application of the State Human Resources Act to local government employees.
The faculty member will teach alongside colleagues in a variety of School of Government courses, many developed specifically for human resources professionals and attorneys. Other teaching will be as part of larger courses directed at other local government officials with supervisory responsibilities.
Successful faculty members in this type of position become statewide experts and trusted advisors for public officials across North Carolina. Every consultation with a public official, every class taught, and every element of their published scholarship contribute to the School’s 90-year legacy of improving North Carolina through better governance.
Minimum Education and Experience Requirements:
J.D., excellent writing skills, strong academic performance, and demonstrated commitment to public service required
Preferred Qualifications, Competencies, and Experience:
3+ years practicing employment law preferred.

The Department of English and Comparative Literature at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill invites applications for a tenure-track position at the rank of Assistant Professor in Writing, Editing, and Digital Publishing, beginning July 1, 2027. Applicants must hold a Ph.D. in Rhetoric and Composition, English, Writing Studies, or a closely related field by the time of appointment.
We seek a teacher-scholar whose research and teaching engage the evolving relationships among writing, editing, digital publishing, and artificial intelligence. We welcome candidates working across rhetoric and composition, writing studies, technical and professional communication, digital rhetoric, literacy studies, or related fields.
The successful candidate will maintain a research program that examines how AI is reshaping writing, editing, digital publishing, and rhetoric. We are particularly interested in scholars who move beyond simple narratives of technological optimism or critique.
We seek candidates who approach artificial intelligence as a complex scholarly problem that demands historical, theoretical, empirical, creative, and pedagogical investigation. Candidates should demonstrate how their work develops and applies questions about authorship, creativity, expertise, communication, labor, literacy, ethics, publishing, and/or the future of humanistic inquiry.
Candidates should also demonstrate a record of research, publication, and practical and pedagogical engagement with emerging technologies. Candidates should demonstrate the ability to work across disciplinary boundaries through expertise in multiple areas of study and the creative integration of diverse approaches.
We also seek candidates with a commitment to collaborative scholarship, which may be demonstrated through leadership and participation in academic programs, research initiatives, or public-facing projects. Beyond research collaborations, we value public outreach, the sharing of resources, and community-building activities that contribute to vibrant intellectual communities and broaden the impact of scholarly work.

We seek candidates who can contribute to UNC’s academic mission as a public institution, especially through commitment to diversity of perspective, intercultural understanding, and engagement with local resources and communities. We encourage candidates to consult our website to learn about the Department’s curriculum, values, and mission. Candidates working across disciplines are encouraged to apply.
The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is the flagship institution of a strong state university system comprising 17 campuses across North Carolina; neighbor institutions within 25 miles include Duke University, North Carolina Central University, North Carolina State University, and Meredith College. Chapel Hill is a vibrant college town near the Research Triangle economic hub and 20 minutes from Raleigh-Durham International Airport.

The successful candidate’s duties will include teaching, research, and service. This Assistant Professor will teach a 2-2 load made up of graduate and undergraduate courses; contribute to both undergraduate and graduate curricula; mentor students; participate in select administrative activities; and engage in ongoing scholarly research.

Ph.D. English, Rhetoric and Composition, or a related degree and instructional experience at the college level by the time of appointment.
Preferred Qualifications, Competencies, and Experience:
Demonstrated excellence in college-level teaching, a strong research portfolio, expertise in research methods, a history of collaboration, experience in research and teaching related to Artificial Intelligence and its relationship to Writing, Editing, and Digital Publishing.
