jobs.title: Assistant Professor, Mechanical Engineering-Multiple Openings
jobs.description:
Job Details
Assistant Professor, Mechanical Engineering-Multiple Openings
RIT's Department of Mechanical Engineering invites applications for three tenure-track Assistant Professor positions. We seek highly motivated individuals who are committed to excellence in both research and teaching and are eager to contribute to a vibrant academic community.
We are specifically looking for candidates in each of the three following broad areas:
Digital Twins in Mechanical Engineering and Design.
Interests include but are not limited to: physics-informed and hybrid physics-ML modeling; digital twins for engineering design and manufacturing, including AI-assisted and generative design, additive manufacturing, and product lifecycle; and uncertainty quantification, verification and validation, and real-time model updating for decision-ready digital twins.
Controls, Systems, and Sensors
Interests include but are not limited to: dynamics and control of robotic and autonomous systems; cyber-physical systems, including estimation, learning-based control, and system integration; and sensors and sensor systems, spanning physical, bio-, and electrochemical sensors, including printed, flexible, and wearable devices.
Composite Materials in Aerospace Applications
Interests include but are not limited to: AI-enabled design and discovery of composite materials; autonomous/intelligent manufacturing of composites; composite materials for extreme environments; and damage prediction and structural health monitoring.
Candidates should only apply to one position that best aligns with their expertise and should clearly indicate the position in their cover letter.
Successful candidates are expected to build and sustain a strong externally funded research program, advise Ph.D. and master's students, develop and teach undergraduate and graduate classes, advise undergraduate researchers and design teams, and work collaboratively to advance the department's goals.
We are seeking individuals who are able and interested in contributing to a community committed to student-centeredness; professional development and scholarship; integrity and ethics; respect; innovation and flexibility; and teamwork and collaboration. Select to view links to RIT's core values, honor code.
Questions for the search committee should be directed to Dr. Xudong Zheng (xxzeme@rit.edu). For full consideration, please submit your application by Friday, November 6, 2026.
Department/College Description:
With over 1000 undergraduate and graduate students, the Mechanical Engineering Department is the largest of the six academic departments in the Kate Gleason College of Engineering. It is currently experiencing significant growth, with enrollment on track to increase by 30% in the upcoming years. The department currently includes 23 tenured and tenure-track faculty, 15 lecturers, and 11 staff members. The department offers a BS in Mechanical Engineering with options in automotive engineering, aerospace engineering, energy and the environment, and bioengineering and an accelerated BS-ME/MS program. Graduate programs include an MS and ME in Mechanical Engineering and a PhD in Mechanical and Industrial Engineering. Faculty research is supported by a wide range of core facilities across campus including a fully staffed mechanical engineering machine shop providing machining, fabrication, design, and manufacturing services. The University houses 17 Research Centers and Institutes, including the AMPrint Center for Additive Manufacturing and Multifunctional Printing, a NY State Center for Advanced Technology, the Battery Prototyping and Testing Center, the Center for Human-aware AI, the NanoPower Research Laboratories, Personalized Healthcare Technology, and the Center for Innovation in Manufacturing and Sustainability, as well as many others. Additional resources include the high-performance computing cluster through RIT Research Computing and the Semiconductor Nanofabrication Laboratory with state-of-the-art cleanroom facilities.
The Kate Gleason College of Engineering | RIT offers bachelor's and master's in biomedical engineering, chemical engineering, computer engineering, electrical engineering, industrial engineering, mechanical engineering, and microelectronics engineering as well as four Ph.D. degrees in biomedical and chemical engineering, electrical and computer engineering, mechanical and industrial Engineering, and microsystems engineering and additional master's programs in engineering management and leadership. Serving over 2600 undergraduates and 400 graduate students, the college is committed to growing its research profile while maintaining a strong commitment to undergraduate education. Major research themes include advanced manufacturing; biomedical and healthcare engineering; artificial intelligence and machine learning; cyber-physical systems; micro- and nanoscale systems devices and materials; energy and environment; and data analysis modeling and simulation. Hallmarks of the undergraduate experience include one full year of cooperative education, an innovative multidisciplinary senior design program, and an impressive variety of well-supported student teams and clubs.
THE UNIVERSITY AND ROCHESTER COMMUNITY:
Rochester Institute of Technology is home to leading creators, entrepreneurs, innovators, and researchers. The university enrolls 16,868 undergraduates and 2,904 graduate students in more than 200 programs, and across nine academic colleges, five international campuses, as well as other degree- granting units, placing it among some of the largest private universities in the U.S. RIT is internationally recognized and ranked for academic leadership in business, computing, engineering, imaging science, liberal arts, sustainability, and fine and applied arts. RIT is also home to the National Technical Institute for the Deaf, the world's first and largest technological college for deaf and hard-of-hearing students. With more than 900 students from around the world, NTID offers unparalleled support services for deaf and hard-of-hearing students. RIT's cooperative education program is one of the oldest and largest in the nation.
In 2019, RIT moved into the high research activity institution or "R2" category under the updated Carnegie Classification of Institutions of Higher Learning, ranking it among the top six percent of colleges and universities in the nation for research activity. U.S. News and World Report (USNWR) now ranks RIT No. 88 in its "National Universities" category, and No. 57 and No. 69 for Best Undergraduate and Graduate Engineering Programs, respectively. The publication also ranks RIT No. 11 in the U.S. for co-op or internship programs, No. 48 among best-value schools, and No. 41 among most innovative. Sponsored research awards totaled $105 million in the fiscal year 2025, up from $78 million in 2018. Today, RIT counts nearly 140,000 alumni around the world. Its endowment is currently valued at $1.257 billion, and the university benefits from sound financial management.
Always on the cutting-edge, RIT's educational programs continue to evolve to meet the needs of today's students. Building on its legacy of excellence across STEM and the arts and its commitment to developing creative thinkers, RIT launched the Performing Arts Scholars program in 2019. In fall of 2022, 482 first- year students accepted scholarships to join this program, regardless of major, bringing the total number of PA Scholars to 1,400. In support of this programming, RIT is unveiling the Student Hall for Exploration and Development (SHED) in the fall of 2023, with major facilities for the performing arts, and new classrooms, surrounding an enormous multi-story core of makerspaces. RIT has also launched a series of very successful Combined Accelerated Bachelor's/Master's Degree (CAB-M) programs, which attracted about 750 of the students in the fall of 2022. In addition, RIT is developing a large suite of online programs with an emphasis on upskilling for adult learners through its offerings at RIT Certified.
QUALIFICATIONS:
REQUIRED:

• Ability and commitment to effectively teach and mentor undergraduate and graduate students
• Record of disseminating scholarly research in refereed (peer-reviewed) publications
• Demonstrated ability or potential to establish an independent externally sponsored research program
• Excellent communication skills
• Ability to contribute meaningfully to the university's continuing commitment to individual differences.
• Interest in working in a collaborative, collegial environment
HOW TO APPLY:
Candidates may apply online at http://careers.rit.edu/faculty; select Faculty Positions, then Keyword Search. Please upload the following documents to complete the application:

Job Details
Overview
Postdoctoral Scholar: Tharin Laboratory, Department of Neurosurgery, UMass Chan Medical School
Dr. Suzanne Tharin, MD, PhD, is seeking a highly motivated and talented Postdoctoral Scholar to join a new, NIH-funded research laboratory at UMass Chan Medical School, an international leader in microRNA research. The lab's long-term goal is to understand the molecular controls over cortical neuronal development and regeneration, including stem cell-based strategies for spinal cord injury repair. Current work focuses on the role of microRNAs in shaping the development and regeneration of corticospinal motor neurons.
Responsibilities
Potential Projects
Depending on the candidate's background and interests, potential projects include:
Investigating microRNA controls over corticospinal motor neuron development, specifically examining how differentially expressed microRNAs direct differentiation between corticospinal motor neurons and callosal projection neurons
Identifying the targets of differentially regulated microRNAs in corticospinal motor neurons and their downstream effects on dendritic morphology and neuron-subtype identity
Studying the in vivo response of corticospinal motor neurons to differentially expressed microRNAs, and evaluating their potential roles in promoting cellular recovery and axon regeneration
Qualifications
Required Qualifications
D., MD/Ph.D., or equivalent degree in Neuroscience or a closely related field
Strong background in molecular biology techniques (RNA extraction, qPCR, cloning, etc.) and mammalian cell culture
Excellent communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively in a multidisciplinary environment
A strong drive to mentor undergraduate and graduate students in the lab
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with in utero electroporation of embryonic mouse brain (highly desirable)
Experience with in vivo rodent models, including stereotaxic surgeries, spinal cord injury models, and neural tracing techniques
Familiarity with transcriptomic analysis (e.g., RNA-seq, miRNA-seq)
Additional Information
Details
Funding: NIH-funded position
Start date: Flexible
Salary: Per NIH and UMass Chan pay scales

Job Title:College of Nursing Tenured/Tenure-Track Faculty
Department:Nursing | Division of Nursing and Health Sciences
Tenure faculty (regardless of rank) - persons with the titles of professor, associate professor, assistant professor and instructor who serve on appointments totaling 50% or more service to the university and who are eligible for tenure or who have obtained tenure. Duties and responsibilities are assigned in accordance with the workload guidelines laid out in the pattern of administration of each faculty member’s tenure initiation unit (TIU) and, as appropriate, regional campus; obligations will include research, service and/or teaching or clinical practice. These faculty will have earned doctorate or other terminal degree in the relevant field of study or possession of equivalent experience.
Position Overview
The Division of Nursing and Health Science invites applications for open-rank, tenured or tenure-track faculty positions at the assistant, associate, or professor level. The Ohio State University is a model 21st century public, land grant, research, urban, community-engaged institution. The College of Nursing is a leading voice and advocate in education, scientific discovery and practice to change the future of healthcare for the better. The Division of Nursing and Health Science serves as a home to nurse and health scientists leading rigorous programs of research addressing critical health challenges across the lifespan, from maternal-infant health to complex care and aging, and many areas in between. This excellence is reflected in our college’s ranking as #6 nationally and #1 among Big Ten nursing schools in NIH funding.
We are seeking two faculty members with programs of research well aligned with the visions and missions of our university, college, and division. While all are welcome to apply, we have particular interest in candidates whose work focuses on health informatics/health services research and/or artificial intelligence. Areas of interest include, but are not limited to, clinical and biomedical informatics; digital health infrastructure and health information exchange; health systems research, healthcare delivery, operations, and patient safety; learning health systems and academic-medical center partnerships; clinical decision support; predictive analytics; and the development and responsible use of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and natural language processing to improve health and healthcare.
The college is also recognized for its strengths in translational biosciences and dissemination and implementation science. Through our state-of-the-art Translational Biosciences Laboratory and robust interdisciplinary research infrastructure, we welcome candidates whose work advances understanding of, for example, the biological basis of health and disease through biomarker research, biotechnology, stress and other biobehavioral sciences, omics research, systems biology, and precision health. The Helene Fuld Health Trust National Institute for Evidence-based Practice in Nursing and Healthcare provides extensive scholarly resources, mentorship, and methodological expertise to support dissemination and implementation research. We seek scholars who wish to leverage this infrastructure to advance the uptake, sustainability, and scale-up of evidence-based practices across healthcare and community settings.
This is not a remote position. Faculty are expected to reside in Ohio and be physically present on campus in Columbus at least three days per week.
Performance Objectives
Show potential for, demonstrated, or sustained contributions to nursing and/or health science.
Develop or expand a nationally or internationally recognized program of research.
Show potential for, demonstrated, or sustained internal and external research funding.
Contribute to undergraduate and graduate nursing education.
Supervise student research and foster critical thinking and inquiry among learners.
Demonstrate leadership and collaboration within academic and clinical environments.
Serve as an engaged member of the College and broader University community.
Show potential for, demonstrated, or sustained evidence of excellence in research mentorship.
Exhibit strong interpersonal and communication skills.
Demonstrate the ability to work constructively, decisively, and collegially.
Demonstrate the ability to work across interdisciplinary teams and with partners.
Operate independently as a proactive self-starter.
Exhibit effective project leadership and organizational skills.
Display innovative thinking, openness, and a commitment to lifelong learning and growth.
Participate actively in service to the College of Nursing, university, and professional community.
Education and Experience Requirements
Required:
PhD in Nursing or other related field
RN licensure in the State of Ohio for those who are nurses (required upon hire)
Desired:
Postdoctoral research experience is strongly preferred for those applying at the assistant level
Ideal applicants will have research programs focused on health informatics/health services research, artificial intelligence, translational biosciences, and/or dissemination and implementation science, which may be applied to the study of health across the lifespan
Additional Information
The offer for this position will be based on internal equity and the candidate's qualifications. Sponsorship is not available for international candidates. Ohio State provides access to a depth and breadth of opportunities and resources. Starting your first day, Ohio State offers you a comprehensive benefits package.
Application materials must include:
Cover letter
Curriculum Vita (CV)
Career Synopsis (a personal statement highlighting your research, teaching, mentoring, and service. Maximum length 3 pages, single spaced, 1” margins, using Arial 11 pt. font).
Additional Information:
The College
The Ohio State University College of Nursing ranks #6 nationally and #1 among Big Ten nursing schools in NIH funding. As part of one of the nation's leading public research universities and academic health centers, faculty benefit from
extensive opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration, access to diverse clinical and community-based research settings, and a strong culture of research excellence, innovation, and impact.
Our colleges’ Division of Nursing and Health Science is home to a diverse community of nurse scientists and health researchers advancing discovery across the lifespan. Through rigorous science, interdisciplinary collaboration, and strong partnerships with patients, families, clinicians, health systems, and communities, our faculty generate evidence that improves health and healthcare and lead innovative research programs spanning clinical, behavioral, implementation, population, and health services research. We are committed to translating discoveries into practice, policy, and measurable health impact.
Division faculty also have access to our in-house Translational Biosciences Laboratory, a dedicated research resource that supports a comprehensive range of bio-based research. As an Ohio State-certified Biosafety Level 2 facility, the laboratory provides the infrastructure for rigorous investigation of the biological basis for health and disease, from biospecimen collection, processing, and storage to molecular and cellular investigations, immune and microbial profiling, biomarker discovery and validation, and quantitative analyses of genetic, hormonal, and protein-based measures. The laboratory supports both investigator-initiated and collaborative research across the translational spectrum, enabling faculty to integrate biological measures into clinical, behavioral, population, and health services research programs.
Division faculty also have access to the Helene Fuld Health Trust National Institute for Evidence-based Practice in Nursing and Healthcare, an internationally recognized center dedicated to advancing the translation of evidence into practice and improving healthcare outcomes. The Institute provides a rich environment for dissemination and implementation research. Through its extensive training programs, methodological expertise, and national and international collaborations, the Institute supports both investigator-initiated and interdisciplinary research aimed at accelerating the uptake of evidence-based interventions across clinical, community, health system, and community settings.
Lastly, division faculty benefit from a rich ecosystem of research-practice partnerships that includes the college's nurse-led Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC), the Ohio State Wexner Medical Center, the OSUCCC–James Comprehensive Cancer Center, and Nationwide Children's Hospital. Together, these organizations provide exceptional opportunities for clinical, translational, and health systems research across broadly representative populations and settings. Our faculty collaborate with clinicians, scientists, and healthcare leaders to address pressing health challenges, access robust clinical and population health data resources, and translate discoveries into practice. The breadth of these partnerships supports the full continuum of research, from prevention and intervention development to implementation, evaluation, and healthcare transformation, creating unique opportunities to improve health and healthcare delivery.
The University
Ohio State is a top-20 public university, and its Ohio State Wexner Medical Center is one of America’s leading academic health centers. Service offerings include dual career partner consultation, potential employer and/or employment opportunity identification, consultation and resources related to relocation, as well as identifying opportunities to engage on campus and in the surrounding community. In addition to being responsive to dual-career opportunities, we strongly promote work-life balance to support our community members through a suite of institutionalized policies. Ohio State is a member of the Michigan, Ohio, Western Pennsylvania & West Virginia HERC.

The area offers a wide range of affordable housing, many cultural and recreational opportunities, excellent schools, and a strong economy based on government as well as service, transportation, and technology industries. Beyond its Columbus campus, Ohio State has four regional campuses including Ohio State Lima, Ohio State Mansfield, Ohio State Marion, and Ohio State Newark, in addition to the College of Food, Agricultural, and Environmental Sciences (CFAES) Wooster Campus, which houses Ohio State ATI.

Job Title:Assistant Clinical-Track Faculty: Business Analytics
Department:Fisher College | Operations and Business Analytics
The Department of Operations and Business Analytics (OBA) within Fisher College of Business, at The Ohio State University, invites applications for a Clinical-Track faculty position specializing in Business Analytics (Assistant Rank). This will be a full-time appointment, to begin Autumn semester 2027. The salary is competitive with leading research universities.
We seek candidates who are committed to excellence in teaching and curriculum development in business analytics and artificial intelligence. The successful candidate will develop and teach courses for undergraduate, graduate, and executive education students, with responsibilities that include curriculum and syllabus design and the development of course content and instructional materials. The candidate will also contribute through service and leadership activities that support the educational and outreach missions of Fisher College of Business.
While teaching and curriculum development are the primary performance objectives for this clinical-track position, the successful candidate will also be expected to generate impactful scholarly output that advances the college’s educational and/or outreach missions. Such contributions may include research, practitioner-oriented writing, teaching cases, textbooks, classroom simulations, and other innovative pedagogical materials.
Immigration/visa sponsorship may be available in very limited situations (e.g., F1/OPT to H-1b, H-1b change of employer), but all decisions concerning immigration/visa sponsorship will depend on an evaluation of complexity and risk.
Performance Objectives:
Principal tasks will include: curriculum and syllabus design, content and materials development, teaching, and service and leadership activities in support of the missions of the college. The selected candidate will be expected to complete activities and provide support for developing and teaching undergraduate, graduate, and executive education students within the domain of business analytics/AI. While excellence in teaching and curriculum development are the primary performance objectives, clinical assistant professors at Fisher are also expected to generate impactful scholarly output within the domain of business analytics that furthers the educational and/or the outreach missions of the college (e.g., through research, writings geared toward practitioners, teaching cases, textbooks, classroom simulations, and other forms of innovative pedagogical materials).
Education and Experience Requirements:
Minimum requirements for the position are a terminal degree (PhD, DBA, or equivalent) in a business or related field, completed by the start date of employment.
Candidates ideally would have an established record of excellence in knowledge dissemination within the domain of business analytics/AI, but we will also consider newly graduating candidates with clear potential to develop such a record. Similarly, candidates ideally would have an established record of effective related service (e.g., curriculum development and program management), but we will also consider candidates with clear potential to do so.
Desired attributes for ideal candidates include the flexibility to teach courses across business analytics and operations management; significant practical business experience within the field of business analytics and, potentially, operations management; experience in teaching executive education; and a strong record of service and outreach with the business community. It is also desired that the candidates have already, or have the potential to, create scholarly output as described above.
Additional Information:
Assistant Clinical Professors in this department currently have a base salary of $150,000-$175,000. The offer for this position will be based on internal equity and the candidate's qualifications.

Fisher College of Business has a rich research tradition and engages through the college and the Graduate School in programs at the undergraduate, master and doctoral levels. Job Title:Associate/Full Professor in Waterfowl Ecology and Wetlands Management
Department:FAES | School of Environment and Natural Resources
Position Description
This is a full-time 9-month tenure-track appointment with responsibilities distributed as described across research, teaching and service. Our aim is to recruit, support, and retain a scholar that will foster science based
conservation of migratory waterfowl and other gamebirds, as well as wetlands and associated upland habitats that sustain wildlife populations and human well-being. Pending Board of Trustee approval, this position will include annual research funds and an Endowed Professorship for those at appropriate rank supported by Winous Point Marsh Conservancy (WPMC). WPMC is committed to providing additional research funding, facilities and logistical support for this research program consistent with their mission.
We encourage applications from scholars with an emphasis on the generation, dissemination, and application of science-based knowledge to inform conservation and management decisions. We strongly
encourage applications whose scholarship demonstrates an integrated program in wildlife ecology and conservation with emphasis on:
Population dynamics of waterfowl and other bird species
Ecology and management of wetlands and associated upland systems
Wetland habitat restoration and ecosystem services
Interactions among ecological function, wildlife conservation, and human use
The successful candidate will teach approximately 2 undergraduate or graduate courses per year, primarily in waterfowl and wetlands ecology, wildlife population management, and experiential learning courses. They
will collaborate with SENR faculty, Ohio State University Extension and SeaGrant, the Ohio Department of Natural Resources Division of Wildlife, the Winous Point Marsh Conservancy, and other partners on applied
research and outreach opportunities. Depending on experience and qualifications, the incumbent may have a significant co-leadership or coordinating role in the Terrestrial Wildlife Ecology Laboratory conducting and administering grant-funded research, education and outreach programs.
Performance Objectives
1. Develop new or enhance existing courses aligned with SENR’s Forestry, Fisheries and Wildlife major.
2. Demonstrate an ability to cultivate learning environments where students feel they belong within the School of Environment and Natural Resources and related professions.
3. Contribute to professional development and outreach workshops for practitioners and stakeholders.
4. Engage with and provide leadership for the Terrestrial Wildlife Ecology Laboratory.
5. Develop and/or expand an independent research program on the ecology and management of waterfowl, wetlands, and associated wildlife communities, including presenting results at national and international meetings, securing extramural funding, and producing impactful publications.
6. Advise graduate and undergraduate students, including Environment and Natural Resources Graduate Program and SENR honors students.
7. Work collaboratively with university faculty and staff, School of Environment and Natural Resources and/or OSU extension, government agencies, non-government organizations, and/or community groups to advance the land grant mission of the college and university.
8. Serve the School of Environment and Natural Resources, university, and professional communities through committee work and other appropriate activities, including serving as faculty advisor for
student organizations such as Ducks Unlimited.
Education and Experience Requirements
Required:
Earned Ph.D. in wildlife ecology, wetlands science, or a closely related field
Demonstrated interest in or experience with applied research on wildlife populations and habitat ecology in wetland systems
Experience conducting field-based studies and ecological investigations
Strong quantitative and analytical skills
Evidence of potential for excellence in research and teaching.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills and a willingness and ability to work closely with diverse groups of academic (e.g., students, staff, faculty) and practitioner audiences.
Demonstrated interest in and/or experience with teaching, recruiting, mentoring, and advising a diverse body of students.
Desired:
Experience integrating research, teaching, and outreach
Evidence of interdisciplinary collaboration, with environmental and social scientists
Experience securing external funding
Engagement with stakeholders, practitioners, and conservation organizations
Additional Information:
How to Apply
To be considered, please submit your application electronically via Workday. Application materials must include:
Required:
Cover letter- Describe your qualifications, area(s) of expertise, career goals, and alignment with desired qualifications and preferred qualifications where applicable
Curriculum Vita (CV)
Statement of Teaching and Mentoring (no more than 2 pages)
Statement of Service/Outreach (no more than 2 pages)
Names/contact information of three references ( Note: Letters of reference are expected to be solicited prior to advancing to the next stage of the hiring process; inform your references when you apply so that letters can be finalized at/soon after time of request )
Initial consideration will be given to applications received by Friday November 16, 2026. Review of applications will continue until the position has been filled. We welcome informal inquiries, which can be made by contacting Search Committee Chair Dr. Chris Tonra at tonra.1@osu.edu.
Department/School Information
Since its inception in 1968, the School of Environment and Natural Resources (SENR) has evolved and changed to meet the changing needs and demands of society, students, and the various natural resource professions. The School’s foundation is its interdisciplinarity, coupling the natural sciences with the social sciences and human dimensions of sustainable natural resources management for the well-being of people and society. The School’s vision is a productive society in harmony with a sustainable and healthy environment. The mission of SENR is to enhance and impart knowledge of natural and social systems and their essential relationships in the context of natural resource use and management and to continuously improve the academic strength of the School through effective teaching, including extension teaching, sound research, and hiring the best possible faculty.
SENR has 5 undergraduate majors and 7 minors and certificates that share the goal of conservation and stewardship of our environment. Our approximately 600 undergraduate students are active in experiential learning opportunities ranging from the field to the lab. Our graduate programs include an MS and PhD program as well as a professional Masters (MENR) program and several minors and certificates. Our approximately 100 graduate students are active in the classroom and in research, participating in over $13 million in annual research expenditures through our diverse research programs.
The College
The College of Food, Agricultural, and Environmental Sciences (CFAES) anchors its mission in a simple, yet powerful phrase: We Sustain Life. Faculty, staff and students alike contribute to this mission in a variety of ways. Our Strategic Alignment outlines the colleges values. These values, which align with the university’s Shared Values, shape our goals of our Strategic Alignment. We are committed to scholarship across three mission areas (teaching, research, Extension) with a commitment to serving our state in addition to the country and world. As a land grant, we are part of a cooperative structure that includes key partners all dedicated to integrating research, education, and Extension to improve the food and agricultural sectors, the environment, and the quality of people’s lives. We educate not just undergraduate and graduate students but learners across the lifespan. We work to ensure groundbreaking scientific discoveries are brought out of the laboratory and into the hands of those who can put them to work.
CFAES houses 11 departments/schools with over 20 undergraduate majors and 9 graduate programs, including 3 interdisciplinary programs affiliated with multiple Ohio State colleges. We also administer OSU Extension, which provides robust and relevant programming to Ohioans and beyond in the areas of Agriculture and Natural Resources, 4-H Youth Development, Family and Consumer Sciences, and Community Development. We are one college spanning three campuses: Columbus, CFAES Wooster, and Statewide. Our CFAES Wooster campus includes a large research station and Ohio State’s only two-year academic unit, Ohio State ATI. The Statewide campus includes 11 research stations and Extension offices in all of Ohio’s 88 counties. Our At a Glance provides additional information regarding our size, capacity, and impact as a college.

Job Title:Assistant Professor of Professional Practice in Urban Forestry
Department:FAES | School of Environment and Natural Resources
Position Description
Our aim is to recruit, support, and retain an educator and practitioner who will advance urban forestry education, practice, and engagement across Ohio and beyond. We welcome applicants with expertise in urban forestry, including community and municipal forestry, urban forest planning and management, arboriculture, tree health and risk assessment, urban ecosystem services, green infrastructure, and the role of trees and greenspaces in supporting healthy, sustainable communities. We strongly encourage applications from individuals whose professional work reflects a commitment to preparing the next generation of urban forestry professionals and strengthening connections among people, trees, and communities.
The successful candidate will contribute to teaching (50%), extension and outreach (40%), and service (10%) in areas related to urban forestry practice and planning, arboriculture, urban forest assessment and management, community engagement, and professional workforce development. The position is designed to advance OSU’s land-grant mission through excellence in teaching, student mentoring, partnership and engagement with public agencies, nonprofit organizations, industry partners, and community stakeholders across Ohio.
Teaching and Non-Classroom Instructional Responsibilities (50%)
The successful candidate is expected to teach approximately three courses per academic year. Teaching responsibilities will include:
Two courses to be developed
Arboriculture and Tree Health Care (or something similar)
Urban Forestry Practice and Planning (or something similar)
One additional existing course, based on programmatic needs and candidate expertise, such as (but not limited to):
ENR 3300 Forestry, Fisheries, and Wildlife;
ENR 3321 Biology and Identification of Woody Forest Plants;
ENR 3323 Forest Biometrics;
ENR 3600 Recreation Management on Public Lands; or
ENR 5642 Environmental and Natural Resource Administration.
The successful candidate will develop innovative, experiential, and field-based learning opportunities that connect students with urban forestry professionals, organizations, and communities. Courses – particularly those to be developed – should integrate contemporary tools and technologies appropriate to professional practice, including urban forest inventories, GIS, canopy assessment, and related decision-support approaches.
The incumbent will be an integral member of the School of Environment and Natural Resources (SENR), advising and mentoring undergraduate and graduate students pursuing careers in urban forestry and related environmental and natural resource professions. The successful candidate will also support student internships, capstone projects, professional certifications, and career placement activities.
Extension and Outreach Responsibilities (40%)
This position includes a 40% extension appointment, and extension and outreach expectations are commensurate with that level of effort. The successful candidate will develop and deliver a coordinated extension and outreach program in urban forestry that addresses the needs of public agencies, nonprofit organizations, industry partners, and community stakeholders across Ohio.
This work will be conducted in collaboration with Extension professionals within SENR, across CFAES, and throughout OSU Extension, as appropriate. Activities may include educational programming, technical assistance, professional training, workshops, and stakeholder engagement. Potential stakeholder groups include city and county governments, park districts, utilities, consulting firms, nonprofit organizations, community groups, and forestry and natural resource professionals.
The extension program is expected to be practical, collaborative, and responsive to stakeholder needs while supporting workforce development and advancing urban forestry initiatives consistent with the land-grant mission of the college and university.
Service (10%)
This position includes a 10% service appointment, with expectations commensurate with those of all faculty in SENR. The successful candidate will provide service to SENR, CFAES, and Ohio State through participation in committees, faculty governance activities, and related service contributions. The incumbent will also be expected to engage in professional service through relevant professional societies, certification programs, and urban forestry organizations.
Research Expectations
This position has no formal research requirement for promotion. However, the incumbent is not precluded from engaging in applied scholarship, demonstration projects, or other professional activities that complement teaching, Extension programming, stakeholder engagement, or workforce development goals.
Performance Objectives
1. Teaching & Curriculum: Teach and continuously improve courses that support urban forestry education and workforce development, including two courses to be developed with consultation of our forestry faculty, and one additional course to be determined based on programmatic needs and faculty expertise.
2. Experiential Learning: Create and expand experiential, field-based, and community-engaged learning opportunities that prepare students for careers in urban forestry and related professions.
3. Student Advising: Advise and mentor undergraduate and graduate students consistent with SENR and CFAES expectations.
4. Inclusive Learning Environments: Cultivate supportive and inclusive learning environments that promote student engagement, belonging, and success.
5. Curricular Leadership: Provide leadership in the development and growth of urban forestry education and contribute to programs that meet state, regional, and national workforce needs.
6. Outreach & Extension Program Development: Develop and deliver impactful extension and outreach programming that meets the needs of public agencies, nonprofit organizations, industry partners, and community stakeholders across Ohio.
7. Extension Collaboration: Collaborate with Extension professionals within SENR, CFAES, and OSU Extension to share evidence-based and practice-oriented knowledge related to urban forestry.
8. Service: Serve SENR, CFAES, the university, and the urban forestry profession through committee work and other service activities.
9. Collaborative Engagement: Build and maintain partnerships with municipalities, park districts, state agencies, utility companies, consulting firms, nonprofit organizations, and community stakeholders to advance urban forestry education and practice.
Education and Experience Requirements
Required:
Earned doctorate or other terminal degree along with equivalent experience in Urban Forestry, Forestry, Arboriculture, Natural Resources, Environmental Science, Landscape Architecture, Urban Planning, or a closely related field.
Demonstrated expertise in urban forestry, community forestry, arboriculture, natural resource management, green infrastructure, or a related field through professional practice, academic training, teaching, Extension, outreach, scholarship, or other relevant activities.
Evidence of excellence, or strong potential for excellence, in teaching, mentoring, and advising students.
Demonstrated ability to build and maintain effective working relationships with diverse academic, professional, governmental, industry, and community partners.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Desired (though not required):
ISA Certified Arborist and/or other relevant professional credentials.
Experience developing partnerships with public agencies, nonprofit organizations, industry partners, and community stakeholders.
Experience designing, implementing, or supporting experiential, workforce-oriented, community-engaged educational programs and/or Extension programming.
Experience applying GIS, remote sensing, inventory methods, LiDAR, or other technologies to support urban forest planning, assessment, and management
Additional Information:
How to Apply
To be considered, please submit your application electronically via Workday. Application materials should be compiled into one PDF and include the following documentation in this order:
Required:
Cover letter- Describe your qualifications, area(s) of expertise, career goals, and alignment with desired qualifications and preferred qualifications where applicable
Curriculum Vita (CV)
Statement of Teaching and Mentoring (no more than 2 pages)
Statement of Service/Outreach (no more than 2 pages)
Names/contact information of three references ( Note: Letters of reference are expected to be solicited prior to advancing to the next stage of the hiring process; inform your references when you apply so that letters can be finalized at/soon after time of request )
Initial consideration will be given to applications received by Friday November 20, 2026. Review of applications will continue until the position has been filled. We welcome informal inquiries, which can be made by contacting Search Committee Chair Dr. Alia Dietsch at Dietsch.29@osu.edu.
Department/School Information
Since its inception in 1968, the School of Environment and Natural Resources (SENR) has evolved and changed to meet the changing needs and demands of society, students, and the various natural resource professions. SENR has become more of an interdisciplinary program that addresses the natural resources sciences for the well-being of society and the biosphere. The School’s foundation is its interdisciplinarity, coupling the natural sciences with the social sciences and human dimensions of sustainable natural resources management for the well-being of people and society.
The School’s vision is a productive society in harmony with a sustainable and healthy environment. SENR will be guided by the enduring vision of a productive society whose use of its resources is in harmony with an environment that is sustainably managed with a deeply held stewardship ethic.
The mission of SENR is to enhance and impart knowledge of natural and social systems and their essential relationships in the context of natural resource use and management and to continuously improve the academic strength of the School through effective teaching, including extension teaching, sound research, and hiring the best possible faculty. Subsequently, the School’s overarching goals are to 1) provide leadership, 2) educate students and the public, and 3) generate new knowledge through research and integrate new and existing knowledge/data sets in order for individuals and society to utilize and manage natural resources in an environmentally compatible and socially acceptable manner.
These goals are achieved through the development and application of science- and research-based management strategies, practices, and policies. These goals are also achieved by hiring high quality faculty who execute effective scholarship in all its forms for a variety of disciplines and programs that integrate the natural and social sciences. The School provides the academic home where natural sciences and social sciences are brought together to address these goals.
The College
The College of Food, Agricultural, and Environmental Sciences (CFAES) anchors its mission in a simple, yet powerful phrase: We Sustain Life. Faculty, staff and students alike contribute to this mission in a variety of ways. Our Strategic Alignment outlines the colleges values. These values, which align with the university’s Shared Values, shape our goals of our Strategic Alignment. We are committed to scholarship across three mission areas (teaching, research, Extension) with a commitment to serving our state in addition to the country and world. As a land grant, we are part of a cooperative structure that includes key partners all dedicated to integrating research, education, and Extension to improve the food and agricultural sectors, the environment, and the quality of people’s lives. We educate not just undergraduate and graduate students but learners across the lifespan. We work to ensure groundbreaking scientific discoveries are brought out of the laboratory and into the hands of those who can put them to work.
CFAES houses 11 departments/schools with over 20 undergraduate majors and 9 graduate programs, including 3 interdisciplinary programs affiliated with multiple Ohio State colleges. We also administer OSU Extension, which provides robust and relevant programming to Ohioans and beyond in the areas of Agriculture and Natural Resources, 4-H Youth Development, Family and Consumer Sciences, and Community Development. We are one college spanning three campuses: Columbus, CFAES Wooster, and Statewide. Our CFAES Wooster campus includes a large research station and Ohio State’s only two-year academic unit, Ohio State ATI. The Statewide campus includes 11 research stations and Extension offices in all of Ohio’s 88 counties. Our At a Glance provides additional information regarding our size, capacity, and impact as a college.
The University
Ohio State is a top-20 public university, and its Ohio State Wexner Medical Center is one of America’s leading academic health centers. Job Title:Assistant Professor – Department of Neurology – Tenure Track
Department:Medicine | Neurology
Tenure faculty (regardless of rank) - persons with the titles of professor, associate professor, assistant professor and instructor who serve on appointments totaling 50% or more service to the university and who are eligible for tenure or who have obtained tenure. Duties and responsibilities are assigned in accordance with the workload guidelines laid out in the pattern of administration of each faculty member’s tenure initiation unit (TIU) and, as appropriate, regional campus; obligations will include research, service and/or teaching or clinical practice. These faculty will have earned doctorate or other terminal degree in the relevant field of study or possession of equivalent experience.
Additional Information:
The Ohio State University College of Medicine and the Wexner Medical Center seeks an Assistant Professor to join the Department of Neurology Academic rank and track commensurate with academic record and experience.
Position Overview
The Department of Neurology is seeking applications from exceptional candidates for a tenure-track position in basic/translational neuroscience anticipated to be appointed at the Assistant Professor level. This faculty candidate will complement and add to our departmental expertise in basic and translational neuroscience research. In particular, the successful candidate will be expected to lead a funded preclinical research program with a focus on axon biology related to neurodegeneration.
Department/Division Overview
The Department of Neurology at the Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center (OSUWMC) consists of 15 specialized divisions, 63 physicians, 5 psychologists, 12 dedicated research faculty, 24 residents, and 14 fellows. We deliver unparalleled subspecialty care across all neurology disciplines, with services spanning 7 state-of-the-art ambulatory facilities and 3 hospitals. The department operates 27 groundbreaking multidisciplinary and personalized clinics, 3 comprehensive inpatient consultation services, an 18-bed neurocritical care unit, a 30-bed stroke ward, and an expanding teleneurology service partnering with 7 regional hospitals. Our telestroke network is among the largest in the nation, encompassing 32 affiliated hospitals. With over $15.5 million in annual research funding, OSU Neurology is at the forefront of discovering new biomarkers and therapeutic targets for neurological disorders. Our fundamental research portfolio focuses on neurogenetics, neuroimmunology and neuroregenerative medicine. Our pioneering Division of Neurology Health Services Research and Center for the Neurobiology of Aging and Resilience are trailblazers in the field. This year alone, our faculty conducted over 320 clinical trials and studies, supported by a cutting-edge biorepository and brain bank. We're equally committed to education, offering 10 prestigious clinical fellowships and international training opportunities through the OSU Global Neurology Initiative, with partner programs in Africa, the Middle East, and Latin America. In 2024, our Neurology Residency Program was ranked in the top 15th percentile nationwide on the Doximity Residency Navigator list. At OSUWMC Neurology faculty participate in a vibrant culture that is actively shaping the future of neurological care and research.
Duties and Responsibilities
Tenure faculty (regardless of rank) - persons with the titles of professor, associate professor, assistant professor and instructor who serve on appointments totaling 50% or more service to the university and who are eligible for tenure or who have obtained tenure. Duties and responsibilities are assigned in accordance with the workload guidelines laid out in the pattern of administration of each faculty member’s tenure initiation unit (TIU) and, as appropriate, regional campus; obligations will include research, service and/or teaching or clinical practice. These faculty will have earned doctorate or other terminal degree in the relevant field of study or possession of equivalent experience.
This is a tenure track research position being hired by the Department of Neurology/College of Medicine.
Duties and Responsibilities
Each faculty member is expected to perform the full range of responsibilities in the areas of funded research, teaching, scholarship, and service under the oversight of the Department Chair. Active participation in divisional, departmental, and/or college committee functions is expected. Participation in local, regional, national, and international professional organizations is also expected. This position is a research focused tenure track faculty position at the Assistant Professor level focused on preclinical research related to neurological diseases (specifically on axon degeneration).
Requirements
Doctorate (PhD or equivalent) in Neuroscience or related field.
High-quality and high-impact research that is evident by a strong publication record in peer-reviewed journals and grant writing experience
High-quality education and mentoring experience that is evident from student mentoring and achievements of mentored students, teaching feedback, and presentation skills
A record of advising, mentoring, motivating, and impacting students from all backgrounds, including students from underrepresented groups
Competitive peer-reviewed extramural research funding.
Demonstrated ability to attract and mentor graduate students.
A commitment to engage in research, teaching, and/or outreach and engagement that reflect Ohio State’s Shared Values
Desired:
Current K-award, R01 or equivalent independent grant funding is highly desired.
How to Apply
To be considered, please submit your application electronically via Workday. Application materials must include cover letter and Curriculum Vita. All inquiries and nominations should be directed in confidence to: Anna Godwin, Research Faculty Recruiter, Anna.Godwin@osumc.edu
Faculty Defined
Clinical faculty (regardless of rank) - Persons with titles of assistant professor-clinical, associate professor-clinical and professor-clinical. These faculty will have earned a doctor of medicine (MD), doctorate (PhD) or other terminal degree in the relevant field. Clinical faculty members are not eligible for tenure and are appointed for terms of three to five years. They may be reappointed to successive terms. Their principal career focus is the delivery of exemplary clinical care, and may include teaching, and/or research.
Tenure-Track faculty (regardless of rank) - Persons with the titles of assistant professor, associate professor, or professor who are eligible for tenure or who have obtained tenure. These faculty will have earned a doctorate (PhD), Doctor of Medicine (MD) or other terminal degree in the relevant field of study. Their primary career focus centers on research, service, and teaching. Tenure-track faculty with MD or MD/PhD degrees may also be involved in clinical care.
Research Faculty (regardless of rank) - Persons with the titles of research assistant professor, research associate professor, or research professor. These faculty will have earned a doctorate (PhD) or other terminal degree in the relevant field of study. Research faculty members are not eligible for tenure and are appointed for terms of one to five years. Their principal career focus is research.
The Ohio State University College of Medicine
The Ohio State University College of Medicine, with more than 5,000 learners, is the only academic medical center in central Ohio. Ranked as the 28th Best Medical School – Research, 40th Best Medical School – Primary Care, and 13th Most Diverse Medical School by U.S. News & World Report, it is known nationwide for curricular innovation, pioneering research, and outstanding patient care at The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center. With more than 2,600 faculty members, the college comprises 20 clinical departments, eight basic science departments and a School of Health and Rehabilitation Sciences.
The Wexner Medical Center
The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center consists of The Ohio State University Health System, the College of Medicine, the Health Sciences Library and the Faculty Group Practice. The Ohio State Wexner Medical Center is committed to providing world-class care. At the Ohio State Wexner Medical Center, we're proud to be celebrating our 31st consecutive year ranked in the U.S. News & World Report Best Hospitals list. This year, the Ohio State Wexner Medical Center has 10 nationally ranked specialties out of 15 and two selected as high performing. U.S. News & World Report consistently ranks the Ohio State Wexner Medical Center as the top hospital in Columbus. The Wexner Medical Center is rated as high performing in 14 out of 20 common procedures and conditions, including abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, aortic valve surgery, heart attack, heart bypass surgery and heart failure.

Ohio State is a top-20 public university, and its Ohio State Wexner Medical Center is one of America’s leading academic health centers and recently ranked No. 4 on Forbes’ list of best U.S. employers for diversity. Eligible Ohio State employees receive comprehensive benefits packages, including medical, dental and vision insurance, tuition assistance for employees and their dependents, and state or alternative retirement options with competitive employer contributions.

Department:
The Ohio State University College of Medicine and the Wexner Medical Center seek a clinical psychologist to join the Department of Urology. Academic rank and track commensurate with academic record and experience.
Position Overview
The Urologic Hospitalist is a specialized physician responsible for providing comprehensive inpatient care for patients with acute and chronic urological conditions. This role involves diagnosing, treating and managing a variety of urological disorders in a hospital setting and directing the urology inpatient consult service which extends to the Emergency Room and the Operating Room. A urologic hospitalist plays a crucial role in bridging the gap between specialized urologic care and comprehensive inpatient management, ensuring that patients receive the highest quality of care during their hospital stay. The practice is supported by a mid-level urology resident and two advanced practice providers.
Department Overview
The Department of Urology at The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center is nationally recognized by U.S. News & World Report (#82) for delivering the highest quality of care for the treatment of urologic conditions. Our mission is to alleviate patient suffering from urologic disorders through an integrative model of extraordinary clinical care, patient-centered discovery and educational innovation in service of the citizens of Ohio and beyond. Our vision is to transform the lives of our patients through this comprehensive approach to urologic practice. The Department of Urology has a rich history and timeline dating back to 1917. Under the leadership of Cheryl Lee, MD, as chair, the Department is composed of six specialty Divisions with 21 adult faculty members and 13 advanced practice providers. Collectively, the Department performs nearly 20,000 clinic and operative procedures, annually. Seven pediatric urologists at Nationwide Children’s Hospital have academic appointments in the Department. Clinical care, research, education, and community service are major priorities, and the Department is engaged in multicenter and multispecialty initiatives. The Department sponsors fellowship programs in Endourology (Endourological Society) and Urologic Oncology (Society of Urologic Oncology) while Nationwide Children’s Hospital sponsors a fellowship in pediatric urology (Society for Pediatric Urology).
Duties and Responsibilities
• Performs surgical procedures where assigned.
• Provides direct and indirect patient care services in the inpatient setting
• Interviews, obtains and reviews medical history of patients; performs physical examinations to access medical or surgical needs; orders special procedures, diagnostic testing, and other ancillary services; responds to consultation requests; determines, prescribes and implements treatment plans and/or medications required; documents all services and instructions provided in the medical record; educates patients and promotes wellness, prevention and early detection by providing materials, resources and services to patients and their families; responds and maintains open communication with referring physicians.
• Maintains accurate and detailed medical records for all patients, ensuring compliance with hospital policies and regulatory standards.
•Participate in peer reviews and audits to ensure the highest standards of care are maintained.
•Participate in hospital quality improvement initiatives aimed at enhancing patient care and outcomes in the urology department.
•Ensures continuing medical educational requirements are met; participates in department, college, and medical center committees and other service activities.
•Serves as preceptor and provides training of residents, fellows, and students, as well as other members of the health professions team including advanced practice providers.
•Performs other duties and/or call assignments as defined by the Chair or her designee.
Requirements
Medical Doctor (MD) or Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine (DO)
•Licensed or license eligible for State of Ohio and DEA licensure
•Board certified or board eligible by the American Board of Urology
•Qualify for appointment at the Assistant, Associate or Professor level
•Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with residents, faculty members, and other stakeholders
•Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously
•Commitment to maintaining high standards of resident education and fostering a positive learning environment

These faculty will have earned a doctorate (PhD), Doctor of Medicine (MD), Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine (DO) or other terminal degree in the relevant field of study. Their primary career focus centers on research, service, and teaching. Tenure-track faculty with MD, DO or MD/PhD degrees may also be involved in clinical care.
Research Faculty (regardless of rank) - Persons with the titles of research assistant professor, research associate professor, or research professor. These faculty will have earned a doctorate (PhD) or other terminal degree in the relevant field of study. Research faculty members are not eligible for tenure and are appointed for terms of one to five years. Their principal career focus is research.
The Ohio State University College of Medicine
The Ohio State University College of Medicine, with more than 5,000 learners, is the only academic medical center in central Ohio. Recognized as a Tier 1 school for research in the 2025–2026 U.S. News & World Report “Best Medical Schools” list, it ranks among the top 16 medical schools for research in the nation. It also remains in Tier 2 for primary care, further demonstrating its strength across the academic spectrum. Known for its innovative curriculum, cutting-edge research, and excellence in clinical care through The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center, the college continues to advance its mission of education, discovery and community impact. With more than 2,700 faculty across 20 clinical departments, eight basic science departments, and the School of Health and Rehabilitation Sciences, Ohio State is shaping the future of academic medicine - locally, nationally and globally.
The Wexner Medical Center
The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center consists of The Ohio State University Health System, the College of Medicine, the Health Sciences Library and the Faculty Group Practice. The Ohio State Wexner Medical Center is committed to providing world-class care. At the Ohio State Wexner Medical Center, we're proud to be celebrating our 33rd consecutive year ranked in the U.S. News & World Report Best Hospitals list. This year, the Ohio State Wexner Medical Center has 9 nationally ranked specialties out of 15 and four selected as high performing. U.S. News & World Report consistently ranks the Ohio State Wexner Medical Center as the top hospital in Columbus. The Wexner Medical Center is rated as high performing in 17 out of 22 common procedures and conditions, including abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, aortic valve surgery, arrhythmia, COPD, colon cancer surgery, diabetes, gynecological cancer surgery, heart attack, heart failure, kidney failure, leukemia, lymphoma and myeloma, lung cancer surgery, pacemaker implantation, pneumonia, prostate cancer, spinal fusion, and transcatheter aortic valve replacement. Our new hospital tower, opened in February, 2026, is the largest single facilities project ever undertaken at Ohio State. It’s designed to enhance a unified Ohio State Wexner Medical Center campus providing world-class patient care, leading-edge research and outstanding clinical training.
• 820 large, private rooms to elevate patient-centered care, nearly doubling the number of beds we have today
• Enhanced connections between the new inpatient hospital and the OSUCCC – James
• More than half an acre of terrace space and a quarter acre of green space for a small park
• 148 additional beds for patients of the OSUCCC – James
• 51 neonatal intensive care unit bassinets
• State-of-the-art diagnostic, treatment and inpatient service areas; imaging; operating rooms; and critical care and medical/surgical beds
The University
Ohio State is a top-20 public university, and its Ohio State Wexner Medical Center is one of America’s leading academic health centers and recently ranked No. 4 on Forbes’ list of best U.S. employers for diversity. Eligible Ohio State employees receive comprehensive benefits packages, including medical, dental and vision insurance, tuition assistance for employees and their dependents, and state or alternative retirement options with competitive employer contributions. Ohio State is a dynamic community where opportunity thrives, and individuals transform themselves and their world. Positions are available in countless fields and specialties. Become a Buckeye and contribute to an incredible legacy that serves to guide our future and shape a better tomorrow.
The Ohio State University is committed to enhancing academic excellence. Recruiting, supporting, and retaining faculty of the highest caliber is a core component of this commitment. The Office of Academic Affairs (OAA) has established Dual Careers and Faculty Relocation (DCFR) to focus on supporting new and prospective faculty and their loved ones. Service offerings include dual careers partner consultations, identifying potential employers and/or employment opportunities, consultation and resources related to relocation, as well as identifying opportunities to engage on campus and in the surrounding community. While employment opportunities are not guaranteed, resources and consultation are provided to support the partners of new and prospective faculty as they are considering or transitioning to The Ohio State University.
In addition to being responsive to dual-career opportunities, we strongly promote work-life balance to support our community members through a suite of institutionalized policies. Ohio State is an NSF ADVANCE institution and a member of the Ohio/Western Pennsylvania/West Virginia Higher Education Recruitment Consortium (HERC).
Columbus, Ohio
Located in Ohio’s capital city, Ohio State’s Columbus campus is near the center of a rapidly growing and diverse metropolitan area with a population of over 1.5 million. The area offers a wide range of affordable housing, many cultural and recreational opportunities, excellent schools, and a strong economy based on government as well as service, transportation, and technology industries. Additional information about the Columbus area is available here. In addition to its Columbus campus, Ohio State has four regional campuses including Ohio State Lima, Ohio State Mansfield, Ohio State Marion, and Ohio State Newark, in addition to Ohio State ATI in Wooster.
Location:Twelfth Ave, 395 W (0356)
Position Type:Regular
Shift:First Shift
Final candidates are subject to successful completion of a background check. A drug screen or physical may be required during the post offer process.
Thank you for your interest in positions at The Ohio State University and Wexner Medical Center. Once you have applied, the most updated information on the status of your application can be found by visiting the Candidate Home section of this site. Please view your submitted applications by logging in and reviewing your status. For answers to additional questions please review the frequently asked questions.
The university is an equal opportunity employer, including veterans and disability.

jobs.description:
Job Details
