jobs.title: Regional Program Coord./Clinical Asst or Assoc Professor - Wichita
jobs.description:
Job Details
Position OverviewThe School of Pharmacy seeks a full-time, non‑tenure‑track faculty member at the rank of Clinical Assistant or Associate Professor to deliver high-quality learning experiences and education for students in the PharmD program. The successful candidate will engage in teaching, service, and scholarly activities, and will work collaboratively with the Director of Experiential Education, Department of Pharmacy Practice, and colleagues in the School of Pharmacy. Additionally, the faculty member will provide mentorship to students and contribute to the visibility, impact, and reputation of the University and its programs through scholarly engagement.
In addition to faculty responsibilities, this position will serve as the Regional Program Coordinator for Region 2 (Wichita, Salina, and Western Kansas). This role is responsible for the comprehensive coordination and support of experiential education sites and preceptors within the region. This work is essential to ensuring high-quality experiential learning experiences through effective site management, preceptor engagement, and continuous quality improvement. The role requires close collaboration with experiential education leadership, preceptors, and practice sites to support student learning and program outcomes.
The selected candidate will also have responsibilities teaching laboratory and didactic courses within the Department of Pharmacy Practice. Subject matter expertise may include, but is not limited to, ambulatory care, community pharmacy, internal medicine, oncology, critical care, pediatrics, cardiology, or related areas. Rank and salary will be commensurate with experience. This is a full-time, 12-month, faculty position with required travel. The position will travel to visit preceptors in Wichita, Salina, and Western Kansas. This position will have set in-person days on the University of Kansas Wichita campus and/or hybrid flexibility aligned with experiential education program needs.
The Clinical Assistant/Associate Professor position is subject to a collective bargaining agreement between The University of Kansas and United Academics. UAKU is the exclusive representative for the bargaining unit, and it is the candidate’s right to be a member or not be a member of a union without fear of personal or professional repercussions.
Culture and Community:
KU’s excellence is a result of the rich tapestry of experiences, perspectives, and backgrounds of our faculty, staff, students, and colleagues from across our nation and the globe. At KU, we invest in continuous learning and growth by creating a climate where people engage in respectful dialogue and debate and support each other’s success. We foster a culture of care where each person is seen, heard and valued. When people feel a true sense of belonging, we believe they are better able to reach their full potential and achieve remarkable things. The successful candidate must be eligible to work in the U.S. by the effective date of the appointment.
Please note that a second Preceptor/Clinical Professor located in Lawrence, KS has been posted and interested applicants should apply here.Job DescriptionPreceptor Support Coordinator – Region 2 (Wichita, Salina, Western KS)
60%
Development, coordination, and ongoing management of student rotation schedules
Maintenance, onboarding, and support of experiential rotation sites
Oversight and management of experiential education policies, procedures, and rotation syllabi
Coordination of assessment and quality improvement initiatives for preceptors and experiential sites
Utilization and optimization of experiential education management systems and departmental websites
Preceptor recruitment and retention activities, including site development and in‑person site visits
Design and implementation of preceptor development programs and educational initiatives
Ongoing preceptor and site relationship management, including issue resolution and problem-solving
Maintains an ongoing understanding of contemporary pharmacy practice, healthcare delivery, and clinical standards to effectively mentor student pharmacists and support high-quality experiential education.
Clinical Assistant/Associate Professor in Pharmacy Practice
25% Teaching
Responsible for instruction, assessment, remediation, and course coordination for didactic and active-learning laboratory courses in the Pharmacy School curriculum for the PharmD program.
Delivery of didactic, laboratory and/or elective instruction in the PharmD program as assigned by the Chair of Pharmacy Practice
Participate in and provide support to interprofessional education activities, as assigned
Participate in and provide support to objective structured learning examination/objective structured clinical examination activities
Earn Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) Instructor Certification in order to provide Basic Life Support training to pharmacy students on the KU Wichita Campus.
10% Service
Serve on department, school, and/or university committees, as assigned
Participate in regional, state, and/or national professional organizations through committee service and volunteer activities
Support student engagement in outreach activities such as health fairs and service initiatives
Contribute to faculty recruitment efforts through participation on search committees, as assigned
Build and sustain productive relationships with professional organizations and partners within the healthcare and pharmacy sectors
Support student development through academic advising, professional mentorship, and active involvement with student organizations and professional societies.
5% Research/Scholarship
Participate in research and scholarship resulting in conference presentations and abstracts, peer-reviewed published manuscripts, peer-reviewed instructional materials, textbook chapters, or invited lectures or presentations.
Research may include any type of practice- or educational-based research, with funding as needed to support the research.
Research support may be obtained via direct grant or contract.
Required QualificationsAs demonstrated by application materials, work history, or interview.
For those applying at the Assistant Clinical Professor level:
A terminal degree in Pharmacy (Doctor of Pharmacy from an ACPE accredited school. For pre-2000 graduates, a BS degree is considered terminal.) OR a Doctor of Philosophy in a health or healthcare related field.
Record of effectiveness in teaching
Experience in Experiential Education or equivalent
Two years of management or leadership experience providing supervising and direction to others.
Strategic vision for experiential education or learning.
Experience with databases
Demonstrated excellence in mentorship or precepting evidenced by evaluations or other written communications
Excellent organizational and communication skills
Record of scholarly activities commensurate with an academic appointment
Evidence of professional leadership, teaching excellence and team management skills
Must be licensed as a registered pharmacist in the State of Kansas or must obtain licensure through the Kansas State Board of Pharmacy within 90 days of start date.
Track record of effectiveness in clinical pharmacy practice
For those applying at the rank of Associate Clinical Professor, all above listed requirements for the Assistant Clinical level apply as well as the following:
A strong documented record of teaching, leadership, scholarship, and service accomplishments.
Preferred Qualifications
Minimum of two years of non-residency work experience in direct patient care
Minimum of two years of teaching experience at the college/university level
Additional Candidate InstructionsA complete online application includes the following materials: (1) cover letter; (2) Curriculum vitae; (3) teaching philosophy statement; and (4) the names, email and contact information for three professional references.
Review of applications will begin November 12th and continues until a qualified pool of applicants is identified.Contact Information to ApplicantsJim Backes, jbackes@kumc.eduAdvertised Salary RangeCommensurate with experienceApplication Review BeginsThursday November 12, 2026Anticipated Start DateFriday January 1, 2027Apply to Job

jobs.title: Assistant/Associate/Full Professor in Architectural Engineering
jobs.description:
Job Details
Position OverviewThe University of Kansas (KU) Department of Civil, Environmental and Architectural Engineering (CEAE) seeks outstanding candidates for two tenured or tenure-track faculty positions, one at the rank of Assistant Professor and a second position at the rank of Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor in architectural engineering. The focus areas for these positions are in building electrical power systems and the broader energy areas described below. The successful candidates are expected to contribute to the continued development of academic and research programs in architectural engineering and to the broader research community.
For the building electrical power systems position, relevant expertise may include building electrical power distribution and utilization; electrical system design for commercial and institutional buildings; power quality, reliability, and resilience; emergency and standby power systems; distributed energy resources and microgrids; grid modernization; smart building electrical systems; and advanced sensing, monitoring, and controls for building power systems. The successful candidate in this area will strengthen the program's research and teaching capacity in building electrical and power systems and contribute to engagement with industry and the profession.
The broader energy areas of interest include integrated building or district energy systems; building-to-grid integration and grid-interactive buildings; distributed energy resource management; building energy resilience; building energy efficiency and decarbonization; environmentally sustainable buildings; renewable energy systems for buildings and communities; grid reliability and energy infrastructure; and net-zero-energy buildings.
Successful candidates must have an earned doctorate in architectural, mechanical, electrical, or civil engineering or a closely related discipline by the time of appointment. Candidates must demonstrate the potential to develop collaborative, externally funded research programs and to design and teach high-quality undergraduate and graduate courses. The anticipated starting date is August 18, 2027. Successful candidates must be eligible to work in the U.S. prior to the start of the position.
These positions are subject to a collective bargaining agreement between the University of Kansas and the United Academics of KU, the exclusive representative for the bargaining unit. Faculty have the right to be a member or not be a member of UAKU without fear of personal or professional repercussions.
The University of Kansas School of Engineering (http://engr.ku.edu/) has undergone a significant expansion while taking explicit care to maintain and improve the high-quality student programs the university is known for. The effort involved a multifaceted approach aimed at growing our facilities, faculty, leadership, and research and, most importantly, supporting students. It also helps industry partners find the new talent, designs, and techniques they need to fuel economic growth and business success.
The CEAE Department (https://ceae.ku.edu/) currently has 26 tenured/tenure-track faculty, four teaching professors and professors of practice, one research professor, and approximately 360 undergraduate students and 140 graduate students, with programs leading to bachelor’s, master's, and doctoral degrees. The department has a strong history of conducting impactful research while focusing on the success of students at all levels. KU's ABET-accredited architectural engineering program benefits from the university's close proximity to the Kansas City metro area, which is home to one of the nation’s largest concentrations of architectural, engineering, and construction firms. This location provides rich opportunities for industry engagement, research partnerships, and student learning.Job DescriptionThe University of Kansas is the state’s flagship university, an R-1 institution and one of just 71 invited members of the prestigious Association of American Universities. Our university consistently earns high rankings for academics and recognition as a premier research university (engaging in $611 million of research in fiscal year 2025). KU offers more than 8,000 courses, 460 degree and certificate programs, and more than 200 fields of study. As of Fall 2025, student enrollment for the Lawrence-Edwards campus was 27,212 representing all 50 states and 115 countries.
KU’s excellence is a result of the rich tapestry of experiences, perspectives, and backgrounds of our faculty, staff, students, and colleagues from across our nation and the globe. At KU, we invest in continuous learning and growth by creating a climate where people engage in respectful dialogue and debate and support each other’s success. We foster a culture of care where each person is seen, heard and valued. When people feel a true sense of belonging, we believe they are better able to reach their full potential and achieve remarkable things. The successful candidate must be eligible to work in the U.S. by the effective date of the appointment.
Job Description:
40% Teaching
Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in architectural engineering. Develop courses and participate in curriculum development. Supervise and mentor undergraduate and graduate students throughout the course of their studies.
40% Research
Develop and conduct an innovative research program in building electrical power systems or one of the broader energy areas associated with the positions. Relevant areas include building electrical power systems; integrated building or district energy systems; building-to-grid integration and grid-interactive buildings; distributed energy resource management; grid modernization; building energy resilience; building energy efficiency and decarbonization; environmentally sustainable buildings; renewable energy systems for buildings and communities; grid reliability and energy infrastructure; and net-zero-energy buildings. Establish a strong research agenda leading to external grant support and publication in recognized refereed journals, and participate in local, national, and international professional conferences and other activities appropriate to the discipline. Supervise M.S. and Ph.D. studies.
20% Service
Perform service activities normally expected of university faculty commensurate with rank, including committee service to the Department, School, and University. Also includes national and international service to the profession.Required QualificationsAll ranks:
Earned doctorate in architectural, mechanical, electrical, or civil engineering or a closely-related discipline by the time of appointment.
Demonstrable expertise in one or more of the following areas: building electrical power systems; integrated building or district energy systems; building-to-grid integration and grid-interactive buildings; distributed energy resource management; grid modernization; building energy resilience; building energy efficiency and decarbonization; environmentally sustainable buildings; renewable energy systems for buildings and communities; grid reliability and energy infrastructure; or net-zero-energy buildings. Candidates considered for the building electrical power systems position must demonstrate expertise in that area and the ability to contribute to architectural engineering coursework in building electrical systems and power engineering.
Ability to communicate ideas effectively and work well with others as demonstrated through application materials and interview.
Demonstrated potential to develop an externally-funded research program and to design and teach high-quality undergraduate and graduate courses.
At the rank of Associate Professor:
Sustained record of scholarship and research;
Evidence of national recognition in the field;
Demonstrated experience in leading multidisciplinary teams;
A minimum of five years of post-Ph.D. professional experience in a faculty role or an equivalent combination of academic and relevant industry/practice experience.
At the rank of Professor:
Sustained record of scholarship and research;
Evidence of national and international recognition in the field;
Demonstrated experience in leading multidisciplinary teams;
A minimum of ten years of post-Ph.D. professional experience in a faculty role or an equivalent combination of academic and relevant industry/practice experience, with a sustained record of leadership.
Additional Candidate InstructionsA complete online application includes the following materials: (1) cover letter, including an indication of the position or positions for which the applicant wishes to be considered (2) curriculum vitae; (3) research agenda (2-page limit); (4) teaching philosophy statement (2-page limit); and (5) the names and contact information, including email addresses, for three professional references.
Application review will begin November 13, 2026, and will continue until a pool of qualified applicants is received.Contact Information to ApplicantsWill Lindquist

Position OverviewThe University of Kansas (KU) Department of Civil, Environmental and Architectural Engineering (CEAE) seeks an outstanding individual for a tenure-track open rank position in environmental engineering, with a specialty in wastewater engineering. The successful candidate will contribute to the continued development of the department's academic and research programs in environmental engineering and to KU's broader research community.
This search is focused on candidates whose scholarship advances wastewater engineering. Relevant areas may include, but are not limited to, advanced physical, chemical, and biological treatment processes; resource and energy recovery; water reuse; emerging contaminants; environmental biotechnology and microbiology; decentralized treatment; process modeling, sensing, automation, and optimization; and resilient and sustainable wastewater systems. The successful candidate will have an earned doctorate in environmental engineering, civil engineering, chemical engineering, or a closely related discipline by the time of appointment. Candidates must demonstrate the potential to develop a collaborative, externally funded research program and to design and teach high-quality undergraduate and graduate courses. The anticipated starting date is August 18, 2027. The successful candidate must be eligible to work in the U.S. prior to the start of the position.
This position is subject to a collective bargaining agreement between the University of Kansas and the United Academics of KU, the exclusive representative for the bargaining unit. Faculty have the right to be a member or not be a member of UAKU without fear of personal or professional repercussions.
About the School of Engineering:
The University of Kansas School of Engineering (http://engr.ku.edu/) has undergone a significant expansion while taking explicit care to maintain and improve the high-quality student programs the university is known for. The effort involved a multi-faceted approach aimed at growing our facilities, faculty, leadership, and research and, most importantly, supporting students. It also helps industry partners find the new talent, designs, and techniques they need to fuel economic growth and business success.

The department has a strong history of conducting impactful research while focusing on the success of students at all levels. The department hosts state-of-the-art research facilities, including greenhouse and piloting facilities, and has long collaborated with regional municipalities, with conventional and advanced nutrient recovery facilities (Bardenpho processes). Our close proximity to the Kansas City metro area, which is home to one of the nation’s largest concentrations of architectural, engineering, and construction firms. About Lawrence, KS:

Home to over 95,000 people, Lawrence is located 45 minutes west of Kansas City and 30 minutes east of Topeka, the state capital. jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Artificial Intelligence
jobs.description:
Job Details
Job Title:
Assistant Professor of Artificial Intelligence
Position Number:
977278, 977301
Department:
Computer Science
Salary:
Commensurate with qualifications and experience
Remote:
No
Job Summary:
The Department of Computer Science at Angelo State University invites applications for the full-time, nine-month, tenure-track Assistant Professor position in Artificial Intelligence, beginning in August 2027. The successful candidate will support undergraduate and graduate programs in Artificial Intelligence and Computer Science and contribute to the interdisciplinary mission of the university’s AI Center of Excellence through teaching, research, student mentoring, curriculum development, and engagement with external partners.
Applications are encouraged from candidates across a broad range of artificial intelligence areas, including technical, applied, and human-centered AI. Relevant areas may include machine learning, generative AI, natural language processing, computer vision, robotics, autonomous systems, edge and embedded AI, AI hardware and systems, human-AI collaboration, AI literacy and education, responsible AI, and interdisciplinary applications of AI.
The faculty member will normally teach three courses per semester, maintain an active research agenda, pursue external funding, mentor students, and collaborate across disciplines on AI-related research and educational initiatives. The academic appointment, tenure home, and formal evaluation pathway are within the Department of Computer Science.
Essential Duties:
Teach three undergraduate and/or graduate courses per semester in artificial intelligence, computer science, data science, computer engineering, or related areas, as assigned by the Department Chair.
Develop and continuously improve courses, laboratories, assignments, and other instructional materials supporting Artificial Intelligence and Computer Science programs, and collaborate on interdisciplinary AI curriculum development.
Maintain an active research and scholarly agenda in artificial intelligence or an AI-related interdisciplinary field, including technical, applied, or human-centered AI.
Develop and submit proposals for external funding and participate in externally funded research, educational, or workforce-development initiatives.
Mentor undergraduate and graduate students in research, capstone projects, applied AI projects, professional development, and career preparation.
Contribute to the interdisciplinary mission of the AI Center of Excellence through collaboration across colleges and departments on AI-related research, educational initiatives, and student projects, including activities that advance AI literacy and responsible AI use.
Participate in departmental, college, and university service, including assessment, advising, recruitment, student success, committee work, outreach, and program development.
Contribute to developing appropriate partnerships with industry, government, educational institutions, and community organizations to support AI education, research, applied projects, and workforce development.
Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:
Knowledge
Knowledge of artificial intelligence concepts, methods, systems, and applications, with depth in one or more technical, applied, or human-centered areas.
Knowledge of current and emerging developments in artificial intelligence and their relevance to academic disciplines, professional practice, and workforce needs.
Knowledge of effective teaching practices, student-learning assessment, curriculum development, and instructional technology.
Knowledge of research methods and scholarly practices appropriate to the candidate’s area of expertise, including scholarly publication, grant development, and externally funded projects.
Knowledge of interdisciplinary approaches to AI research, education, and integration, including AI literacy and human-AI collaboration.
Knowledge of ethical, secure, responsible, and transparent uses of artificial intelligence, including privacy, bias, reliability, and societal impact.
Skills
Effective teaching and student-engagement skills at the undergraduate and graduate levels.
Research, scholarly writing, technical presentation, and grant-development skills appropriate to the candidate’s area of expertise.
Skills in developing and improving curricula, courses, laboratories, assignments, and applied AI projects.
Effective written, oral, and interpersonal communication skills, including communicating AI concepts to technical and nontechnical audiences.
Student mentoring, academic advising, and career-development skills.
Collaboration and partnership-development skills across academic disciplines, industry, government, educational institutions, and community organizations.
Abilities
Ability to teach courses in artificial intelligence, computer science, computer engineering, data science, or related areas.
Ability to maintain an active research agenda and produce scholarly contributions appropriate to the candidate’s area of expertise.
Ability to mentor students in research, capstone experiences, applied AI projects, and professional development.
Ability to teach effectively in face-to-face, online, or hybrid formats as assigned.
Ability to collaborate across colleges and departments on AI-related research, curriculum development, and educational initiatives.
Ability to contribute to the AI Center of Excellence through interdisciplinary projects, AI literacy activities, and engagement with external partners.
Ability to adapt teaching and research activities in response to evolving technologies and workforce needs.
Ability to contribute effectively to departmental, college, university, professional, and community service.
Minimum Qualifications:
An earned doctorate in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Data Science, or a closely related field from an accredited institution or international equivalent. ABD candidates will be considered, provided the doctorate is completed no later than September 1, 2027.
Academic preparation and expertise appropriate for teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in Artificial Intelligence, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or related areas.
Evidence of, or demonstrated potential for, effective university-level teaching and student mentoring.
Evidence of, or demonstrated potential for, an active research and scholarly agenda in artificial intelligence or an AI-related interdisciplinary field, including technical, applied, or human-centered AI.
Ability to collaborate across disciplines and contribute to the instructional, research, and service missions of the Department of Computer Science, the AI Center of Excellence, and the university.
Physical Requirements:
No physical requirements.
EEO Statement:
All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, or status as a protected veteran.

jobs.title: Associate Full Professor of Interactive Media
jobs.description:
Job Details
Associate/ Full Professor of Interactive Media
Film and Media Arts, School of Communication, American University
The School of Communication at American University (AU) in Washington, D.C., invites applications for a full-time, faculty position at the rank of associate or full professor, with an emphasis on interactive storytelling, worldbuilding, and/or playful design in the public interest. Depending on qualifications, the appointee may be recommended for tenure at the time of hiring. Candidates should hold a terminal degree as appropriate to their focus, such as an MFA or Ph.D. The salary range is from $105,000- $124,000.
The School of Communication (SOC) at American University engages the most pressing issues of our time through teaching, scholarship, and professional experiences in communication and media. In the Film and Media Arts division, our faculty and students make media that matters in and beyond one of the most dynamic and influential cities in the world.
The candidate is expected to work closely with or lead American University’s Game & Interactive Media Center, which is a world-class hub for experiential education, interactive storytelling, and computational media with a public purpose. While the Center is increasingly focused on undergraduate learning, its graduate programs were ranked #24 in the world by the Princeton Review in 2026, including the MA in Game Design and the MFA in Games and Interactive Media. The Center recently launched a new minor in Game Design, with one track for media studies students and another for those with an interest in computer science and game development.
The ideal candidate will be an outstanding media maker, educator, and curricular strategist. They should ideally be comfortable with many principles of good game design. The candidate’s practice in interactive media should connect to one or more domains in the public interest: the environment, health, urban and spatial planning, education, or social issue storytelling, and should interface with science communication and journalism, museums, nonprofits, etc. As more AI tools are integrated into production pipelines, the candidate should have some knowledge of where such tools are useful and how they can be guided, and be able to engage thoughtfully with students who are both AI resistant and AI enthusiasts. Job responsibilities may include teaching courses; directing undergraduate and graduate game programs; mentoring students; securing new partnerships and funding for original media projects and high-impact collaborations; and participating in School of Communication and University governance.
The position, which will begin in August of 2027, comes with powerful opportunities for collaboration with a tremendous mix of organizations in Washington, DC, from arts funders to policy think tanks to global nonprofits. Collaborating across the university with our world-class faculty is particularly well-suited to the Game & Interactive Media Center and is encouraged.
Consideration of applications will commence on November 1, 2026. Candidate interviews will begin in late 2026/early 2027 and continue until the position is filled. To apply, submit a letter of application, curriculum vitae, one letter of recommendation (two more letters will be requested for those who reach the interview stage), a teaching portfolio, optional creative portfolio, and optional excerpt of exemplary publications; finalist candidates will be asked for two letters of recommendation (likely to coincide with interviews). Please submit applications via Workday. Please contact the SOC Faculty Affairs Coordinator at 202-885-2133 or email facultyaffairs_SOC@american.edu if you have any questions.
For more about the School of Communication, please visit www.american.edu/soc. American University is an equal opportunity, affirmative action institution that operates in compliance with applicable laws and regulations. The university does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, religion, sex (including pregnancy), age, sexual orientation, disability, marital status, personal appearance, gender identity and expression, family responsibilities, political affiliation, source of income, veteran status, an individual’s genetic information or any other bases under federal or local laws (collectively “Protected Bases”) in its programs and activities.
American University is a tobacco- and smoke-free campus. Hiring offers for this position are contingent on the successful completion of a background check.
American University is required to comply with the Jeanne Clery Disclosure of Campus Security Policy and Campus Crime Statistics Act (Clery Act). In accordance with the Clery Act, each year American University prepares an Annual Security Report. This report contains campus crime statistics as well as descriptions of Public Safety's services. It is available to all applicants upon request by calling the Department of Public Safety at 202-885-2537 or the Annual Security Report is also available online.

SUMMARY
South Texas College is a comprehensive institution, which places primary emphasis on excellence in classroom instruction. Faculty members are expected to demonstrate and maintain competence in each of the following areas throughout their employment at the College.

Demonstrates a thorough and accurate knowledge of the field or discipline
Possesses appropriate educational/professional credentials to teach in field or discipline

Maintains currency in subject matter through professional development

Contributes to planning and development processes through appropriate channels

Facilitates recruitment and retention of students

4. Excellent organizational skills

Applicant must meet the STC credential requirements as per Board Policy DBA - Employment Requirements and Restrictions: Credentials and Records located at https://pol.tasb.org/PolicyOnline/PolicyDetails?key=632&code=DBA#localTabContent

jobs.title: Part- Time Faculty - Cell/Molecular Biology
jobs.description:
Job Details
El Camino College
Part- Time Faculty - Cell/Molecular Biology
Req: A2627-007
Division: Natural Sciences
Close Date: MONDAY, OCTOBER 26, 2026 AT 3:00 P.M.
Complete job description and application available online at: https://elcamino.igreentree.com/css_academic
The El Camino Community College District is now accepting applications for anticipated part-time faculty positions in the following subject area for spring 2027:
BIOL-110: CELL & MOLECULAR BIOLOGY
Faculty job responsibilities include the development of class curriculum to meet the requirements detailed in the Course Outline of Record, conducting office hours at regularly scheduled days and times, and the assessment of learning outcomes to improve teaching and learning in achieving El Camino College's mission of institutional effectiveness, quality educational programs, and vibrant student support services.
Faculty assignments may include morning, afternoon, evening, or weekend hours. Dual enrollment, distance education, on-line or hybrid with required distance education certification assignments are voluntary. For faculty who are interested in teaching online or hybrid courses, completion of El Camino College's distance education certification process is required or submission of a waiver with evidence of prior certification to develop and teach quality online courses.
Faculty may participate in initiatives set forth by the College that support students to achieve their educational goals through collaborations with employers, advisory committees, industry/trade groups, universities, high schools, or other partnerships with related instructional disciplines.
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
Education and Experience:
Master's degree in biological science; OR
Bachelor's degree in biological science AND a Master's degree in biochemistry, biophysics, or marine sciences; OR
The equivalent - Candidates not possessing the required qualification(s) as stated on this announcement must complete the Request For Equivalency Form as part of the application process to explain in detail how their qualifications are equivalent to those above; OR
Valid California community college instructor credential in appropriate subject issued prior to July 1, 1990 (per California Education Code 87355); AND
Sensitivity to and understanding of diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, and ethnic backgrounds of community college students and of individuals with disabilities.
DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS

The Department of Physical and Environmental Sciences (DPES) at the University of Toronto Scarborough (UTSC) invites applications for a full-time tenure-stream position in the field of Food Studies. REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS
Candidates must have earned a PhD degree in Food Studies or a related discipline by the time of appointment, or shortly thereafter, with a demonstrated record of excellence in research and teaching in Food Studies. We seek candidates whose research and teaching interests complement and enhance our existing departmental strengths. The proposed position would add to the existing departmental research performed within the Food and Environmental Studies discipline. This discipline incorporates a humanities and social science focus within the broader science department. Demonstrated commitment to the interdisciplinary field of Food Studies through scholarship, teaching, and professional activity is essential. We look for a scholar conducting culturally aware, community-engaged research with global scope.
Candidates must provide evidence of research excellence which can be demonstrated through a record of publications in top-ranked Food Studies journals or forthcoming publications that meet high international standards; the submitted research statement that outlines a high quality and innovative multi-year research plan; presentations at significant conferences; awards and accolades; and strong endorsements from referees of high standing.
Evidence of excellence in teaching will be demonstrated through teaching accomplishments, the teaching dossier (including the required materials outlined below, as well as evidence of superior performance in other teaching-related activities), and strong letters of reference. In addition, the successful candidate will be assigned a teaching and service load. The position requires teaching graduate and undergraduate courses in the Department of Physical and Environmental Sciences, as well as providing service to the Department and University. POSITION DESCRIPTION
The Lawrence Bloomberg Faculty of Nursing at the University of Toronto invites applications for up to two full-time tenure stream positions in Nursing. The appointment will be at the rank of Assistant Professor, with an anticipated start date of July 1, 2027.
This position is being advertised concurrently with the full-time tenure stream position in Nursing at the rank of Associate Professor (ID: 50146). To be considered for the full-time tenure stream position in Nursing at the rank of Associate Professor (ID: 50146), you must submit a separate application for each posting.
This search aligns with the University’s commitment to strategically and proactively promote diversity among our community members (Statement on Equity, Diversity & Excellence). Recognizing that Black, Indigenous, and other Racialized communities have experienced inequities that have developed historically and are ongoing, we strongly welcome and encourage candidates from those communities to apply.
Preference will be given to candidates who self-identify as Indigenous. Recognizing that there are a variety of terms that potential candidates may use to self-identify, the University uses the term “Indigenous” in this search, which forms part of the U of T Response to Canada’s Truth and Reconciliation Commission, to encompass the people of Turtle Island, including those who identify as First Nations, Métis, Inuk (Inuit), Alaska Native, Native American, and Native Hawaiian people.
REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS
Candidates must have an entry-to-practice degree (BScN or MN) in nursing, as well as a PhD degree in nursing or a related discipline by the time of appointment, or shortly thereafter, with a demonstrated record of excellence in research and teaching. We seek candidates whose research and teaching interests complement and enhance our existing departmental strengths. All applicants must be eligible for registration with the College of Nurses of Ontario.
Candidates must provide evidence of research excellence which can be demonstrated through a record of publications in top-ranked and field-relevant journals or forthcoming publications that meet high international standards; the submitted research statement; presentations at significant conferences; awards and accolades; and strong endorsements from referees.
Evidence of excellence in teaching will be demonstrated through teaching accomplishments, the teaching dossier including a teaching statement, sample course materials, and teaching evaluations or other evidence of superior performance in teaching-related activities submitted as part of the application, and strong letters of reference. Other teaching-related activities can include performance as a teaching assistant or course instructor, experience leading successful workshops or seminars, student mentorship, or excellent conference presentations or posters.
Candidates must also have experience working with, teaching, or mentoring/supervising diverse groups or diverse students along with the ability to contribute to fostering diversity on campus, and within the curriculum or nursing profession, demonstrated through the application materials.
RESPONSIBILITIES
The successful candidate will be expected to pursue innovative and independent research, and to establish an outstanding, competitive, and externally funded research program.
In addition, the successful candidate will be assigned a teaching and service load.
HIRING SALARY RANGE
The expected salary range is $130,000 - $150,000 CAD per annum, depending on experience. Negotiations beyond this salary range will be considered for exceptionally qualified candidates.
ABOUT US
The Setting
Toronto is one of the world’s most dynamic and multicultural cities. The population of the Greater Toronto Region is nearly 6 million, making it one of the largest metropolitan regions in North America. Over 150 languages are spoken in the city, and half of the city’s population was born outside Canada. The Toronto Region is served by North America’s second largest public transit system, and it has an abundance of parks and green spaces. With a rich and diverse cultural life of music, art and museums, the Toronto Region has more than 70 ﬁlm festivals and 200 professional performing arts organizations. It is Canada’s number-one tourist destination.
The city is home to a burgeoning research environment. The area boasts the fourth-largest cluster of medical expertise in North America. The downtown “Discovery District,” in which the St. George campus of the University of Toronto is situated, contains nine teaching hospitals, numerous scientiﬁc research institutes, and MaRS, an innovation centre that brings ideas in science and technology together with business acumen and ﬁnancing. This intellectual dynamism is evident across all areas of research, education and the arts in the city.
The University
Established in 1827 by royal charter, the University of Toronto is the largest and most prestigious research-intensive university in Canada. The historical strengths that have shaped the University’s progress and achievements include excellence across a wide array of disciplines, leadership in professional education, pre-eminence in graduate education, three federated universities, and decentralized management with strong decanal leadership. The quality and range of the University’s programs—undergraduate, graduate and professional—attract students from all parts of Ontario and Canada, and internationally. The University is home to 18 Faculties and the School of Graduate Studies, and its educational programs are delivered on the historic St. George campus in downtown Toronto, on campuses in Mississauga and Scarborough, and in nine fully aﬃliated teaching hospitals in Toronto. The 2025 Times Higher Education World University Rankings place the University of Toronto at 21st in the world.
The University currently has more than 20,000 faculty and staﬀ; some 80,000 students across its three campuses; almost 250 Canada Research Chairs; an annual budget of $2.0 billion; and an endowment of $1.9 billion. The University of Toronto’s library system ranks third among research libraries in North America and subscribes to over 17,000 electronic journals in all disciplines.
The Lawrence Bloomberg Faculty of Nursing is served by the Gerstein Science Information Centre, the largest academic health science library in Canada. In addition to its extensive print collection, the library has licensed access to several hundred electronic databases in the health sciences including all major nursing and health science indices. All electronic resources are available to faculty and students both from campus and hospital locations and via remote access. In 2020, the University was named one of Canada’s Top 100 Employers, Canada’s Top Family-Friendly Employers and Greater Toronto’s Top Employers. For more information, please visit www.utoronto.ca.
The Lawrence Bloomberg Faculty of Nursing
The Lawrence Bloomberg Faculty of Nursing is consistently ranked in the top 10 in the QS World University Rankings by Subject for nursing and is a research-intensive Faculty that embraces the University's tripartite mission of excellence in research, education, and practice. The Bloomberg Faculty of Nursing oﬀers multiple innovative graduate and undergraduate degree programs, drawing on a partnership with one of North America’s largest academic health science complexes; the Toronto Academic Health Sciences Network (TAHSN), which incorporates fourteen multi-site, fully aﬃliated teaching hospitals, as well as a network of aﬃliated community hospitals and public health agencies. The Faculty is committed to the mission of international leadership in nursing research and education. Through the leadership and mentorship of outstanding faculty members, the Faculty’s graduates excel in professional practice, lead in nursing research and scholarship, and improve health locally and globally.
The Bloomberg Faculty of Nursing oﬀers a 20-month, second entry, Baccalaureate program. In addition, the Faculty oﬀers a highly sought after professional master’s program comprising three ﬁelds (clinical, health systems leadership and administration, and nurse practitioner) and world-leading doctoral programs. The Faculty now has an academic presence on all three campuses – University of Toronto St. George, University of Toronto Mississauga and University of Toronto Scarborough. Through the TAHSN partnership and our state-of-the-art simulation laboratory, the Faculty provides its students with a strong foundation in all practice settings through ﬁrst class clinical experiences. The Faculty is committed to excellence and supports an environment of creativity and innovation in pedagogy. For more information on the Lawrence Bloomberg Faculty of Nursing please visit our home page at http://bloomberg.nursing.utoronto.ca/.

Recognizing that there are a variety of terms that potential candidates may use to self-identify, the University uses the term “Indigenous” in this search, which forms part of the U of T Response to Canada’s Truth and Reconciliation Commission, to encompass the people of Turtle Island, including those who identify as First Nations, Métis, Inuk (Inuit), Alaska Native, Native American, and Native Hawaiian people.
REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS
Applicants must have an entry-to-practice degree (BScN or MN) in nursing, as well as a PhD degree in nursing or a related area, with a clearly demonstrated record of excellence in research and teaching. Candidates must have an established international reputation. We seek candidates whose research and teaching interests complement and enhance our existing departmental strengths. All applicants must be eligible for registration with the College of Nurses of Ontario.
Candidates must provide evidence of research excellence, as demonstrated by a record of sustained high-impact contributions and publications in top-ranked and field-relevant journals; the submitted research statement; presentations at significant conferences; awards and accolades; other noteworthy activities that contribute to the visibility and prominence of the discipline; and strong endorsements from referees.
Evidence of excellence in teaching will be demonstrated through teaching accomplishments, the teaching dossier, including a teaching statement, sample course materials, and teaching evaluations or other evidence of superior performance in teaching-related activities submitted as part of the application and strong letters of reference.
Candidates must also have experience working with, teaching, or mentoring/supervising diverse groups or diverse students along with the ability to contribute to fostering diversity on campus, and within the curriculum or nursing profession, demonstrated through the application materials.
RESPONSIBILITIES
Candidates will be expected to sustain and lead innovative and independent research, and to maintain an outstanding, competitive, and externally funded research program.
In addition, the successful candidate will be assigned a teaching and service load.
HIRING SALARY RANGE
The expected salary range is $150,000 - $180,000 CAD per annum. Exceptionally qualified candidates may be considered for compensation beyond this stated range.
ABOUT US
The Setting
Toronto is one of the world’s most dynamic and multicultural cities. The population of the Greater Toronto Region is nearly 6 million, making it one of the largest metropolitan regions in North America. Over 150 languages are spoken in the city, and half of the city’s population was born outside Canada. The Toronto Region is served by North America’s second largest public transit system, and it has an abundance of parks and green spaces. With a rich and diverse cultural life of music, art and museums, the Toronto Region has more than 70 ﬁlm festivals and 200 professional performing arts organizations. It is Canada’s number-one tourist destination.
The city is home to a burgeoning research environment. The area boasts the fourth-largest cluster of medical expertise in North America. The downtown “Discovery District,” in which the St. George campus of the University of Toronto is situated, contains nine teaching hospitals, numerous scientiﬁc research institutes, and MaRS, an innovation centre that brings ideas in science and technology together with business acumen and ﬁnancing. This intellectual dynamism is evident across all areas of research, education and the arts in the city.
The University
Established in 1827 by royal charter, the University of Toronto is the largest and most prestigious research-intensive university in Canada. The historical strengths that have shaped the University’s progress and achievements include excellence across a wide array of disciplines, leadership in professional education, pre-eminence in graduate education, three federated universities, and decentralized management with strong decanal leadership. The quality and range of the University’s programs—undergraduate, graduate and professional—attract students from all parts of Ontario and Canada, and internationally. The University is home to 18 Faculties and the School of Graduate Studies, and its educational programs are delivered on the historic St. George campus in downtown Toronto, on campuses in Mississauga and Scarborough, and in nine fully aﬃliated teaching hospitals in Toronto. The 2025 Times Higher Education World University Rankings place the University of Toronto at 21st in the world.
The University currently has more than 20,000 faculty and staﬀ; some 80,000 students across its three campuses; almost 250 Canada Research Chairs; an annual budget of $2.0 billion; and an endowment of $1.9 billion. The University of Toronto’s library system ranks third among research libraries in North America and subscribes to over 17,000 electronic journals in all disciplines.
The Lawrence Bloomberg Faculty of Nursing is served by the Gerstein Science Information Centre, the largest academic health science library in Canada. In addition to its extensive print collection, the library has licensed access to several hundred electronic databases in the health sciences including all major nursing and health science indices. All electronic resources are available to faculty and students both from campus and hospital locations and via remote access. In 2020, the University was named one of Canada’s Top 100 Employers, Canada’s Top Family-Friendly Employers and Greater Toronto’s Top Employers. For more information, please visit www.utoronto.ca.
The Lawrence Bloomberg Faculty of Nursing
The Lawrence Bloomberg Faculty of Nursing is consistently ranked in the top 10 in the QS World University Rankings by Subject for nursing and is a research-intensive Faculty that embraces the University's tripartite mission of excellence in research, education, and practice. The Bloomberg Faculty of Nursing oﬀers multiple innovative graduate and undergraduate degree programs, drawing on a partnership with one of North America’s largest academic health science complexes; the Toronto Academic Health Sciences Network (TAHSN), which incorporates fourteen multi-site, fully aﬃliated teaching hospitals, as well as a network of aﬃliated community hospitals and public health agencies. The Faculty is committed to the mission of international leadership in nursing research and education. Through the leadership and mentorship of outstanding faculty members, the Faculty’s graduates excel in professional practice, lead in nursing research and scholarship, and improve health locally and globally.
The Bloomberg Faculty of Nursing oﬀers a 20-month, second entry, Baccalaureate program. In addition, the Faculty oﬀers a highly sought after professional master’s program comprising three ﬁelds (clinical, health systems leadership and administration, and nurse practitioner) and world-leading doctoral programs. The Faculty now has an academic presence on all three campuses – University of Toronto St. George, University of Toronto Mississauga and University of Toronto Scarborough. Through the TAHSN partnership and our state-of-the-art simulation laboratory, the Faculty provides its students with a strong foundation in all practice settings through ﬁrst class clinical experiences. The Faculty is committed to excellence and supports an environment of creativity and innovation in pedagogy. For more information on the Lawrence Bloomberg Faculty of Nursing please visit our home page at http://bloomberg.nursing.utoronto.ca/.

Description:
Division of Rheumatology - Department of Paediatrics
Effective immediately the Department of Paediatrics at the Hospital for Sick Children, (SickKids), 555 University Avenue, Toronto, Ontario is recruiting for a permanent full-time faculty position as an Academic Clinician in the Division of Rheumatology. SickKids is an academic health science centre dedicated to the care of children and is a fully affiliated hospital with the University of Toronto.
The Division provides tertiary and quaternary care for children with rheumatic diseases and has established a tradition of excellence in clinical care, education and research. Subspecialty clinics for children and adolescents with dermatomyositis, morphea, systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis, autoinflammatory diseases, spondyloarthritis, CNO, vasculitis and systemic lupus erythematosus are well established. The Fellowship Training Program is fully accredited by the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada. Independent and collaborative clinical and basic science research is performed by Division members.
We encourage applications from individuals within 10 years of completing their rheumatology training, with preference given to applicants who are in early to mid-career stage. Expertise or a focused interest in autoinflammatory diseases or vasculitis is preferred; training in quality improvement and safety or musculoskeletal ultrasound would be an asset. The role’s primary responsibilities are delivering excellent clinical care and pursuing scholarly academic work. Our large, collaborative multidisciplinary team of physicians, nurses, allied health professionals, researchers, and administrative staff provides many opportunities for academic contribution.
Clinical activities will include ambulatory clinics, attending and consulting inpatients, and participating in on-call responsibilities. In addition to scholarly academic work, educational activities will include the teaching and supervision of learners including students, residents and fellows. Additional responsibilities include attending divisional meetings, participating in the weekly academic half day, weekly Paediatric Grand Rounds and other educational sessions. The candidate is also expected to take part in divisional and departmental administrative duties and participate in CME events.
The successful candidate will be eligible for an academic appointment at the University of Toronto. Rank and salary ($275,548 to $340,000) will be commensurate with qualifications and experience. The successful candidate will be eligible for a benefit package which includes medical, dental, life insurance, long term disability insurance, group insurance, pension plan, vision care, academic allowance, and a relocation package.
All candidates must be able to function proficiently in English, hold an MD, MBBS or the equivalent thereto and be certified or eligible for certification by the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada or have comparable qualification. The successful candidate must have completed subspecialty training in Rheumatology and must hold or be eligible for licensure with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario.
All qualified candidates are invited to apply online before November 30, 2026, at the Hospital for Sick Children, 555 University Avenue, Toronto, Ontario, M5G 1X8. Applications should include a cover letter, curriculum vitae, and a statement outlining current and future clinical, academic and research interests. Applicants should also provide names and addresses of three references by email to Dr. Deborah Levy, Head, Division of Rheumatology at deborah.levy@sickkids.ca
For additional information regarding the Department of Paediatrics, see http://www.sickkids.ca/paediatrics/.

Next Lives at the University of Cincinnati
Founded in 1819, the University of Cincinnati ranks among the nation’s best urban public research universities. Home to more than 53,600 students, 12,000 faculty and staff, and over 360,000 living alumni, UC, a Carnegie 1 institution, combines research prowess with a physical setting The New York Times has called “the most ambitious campus design program in the country." UC's momentum has never been stronger as the anchor of the Cincinnati Innovation District, the oldest cooperative education (co-op) program in the country with students earning $94 million annually through paid experiences, an academic health system, and as a member of the Big 12 Conference. The university contributes $10.6 billion in economic impact to the city and $22.7 billion to the state of Ohio. At UC, next is all of us. Learn more at uc.edu.

Job Details

Location:

Open Date:
Nov 4, 2025
Description:
The Dartmouth Cancer Center (DCC) invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the rank of Assistant Professor at the Geisel School of Medicine to join either our Immunotherapy and Cancer Immunology (ICI) or Signaling, Genomes and Networks (SGN) Research Programs. Exceptional candidates at senior ranks may also be considered.
We seek an outstanding and collaborative individual to develop an innovative research program in cancer immunology or cancer biology. Research areas of interest include, but are not limited to, cellular therapy, tumor microenvironment and myeloid cells, antibody therapeutics, immune checkpoints, cancer vaccines, and T-cell immunology, the study of vertebrate models of cancer, the development of therapeutic strategies for or resistance mechanisms of cancer, and studies of cancer signaling pathways. The successful candidate will be appointed into one of several academic departments at the Geisel School of Medicine based on the focus of their research program, including Microbiology and Immunology, Biochemistry and Cell Biology, or Molecular and Systems Biology. DCC, one of 57 NCI-designated Comprehensive Cancer Centers, offers a dynamic and interactive environment, with a commitment to research excellence commensurate with Dartmouth’s status as an R1 Doctoral University. The successful candidate will have access to thriving multidisciplinary graduate programs through the Guarini School of Graduate and Advanced Studies (e.g., the Program in Molecular and Cellular Biology, which contains a concentration in Cancer Biology, and the Program in Quantitative Biomedical Sciences). Faculty members at the Geisel School of Medicine benefit from highly collaborative and collegial interactions across Dartmouth, inclusive of other departments at Geisel, the School of Arts & Sciences, and the Thayer School of Engineering. Job Details
Manager, Faculty Experience and Systems (FT), MFRE10220TLE
Manager, Faculty Experience and Systems (FT), MFRE10220TLE
The College of DuPage is a comprehensive community college located 27 miles west of downtown Chicago, vitally connected to our local area for over 50 years. We prepare students for a lifelong passion for learning on our 273-acre campus which is home to nine associate degrees and a wide variety of professional and technical certificates. Many of these credentials prepare students to seamlessly articulate into the baccalaureate programs of our higher education partner institutions.
College of DuPage is committed to student success and values an inclusive and welcoming community environment. We are an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity in the workforce. Our connection to the larger metropolitan area is essential to our success and provides a wealth of diverse cultural and recreational opportunities.
Primary Duties and Responsibilities:
This position provides leadership and operational oversight for faculty support systems and services across the Divisions of Business & Technology, Nursing & Health Sciences, Liberal Arts, Social & Behavioral Sciences, STEM, Art, Communication & Hospitality, Continuing Education & Extended Learning, Learning Resources, and Student Affairs. Serving as a central resource for faculty-facing systems and processes, the role integrates learning systems administration, division support, and program management to enhance faculty experience and promote student success. The position is responsible for the administration, coordination, and continuous improvement of systems that support faculty evaluation and instructional effectiveness, including student evaluation platforms and observation-related processes through various systems. While not directly conducting classroom observations, the role supports the full observation lifecycle through system management, process coordination, and data integrity. Working collaboratively with cross-functional teams, this position leads the implementation and support of institutional initiatives related to instructional technology and artificial intelligence, ensuring alignment with college priorities and effective adoption across divisions. The role also partners with academic and administrative areas to identify opportunities for system enhancements, streamline workflows, and improve faculty engagement with institutional tools and resources. This position leads the planning and delivery of faculty professional development initiatives, including new hire orientation, in-service programming, and ongoing training focused on instructional excellence, technology integration, and emerging practices such as AI in education. Additionally, the role supports key institutional events, including commencement and faculty recognition efforts such as teacher appreciation programs. The position manages supporting documentation, oversees data collection and reporting, and analyzes outcomes related to faculty development, system utilization, and evaluation processes. Through a combination of systems management, data-informed decision-making, and cross-divisional collaboration, this role contributes to continuous improvement in teaching effectiveness and the overall faculty experience.
Lead the administration, maintenance, and continuous improvement of faculty support systems, including student evaluation platforms (e.g., Watermark), learning management system (LMS) functions, and related instructional technologies.
Oversee the collection, analysis, and reporting of data related to faculty evaluations, professional development, and system utilization; provide actionable insights to Deans and institutional leadership to support decision-making and continuous improvement.
Support and advance institutional initiatives related to artificial intelligence and instructional technology by facilitating adoption, providing training, and identifying opportunities for innovation in teaching and learning.
Develop, refine, and monitor metrics and key performance indicators related to instructional quality, faculty engagement, and effectiveness of faculty support systems.
Collaborate with academic and administrative divisions to streamline processes, enhance system functionality, and improve the overall faculty experience.
Manage and coordinate the full lifecycle of student evaluations and observation-related processes, ensuring accuracy, efficiency, and alignment across all academic divisions in partnership with the Office of Information Technology.
Design, implement, and deliver faculty onboarding experiences, including new hire orientation programs, using multiple delivery modalities to support diverse faculty needs.
Lead the planning, coordination, and facilitation of faculty professional development initiatives, including in-service (kickoff) events and ongoing training focused on instructional excellence, technology integration, and emerging practices such as artificial intelligence in education.
Provide operational leadership for faculty evaluation processes by ensuring timely execution, clear communication, and alignment with institutional standards; support feedback workflows for Deans, Coordinators, and faculty.
Support and advance institutional initiatives related to artificial intelligence and instructional technology by facilitating adoption, providing training, and identifying opportunities for innovation in teaching and learning.
Plan and support institutional events related to faculty engagement, including commencement, in-service programming, and faculty recognition initiatives such as teacher appreciation.
Serve on College committees and participate in cross-functional initiatives to support institutional priorities.
Other duties and projects as assigned.
Qualifications:
Education
Master's degree in Strategic Management, Organizational Leadership, Higher Education Administration, Business Administration, or a closely related field required.
Doctoral degree (PhD or EdD) in a relevant discipline preferred, or in progress.
Experience
Minimum of 3 years of experience in higher education, academic operations, faculty support, instructional technology, or a related area required.
Experience managing or supporting learning management systems (LMS), faculty evaluation platforms (e.g., Watermark), or similar enterprise systems strongly preferred.
Demonstrated experience in data analysis, process improvement, and cross-functional collaboration preferred.
Project management experience in complex, multi-stakeholder environments preferred; Project Management Professional (PMP) certification or equivalent training is a plus preferred.
Demonstrated experience leading or supporting system implementations, upgrades, or process improvement initiatives, particularly within higher education or similar organizational settings preferred.
Proven ability to manage multiple priorities, drive initiatives from concept to completion, and adapt to evolving institutional needs preferred.
Supervisory or managerial experience preferred, including leading projects, coordinating cross-functional teams, or providing functional oversight in a collaborative environment preferred.
Experience designing and delivering professional development or training programs, preferably in an academic or faculty-facing environment.
Familiarity with emerging technologies in education, including artificial intelligence applications in teaching and learning, preferred.
Working Conditions:
Utilizes standard office equipment, including computers, in order to perform the duties of the job.
Work is primarily indoor and sedentary in nature.
Evening hours are required periodically as well as occasional travel to Regional Centers and other COD locations as needed to work with adjunct/part-time faculty.
We do not offer visa sponsorship for this position. Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States without restriction.
Hiring Range:
13 Salary Starting salary beginning at $84,672, based on education and experience
If you require assistance or accommodations during the application or interview process, please notify Human Resources by humanresources@cod.edu or (630) 942-2460
Competitive starting pay is dependent on education and experience. College of DuPage also offers a generous benefits plan which includes paid time off, tuition discounts for employees and dependents, medical, dental, vision effective the first day of employment, and retirement benefits in a collaborative and friendly environment.
College of DuPage is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to diversity and creating an inclusive environment for all employees.
College of DuPage does not discriminate against individuals in employment opportunities, programs and/or activities on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, age, national origin, ancestry, veterans' status, marital status, disability, military status, unfavorable discharge from military service, or on any other basis protected by law.

Job Details
Assistant/Associate Professor of Education
Job ID: 304477

About Us
Georgia College & State University (GCSU) is the state's designated public liberal arts university, where students learn the essential skills to compete in a fast-paced and technology-driven global society. The university prepares students for successful careers, leadership in communities, problem solving and life-long learning through personalized attention in a residential setting with opportunities for a variety of transformational experiences through its award-winning, high-impact practices. One of only three selective universities within the University System of Georgia and a top 10 ranked public university in the Southeast, GCSU offers undergraduate degrees in more than 40 majors, more than 30 graduate programs, doctorates in education and nursing, professional certificates, and continuing education programs.
As a member of the prestigious Council of Public Liberal Arts Colleges (COPLAC), GCSU is committed to fostering a liberal arts environment that values academic preeminence, interdisciplinary inquiry and an inclusive learning community. GCSU enjoys a strong reputation for academic excellence and nationally ranked programs according to US News & World Report, The Princeton Review and Colleges of Distinction - among other ranking sources.
Georgia College & State University takes great pride in combining the educational experience of a private liberal arts college with the affordability of a public university. Faculty and staff are dedicated to student engagement and experiential learning through high-impact practices such as internships, service- and community-based learning, leadership development, study abroad opportunities, mentored undergraduate research and a capstone project that fosters intellectual curiosity, reasoned inquiry and critical thinking.
The university's beautiful and historic campus is located downtown in Milledgeville, Georgia, a charming college town of approximately 19,000 residents in Central Georgia, and only 90 miles southeast of Atlanta. Milledgeville is also the home of noted American author and alumna, Flannery O'Connor, '45, and the college community enjoys many exciting literary arts programs at O'Connor's former home, Andalusia, a National Historic Landmark owned by the university. Milledgeville is located on the banks of beautiful Lake Sinclair and Lake Oconee, allowing faculty, staff and students to take full advantage of the environmental and recreational benefits of being part of a lake community. For cultural, educational and leisure opportunities beyond Milledgeville - Macon and Atlanta are located within easy driving distances.
Georgia College & State University is dedicated to protecting academic freedom in addition to supporting freedom of expression as outlined in the University System of Georgia's Freedom of Expression and Academic Freedom policy and its Ethics Code of Conduct. For more information, visit us online at gcsu.edu.
Job Summary
The John H. Lounsbury College of Education at Georgia College & State University invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant/Associate Professor position. The successful candidate will teach graduate and/or undergraduate courses in the college and maintain an active record of scholarship and service. The faculty member may also be assigned responsibilities supporting collegewide assessment, accreditation, and continuous improvement, including work associated with the Georgia Professional Standards Commission (GaPSC) and the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP). Reassigned time may be provided for these responsibilities based on College needs.
Georgia College & State University seeks faculty who understand and embrace our public liberal arts mission and are dedicated to the advancement of knowledge through teaching, scholarship, and service. All Georgia College & State University faculty share the responsibility of teaching our core curriculum and providing foundation courses for majors and non-majors alike.
Responsibilities
Faculty - Teaching/Instructing -
The successful candidate will teach graduate and/or undergraduate courses offered within the John H. Lounsbury College of Education and fulfill the teaching, scholarship, and service expectations of a tenure-track Assistant/Associate Professor. The standard teaching load is 4-4 during the fall and spring semesters, with courses offered both on campus and online. Faculty are expected to maintain a regular on-campus presence. Candidates must demonstrate successful teaching experience.
As part of the faculty member's role, the individual may also be assigned responsibilities supporting collegewide assessment, accreditation, and continuous improvement. Reassigned time may be provided based on the scope of the assignment and College needs. Responsibilities may include supporting GaPSC and CAEP compliance, reporting, self-studies, accreditation documentation, and site visits.
Faculty - Professional Development -
Faculty are expected to conduct research and develop within the profession. Engaging in scholarly activity that informs classroom instruction is strongly encouraged. Scholarship of teaching and learning is especially valued. Academic achievement may include:
- Publications, including editing and citations
- Peer-reviewed scholarship
- Presentations at professional meetings
- Current work in circulation or in progress
- Grants received or applied for
- Membership and participation in professional organizations
- Other professional service and development activities
Faculty - Service to Institution -
All faculty are expected to support the advancement of the department, college, and university mission by providing service to the institution. Service may be at the department, college, university, community, and disciplinary levels. Duties include service on college-level and university-level committees, advising students regarding career options, and supporting department-level outreach activities. Service may include:
- Committee memberships and offices
- Programs directed and advised
- Participation in special programs or projects
- Other service to the institution
Faculty are expected to work collegially with others in service to the University and to support the advancement of the department, college, and University mission.
Faculty - Public Service -
Engage in service to the institution and provide service in the community and local schools.
Other duties and responsibilities -
Assist with continual program development.
Participate in program, department, college, university, and other committees.
The faculty member may also be assigned responsibilities supporting collegewide assessment , accreditation, and continuous improvement, including work associated with the Georgia professional Standards Commission (GaPSC) and the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP). Reassigned time may be provided for these responsibilities based on College needs.
Participate in student recruitment and placement activities.
Perform administrative duties as needed.
Required Qualifications
Educational Requirements
Ph.D. or Ed.D. degree in Education or closely related field
Must meet SACSCOC accreditation requirements stated in C.S. 3.7.1 (www.sacscoc.org (faculty credentials))
Required Experience
Three years teaching PreK-12 learners.
Preferred Qualifications
Additional Preferred Qualifications
Face-to-face and online course design experience.
Working knowledge of Quality Matters Standards.
Experience with accreditation reporting.
Preferred Experience
Evidence of successful teaching in higher education.
CAEP & GaPSC Experience.
Proposed Salary
The proposed salary range is $61,192 - $70,000. Salary is based on relevant experience.
Relocation is negotiable.
Rank will be determined by the candidate's qualifications and record of teaching, scholarship, and service. Appointment at the associate level requires a record that meets GCSU and College of Education criteria for that rank.
Required Documents to Attach
Transcripts
List of References
Teaching Philosophy
CV/Resume
Cover Letter
Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities
ABILITIES
Build positive student relationships and provide mentorship
Manage multiple courses and administrative responsibilities
Solve problems and make data-driven decisions
Collaborate with colleagues and participate in service
Demonstrate leadership and take initiative
Adapt to changing institutional needs
Maintain accurate records and meet deadlines
Ability to be an effective member of a learning community, program, and committee
Ability to effectively participate in professional development and apply the new knowledge and skills to one's practice
Ability to develop and demonstrate knowledge of current philosophies, practices, and theories related to the academic discipline
KNOWLEDGE
Subject matter expertise and current disciplinary trends
Curriculum design and program outcome alignment
Assessment methods and student learning measurement
Accreditation standards (SACSCOC and discipline-specific)
Academic policies, procedures, and ethics
Adult learning principles and adaptive learning styles
Educational technology and learning management systems
SKILLS
Teaching:
Course design and delivery
